# Free Data Feed Inventory — Prediction Market Research Panel

Swept 2026-09-20 by 18 parallel research agents (843 tool calls). Every entry
below carries a live-check flag: `LIVE` means an agent actually fetched the
docs page or endpoint and confirmed it responds. Unflagged = documented but
not exercised.

**A dead end is as valuable as a feed.** Section 3 lists 420 sources that look
free and are not, or that died between 2023 and 2026. Most tutorials and most
pre-2026 model knowledge still recommend them.

---

## 1. Summary

- **732 feeds** across 18 domains
- **302 rated CORE** (build on these)
- **626 live-verified**
- **420 dead ends flagged**
- **317 GitHub repos worth stealing from**

---

## 2. Feeds by domain

### API catalogs and open-data indexes

#### CORE

**public-apis (README catalog)** — public-apis/public-apis GitHub org (sponsored by APILayer) `LIVE`

- The single largest community-curated directory of free public REST APIs. Verified 2026-09-20: 1,902 table entries across 52 category headings in a 268,910-byte README.md. Each row carries API name, link, description, Auth type (No/apiKey/OAuth), HTTPS flag, and CORS flag.
- Docs: https://github.com/public-apis/public-apis
- Base: `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/public-apis/public-apis/master/README.md`
- Auth: none | Limits: Unlimited via raw.githubusercontent.com (GitHub raw soft limit ~5,000 req/hr per IP). Repo is MIT-licensed, so full local mirroring is permitted and recommended.
- Latency: daily (pushed_at 2026-09-20T20:48:35Z; commits land most days) | Format: scrape-only (Markdown tables) — NO JSON index exists in the repo
- Relevance: Tier-0 discovery layer. This is the breadth map that tells you which free endpoints exist at all for weather, sports, crypto, finance, government, transport, health and news contracts. It does not price anything itself; it is the index you crawl once to enumerate candidate feeds for every other market vertical.

**public-api-lists JSON API** — public-api-lists/public-api-lists (GitHub Pages) `LIVE`

- The best drop-in machine-readable replacement for the dead api.publicapis.org. Verified 2026-09-20: 837 APIs across 48 categories. Endpoints: /api/all.json (221,269 bytes, full entry list), /api/categories.json, /api/stats.json, /api/random.json, and /api/{category-slug}.json. stats.json reports auth_breakdown (No:397, apiKey:359, OAuth:77, X-Mashape-Key:4), https_percentage 92.8, cors_breakdown (Yes:291, No:52, Unknown:494), last_updated 2026-09-14T07:20:04Z. Each entry: name, url, description, auth, https, cors, category.
- Docs: https://github.com/public-api-lists/public-api-lists
- Base: `https://public-api-lists.github.io/public-api-lists/api/all.json`
- Auth: none | Limits: No documented limit — static JSON on GitHub Pages (GitHub Pages soft bandwidth cap 100GB/month for the repo owner, not per-consumer). Rebuilt automatically by GitHub Actions on every README.md push to master.
- Latency: weekly-to-daily (rebuild triggers only on README.md change; last build 2026-09-14) | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: Same discovery role as public-apis but consumable by a program without writing a Markdown parser. For a research panel this is the bootstrap file: load all.json at build time to seed the connector registry, then filter by auth==='No' for the zero-friction subset.

**APIs.guru OpenAPI Directory** — APIs.guru `LIVE`

- The largest repository of machine-readable API descriptions. Verified 2026-09-20 via /v2/metrics.json: 2,529 APIs, 3,992 OpenAPI specs, 108,837 individual endpoints, 166 unreachable, 688 invalid, 25 unofficial. /v2/list.json returns a keyed object (e.g. '1forge.com', 'ably.io:platform', 'abstractapi.com:geolocation') where each value carries versions, swaggerUrl, swaggerYamlUrl, info block, contact, license and added/updated timestamps.
- Docs: https://apis.guru/api-doc/
- Base: `https://api.apis.guru/v2/list.json`
- Auth: none | Limits: No key, no documented rate limit. Full list.json is a single fetch; each spec is a separate static file.
- Latency: daily (specs are re-crawled and re-validated continuously) | Format: REST JSON + downloadable OpenAPI 3 / Swagger 2 specs per API
- Relevance: The highest-value catalog for automated integration: because every entry ships a full OpenAPI spec with 108,837 typed endpoints, you can machine-generate typed clients rather than hand-writing connectors. This is how you scale from ~20 hand-built feeds to hundreds without linear engineering cost.

**DataPortals.org portal registry** — Open Knowledge Foundation / DataPortals.org `LIVE`

- The registry-of-registries. Verified 2026-09-20: a single 567,819-byte JSON object containing 631 open-data portals worldwide. Critically, each record includes api_endpoint and api_type fields (plus name, title, url, publisher, publisher_classification, description, tags, license_id, license_url, place, location, country, language, status, generator, full_metadata_download). api_type tells you whether a given national/regional/city portal runs CKAN, Socrata, OpenDataSoft or DKAN.
- Docs: https://dataportals.org/
- Base: `https://dataportals.org/api/data.json`
- Auth: none | Limits: No documented limit; single static JSON file.
- Latency: monthly-to-yearly (community-maintained; many issued dates are historical — treat individual portal liveness as UNVERIFIED and health-check before use) | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: This is the force multiplier for a god's-eye panel. Because it records api_type per portal, you can write ONE CKAN adapter, ONE Socrata adapter and ONE OpenDataSoft adapter, then auto-federate across hundreds of government portals covering mining permits, minerals output, local incidents, transport, budgets and elections — rather than integrating each country by hand.

**data.europa.eu (EU Official Open Data Portal)** — European Commission / Publications Office of the EU `LIVE`

- Verified 2026-09-20: 1,904,033 datasets and 213 source catalogues federated from all EU member states plus EU institutions. Search endpoint returns DCAT-AP metadata. /api/hub/search/catalogues enumerates the 213 upstream catalogue IDs (erpd, sesar, trade, taxud, zenodo, sandre, cedefop, bev-at, cor, cpvo, …), each of which can be queried individually.
- Docs: https://data.europa.eu/en/developers-corner
- Base: `https://data.europa.eu/api/hub/search/search`
- Auth: none | Limits: No key required, no published quota. UNKNOWN whether an undocumented rate limit applies — throttle defensively.
- Latency: daily (harvests member-state portals on a rolling schedule) | Format: REST JSON (DCAT-AP vocabulary), SPARQL endpoint also available
- Relevance: Largest single open-data surface on Earth by dataset count. Feeds European energy, agriculture, minerals/mining, trade, transport and regulatory contract types, and is the authoritative source for EU statistical releases that markets resolve against.

**data.gov.uk CKAN API** — UK Government Digital Service `LIVE`

- Verified 2026-09-20: 59,028 datasets via a standard CKAN 3 Action API. Full CKAN verb surface available — package_search (with Solr query syntax and facets), package_show, organization_list, group_list, resource_show.
- Docs: https://guidance.data.gov.uk/
- Base: `https://ckan.publishing.service.gov.uk/api/3/action/package_search`
- Auth: none | Limits: No key, no published quota. Standard CKAN paging: rows (max 1000 per call) + start offset.
- Latency: daily | Format: REST JSON (CKAN Action API)
- Relevance: UK-specific resolution source for energy, transport, health, crime, planning and environment contracts. Notably still a genuine CKAN portal — unlike the US, so generic CKAN tooling works unmodified.

**data.gov Search API v4 (US, post-CKAN)** — US General Services Administration (api.gsa.gov) `LIVE`

- The replacement for the retired catalog.data.gov CKAN API. Verified live 2026-09-20 with api_key=DEMO_KEY: returns _score-ranked results where each hit carries a full dcat object (@type dcat:Dataset, accessLevel, contactPoint, description, identifier, title, keyword, publisher, organization, theme, distribution_titles, harvest_record). Pagination is cursor-based via an opaque `after` token, NOT offset-based.
- Docs: https://open.gsa.gov/api/datadotgov/
- Base: `https://api.gsa.gov/technology/datagov/v4/search`
- Auth: free API key (api.data.gov key; DEMO_KEY works for evaluation) | Limits: DEMO_KEY is heavily throttled (api.data.gov documents DEMO_KEY at 30 req/hour per IP, 50/day). A free registered api.data.gov key raises this to the standard 1,000 req/hour default. Total dataset count is NOT exposed in the response — the v4 API returns no total field, only the cursor.
- Latency: daily | Format: REST JSON (DCAT-US wrapped)
- Relevance: US federal resolution source across every agency — energy (EIA), agriculture (USDA), labor, transport (DOT/FAA), health (CDC/FDA), NOAA weather and USGS minerals/mining. Essential, but you MUST use v4; anything written against the CKAN path is now broken.

**Socrata Discovery API** — Tyler Technologies (Socrata) `LIVE`

- A single federated search across every Socrata-powered government portal (most large US cities and states, plus some national portals). Verified 2026-09-20: returns resource objects with name, id (4x4 dataset identifier), description, resource_name, parent_fxf, columns, and the owning domain. Example hit: 'Dallas Police Active Calls' / id 9fxf-t2tr.
- Docs: https://socratadiscovery.docs.apiary.io/
- Base: `https://api.us.socrata.com/api/catalog/v1`
- Auth: none (optional free app token raises limits) | Limits: Anonymous access is shared-pool throttled and can 429 under load. A free Socrata app token gives a per-token bucket. Observed resultSetSize caps at 10,000 for broad queries — paginate by facet, not by deep offset.
- Latency: realtime for the catalog; individual datasets update per-publisher (some are minutely, e.g. active police calls) | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: The single best source of municipal-level, sub-daily incident data — 911/police active calls, fire dispatch, permits, inspections, transit. This is the closest thing to a live city-incident firehose that requires no auth, and it is what a god's-eye local-events panel should be built on.

**OpenDataSoft federated catalog (Explore API v2.1)** — OpenDataSoft `LIVE`

- Verified 2026-09-20: data.opendatasoft.com hub exposes 101,374 datasets federated across OpenDataSoft-hosted portals (public.opendatasoft.com itself holds 419). Each dataset record returns dataset_id, dataset_uid, visibility, fields schema, features and has_records, and records are queryable with ODSQL (a SQL-like where/select/group_by language) directly over HTTP.
- Docs: https://help.opendatasoft.com/apis/ods-explore-v2/
- Base: `https://data.opendatasoft.com/api/explore/v2.1/catalog/datasets`
- Auth: none for public domains | Limits: Anonymous calls are rate-limited per domain (OpenDataSoft documents ~10,000 calls/day anonymous on most public domains; exact figure varies by tenant). limit max 100 per page for records; use offset or the export endpoint for bulk.
- Latency: varies by dataset — many are hourly or daily; catalog metadata is realtime | Format: REST JSON + CSV/GeoJSON/Parquet bulk export endpoints
- Relevance: Strong European and utility/energy coverage (grid operators, rail, municipal). The ODSQL layer means you can compute aggregates server-side rather than pulling raw rows — valuable when a contract resolves on a sum or a threshold.

#### USEFUL

**re3data Registry of Research Data Repositories** — DataCite / re3data.org `LIVE`

- Verified 2026-09-20: 3,525 research-data repositories indexed, each with a persistent re3data ID (r3d1000…), DOI, name, institution, subject classification, content type, access conditions, API endpoints and licence terms. /api/v1/repositories returns the full 1,112,192-byte list; /api/v1/repository/{id} returns the detailed record.
- Docs: https://www.re3data.org/api/doc
- Base: `https://www.re3data.org/api/v1/repositories`
- Auth: none | Limits: No key, no published quota.
- Latency: monthly | Format: REST XML (no JSON variant)
- Relevance: The authoritative map of where scientific data physically lives, by discipline. This is how you find the domain-specific repository (seismology, oceanography, epidemiology, particle physics) behind a science-resolution contract rather than guessing.

**Zenodo REST API** — CERN / OpenAIRE `LIVE`

- Verified 2026-09-20: 7,315,322 records. Full-text and metadata search over datasets, publications, software and preprints, each with a DOI, versioned files, and direct file download URLs.
- Docs: https://developers.zenodo.org/
- Base: `https://zenodo.org/api/records`
- Auth: none for read; free personal access token for write/higher limits | Limits: Documented at 60 req/min and 2,000 req/hour for anonymous; 100 req/min and 5,000 req/hour with a free token. OPERATIONAL QUIRK VERIFIED: the WAF returns HTTP 403 for browser-like User-Agent strings (Mozilla/5.0) but HTTP 200 for a default curl UA — do not send a spoofed browser UA.
- Latency: realtime for deposits; effectively daily for anything you would track | Format: REST JSON + OAI-PMH bulk harvest
- Relevance: Where preprints and their supporting datasets land first. Relevant to science/discovery contracts (fusion milestones, drug trial readouts, climate records) where the market moves on a preprint before peer review.

**OpenAIRE Research Graph API** — OpenAIRE AMKE `LIVE`

- Verified 2026-09-20: 108,282,207 dataset-type research records (the full graph including publications and software is far larger). Aggregates metadata from thousands of repositories, journals and funders with linkage between publications, datasets, software, projects and funding streams.
- Docs: https://graph.openaire.eu/docs/
- Base: `https://api.openaire.eu/search/datasets`
- Auth: none for legacy search endpoints; free registered token for the Graph API and higher limits | Limits: Anonymous legacy endpoints are throttled (~60 req/hour per IP documented); registered free clients get 7,200 req/hour. Legacy /search/* endpoints are deprecated in favour of the newer Graph API — UNKNOWN retirement date, so pin to the Graph API for new work.
- Latency: weekly | Format: REST JSON and XML; bulk dumps on Zenodo
- Relevance: Funding-and-project linkage is the differentiator: you can see which grants and institutions are behind an emerging research area, which is a leading indicator for science-milestone markets.

**DataCite REST API** — DataCite `LIVE`

- Metadata for every DataCite-registered DOI — datasets, software, samples, preprints — with creators, affiliations, subjects, related identifiers, funding references and citation counts. Verified 2026-09-20 (example hit 10.5281/zenodo.22865609).
- Docs: https://support.datacite.org/docs/api
- Base: `https://api.datacite.org/dois`
- Auth: none for read | Limits: Documented at 3,000 req/5-minute window per IP. INTEGRATION GOTCHA VERIFIED: bracket query params must be percent-encoded (page%5Bsize%5D=1, not page[size]=1) or curl/most HTTP clients will mangle or glob the URL.
- Latency: realtime on DOI registration | Format: REST JSON (JSON:API spec)
- Relevance: The cross-repository join key. Because DataCite DOIs are global, this is how you deduplicate the same dataset appearing in Zenodo, Figshare, OpenAIRE and a national repository — a real problem when you aggregate all of them into one panel.

**Hugging Face Datasets & Models API** — Hugging Face `LIVE`

- Programmatic listing and metadata for the entire public Hub — dataset id, author, lastModified, likes, trendingScore, private/gated flags, sha, cardData (licence, pretty_name, config/split structure). Verified 2026-09-20. Companion endpoints cover models, Spaces, and the datasets-server for row-level preview and Parquet conversion of most public datasets.
- Docs: https://huggingface.co/docs/hub/api
- Base: `https://huggingface.co/api/datasets`
- Auth: none for public listing; free user token raises limits and unlocks gated repos | Limits: Anonymous is rate-limited (unpublished exact figure — UNKNOWN); a free token gives a substantially higher bucket. Pagination is CURSOR-based via the RFC-5988 Link header (rel="next"), not offset — there is no total count in the response and no X-Total-Count header despite it being listed in access-control-expose-headers.
- Latency: realtime (trendingScore updates continuously) | Format: REST JSON + Parquet bulk via datasets-server
- Relevance: Indirect but real: the datasets-server auto-converts most public datasets to Parquet, meaning HF is often the fastest path to a queryable copy of a corpus that is otherwise a zip file on a university FTP server.

**Kaggle Datasets API** — Kaggle (Google) `LIVE`

- Listing and metadata for Kaggle's public dataset corpus — title, subtitle, creator, URL, size, file types, licence, vote count, usability rating, last-updated. Verified 2026-09-20: the LIST endpoint responds 200 with ~100KB of JSON WITHOUT any authentication, which contradicts the common assumption that all Kaggle API access requires a token.
- Docs: https://www.kaggle.com/docs/api
- Base: `https://www.kaggle.com/api/v1/datasets/list`
- Auth: none for listing (verified); free API token (kaggle.json) required for downloads | Limits: Listing is paginated at 20 per page by default. Downloads require a token and are subject to per-account throttling; Kaggle does not publish exact numbers — UNKNOWN. ToS restricts redistribution of many hosted datasets, so treat Kaggle as a discovery and prototyping surface, not a redistribution source.
- Latency: daily | Format: REST JSON (list) + authenticated zip/CSV download
- Relevance: Best-in-class for finding a pre-cleaned historical corpus to backtest a pricing model, especially sports, finance and weather. Licence-check every dataset before it enters a commercial pipeline.

**OpenSanctions dataset catalog** — OpenSanctions (Friedrich Lindenberg) `LIVE`

- Verified 2026-09-20: a 1,715,129-byte JSON catalog enumerating every constituent sanctions, PEP, watchlist and corporate-registry dataset with name, title, licence, summary, url, updated_at, last_export, entity_count, thing_count, version and category. Each entry links to bulk FollowTheMoney JSON/CSV exports.
- Docs: https://www.opensanctions.org/docs/api/
- Base: `https://api.opensanctions.org/catalog`
- Auth: none for the catalog and bulk data; API key required for the hosted matching/screening API | Limits: Catalog and bulk downloads are free under CC-BY-NC 4.0 — NON-COMMERCIAL. Commercial use of the data requires a paid licence. The hosted screening API is paid. Self-hosting the open-source yente index over the free bulk data is the free commercial-safe path only if licensing permits your use.
- Latency: daily (last_export timestamps update daily; observed version 20260917085118) | Format: REST JSON catalog + bulk FollowTheMoney JSON/CSV
- Relevance: Directly prices sanctions-designation, export-control and PEP-exposure contracts, and is a hard dependency for any geopolitical panel. The catalog endpoint is what makes it a catalog rather than just a feed: it tells you which of dozens of national lists are covered and how fresh each one is.

**RapidAPI Hub** — RapidAPI (Nokia)

- The largest commercial API marketplace — reported at 40,000+ APIs serving 4M+ developers as of 2026, with unified auth (one X-RapidAPI-Key across all providers), consistent billing and per-endpoint usage metering.
- Docs: https://docs.rapidapi.com/docs/faqs
- Base: `https://rapidapi.com/hub`
- Auth: free API key (registration required); per-API subscription on top | Limits: Per-API, not per-account. Documented default free plans are capped at 1,000 requests/hour and 500,000 requests/month, but each provider sets its own BASIC tier and many are far stricter (100-500/month is common). CRITICAL: there is NO free bulk catalog API — you cannot programmatically enumerate the 40,000 APIs; the hub is browse-only and third parties resort to scraping it.
- Latency: varies entirely by underlying API | Format: REST JSON per API; catalog itself is scrape-only
- Relevance: Fills verticals where no free direct source exists — niche sports statistics, some financial data, specialised geocoding. Treat as a fallback with real cost risk, not as a foundation: unified auth is convenient but you inherit 40,000 different rate limits and TOS.

#### NICHE

**Figshare API v2** — Figshare (Digital Science) `LIVE`

- Public articles, datasets, figures, media and collections with DOIs, handles, published dates, thumbnails and direct file endpoints. Verified live 2026-09-20.
- Docs: https://docs.figshare.com/
- Base: `https://api.figshare.com/v2/articles`
- Auth: none for public reads; free OAuth token for private/institutional content | Limits: UNKNOWN — Figshare does not publish an anonymous rate limit. page_size max 1000. Throttle defensively.
- Latency: realtime on publication | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: Complements Zenodo for institutional and publisher-deposited supplementary data. Secondary source; use it to fill gaps rather than as a primary.

**APIs.io federated discovery (APIs.json)** — API Evangelist (Kin Lane) `LIVE`

- An API search engine built on the APIs.json specification — a machine-readable 'sitemap.xml for APIs'. Verified 2026-09-20: https://apis.io/apis.json returns a 43,931-byte APIs.json document (aid, name, description, url, created, modified, specificationVersion, tags, apis[19], common[67], maintainers, type, deliveryModel, accessModel, network). Sub-APIs expose the index itself: APIs API, Areas API (authentication/topic taxonomy), Artifact Types API (OpenAPI/AsyncAPI/Arazzo collections), Industries API, Insights API (demand signals from ~5,800 Fortune-1000 and API-provider companies).
- Docs: https://apisjson.org/
- Base: `https://apis.io/apis.json`
- Auth: none for the root index; UNKNOWN for some sub-APIs | Limits: UNKNOWN — no published quota. /index.json returns 404; only /apis.json is the valid entry point.
- Latency: weekly | Format: REST JSON (APIs.json specification)
- Relevance: Structurally the most interesting long-term bet: APIs.json is a federation format, so an aggregator that speaks it can ingest any provider that publishes one, without a bespoke connector. Small catalog today, but the right shape for a self-expanding panel.

**iamtekson/awesome-geospatial-data-sources** — Tek Kshetri `LIVE`

- Narrowly scoped to open-source geospatial DATA DOWNLOAD sites (as opposed to tooling) — national elevation, land cover, administrative boundaries, imagery archives. Verified 2026-09-20: pushed 2026-08-19, NOT archived (74 stars — small but current and precisely on-topic).
- Docs: https://github.com/iamtekson/awesome-geospatial-data-sources
- Base: `https://github.com/iamtekson/awesome-geospatial-data-sources`
- Auth: none | Limits: Unlimited (GitHub raw).
- Latency: monthly | Format: scrape-only (Markdown)
- Relevance: Complements Awesome-Geospatial by pointing at the actual data portals rather than the libraries. Useful for boundary and basemap layers a mapping panel needs.

**APILayer Marketplace** — APILayer (idealo / Nokia)

- A curated marketplace of 100+ first-party production APIs across geolocation, currency/FX, weather, dev tools, marketing, finance, security and AI/ML, reported at 445,000+ developers and 30M+ monthly calls. Notably, APILayer sponsors and is the homepage link target of public-apis/public-apis.
- Docs: https://marketplace.apilayer.com/docs/article/rate-limits
- Base: `https://api.apilayer.com`
- Auth: free API key (registration required) | Limits: Free tier exists on every API but is small and varies per product. Verified example: Currencylayer free plan is 100 calls/month AND locks the base currency to USD. Others are in the 100-1,000 calls/month range. These are prototype-only quotas — NOT viable for a live panel without paying.
- Latency: varies by API; FX and weather products are minutely-to-hourly | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: Convenient single-key access to FX and geolocation, but the free quotas are too thin for continuous market pricing. Prefer free direct sources (ECB/Frankfurter for FX, national met services for weather) and keep APILayer as a gap-filler.

**data.world** — data.world, Inc.

- Hosted dataset catalog and collaboration platform with SPARQL and SQL query over uploaded datasets, plus a community open-data corpus.
- Docs: https://apidocs.data.world/
- Base: `https://api.data.world/v0`
- Auth: free API token (registration required) — VERIFIED: unauthenticated calls to /v0/ and /v0/search/datasets both return HTTP 404 with a JSON error body, so there is no anonymous discovery surface at all | Limits: UNKNOWN for the free tier — data.world no longer publishes anonymous or free-tier request quotas, and the product has shifted toward enterprise data-catalog sales. Free community accounts still exist but the open-data emphasis has declined markedly since ~2023.
- Latency: varies by dataset; mostly static uploads | Format: REST JSON + SPARQL + SQL
- Relevance: Low priority in 2026. The registration wall plus the enterprise pivot means the cost-to-value is poor next to Kaggle, HuggingFace and Socrata for the same discovery job.

**publicapis.io** — publicapis.io `LIVE`

- A Next.js-rendered directory advertising 1,000+ free public APIs with category browsing (including a dedicated open-data collection) and per-API landing pages. Verified 2026-09-20: site responds 200 with 230,977 bytes of server-rendered HTML.
- Docs: https://publicapis.io/
- Base: `https://publicapis.io/`
- Auth: none | Limits: No documented public API. UNKNOWN whether a stable JSON endpoint exists — content is embedded in Next.js server-rendered payloads, which are internal implementation details and can break without notice.
- Latency: UNKNOWN (no exposed last-updated signal) | Format: scrape-only
- Relevance: Marginal. Overlaps almost entirely with public-apis and public-api-lists, both of which are better sourced and one of which has a real JSON API. Include only for cross-validation of link liveness.

**publicapi.dev** — publicapi.dev `LIVE`

- Another searchable free-API directory with filtering and bookmarking. Verified 2026-09-20: responds 200 with 135,106 bytes.
- Docs: https://publicapi.dev/
- Base: `https://publicapi.dev/`
- Auth: none | Limits: No documented programmatic API. UNKNOWN.
- Latency: UNKNOWN | Format: scrape-only
- Relevance: Marginal; same overlap problem as publicapis.io.

**APIList.fun** — apilist.fun `LIVE`

- A long-running static directory advertising 800+ free APIs for developers. Verified 2026-09-20: responds 200 with 91,613 bytes of static HTML.
- Docs: https://apilist.fun/
- Base: `https://apilist.fun/`
- Auth: none | Limits: No API. Static HTML only.
- Latency: UNKNOWN — static site with no visible update signal; likely stale relative to the GitHub-backed lists | Format: scrape-only
