#### Repos

- `public-apis/public-apis` — The canonical free-API directory. 481,894 stars, MIT, pushed 2026-09-20, NOT archived. 1,902 entries / 52 categories in a 268,910-byte README.md. · Largest single enumeration of free endpoints in existence and MIT-licensed, so you can mirror and redistribute it. BUT: the repo tree contains only README.md, scripts/ and .github/ — there is NO JSON build artifact. You must write the Markdown table parser yourself, or use public-api-lists which has already done it.
- `public-api-lists/public-api-lists` — Active community fork lineage of the free-API list that actually ships a JSON API. 15,858 stars, pushed 2026-09-14. 837 APIs / 48 categories. · Steal .github/scripts/build_api.py wholesale — it is a clean, dependency-free Markdown-table-to-JSON parser (TABLE_ENTRY_RE + SECTION_RE) that emits all.json, categories.json, stats.json, random.json and per-category files, wired to GitHub Pages via deploy-pages.yml. Point it at public-apis' README.md and you get a 1,902-entry JSON index for free. Also has broken-link-collectorr.py and check_all_links.py for automated feed health monitoring, and validate_pr.py for schema enforcement.
- `lockfale/OSINT-Framework` — The OSINT Framework behind osintframework.com. 12,171 stars, pushed 2026-09-11. · public/arf.json is the single best machine-readable investigative taxonomy available free: 1,112,073 bytes, 1,168 leaf entries, 30 top-level categories as a nested {name, type, url, children} tree. Drop it straight into a panel's category navigation — no parsing, no scraping. Its Compliance & Risk Intelligence, Business Records, Transportation, Blockchain & Cryptocurrency and Disinformation & Media Verification branches are the conflict/geopolitics/corporate-event discovery paths.
- `awesomedata/awesome-public-datasets` — Topic-centric index of high-quality open datasets. 79,062 stars, pushed 2026-09-18, NOT archived. · ~1,994 links organised by scientific and economic domain. INTEGRATION TRAP: the list is README.rst (reStructuredText, 245,270 bytes) — README.md returns HTTP 404. Any scraper written against the usual README.md path silently gets nothing. Parse RST, not Markdown.
- `jivoi/awesome-osint` — Most-starred OSINT list. 29,653 stars, pushed 2026-09-09, NOT archived. 150,537-byte README, ~1,453 links. · Best human-curated coverage of flight/vessel/rail tracking, conflict monitoring, dark web and threat intelligence — the feeds behind geopolitical and shipping-disruption pricing. README-only, so pair it with OSINT-Framework's arf.json for the structured version of overlapping content.
- `bytewax/awesome-public-real-time-datasets` — The only curated list scoped specifically to real-time/streaming public datasets. 2,924 stars, pushed 2026-07-10. · Every other catalog in this domain indexes mostly static or daily data. This one indexes WebSocket and push feeds — the sub-minute tier a live pricing panel actually needs. Small and the slowest-updating of the CORE lists, but uniquely on-target.
- `Astrosp/Awesome-OSINT-List` — Modern OSINT collection covering information gathering, reverse search, red team, trust & safety and AI tooling. 4,445 stars, pushed 2026-09-16. · Fresher than jivoi/awesome-osint and much better on 2025-2026 AI-era tools. Diff it against jivoi to find what appeared in the last two years.
- `sindresorhus/awesome` — Root meta-index of the awesome-list ecosystem. 508,250 stars, pushed 2026-09-02. ~676 indexed lists. · The recursive discovery step: crawl these 676 lists to reach the domain-specific catalog for any vertical not yet covered. NOTE the exact path — readme.md lowercase on branch main; README.md and branch master both 404. PRs are currently paused per the repo description, so it churns slower than its star count implies.
- `marcelscruz/public-apis` — Independently curated public-API directory powering publicapis.dev. 9,485 stars, pushed 2026-09-20 (same day verified), branch main. · An independent second opinion on the same universe as public-apis. Intersecting the two lists and health-checking the overlap yields the highest-confidence integration set. Its maintainer prunes dead links more aggressively than the 481k-star list can.
- `sacridini/Awesome-Geospatial` — Long-running geospatial tools and resources index. 5,293 stars, pushed 2026-09-19, NOT archived. · Path to STAC catalogs and free Sentinel/Landsat Earth-observation archives — how you independently verify physical claims about mines, ports, crops, fires and floods rather than trusting a press release.
- `iamtekson/awesome-geospatial-data-sources` — Small (74 stars) but current list of open geospatial DATA download sites, pushed 2026-08-19. · Complements Awesome-Geospatial by indexing the data portals rather than the libraries. Precisely scoped; low noise.
- `burningtree/awesome-json` — Curated list of JSON libraries, tools, specifications and resources. 1,568 stars, pushed 2026-06-19, NOT archived. · The practical replacement path for the ARCHIVED jdorfman/awesome-json-datasets. Not a dataset list itself, but it indexes the JSON schema, streaming-parse and query tooling (JSONPath, JMESPath, JSON Schema, ndjson) you need when normalising hundreds of heterogeneous feeds into one store.
- `marcelscruz/dev-resources` — Broader developer-resource directory from the same maintainer as publicapis.dev. 1,337 stars, pushed 2026-09-20. · Wider than APIs alone — includes datasets, tools and services. Worth a single crawl for coverage gaps the API-only lists miss.
- `soxoj/awesome-osint-mcp-servers` — Curated list of OSINT MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers. 493 stars, pushed 2026-09-19 — very actively maintained. · Genuinely 2026-native and directly relevant to the stated goal of running an AI model over aggregated data: these are OSINT sources already wrapped as MCP servers, so an LLM can query them as tools with no connector work at all. Fastest path from 'we have feeds' to 'the model can use the feeds'.
- `api-evangelist/specifications` — Meta-index of the specification languages used to describe APIs, events, schemas and service interfaces. Pushed 2026-09-20 (actively maintained despite only 1 star). · Low social proof but high substance and updated the day of verification. Useful for deciding which description format to normalise on (OpenAPI vs AsyncAPI vs APIs.json vs Arazzo) when you ingest catalogs that each speak a different one.
- `open-free-llm-api/awesome-freellm-apis` — 134+ free LLM APIs and AI API keys from 40+ providers (Gemini, NVIDIA NIM, Groq, OpenRouter). 3,156 stars, pushed 2026-09-20. · Relevant to the synthesis half of the panel rather than the ingestion half: if the design is to run models over aggregated feeds, this indexes the free inference capacity to do it. Updated same-day as verification.

---

### OSINT and real-time world monitoring

#### CORE

**GDELT 2.0 Raw 15-Minute File Feed (Events / Mentions / GKG)** — The GDELT Project (Kalev Leetaru) `LIVE`

- Every news-derived geopolitical event on Earth, coded to CAMEO actor/action taxonomy, with lat/lon, Goldstein scale, tone, and source URL. Three files every 15 minutes: export.CSV (events), mentions.CSV (every re-mention of an event, enabling attention-decay curves), gkg.csv (Global Knowledge Graph: themes, persons, orgs, locations, emotional dimensions). Monitors ~65 languages translated in realtime. Verified live: masterfilelist.txt returns entries through 2026-09-21T00:00:00Z, and the archive runs back to 2015-02-18.
- Docs: https://www.gdeltproject.org/data.html#rawdatafiles
- Base: `http://data.gdeltproject.org/gdeltv2/lastupdate.txt (rolling 15-min pointer) and http://data.gdeltproject.org/gdeltv2/masterfilelist.txt (full archive index, MD5 + size + URL per line)`
- Auth: none | Limits: No key, no documented request cap. This is the path GDELT explicitly steers high-volume users toward. Per-cycle volume observed 2026-09-21: export 63,893 bytes, mentions 47,733 bytes, gkg 1,860,250 bytes (zipped). ~96 cycles/day, ~180MB/day gzipped mostly from GKG.
- Latency: minutely (15-minute cycles, typically published within ~15 min of the cycle timestamp) | Format: CSV bulk (zipped, tab-delimited, no header row — column order is defined in the GDELT 2.0 codebook)
- Relevance: The single best backbone for any event-occurrence contract: 'will there be a coup in X by date', 'will country A strike country B', 'will protests exceed N'. CAMEO codes 18x (assault), 19x (fight), 20x (mass violence), 14x (protest) map almost directly onto conflict-market resolution criteria. The Mentions file gives an attention-volume signal that front-runs resolution-source reporting.

**GDELT on Google BigQuery (gdelt-bq)** — The GDELT Project / Google Cloud public datasets

- The same Events, Mentions and GKG data as SQL tables, updated every 15 minutes, plus large historical backfills. Lets you do 'count events of CAMEO type 193 in country X per week since 2015' as one query instead of parsing 400,000 CSV files. Tables: gdelt-bq.gdeltv2.events, gdelt-bq.gdeltv2.eventmentions, gdelt-bq.gdeltv2.gkg, gdelt-bq.gdeltv2.gkg_partitioned, plus gdelt-bq.full.events for the 1979-onward 1.0 history.
- Docs: https://blog.gdeltproject.org/google-bigquery-gkg-2-0-sample-queries/
- Base: `bq://gdelt-bq.gdeltv2 (BigQuery console or the BigQuery REST/Storage API)`
- Auth: free API key | Limits: Google Cloud free tier: 1 TiB of query processing per month, free forever, plus 10 GiB storage. The GDELT tables themselves cost nothing to host (public dataset) — you only pay for bytes scanned beyond 1 TiB/month. GKG is very wide, so ALWAYS select specific columns and use the _PARTITIONTIME / partitioned table or a single month of GKG can burn the whole monthly allowance.
- Latency: minutely (15-minute load cadence, same as raw files) | Format: REST JSON (BigQuery API) / SQL
- Relevance: This is where you compute base rates. Every prediction market needs a prior: 'how often has an event of this type happened in this country in the last 10 years'. BigQuery over gdelt-bq.full.events answers that in one query. Also the only practical way to build a training corpus for an event-forecasting model.

**GDELT DOC 2.0 API** — The GDELT Project `LIVE`

- Keyword/boolean search over the last ~3 months of global online news in 65 languages, with output modes ArtList (article list), TimelineVol (coverage volume over time), TimelineVolRaw, TimelineTone, TimelineLang, TimelineSourceCountry, ToneChart, WordCloud. Supports operators: domain:, domainis:, sourcelang:, sourcecountry:, theme:, tone:, toneabs:, near:, repeat:.
- Docs: https://blog.gdeltproject.org/gdelt-doc-2-0-api-debuts/
- Base: `https://api.gdeltproject.org/api/v2/doc/doc?query=<q>&mode=ArtList&maxrecords=250&format=json&timespan=24h`
- Auth: none | Limits: HARD LIMIT: 1 request per 5 seconds, enforced server-side. VERIFIED BEHAVIOUR 2026-09-20: the first call returned HTTP 200 with JSON; after two calls inside a few seconds the endpoint returned HTTP 429 with a PLAIN-TEXT (not JSON) body and stayed 429 for over 60 seconds. The cooldown is longer than the stated 5s once you trip it. maxrecords caps at 250. timespan max is roughly 3 months of rolling coverage.
- Latency: sub-minute (indexes articles within ~15 min of publication) | Format: REST JSON (but error responses are plain text — parse defensively)
- Relevance: Best for ad-hoc research inside a market detail panel: 'show me every article about this contract's subject in the last 24h, and the coverage-volume curve'. The TimelineVol mode is a direct market-attention proxy — coverage spikes usually precede price moves on news-driven contracts.

**USGS Earthquake Hazards GeoJSON Feeds** — United States Geological Survey `LIVE`

- Every detected earthquake worldwide with magnitude, depth, lat/lon, USGS event ID, felt reports, alert level (PAGER), tsunami flag. Pre-cut feeds by time window and magnitude: all_hour, all_day, all_week, all_month, plus significant_*, 4.5_*, 2.5_*, 1.0_*. Verified live 2026-09-20: all_hour 7,439 bytes, all_day 156,721 bytes. A full FDSNWS query API also exists for arbitrary historical windows.
- Docs: https://earthquake.usgs.gov/earthquakes/feed/v1.0/geojson.php
- Base: `https://earthquake.usgs.gov/earthquakes/feed/v1.0/summary/all_hour.geojson and https://earthquake.usgs.gov/fdsnws/event/1/query?format=geojson&starttime=...&minmagnitude=...`
- Auth: none | Limits: No key. No published hard cap; USGS asks you not to poll the summary feeds more than once per minute (they regenerate每 1-5 min depending on feed). The FDSNWS query endpoint caps at 20,000 events per request.
- Latency: minutely (feeds regenerate every 1-5 minutes; events appear within ~2-20 min of origin time depending on review status) | Format: REST JSON (GeoJSON)
- Relevance: Earthquake magnitude/occurrence contracts resolve directly off USGS — it is almost always the named resolution source. Because it IS the resolution source, latency between the feed updating and the market repricing is a genuine, mechanical edge window. Also the input to cascading contracts (tsunami, nuclear plant status, aid appeals).

**EMSC Seismic Portal (FDSN + real-time WebSocket)** — European-Mediterranean Seismological Centre `LIVE`

- Independent global earthquake catalog, frequently faster than USGS for European, Mediterranean and Middle-Eastern events, plus crowd-sourced 'felt' reports. Offers a genuine push WebSocket so you do not have to poll. Verified live 2026-09-20 (HTTP 200).
- Docs: https://www.seismicportal.eu/realtime.html
- Base: `https://www.seismicportal.eu/fdsnws/event/1/query?limit=100&format=json and wss://www.seismicportal.eu/standing_order/websocket`
- Auth: none | Limits: No key. FDSN query limit parameter is honored; no documented request cap. WebSocket is unauthenticated and open.
- Latency: realtime/websocket | Format: WebSocket + REST JSON
- Relevance: Second independent source for seismic contracts. Divergence between EMSC and USGS magnitude estimates in the first minutes after an event is itself tradeable information when a contract has a magnitude threshold — the two agencies routinely differ by 0.2-0.4 Mw before final review.

**GDACS (Global Disaster Alert and Coordination System)** — European Commission JRC + UN OCHA `LIVE`

- Automated multi-hazard alerts with a Green/Orange/Red severity score and modeled population exposure: earthquakes, tropical cyclones, floods, volcanoes, droughts, wildfires. Each alert carries estimated affected population and a unique eventid. Verified live 2026-09-20: RSS returned 1,261,501 bytes.
- Docs: https://www.gdacs.org/About/datasharing.aspx
- Base: `https://www.gdacs.org/xml/rss.xml (current alerts) and https://www.gdacs.org/gdacsapi/api/events/geteventlist/SEARCH for the JSON API`
- Auth: none | Limits: No key, no documented cap. RSS regenerates continuously. The JSON API at /gdacsapi/ is undocumented but public.
- Latency: sub-minute to hourly depending on hazard type (seismic near-immediate, flood/drought daily) | Format: RSS + REST JSON
- Relevance: GDACS Red/Orange alerts are the standard trigger for humanitarian-response, aid-appeal and disaster-declaration contracts. The modeled population-exposure number is often the closest available real-time proxy for 'will casualties exceed N' before official counts exist.

**NASA EONET v3 (Earth Observatory Natural Event Tracker)** — NASA Earth Science Data Systems `LIVE`

- Curated, de-duplicated natural event objects with stable IDs and full geometry time-series: wildfires, storms, volcanoes, sea/lake ice, dust/haze, landslides, icebergs, drought. Unlike raw satellite hotspot feeds, EONET clusters detections into named ongoing events. Verified live 2026-09-20 (events and categories endpoints both HTTP 200).
- Docs: https://eonet.gsfc.nasa.gov/docs/v3
- Base: `https://eonet.gsfc.nasa.gov/api/v3/events?status=open&limit=100 and /api/v3/categories`
- Auth: none | Limits: No key, no published rate limit. Supports days, source, category, bbox, status filters.
- Latency: hourly to daily depending on source | Format: REST JSON (GeoJSON available via /geojson)
- Relevance: The stable event ID with an evolving geometry time-series is exactly the shape you need for 'will wildfire X exceed N acres' or 'will hurricane Y make landfall in Z' — you can track one contract subject across days without re-doing entity resolution.

**NASA FIRMS (Fire Information for Resource Management System)** — NASA / University of Maryland `LIVE`

- Near-real-time active fire and thermal anomaly detections from VIIRS (375m, S-NPP + NOAA-20 + NOAA-21) and MODIS (1km), with lat/lon, brightness temperature, fire radiative power, confidence and acquisition timestamp. Global coverage, typically within 3 hours of satellite overpass; US/Canada within 1 minute via the ultra-real-time feed. URL pattern verified 2026-09-20 (endpoint rejected a fake key with 'Invalid MAP_KEY', confirming the path is correct).
- Docs: https://firms.modaps.eosdis.nasa.gov/api/area/
- Base: `https://firms.modaps.eosdis.nasa.gov/api/area/csv/<MAP_KEY>/VIIRS_SNPP_NRT/<west,south,east,north>/<days>`
- Auth: free API key | Limits: Free MAP_KEY on email signup. Documented transaction limit: 5,000 transactions per 10-minute interval per key; each API call counts as one transaction. Max 10 days back per request; area requests capped at a bounding box, and /api/country/ variants exist. Check remaining quota at /mapserver/mapkey_status/?MAP_KEY=<key>.
- Latency: sub-minute (US/Canada URT) to ~3 hours (global NRT) | Format: CSV bulk (also GeoJSON and KML variants)
- Relevance: Thermal detections are a dual-use signal. Obviously they price wildfire-extent contracts. Less obviously, FRP spikes at known industrial coordinates (refineries, oil terminals, ammunition depots, smelters) are a near-real-time strike/accident detector that beats news reporting by hours — directly relevant to energy-infrastructure and conflict contracts, and to mining/minerals production-disruption contracts.

**NOAA / National Weather Service API (api.weather.gov)** — NOAA National Weather Service `LIVE`

- All active US weather alerts, watches and warnings as GeoJSON with CAP severity/urgency/certainty, plus forecasts, observations, radar station metadata and hurricane products. Verified live 2026-09-20: /alerts/active returned 2,064,179 bytes.
- Docs: https://www.weather.gov/documentation/services-web-api
- Base: `https://api.weather.gov/alerts/active (add ?area=CA or ?event=Tornado%20Warning to filter)`
- Auth: none | Limits: No key. NWS requires a User-Agent header identifying your app (they may throttle generic agents). No published numeric cap; they ask for reasonable use. GOTCHA VERIFIED: ?limit=1 alone returns HTTP 400 — limit must be combined with a valid filter or cursor.
- Latency: sub-minute | Format: REST JSON (GeoJSON / CAP)
- Relevance: US weather contracts (temperature thresholds, hurricane landfall, snowfall) very often name NWS as the resolution source, and NWS station observations are the literal settlement data. 'That station's historical error' in a weather research panel is computed against exactly this API's observation history.

**Open-Meteo** — Open-Meteo (Zurich, open source) `LIVE`

- Free multi-model numerical weather prediction: ECMWF IFS, GFS, ICON, MET Norway, JMA, GEM, plus ERA5 reanalysis back to 1940, historical forecast archive (what each model predicted at each past time — crucial for backtesting), marine, air quality, flood (GloFAS) and climate projection endpoints. Verified live 2026-09-20.
- Docs: https://open-meteo.com/en/docs
- Base: `https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast?latitude=52&longitude=13&hourly=temperature_2m&models=ecmwf_ifs025,gfs_seamless,icon_seamless`
- Auth: none | Limits: Genuinely free, no key, for non-commercial use: 10,000 calls/day, 5,000/hour, 600/minute. Commercial use requires a paid plan. The historical-forecast archive (previous_runs / archive-api.open-meteo.com) is included and is the piece that makes model-vs-outcome scoring possible.
- Latency: hourly (model runs at 00/06/12/18Z, data available within ~1-4h of run time) | Format: REST JSON (also FlatBuffers for bulk)
- Relevance: This is the single highest-value feed for a weather-market research panel and it directly answers the user's stated design: multi-model ensemble forecast, model spread across ECMWF/GFS/ICON, and — via the historical forecast archive — that station's historical error. You cannot compute a calibrated implied probability or an edge versus market price without the archive endpoint.

**OpenSky Network REST API** — OpenSky Network (association, Switzerland) `LIVE`

- Live ADS-B/Mode-S aircraft state vectors globally from a volunteer receiver network: ICAO24, callsign, position, altitude, velocity, vertical rate, squawk, on-ground flag. Plus flights-by-aircraft, flights-by-airport and track endpoints, and a large historical archive via Trino/Impala for contributors. Verified live 2026-09-20: anonymous /states/all with a bbox returned HTTP 200, 3,220 bytes.
- Docs: https://openskynetwork.github.io/opensky-api/rest.html
- Base: `https://opensky-network.org/api/states/all?lamin=&lomin=&lamax=&lomax= ; token endpoint https://auth.opensky-network.org/auth/realms/opensky-network/protocol/openid-connect/token`
- Auth: OAuth | Limits: MAJOR 2026 CHANGE: HTTP Basic auth with username/password was retired in March 2026. You must now create an API client to get client_id/client_secret and use the OAuth2 client-credentials flow; tokens expire in ~30 minutes. Credit-based daily quota: ~400 credits/day anonymous, ~4,000/day authenticated, ~8,000/day if you feed a receiver that was online >30% of the month. A bounded-bbox request costs fewer credits than a global one. Anonymous access is limited to 10-second time resolution; authenticated gets 5-second.
- Latency: realtime/websocket (5-10 second state vector resolution via polling; no true push) | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: Aircraft movement is the classic leading indicator: diplomatic-jet arrivals before announced talks, military transport surges before operations, airline route suspensions before an airspace-closure contract resolves. Also prices aviation-disruption and airspace-closure contracts directly.

**adsb.lol and adsb.fi (community ADS-B aggregators)** — adsb.lol / adsb.fi volunteer networks `LIVE`

- Open, unauthenticated ADS-B feeds including purpose-built military filters (/v2/mil returns only military-registered aircraft currently airborne), plus /v2/pia, /v2/ladd, lat/lon radius search, hex lookup, callsign lookup, and squawk search (e.g. 7700 emergency). Both verified live 2026-09-20: adsb.lol/v2/mil returned 41,161 bytes, adsb.fi returned 53,074 bytes.
- Docs: https://api.adsb.lol/docs
- Base: `https://api.adsb.lol/v2/mil and https://opendata.adsb.fi/api/v2/mil ; also /v2/lat/<lat>/lon/<lon>/dist/<nm>`
- Auth: none | Limits: No key at all. adsb.lol asks for ~1 request/second courtesy; adsb.fi similar. Both are ODbL/open-data licensed and explicitly permit reuse. IMPORTANT: this is the free replacement for ADS-B Exchange, which went commercial after its 2024 acquisition by Jetnet and now requires a paid RapidAPI subscription.
- Latency: realtime/websocket (aggregated every few seconds) | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: The /v2/mil endpoint is the cheapest military-activity tripwire available anywhere — zero auth, zero cost, global. Surges in tanker and ISR aircraft over a theater are a well-documented precursor to strike operations, which prices conflict-escalation contracts hours ahead of news.

**AISStream.io** — AISStream.io

- Global real-time AIS vessel traffic over a WebSocket: position reports, ship static data, voyage data (destination, ETA, draught), with bounding-box and MMSI subscription filters. Message types include PositionReport, ShipStaticData, StandardClassBPositionReport, AidsToNavigationReport.
- Docs: https://aisstream.io/documentation
- Base: `wss://stream.aisstream.io/v0/stream (send a JSON subscription message with APIKey, BoundingBoxes, optional FiltersShipMMSI and FilterMessageTypes)`
- Auth: free API key | Limits: Free key on signup, no credit card. WebSocket-only — there is no REST endpoint, so you cannot do point-in-time lookups; you must maintain a connection and persist state yourself. Free tier is for non-commercial use; coverage is terrestrial-receiver based, so mid-ocean coverage is sparse compared to satellite AIS.
- Latency: realtime/websocket | Format: WebSocket
- Relevance: Chokepoint transit counts (Hormuz, Suez, Bab el-Mandeb, Panama, Malacca, Bosphorus) are directly tradeable and are the input to shipping-rate, oil-price and supply-disruption contracts. Vessel 'going dark' (AIS transponder off) in a sanctioned-trade corridor is a sanctions-evasion signal. Port-call counts are a high-frequency proxy for export volumes ahead of official customs data — including for mineral and ore shipments.

**DeepStateMap.live API** — DeepState (Ukrainian OSINT collective) `LIVE`

- The actual Ukraine front-line as machine-readable GeoJSON — polygons of occupied territory, contested zones and liberated areas, updated near-daily with dated history. Verified live 2026-09-20: /api/history/last returned 627,479 bytes of a FeatureCollection with Polygon geometry, unauthenticated.
- Docs: https://deepstatemap.live/
- Base: `https://deepstatemap.live/api/history/last (also /api/history/<timestamp>/geojson for a specific date)`
- Auth: none | Limits: No key, no documented cap, but this is an undocumented internal API of a volunteer project — treat it as best-effort, cache aggressively, and set a polite User-Agent. Payload is large (~600KB) so do not poll faster than the data changes (roughly daily).
- Latency: daily | Format: REST JSON (GeoJSON)
- Relevance: Territorial-control contracts ('will Russia control city X by date', 'will the front move N km') resolve on exactly this kind of polygon. Because the history endpoint is date-addressable, you can compute the empirical distribution of front-line movement per week and turn it into a calibrated prior — which is the single hardest input to source for Ukraine territorial markets.

**ACLED (Armed Conflict Location & Event Data Project)** — ACLED `LIVE`

- The gold-standard hand-coded conflict event dataset: battles, explosions/remote violence, violence against civilians, protests, riots, strategic developments — each with date, precise lat/lon, actors, associated actors, fatalities, source list and a geo-precision code. Global coverage, weekly releases.
- Docs: https://acleddata.com/api-documentation/getting-started
- Base: `https://acleddata.com/api/acled/read (POST https://acleddata.com/oauth/token first for a Bearer token)`
- Auth: OAuth | Limits: MAJOR CHANGE — the old api.acleddata.com key+email scheme is dead (VERIFIED: returns HTTP 403/000 on 2026-09-20). You now register for a myACLED account and use OAuth2: access token valid 24 hours, refresh token valid 14 days. Access is free for academic, non-profit and personal research use; commercial use requires a paid license — a prediction-market product is commercial, so read the terms before you build on it. Default page size 5,000 rows, paginate with the page parameter.
- Latency: weekly (Monday releases; some regions get mid-week updates) | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: The fatality counts are the resolution basis for many conflict-intensity contracts, and the actor coding lets you condition on specific armed groups. The weekly cadence means ACLED is the settlement/base-rate source, NOT the real-time signal — pair it with GDELT for nowcasting and use ACLED to calibrate GDELT's false-positive rate.

**Wikimedia EventStreams (SSE)** — Wikimedia Foundation `LIVE`

- A genuine unauthenticated push firehose of every edit to every Wikimedia project in real time — recentchange, revision-create, page-create, page-delete, page-move, page-links-change streams. Each event carries wiki, title, user, bot flag, comment, byte delta and timestamps. Verified live 2026-09-20 (HTTP 200 on the SSE endpoint).
- Docs: https://wikitech.wikimedia.org/wiki/Event_Platform/EventStreams
- Base: `https://stream.wikimedia.org/v2/stream/recentchange (Server-Sent Events; supports Last-Event-ID for resume and a since= parameter for replay up to ~7 days)`
- Auth: none | Limits: No key, no cap, no registration. Wikimedia asks for a descriptive User-Agent. Connection is long-lived SSE; the replay window is roughly 7 days via since=.
- Latency: realtime/websocket (SSE, sub-second) | Format: WebSocket (Server-Sent Events) / JSON
- Relevance: Wikipedia edit velocity on a person's or event's page is one of the fastest, cheapest crowd-attention signals in existence and reliably spikes at the moment of death announcements, resignations, coups, acquisitions and disaster onset — often before wire services. A burst of non-bot edits to a head-of-state page is a strong nowcast for political-survival contracts. It is free, unlimited and push-based, which makes it unusually good value.

**Wikimedia Pageviews / Analytics REST API** — Wikimedia Foundation `LIVE`

- Hourly and daily pageview counts per article per project per access method, top-1000 articles per day, and per-country breakdowns. Verified live 2026-09-20: both the top-articles and per-article daily endpoints returned HTTP 200 with real data.
- Docs: https://wikimedia.org/api/rest_v1/#/Pageviews%20data
- Base: `https://wikimedia.org/api/rest_v1/metrics/pageviews/per-article/en.wikipedia/all-access/user/<Article>/daily/<YYYYMMDD>/<YYYYMMDD> and /pageviews/top/en.wikipedia/all-access/<YYYY>/<MM>/<DD>`
- Auth: none | Limits: No key. Documented courtesy limit ~200 requests/second (effectively unlimited for this use case); descriptive User-Agent requested. Data available from 2015-07 onward. Pageview data has a ~1-2 hour lag for hourly granularity, ~1 day for daily.
- Latency: hourly | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: The cleanest public attention proxy with a decade of clean history, which means you can actually backtest 'attention spike → market move' rather than guess at it. Useful for election contracts (candidate page traffic), celebrity/political-death contracts, and as the denominator that normalizes a news-volume spike against baseline interest.

**Polymarket Gamma API** — Polymarket `LIVE`

- All Polymarket markets and events with current prices, outcome definitions, resolution source text, volume, liquidity, and end dates. Verified live 2026-09-20 (HTTP 200, 6,284 bytes). Companion CLOB API gives order books and historical price series.
- Docs: https://docs.polymarket.com/
- Base: `https://gamma-api.polymarket.com/markets?limit=100&closed=false and https://clob.polymarket.com/prices-history?market=<id>&interval=1d`
- Auth: none | Limits: Read endpoints are unauthenticated with no published cap. NOTE: Polymarket sits behind Cloudflare and fingerprints TLS — some HTTP clients get challenged where curl does not. worldmonitor implements a three-tier fallback (browser-direct, native TLS, cloud proxy) specifically for this. Trading requires wallet auth; reading does not.
- Latency: realtime/websocket (WSS available on the CLOB API) | Format: REST JSON + WebSocket
- Relevance: This IS the market side of the panel — it supplies the live price and implied probability that your ensemble forecast is compared against, and the resolution-source field tells you which of the feeds above actually settles the contract. Essential, not optional.

**Kalshi Trade API v2** — Kalshi (CFTC-regulated US exchange) `LIVE`

- All Kalshi markets, events and series with bid/ask, last price, volume, open interest, plus explicit structured settlement rules. Verified live 2026-09-20 (HTTP 200, 2,972 bytes).
- Docs: https://trading-api.readme.io/reference/getting-started
- Base: `https://api.elections.kalshi.com/trade-api/v2/markets?limit=100&status=open`
- Auth: none | Limits: Public market-data endpoints need no auth. Documented limits by tier: Basic ~10 reads/second. Trading and portfolio endpoints require an RSA-signed API key. Historical candlesticks available via /series/{ticker}/markets/{ticker}/candlesticks.
- Latency: realtime/websocket | Format: REST JSON + WebSocket
- Relevance: Kalshi's settlement rules are unusually explicit and machine-readable — they name the exact NOAA station, the exact BLS release, the exact agency publication. That makes Kalshi the best exchange for auto-wiring a contract to its upstream data feed, and cross-exchange price divergence against Polymarket on equivalent contracts is itself a signal.

**World Monitor hosted API and MCP server** — World Monitor (Elie Habib) — the hosted service behind github.com/koala73/worldmonitor `LIVE`

- 231 pre-normalized endpoints spanning almost every domain in this report — verified by fetching the public OpenAPI 3.1.0 spec at api.worldmonitor.app/openapi.json (948KB, HTTP 200, no auth needed to READ THE SPEC). Endpoint families include conflict (list-acled-events, list-ucdp-events, list-iran-events), supply-chain (get-critical-minerals, get-mineral-production, get-chokepoint-status, list-pipelines), military (list-military-flights, list-military-bases, get-theater-posture, get-usni-fleet-report), intelligence (search-gdelt-documents, list-gps-interference, list-oref-alerts, list-telegram-feed, get-social-velocity, get-country-risk), maritime, wildfire, seismology, radiation, cyber, displacement, sanctions, trade, prediction markets, and forecast scoring (get-forecast-scorecard, trigger-simulation).
- Docs: https://api.worldmonitor.app/openapi.json
- Base: `https://api.worldmonitor.app/api/<domain>/v1/<operation>`
- Auth: free API key | Limits: NOT FREE IN PRACTICE. VERIFIED 2026-09-20: every data endpoint tested returned HTTP 403 {"code":"agent_request_blocked"} — they block agent User-Agents AND require an X-WorldMonitor-Key or X-Api-Key header. The MCP server at worldmonitor.app/mcp returns JSON-RPC error -32001 'Authentication required' pointing at a Pro upgrade funnel. The OpenAPI spec and the MCP tools/list ARE readable without auth, which is the real value: treat the spec as a free, complete blueprint of a working god's-eye data model and self-host the AGPL source instead.
- Latency: minutely (varies per endpoint; responses carry cached_at and an explicit stale boolean) | Format: REST JSON + MCP
- Relevance: The response schema is worth copying wholesale: every payload carries cached_at, a stale flag with a documented freshness contract, and an activationUnknown flag that distinguishes 'producer never ran' from 'marker unreadable'. That is exactly the missing-measurement-is-not-a-measured-zero discipline a forecasting panel needs, already designed.

#### USEFUL

**GDELT TV 2.0 API (Television Explorer)** — The GDELT Project / Internet Archive TV News Archive `LIVE`

- Closed-caption keyword search across US and international television news since 2009, by station, with airtime-normalized volume. Verified live 2026-09-20: a query for 'climate (station:CNN)' returned a monthly timeline series from 2009-06 through 2026-09-21.
- Docs: https://blog.gdeltproject.org/gdelt-2-0-television-api-debuts/
- Base: `https://api.gdeltproject.org/api/v2/tv/tv?query=<q>%20(station:CNN)&mode=timelinevol&format=json&datanorm=perc&last24=yes`
- Auth: none | Limits: No key. Same courtesy rate limit as DOC (1 req/5s) applies to the api.gdeltproject.org host. GOTCHA: the query MUST contain at least one station: operator or the API returns the plain-text error 'Your query must contain at least one station.' Stations include CNN, FOXNEWS, MSNBC, BBCNEWS and ~150 others.
- Latency: hourly (TV captions land with a delay of roughly 24-72h for some stations) | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: Television mention volume is a distinct attention channel from online news and is the better proxy for US mass-public salience — relevant for election, political-survival, and policy-announcement contracts. Also useful as an independent confirmation signal when online coverage might be bot-amplified.

**GDELT Context API and Summary API** — The GDELT Project `LIVE`

- Context API returns the actual sentence-level snippets around a matched phrase across global news (not just article links), which is what you want for extracting a quantitative claim. Summary API is a unified wrapper returning a multi-panel summary (web, TV, images) for a keyword. Both verified HTTP 200 on 2026-09-20; Summary returned a 76KB payload.
- Docs: https://blog.gdeltproject.org/announcing-the-gdelt-context-api/
- Base: `https://api.gdeltproject.org/api/v2/context/context?query=<q>&format=json&mode=artlist and https://api.gdeltproject.org/api/v2/summary/summary?d=web&t=summary&k=<q>&output=json`
- Auth: none | Limits: No key; shares the api.gdeltproject.org 1 req/5s limit. Context returns {"articles": []} rather than an error for a no-match query, so an empty array is genuinely 'no coverage', not a failure.
- Latency: sub-minute | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: Snippet-level extraction is what lets an LLM cite a specific sentence as evidence for a forecast rather than hallucinating from a headline. Directly supports the 'evidence behind the ensemble forecast' part of a research panel.

**GDELT Global Frontpage Graph (GFG)** — The GDELT Project `LIVE`

- Hourly snapshot of the link structure of the front pages of ~50,000 news sites worldwide — i.e. what every newsroom on Earth chose to put at the top, which is editorial prioritization rather than raw publication volume. Verified live: lastupdate.txt returned the 2026-09-20T23:00:00Z LINKS.TXT.gz file.
- Docs: https://blog.gdeltproject.org/announcing-the-global-frontpage-graph/
- Base: `http://data.gdeltproject.org/gdeltv3/gfg/alpha/lastupdate.txt`
- Auth: none | Limits: No key, no cap. Hourly files, gzipped.
- Latency: hourly | Format: CSV bulk (gzipped)
- Relevance: Front-page placement is a much stronger salience signal than article count — a story that 200 newsrooms lead with is categorically different from one 200 newsrooms merely covered. Good feature for 'will this become a major story' / resolution-attention contracts.

**UCDP (Uppsala Conflict Data Program) API** — Uppsala University, Department of Peace and Conflict Research `LIVE`

- Georeferenced Event Dataset (GED) of organized violence back to 1989 with conservative, best and high fatality estimates per event; plus UCDP/PRIO Armed Conflict Dataset, Battle-Related Deaths, Non-State Conflict and One-Sided Violence datasets, and monthly 'candidate' releases for recent months.
- Docs: https://ucdp.uu.se/apidocs/
- Base: `https://ucdpapi.pcr.uu.se/api/gedevents/<version>?pagesize=1000 — send header x-ucdp-access-token: <token>`
- Auth: free API key | Limits: CHANGED: the API is no longer fully open. VERIFIED 2026-09-20: an unauthenticated request returns the plain-text body 'API token required. Add header: x-ucdp-access-token: <your-token>' with HTTP 401. Tokens are free on request. Data is CC BY 4.0. Note the version string in the path (e.g. 25.1) changes with each annual release and old versions keep working — worldmonitor implements automatic version discovery with backoff for exactly this reason.
- Latency: monthly (candidate releases) to yearly (definitive GED) | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: UCDP's conservative/best/high fatality bands are the most defensible academic ground truth for 'will deaths exceed N' contracts, and the 25+ year history is the best available base-rate source for war onset and war termination probabilities. Too slow to trade on; essential to calibrate on.

**Bluesky Jetstream** — Bluesky / AT Protocol `LIVE`

- The full Bluesky firehose converted from CBOR/MST to plain JSON over WebSocket — every post, like, follow and repost as it happens, with collection-level filtering (wantedCollections=app.bsky.feed.post) and DID filtering. Four public instances operated by Bluesky. Verified: the HTTP probe to the /subscribe path returned HTTP 400, which is the expected response for a non-WebSocket request to a WebSocket endpoint.
- Docs: https://bsky.network/docs/jetstream/
- Base: `wss://jetstream1.us-east.bsky.network/subscribe?wantedCollections=app.bsky.feed.post (also jetstream2.us-east, jetstream1.us-west, jetstream2.us-west)`
- Auth: none | Limits: Completely unauthenticated public service, no key, no quota. Bluesky operates and monitors these instances for public developer use. Supports zstd compression and cursor-based replay. Full unfiltered firehose is roughly 200-1000 events/second — filter server-side with wantedCollections or you will drown.
- Latency: realtime/websocket | Format: WebSocket
- Relevance: The only major social firehose that is still free and unauthenticated after Twitter/X closed theirs and Reddit locked down its JSON endpoints. Social velocity around a contract subject is a genuine leading indicator for fast-moving news markets, and this is the only way left to get it at zero cost.

**CelesTrak GP / TLE Data** — CelesTrak (Dr. T.S. Kelso) `LIVE`

- Orbital elements (TLE/OMM) for every tracked object in Earth orbit, grouped by category: active satellites, Starlink, GPS/GNSS, military, weather, science, recent launches, plus SATCAT metadata and SOCRATES conjunction analyses. Verified live 2026-09-20: GROUP=active&FORMAT=json returned 6,982,914 bytes.
- Docs: https://celestrak.org/NORAD/documentation/gp-data-formats.php
- Base: `https://celestrak.org/NORAD/elements/gp.php?GROUP=active&FORMAT=json (also GROUP=last-30-days, GROUP=military, CATNR=<id>, INTDES=<id>)`
- Auth: none | Limits: No key. CelesTrak explicitly asks you not to re-query more often than the data updates (roughly every few hours) and to use the GROUP queries rather than hammering per-object CATNR calls. Bulk files are large — cache them.
- Latency: hourly to daily | Format: REST JSON (also TLE, XML, CSV)
- Relevance: Space-launch and satellite-deployment contracts resolve on catalog additions — a new INTDES appearing in last-30-days is the mechanical confirmation that a launch succeeded and deployed. Also lets you compute when a specific imaging satellite will pass over a contested coordinate, which is how you time an imagery request for visual confirmation of a ground event.

**NASA GIBS (Global Imagery Browse Services) / Worldview** — NASA EOSDIS `LIVE`

- ~1,000 pre-rendered global satellite imagery layers as standard WMTS/WMS tiles, most available within 3 hours of observation: MODIS and VIIRS true-color and corrected-reflectance, thermal anomalies, aerosol, NO2, night-lights (VIIRS DNB), sea ice, snow cover. Verified live 2026-09-20: the WMTS capabilities document returned 5,264,409 bytes.
- Docs: https://nasa-gibs.github.io/gibs-api-docs/
- Base: `https://gibs.earthdata.nasa.gov/wmts/epsg4326/best/1.0.0/WMTSCapabilities.xml and tile pattern /wmts/epsg4326/best/<layer>/default/<time>/<tilematrixset>/<z>/<y>/<x>.png`
- Auth: none | Limits: Completely free, no key, no registration, no documented rate cap. This is the easiest satellite-imagery basemap to put behind a map panel. Resolution is coarse (250m-1km for most layers) — it is for situational context, not for counting vehicles.
- Latency: hourly (most NRT layers within 3h of overpass) | Format: WMTS / WMS tiles (PNG/JPEG)
- Relevance: Gives a research panel a live satellite backdrop for free. VIIRS night-lights specifically is a usable proxy for power-grid failure and for conflict-driven depopulation — a measurable, resolvable quantity for infrastructure-damage contracts.

**Copernicus Data Space Ecosystem (Sentinel-1/2/3/5P)** — European Space Agency / European Commission `LIVE`

- Full free access to the entire Sentinel archive: Sentinel-2 optical (10m), Sentinel-1 SAR (sees through cloud and at night — the only free source that can image a conflict zone in bad weather), Sentinel-3 ocean/land, Sentinel-5P atmospheric (NO2, SO2, CH4, CO). Access via OData catalogue, STAC, OpenSearch, openEO, and a free-tier Sentinel Hub Process API. Verified live 2026-09-20: the OData Products endpoint returned HTTP 200.
- Docs: https://documentation.dataspace.copernicus.eu/APIs.html
- Base: `https://catalogue.dataspace.copernicus.eu/odata/v1/Products and https://sh.dataspace.copernicus.eu/api/v1/process`
- Auth: free API key | Limits: Free account required. Quotas are enforced monthly/hourly on downloaded volume to guarantee fair sharing. The bundled Sentinel Hub free tier gives 30,000 requests and 30,000 processing units per month for the Copernicus-hosted instance (the commercial sentinel-hub.com trial is a different, much smaller 30-day thing — do not confuse them). Catalogue browsing via OData/STAC is effectively unmetered.
- Latency: daily (Sentinel-2 revisit 5 days at equator, 2-3 days mid-latitude; Sentinel-1 6-12 days) | Format: REST JSON (OData/STAC) + GeoTIFF/JP2 rasters
- Relevance: Sentinel-1 SAR is the serious tool here: cloud-independent, night-capable change detection over ports, airfields, mines and front lines. For mining/minerals contracts you can measure tailings-pond and stockpile extent over time; for conflict you can confirm runway damage or bridge destruction independently of any reporting. This is the closest a free tier gets to genuine overhead-imagery intelligence.

**Element 84 Earth Search (STAC)** — Element 84 / AWS Open Data `LIVE`

- A fast, free STAC API over AWS-hosted public Earth-observation collections: Sentinel-2 L2A COGs, Sentinel-1 GRD, Landsat Collection 2, NAIP, COP-DEM. Because assets are Cloud-Optimized GeoTIFFs on S3, you can byte-range read a single small window rather than downloading a whole scene. Verified live 2026-09-20: /v1/collections returned 82,397 bytes.
- Docs: https://earth-search.aws.element84.com/v1
- Base: `https://earth-search.aws.element84.com/v1/search (POST STAC search with bbox, datetime, collections, query)`
- Auth: none | Limits: No key for the STAC catalogue. The underlying S3 buckets are AWS Open Data (requester-pays is NOT enabled for most of these, so reads are free); you pay only egress if you pull them out of AWS.
- Latency: daily | Format: REST JSON (STAC) + COG rasters
- Relevance: The practical way to get a specific 5km window of Sentinel-2 imagery over a mine, port or airbase in under a second without an ESA account or a download pipeline. Makes 'show me this contract's location from orbit, last cloud-free pass' a real panel feature rather than an aspiration.

**CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) Catalog** — US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency `LIVE`

- The authoritative list of vulnerabilities confirmed to be exploited in the wild, with CVE ID, vendor, product, date added, required remediation date and ransomware-campaign-use flag. Verified live 2026-09-20: 1,735,385 bytes of JSON.
- Docs: https://www.cisa.gov/known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog
- Base: `https://www.cisa.gov/sites/default/files/feeds/known_exploited_vulnerabilities.json`
- Auth: none | Limits: Static JSON file, no key, no cap. Updated on an irregular but roughly weekly cadence when new exploitation is confirmed. Public domain.
- Latency: weekly | Format: REST JSON (static file)
- Relevance: KEV addition is a discrete, dated, officially-published event — exactly the shape of a resolvable contract ('will CVE-X be added to KEV by date', 'will a KEV entry name vendor Y'). The ransomware flag is a leading indicator for breach-disclosure and cyber-incident contracts.

**RIPE Atlas API** — RIPE NCC `LIVE`

- Results from a global network of ~12,000 hardware probes doing continuous ping, traceroute, DNS, SSL and HTTP measurements, plus RIPEstat for BGP routing history, AS relationships and country-level reachability. Verified live 2026-09-20 (HTTP 200).
- Docs: https://atlas.ripe.net/docs/apis/rest-api-manual/
- Base: `https://atlas.ripe.net/api/v2/measurements/ and https://stat.ripe.net/data/<endpoint>/data.json`
- Auth: free API key | Limits: Reading public measurement results and all of RIPEstat is unauthenticated. Creating your own measurements requires an account and spends 'credits', which you earn by hosting a probe or receive as a small starting allowance. RIPEstat asks for a sourceapp= parameter identifying your tool.
- Latency: minutely | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: Independent, hard-to-fake confirmation of national internet shutdowns, which are a standard precursor to and marker of coups, contested elections and violent crackdowns. When a government cuts the internet, probe reachability drops before any news report exists — and internet-shutdown contracts resolve on exactly this kind of measurement.

**Federal Register API** — US National Archives / GPO `LIVE`

- Every US federal rule, proposed rule, notice, and presidential document (executive orders, proclamations) as structured JSON with full text, agency, docket, comment period, and effective dates, from 1994 onward. Verified live 2026-09-20 (HTTP 200).
- Docs: https://www.federalregister.gov/developers/documentation/api/v1
- Base: `https://www.federalregister.gov/api/v1/documents.json?per_page=100&order=newest&conditions[type][]=PRESDOCU`
- Auth: none | Limits: No key, no registration, no published rate limit. Public domain. Full-text search, agency filters and date conditions all supported.
- Latency: daily (published each business day ~06:00 ET, with public inspection documents available the prior afternoon) | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: Executive orders, sanctions designations, tariff actions and regulatory approvals are heavily traded and resolve on Federal Register publication. The 'public inspection' pre-publication list is a genuine few-hours edge over the official publication date.

**WHO Disease Outbreak News + health advisory feeds** — World Health Organization (plus CDC, ECDC, ProMED, HealthMap) `LIVE`

- Official verified outbreak reports with country, pathogen, case and death counts, and WHO risk assessment. ProMED-mail and HealthMap provide the faster, less-verified layer. All four verified reachable 2026-09-20 (WHO DON API returned 271,767 bytes).
- Docs: https://www.who.int/emergencies/disease-outbreak-news
- Base: `https://www.who.int/api/news/diseaseoutbreaknews ; https://promedmail.org/promed-posts/ (RSS) ; https://www.healthmap.org/`
- Auth: none | Limits: WHO's /api/news/ endpoint is an undocumented public JSON API backing their website — no key, but no stability guarantee. ProMED is RSS/scrape. HealthMap has no documented open API as of 2026 and is effectively scrape-only.
- Latency: daily to weekly | Format: REST JSON + RSS
- Relevance: Pandemic and outbreak contracts almost always name WHO declarations (PHEIC status, DON publication) as the resolution criterion. ProMED historically leads WHO by days-to-weeks on novel outbreaks, which is where the edge lives.

**OpenStreetMap changeset and Overpass APIs** — OpenStreetMap Foundation `LIVE`

- Every map edit worldwide as it happens (changesets with bbox, user, comment, timestamp) plus Overpass QL for querying current map features — every mine, port, airfield, power plant, pipeline, border crossing on Earth with tags. Verified live 2026-09-20 (changesets.json HTTP 200).
- Docs: https://wiki.openstreetmap.org/wiki/API_v0.6
- Base: `https://api.openstreetmap.org/api/0.6/changesets.json?limit=100 and https://overpass-api.de/api/interpreter`
- Auth: none | Limits: Read APIs are unauthenticated. Overpass public instances enforce a fair-use slot system — roughly 2 concurrent slots and a ~1GB/day download budget per IP; heavy users should self-host Overpass. ODbL licensed (share-alike — matters if you redistribute derived geodata).
- Latency: minutely (changesets) / daily (Overpass reflects the main DB with minutes-to-hours lag) | Format: REST JSON/XML + Overpass QL
- Relevance: Overpass is how you get the coordinate list of every lithium mine, copper smelter, oil refinery or military airbase in a country, for free, which is the georeferencing layer that turns a FIRMS thermal detection or a Sentinel-1 scene into 'something happened at THIS facility'. Indispensable for mining, minerals and energy-infrastructure contracts.

**IMF PortWatch** — International Monetary Fund + Oxford University

- Daily port-call and trade-volume estimates for ~1,400 ports and 20+ maritime chokepoints, derived from AIS, with disruption simulation tooling. Free and public via an ArcGIS feature-service API.
- Docs: https://portwatch.imf.org/
- Base: `https://portwatch.imf.org/datasets (ArcGIS REST feature services; query endpoints follow the /FeatureServer/0/query?where=1=1&outFields=*&f=json pattern)`
- Auth: none | Limits: Free and open. Served from ArcGIS Online, which applies standard feature-service paging (typically 1,000-2,000 records per request via resultOffset/resultRecordCount).
- Latency: daily | Format: REST JSON (ArcGIS FeatureServer / GeoJSON)
- Relevance: Chokepoint transit counts and port throughput price shipping-disruption, oil-flow and trade-volume contracts, and this is the cleanest free pre-aggregated version — it saves you building the AIS-to-chokepoint pipeline yourself. Also the best free proxy for bulk-commodity and ore export volumes ahead of official customs releases.

**NGA Maritime Safety Information (Navigational Warnings)** — US National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency

- Broadcast and hydrographic navigational warnings worldwide: live-fire exercise areas, missile-test closure zones, GPS interference notices, piracy alerts, naval exercise areas — each with coordinates and effective window.
- Docs: https://msi.nga.mil/api-docs
- Base: `https://msi.nga.mil/api/publications/broadcast-warn?status=active&output=json`
- Auth: none | Limits: Public US government API, no key, no published cap. Public domain.
- Latency: daily | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: Missile-test and live-fire closure notices are published BEFORE the event by international obligation — this is one of the few genuinely forward-looking official feeds. A NOTAM/NAVWARN closure box off a coast is direct advance evidence for missile-test and military-exercise contracts.

**Cloudflare Radar API** — Cloudflare `LIVE`

- Internet-scale telemetry: detected national and regional outages with cause annotations, traffic anomalies, DDoS attack volumes by target country and industry, BGP hijack/leak events, protocol and bot-traffic breakdowns. Verified 2026-09-20 that the endpoint exists and rejects unauthenticated calls with error code 9106.
- Docs: https://developers.cloudflare.com/radar/
- Base: `https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/radar/annotations/outages (Authorization: Bearer <token>)`
- Auth: free API key | Limits: Requires a free Cloudflare account and an API token with the Radar read scope — VERIFIED, unauthenticated requests return 'Missing X-Auth-Key, X-Auth-Email or Authorization headers'. Free-plan Radar access exists with standard Cloudflare API limits (1,200 requests per 5 minutes per account).
- Latency: sub-minute | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: Cloudflare sees a large share of global traffic, so its outage annotations are the fastest credible detection of a national internet shutdown — which prices coup, election-crackdown and internet-shutdown contracts, and often front-runs the news by an hour or more.

**GPSJAM** — John Wiseman (lemon.cx) `LIVE`

- Daily global maps of GPS/GNSS interference, derived from ADS-B aircraft self-reported navigation integrity category — effectively a crowdsourced electronic-warfare detector. Verified reachable 2026-09-20.
- Docs: https://gpsjam.org/
- Base: `https://gpsjam.org/data/<YYYY-MM-DD>-h3_4.json (H3 resolution-4 hex grid, one file per day)`
- Auth: none | Limits: Static daily JSON files, no key, no cap. Undocumented but stable URL pattern; worldmonitor consumes exactly this file. One file per day — trivial to archive.
- Latency: daily | Format: REST JSON (H3 hex grid)
- Relevance: GPS jamming intensity is a direct, quantified electronic-warfare indicator that correlates with active military operations and is essentially impossible to fake at scale. Jamming expansion over a border region is meaningful advance evidence for escalation contracts.

**ReliefWeb API v2** — UN OCHA `LIVE`

- The humanitarian sector's document and disaster index: situation reports, needs assessments, disaster records, job and training listings, from 4,000+ organizations, with country/disaster-type/theme taxonomies.
- Docs: https://apidoc.reliefweb.int/
- Base: `https://api.reliefweb.int/v2/reports?appname=<approved-appname>&limit=10 (also /v2/disasters, /v2/countries, /v2/sources)`
- Auth: registration required | Limits: BREAKING CHANGE VERIFIED 2026-09-20: v1 is DECOMMISSIONED and returns HTTP 410 with the message "The API version 'v1' has been decommissioned. Please use version 'v2' instead." And v2 no longer accepts an arbitrary appname — an unregistered one returns HTTP 403 'You are not using an approved appname.' You must request an approved appname via the apidoc site before any call will work. Every tutorial and library predating this is broken.
- Latency: daily | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: Structured disaster records with OCHA's own severity classification and consolidated situation reports — the narrative layer that explains a GDACS alert, and a common resolution source for humanitarian-crisis contracts.

#### NICHE

**AISHub** — AISHub (AIS data sharing community) `LIVE`

- Community AIS exchange giving JSON/XML/CSV ship position snapshots. Verified live 2026-09-20 (site returned 113,743 bytes).
- Docs: https://www.aishub.net/api
- Base: `https://data.aishub.net/ws.php?username=<user>&format=1&output=json&compress=0`
- Auth: registration required | Limits: Free ONLY if you contribute your own AIS receiver feed — this is a strict reciprocity model, not an open API. Non-contributors get no access. If you do contribute: 1 request per minute, and you receive the full shared pool.
- Latency: minutely | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: Same chokepoint and port-call use cases as AISStream, useful as a second source, but the receiver-contribution requirement makes it impractical unless you already run hardware.

**NVD CVE API 2.0** — US NIST National Vulnerability Database `LIVE`

- Every published CVE with CVSS v2/v3.1/v4 vectors and scores, CWE mapping, CPE applicability, references and publication/modification timestamps. Verified live 2026-09-20 (HTTP 200).
- Docs: https://nvd.nist.gov/developers/vulnerabilities
- Base: `https://services.nvd.nist.gov/rest/json/cves/2.0?resultsPerPage=2000&pubStartDate=&pubEndDate=`
- Auth: free API key | Limits: Works without a key at 5 requests per rolling 30 seconds. With a free key: 50 requests per rolling 30 seconds. resultsPerPage max 2000. Date range per request capped at 120 days. NIST strongly recommends sleeping 6 seconds between calls even with a key.
- Latency: daily | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: Base rates for cyber contracts: CVE publication volume by vendor, time-from-publication-to-KEV, and CVSS distribution. Pairs with KEV as the 'all disclosed' denominator against KEV's 'confirmed exploited' numerator.

**IFRC GO API** — International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies `LIVE`

- Disaster emergency records, DREF and Emergency Appeal allocations with amounts and dates, field reports, and national-society response status. Verified live 2026-09-20: /api/v2/event/ returned 9,709 bytes unauthenticated.
- Docs: https://go.ifrc.org/docs/
- Base: `https://goadmin.ifrc.org/api/v2/event/?limit=50 (also /appeal/, /field-report/, /dref/)`
- Auth: none | Limits: Public read access with no key for most endpoints. No documented rate limit. Standard DRF pagination via limit/offset.
- Latency: daily | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: Humanitarian-appeal contracts ('will an international appeal exceeding $N be launched for X') resolve on IFRC appeal records, and appeal size is a quantified severity signal that arrives days after a disaster — useful as a settlement source and as a label for training a severity model on GDACS alerts.

**Safecast API** — Safecast (volunteer radiation monitoring) `LIVE`

- Crowd-sourced environmental radiation measurements (CPM/µSv/h) with lat/lon and timestamp, over 200 million points since Fukushima, plus air-quality. Verified live 2026-09-20 (HTTP 200).
- Docs: https://api.safecast.org/
- Base: `https://api.safecast.org/measurements.json?limit=100&order=created_at%20desc`
- Auth: none | Limits: No key for reads. No documented cap. CC0 licensed. Coverage is dense in Japan and patchy elsewhere — absence of a reading is not absence of radiation.
- Latency: hourly (depends entirely on volunteer upload cadence) | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: Nuclear-incident contracts (Zaporizhzhia, reactor accidents, weapons testing) need an independent radiation signal. Safecast plus the IAEA/CTBTO networks is roughly the only non-governmental option. Be honest about coverage gaps — outside Japan this is sparse.

**abuse.ch threat intelligence feeds (URLhaus, ThreatFox, MalwareBazaar, Feodo Tracker)** — abuse.ch / Institute for Cybersecurity and Engineering ICE, Bern University `LIVE`

- Live malware URLs, C2 infrastructure IOCs, malware samples and botnet tracker data. Verified 2026-09-20: the bulk CSV download at urlhaus.abuse.ch/downloads/csv_recent/ returned 2,409,587 bytes with no auth, while the JSON API endpoints returned HTTP 401.
- Docs: https://urlhaus-api.abuse.ch/
- Base: `https://urlhaus.abuse.ch/downloads/csv_recent/ (open bulk) ; https://urlhaus-api.abuse.ch/v1/ and https://threatfox-api.abuse.ch/api/v1/ (require Auth-Key header)`
- Auth: free API key | Limits: CHANGED IN 2025: the programmatic APIs now require a free Auth-Key header obtained from an abuse.ch account — VERIFIED, unauthenticated API calls return HTTP 401. The bulk CSV/JSON downloads remain open with no key. Free for non-commercial use; commercial redistribution needs permission.
- Latency: minutely (bulk files regenerate every 5 minutes) | Format: CSV bulk (open) + REST JSON (keyed)
- Relevance: Campaign-level spikes in C2 infrastructure attributed to a known actor are a weak-but-real precursor signal for disclosed-breach and cyberattack contracts. Treat as a secondary indicator; attribution in these feeds is noisy.

**OSINT Framework and Bellingcat Online Investigation Toolkit** — lockfale (OSINT Framework) / Bellingcat `LIVE`

- Two curated master indexes of OSINT tooling. OSINT Framework is a browsable tree of several hundred tools by investigation type. Bellingcat's toolkit is a categorized, actively-maintained database of satellite/mapping, transport tracking, social media, archiving and geolocation tools with notes on cost and access. Both verified reachable 2026-09-20 (Bellingcat returned 675,095 bytes).
- Docs: https://osintframework.com/
- Base: `https://osintframework.com/ and https://bellingcat.gitbook.io/toolkit`
- Auth: none | Limits: Web directories, not APIs. OSINT Framework's underlying data is a JSON tree in the lockfale/OSINT-Framework GitHub repo (MIT licensed, 12.1k stars) that you can parse programmatically. Bellingcat's toolkit is a GitBook over a Google Sheet.
- Latency: monthly | Format: scrape-only
- Relevance: Not a data feed — a discovery layer. Use these to find the niche per-domain source you need (a specific country's mining registry, a particular flight tracker) rather than as a runtime dependency.

#### Repos

- `koala73/worldmonitor` — THIS IS THE 'GOD'S EYE' REPO THE USER DESCRIBED. Verified via the GitHub API on 2026-09-20: 87,092 stars, 13,235 forks, AGPL-3.0, last pushed 2026-09-20T19:03:45Z (actively maintained, 7,627 commits), 405 open issues. Repo topics literally include 'osint', 'palantir', 'geopolitics', 'situation', 'mcp-server'. A real-time global intelligence dashboard: 3D globe + deck.gl flat map, 170+ RSS feeds across 15 categories, 26 Telegram OSINT channels, and a documented data-source catalog spanning geopolitics/conflict (ACLED, UCDP, GDELT, IMF PortWatch, Taiwan MND, Japan Joint Staff, OREF, UN OCHA HAPI), military (CelesTrak, gpsjam.org, LiveUAMap, SIPRI, World Bank MS.MIL.*), aviation (FAA, adsb.lol, AviationStack), disasters (USGS, GDACS, NASA FIRMS/EONET, Open-Meteo), infrastructure/cyber (Cloudflare Radar, Submarine Cable Map, abuse.ch), finance (FRED, ECB, BIS, Eurostat, World Bank, CoinGecko), energy (GIE AGSI+, EIA, IEA, CFTC), demographics (UN WPP, UNESCO UIS, ILOSTAT), and China coverage (NBS, SAFE, PBoC, SSE/SZSE). Ships an MCP server, a REST API, CLI and Python/Ruby/Go SDKs. · It is the single highest-leverage artifact for this entire project. It has already solved the hard, boring 80%: per-source collectors, normalization, Redis caching with per-key freshness budgets, source-credibility metadata (source tier, propaganda-risk rating, state-affiliation flag), and a stale/activationUnknown contract on every response. Two caveats that matter. First, AGPL-3.0 is viral over a network service — if you serve a derived product, you must release your source; check this against your commercial plans BEFORE building on it. Second, the hosted api.worldmonitor.app is keyed and blocks agent user-agents, so the free path is self-hosting the code, not calling their service.
- `koala73/worldmonitor (docs/data-sources page)` — The catalog at worldmonitor.app/docs/data-sources, which enumerates every provider with its license and collection method (API vs web scrape), and the full 170+ RSS feed list broken out by region: Europe (~75 outlets including Kyiv Independent, Meduza, Ukrinform, Balkan Insight), Middle East (~26 including Rudaw, Enab Baladi, Mada Masr), Africa (~33 including Radio Tamazuj, Dabanga Sudan, Actualite.cd), Asia (~48), Latin America (~16 including InSight Crime, Efecto Cocuyo), plus Intel (Bellingcat, Oryx OSINT, OCCRP, DFRLab, Lighthouse Reports, VSquare, Correctiv) and a full commodity/mining set (Mining.com, Northern Miner, Benchmark Mineral, IEA Critical Minerals, LME Metals, Rare Earths News). · The regional RSS list alone answers a large part of the user's 'every domain on this planet' ask and is worth extracting verbatim. It is a hand-curated, regionally-balanced source list that would take months to assemble, and it includes the local-language outlets that break regional news well before the wires — which is where the actual information edge is. The commodity/mining feed set directly covers the 'mines, minerals, what is happening there' requirement.
- `ilhamhakm/Spectre` — MIT-licensed (verified 2026-09-20, last pushed 2026-09-03) Next.js/Cesium 3D-globe intelligence dashboard. Distinct from worldmonitor in what it covers: CCTV/webcam aggregation (Windy, Shodan, NY511, LTA Singapore, TfNSW), traffic flow (TomTom tiles, Overpass road data), satellite tracking via CelesTrak TLE propagation, imagery layers (Sentinel-2 WMS via Copernicus, NASA GIBS MODIS Terra, Google Photorealistic 3D Tiles, NASA FIRMS), internet radio, OpenSky commercial flights with a VIP/notable-aircraft registry and dead-reckoning interpolation, and adsb.lol military flights. Its unrest pipeline fuses GDELT + RSS + ACLED + CIVICUS + Mastodon + Reddit + Telegram + YouTube + ReliefWeb + UCDP with event clustering, verification levels and instability scoring. · MIT license makes it commercially safe to borrow from, unlike worldmonitor's AGPL — this matters a great deal if the panel is a product. Its ground-level layers (CCTV, traffic cameras, street view, radio) are a category worldmonitor does not cover and give human-verifiable confirmation of an event. The env-var list is an efficient checklist of which keys you actually need. Caveat: 0 stars, so it is unvetted single-author code — read it, do not trust it.
- `jivoi/awesome-osint` — The canonical awesome-list for OSINT. Verified 2026-09-20: 29,653 stars, last pushed 2026-09-09, so it is actively maintained rather than an abandoned list. · The broadest discovery index for per-domain sources — when you need the one registry or tracker for a narrow subdomain (a national mining cadastre, a specific country's court filings), this is where to look first. It is a directory, not a dependency: harvest from it offline, do not call it at runtime.
- `lockfale/OSINT-Framework` — MIT-licensed, 12,171 stars, last pushed 2026-09-11 (verified). The web app behind osintframework.com, backed by a machine-parseable JSON tree of several hundred tools organized by investigation type. · Unlike a flat markdown awesome-list, the underlying arf.json is structured data you can ingest programmatically to auto-populate a 'related tools' section per domain in the research panel. MIT license means no redistribution friction.
- `Astrosp/Awesome-OSINT-List` — 4,445 stars, GPL-3.0, last pushed 2026-09-16 (verified) — the most recently-maintained of the large OSINT lists, oriented toward cybersecurity, reverse search, trust-and-safety and AI-assisted OSINT. · Its recency is the point: OSINT tools die constantly (ADS-B Exchange going commercial, Twitter's API closing, abuse.ch adding auth), and a list updated four days before this research is far more likely to reflect what actually still works in 2026 than a list last touched in 2023.
- `alex9smith/gdelt-doc-api` — MIT-licensed Python client for the GDELT DOC 2.0 API (231 stars, last pushed 2025-04-22). Wraps Filters (keyword, start_date, end_date, country, domain, theme) and all the timeline modes, returning pandas DataFrames. · Saves you writing the query-string builder and the timeline-response parsers. CRITICAL CAVEAT from live testing: it does not handle GDELT's 1-request-per-5-seconds limit, and GDELT returns 429 with a PLAIN-TEXT body that a JSON parser will choke on. Wrap every call in your own rate limiter and content-type check before using this in anything that polls.
- `linwoodc3/gdeltPyR` — GPL-3.0 Python library (257 stars) for pulling and parsing the GDELT 1.0 and 2.0 raw CSV files — events, mentions and GKG — into pandas, handling the column schemas and the 15-minute file naming convention. Last pushed 2023-11-30. · The raw-file path is the one GDELT actually wants high-volume users on, and the GDELT 2.0 CSVs are headerless with ~61 columns whose order you must know exactly. This library encodes that schema. It is unmaintained since 2023, so verify the column mapping against the current codebook, but it is still the fastest way to avoid hand-writing the parser.
- `openskynetwork/opensky-api` — Official OpenSky Python and Java client (468 stars, GPL-3.0, last pushed 2026-09-14 — actively maintained through the auth migration). · OpenSky retired HTTP Basic auth in March 2026 in favor of OAuth2 client-credentials with ~30-minute token expiry. This repo's recent commits contain the correct token-refresh implementation. Any tutorial or Stack Overflow answer showing username/password auth is now wrong, so take the flow from here rather than from documentation you find elsewhere.
- `aisstream/aisstream` — Official example clients (207 stars, last pushed 2025-02-07) for the AISStream.io WebSocket, in Go, Python, JavaScript and others, showing the JSON subscription handshake with APIKey, BoundingBoxes, FilterMessageTypes and FiltersShipMMSI. · AISStream is WebSocket-only with no REST fallback, so there is no way to 'just curl it' to understand the protocol — you need a working handshake example, and the subscription-message format is not obvious. These examples are the shortest path to a running vessel feed.
- `bluesky-social/jetstream` — Apache-2.0 official Jetstream server (37 stars, last pushed 2026-09-20 — updated the same day as this research). Converts the CBOR/MST ATProto firehose into filterable JSON over WebSocket. · Apache-2.0 and self-hostable, which matters because the four public instances are a shared courtesy resource. If social velocity becomes a load-bearing signal for the panel, run your own Jetstream against the upstream relay rather than depending on Bluesky's free public endpoints staying open.
