### Weather, Climate and Atmosphere

#### CORE

**Open-Meteo Forecast API (multi-model: GFS, ECMWF IFS/AIFS, ICON, GEM, HRRR, AROME, UKMO, JMA, BoM, CMA)** — Open-Meteo (Patrick Zippenfenig, CH) `LIVE`

- Hourly and 15-minutely deterministic forecasts for any lat/lon from ~20 NWP models, selectable per-model via /v1/gfs, /v1/ecmwf, /v1/dwd-icon, /v1/gem, /v1/meteofrance, /v1/jma, /v1/ukmo, /v1/bom, /v1/cma, /v1/knmi, /v1/metno, plus a 'best_match' blend. Variables include temperature_2m, precipitation, snowfall, snow_depth, wind, cloud cover, CAPE, freezing level. Supports past_days for recent verification and &models= to get several models in one call for spread.
- Docs: https://open-meteo.com/en/docs
- Auth: none (no API key for non-commercial; key only for the paid customer-api host) | Limits: 600 calls/min, 5,000 calls/hour, 10,000 calls/day, 300,000 calls/month. Non-commercial use only. No uptime guarantee. (Verified on https://open-meteo.com/en/pricing)
- Latency: hourly (model runs refresh 4x/day for GFS/IFS; 15-min product updates sub-hourly for HRRR/AROME domains) | Format: REST JSON (also flatbuffers, CSV, XLSX)
- Relevance: The single best free source for DAILY CITY TEMPERATURE AND PRECIPITATION contracts. One call returns 10+ models for the same point, which is exactly the model-spread input a research panel needs. Feeds the ensemble-forecast and model-spread panes directly.

**Open-Meteo Ensemble API (GFS ENS 31-member, ICON-EPS, ECMWF IFS ENS 51-member, GEM ENS, BoM ACCESS-GE)** — Open-Meteo `LIVE`

- Per-member ensemble traces at a point: every perturbed member's temperature_2m, precipitation, snowfall etc. for the full lead time. This is what you convert into a probability distribution and then into an implied probability for a threshold contract.
- Docs: https://open-meteo.com/en/docs/ensemble-api
- Auth: none | Limits: Same shared quota as the forecast API: 600/min, 5,000/hour, 10,000/day, 300,000/month. NOTE: ensemble calls are weighted more heavily in Open-Meteo's cost accounting than a single-model call — exact weighting factor UNKNOWN.
- Latency: hourly (ensemble runs 00/06/12/18Z, available ~5-7h after run time) | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: CORE. Direct route from raw ensemble members to P(high temp > X) without you having to download and decode GRIB. This is the probability-generating engine for every threshold weather contract.

**Open-Meteo Previous Model Runs API** — Open-Meteo `LIVE`

- The same forecast variables but tagged by which prior model run produced them (temperature_2m_previous_day1 ... previous_day7). Lets you reconstruct what each model said N days ago for a given target date.
- Docs: https://open-meteo.com/en/docs/previous-runs-api
- Auth: none | Limits: Shared quota with forecast API (10,000 calls/day). History of previous runs retained: UNKNOWN beyond the documented ~7 prior days per variable.
- Latency: hourly | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: CORE and badly underused. This is how you build 'model vs. market over time' charts and how you measure each model's historical error at a specific station — the exact two things the research panel spec asks for. Without this you cannot score a model's skill at a station.

**Open-Meteo Historical Weather API (ERA5, ERA5-Land, ERA5-Ensemble, CERRA, operational IFS archive)** — Open-Meteo / ECMWF reanalysis `LIVE`

- Hourly reanalysis back to 1940 (ERA5, 0.25 deg) and 1950 (ERA5-Land, 0.1 deg) for any point, plus an operational ECMWF IFS 9km archive from 2017. Pre-interpolated to a point — no GRIB decoding, no CDS queue.
- Docs: https://open-meteo.com/en/docs/historical-weather-api
- Auth: none | Limits: Shared quota (10,000 calls/day) but long date ranges consume more; exact per-call weighting UNKNOWN. ERA5 lag: 5 days. IFS assimilation long-window: 2 days.
- Latency: daily (5-day lag for ERA5; use forecast API &past_days for the recent gap) | Format: REST JSON / CSV
- Relevance: CORE for backtesting. 85 years of history at a point is the climatological prior you need before you trust any model. But see the caveat: reanalysis grid values are NOT the station values contracts settle on — use ACIS/NWS CLI for settlement truth and ERA5 only for climatology.

**NOAA / National Weather Service API (api.weather.gov)** — NOAA NWS (US Government) `LIVE`

- Official US forecasts on the 2.5km NDFD grid, hourly forecasts, active alerts/warnings in CAP, station metadata, latest and historical station observations, zone/county geometry, and the full raw NWS text-product archive (/products, /products/types).
- Docs: https://www.weather.gov/documentation/services-web-api
- Auth: none — but a descriptive User-Agent header with contact info is mandatory; requests without it are rejected. NWS states this will eventually be replaced by an API key. | Limits: UNKNOWN — NWS does not publish numeric limits. Docs say only 'reasonable rate limits', 429 on exceed, retry after ~5 seconds, and that proxied/shared-IP requests hit limits sooner than direct client requests.
- Latency: alerts near-realtime; observations sub-hourly (5-20 min per station); gridded forecast updated ~hourly | Format: REST GeoJSON / JSON-LD / CAP XML / DWML
- Relevance: CORE. This is the authoritative US government feed and the source most US weather contracts ultimately trace to. Alerts drive hurricane-warning and winter-storm contracts. Verified live: /points/40.7128,-74.0060 and /alerts/active?area=NY both returned 200.

**NWS CLI Daily Climate Report products (api.weather.gov/products/types/CLI)** — NOAA NWS `LIVE`

- The official daily climate summary text product issued by each WFO for its climate sites: observed max temp, min temp, precipitation, snowfall, snow depth, plus records and normals. Retrieved by product type CLI and by location code (e.g. /products/types/CLI/locations/NYC).
- Docs: https://www.weather.gov/documentation/services-web-api
- Auth: none (User-Agent header required, same as the parent API) | Limits: UNKNOWN (inherits api.weather.gov's unpublished limits). Product archive depth on the API: UNKNOWN — for deep history use IEM's AFOS archive instead.
- Latency: daily, typically issued shortly after local midnight plus a preliminary afternoon issuance | Format: REST JSON wrapper around fixed-width text (you must parse the text body)
- Relevance: CORE — and this is the point most builders miss. Kalshi-style daily city high/low temperature contracts SETTLE on the CLI report for the designated station (e.g. NYC = Central Park), not on any weather API's 'current temperature'. If you price against a forecast API but settle against CLI, you will be systematically wrong. Verified: /products/types/CLI returned live 2026-09-20 products and /products/types/CLI/locations returned the full station code table.

**RCC-ACIS (Applied Climate Information System) — StnData / MultiStnData** — NOAA Regional Climate Centers `LIVE`

- Quality-controlled daily station climate data: maxt, mint, pcpn, snow, snwd, degree days, plus normals, records, and ThreadEx long-period station threads. Accepts GHCN/WBAN/ICAO/coop IDs interchangeably. Supports multi-station queries and reductions (e.g. count of days above a threshold) server-side.
- Docs: https://www.rcc-acis.org/docs_webservices.html
- Auth: none | Limits: UNKNOWN — no published numeric limit. ACIS asks for reasonable use and prefers MultiStnData over many single-station calls.
- Latency: daily (next-day for most stations; preliminary values can be revised) | Format: REST JSON over POST
- Relevance: CORE. The fastest path to settlement-grade station history. Verified live with a real query: POST to https://data.rcc-acis.org/StnData for sid USW00094728 returned NY CITY CENTRAL PARK daily max/min/precip/snow for 2026-09-15 through 2026-09-19. This gives you both the settlement values and the station's historical error distribution in one call.

**Iowa Environmental Mesonet (IEM) — API v1, ASOS bulk download, MOS archive, AFOS text archive** — Iowa State University (daryl herzmann) `LIVE`

- Decades of 1-minute and standard ASOS/AWOS/METAR observations by bulk CSV; /api/1/daily.json with max_tmpf, min_tmpf, precip, snow, snowd per station-day; /api/1/mos.json with GFS/NAM/NBM Model Output Statistics station guidance; /api/1/nws/afos/list.json + /api/1/nwstext/{id} for the full raw NWS text-product archive including historical CLI reports; /api/1/usdm_bypoint.json for drought class at a point; IEM Reanalysis (iemre); NEXRAD composites; VTEC warning archive.
- Docs: https://mesonet.agron.iastate.edu/api/1/docs
- Auth: none | Limits: UNKNOWN — no numeric limit published. The API docs explicitly say: 'These services and the backend server answering the requests have finite capacity. I would suggest not using these on a highly trafficked website, nor launch a AWS region of EC2 instances against me.' Treat as courtesy-limited; cache aggressively.
- Latency: observations sub-hourly; MOS 4x/day; daily summaries next-day | Format: REST JSON (pandas table-schema envelope), CSV bulk download
- Relevance: CORE and the highest-value single site in this whole list. MOS is station-point statistical guidance calibrated to the exact station a contract settles on — far better than raw gridded model output for daily temp contracts. The AFOS archive is how you backtest against historical CLI reports. Verified live: openapi.json, daily.json for KNYC, currents.json, mos.json (NBS), and nws/afos/list.json for KOKX all returned 200 with real data.

**NOAA National Blend of Models (NBM) on AWS Open Data** — NOAA / AWS Open Data Program `LIVE`

- The operational statistically post-processed multi-model blend — the NWS's own best-guess product. GRIB2 grids plus, critically, station-point TEXT bulletins (blend_nbstx = NBM station text, blend_nbhtx = hourly, blend_nbxtx = extended) with percentile temperature and probability-of-precipitation fields at named stations. Hourly cycles.
- Docs: https://registry.opendata.aws/noaa-ndfd/
- Auth: none (anonymous S3; aws s3 ls --no-sign-request s3://noaa-nbm-grib2-pds/) | Limits: No call limit. Standard S3 anonymous access, requester pays nothing for in-region reads; out-of-AWS egress is free for Open Data Program buckets. Bucket retention depth: UNKNOWN (rolling; verify with a prefix list before relying on deep history).
- Latency: hourly (cycles every hour, blend.YYYYMMDD/HH/) | Format: GRIB2 + fixed-width text bulletins on S3
- Relevance: CORE for US daily temperature contracts. NBM already carries calibrated percentiles, so you can read an implied probability almost directly rather than building one from ensemble members. Verified live: s3://noaa-nbm-grib2-pds/blend.20260920/00/text/ contained blend_nbstx.t00z, blend_nbhtx.t00z, blend_nbptx.t00z, blend_nbetx.t00z, blend_nbxtx.t00z, and hourly cycle directories 00 through 04+ existed for today's date.

**NOAA GFS on AWS Open Data (noaa-gfs-bdp-pds)** — NOAA NODD / AWS Open Data `LIVE`

- Full-resolution 0.25-degree GFS deterministic output, all atmospheric and land-soil variables, out to 384 hours, plus GFS warm-start initial conditions in noaa-gfs-warmstart-pds.
- Docs: https://registry.opendata.aws/noaa-gfs-bdp-pds/
- Auth: none (anonymous S3) | Limits: No call or volume limit; no AWS account required (--no-sign-request). Archive depth: UNKNOWN — registry page does not state retention; confirm by listing before assuming deep history.
- Latency: 4x daily (00/06/12/18 UTC), files land progressively ~3.5h after cycle time | Format: GRIB2 on S3 (also mirrored on Google Cloud and Azure via NODD)
- Relevance: CORE as the raw-truth backstop. Use Open-Meteo for day-to-day queries and drop to the bucket when you need a variable Open-Meteo does not expose, or when you need the exact grid a counterparty is quoting.

**NOAA GEFS ensemble on AWS Open Data (noaa-gefs-pds)** — NOAA NODD / AWS Open Data `LIVE`

- Global Ensemble Forecast System — 31 members (control + 30 perturbed), 0.25/0.5 degree, out to 16 days, 4 cycles daily. Includes GEFS reforecast in a companion bucket for skill calibration.
- Docs: https://registry.opendata.aws/noaa-gefs/
- Auth: none (anonymous S3) | Limits: No call limit. Retention depth: UNKNOWN.
- Latency: 4x daily (00/06/12/18 UTC) | Format: GRIB2 on S3
- Relevance: CORE for probability construction beyond day 7, where deterministic models are useless and ensemble spread is the only honest signal. Verified live: gefs.20260920/00/, /06/, /12/ prefixes present.

**NOAA HRRR on AWS Open Data (noaa-hrrr-bdp-pds)** — NOAA NODD / AWS Open Data `LIVE`

- High-Resolution Rapid Refresh — 3km CONUS convection-allowing model, hourly cycles, 18h forecasts (48h on the 00/06/12/18Z cycles). Includes wrfsfcf (surface), wrfprsf (pressure levels), wrfnatf (native levels), and BUFR soundings.
- Docs: https://registry.opendata.aws/noaa-hrrr-bdp-pds/
- Auth: none (anonymous S3) | Limits: No call limit. Retention: UNKNOWN (rolling archive; 2014-present is claimed by third-party mirrors but not verified here).
- Latency: hourly (sub-hourly value for nowcasting) | Format: GRIB2 on S3
- Relevance: CORE for same-day and next-day US precipitation, snowfall and severe-weather contracts, and for rain-out contracts tied to a specific game time. Verified live: hrrr.20260920/conus/ contained hrrr.t00z.wrfnatf00.grib2, hrrr.t00z.bufrsnd.tar.gz, hrrr.t00z.class1.bufr.tm00.

**ECMWF Open Data (IFS HRES, IFS ENS, AIFS Single, AIFS ENS)** — ECMWF `LIVE`

- Real-time 0.25-degree GRIB2 from the world's best-scoring global model, free and CC-BY-4.0. IFS 00z/12z to 360h (3-hourly to 144h, then 6-hourly), 06z/18z to 144h. AIFS (ECMWF's ML model) to 360h at 6-hourly from all four cycles, both deterministic (aifs-single) and ensemble (aifs-ens), released immediately after production.
- Docs: https://www.ecmwf.int/en/forecasts/datasets/open-data
- Auth: none — no registration required for the open 0.25-degree data. Higher resolution requires a service agreement and charges. | Limits: No call limit stated. Rolling archive: the most recent 12 forecast runs only, approximately 2-3 days. You must pull and persist it yourself if you want history. Also mirrored on AWS at s3://ecmwf-forecasts/ (verified live).
- Latency: 4x daily; AIFS released immediately after production, IFS follows the dissemination schedule | Format: GRIB2 over HTTPS (data.ecmwf.int) and anonymous S3; official Python client ecmwf/ecmwf-opendata
- Relevance: CORE. ECMWF IFS is the model to beat for medium-range temperature, and AIFS is now competitive at a fraction of the compute — having both free is the biggest change in this domain since 2023. Verified live: https://data.ecmwf.int/forecasts/20260920/00z/ listed both aifs-ens/ and aifs-single/ directories on today's date.

**Copernicus Climate Data Store (CDS) — ERA5, ERA5-Land, C3S seasonal forecasts, CMIP6** — ECMWF / EU Copernicus C3S `LIVE`

- The canonical reanalysis: ERA5 hourly 0.25-degree from 1940, ERA5-Land 0.1-degree from 1950, ERA5 back-extension, plus C3S multi-system SEASONAL forecasts (ECMWF SEAS5, Met Office, Météo-France, DWD, CMCC, NCEP, JMA, ECCC) at monthly and daily aggregation out to 6-7 months, and CMIP6 climate projections.
- Docs: https://cds.climate.copernicus.eu/how-to-api
- Auth: free registration + personal access token in $HOME/.cdsapirc; you must also individually accept each dataset's Terms of Use before it will serve you | Limits: UNKNOWN as fixed numbers. CDS applies a per-user quota on concurrent requests and total download volume, scheduled by a quality-of-service module that weighs request cost; ECMWF states these limits change with system workload and does not publish them. Practically: requests queue, and large ERA5 pulls can take hours.
- Latency: ERA5 ~5-day lag; seasonal forecasts monthly (released around the 5th-13th) | Format: NetCDF / GRIB via the cdsapi Python client (asynchronous job + download)
- Relevance: CORE for climatology and the ONLY free source of genuine multi-model seasonal forecasts, which is what you need for monthly-anomaly and ENSO contracts. Not suitable for anything time-sensitive because of the queue — pre-stage it. Verified live: how-to-api page and the seasonal-monthly-single-levels dataset page both returned 200.

**NOAA National Hurricane Center (CurrentStorms.json, advisories, forecast cones, GIS shapefiles, wind-speed probabilities)** — NOAA NHC `LIVE`

- Machine-readable active storm list with id, name, classification, intensity, pressure, lat/lon, movement, and links to every product; forecast advisories (TCM), public advisories (TCP), forecast discussions (TCD), wind speed probability products, track/cone/wind-swath shapefiles and KML, plus the GIS best-track archive.
- Docs: https://www.nhc.noaa.gov/productexamples/
- Auth: none | Limits: UNKNOWN — no published limit. NHC serves static files; poll at the advisory cadence (every 3 hours, hourly for intermediate advisories), not faster.
- Latency: every 3 hours during active storms (00/06/12/18 UTC advisories plus intermediate at 03/09/15/21); near-realtime for updates | Format: JSON (CurrentStorms.json), fixed-width text, shapefile, KML, RSS
- Relevance: CORE for every hurricane contract. NHC is the settlement authority for named-storm formation, category at landfall and landfall location — no third-party API substitutes for it. The wind speed probability product gives you an official probability you can compare directly against market price. Verified live: https://www.nhc.noaa.gov/CurrentStorms.json returned active storm al062026 'Fay', TS, 55kt, 999mb, last update 2026-09-20T21:00Z.

**NOAA NOHRSC National Snow Analysis / SNODAS** — NOAA National Operational Hydrologic Remote Sensing Center `LIVE`

- Daily 1km gridded snow depth, snow water equivalent, snowmelt, snowpack temperature and 24h snowfall for CONUS and southern Canada; the SNODAS assimilation product archive on NSIDC (G02158) back to 2003; plus station-level snowfall and snow-depth reports.
- Docs: https://www.nohrsc.noaa.gov/nsa/
- Auth: none | Limits: UNKNOWN — static file server, no published limit.
- Latency: daily (06 UTC model cycle) | Format: GRIB / GeoTIFF / shapefile / text; SNODAS archive as tarred .dat.gz on NSIDC
- Relevance: CORE for SNOWFALL contracts, which are one of the four contract families the task named. Gridded snowfall is what you price against; station snowfall in the CLI report is what settles. Verified live: nohrsc.noaa.gov/nsa/ returned 200 and https://noaadata.apps.nsidc.org/NOAA/G02158/masked/2026/09_Sep/ returned 200.

**NCEI Access Data Service (GSOD, GHCN-Daily, ISD global-hourly, normals) + NOAA bulk archives** — NOAA NCEI `LIVE`

- Bulk station climate history: Global Summary of the Day, GHCN-Daily (~120,000 stations, some back to the 1700s), Integrated Surface Database hourly observations, and 1991-2020 climate normals. Query by station, date range, and data type in one URL; or pull the raw yearly tarballs from the FTP-over-HTTP tree; or read them from s3://noaa-gsod-pds and s3://noaa-ghcn-pds.
- Docs: https://www.ncei.noaa.gov/support/access-data-service-api-user-documentation
- Auth: none | Limits: UNKNOWN — no published numeric limit on the Access Data Service. NCEI asks large users to use the bulk file tree or the AWS buckets instead of hammering the query service.
- Latency: daily for GSOD/GHCN-D (1-2 day lag); hourly ISD lags days to weeks | Format: REST JSON/CSV, plus bulk CSV/fixed-width over HTTPS and anonymous S3
- Relevance: CORE for backtesting and for building each station's historical error distribution. Verified live: the Access Data Service returned 200 for a global-summary-of-the-day query; s3://noaa-gsod-pds and s3://noaa-ghcn-pds both list anonymously; https://www.ncei.noaa.gov/pub/data/ghcn/daily/ returned 200. Note https://www.ncei.noaa.gov/data/global-hourly/access/2026/ returned 404 — the ISD directory layout differs by product, so probe before wiring paths.

#### USEFUL

**Open-Meteo Air Quality API (CAMS global + CAMS Europe, includes pollen and UV)** — Open-Meteo / Copernicus CAMS `LIVE`

- PM2.5, PM10, NO2, O3, SO2, CO, European AQI, US AQI, dust, ammonia; alder/birch/grass/mugwort/olive/ragweed pollen (Europe only); UV index and UV index clear-sky. Forecast to 5 days plus archive back to 2013.
- Docs: https://open-meteo.com/en/docs/air-quality-api
- Auth: none | Limits: Shared Open-Meteo quota: 10,000 calls/day, 5,000/hour, 600/min.
- Latency: hourly | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: USEFUL. Prices AQI-exceedance-day contracts and wildfire-smoke contracts. Pollen coverage is Europe-only — for US pollen there is no free gridded feed (see deadEnds).

**Open-Meteo Marine, Seasonal and Flood APIs (wave/swell, NOAA CFSv2 seasonal, GloFAS river discharge)** — Open-Meteo / NOAA / Copernicus EFAS `LIVE`

- Marine: wave height, swell period/direction, sea surface temperature, ocean currents. Seasonal: NOAA CFSv2 6-hourly out to 9 months. Flood: GloFAS river discharge forecast and 1984-present archive per river reach.
- Docs: https://open-meteo.com/en/docs/marine-weather-api
- Auth: none | Limits: Shared Open-Meteo quota: 10,000 calls/day.
- Latency: marine hourly; seasonal daily; flood daily | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: USEFUL. Marine SST feeds hurricane-intensity and Atlantic-MDR contracts. Seasonal CFSv2 is a weak but free long-range signal for monthly-anomaly contracts. Flood is NICHE unless flood contracts exist.

**NOAA NOMADS GRIB filter (nomads.ncep.noaa.gov)** — NOAA NCEP `LIVE`

- Server-side subsetting of every NCEP model (GFS, GEFS, HRRR, NAM, RAP, RTMA, NBM, WW3, GFSwave) by variable, level and lat/lon box, plus OPeNDAP/DODS access. Lets you pull a 20KB slice instead of a 400MB GRIB file.
- Docs: https://nomads.ncep.noaa.gov/
- Auth: none | Limits: NOMADS enforces an IP-based abuse throttle; the commonly cited figure is 120 hits/minute before a temporary block, but I could not verify an official published number — treat the exact threshold as UNKNOWN and back off on 403. NOMADS retains roughly the last 7-10 days; older data must come from AWS/NCEI.
- Latency: hourly to 6-hourly, matches each model's cycle | Format: GRIB2 subsets over CGI, plus OPeNDAP
- Relevance: USEFUL. Best when you need one variable at one point from many models fast and do not want to run S3 range reads. For production volume, prefer the AWS buckets — NOMADS will block you.

**Copernicus Atmosphere Data Store (ADS) — CAMS global and European air quality, dust, fire emissions, UV** — ECMWF / EU Copernicus CAMS `LIVE`

- CAMS global atmospheric composition forecasts and reanalysis (EAC4), CAMS European air quality ensemble (9 regional models, 4km), pollen forecasts for Europe, GFAS fire emissions, UV index, aerosol optical depth, solar radiation.
- Docs: https://ads.atmosphere.copernicus.eu/how-to-api
- Auth: free registration + personal access token (same cdsapi client, different endpoint) | Limits: UNKNOWN — same unpublished queue/quota model as CDS.
- Latency: daily to twice-daily for forecasts; reanalysis lags months | Format: NetCDF / GRIB via cdsapi
- Relevance: USEFUL. The authoritative source for European AQI and pollen contracts, and for wildfire-smoke-transport contracts. For quick point queries use Open-Meteo's Air Quality API instead — it is CAMS under the hood without the queue.

**NOAA Climate Data Online (CDO) API v2** — NOAA NCEI `LIVE`

- Token-authenticated REST access to GHCND (daily summaries), GSOM (monthly), GSOY (yearly), NORMAL_DLY/MLY (climate normals), PRECIP_15 and PRECIP_HLY, with station metadata, location hierarchies and data-type discovery.
- Docs: https://www.ncei.noaa.gov/cdo-web/webservices/v2
- Auth: free token by email request; sent as a 'token:' request header | Limits: 5 requests per second and 10,000 requests per day per token (explicitly published). Result sets are paginated at 1,000 records per request.
- Latency: daily (GHCND lags 1-2 days; normals are static) | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: USEFUL rather than CORE. It is the friendliest interface to climate normals and records — the 'is this a record high?' question — but it is slow and pagination-bound, so for volume use ACIS or the NCEI bulk tree. Verified live: https://www.ncei.noaa.gov/cdo-web/api/v2/datasets returned {"status":"400","message":"Token parameter is required."}, confirming the service is up and gated.

**MET Norway Locationforecast 2.0 and Nowcast 2.0 (api.met.no)** — Norwegian Meteorological Institute `LIVE`

- Global point forecasts from MET's post-processed blend (locationforecast/2.0/compact and /complete), plus Nordic 5-minute precipitation nowcasting (nowcast/2.0), radar, oceanforecast, sunrise/sunset, and text warnings in CAP.
- Docs: https://api.met.no/weatherapi/locationforecast/2.0/documentation
- Auth: none — but a unique identifying User-Agent with contact info is mandatory and enforced; generic agents get 403 | Limits: 20 requests/second per application (published in MET's Terms of Service), and clients MUST honour Expires/If-Modified-Since caching headers — ignoring them gets you blocked. Coordinates must be truncated to 4 decimals or the request is rejected.
- Latency: hourly for locationforecast; 5-minutely for Nordic nowcast | Format: REST JSON / GeoJSON / XML
- Relevance: USEFUL globally, CORE if any contract references a Nordic city. The nowcast product is genuinely sub-hourly precipitation, which very few free feeds offer. Verified live: both locationforecast/2.0/compact and nowcast/2.0/complete returned 200.

**DWD Open Data + Bright Sky API (Germany, ICON global / ICON-EU / ICON-D2)** — Deutscher Wetterdienst / Jakob de Maeyer (Bright Sky) `LIVE`

- DWD opendata: raw ICON (13km global), ICON-EU (6.5km), ICON-D2 (2.2km convection-allowing) GRIB2; RADOLAN radar-gauge precipitation; MOSMIX station forecasts; and the CDC climate archive with German station records back to the 1700s. Bright Sky wraps DWD's station observations and MOSMIX forecasts in a clean free JSON API.
- Docs: https://brightsky.dev/docs/
- Auth: none for either DWD opendata or the public Bright Sky instance | Limits: DWD opendata: no published limit (static file server, rolling ~24-48h retention for NWP). Bright Sky public instance: no hard published quota; the operator asks for 'reasonable' use and recommends self-hosting for heavy traffic — exact threshold UNKNOWN.
- Latency: ICON-D2 hourly; ICON-EU/global 4-8x daily; RADOLAN 5-minutely; Bright Sky observations hourly | Format: GRIB2 / bz2 on HTTP (DWD); REST JSON (Bright Sky)
- Relevance: USEFUL. ICON-D2 is one of the best free convection-allowing models outside the US and matters for any European city precipitation contract. Verified live: https://api.brightsky.dev/current_weather, https://opendata.dwd.de/weather/nwp/icon/grib/, https://opendata.dwd.de/weather/nwp/icon-d2/grib/ and https://opendata.dwd.de/climate_environment/CDC/ all returned 200.

**Environment and Climate Change Canada — MSC Datamart + GeoMet OGC API** — ECCC / Meteorological Service of Canada `LIVE`

- GEM Global (15km), GEM Regional (10km), HRDPS (2.5km), GEPS ensemble, RDPA precipitation analysis, CaPA, radar mosaics, SWOB station observations, and public alerts in CAP — all as open GRIB2/XML on Datamart, plus OGC API Features/Coverages/EDR via GeoMet and an MQTT/AMQP notification stream (sarracenia) for push delivery.
- Docs: https://eccc-msc.github.io/open-data/msc-datamart/readme_en/
- Auth: none | Limits: No published call limit. Datamart retains a rolling window — dated directories were present from 20260822 to 20260920 when probed, i.e. roughly 30 days. Beyond that use the HPFX server or the climate archive.
- Latency: HRDPS hourly; GEM Global 2x daily; radar 6-minutely; observations sub-hourly | Format: GRIB2, XML/CAP, GeoJSON, CoverageJSON; OGC API + MQTT push
- Relevance: USEFUL. CORE if any contract references a Canadian city. The MQTT push feed is a rare free capability — you get notified the instant a file lands rather than polling. Verified live: https://dd.weather.gc.ca/ returned 200 with 30 days of dated directories, https://api.weather.gc.ca/collections returned 200, https://hpfx.collab.science.gc.ca/ returned 200.

**Japan Meteorological Agency — bosai JSON endpoints and JMA XML feeds** — JMA (Japan) `LIVE`

- Per-prefecture forecast JSON (www.jma.go.jp/bosai/forecast/data/forecast/{areacode}.json), warnings, AMeDAS station observations, typhoon tracks and advisories, earthquake and tsunami feeds, and the JMA XML (Atom) push feed for all official products.
- Docs: https://www.data.jma.go.jp/developer/xml/
- Auth: none | Limits: UNKNOWN — the bosai JSON endpoints are undocumented internal APIs with no published terms or limits, which is a real operational risk: they can change shape without notice. The JMA XML feed at data.jma.go.jp/developer/xml/ IS officially documented and intended for developers.
- Latency: forecasts 3x daily; AMeDAS 10-minutely; warnings near-realtime | Format: JSON (bosai, undocumented), Atom/XML (official developer feed)
- Relevance: USEFUL for any Japan city contract and for West Pacific typhoon contracts (JMA is the RSMC for that basin, so JMA — not NHC — is the settlement authority there). Verified live: https://www.jma.go.jp/bosai/forecast/data/forecast/130000.json and https://www.data.jma.go.jp/developer/xml/feed/regular.xml both returned 200.

**Meteostat — Bulk Data interface and JSON API** — Meteostat (open project, DE) `LIVE`

- Consolidated station history from NOAA GHCN/ISD, DWD and national services in one normalized schema: hourly, daily, monthly and climate normals for ~20,000+ stations worldwide, downloadable as gzipped CSV/Parquet per station.
- Docs: https://dev.meteostat.net/
- Auth: Bulk endpoint: none. JSON API: RapidAPI key required (X-RapidAPI-Key header). | Limits: JSON API free plan: 500 calls PER MONTH via RapidAPI — effectively unusable for anything live. Bulk endpoint (bulk.meteostat.net): no published call limit, and no key. Directory listing is 403 but individual files serve fine.
- Latency: daily (station data typically 1-3 days behind) | Format: REST JSON (RapidAPI); gzipped CSV and Parquet (bulk)
- Relevance: USEFUL — but only via bulk. Meteostat's real value is that it has already done the cross-provider station reconciliation you would otherwise write yourself. Verified live: https://bulk.meteostat.net/v2/daily/72503.csv.gz and .../stations/lite.json.gz both returned 200, and the decompressed daily file contained real 2026 rows.

**Visual Crossing Weather API** — Visual Crossing Corporation `LIVE`

- Unified timeline endpoint covering 50+ years of hourly history, 15-day forecast, sub-hourly history, historical summaries, and weather event data (hail, tornado, wind) through a single query interface — history and forecast in one response, which most providers split.
- Docs: https://www.visualcrossing.com/resources/documentation/weather-api/timeline-weather-api/
- Auth: free API key (registration, no credit card for the free plan) | Limits: 1,000 records per day free (a 'record' is one day or one hour of data, so a 15-day daily forecast costs 15 records). Max 1,000 records per single query, up to 5 locations per query, 1 concurrent request. 50+ years of history included on the free tier.
- Latency: hourly | Format: REST JSON / CSV
- Relevance: USEFUL. The free tier's deep history with no credit card is unusual — most competitors paywall history entirely. The 1,000 records/day cap means you use it for targeted backfill, not for polling. Its 'weather events' dataset is the only free source here for hail/tornado event contracts.

**NOAA MRMS (Multi-Radar Multi-Sensor) on AWS Open Data** — NOAA NSSL / AWS Open Data `LIVE`

- 2-minute 1km national radar mosaic: reflectivity, precipitation rate, quantitative precipitation estimate (QPE) at 1/3/6/12/24/48/72h accumulations, precipitation flags (rain/snow/hail), rotation tracks, and hail size estimates.
- Docs: https://registry.opendata.aws/noaa-mrms-pds/
- Auth: none (anonymous S3) | Limits: No call limit. Retention on the PDS bucket: UNKNOWN (rolling; verify by listing).
- Latency: 2-minutely — genuinely realtime for a free gridded product | Format: GRIB2 (gzipped) on S3
- Relevance: USEFUL and the best free precipitation-verification source. MRMS QPE is how you know, within minutes, whether a precipitation contract has already resolved — critical for intraday trading on daily precip contracts. Verified live: s3://noaa-mrms-pds lists anonymously.

**RainViewer public radar API** — RainViewer (LLC) `LIVE`

- Global composited radar tile pyramids from 1200+ radars across 150+ countries, past frames plus a short nowcast, refreshed every 5 minutes; weather-maps.json indexes every available frame with its timestamp and tile path. Satellite infrared tiles also available.
- Docs: https://www.rainviewer.com/api.html
- Auth: none for the public weather-maps.json and its tiles | Limits: UNKNOWN — no numeric rate limit is published. The terms restrict the free public API to 'personal and educational use only' and explicitly disclaim availability: 'We do not guarantee the availability of radar data.' Commercial use requires their paid plan.
- Latency: 5-minutely | Format: REST JSON index + PNG/WebP raster tiles
- Relevance: USEFUL for the panel's radar layer, especially outside the US where MRMS does not reach. The personal/educational licence restriction is a real blocker for a commercial terminal — verify licensing before you ship. Verified live: https://api.rainviewer.com/public/weather-maps.json returned a current frame index (generated 1789950023).

**NOAA GOES-19 / GOES-18 on AWS Open Data** — NOAA NESDIS / AWS Open Data `LIVE`

- Full GOES-R ABI imagery: 16 spectral bands at full disk (10 min), CONUS (5 min) and mesoscale (30-60 sec), plus derived products — cloud top height, derived motion winds, total precipitable water, land surface temperature, aerosol detection, fire hot-spot characterization, and GLM geostationary LIGHTNING mapper flash/group/event data.
- Docs: https://registry.opendata.aws/noaa-goes/
- Auth: none (anonymous S3) | Limits: No call limit. Full archive from each satellite's operational start is retained.
- Latency: 30 seconds (mesoscale) to 10 minutes (full disk) — effectively realtime | Format: NetCDF4 on S3
- Relevance: USEFUL. GLM is the only free realtime LIGHTNING source with clear terms (Blitzortung's API is dead — see deadEnds), which matters for sports rain/lightning-delay contracts. ABI is how you watch a hurricane's eye between NHC advisories. Verified live: s3://noaa-goes19 lists anonymously.

**Aviation Weather Center Data API (METAR, TAF, PIREP, SIGMET, AIRMET)** — NOAA NWS Aviation Weather Center `LIVE`

- Raw and decoded METAR/SPECI observations and TAF forecasts for airports worldwide, plus pilot reports, SIGMETs, AIRMETs, G-AIRMETs, center weather advisories and station metadata. JSON, XML, CSV or raw text by station, bbox or region.
- Docs: https://aviationweather.gov/data/api/
- Auth: none | Limits: UNKNOWN — no published numeric limit. AWC asks that you not poll faster than the data updates (METARs are hourly, SPECIs are event-driven).
- Latency: hourly, with off-cycle SPECI observations on significant change | Format: REST JSON / XML / CSV / raw text
- Relevance: USEFUL. Airport METARs are the observation of record for many station-based contracts (most US climate sites ARE airport ASOS stations), and this is the cleanest free decoded METAR feed. Verified live: https://aviationweather.gov/api/data/metar?ids=KJFK&format=json returned 200.

**NOAA NDBC buoys + NOAA CO-OPS Tides and Currents API** — NOAA National Data Buoy Center / NOS CO-OPS `LIVE`

- NDBC: realtime and historical wind, wave height/period/direction, air and sea surface temperature, pressure from ~1,300 moored buoys and coastal stations, as plain text per station and multi-decade historical archives. CO-OPS: observed and predicted water level, storm surge, currents, water temperature and meteorological data at 200+ tide stations, plus datums.
- Docs: https://api.tidesandcurrents.noaa.gov/api/prod/
- Auth: none | Limits: CO-OPS: no published call limit, but a single request is capped by product (e.g. 31 days for 6-minute water level, 1 year for hourly). NDBC: no published limit on the static text files. Exact throttles UNKNOWN for both.
- Latency: NDBC hourly (some buoys 10-minutely); CO-OPS 6-minutely | Format: NDBC fixed-width text / NetCDF; CO-OPS REST JSON/XML/CSV
- Relevance: USEFUL for hurricane contracts specifically — storm surge height at a named tide gauge is a settleable quantity, and buoy SST in the Main Development Region is a leading indicator for intensity. Verified live: NDBC 41001 realtime text and the CO-OPS datagetter for station 8518750 (The Battery, NYC) both returned 200.

**OpenAQ API v3** — OpenAQ (nonprofit) `LIVE`

- Aggregated ground-level air quality measurements from ~15,000 government reference monitors and low-cost sensors in 100+ countries: PM2.5, PM10, O3, NO2, SO2, CO, BC, with location, sensor and instrument metadata and a full historical archive.
- Docs: https://docs.openaq.org/
- Auth: free API key from registration, sent as X-API-Key header (v3 requires it; the old keyless v2 is retired) | Limits: 60 requests per minute and 2,000 requests per hour on the free plan (published on the rate-limits page). Repeated violation can lead to permanent suspension.
- Latency: hourly (varies by source network) | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: USEFUL for AQI-exceedance contracts outside the US and for the panel's air-quality layer. Verified live: https://api.openaq.org/v3/parameters returned 401 without a key, confirming the service is up and gated.

**EPA AirNow API** — US EPA / AirNow program `LIVE`

- Official US AQI: current observations and forecasts by ZIP code or lat/lon, historical observations, and AQI contour GIS files. This is the AQI number US media and regulators quote.
- Docs: https://docs.airnowapi.org/
- Auth: free API key by registration | Limits: 500 requests per hour per API key, applied PER API SERVICE — so 500/hr for current-by-ZIP plus 500/hr for current-by-latlon plus 500/hr for forecast-by-ZIP, etc. Limits cannot be raised on request; 429 on exceed.
- Latency: hourly | Format: REST JSON / CSV / XML
- Relevance: USEFUL and it is the SETTLEMENT source for any US AQI contract — AirNow's official AQI is not the same number OpenAQ or a raw PM2.5 feed would give you, because of EPA's NowCast averaging. Verified live: unauthenticated call returned 401.

**NOAA CPC long-range and seasonal outlooks (+ ENSO / ONI)** — NOAA Climate Prediction Center `LIVE`

- 6-10 day, 8-14 day, monthly and seasonal (3-month) probabilistic temperature and precipitation outlooks for the US as probability-of-above/below/near-normal, published as GIS shapefiles and gridded text; plus the official ENSO diagnostic discussion, weekly Niño region SST anomalies, and the Oceanic Niño Index table.
- Docs: https://www.cpc.ncep.noaa.gov/products/predictions/long_range/
- Auth: none | Limits: UNKNOWN — static file server (ftp.cpc.ncep.noaa.gov over HTTPS), no published limit.
- Latency: 6-10/8-14 day daily; monthly outlook mid-month and end-of-month; seasonal on the 3rd Thursday; ONI monthly | Format: shapefile, GeoTIFF, fixed-width text, GRIB
- Relevance: USEFUL and it is the settlement authority for ENSO-state contracts (ONI threshold crossings) and the reference for US monthly/seasonal anomaly contracts. CPC's stated probabilities are directly comparable to market implied probabilities — an immediate edge calculation. Verified live: the long_range product page and https://ftp.cpc.ncep.noaa.gov/GIS/us_tempprcpfcst/ both returned 200.

**NSIDC Sea Ice Index (G02135) and Sea Ice Concentration CDR** — NSIDC / NOAA@NSIDC `LIVE`

- Daily and monthly Arctic and Antarctic sea ice extent and area in a plain CSV going back to November 1978, plus gridded concentration fields, anomaly and trend products, and the AMSR2-based daily concentration source files.
- Docs: https://nsidc.org/data/g02135/versions/4
- Auth: none for the HTTPS file tree (some NSIDC DAAC products require a free Earthdata Login; G02135 does not) | Limits: UNKNOWN — static file server, no published limit. One file covers the entire record, so one fetch per day is enough.
- Latency: daily, roughly 1-2 day lag | Format: CSV, GeoTIFF, NetCDF, shapefile; also s3://noaa-cdr-sea-ice-concentration-pds
- Relevance: USEFUL and it is the SETTLEMENT source for Arctic sea ice minimum/maximum extent contracts — there is no competing authority. Verified live: https://noaadata.apps.nsidc.org/NOAA/G02135/north/daily/data/N_seaice_extent_daily_v4.0.csv returned 200 with rows through 2026-09-19 (4.708 million km2). WARNING: the v3.0 paths that most tutorials and older code use now 404 — v3 is retired, you must use v4.0.

**US Drought Monitor (+ IEM usdm_bypoint)** — NDMC (Univ. of Nebraska-Lincoln) / USDA / NOAA `LIVE`

- Weekly D0-D4 drought classification polygons for the US with statistics by state, county, climate division and watershed; percent-area-in-category tables; plus a full archive back to 2000. IEM's /api/1/usdm_bypoint.json gives the drought class time series at any lat/lon.
- Docs: https://droughtmonitor.unl.edu/DmData/GISData.aspx
- Auth: none | Limits: UNKNOWN — no published limit on the DM web services or the IEM wrapper.
- Latency: weekly (released Thursday 08:30 ET, valid the preceding Tuesday) | Format: shapefile, GeoJSON, KMZ, CSV statistics; REST JSON via IEM
- Relevance: USEFUL. Drought-coverage contracts settle on the USDM percent-area figures directly, and the weekly cadence with a known release time makes it a clean, tradeable event. Verified live: droughtmonitor.unl.edu GIS data page returned 200; IEM's usdm_bypoint endpoint responded (422 for a missing required param, confirming it is live and correctly validating).

**USDA NRCS SNOTEL / AWDB REST API** — USDA Natural Resources Conservation Service `LIVE`

- Daily and hourly snow water equivalent, snow depth, precipitation accumulation, soil moisture and temperature from ~900 automated SNOTEL and SCAN stations across the western US, with multi-decade history and percent-of-median comparisons.
- Docs: https://wcc.sc.egov.usda.gov/awdbRestApi/swagger-ui/index.html
- Auth: none | Limits: UNKNOWN — no published limit on the AWDB REST API.
- Latency: daily, with hourly sensor data available | Format: REST JSON (OpenAPI/Swagger documented)
- Relevance: USEFUL for Western US snowpack and water-year contracts, and for seasonal snowfall contracts in mountain markets. SWE percent-of-median is the standard settlement quantity. Verified live: both the Swagger UI and a real station query (stationTriplets=302:OR:SNTL) returned 200.

**NASA POWER API** — NASA Langley Research Center `LIVE`

- Global solar irradiance and meteorology from satellite and MERRA-2 reanalysis, 1981-present, at daily/monthly/hourly/climatology temporal resolution for any point or region: temperature, precipitation, humidity, wind at multiple heights, all-sky and clear-sky irradiance components.
- Docs: https://power.larc.nasa.gov/docs/services/api/
- Auth: none | Limits: UNKNOWN — no published numeric limit. POWER asks heavy users to use the regional/bulk download services rather than looping point queries.
- Latency: daily (roughly 2-3 month lag for the full-quality product; a near-realtime variant lags ~1 week) | Format: REST JSON / CSV / NetCDF / ASCII
- Relevance: USEFUL for solar-generation-adjacent weather contracts and as a second independent climatology in regions where station coverage is thin. The lag rules it out for anything near-term. Verified live: a real daily T2M query for 40N/74W returned 200.

**Google DeepMind WeatherNext (BigQuery public dataset + Earth Engine)** — Google DeepMind / Google Cloud `LIVE`

- ML-model global forecasts — WeatherNext Graph (deterministic) and WeatherNext Gen (probabilistic ensemble) — published as analysis-ready datasets on BigQuery and Earth Engine, plus the ARCO-ERA5 Zarr store that they train and verify against.
- Docs: https://github.com/google-deepmind/weathernext
- Auth: Google Cloud account required. The datasets themselves are free/public, but BigQuery query bytes and Earth Engine compute are billed beyond the free allowance. | Limits: BigQuery free tier: 1 TiB of query processing per month plus 10 GiB storage, then billed. Earth Engine: free for research/education/nonprofit use only; commercial use requires a paid plan. The datasets carry no separate quota. So: free for evaluation, NOT free for a commercial terminal at volume.
- Latency: daily (matches the model's operational cadence) | Format: BigQuery tables, Earth Engine ImageCollections, Zarr on GCS
- Relevance: USEFUL. ML models now beat IFS on several headline scores, and having a second independent ML family alongside ECMWF's AIFS genuinely widens your model spread. The billing model means this is a research input, not a polling source. Verified live: both the Earth Engine catalog page and the BigQuery marketplace listing returned 200; the GitHub repo is at 7,684 stars with a 2026-09-04 push.

**IBTrACS — International Best Track Archive for Climate Stewardship** — NOAA NCEI / WMO `LIVE`

- The consolidated global tropical cyclone best-track database: every named storm in every basin since 1842, merged from all RSMC agencies, with 3-hourly/6-hourly position, intensity, pressure, radii and landfall flags. Available as CSV, NetCDF and shapefile, split by basin, by period, or 'last 3 years' for currency.
- Docs: https://www.ncei.noaa.gov/products/international-best-track-archive
- Auth: none | Limits: UNKNOWN — static file server, no published limit. One download covers the whole archive.
- Latency: weekly to monthly updates; not a realtime feed | Format: CSV / NetCDF / shapefile
- Relevance: USEFUL — this is the climatological base rate for every hurricane contract. 'How often has a Cat 3+ made landfall in Florida in September?' is answered here and nowhere else as cleanly. Pair with NHC for the live storm and IBTrACS for the prior. Verified live: the NCEI v04r01 CSV access directory returned 200.

#### NICHE

**Met Office Weather DataHub (UK)** — UK Met Office `LIVE`

- Site-specific blended probabilistic point forecasts (hourly/three-hourly/daily), atmospheric model data (UKV, MO Global), observations, and map imagery.
- Docs: https://datahub.metoffice.gov.uk/docs/getting-started
- Auth: free registration required; API key + client credentials | Limits: 55 calls per day on the free Site-Specific plan (quoted verbatim from the pricing page: 'Up to 55 calls per day'). Daily limits reset at 00:00 UTC. Atmospheric-model and observations products have separate plans with their own free allowances — those specific numbers UNKNOWN.
- Latency: hourly for site-specific; model data on cycle | Format: REST JSON, plus GRIB/NetCDF for atmospheric products
- Relevance: NICHE despite being the UK's national service. 55 calls/day cannot support polling even a handful of cities several times a day. Use Open-Meteo's /v1/ukmo endpoint for UKMO model data instead — same underlying model, 10,000 calls/day. Verified live: unauthenticated call to data.hub.api.metoffice.gov.uk returned 401 (service up, key required).

**OpenWeatherMap (Free Access APIs + One Call 3.0)** — OpenWeather Ltd (UK) `LIVE`

- Current weather, 5-day/3-hour forecast, air pollution, geocoding and weather map tiles on the keyless-tier product set; One Call 3.0 adds minutely precipitation for 1 hour, hourly for 48h, daily for 8 days, government alerts, and 45+ years of historical time-machine data.
- Docs: https://openweathermap.org/api
- Auth: free API key by registration for the classic Free tier; One Call 3.0 additionally requires a payment card on file | Limits: Classic Free APIs (current weather, 3-hour forecast, air pollution, maps, geocoding): 60 calls/minute and up to 1,000,000 calls/month, no credit card. One Call API 3.0: 1,000 calls/day included free BUT a payment card is mandatory and calls beyond 1,000/day are billed automatically — set the cap in your account or you will be charged.
- Latency: ~10 minutes for current conditions; hourly forecasts | Format: REST JSON / XML
- Relevance: NICHE for pricing. Huge call allowance, but the underlying forecast is a proprietary blend you cannot decompose, there is no ensemble, and no model attribution — so it cannot contribute to model spread. Fine as a redundancy check or for the panel's 'current conditions' tile.

**WeatherAPI.com** — WeatherAPI.com `LIVE`

- Realtime, forecast, history, future (300 days ahead), marine, air quality, astronomy, timezone, sports-fixture weather, IP lookup and bulk request endpoints through one consistent JSON interface.
- Docs: https://www.weatherapi.com/docs/
- Auth: free API key by registration | Limits: 100,000 calls per month. Forecast capped at 3 days. History limited to 'Past 1 days' only. No marine, no pollen, no air-quality history, no bulk requests, no sports history on free. 95.5% uptime SLA. Free use requires a visible link back to WeatherAPI.com.
- Latency: ~15 minutes for realtime | Format: REST JSON / XML
- Relevance: NICHE. The call allowance is generous but the 1-day history ceiling makes backtesting impossible, and a 3-day forecast horizon misses most of the contract window. Its one genuinely distinctive free feature is the sports-fixture weather endpoint, which maps football/cricket/golf fixtures to forecasts — directly relevant if you price weather-delay contracts on scheduled events.

**Tomorrow.io Weather API** — Tomorrow.io `LIVE`

- Realtime, forecast (timelines) and historical endpoints with an unusually wide variable set — road risk, pollen index (US included), fire index, flood index, 80+ proprietary data layers — plus event-based alerting.
- Docs: https://docs.tomorrow.io/reference/welcome
- Auth: free API key by registration | Limits: Widely reported as 500 requests/day, 25 requests/hour, 3 requests/second on the free plan. CAVEAT: I could NOT verify this against the official source — support.tomorrow.io's 'Free API Plan Rate Limits' article is behind a Cloudflare JS challenge and returned 403/blocked on every attempt, and docs.tomorrow.io/reference/rate-limiting states only 'According to your plan, you are limited to a certain amount of requests per hour and day' without numbers. Treat the specific figures as UNVERIFIED secondary-source.
- Latency: minutely for nowcast; hourly for forecast | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: NICHE. 25 requests/hour is too tight to poll a portfolio of cities. Its one real draw is US pollen index, which no other free feed here provides (Open-Meteo's pollen is Europe-only). Worth a key purely for that one variable.

#### Repos

- `blaylockbk/Herbie` — 790 stars, pushed 2026-09-20. Python library that finds and downloads NWP output (HRRR, RAP, GFS, GEFS, NBM, IFS, AIFS, RRFS, NAM, GDPS) from whichever mirror has it — NOMADS, AWS, Google Cloud, Azure, ECMWF — and hands you an xarray Dataset. · The single highest-leverage repo in this domain. It already solves the two hard problems: knowing each model's S3 key layout (which is undocumented and inconsistent), and doing GRIB byte-range reads so you fetch one variable's 40KB instead of the 400MB file. Actively maintained as of today. Build the model-ingest layer on this rather than writing S3 paths by hand.
- `ecmwf/ecmwf-opendata` — 338 stars, pushed 2026-07-30. ECMWF's own official Python client for the free 0.25-degree open data feed. · Handles the IFS/AIFS dissemination filename grammar and the rolling-archive availability check. Since ECMWF only retains ~12 runs (2-3 days), you need a reliable poller that knows the instant a run lands — this is it.
- `ecmwf/cfgrib` — 463 stars, pushed 2026-07-08. Maps GRIB files into the NetCDF/CF data model so xarray can open them directly (engine='cfgrib'). · Unavoidable dependency. Every free NWP feed in this catalog ships GRIB2 and nothing else. Pair with ecmwf/eccodes-python (137 stars) for the low-level decoder.
- `google-research/arco-era5` — 504 stars, pushed 2026-09-17. Recipes and public Zarr stores for Analysis-Ready Cloud-Optimized ERA5 on Google Cloud Storage. · The escape hatch from the Copernicus CDS download queue. ERA5 as Zarr means you slice a single point's 85-year hourly series in seconds instead of submitting a job and waiting hours. This is how you build station climatologies at scale.
- `google-deepmind/weathernext` — 7,684 stars, pushed 2026-09-04. DeepMind's WeatherNext Graph and WeatherNext Gen model releases with data access instructions for BigQuery and Earth Engine. · Gives you a second independent ML forecast family alongside ECMWF's AIFS. Two uncorrelated ML models plus the physics models is a materially wider and better-calibrated spread than physics models alone.
- `ecmwf-lab/ai-models` — 592 stars, pushed 2026-08-06. Runs published AI weather models (GraphCast, Pangu-Weather, FourCastNet, AIFS) against ECMWF open data as initial conditions. · Lets you generate your OWN forecasts from free open data on a GPU, rather than only consuming someone else's. That is the only route to a forecast the market has not already priced in.
- `earthobservations/wetterdienst` — 455 stars, pushed 2026-09-20. 'Open weather data for humans' — unified Python client across DWD, NOAA GHCN, Environment Canada, ECCC, EA (UK), IMGW (PL), NWS, WSV and more. · Actively maintained today, and it has already done the provider-by-provider station-identifier and unit reconciliation that is the tedious 80% of any multi-source weather ingest. Read its provider adapters even if you do not use the library.
- `meteostat/meteostat` — 664 stars, pushed 2026-09-17. Official Python library for Meteostat's consolidated station history (hourly/daily/monthly/normals). · Reads the free bulk endpoints directly, sidestepping the 500-calls-per-month RapidAPI ceiling entirely. Its station-matching and gap-filling logic against GHCN/ISD/DWD is worth reading on its own.
- `Unidata/MetPy` — 1,442 stars, pushed 2026-09-14. The reference Python toolkit for meteorological calculation, unit handling and plotting. · Correct, unit-aware implementations of every derived quantity you will need — dewpoint, wet bulb, heat index, wind chill, CAPE, degree days. Getting heat index or wet-bulb wrong by hand is a real and common source of mispricing.
- `Unidata/siphon` — 246 stars, pushed 2026-09-14. Client for THREDDS/OPeNDAP catalogs, the NWS NDFD/NDBC/radar services, and the Wyoming and IGRA upper-air archives. · The clean route into THREDDS-served archives that have no REST API, including historical radiosonde soundings that no commercial API exposes.
- `tropycal/tropycal` — 173 stars, pushed 2026-08-13. Python package for retrieving and analyzing tropical cyclone data. · Wraps HURDAT2, IBTrACS and live NHC products behind one interface with built-in ACE calculation, landfall detection, track climatology and recon data. If you price hurricane contracts, this saves weeks — do not reimplement best-track parsing.
- `google/weather-tools` — 252 stars, pushed 2026-09-10. Google's 'weather-dl' / 'weather-mv' pipeline tools for downloading from ECMWF/Copernicus and loading into BigQuery or Earth Engine at scale. · Production-grade Apache Beam pipelines for the exact ingest problem a terminal has — continuous multi-source NWP into a queryable store. Steal the architecture even if you do not run Beam.
- `blaylockbk/goes2go` — 260 stars, pushed 2026-06-17. Downloads and processes GOES-16/17/18/19 ABI and GLM data from the AWS archive. · Handles the GOES S3 naming scheme and the RGB composite recipes. The GLM path is your free realtime lightning source now that Blitzortung's API is gone.
- `pySTEPS/pysteps` — 587 stars, pushed 2026-09-15. Framework for probabilistic precipitation nowcasting from radar, using optical-flow extrapolation and stochastic ensemble generation. · Turns a MRMS or RainViewer radar sequence into a probabilistic 0-6 hour precipitation forecast. That is the horizon where NWP is worst and where same-day precipitation contracts actually trade — a genuine edge if you run it.
- `ARM-DOE/pyart` — 601 stars, pushed 2026-09-17. The Python ARM Radar Toolkit — reads NEXRAD Level II/III, gridding, QC, dealiasing. · The only practical way to read raw NEXRAD Level II. Also worth noting: its NEXRAD-on-S3 access helpers work around the fact that anonymous bucket listing is denied (see deadEnds).
- `pytroll/satpy` — 1,207 stars, pushed 2026-09-18. Reads, calibrates and composites data from 100+ earth-observing satellite instruments. · If you need EUMETSAT/Meteosat or Himawari alongside GOES for non-US basins, satpy is the only library that normalizes across all of them.
- `open-meteo/open-meteo` — 6,223 stars, pushed 2026-09-20. The complete server implementation of the Open-Meteo API, in Swift, under AGPL. · You can self-host it. That removes the 10,000-calls/day cap and the non-commercial licence restriction in one move — which matters enormously if Open-Meteo is your backbone and you intend to run this commercially. Read open-meteo/open-data (172 stars) for the companion S3 layout.
- `awslabs/open-data-registry` — 1,784 stars, pushed 2026-09-18. The machine-readable YAML registry behind registry.opendata.aws. · Grep the YAML for 'weather', 'climate', 'atmospheric', 'NOAA' and you get a complete, current, structured inventory of every free weather bucket on AWS with its region, licence and example usage. This is the fastest way to find feeds nobody has written a blog post about.
- `pangeo-data/awesome-open-climate-science` — 598 stars. Curated index of open atmospheric, ocean and climate science software and data. · The domain-specific catalog for this vertical, far denser than the general public-apis lists. Start discovery here rather than in public-apis/public-apis, which carries maybe eight weather entries and several dead ones.
- `python-metar/python-metar` — 304 stars, pushed 2026-09-16. Parses coded METAR reports into structured objects. · METAR is a 1960s fixed-width format with real parsing traps (trace precipitation, variable wind groups, remarks section where the 6-hour max/min temps actually live). Since many contracts settle on ASOS station values, correct METAR remarks parsing is load-bearing. See also avwx-rest/avwx-engine (123 stars) for METAR + TAF.
- `paulokuong/noaa` — 256 stars, pushed 2026-04-13. Python SDK for the NOAA/NWS api.weather.gov service. · Handles the mandatory User-Agent requirement and the points-to-gridpoint indirection that trips up every first attempt against api.weather.gov.
- `ecmwf/earthkit-data` — 120 stars, pushed 2026-09-18. Format-agnostic Python interface over GRIB, NetCDF, BUFR, ODB and CSV geospatial data. · ECMWF's successor to the older ad-hoc readers. Gives you one access pattern across GRIB from NOAA and NetCDF from Copernicus, which removes a whole class of format-branching from your ingest code.
- `visualcrossing/WeatherApi` — 55 stars, pushed 2026-09-09. Vendor sample code for the Visual Crossing Timeline API. · Worth reading specifically for their record-costing examples — the free tier is metered in 'records', not calls, and it is easy to burn 1,000 records in three careless queries.
