### Natural Disasters & Geophysical Hazards

#### CORE

**USGS Earthquake Catalog (FDSN Event / ComCat)** — U.S. Geological Survey / ANSS `LIVE`

- Authoritative global earthquake catalog: origin time, lat/lon, depth, magnitude + magnitude type, network, event ID, felt reports, alert level, significance. Query by time, bbox, radius, depth, magnitude range. Also serves scenario catalog at /fdsnws/scenario/1/.
- Docs: https://earthquake.usgs.gov/fdsnws/event/1/
- Base: `https://earthquake.usgs.gov/fdsnws/event/1/query`
- Auth: none | Limits: Max 20,000 events per request (limit param 1–20000; exceeding returns HTTP 400). Default time window = NOW-30 days if unspecified. No published rate limit — UNKNOWN. Catalog depth: no documented maximum; ANSS ComCat goes back to historic events (1900s), full modern coverage from ~1970s.
- Latency: sub-minute for US events, typically 1–20 min globally depending on network review | Format: REST JSON (GeoJSON), QuakeML XML, CSV, KML, plain text
- Relevance: THE settlement source for essentially every earthquake-magnitude contract on Kalshi (e.g. KXEARTHQUAKECALIFORNIA resolves on USGS epicenter + magnitude). Direct, unambiguous resolution feed. Note magnitude is revised post-event — you must poll for updates, not snapshot once.

**USGS Real-time Earthquake GeoJSON Summary Feeds** — U.S. Geological Survey `LIVE`

- Pre-baked rolling summary feeds at fixed URLs: significant/M4.5+/M2.5+/M1.0+/all, over past hour / day / week / month. 24 files total. Cheap to poll — no query construction, CDN-cached.
- Docs: https://earthquake.usgs.gov/earthquakes/feed/v1.0/
- Base: `https://earthquake.usgs.gov/earthquakes/feed/v1.0/summary/significant_week.geojson`
- Auth: none | Limits: No documented call limit — UNKNOWN. Files update approximately every 1 minute (USGS asks you not to poll faster than once per minute). History depth fixed by feed name: max 30 days.
- Latency: sub-minute (files regenerated ~1/min) | Format: REST JSON (GeoJSON), CSV, Atom/RSS, KML
- Relevance: The polling backbone for live earthquake contracts. Use these for the tick loop and the full FDSN query API for backfill/base rates. significant_*.geojson is the low-noise trigger stream.

**USGS Event Detail Products — ShakeMap, PAGER, DYFI, Ground Failure, Moment Tensor** — U.S. Geological Survey `LIVE`

- Per-event derived products reached via the 'detail' URL on any ComCat event: ShakeMap (PGA/PGV/MMI grids + contours), losspager (fatality and economic-loss probability brackets, green/yellow/orange/red), dyfi (Did You Feel It crowd-sourced intensity), ground-failure (landslide + liquefaction probability), moment-tensor. Verified on event us7000tiqc (M6.4 Papua New Guinea): products = dyfi, ground-failure, losspager, moment-tensor, origin, phase-data, shakemap.
- Docs: https://earthquake.usgs.gov/data/comcat/
- Base: `https://earthquake.usgs.gov/earthquakes/feed/v1.0/detail/{eventid}.geojson`
- Auth: none | Limits: No documented rate limit — UNKNOWN. Product files (grid.xml, cont_mi.json, GeoJSON contours) served from static CDN paths. Retained for full catalog history where computed.
- Latency: ShakeMap ~5–15 min after event, revised repeatedly for hours–days; PAGER within ~30 min | Format: REST JSON + per-product GeoJSON/XML/GeoTIFF downloads
- Relevance: Prices anything intensity- or damage-based rather than magnitude-based: 'will MMI reach VIII in county X', PAGER loss-bracket contracts, and post-quake insured-loss markets. ShakeMap is the only free authoritative shaking-intensity grid.

**EMSC SeismicPortal FDSN Event Service** — European-Mediterranean Seismological Centre (EMSC-CSEM) `LIVE`

- Independent global earthquake catalog, strongest in Europe/Mediterranean/Middle East. Often publishes a solution minutes before USGS for Eurasian events. Full FDSN event query surface plus origins and arrivals.
- Docs: https://www.seismicportal.eu/fdsn-wsevent.html
- Base: `https://www.seismicportal.eu/fdsnws/event/1/query`
- Auth: none | Limits: Max 20,000 events per request (raised from 1,000 in March 2023). No published call-rate limit — UNKNOWN. History depth UNKNOWN from docs; catalog covers modern instrumental era.
- Latency: sub-minute to a few minutes | Format: REST JSON, QuakeML XML, CSV/text
- Relevance: Second independent opinion on magnitude for non-US quakes. Critical for disagreement detection: if EMSC says M6.9 and USGS says M6.4, a magnitude-threshold contract is mispriced by whoever is watching only one source. Licensed CC-BY 4.0.

**EMSC SeismicPortal WebSocket (standing order)** — European-Mediterranean Seismological Centre `LIVE`

- Push stream of new and updated earthquake events as JSON messages — no polling. Includes revision events (action: update) so you see magnitude revisions the moment they land.
- Docs: https://www.seismicportal.eu/realtime.html
- Base: `wss://www.seismicportal.eu/standing_order/websocket`
- Auth: none | Limits: No documented connection or message limit — UNKNOWN. No history — live stream only; pair with the FDSN service for backfill.
- Latency: realtime/websocket | Format: WebSocket
- Relevance: Lowest-latency free global earthquake trigger available. For magnitude-threshold contracts, latency IS the edge — this beats polling USGS GeoJSON by tens of seconds on Eurasian events.

**NOAA NHC Tropical Cyclone Status JSON (CurrentStorms.json)** — NOAA National Hurricane Center `LIVE`

- Static-URL JSON listing every active Atlantic / East Pacific / Central Pacific tropical cyclone: storm ID (e.g. AL062026), name, classification (TD/TS/HU), intensity in kt, min pressure, lat/lon, movement, advisory number, and direct links to every product file for that storm.
- Docs: https://www.nhc.noaa.gov/productexamples/NHC_Tropical_Cyclone_Status_JSON_File_Reference.pdf
- Base: `https://www.nhc.noaa.gov/CurrentStorms.json`
- Auth: none | Limits: No documented rate limit — UNKNOWN. No history (current storms only; file is empty-ish when basin is quiet). Updated on advisory cycle: every 6 h routine, every 3 h intermediate when land threat exists, special advisories any time.
- Latency: 3–6 hourly (advisory-driven), plus special advisories | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: The single highest-value hurricane feed. Kalshi named-storm-count, category-at-landfall, and max-wind contracts all trace to NHC advisories, and this file is the machine-readable index of them. Storm ID + advisory number gives you an exact settlement key.

**NOAA NHC GIS Products (cone, track, wind radii, wind-speed probabilities, storm surge)** — NOAA National Hurricane Center `LIVE`

- Per-advisory geospatial products: 5-day forecast track + cone + watches/warnings (AL062026_5day_latest.zip), initial and forecast wind radii, Wind Speed Probabilities (34/50/64 kt at 120 h, as shapefile AND GRIB1/GRIB2 via ftp.nhc.ncep.noaa.gov/wsp/), arrival time of TS-force winds, Probabilistic Storm Surge (P-Surge, GRIB2), Potential Storm Surge Flooding inundation, storm surge watch/warning polygons, preliminary best track, Graphical Tropical Weather Outlook.
- Docs: https://www.nhc.noaa.gov/gis/index.php
- Base: `https://www.nhc.noaa.gov/gis/`
- Auth: none | Limits: No documented rate limit — UNKNOWN. No registration. Latest-file URLs are stable; per-advisory archive under /gis/archive_* by year. NHC warns support 'may not always be available or timely'.
- Latency: 3–6 hourly on advisory cycle | Format: Shapefile (.zip), KML/KMZ, GRIB1/GRIB2, RSS index feeds per basin
- Relevance: Wind Speed Probabilities is the closest free thing to an official implied probability for landfall/intensity contracts — NHC literally publishes P(64kt winds at point X within 120h). That is a direct market-comparable number for Kalshi landfall markets. P-Surge does the same for surge contracts.

**NHC Data Archive — HURDAT2 best track** — NOAA National Hurricane Center `LIVE`

- Complete post-analysis best track for every Atlantic cyclone 1851–2024 (and a separate NE/NC Pacific file 1949–2024): 6-hourly position, max sustained wind, min pressure, storm type, plus landfall ('L') record identifiers and 34/50/64-kt wind radii from 2004 onward. Verified: 7.03 MB file, current release dated 04/04/25.
- Docs: https://www.nhc.noaa.gov/data/
- Base: `https://www.nhc.noaa.gov/data/hurdat/hurdat2-1851-2024-040425.txt`
- Auth: none | Limits: None — flat text file over HTTPS, no key, no throttle observed. History depth: 1851–2024 (Atlantic), reissued roughly annually after post-season reanalysis.
- Latency: annual (post-season reanalysis) | Format: CSV bulk (comma-delimited fixed schema text)
- Relevance: Base rates. Every 'how many named storms / hurricanes / major hurricanes in 2026' contract needs a climatological prior, and the 'L' landfall flags give you an exact historical landfall frequency per coastline segment. This is how you build the prior your ensemble updates.

**IBTrACS — International Best Track Archive for Climate Stewardship v04r01** — NOAA NCEI / WMO `LIVE`

- Global unified best-track archive merging all WMO RSMC agencies (NHC, JTWC, JMA, IMD, BoM, Meteo-France, etc.) — every tropical cyclone worldwide since 1841, with per-agency wind/pressure so you can see inter-agency disagreement. Verified: last3years CSV = 10.46 MB.
- Docs: https://www.ncei.noaa.gov/products/international-best-track-archive
- Base: `https://www.ncei.noaa.gov/data/international-best-track-archive-for-climate-stewardship-ibtracs/v04r01/access/csv/`
- Auth: none | Limits: None — open HTTPS directory, no key. Slices provided: ALL, last3years, since1980, and per-basin. History depth 1841–present. Updated roughly every 2 weeks (provisional) plus annual reanalysis.
- Latency: biweekly (provisional) to annual (final) | Format: CSV bulk, NetCDF, shapefile
- Relevance: Only free source for West Pacific / Indian Ocean / Southern Hemisphere cyclone base rates — NHC covers only Atlantic + EPac. Essential for any non-Atlantic typhoon contract, and for ACE-index markets in any basin.

**NWS API (api.weather.gov) — Active Alerts / CAP** — NOAA National Weather Service `LIVE`

- Every active US watch, warning, advisory and statement as structured JSON or native CAP XML: event type, severity, certainty, urgency, affected UGC zones/SAME codes, onset/expiry, full text. Covers tornado warnings, hurricane warnings, flash flood emergencies, excessive heat warnings, red flag warnings, tsunami warnings, winter storm warnings — the whole alert taxonomy in one endpoint.
- Docs: https://www.weather.gov/documentation/services-web-api
- Base: `https://api.weather.gov/alerts/active?area=FL`
- Auth: none (User-Agent header REQUIRED and must identify your app, e.g. '(myapp.com, contact@myapp.com)'; NWS states it will be replaced by an API key in future) | Limits: Rate limit exists but is explicitly NOT public — docs say 'reasonable rate limits in place to prevent abuse… allows a generous amount for typical use'. EXACT NUMBER UNKNOWN. /alerts retains the past 7 days only. Note: there is no 'limit' query param — passing one returns HTTP 400.
- Latency: sub-minute (alerts appear as issued) | Format: REST JSON (GeoJSON / JSON-LD), CAP XML via Accept: application/cap+xml, Atom
- Relevance: CORE for tornado, flash-flood, heat and red-flag contracts, and it is the US government's own landfall-adjacent warning record. For hurricane markets the Hurricane Warning polygon issuance is itself tradeable and is here before the NHC GIS shapefile posts.

**NASA FIRMS — Fire Information for Resource Management System** — NASA Earth Science Data / LANCE `LIVE`

- Near-real-time active fire / thermal anomaly detections from MODIS (Terra+Aqua), VIIRS S-NPP, VIIRS NOAA-20, VIIRS NOAA-21, and Landsat (US/Canada only). Per-detection lat/lon, brightness temperature, Fire Radiative Power, confidence, acquisition datetime, day/night flag. Area, country, and bounding-box query modes.
- Docs: https://firms.modaps.eosdis.nasa.gov/api/area/
- Base: `https://firms.modaps.eosdis.nasa.gov/api/area/csv/{MAP_KEY}/VIIRS_SNPP_NRT/{bbox}/{day_range}/{date}`
- Auth: free API key (MAP_KEY) — self-service request, no approval wait | Limits: 5,000 transactions per 10-minute interval per MAP_KEY (large requests consume multiple transaction slots). Max day range documented as 1–5 days per request. Requests without a valid key return HTTP 401 (verified). Archive history depth NOT stated on the API docs page — UNKNOWN; a separate /api/data_availability/ endpoint reports it per sensor.
- Latency: sub-hourly (NRT products ~3 h after overpass; US/Canada URT ~60 s) | Format: REST CSV / JSON, plus WMS/WFS
- Relevance: CORE for wildfire markets, but with a caveat that matters: FIRMS gives you fire DETECTION and radiative power, not acreage. Kalshi/Polymarket wildfire-acreage contracts settle on NIFC/CAL FIRE reported acres. Use FIRMS as the leading indicator (you see a new fire's FRP explode hours before an official acreage update) and NIFC as the settlement source.

**NIFC WFIGS — Wildland Fire Interagency Geospatial Services (ArcGIS FeatureServer)** — National Interagency Fire Center / USDA-USDOI `LIVE`

- The authoritative US wildfire incident record: Incident Locations Current (97 fields, verified — includes IncidentName, DiscoveryAcres, InitialResponseAcres, FinalAcres, PercentContained, FireCause, FireDiscoveryDateTime, IncidentManagementOrganization, poo_state) and Interagency Perimeters Current (fire polygons with GIS-computed acres). Also year-to-date and historical archive layers.
- Docs: https://data-nifc.opendata.arcgis.com/
- Base: `https://services3.arcgis.com/T4QMspbfLg3qTGWY/arcgis/rest/services/WFIGS_Incident_Locations_Current/FeatureServer/0/query`
- Auth: none | Limits: Standard ArcGIS Online public FeatureServer — default max 1,000–2,000 records per query page (use resultOffset to page), supports where/outFields/orderByFields/returnCountOnly. No documented daily call cap — UNKNOWN. History: Current layers = active season; separate archive layers go back to 2020+.
- Latency: sub-hourly to daily (incident-reported, updated as IRWIN records change) | Format: REST JSON (Esri JSON + GeoJSON), OGC via Open Data portal
- Relevance: THE settlement source for US wildfire acreage contracts. 'Will the X Fire exceed N acres' and national season-total acreage markets resolve on NIFC-reported numbers. DailyAcres/FinalAcres are the exact fields to watch. Beware: acreage is revised downward as often as upward when perimeters are re-flown.

**CAL FIRE Incidents API** — California Department of Forestry and Fire Protection `LIVE`

- All CAL FIRE-tracked California incidents by year: incident name, acres burned, containment %, started/updated timestamps, county, lat/lon, structures destroyed/damaged, injuries, fatalities, evacuation status, cooperating agencies.
- Docs: https://www.fire.ca.gov/incidents
- Base: `https://incidents.fire.ca.gov/umbraco/api/IncidentApi/List?year=2026`
- Auth: none | Limits: Undocumented public JSON endpoint — no published rate limit, UNKNOWN. History: year parameter works back to ~2013. No registration.
- Latency: sub-hourly during active incidents | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: California-specific wildfire contracts (a disproportionate share of wildfire market volume) settle on CAL FIRE numbers, which can differ from NIFC for state-responsibility-area fires. Structures-destroyed field prices damage contracts. Unofficial endpoint — treat as scrape-grade reliability.

**GDACS — Global Disaster Alert and Coordination System** — European Commission JRC + UN OCHA `LIVE`

- Unified multi-hazard alert stream with Green/Orange/Red humanitarian-impact scoring across event types EQ (earthquake), TC (tropical cyclone), FL (flood), VO (volcano), DR (drought), WF (wildfire). Each event carries eventid, eventtype, alertlevel, alertscore, episode, name, country, population exposed, and links to per-event impact reports. Verified live with pubDate Sun, 20 Sep 2026.
- Docs: https://www.gdacs.org/Alerts/api.aspx
- Base: `https://www.gdacs.org/gdacsapi/api/events/geteventlist/SEARCH?fromDate=2026-09-15&alertlevel=Orange;Red`
- Auth: none | Limits: No published rate limit — UNKNOWN. No key. RSS file is ~1.2 MB (413 records at time of check) so poll it sparingly. History: SEARCH endpoint accepts fromDate/toDate; archive goes back to ~2004. Event detail via /gdacsapi/api/Events/geteventdata?eventtype=EQ&eventid={id}.
- Latency: sub-hourly (derives from USGS/NHC/GloFAS upstream, adds impact modelling) | Format: REST JSON (GeoJSON), GeoRSS, CAP
- Relevance: The best single free 'is something big happening anywhere on Earth right now' trigger — one poll covers six hazard classes globally with a severity score already attached. Its alertscore is a usable severity prior for humanitarian-impact and disaster-declaration contracts. Not a settlement source; it is a router.

**NOAA SPC — Storm Prediction Center reports, outlooks, and severe GIS archive** — NOAA Storm Prediction Center `LIVE`

- Daily preliminary storm reports CSV (tornado / hail / wind, with time, F/EF-scale estimate, magnitude, lat/lon, county, state, comments) at a date-keyed URL; convective outlook day 1–8 with categorical and probabilistic risk polygons; watch/warning RSS; and the SVRGIS archive of all tornado/hail/wind reports 1950–present as shapefiles.
- Docs: https://www.spc.noaa.gov/climo/reports/
- Base: `https://www.spc.noaa.gov/climo/reports/260919_rpts.csv`
- Auth: none | Limits: No published rate limit — UNKNOWN. Daily report CSVs are date-keyed (YYMMDD_rpts.csv) and available back many years; note today.csv can return 0 bytes early in the UTC day before any reports exist. SVRGIS archive covers 1950–present.
- Latency: sub-hourly during events (preliminary reports), daily finalization | Format: CSV, RSS (spcwwrss.xml), shapefile bulk, KML
- Relevance: CORE for tornado-count markets. The probabilistic day-1 outlook (e.g. 10%/15%/30% tornado probability within 25 mi) is a free official probability you can price directly against a market. Critical caveat: SPC preliminary reports overcount — multiple reports of one tornado — so annual-count contracts settle on NCEI Storm Events final counts, not these.

**ECMWF Open Data (IFS / AIFS open forecasts)** — European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts `LIVE`

- Full open-licensed ECMWF forecast fields at 0.25°: HRES/oper deterministic, ENS ensemble (51 members), and the AIFS machine-learning model. Surface and pressure-level variables including MSLP, 10 m wind, precipitation, 2 m temperature. Verified: directory /forecasts/20260920/00z/ifs/0p25/oper/ listing 481 KB of index files.
- Docs: https://www.ecmwf.int/en/forecasts/datasets/open-data
- Base: `https://data.ecmwf.int/forecasts/`
- Auth: none | Limits: No key, no registration, CC-BY-4.0 licensed. No published request cap — UNKNOWN, but files are large GRIB2 (use the .index sidecar files to byte-range fetch single fields). Retention on the open server is short — roughly the last few days of runs; UNKNOWN exact retention. 4 runs/day (00/06/12/18z).
- Latency: 4x daily, ~7–9 h after run initialization | Format: GRIB2 (with .index sidecars for byte-range access)
- Relevance: This is your model-spread engine. ENS 51-member spread on MSLP and 10 m wind at a landfall point IS the ensemble forecast half of the research panel. ECMWF has the best track-forecast skill of any free global model, so ECMWF-vs-market divergence is the highest-quality edge signal for cyclone contracts.

**NOAA NOMADS — GFS / GEFS / HRRR / NAM GRIB filter** — NOAA NCEP `LIVE`

- Every operational NCEP model: GFS 0.25° deterministic, GEFS 31-member ensemble, HRRR 3 km CONUS rapid refresh, NAM, RTMA, plus the GFS/GEFS tropical cyclone track files (a-decks/b-decks). The cgi-bin filter scripts let you pull a single variable/level/subregion instead of a 400 MB file.
- Docs: https://nomads.ncep.noaa.gov/
- Base: `https://nomads.ncep.noaa.gov/cgi-bin/filter_gfs_0p25.pl`
- Auth: none | Limits: NOAA enforces an abuse throttle on NOMADS — commonly cited as roughly 120 hits/minute per IP with temporary blocking, but this is NOT in formal docs — treat the exact number as UNKNOWN and rate-limit yourself conservatively. Retention on NOMADS is ~10 days; older runs live in NCEI/AWS Open Data S3 buckets (noaa-gfs-bdp-pds) with no limits at all.
- Latency: 4x daily for GFS/GEFS (~3.5–5 h lag), hourly for HRRR | Format: GRIB2 via filter CGI, OPeNDAP, plus full mirror on AWS S3
- Relevance: GEFS gives a second independent ensemble to compare against ECMWF ENS — the disagreement between the two IS the model spread number the research panel should display. The a-deck files contain every model's tropical cyclone track guess, which is exactly the 'spaghetti model' input for landfall markets.

**Open-Meteo (forecast, ensemble, historical archive, flood)** — Open-Meteo (open source, Zurich) `LIVE`

- Normalized JSON over many NWP models without touching GRIB. Four endpoints all verified working with no key: /v1/forecast (multi-model), ensemble-api /v1/ensemble (GFS/ICON/ECMWF member-level output — the model-spread number, precomputed), archive-api /v1/archive (ERA5 reanalysis 1940–present), and flood-api /v1/flood (GloFAS river discharge forecast + historical, by lat/lon).
- Docs: https://open-meteo.com/en/docs
- Base: `https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast`
- Auth: none for the free tier | Limits: EXACT: 600 calls/minute, 5,000 calls/hour, 10,000 calls/day, 300,000 calls/month. NON-COMMERCIAL USE ONLY — a paid subscription is what grants a commercial-use licence. Archive history: ERA5 from 1940. I verified archive-api, ensemble-api and flood-api all return HTTP 200 with no key, so the pricing page's tier table does not gate them technically — but the non-commercial licence still applies.
- Latency: hourly updates; ensemble 4x daily | Format: REST JSON (also CSV, FlatBuffers, Parquet)
- Relevance: The fastest way to stand up ensemble spread and station-level history without a GRIB pipeline — it directly serves 'ensemble forecast + model spread + that station's historical error' for temperature and wind contracts. LICENSING WARNING: a prediction-market product is commercial, so the free tier does not cover you. Prototype on it, then either pay or move to raw ECMWF/NOMADS (both of which are licence-clean for commercial use).

**Iowa Environmental Mesonet (IEM) — NWS warning & Local Storm Report archive** — Iowa State University Department of Agronomy `LIVE`

- The complete searchable archive of every NWS warning polygon ever issued (2002–present) with issuance/expiry, plus Local Storm Reports (LSR) in GeoJSON, plus ASOS/AWOS station archives, plus NEXRAD composites. Verified: /geojson/lsr.py 28 KB of last-6-hours reports; /cgi-bin/request/gis/watchwarn.py help page 34 KB.
- Docs: https://mesonet.agron.iastate.edu/api/1/docs
- Base: `https://mesonet.agron.iastate.edu/geojson/lsr.py?inc_ap=no&hours=6`
- Auth: none | Limits: No key. IEM asks that heavy users throttle and identify themselves; no published numeric cap — UNKNOWN. Warning archive depth: 2002–present for polygon warnings, earlier for county-based. Bulk shapefile/CSV downloads available for arbitrary date ranges.
- Latency: sub-hourly (LSR near-real-time); archive continuously backfilled | Format: REST JSON/GeoJSON, CSV, shapefile bulk, Excel
- Relevance: api.weather.gov keeps only 7 days of alerts — IEM keeps 20+ years. This is how you compute 'how often has a tornado warning been issued in county X in September' — the historical-error and base-rate half of the research panel for every US severe-weather contract. Effectively irreplaceable and free.

**NOAA NCEI Storm Events Database (bulk CSV)** — NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information `LIVE`

- The official, quality-controlled US severe weather event record 1950–present: tornado (with final EF rating, path length/width, fatalities), hail, wind, flood, flash flood, excessive heat, winter storm, wildfire, and ~50 other event types, with damage estimates in dollars. Three file families per year: details, fatalities, locations. Verified: directory listing 53 KB.
- Docs: https://www.ncei.noaa.gov/stormevents/
- Base: `https://www.ncei.noaa.gov/pub/data/swdi/stormevents/csvfiles/`
- Auth: none | Limits: None — open HTTPS directory of gzipped CSVs, no key, no throttle observed. History: 1950–present (tornado only 1950–1954, all types from 1996). Lag: final data typically 3–4 months behind present.
- Latency: monthly | Format: CSV bulk (gzipped)
- Relevance: This is the settlement source for annual US tornado-count contracts — NOT the SPC preliminary reports, which overcount. The 3–4 month publication lag is itself tradeable information: a market settling on NCEI counts cannot resolve until NCEI publishes, and the gap between SPC preliminary and NCEI final is systematic and estimable.

#### USEFUL

**Smithsonian Global Volcanism Program — GeoServer WFS + Weekly Volcanic Activity Report** — Smithsonian Institution / USGS `LIVE`

- The canonical global volcano database: Holocene and Pleistocene volcano inventory, eruption history with VEI, and the joint Smithsonian/USGS Weekly Volcanic Activity Report. Verified WFS GetCapabilities (107 KB) and a GetFeature JSON query; weekly RSS confirmed carrying 10–16 September 2026 reports for Krakatau, Aira, Dukono, Great Sitkin, Ibu.

Eruption history depth: Holocene (~12,000 years) with VEI assigned where known. IMPORTANT: volcano.si.edu/api returns HTTP 403 to non-browser clients — use the webservices.volcano.si.edu GeoServer host instead.
- Latency: weekly (activity report); database updated continuously | Format: WFS (GeoJSON/GML), RSS, CSV export
- Relevance: The eruption-history table with VEI is the only free source for volcano base rates — essential for pricing 'will volcano X erupt by date Y'. The weekly report is the accepted narrative record of new eruptive activity. Pair with USGS HANS for US real-time alert-level changes, since weekly cadence is too slow to trade on alone.

**USGS Volcano Hazards HANS API (elevated volcanoes / alert levels)** — USGS Volcano Hazards Program `LIVE`

- Current US volcano alert level (NORMAL / ADVISORY / WATCH / WARNING) and aviation color code (GREEN/YELLOW/ORANGE/RED) for every US volcano currently above normal, plus Volcanic Activity Notices and observatory status reports. Covers AVO (Alaska), CVO (Cascades), HVO (Hawaii), YVO (Yellowstone), CalVO.
