- Auth: none | Limits: Public undocumented JSON API — no published limit, UNKNOWN. Companion endpoints: getVolcanoesWithNotices, getVanNotices. Small responses (~2.6 KB). History depth UNKNOWN for the notices endpoint.
- Latency: sub-hourly (updated whenever an observatory changes status) | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: Alert-level and aviation-color-code escalation is itself a clean, objectively-resolvable contract (Kilauea, Great Sitkin, Mount Spurr). This is the only free real-time machine-readable US volcano status feed; the Smithsonian weekly report lags it by up to 7 days.

**NOAA Tsunami Warning Centers — PTWC / NTWC Atom + CAP feeds** — NOAA / National Tsunami Warning Center + Pacific Tsunami Warning Center `LIVE`

- Per-center Atom feeds of tsunami messages: Information Statement, Advisory, Watch, Warning — with event magnitude, epicenter, affected coastlines, and forecast arrival times at named locations. Verified PAAQAtom (NTWC, Alaska/US West Coast/Canada — carrying 'Tsunami Information Statement Number 1, 45 miles NE of Amukta Pass, Alaska') and PHEBAtom (PTWC Caribbean — 'VICINITY OF PUERTO RICO').
- Docs: https://www.tsunami.gov/
- Base: `https://www.tsunami.gov/events/xml/PAAQAtom.xml`
- Auth: none | Limits: No published rate limit — UNKNOWN. Small files (~2 KB). Feeds carry only the current/most recent event set; directory listing at /events/xml/ is 403 so you must know the feed code (PAAQ = NTWC, PHEB = PTWC Caribbean, PHEB/WEAK variants, WEPA/WEHW = Pacific). History depth on the feed is effectively nil — archive separately.
- Latency: sub-minute after a qualifying earthquake | Format: Atom XML, CAP XML
- Relevance: Tsunami warning ISSUANCE is directly tradeable and is a fast second-order signal on large offshore earthquakes — a PTWC warning within minutes of an M7.5 tells you the magnitude estimate will likely hold or rise. Also settles 'will a tsunami warning be issued for X' contracts.

**NASA EONET — Earth Observatory Natural Event Tracker** — NASA Earth Observatory / GSFC `LIVE`

- Curated global natural-event index with stable event IDs, categories (wildfires, severe storms, volcanoes, floods, drought, dust/haze, earthquakes, landslides, sea/lake ice, snow, temperature extremes, manmade, water color), geometry track over time, and source links back to the originating agency.
- Docs: https://eonet.gsfc.nasa.gov/docs/v3
- Base: `https://eonet.gsfc.nasa.gov/api/v3/events?limit=1`
- Auth: none | Limits: No published rate limit — UNKNOWN. No key. Supports limit, days, start/end, status (open/closed), category, source, bbox, magnitude filters. History depth: events back to 2015 for most categories.
- Latency: daily (curated, not real-time) | Format: REST JSON (GeoJSON), also GeoJSON/KML layers
- Relevance: USEFUL as a cross-hazard event spine for joining a market to a canonical event ID across sources — EONET carries the same event with pointers to USGS, GDACS, InciWeb, etc. Too slow and too curated to be a trading trigger; use it as the entity-resolution layer, not the tick source.

**USGS Water Services (NWIS Instantaneous Values)** — U.S. Geological Survey Water Resources `LIVE`

- Real-time gauge height and discharge from ~11,000 US stream gauges, at 15-minute resolution, plus daily values and full historical statistics. Parameter codes 00060 (discharge cfs) and 00065 (gage height ft).
- Docs: https://waterservices.usgs.gov/docs/instantaneous-values/
- Base: `https://waterservices.usgs.gov/nwis/iv/?format=json&sites=01646500&parameterCd=00060`
- Auth: none | Limits: No key. USGS does not publish a hard call cap — UNKNOWN — but documents that very large multi-site/multi-year requests should use the bulk/statistics services instead. Instantaneous Values service retains ~120 days; use the Daily Values and Statistics services for the long archive (many gauges back to early 1900s).
- Latency: sub-hourly (most gauges report every 15 min, transmitted hourly) | Format: REST JSON (WaterML JSON), WaterML XML, RDB tab-delimited
- Relevance: Settles river-crest and flood-stage contracts at a named gauge, and its multi-decade daily archive gives you the exceedance probability prior. This is the ground-truth measurement layer under any flood market; NWPS below gives the forecast layer.

**NOAA NWPS — National Water Prediction Service API** — NOAA / National Weather Service Office of Water Prediction `LIVE`

- Per-gauge observed stage plus NWS river forecast: current stage, forecast trajectory, flood categories (action / minor / moderate / major stage thresholds), crest forecast and time, and National Water Model streamflow. Verified: /gauges/01646500 returned 44 KB.
- Docs: https://api.water.noaa.gov/nwps/v1/docs/
- Base: `https://api.water.noaa.gov/nwps/v1/gauges/01646500`
- Auth: none | Limits: No published rate limit — UNKNOWN. Note the search form /gauges?srch= did not respond in testing; query by explicit gauge ID. Forecast horizon typically 3–5 days (short-range) with NWM medium-range to 10 days. History depth on the API is limited — UNKNOWN; use USGS NWIS for archive.
- Latency: sub-hourly to 6-hourly (forecast issuance driven) | Format: REST JSON, GeoJSON
- Relevance: The official flood-category thresholds here are exactly what flood contracts are written against ('will the river reach major flood stage at gauge X'), and the crest forecast is the free official point estimate you price the market's implied probability against.

**Copernicus GloFAS — Global Flood Awareness System (via EWDS / Open-Meteo flood-api)** — Copernicus Emergency Management Service / ECMWF JRC `LIVE`

- Global gridded river discharge forecast and reanalysis: daily ensemble river discharge, return-period exceedance (2/5/20-year) flood alerts, soil wetness index, snow water equivalent, runoff. v5.0 hydrological reanalysis covers 1980–2025. Two access paths verified: the Early Warning Data Store (ewds.climate.copernicus.eu, HTTP 200) and — far easier — Open-Meteo's flood-api which resells GloFAS river discharge as plain JSON by lat/lon with no key (verified HTTP 200).
- Docs: https://global-flood.emergency.copernicus.eu/technical-information/glofas-api/
- Base: `https://flood-api.open-meteo.com/v1/flood?latitude=25&longitude=-80&daily=river_discharge`
- Auth: free account + API token for EWDS (registration required); none for the Open-Meteo flood-api mirror | Limits: EWDS: registration required, queue-based CDS-API request system — no published per-day call limit, UNKNOWN; large NetCDF requests queue for minutes to hours. Open-Meteo mirror: same 600/min, 5,000/hr, 10,000/day, 300,000/month non-commercial limits. Forecast latency ~11 h after daily run. Reanalysis history 1980–2025.
- Latency: daily | Format: REST JSON (via Open-Meteo), NetCDF/GRIB (via EWDS CDS-API), WMS
- Relevance: The only free global flood forecast with return-period framing — indispensable for non-US flood contracts where USGS/NWPS do not reach (Pakistan, Bangladesh, Brazil, Sahel). Return-period exceedance maps cleanly onto 'severe flood event' contract language.

**MeteoAlarm — European multi-hazard warning aggregator** — EUMETNET (aggregating 38 European national met services) `LIVE`

- Harmonized CAP warnings from every European NMHS in one place: wind, rain/flood, thunderstorm, fog, extreme high/low temperature, snow/ice, coastal event, forest fire, avalanche, rain — each with awareness level (yellow/orange/red) and region polygons. Verified: /api/v1/warnings/feeds-italy returned 1.5 MB.
- Docs: https://feeds.meteoalarm.org/docs
- Base: `https://feeds.meteoalarm.org/api/v1/warnings/feeds-italy`
- Auth: none | Limits: No published rate limit — UNKNOWN. Per-country feed endpoints plus a legacy Europe-wide Atom feed. IMPORTANT: the legacy RSS feed (meteoalarm-legacy-rss-europe) now returns only a deprecation notice directing you to meteoalarm-legacy-atom-europe — and that Atom URL returned HTTP 404 in my test, so use the /api/v1/ endpoints. Responses are large; poll per-country, not Europe-wide.
- Latency: sub-hourly | Format: REST JSON, CAP XML, Atom (legacy)
- Relevance: Covers European heat waves, windstorms, and Mediterranean floods that Kalshi/Polymarket increasingly write contracts on, and is the only single feed unifying 38 national warning authorities. Red-level issuance is a clean binary settlement trigger.

**JMA Developer XML Feeds (eqvol / extra)** — Japan Meteorological Agency `LIVE`

- Machine-readable JMA push feeds. eqvol.xml carries earthquake information, JMA seismic intensity (shindo) reports, tsunami warnings and volcanic bulletins; extra.xml carries the high-volume general weather/warning stream. Verified: eqvol.xml 36 KB, extra.xml 319 KB.
- Docs: https://xml.kishou.go.jp/open-data.html
- Base: `https://www.data.jma.go.jp/developer/xml/feed/eqvol.xml`
- Auth: none | Limits: No published call limit — UNKNOWN. JMA requests reasonable polling (the feeds are Atom with updated timestamps; conditional GET is expected). Feed retains recent entries only — archive the individual XML documents yourself. Note the newer www.jma.go.jp/bosai/*/data/*.json paths are unstable (volcano list and quake.json both returned 404); the developer XML feeds are the reliable interface.
- Latency: sub-minute for earthquake and tsunami bulletins | Format: Atom XML index + per-event JMX XML documents
- Relevance: Japan earthquake contracts should settle on JMA magnitude and JMA shindo intensity, not USGS — JMA magnitude differs systematically from Mw. If a contract says 'JMA', this is the only authoritative free feed. Also the fastest tsunami warning source for the Pacific.

**MSC GeoMet-OGC-API + dd.weather.gc.ca CAP (Canada)** — Environment and Climate Change Canada / Meteorological Service of Canada `LIVE`

- OGC API Features with 40+ collections verified live, including hurricanes-cyclone-realtime, hurricanes-track-realtime, hurricanes-error_cone-realtime, hurricanes-wind_radii-realtime, hydrometric-realtime, hydrometric-annual-peaks, swob-realtime (surface observations), aqhi-*, climate-daily/hourly, and GDPS/RDPS model layers. Canadian CAP alerts are published as files under the datamart.
- Docs: https://eccc-msc.github.io/open-data/msc-geomet/readme_en/
- Base: `https://api.weather.gc.ca/collections`
- Auth: none | Limits: No published call limit — UNKNOWN; MSC publishes it as fully open data (Open Government Licence – Canada, commercial use permitted). OGC API paging via limit/offset. IMPORTANT path change: CAP alerts are NOT at dd.weather.gc.ca/alerts/cap/ (404) — they are under the date-partitioned tree dd.weather.gc.ca/YYYYMMDD/WXO-DD/alerts/cap/ (verified HTTP 200).
- Latency: sub-hourly; hydrometric-realtime every 5–15 min | Format: REST JSON (OGC API Features / GeoJSON), CAP XML, GRIB2, WMS/WMTS
- Relevance: An independent hurricane track + error cone + wind radii source for storms entering Canadian waters, and licence-clean for commercial use (unlike Open-Meteo's free tier). Canadian wildfire and flood contracts also settle here.

**InciWeb — Incident Information System RSS** — USDA Forest Service / National Wildfire Coordinating Group `LIVE`

- Public incident narrative feed for major US wildfires: incident name, state, acreage, containment, growth description, closures, evacuations, and per-incident detail pages. Verified: 123 KB RSS.
- Docs: https://inciweb.wildfire.gov/
- Base: `https://inciweb.wildfire.gov/incidents/rss.xml`
- Auth: none | Limits: No published rate limit — UNKNOWN. RSS carries currently-listed incidents only; no historical archive in the feed. There is also a GeoJSON/ArcGIS layer of InciWeb incidents.
- Latency: sub-hourly to daily (incident-team-updated) | Format: RSS/XML, plus ArcGIS GeoJSON layer
- Relevance: Narrative context for wildfire markets — evacuation orders, structure threat, containment trajectory — that the NIFC numeric feed does not carry. Use as a qualitative overlay for an LLM synthesis layer; do not settle contracts on it, since InciWeb acreage lags NIFC.

**ReliefWeb API v2** — UN OCHA `LIVE`

- Structured humanitarian record: disasters (with GLIDE numbers, type, country, status, date), situation reports, and 900k+ documents from 4,000+ organizations. Full-text search plus faceted filters.
- Docs: https://apidoc.reliefweb.int/
- Base: `https://api.reliefweb.int/v2/disasters?appname=YOUR_APPROVED_APPNAME`
- Auth: registration required — since 1 November 2025 you MUST use a PRE-APPROVED appname; an arbitrary appname now returns HTTP 403 AccessDeniedHttpException (verified) | Limits: EXACT: maximum 1,000 entries returned per call, maximum 1,000 calls per day. No per-minute limit documented. History: disaster records back to 1981 with GLIDE cross-referencing. v2 is documented as fully backward-compatible with v1.
- Latency: daily | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: USEFUL for the humanitarian/impact layer: official disaster declarations, GLIDE identifiers (which let you join an event across GDACS, EM-DAT and ReliefWeb), and casualty/displacement situation reports. Not a trading trigger — days of lag — but it is the authoritative narrative record for impact-bracket contracts. Register the appname before you build on it.

#### NICHE

**GeoNet API (New Zealand)** — GNS Science / GeoNet, New Zealand `LIVE`

- NZ earthquake catalog with MMI, quality flag, depth, locality; volcanic alert levels (/volcano/val); volcano quantitative data; strong-motion and intensity reports; news feed. Verified: /quake?MMI=3 returned 28 KB including event 2026p673226, M3.58, MMI 5, near Te Kaha, dated 2026-09-07.
- Docs: https://api.geonet.org.nz/
- Base: `https://api.geonet.org.nz/quake?MMI=3`
- Auth: none | Limits: No published rate limit — UNKNOWN. Requires an Accept header specifying version (e.g. application/vnd.geo+json;version=2). /quake returns only the last ~365 days; deeper history via the separate GeoNet FDSN and AWS S3 open data bucket.
- Latency: sub-minute | Format: REST JSON (GeoJSON), CSV, FDSN
- Relevance: NICHE-to-USEFUL: NZ-specific earthquake and volcano (Whakaari/White Island, Ruapehu, Taupo) contracts. Volcanic Alert Level endpoint is a clean settlement source. Low market volume, but the data quality is excellent and free.

**NOAA NCEI Hazel — Natural Hazards (tsunami / significant earthquake / volcano) historical database** — NOAA NCEI / former NGDC World Data Service `LIVE`

- Curated deep-history hazard event catalogs: tsunami events and runups (with measured wave heights at named locations, 2000 BC–present), significant earthquakes, and significant volcanic eruptions — each with deaths, damage, and intensity fields. Verified: /tsunamis/events?minYear=2020 returned 56 KB.
- Docs: https://www.ngdc.noaa.gov/hazel/view/swagger
- Base: `https://www.ngdc.noaa.gov/hazel/hazard-service/api/v1/tsunamis/events?minYear=2020`
- Auth: none | Limits: No published rate limit — UNKNOWN. Note the volcanoes/events path returned HTTP 400 with minYear alone — parameter names differ per collection; consult the Swagger doc. History: tsunamis back to 2000 BC, significant earthquakes back to 2150 BC.
- Latency: monthly to annual (curated archive) | Format: REST JSON, CSV export, Swagger/OpenAPI
- Relevance: Tsunami runup heights at named tide-gauge locations over millennia = the only free base-rate source for 'will wave height exceed N metres at location X'. Also the deep prior for significant-earthquake-fatality contracts.

**avalanche.org Public API (US) + EAWS (Europe)** — American Avalanche Association / National Avalanche Center; European Avalanche Warning Services `LIVE`

- US: the map-layer endpoint returns every US avalanche center's current forecast zone polygons with danger rating (1 Low – 5 Extreme), travel advice, and expiry; per-center endpoints give full forecast products, observations and avalanche incident reports. Verified: /v2/public/products/map-layer 273 KB; /v2/public/avalanche-center/NWAC 16 KB. Europe: EAWS publishes harmonized CAAML bulletins via avalanches.org (verified reachable).
- Docs: https://api.avalanche.org/v2/public/docs
- Base: `https://api.avalanche.org/v2/public/products/map-layer`
- Auth: none | Limits: No published rate limit — UNKNOWN. map-layer is a large single response (273 KB) — poll at most a few times daily, since forecasts issue once or twice per day. History depth on the public API is limited to current/recent products — UNKNOWN.
- Latency: daily (forecasts issued each morning in season, some centers twice daily) | Format: REST JSON; CAAML XML for EAWS
- Relevance: NICHE — thin markets. Danger-rating levels are cleanly binary-resolvable and seasonal avalanche-fatality counts occasionally appear as contracts. Include for completeness of the hazard taxonomy rather than expected volume.

**EFFIS — European Forest Fire Information System** — European Commission JRC / Copernicus EMS `LIVE`

- European burnt-area statistics and estimates by country and year, active fire detections over Europe/MENA, fire danger forecast (FWI) and seasonal trend charts. Verified: /apps/effis.statistics/estimates/EU/2026 returned 3 KB of 2026 season data.
- Docs: https://forest-fire.emergency.copernicus.eu/applications/data-and-services
- Base: `https://effis.jrc.ec.europa.eu/apps/effis.statistics/estimates/EU/2026`
- Auth: none for the statistics/current-situation viewer endpoints; registration for some bulk downloads | Limits: No published rate limit — UNKNOWN. The newer api2.effis.emergency.copernicus.eu host returned HTTP 404 for the paths I tried, so use the effis.jrc.ec.europa.eu apps endpoints. Burnt-area statistics history: 2000–present by country.
- Latency: daily | Format: REST JSON, WMS/WFS, CSV/shapefile bulk
- Relevance: NICHE for US-centric venues but the only free authoritative source for European wildfire-acreage contracts (Greece, Spain, Portugal, Italy) — a growing market category. Burnt-area-by-country-by-year is the base-rate table.

**NOAA WPC HeatRisk** — NOAA Weather Prediction Center + CDC `LIVE`

- 7-day gridded national heat-risk forecast on a 0–4 scale (Green/Yellow/Orange/Red/Magenta) that blends forecast temperature against local climatology and known health-impact thresholds — i.e. anomaly-aware rather than absolute-threshold heat risk. Verified: HeatRisk page HTTP 200, 47 KB.
- Docs: https://www.wpc.ncep.noaa.gov/heatrisk/
- Base: `https://www.wpc.ncep.noaa.gov/heatrisk/`
- Auth: none | Limits: No published rate limit — UNKNOWN. Delivered primarily as daily GIS raster/shapefile products and map images rather than a clean JSON API — you will need to pull the geospatial files. History depth on the live site is short (current 7-day cycle); archive availability UNKNOWN.
- Latency: daily | Format: GeoTIFF / shapefile / image products; no documented JSON REST API
- Relevance: NICHE-to-USEFUL for extreme-heat contracts. Most heat markets settle on a raw station high temperature (use NWS/NCEI for that), but HeatRisk level is increasingly the language of heat-emergency declarations, which are themselves becoming contract subjects.

**GDELT DOC 2.0 API** — The GDELT Project `LIVE`

- Global news monitoring across 100+ languages with 15-minute updates: article search, timeline volume, tone, and geographic extraction. Useful for detecting disaster events reported in local media before official agencies confirm them.
- Docs: https://blog.gdeltproject.org/gdelt-doc-2-0-api-debuts/
- Base: `https://api.gdeltproject.org/api/v2/doc/doc?query=earthquake&mode=artlist&format=json&maxrecords=1`
- Auth: none | Limits: No published numeric rate limit, but the API aggressively throttles — my test request returned HTTP 429 Too Many Requests immediately from a cold IP, so the practical shared-pool limit is low and UNKNOWN. maxrecords capped at 250 per call. DOC API searches only the rolling last 3 months; deeper history requires the BigQuery GDELT dataset or the raw 15-minute CSV files (both free).
- Latency: sub-hourly (15-minute update cycle) | Format: REST JSON, CSV, plus free BigQuery public dataset and raw CSV bulk
- Relevance: NICHE for settlement, USEFUL as an early-warning tripwire for disasters in regions with thin official instrumentation. Treat the 429 as the normal case and architect around the raw 15-minute CSV files or BigQuery rather than the live API.

**NASA Global Landslide Catalog / COOLR + LHASA nowcast** — NASA Goddard Space Flight Center `LIVE`

- Cooperative Open Online Landslide Repository: 11,000+ rainfall-triggered landslide events globally with date, location, trigger, fatalities, size; plus the LHASA model's near-real-time global landslide hazard nowcast. Verified: data.nasa.gov catalog page HTTP 200.
- Docs: https://landslides.nasa.gov/
- Base: `https://data.nasa.gov/dataset/global-landslide-catalog-export`
- Auth: none for the catalog export; NASA Earthdata login for some LHASA products | Limits: Catalog is a bulk CSV/GeoJSON export with no limits. LHASA nowcast distribution varies by product — UNKNOWN. Note maps.nccs.nasa.gov and maps.disasters.nasa.gov ArcGIS roots did not respond in testing, so the ArcGIS delivery path appears to have moved — verify before depending on it. Catalog history: 2007–2017 for the core GLC, with COOLR citizen reports continuing.
- Latency: daily (nowcast); the core catalog is a static historical export | Format: CSV bulk, GeoJSON, ArcGIS layers
- Relevance: NICHE. Landslide contracts are rare, but post-wildfire debris-flow markets in California reference this hazard class, and USGS ground-failure (already listed) covers the earthquake-triggered case better for trading purposes.

**ESRI / NOAA USA Wildfires live feature layer** — Esri Living Atlas (aggregating NIFC/IRWIN) `LIVE`

- Consolidated live US wildfire point and perimeter layer maintained in Esri's Living Atlas, with a stable FeatureServer endpoint. A lighter-weight mirror of the NIFC data for quick map integration.
- Docs: https://livingatlas.arcgis.com/
- Base: `https://services9.arcgis.com/RHVPKKiFTONKtxq3/arcgis/rest/services/USA_Wildfires_v1/FeatureServer/0/query`
- Auth: none | Limits: Public ArcGIS Online FeatureServer — typical 1,000–2,000 record page cap, no documented daily limit, UNKNOWN. Current-season data only. Verified HTTP 200 but returned a small (520 B) response for a generic query, so field names need checking against the layer metadata before use.
- Latency: sub-hourly | Format: REST JSON (Esri JSON / GeoJSON)
- Relevance: NICHE — it is a derivative of NIFC WFIGS, which you should use directly for settlement. Included only as a redundancy path if WFIGS is unreachable during an event.

#### Repos

- `tropycal/tropycal` — Python package for retrieving, analyzing and plotting tropical cyclone data — reads HURDAT2, IBTrACS, NHC real-time advisories, and the a-deck/b-deck model track files, all through one object model. 173 stars, last pushed 2026-08-13 (actively maintained, verified via GitHub API). · This is the single highest-leverage repo in the whole domain. It already solves HURDAT2 parsing, NHC realtime ingestion, and — critically — reading the a-deck spaghetti-model files, which is the hard part of building hurricane model-spread. It gives you storm objects with .to_dataframe() so you can go from raw NHC to a landfall probability distribution in a few lines. Steal its NHC realtime module wholesale.
- `exxamalte/python-aio-georss-gdacs` — Async Python client for the GDACS GeoRSS feed, with typed per-hazard entry classes (earthquake, cyclone, flood, volcano, drought, wildfire) that parse GDACS's non-obvious custom XML namespace. 5 stars but pushed 2026-07-20 — actively maintained. · GDACS's RSS uses a bespoke gdacs: namespace with alert level, alert score, population exposed and episode ID buried in it. This library already maps every field correctly and does it asynchronously with proper feed-diffing (new/updated/removed entries), which is exactly the update semantics you need for a live panel. Saves a day of XML archaeology.
- `seevee/cap_alerts` — Multi-region CAP (Common Alerting Protocol) weather-alert integration that normalizes alerts into one entity per active alert, modeled directly on CAP fields. 10 stars, pushed 2026-09-20 — literally updated the day of this research. · CAP is the lingua franca across NWS, MeteoAlarm, Environment Canada, JMA and tsunami.gov — normalizing all of them into one schema is a real chunk of work. This repo's field mapping and multi-region handling is a ready-made normalization layer for the alerting half of the panel.
- `kelvinn/capparselib` — Library that standardizes CAP messages across CAP 1.0/1.1/1.2 and the Atom/RSS wrappers different agencies use. 30 stars, pushed 2025-03-17. · The complement to the above: every alerting authority emits a slightly different CAP dialect and wrapper. capparselib collapses them to one parsed structure, which is what lets you treat a Japanese tsunami bulletin and a Kansas tornado warning as the same object type in your event store.
- `EMSC-CSEM/webservices101` — EMSC's own official tutorial repo for its web services, including working Python examples for the FDSN event service and — the valuable part — the seismicportal WebSocket standing-order client. 20 stars, pushed 2025-03-05. · First-party documentation-as-code from the data provider. The WebSocket example shows the exact message envelope (action: create/update, data.properties) so you can handle magnitude revisions correctly rather than treating every message as a new event. Magnitude revision handling is where naive earthquake integrations get contracts wrong.
- `datadesk/nasa-wildfires` — Los Angeles Times Data Desk's Python client for downloading NASA FIRMS hotspots, with sensible geographic filters. 34 stars, pushed 2025-06-26. · Built by a newsroom that actually uses it under wildfire deadline pressure, so it handles the FIRMS API's quirks (MAP_KEY transaction accounting, day-range caps, sensor naming). Good reference for staying inside the 5,000-per-10-minutes budget while polling a large area.
- `nodcat/firms-java` — High-performance Java client for NASA FIRMS with Spring integration and explicit attention to throughput. 10 stars, pushed 2026-06-28. · Worth reading even if you are not on the JVM: it is the only FIRMS client I found that treats the 5,000/10-min transaction budget as a first-class concern with batching and backoff, which is the actual production constraint when you are polling many bounding boxes.
- `aaronmayeux/ha-hurricane-tracker` — Home Assistant integration that consumes NHC CurrentStorms.json and renders the forecast cone. 7 stars, pushed 2026-09-05 — current with the 2026 season. · A small, current, working example of parsing CurrentStorms.json including the 2026 file structure and the new-for-2026 cone graphics changes. Useful as a schema sanity check, since NHC changed its cone products for the 2026 season.
- `Kamparia/gdacs-api` — Unofficial Python library wrapping the GDACS API with event-type enums and typed responses. 11 stars, but last pushed 2022-06-10 — STALE, roughly 4 years without a commit. · Read it for the endpoint map and the eventtype taxonomy, which are still correct, but do not depend on it: GDACS has changed response shapes since 2022. Use it as documentation, use exxamalte/python-aio-georss-gdacs as the dependency.
- `BlakeJC94/quaker` — Lightweight Python client + CLI for the USGS earthquake catalog, handling CSV/GeoJSON/text output and query paging. 3 stars but pushed 2026-03-26 — maintained. · Small and current. Its value is the paging logic around the hard 20,000-event cap: backfilling a multi-year catalog requires splitting queries by time window, and this repo already implements that split correctly.
- `titusjoyson/reliefweb-python` — Python client for the ReliefWeb API. 1 star, pushed 2025-07-30. · Thin, but relevant because it postdates the v2 migration. Check whether it threads the appname parameter properly before use — the pre-approved-appname requirement only landed 2025-11-01, so even this may need patching.
- `google/cap-library` — Google's Common Alerting Protocol library — validation, parsing and generation across CAP profiles. 88 stars, but last pushed 2019-09-23 — ARCHIVED-IN-PRACTICE / unmaintained. · Listed with a warning. It remains the most rigorous CAP validator ever written and is a good reference for CAP profile edge cases, but it is seven years stale and should not be a runtime dependency. Read it, do not import it.

---

### Economics & Macro Statistics

#### CORE

**FRED API (Federal Reserve Economic Data)** — Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis `LIVE`

- ~830,000 US and international time series aggregated from 100+ sources: CPI (CPIAUCSL, CPILFESL), PCE, nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS), unemployment (UNRATE), GDP/GDPC1, fed funds target (DFEDTARU/DFEDTARL), EFFR, SOFR, M2SL, UMich sentiment, housing starts, retail sales, industrial production. Daily/weekly/monthly/quarterly. ALFRED companion gives vintage (as-first-released) data, which is what actually settles a revision-sensitive contract. Full history to 1913 for some series.
- Docs: https://fred.stlouisfed.org/docs/api/fred/
- Auth: free API key (32-char, self-service at https://fredaccount.stlouisfed.org/apikeys) | Limits: No rate limit is stated anywhere in the official FRED docs. The widely-cited figure is 120 requests/minute per key, returning HTTP 429 when exceeded — this comes from the FRED team via email to the fredr R-package maintainers, NOT from published documentation. Treat 120/min as UNVERIFIED-BUT-OPERATIVE. No documented daily cap. History depth: full series history, no truncation on free tier. Observations per call effectively capped at 100,000.
- Latency: Varies by series: daily series updated daily; CPI/payrolls appear within minutes-to-hours of the official BLS release | Format: REST JSON or XML
- Relevance: The single best general-purpose backbone. Directly prices Kalshi CPI-range, unemployment-rate, GDP-print, and Fed-target-range contracts. ALFRED vintages matter enormously: many contracts settle on FIRST PRINT, not on the revised number FRED shows today. Use ALFRED, not FRED, for backtesting settlement.

**FRED Releases & Release Dates endpoint (US economic calendar)** — Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis `LIVE`

- fred/releases/dates returns the publication schedule for every one of ~300 FRED data releases. Setting include_release_dates_with_no_data=true returns FUTURE release dates — i.e. this is a free, structured, machine-readable US economic calendar keyed to release_id, which then joins to fred/release/series to tell you exactly which series that release will move. fred/release/tables gives the release's internal structure.
- Docs: https://fred.stlouisfed.org/docs/api/fred/releases_dates.html
- Auth: same free FRED API key | Limits: Same as FRED API — no officially documented rate limit; 120/min is the community/FRED-email figure. Calendar forward-window: releases are scheduled roughly 12 months ahead by the source agencies. Does NOT include consensus forecasts.
- Latency: daily (schedule updated as agencies publish their calendars) | Format: REST JSON or XML
- Relevance: Answers the 'when does it drop' half of the problem for US prints with official precision, sourced from the issuing agency rather than scraped. Essential for timing contract expiry, pre-positioning, and knowing when a market should be illiquid vs. about to gap. Weakness: no consensus/forecast field — pair with ForexFactory JSON for that.

**BLS Public Data API v2** — US Bureau of Labor Statistics `LIVE`

- The authoritative settlement source for CPI, PPI, employment situation (nonfarm payrolls, unemployment rate, average hourly earnings), JOLTS, ECI, productivity, and regional CPI. Series IDs like CUUR0000SA0 (CPI-U NSA, the one that settles CPI contracts), CUSR0000SA0 (SA), CES0000000001 (total nonfarm), LNS14000000 (U-3). Includes calculations (net/pct change) and optional catalog metadata.
- Docs: https://www.bls.gov/developers/api_faqs.htm
- Auth: free API key for v2 (registration, must be renewed annually); v1 works with NO key at lower limits | Limits: REGISTERED v2: 500 queries/day, 50 series per query, 20 years per query, 50 requests per 10 seconds. UNREGISTERED v1: 25 queries/day, 25 series per query, 10 years per query, 50 requests per 10 seconds. No net/pct-change calculations or catalog metadata on v1.
- Latency: Data posts at the official release instant (CPI 8:30am ET); API reflects it within minutes | Format: REST JSON (POST for multi-series)
- Relevance: HIGHEST PRIORITY. Kalshi CPI and payrolls contracts settle on the BLS number — usually the NSA CPI-U index level or the SA month-over-month print. Going to FRED instead of BLS adds a middleman to a settlement-critical value. Note the 500/day cap is genuinely tight if you poll; batch 50 series per POST.

**BEA API (Bureau of Economic Analysis)** — US Bureau of Economic Analysis `LIVE`

- GDP and the full NIPA tables (advance / second / third estimates), PCE price index and core PCE (the Fed's actual target measure), personal income and outlays, GDP by industry and by state/metro, international trade in goods and services, ITA/IIP balance of payments, fixed assets.
- Docs: https://apps.bea.gov/api/_pdf/bea_web_service_api_user_guide.pdf
- Auth: free API key (email registration at https://apps.bea.gov/API/signup/) | Limits: 100 requests per minute, 100 MB data volume per minute, and 30 errors per minute — per API key. Breaching any of the three triggers a 1-minute timeout during which all requests error. History depth: full published history, no free-tier truncation. (User guide dated April 20, 2026.)
- Latency: at official release (8:30am ET), typically same-minute | Format: REST JSON or XML
- Relevance: CORE for GDP-print contracts and for core-PCE contracts. The Fed targets PCE, not CPI, so any market on 'will the Fed cut' is fundamentally a core-PCE market. BEA's three-estimate structure (advance/second/third) creates distinct contract settlement points on the same quarter — get the vintage right.

**Atlanta Fed Market Probability Tracker (mpt_histdata.xlsx)** — Federal Reserve Bank of Atlanta / CenFIS `LIVE`

- Daily market-implied PROBABILITY DISTRIBUTIONS over future fed funds / SOFR outcomes, estimated from CME options on 3-month compounded-average SOFR futures. Gives the full density, not just a point forecast — i.e. P(rate in bucket X at meeting date Y). The historical file carries the complete back-history of these estimates.
- Docs: https://www.atlantafed.org/research-and-data/data/market-probability-tracker
- Auth: none | Limits: No API, no key, no documented rate limit — it is a static XLSX re-published daily. Verified: HTTP 200, 6,871,981 bytes, valid OOXML, at https://www.atlantafed.org/-/media/Project/Atlanta/FRBA/Documents/cenfis/market-probability-tracker/mpt_histdata.xlsx . History depth: full tracker history in the one file. Be polite — fetch once per day, not per request.
- Latency: daily, using previous-day option settlements (so it lags live pricing by ~1 session) | Format: XLSX bulk download
- Relevance: THIS IS THE ANSWER to 'where do free Fed funds implied probabilities come from.' CME FedWatch charges for its API; this is a Federal Reserve Bank publishing a methodologically superior product (full distribution from options, vs FedWatch's futures-implied point method) for free. Directly prices every Kalshi/Polymarket FOMC rate-decision contract. The one-session lag is the cost — for intraday you still need futures prices.

**ForexFactory Economic Calendar JSON (faireconomy mirror)** — ForexFactory / FairEconomy media endpoint `LIVE`

- Global economic calendar as flat JSON: event title, country/currency, exact ISO timestamp with timezone offset, impact rating (High/Medium/Low/Holiday), FORECAST (market consensus), and PREVIOUS. Covers USD, EUR, GBP, JPY, AUD, CAD, CHF, NZD, CNY. Weekly files: ff_calendar_thisweek.json, ff_calendar_nextweek.json, ff_calendar_lastweek.json (last week's file carries ACTUAL once released).
- Docs: https://nfs.faireconomy.media/ff_calendar_thisweek.json
- Auth: none | Limits: No key, no published rate limit, no published terms — it is an undocumented static JSON endpoint that ForexFactory's own site consumes. Verified live: returned 2026-09-20 events with forecast/previous fields populated. History depth: THREE WEEKS ONLY (last/this/next). No archive — you must snapshot it yourself daily to build history. Undocumented endpoints can vanish without notice; treat as fragile and cache aggressively.
- Latency: minutely for actuals once a release prints; calendar itself refreshed continuously | Format: REST JSON (static file)
- Relevance: CORE, and the only free source that carries CONSENSUS FORECAST alongside the schedule. The market price of a CPI contract is mostly a function of consensus vs. your own estimate — without consensus you cannot compute the surprise. FRED's calendar tells you when; this tells you when AND what the street expects AND what printed. Combine both: FRED for authoritative timing, FF for consensus.

**DBnomics API** — Cepremap (French public research) `LIVE`

- Meta-aggregator of 100+ statistical providers under one schema and one query language: BLS, BEA, Eurostat, ECB, IMF, OECD, World Bank, BIS, national statistics offices, ISM, and many more. Verified live counts: 47,062 datasets and 1,725,529,719 series. Endpoints for /providers, /datasets, /series, and full-text /search across all of them.
- Docs: https://api.db.nomics.world/v22/apidocs
- Auth: none | Limits: NO API KEY, NO REGISTRATION. No rate limit documented anywhere and none observed. Default page limit 1000 per request with offset paging. History depth: whatever the upstream provider publishes, unmodified. Fair-use expectation is implied but unstated — it is publicly funded infrastructure, so don't hammer it. Note the source code lives on GitLab (git.nomics.world), not GitHub.
- Latency: provider-dependent; DBnomics re-indexes upstream sources on its own cadence, typically daily — so it lags the primary source by hours and is NOT suitable for settlement-instant data | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: The highest-leverage single integration in this entire domain for BREADTH. One auth-free client gets you 1.7 billion series across every major statistical agency on earth. Use it for coverage, backfill, cross-country markets, and anything obscure. Do NOT use it for the settlement print — its re-index lag means you'd learn the CPI number after everyone else. Primary sources for speed, DBnomics for breadth.

**US Treasury Daily Yield Curve Rates (CSV export)** — US Department of the Treasury `LIVE`

- The official daily par yield curve: 1M, 1.5M, 2M, 3M, 4M, 6M, 1Y, 2Y, 3Y, 5Y, 7Y, 10Y, 20Y, 30Y constant-maturity Treasury yields. Also available: daily bill rates, long-term rates, real (TIPS) yield curve, and high-quality market corporate bond yields.
- Docs: https://home.treasury.gov/resource-center/data-chart-center/interest-rates/daily-treasury-yield-curve-rates
- Auth: none | Limits: No key, no documented rate limit. CSV by calendar year via ?type=daily_treasury_yield_curve&field_tdr_date_value=YYYY&_format=csv. Verified live returning 09/18/2026 data (10Y = 5.01, 2Y = 4.76). History depth: daily back to 1990.
- Latency: daily, posted ~6pm ET after market close | Format: CSV bulk (per-year files); also XML feed
- Relevance: CORE for any rate-level, curve-shape, or 10Y-threshold contract, and as the risk-free discount input for pricing every other contract's time value. The 2s10s spread is a recession-market input. Free, authoritative, no auth — there is no reason not to ingest this.

**Federal Reserve Data Download Program (DDP) — H.15, H.4.1, H.6, G.17, Z.1** — Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System `LIVE`

- H.15 selected interest rates (fed funds effective, prime, CMT yields, commercial paper); H.4.1 Fed balance sheet factors; H.6 money stock (M1, M2, components); G.17 industrial production and capacity utilization; G.19 consumer credit; Z.1 financial accounts; H.8 bank assets/liabilities.
- Docs: https://www.federalreserve.gov/datadownload/
- Auth: none | Limits: No key, no documented rate limit. Output.aspx supports filetype=csv|xml with lastobs=N, from/to date filters, and seriescolumn|serieprow layouts. Verified live returning H.15 CMT series. History depth: full published history (H.15 daily back to 1962 for many series).
- Latency: H.15 daily (~4:15pm ET), H.4.1 weekly Thursday 4:30pm ET, H.6 weekly, G.17 monthly | Format: CSV / XML bulk download (URL-parameterized, effectively an API)
- Relevance: CORE for money-supply contracts, Fed balance-sheet / QT-pace contracts, and industrial-production prints. H.4.1 is the only place to watch reserve balances and the standing repo facility, which drive 'will the Fed end QT' markets. G.17 industrial production is a direct Kalshi-style print.

**Atlanta Fed GDPNow** — Federal Reserve Bank of Atlanta / CQER `LIVE`

- Real-time running nowcast of current-quarter real GDP growth, rebuilt after each monthly source-data release, plus the full subcomponent contributions (PCE, investment, net exports, government) and the complete historical vintage record of every nowcast ever published. Companion file gives the data-release dates that trigger each update.
- Docs: https://www.atlantafed.org/cqer/research/gdpnow
- Auth: none | Limits: No API, no key, no rate limit. Verified live: GDPTrackingModelDataAndForecasts.xlsx HTTP 200, 10,883,697 bytes, valid XLSX, at https://www.atlantafed.org/-/media/Project/Atlanta/FRBA/Documents/cqer/researchcq/gdpnow/GDPTrackingModelDataAndForecasts.xlsx ; release-date schedule at .../gdpnow/GDPNowcastDataReleaseDates.xlsx (16,944 bytes). Headline number also on FRED as GDPNOW. History: every vintage since 2011.
- Latency: updated 6-7 times per quarter, within hours of each triggering source release | Format: XLSX bulk download (plus FRED series GDPNOW for the headline only)
- Relevance: CORE for GDP-print contracts. GDPNow is the market's de facto prior for the advance GDP estimate, and its revision path between releases IS the tradeable signal — when GDPNow jumps on a retail sales surprise, the GDP contract should reprice before the print. The historical vintage file lets you backtest exactly that.

**US Census Bureau Data API (Economic Indicators / timeseries EITS)** — US Census Bureau `LIVE`

- The primary source for retail sales (MARTS advance + MRTS), housing starts and building permits (RESCONST), new residential sales, durable goods and manufacturers' shipments (M3), wholesale and business inventories, international trade in goods (FT900), construction spending, and QSS services. Plus the full demographic/ACS catalog.
- Docs: https://www.census.gov/data/developers/guidance/api-user-guide.html
- Auth: free API key required for essentially all queries (self-service at https://www.census.gov/data/developers/api-key.html) | Limits: Up to 50 variables per query is the only limit stated in the official Query Limits page. Daily call cap and rows-per-query cap: UNKNOWN — not published. Historically 500 calls/day without a key was enforced before keys became mandatory; current keyed daily cap is undocumented. History depth: EITS timeseries generally back to 1992-2001 depending on program.
- Latency: at official release (8:30am ET); advance retail sales ~mid-month | Format: REST JSON (array-of-arrays)
- Relevance: CORE. Retail sales and housing starts are heavily-traded monthly prints and are also the largest single movers of GDPNow between updates. Census is the settlement source — FRED is a mirror. Note Census is also the release agency for trade data, which matters for tariff-related markets.

**Treasury FiscalData API** — US Department of the Treasury / Bureau of the Fiscal Service `LIVE`

- Debt to the penny, Daily Treasury Statement (cash balance, deposits, withdrawals — a real-time read on tax receipts and shutdown risk), Monthly Treasury Statement (deficit), average interest rates on outstanding debt by security type, auction results, exchange rates, debt subject to limit.
- Docs: https://fiscaldata.treasury.gov/api-documentation/
- Auth: none | Limits: No API key, no registration, and NO documented rate limit. Default page size 100, max page[size]=10000. Verified live returning avg_interest_rates back to 2001-01-31. History depth: varies by dataset; debt-to-the-penny daily back to 1993, average interest rates back to 2001.
- Latency: Daily Treasury Statement is next-business-day (~4pm ET); debt to the penny daily; MTS monthly | Format: REST JSON / CSV / XML with full filter+sort+pagination
- Relevance: CORE for debt-ceiling, shutdown, and deficit-threshold contracts — the Daily Treasury Statement operating cash balance is THE number for 'X-date' markets. Also USEFUL as an indirect real-time tax-receipts proxy that leads official income data.

**ECB Data Portal API** — European Central Bank `LIVE`

- Euro area HICP and core HICP, ECB policy rates (MRO, deposit facility, marginal lending), €STR, monetary aggregates, bank lending survey, euro reference exchange rates, balance of payments, Survey of Professional Forecasters. SDMX key-based addressing (e.g. ICP/M.U2.N.000000.4.ANR for euro-area HICP annual rate).
- Docs: https://data.ecb.europa.eu/help/api/data
- Auth: none | Limits: No API key, no registration, no documented rate limit. Verified live at https://data-api.ecb.europa.eu/service/data/... in both jsondata and csvdata. Supports lastNObservations, startPeriod/endPeriod, and If-Modified-Since for cheap polling. History depth: full series history back to 1999 (euro inception) for most.
- Latency: daily for rates/FX; HICP at Eurostat flash release | Format: SDMX-JSON, SDMX-ML, CSV
- Relevance: CORE for any ECB rate-decision or euro-area inflation contract. Note the ECB docs host (data.ecb.europa.eu) intermittently returns 503; the data host (data-api.ecb.europa.eu) is the reliable one — hit the data host directly and don't depend on the docs page being up.

**Eurostat API (dissemination / statistics 1.0)** — European Commission — Eurostat `LIVE`

- HICP monthly and flash estimates for every EU member state and the euro aggregate, unemployment (LFS), GDP flash and detailed national accounts, industrial production, retail trade, PPI, government deficit/debt (EDP), trade. Plus a catalogue RSS of data updates.
- Docs: https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/web/main/data/web-services
- Auth: none | Limits: No key, no registration. Documented hard limit: a single query may not exceed 50 dimension items per dimension and the response is capped (historically ~1,000,000 cells) — exceed it and you get an error, not truncation. No documented calls/day. Verified live returning 2026-02-06-updated HICP. History depth: full, typically back to 1996-2000 for HICP.
- Latency: at release; flash HICP ~end of reference month, final ~mid-following-month | Format: JSON-stat 2.0, SDMX-ML, TSV bulk
- Relevance: CORE for euro-area inflation contracts and the input to ECB-path markets. The flash-vs-final HICP gap is itself a tradeable revision. The catalogue RSS (verified live at .../catalogue/rss/en/statistics-update.rss) doubles as a free EU release-notification feed.

**New York Fed Markets Data API** — Federal Reserve Bank of New York `LIVE`

- SOFR, EFFR, OBFR, BGCR, TGCR reference rates with full percentile distribution and transaction volume; repo and reverse-repo operation results; SOMA holdings; primary dealer positions and survey; Treasury securities operations; central bank swap lines; and the Survey of Consumer Expectations (inflation expectations at 1yr/3yr/5yr horizons).
- Docs: https://markets.newyorkfed.org/static/docs/markets-api.html
- Auth: none | Limits: No API key, no registration, no documented rate limit. Verified live: SOFR for 2026-09-17 = 3.85% with 1st/25th/75th/99th percentiles and $2,992bn volume. Endpoints support /last/{n}, /search date ranges. History depth: SOFR back to 2018 inception, EFFR back to 2016.
- Latency: reference rates published ~8am ET next business day; repo operation results same-day within minutes | Format: REST JSON / XML / CSV
- Relevance: CORE for money-market and Fed-plumbing contracts. SOFR is what the Atlanta Fed probability tracker's options reference, so this is the underlying for the rate-path distribution. Reverse-repo balances and reserve levels drive 'will the Fed stop QT' markets. The SCE inflation expectations series is a direct input to Fed-reaction-function models.

**Federal Reserve FOMC calendar, statements, minutes, SEP and press RSS** — Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System `LIVE`

- Official FOMC meeting dates (scheduled ~2 years ahead), post-meeting statements, implementation notes, the Summary of Economic Projections including the dot plot, minutes (3-week lag), press-conference transcripts, and speeches. Monetary-policy press RSS feed for push notification of statement release.
- Docs: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm
- Auth: none | Limits: No key, no rate limit. Calendar page and https://www.federalreserve.gov/feeds/press_monetary.xml both verified live. NOT a structured API — the calendar is HTML and the SEP is PDF/HTML tables, so ingestion requires parsing. History depth: statements and minutes back to 1936 in the archive.
- Latency: statement at 2:00pm ET on decision day (RSS fires within seconds); minutes at 2:00pm ET three weeks later; SEP concurrent with statement at four meetings/year | Format: RSS + HTML scrape + PDF (SEP)
- Relevance: CORE. The meeting calendar defines the expiry date of every FOMC contract. The dot plot is the Fed's own rate path and is the single largest scheduled repricing event for rate markets. The RSS feed is the cheapest way to get sub-second notification that a statement has dropped. Statement-language diffing (hawkish/dovish word changes) is a well-known alpha source and is exactly what an LLM synthesis layer is good at.

**Cleveland Fed Inflation Nowcasting and Inflation Expectations** — Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland `LIVE`

- Daily-updated nowcasts of current-month and next-month CPI, core CPI, PCE and core PCE — published BEFORE the BLS/BEA release. Also model-based inflation expectations at 1-30 year horizons, trimmed-mean CPI, and median CPI.
- Docs: https://www.clevelandfed.org/indicators-and-data/inflation-nowcasting
- Auth: none | Limits: No key, no rate limit — but there is NO JSON API. The page is verified live (HTTP 200) but my probe of a guessed JSON path returned 404, so data access is HTML scrape or the XLSX/CSV linked on the page. Headline nowcast series are also mirrored on FRED. History depth: nowcast archive back to ~2000 in the downloadable file.
- Latency: DAILY — updated every business day as new daily price data arrives | Format: HTML / XLSX download; headline series on FRED
- Relevance: CORE in substance even though it is only a scrape. This is a Federal Reserve Bank publishing a daily-updating point forecast of the exact number Kalshi CPI contracts settle on, before it is released. Its nowcast-vs-market-implied gap is the most direct free edge available on CPI contracts. The scraping friction is the price of admission and worth paying — but the absence of a real API is a genuine limitation, so build the parser defensively.

#### USEFUL

**World Bank Indicators API** — World Bank Group `LIVE`

- Verified live: 29,544 indicators across World Development Indicators, International Debt Statistics, Doing Business archive, poverty and equity, and more — for ~217 economies. CPI inflation, GDP and GDP growth, unemployment (ILO modelled), government debt/GDP, current account, FDI, population.
- Docs: https://datahelpdesk.worldbank.org/knowledgebase/topics/125589
- Auth: none | Limits: No API key, no registration, no documented rate limit. per_page max 32,500; supports date ranges, MRV (most recent values), and JSON/XML. Verified live, lastupdated 2026-07-13. History depth: annual data typically 1960-present.
- Latency: ANNUAL for most series, with 1-2 year publication lag. This is the key weakness. | Format: REST JSON / XML
- Relevance: USEFUL, not CORE — the annual frequency and multi-year lag make it useless for pricing a monthly CPI print. Its value is cross-country breadth for long-dated or emerging-market contracts (e.g. 'will country X's debt/GDP exceed Y by 2028') and as a structural prior. Do not confuse breadth with timeliness here.

**OECD Data Explorer SDMX API** — Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development `LIVE`

- Harmonised cross-country macro for 38 members plus partners: CPI and core CPI on a comparable basis, Composite Leading Indicators (CLI), quarterly national accounts, labour force statistics, Main Economic Indicators, Economic Outlook projections, PPP and exchange rates, business and consumer confidence.
- Docs: https://gitlab.com/sis-cc/dotstatsuite-documentation/-/wikis/Using-API/API-documentation
- Auth: none | Limits: No key, no registration. Verified live at https://sdmx.oecd.org/public/rest/data/{agency},{dataflow},{version}/{key}. Accepts format=jsondata|csv; structure queries require format=structure|sdmx-3.0|json-structure-2.0.0 (passing an unsupported value returns HTTP 406 listing the valid set). No documented rate limit, but responses are slow and large — cache. History depth: varies, MEI typically back to 1955-1960.
- Latency: monthly for MEI/CPI, with a 1-2 month lag behind the national source | Format: SDMX-JSON, SDMX-ML, CSV
- Relevance: USEFUL for cross-country inflation comparisons and for the CLI as a recession-probability input. Lags national sources, so never use it for settlement. Its real edge is harmonisation — if a contract is written on a cross-country comparable basis, OECD is the arbiter.

**BIS Statistics API v2 (SDMX)** — Bank for International Settlements `LIVE`

- Central bank POLICY RATES for ~38 jurisdictions in one dataflow (WS_CBPOL) — daily and monthly; plus effective exchange rates, credit-to-GDP gaps, debt securities statistics, locational and consolidated banking statistics, residential property prices, and global liquidity indicators.
- Docs: https://stats.bis.org/api-doc/v2/
- Auth: none | Limits: No API key, no registration, no documented rate limit. Verified live: https://stats.bis.org/api/v2/data/dataflow/BIS/WS_CBPOL/1.0/D.US?format=csv returns daily US policy rate. History depth: policy rates back to 1946 for some jurisdictions.
- Latency: daily for policy rates; quarterly for banking statistics | Format: SDMX 2.1/3.0 — CSV, JSON, XML
- Relevance: USEFUL and underrated: WS_CBPOL is the cleanest single free feed for 'what is every central bank's policy rate right now' in one normalised dataflow. For a panel pricing BoE/ECB/BoJ/EM rate-decision contracts simultaneously, this beats integrating 38 separate central bank sites. Daily-frequency policy rates are unusual and valuable.

**Bank of Brazil (BCB) — SGS time series + Olinda Focus market expectations** — Banco Central do Brasil `LIVE`

- SGS: Selic target and effective rate, IPCA inflation, exchange rate, credit aggregates — thousands of series by numeric code (432 = Selic target). OLINDA/Expectativas: the FOCUS survey — the weekly poll of ~130 market economists giving mean, median, std-dev, min/max and respondent count for IPCA, Selic, GDP and FX at monthly, quarterly, annual and 12-month-ahead horizons.
- Docs: https://dadosabertos.bcb.gov.br/
- Auth: none | Limits: No API key, no registration, no documented rate limit on either service. Both verified live: SGS returned Selic 13.75 for 03-04/11/2026; Olinda Focus returned IPCA expectations surveyed 2026-09-11 for reference month 09/2028 (mean 0.3061, median 0.2800, sd 0.1403). Olinda uses full OData ($top/$filter/$format). History depth: SGS often back to 1994; Focus back to 2001.
- Latency: SGS daily; Focus survey published weekly (Monday morning) with daily incremental updates | Format: REST JSON (SGS) and OData JSON (Olinda)
- Relevance: USEFUL, and a genuinely rare find: the Focus survey is a free, structured, full-distribution CONSENSUS FORECAST feed with a respondent count and dispersion measure. Almost no other central bank publishes survey expectations as a queryable API. For any Brazil rate or inflation contract this is the market's prior, and the dispersion is a direct uncertainty input. Methodologically it is also the best free template for what a consensus feed should look like.

**NY Fed Survey of Consumer Expectations (SCE)** — Federal Reserve Bank of New York `LIVE`

- Monthly panel survey of household expectations: 1-year and 3-year ahead inflation expectations (median, mean, IQR), home price expectations, wage growth expectations, job-loss and job-finding probabilities, household spending and credit access expectations. Microdata also released.
- Docs: https://www.newyorkfed.org/microeconomics/sce
- Auth: none | Limits: No key, no rate limit — static XLSX. Verified live: https://www.newyorkfed.org/medialibrary/interactives/sce/sce/downloads/data/frbny-sce-data.xlsx returns a valid XLSX (PK header confirmed). History depth: June 2013 to present.
- Latency: monthly, released ~2nd Monday at 11am ET | Format: XLSX bulk download
- Relevance: USEFUL for Fed-path contracts. Powell has repeatedly cited consumer inflation expectations as a policy input, so a de-anchoring in the SCE is a leading indicator for hawkish surprises. Also feeds 'will inflation expectations exceed X' style contracts directly.

**Statistics Canada Web Data Service (WDS)** — Statistics Canada `LIVE`

- Full Canadian macro: CPI, Labour Force Survey (the Canadian payrolls equivalent), GDP by month and industry, retail trade, housing starts, trade. Table/cube-based (productId), with getAllCubesListLite for discovery and getChangedSeriesList to detect what just updated.
- Docs: https://www.statcan.gc.ca/en/developers/wds/user-guide
- Auth: none | Limits: No API key, no registration. Documented guidance is a soft limit of roughly 25 requests per second and up to 300,000 records per request — treat the rate figure as approximate, StatCan words it as guidance rather than a hard cap. Verified live: getAllCubesListLite returned the full cube catalogue; getChangedSeriesList correctly returned {'message':'The product is not released yet'} (an application-level response, confirming the service is up). History depth: full published history, many series to 1914.
- Latency: at official release, 8:30am ET | Format: REST JSON (GET and POST)
- Relevance: USEFUL. getChangedSeriesList is the interesting piece — it is a change-detection endpoint, so you can poll for 'what data just moved' rather than polling every series. That pattern is exactly right for a real-time panel. Relevant to Bank of Canada rate contracts.

**Destatis GENESIS-Online REST API** — Statistisches Bundesamt (German Federal Statistical Office) `LIVE`

- German CPI/VPI and the HICP contribution, ifo-adjacent production and orders data, GDP, labour market, foreign trade, producer prices, construction. Germany is ~29% of euro-area HICP, so German inflation leads the euro-area print.
- Docs: https://www-genesis.destatis.de/datenbank/online/docs/
- Auth: free registration required for data calls (username/password, not a bearer key); a small set of open endpoints work without credentials | Limits: Registration is free. Exact per-day or per-minute call limits: UNKNOWN — not published. Result-size limits apply per table and large tables must be requested as background jobs. Verified live: the unauthenticated /helloworld/whoami endpoint returned HTTP 200. History depth: varies by table, CPI back to 1948 for some aggregates.
- Latency: German flash CPI ~end of reference month, roughly 2 days before euro-area flash HICP | Format: REST JSON / CSV / XML
- Relevance: USEFUL specifically because German flash CPI prints BEFORE euro-area flash HICP and is its largest component. That 2-day lead is a real, exploitable information edge on euro-area inflation contracts. The registration friction is worth paying for that alone.

**ONS Beta API v1 (UK)** — UK Office for National Statistics `LIVE`

- UK CPIH/CPI, labour market (unemployment, earnings), GDP monthly and quarterly, retail sales, trade, public sector finances. Dataset/edition/version addressing with full metadata and contact details.
- Docs: https://developer.ons.gov.uk/
- Auth: none | Limits: No API key, no registration, no documented rate limit. Verified live at https://api.beta.ons.gov.uk/v1/datasets. CRITICAL: this is the REPLACEMENT API. The old https://api.ons.gov.uk/timeseries/... endpoints were fully retired on 25 November 2024 and now return a decommission notice — any tutorial or repo using that path is dead. History depth: varies by dataset.
- Latency: at official release, 7:00am UK time | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: USEFUL for Bank of England rate contracts and UK inflation markets. The migration is the trap here: most existing UK macro code on GitHub still targets the retired endpoint and will silently fail or return the decommission string as if it were data.

**Bank of England Interactive Statistical Database (IADB)** — Bank of England

- Bank Rate (IUDBEDR), SONIA, gilt yields, money and credit aggregates (M4), mortgage approvals and rates, effective interest rates on household and corporate lending, banknote circulation. Also the MPC decision calendar, minutes, and the Monetary Policy Report.
- Docs: https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/boeapps/database/
- Auth: none | Limits: No API key, no registration, no documented rate limit. The database front-end is verified live (HTTP 200); the CSV export path (fromshowcolumns.asp with SeriesCodes, Datefrom/Dateto, CSVF=TN, UsingCodes=Y) returned a 302 redirect on my probe, so the exact working parameter set is NOT confirmed and may need a session cookie or corrected date format. Treat the CSV export as IMPLEMENTED / NOT VERIFIED. History depth: Bank Rate back to 1694.
- Latency: daily for rates; monthly for money and credit | Format: CSV export via URL parameters (unofficial but long-standing); HTML front-end
- Relevance: USEFUL for BoE rate-decision contracts — Bank Rate and SONIA are the settlement references. The fragility of the CSV export is a real integration risk; DBnomics carries BoE series as a more stable fallback.

**IMF Data Portal SDMX 3.0 API** — International Monetary Fund

- International Financial Statistics (IFS), World Economic Outlook projections, Direction of Trade Statistics, Government Finance Statistics, Balance of Payments, Fiscal Monitor, Consumer Price Index database, and the Primary Commodity Price System.
- Docs: https://data.imf.org/
- Auth: UNKNOWN — the new portal's auth model is not clearly documented; the legacy service required none | Limits: UNKNOWN. The IMF migrated from the SDMX 2.0 service to an SDMX 3.0 API on the new data.imf.org portal, and the migration broke every existing client (the imfp and imfr packages stopped working without warning). I could NOT confirm a working base path: my probe of https://api.imf.org/external/sdmx/3.0/dataflow returned HTTP 404, and the legacy https://dataservices.imf.org/REST/SDMX_JSON.svc/ failed to connect at all. Rate limits, history depth and the correct endpoint are all UNKNOWN. Verify the exact base URL against the live portal before building.
- Latency: monthly to annual depending on dataset; WEO twice yearly (April/October) | Format: SDMX 3.0 REST (JSON/XML)
- Relevance: USEFUL in principle for cross-country and EM contracts, and WEO projections are the reference forecast for many sovereign markets. But given the unresolved endpoint, route IMF data through DBnomics instead — DBnomics carries IMF series and absorbs the migration risk for you.

**Japan e-Stat API** — Japan Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications / Statistics Bureau

- Japanese CPI (national and Tokyo advance), labour force survey, GDP, industrial production, trade, retail. 6,000+ survey tables with bilingual Japanese/English labels. Companion Statistics Dashboard API offers a simpler pre-aggregated indicator set.
- Docs: https://www.e-stat.go.jp/api/
- Auth: free application ID (appId) via registration at e-stat.go.jp; the Statistics Dashboard API at dashboard.e-stat.go.jp requires no key | Limits: UNKNOWN — no published call limit for the main e-Stat API. Registration is free with no credit card. I did NOT verify either endpoint live. History depth: UNKNOWN, varies by survey.
- Latency: at official release; Tokyo CPI advance prints ~3 weeks before national CPI | Format: REST JSON / XML / CSV
- Relevance: USEFUL for BoJ policy contracts, which became genuinely tradeable once Japan exited negative rates. The Tokyo CPI advance is a well-known ~3-week leading indicator of national CPI — a real structural edge on Japan inflation markets. Unverified, so confirm before relying on it.

**BEA and agency release RSS feeds** — BEA, Federal Reserve, ECB, Eurostat `LIVE`

- Push notification that a release has dropped, with title, link and timestamp. Verified live: BEA at https://apps.bea.gov/rss/rss.xml, Fed monetary policy at https://www.federalreserve.gov/feeds/press_monetary.xml, ECB at https://www.ecb.europa.eu/rss/press.html, Eurostat catalogue updates at https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/api/dissemination/catalogue/rss/en/statistics-update.rss.
- Docs: https://www.federalreserve.gov/feeds/feeds.htm
- Auth: none | Limits: No key, no documented rate limit on any of the four. All four verified live and returning well-formed RSS 2.0. History depth: typically last 20-50 items only — these are notification feeds, not archives.
- Latency: seconds — RSS fires at publication | Format: RSS 2.0 / XML
- Relevance: USEFUL as the low-latency trigger layer. Polling an RSS feed every few seconds is far cheaper than polling a data API, and gives you the 'it just dropped, go fetch' signal. Pair with the data APIs rather than replacing them. For FOMC statements specifically, the Fed RSS feed is the cheapest sub-second notification available for free.

**CME Group daily settlement prices (30-Day Fed Funds, ZQ) — public web pages** — CME Group

- Daily settlement prices for the 30-Day Fed Funds futures strip (ZQ), from which fed-funds-implied probabilities are computed. Implied rate = 100 minus price. The first 12 contract months settle on Globex bid/ask activity 13:59:00-14:00:00 CT.
- Docs: https://www.cmegroup.com/markets/interest-rates/stirs/30-day-federal-fund.quotes.html
- Auth: none for the public quotes page; CME DataMine and the FedWatch API are paid | Limits: The public quotes page is free but is NOT an API and is bot-protected — I did not verify a stable machine-readable path, so treat it as scrape-only and fragile. There is no free CME settlement API. Historical settlement archives are behind CME DataMine (paid). History depth via free path: effectively current-day only.
- Latency: daily settlement ~2pm CT; delayed quotes intraday | Format: scrape-only (HTML); paid API otherwise
- Relevance: USEFUL but do not start here. The reason to care is that ZQ is the underlying for fed-funds probability math — but the Atlanta Fed Market Probability Tracker already gives you a better (full-distribution, options-based) version of that computation for free as a clean XLSX. Use CME only if you need intraday probability updates that the Atlanta Fed's one-session lag cannot provide, and budget for the paid feed if so.

#### NICHE

**Alpha Vantage Economic Indicators** — Alpha Vantage `LIVE`

- Pre-normalised US macro endpoints: REAL_GDP, REAL_GDP_PER_CAPITA, TREASURY_YIELD, FEDERAL_FUNDS_RATE, CPI, INFLATION, RETAIL_SALES, DURABLES, UNEMPLOYMENT, NONFARM_PAYROLL. Clean JSON, no series-ID lookup needed.
- Docs: https://www.alphavantage.co/documentation/#economic-indicators
- Auth: free API key (self-service email registration); the literal key 'demo' works for a few sample calls | Limits: 25 API requests PER DAY and 5 requests per minute on the free tier. That is a severe cap — it is a convenience layer, not an ingestion source. Premium starts at $49.99/mo for 75 req/min. Verified live with apikey=demo: CPI returned 2026-08-01 = 334.980, exactly matching the BLS print, confirming it is a faithful mirror and current in 2026. History depth: full (CPI back to 1913).
- Latency: mirrors BLS/BEA/Fed with an unstated lag — not a primary-release source | Format: REST JSON / CSV
- Relevance: NICHE. The 25/day cap disqualifies it as a backbone, and everything in it is free and uncapped from FRED. Worth listing only as a fallback and because the normalised schema saves prototyping time. Do not build on it.

**Swiss National Bank data API** — Schweizerische Nationalbank `LIVE`

- SNB policy rate, SARON, Swiss CPI, bond yields, FX reserves and interventions, monetary aggregates, balance of payments, Swiss GDP. Cube-based addressing with a clean JSON envelope including metadata and frequency.
- Docs: https://data.snb.ch/en/help/api
- Auth: none | Limits: No key, no registration, no documented rate limit. Verified live: https://data.snb.ch/api/cube/{cubeId}/data/json/en returned bond-yield series with history from 1988-01. Also supports /csv and /xlsx output. History depth: often back to the 1970s-1980s.
- Latency: daily for rates and FX; monthly for CPI and reserves | Format: REST JSON / CSV / XLSX
- Relevance: NICHE unless SNB rate contracts are listed. Its broader value is as the cleanest small-central-bank API design and as a source for CHF safe-haven flow analysis during risk events. FX intervention data is unusually transparent here.

**Banco de México SIE API** — Banco de México `LIVE`

- Mexican policy (Objetivo) rate, TIIE, INPC inflation, FX (peso), international reserves, IGAE activity indicator, remittances. Series-code addressing (SF43718 = FIX exchange rate).
- Docs: https://www.banxico.org.mx/SieAPIRest/service/v1/
- Auth: free bearer token required (self-service at https://www.banxico.org.mx/SieAPIRest/service/v1/token) | Limits: Token is free and instant. Exact call limits: UNKNOWN — not published. Documented constraint: a maximum of 20 series per request and a maximum of 100 series in the token's catalogue query. Verified live: the endpoint responded with a well-formed Spanish-language auth error ('Token inválido') pointing at the token URL, confirming the service is up in 2026. History depth: many series back to 1954.
- Latency: daily for FX and rates; biweekly for INPC (Mexico publishes twice monthly) | Format: REST JSON / XML
- Relevance: NICHE unless Banxico or MXN contracts are listed. Mexico's biweekly (quincenal) CPI is unusual and creates more frequent inflation print events than most countries.

**Norges Bank / Riksbank / other Nordic central bank SDMX APIs** — Norges Bank, Sveriges Riksbank

- Policy rates, FX reference rates, government bond yields, CPI links. Norges Bank exposes SDMX at data.norges-bank.no; Riksbank exposes a SWEA REST API.
- Docs: https://data.norges-bank.no/
- Auth: none for both | Limits: UNKNOWN — neither publishes rate limits. My probe of https://data.norges-bank.no/api/data/IR/... failed to connect (HTTP 000), so the exact dataflow key is unconfirmed; the service may simply have rejected my guessed series key. Treat as NOT VERIFIED. History depth: UNKNOWN.
- Latency: daily for rates and FX | Format: SDMX-JSON / SDMX-ML (Norges Bank); REST JSON (Riksbank SWEA)
- Relevance: NICHE. Only relevant if Nordic rate contracts appear. Listed for completeness of central-bank coverage — BIS WS_CBPOL already carries both policy rates and is verified, so prefer that.

**Bank of Korea ECOS Open API** — Bank of Korea

- BoK base rate, Korean CPI, M1/M2 aggregates, real and nominal GDP, FX reserves, balance of payments and trade balance, KORIBOR.
- Docs: https://ecos.bok.or.kr/api/
- Auth: free API key via registration | Limits: Reported at approximately 1,000 calls per day per key, and a maximum of 100,000 rows per request. I did NOT verify this endpoint live and the 1,000/day figure is secondary-sourced, not read off the official docs — treat as UNCONFIRMED. History depth: UNKNOWN.
- Latency: monthly for CPI; daily for rates | Format: REST JSON / XML
- Relevance: NICHE. Korea is a bellwether for global trade and semiconductor cycles — Korean 20-day export data (from Korea Customs, separate source) is one of the earliest reads on global trade volumes and prints ~10 days before most trade data.

**Australian Bureau of Statistics Data API (SDMX)** — Australian Bureau of Statistics `LIVE`

- Australian CPI (quarterly, plus the newer monthly indicator), labour force, GDP, retail trade, building approvals, wage price index.
- Docs: https://api.data.abs.gov.au/
- Auth: none | Limits: No key, no registration, no documented rate limit. The service is live — my request returned a well-formed application error ('Could not find Dataflow and/or DSD related with this data request'), meaning the host is up and my guessed dataflow ID was wrong. The correct dataflow IDs must be discovered via the /dataflow endpoint. History depth: UNKNOWN.
- Latency: quarterly for headline CPI; monthly for the CPI indicator | Format: SDMX-JSON / SDMX-ML / CSV
- Relevance: NICHE. Relevant to RBA rate contracts. Australia's quarterly-primary CPI (rather than monthly) makes each print unusually high-variance and therefore unusually tradeable.

#### Repos

- `OpenBB-finance/OpenBB` — 73,308 stars, pushed 2026-09-19. Open data platform for analysts and quants with a unified provider abstraction over FRED, BLS, BEA, ECB, Eurostat, OECD, IMF, Census, Treasury and dozens more, exposed as a Python SDK and REST API. · The single highest-leverage repo here. Rather than writing 30 connectors, steal OpenBB's provider interface — it already normalises heterogeneous macro schemas into one model and handles the auth, paging and retry differences. Actively maintained as of this week, so its connectors reflect the 2026 state of these APIs (including the IMF SDMX 3.0 migration and the ONS endpoint retirement). Read openbb_fred and openbb_econdb providers first.
- `KMueller-Lab/Global-Macro-Database` — 273 stars, pushed 2026-07-01. A harmonised panel combining 33 contemporary sources (IMF, World Bank, OECD) with 127 historical datasets — 160 sources total — into one long-run macro database. The 2026_06 quarterly update added 39 new aggregator and country-level historical sources. Python, R and Stata accessors; all construction code open. · Solves the backfill problem that every one of these APIs has: deep pre-1960 history with documented source precedence and splice logic. For backtesting a pricing model across multiple business cycles you need history that no single agency API provides. The fact that the splicing rules are open source means you can audit which source a given observation came from rather than trusting an opaque blend.
- `pydata/pandas-datareader` — 3,269 stars, pushed 2026-07-21. Pulls FRED, World Bank, OECD, Eurostat, Bank of Canada, Fama/French and more directly into pandas DataFrames. · The lowest-friction way to prototype a macro pull. Battle-tested against these specific endpoints for over a decade, so its code documents the quirks (date parsing, missing-value conventions, series-ID formats) that the official docs omit. Note it is maintenance-mode rather than feature-rich — good for reading, adequate for using.
- `mortada/fredapi` — 1,658 stars, pushed 2026-01-28. Python client for both FRED and ALFRED, returning pandas Series/DataFrame. Crucially it wraps the ALFRED vintage endpoints (get_series_first_release, get_series_as_of_date, get_series_all_releases). · The ALFRED vintage support is the reason to use this over a raw HTTP client. Prediction-market contracts settle on the FIRST PRINT; FRED's current values are revised. Backtesting against revised data will make your model look far better than it is. This library makes as-of-date retrieval a one-liner and is the standard defence against that specific, very common, very expensive mistake.
- `us-bea/beaapi` — 69 stars, pushed 2026-02-17. The BEA's OWN official Python library for its API. · First-party, so it encodes BEA's actual throttling behaviour (the 100 req/min, 100MB/min, 30 errors/min triple) and the NIPA table-addressing scheme correctly. When an agency publishes its own client, its retry and backoff logic is the authoritative statement of what the server will tolerate — read it rather than guessing.
- `nikhilxsunder/fedfred` — 9 stars but pushed 2026-09-19 (this week). Modern FRED client with sync and async access, built-in rate-limiting, caching, and output to pandas, Polars or Dask. · The async plus native rate-limiting is what you want for a panel polling hundreds of series against an undocumented ~120/min ceiling. Low star count means low battle-testing — read the rate-limiter implementation and vendor the idea rather than depending on the package.
- `bdecon/econ_data` — 95 stars, pushed 2026-03-17. Worked Python 3 examples for BLS, BEA, Census and FRED APIs, plus tooling for CPS microdata (bd CPS). · The most practical BLS reference available — BLS's own docs are thin and this shows the POST multi-series pattern that gets you 50 series per query against the 500/day cap. The CPS microdata tooling matters if you ever want to compute an unemployment rate yourself rather than waiting for the headline.
- `fizahkhalid/forex_factory_calendar_news_scraper` — 103 stars, pushed 2026-08-02. Scrapes the ForexFactory economic calendar into structured CSV/JSON, filters by currency and impact, converts timezones, and fires configurable pre-event alerts to Discord, Telegram or webhooks. · Actively maintained, which matters because calendar scrapers rot fast. Two things to steal even if you use the faireconomy JSON endpoint instead: the timezone normalisation (calendar timestamps are a notorious source of off-by-one-hour bugs around DST) and the pre-event alert scheduling pattern.
- `andrevlima/economic-calendar-api` — 57 stars, last pushed 2024-03-04. Wraps the forex economic calendar into a JSON HTTP API. · Useful as a reference implementation of the calendar-as-a-service shape. Flag: no commits in over two years, so assume its selectors are broken against the current ForexFactory DOM. Read it, don't run it.
- `viandwi24/forexfactory` — Small repo, pushed 2026-01-07. Unofficial API client for the Forex Factory economic calendar. · Recent enough to reflect the current site structure. Cross-check its endpoint against the faireconomy JSON path — if it targets the same static file, that is independent confirmation the undocumented endpoint is the one the ecosystem relies on, which slightly lowers the risk of it disappearing.
- `dbnomics/rdbnomics` — 36 stars. R client for DBnomics. Note this is a GitHub MIRROR — DBnomics develops on its own GitLab at git.nomics.world, where the Python client (dbnomics-python-client) and the data-model repos actually live. · Worth knowing because searching GitHub for DBnomics tooling turns up mostly stale mirrors (the Python mirror ceschi/dbnomics-python-client last moved in 2019). Go to git.nomics.world for the live code. The client is thin anyway — the API needs no key and is simple enough to call directly.
- `dkgaraujo/OpenSourcedMacroModels` — A curated collection of open-sourced macroeconomic models actually run by central banks and finance ministries. · Not a data feed but a modelling reference: if you want to forecast the number a contract settles on, these are the structural models the policymakers themselves use. Particularly relevant for understanding the Fed's reaction function when pricing FOMC contracts.
