### Financial Markets (equities, options/IV, rates, credit, FX, futures, crypto, volatility, breadth, positioning, filings)

#### CORE

**Cboe Delayed Quotes CDN (full option chains with IV + greeks)** — Cboe Global Markets `LIVE`

- Complete US option chain for any optionable symbol and for cash indices (SPX, NDX, RUT): per-contract bid/ask/size, last, volume, open interest, implied volatility, delta, gamma, vega, theta, rho, and Cboe's theoretical value. Underlying quote included. ~15-minute delayed. SPX payload is ~13 MB (every listed strike/expiry); AAPL ~1.5 MB. Equity symbols use /options/<TICKER>.json, cash indices use /options/_<INDEX>.json. Separate /quotes/_VIX.json returns the live-ish VIX level.
- Docs: https://www.cboe.com/delayed_quotes/spx/quote_table
- Base: `https://cdn.cboe.com/api/global/delayed_quotes/options/`
- Auth: none | Limits: No published rate limit, no key, no registration. UNKNOWN whether an undocumented IP throttle exists. Data is ~15 min delayed. NO OFFICIAL API DOCS EXIST — this is the JSON backing the public Cboe quote-table web page; it can be withdrawn without notice. Licensing for redistribution is UNKNOWN — Cboe's site terms restrict scraping, so treat as internal-use-only until legal review.
- Latency: sub-minute polling of a ~15-minute-delayed snapshot | Format: REST JSON (static CDN objects)
- Relevance: THE single highest-value free feed for prediction-market pricing. A full strike ladder with IV and delta lets you extract a risk-neutral probability distribution (butterfly spreads / Breeden-Litzenberger) and read off P(SPX > X by date) directly comparable to a Kalshi/Polymarket 'will the S&P close above X' contract. Also prices single-name event contracts (earnings moves, takeover probability via skew) and gives a real-time vol surface for any 'will X be volatile' market. Almost nobody wires this up because it is undocumented.

**SEC EDGAR — XBRL company facts, frames and submissions API** — US Securities and Exchange Commission `LIVE`

- data.sec.gov/api/xbrl/companyfacts and /companyconcept give every XBRL-tagged financial fact a filer has ever reported, with the accession number and filing date for each. /api/xbrl/frames/<taxonomy>/<tag>/<unit>/<period> returns that concept for ALL filers in one call (cross-sectional). /submissions/CIK##########.json gives the complete filing history, ticker-to-CIK map, exchange, SIC.
- Docs: https://www.sec.gov/search-filings/edgar-application-programming-interfaces
- Base: `https://data.sec.gov/api/xbrl/`
- Auth: none — but a descriptive User-Agent header containing a contact email is MANDATORY; generic browser UAs get HTTP 403 | Limits: 10 requests/second (SEC fair-access policy), no daily cap, no key. Full history back to ~2009 for XBRL, back to 1993 for raw filings. Bulk alternatives: companyfacts.zip and submissions.zip (multi-GB, refreshed nightly).
- Latency: minutely (filings appear within minutes of acceptance); XBRL frames update as filings arrive | Format: REST JSON + bulk ZIP
- Relevance: Ground truth for any contract on reported revenue/EPS/guidance, 'will company X report above $Y', bankruptcy/going-concern markets, and as the authoritative resolution source when a market says 'per SEC filings'. Frames endpoint lets you rank the whole universe on one metric in a single call.

**SEC EDGAR Full-Text Search API (efts)** — US Securities and Exchange Commission `LIVE`

- Elasticsearch-backed full-text search over the body of every EDGAR filing since 2001. Filter by form type (8-K, S-1, SC 13D, 425, DEFM14A), CIK, and date range. Returns filing id, CIK list, form type, filing date and matched document path.
- Docs: https://efts.sec.gov/LATEST/search-index?q=%22merger%22&forms=8-K
- Base: `https://efts.sec.gov/LATEST/search-index?q=`
- Auth: none (same User-Agent requirement as EDGAR) | Limits: 10 req/sec fair-access. Results capped at 10,000 hits per query (hits.total reports 'gte 10000'); paginate with &from=. History from 2001. Undocumented/unsupported — SEC publishes the UI at efts.sec.gov but not a formal API contract. POST is rejected (403 Missing Authentication Token); GET only.
- Latency: minutely | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: Event detection engine for corporate-event contracts: merger announcements (425, DEFM14A, SC 13D), CEO departures and restatements (8-K Item 5.02 / 4.02), IPO filings (S-1), bankruptcy. Lets you resolve 'will X announce a merger before date D' from the primary document rather than from news.

**FINRA Reg SHO Daily Short Sale Volume Files** — FINRA `LIVE`

- One pipe-delimited file per trading day covering EVERY US equity symbol: Date|Symbol|ShortVolume|ShortExemptVolume|TotalVolume|Market. Consolidated (CNMS) file plus per-venue files. ~544 KB/day, thousands of symbols. Verified with the 2026-09-18 file.
- Docs: https://www.finra.org/finra-data/browse-catalog/short-sale-volume-data/daily-short-sale-volume-files
- Base: `https://cdn.finra.org/equity/regsho/daily/CNMSshvol<YYYYMMDD>.txt`
- Auth: none | Limits: No key, no published rate limit, no daily cap. Files posted each trading day; archive goes back years. Monthly ZIPs also available. UNKNOWN whether an undocumented CDN throttle exists.
- Latency: daily (next-day, posted after close) | Format: CSV/pipe-delimited bulk file
- Relevance: Free daily market-breadth and positioning signal across the ENTIRE US universe — no other free source gives per-symbol short volume daily. Short-volume ratio spikes precede squeeze/volatility contracts; aggregate TotalVolume across symbols gives you an advance/decline-style breadth proxy and a free consolidated volume denominator.

**FINRA Equity Short Interest (consolidated, semi-monthly) API** — FINRA `LIVE`

- Exchange-reported short interest per symbol: current and previous short position, average daily volume, days-to-cover, settlement date, split flag. Covers NYSE/Nasdaq/NYSE American listed plus OTC.
- Docs: https://developer.finra.org/docs#query_api-market_data-equity_short_interest
- Base: `https://api.finra.org/data/group/otcMarket/name/consolidatedShortInterest`
- Auth: none for this dataset in practice (a 200 with data was returned with no credentials); FINRA documents an OAuth2 FIP credential for higher limits | Limits: Anonymous access returned data with limit=1 and limit=2. Documented anonymous cap is 'limited' — FINRA states unauthenticated users get a reduced quota; EXACT anonymous calls/day and max rows per request: UNKNOWN. With a free FINRA API account the documented limits are higher but the exact numbers are UNKNOWN. History: back to ~2010s, semi-monthly settlement dates.
- Latency: semi-monthly (two settlement dates per month, published ~8 business days later) | Format: REST, returns CSV by default (JSON via Accept header)
- Relevance: Prices squeeze/meme-stock contracts and 'will X be above $Y' markets where crowding matters. Days-to-cover is the canonical squeeze input. This is the authoritative source that paid vendors resell.

**Alpha Vantage — HISTORICAL_OPTIONS and INSIDER_TRANSACTIONS (free-tier endpoints)** — Alpha Vantage `LIVE`

- HISTORICAL_OPTIONS returns a full historical option chain for a symbol on a given date with strike, expiration, bid/ask, volume, open interest, implied volatility and delta/gamma/theta/vega/rho — 15+ years of history. INSIDER_TRANSACTIONS returns parsed Form 4 activity (date, executive, title, acquisition/disposal, shares, price). Also: TIME_SERIES_DAILY, FX, crypto, 50+ technical indicators, earnings, NEWS_SENTIMENT, economic indicators.
- Docs: https://www.alphavantage.co/documentation/
- Base: `https://www.alphavantage.co/query`
- Auth: free API key (email signup); the literal key 'demo' works for a handful of sample symbols and returned real 2026 data for IBM | Limits: 25 API requests per DAY and 5 requests per MINUTE on the free key (reduced from 500/day historically — confirm before building). HISTORICAL_OPTIONS works on all key tiers including free. REALTIME_OPTIONS, TIME_SERIES_INTRADAY realtime, TIME_SERIES_DAILY_ADJUSTED, realtime bulk quotes and index endpoints are PREMIUM-ONLY.
- Latency: daily (free tier); realtime is premium | Format: REST JSON / CSV
- Relevance: The only free source of LONG-HISTORY option chains with IV and greeks — essential for backtesting whether options-implied probabilities beat prediction-market prices. Insider transactions feed 'will insiders buy/sell' and conviction-signal contracts. Crippled by 25 calls/day, so use it for backfill and calibration, not live pricing.

**FRED — fredgraph CSV (keyless) and FRED REST API** — Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis `LIVE`

- ~800,000 economic and financial time series. Directly relevant: DGS1M–DGS30 (full Treasury constant-maturity curve), T10Y2Y and T10Y3M (curve inversion), SOFR/EFFR, VIXCLS (VIX daily close), BAMLH0A0HYM2 (ICE BofA US High Yield OAS), BAMLC0A0CM (IG OAS), BAMLEMCBPIOAS (EM), CPIAUCSL, UNRATE, PAYEMS, DFF, plus FX and commodity series.
- Docs: https://fred.stlouisfed.org/docs/api/fred/
- Base: `https://api.stlouisfed.org/fred/ (keyed) and https://fred.stlouisfed.org/graph/fredgraph.csv?id=<SERIES> (keyless)`
- Auth: REST API: free API key required (verified — returns HTTP 400 'Variable api_key is not set' without one). fredgraph.csv: NO auth at all — verified returning VIXCLS through 2026-09-17. | Limits: Keyed REST API: 120 requests/minute per key (30/min unauthenticated elsewhere on the site); no documented daily cap; no paid tier exists. Full history per series (VIXCLS from 1990, DGS10 from 1962). fredgraph.csv: no published limit; a single-series request returns CSV, a MULTI-series request (id=A,B,C) returns a ZIP, not CSV.
- Latency: daily for market series (posted with a 1-day lag); monthly/quarterly for macro | Format: REST JSON/XML + keyless CSV/ZIP
- Relevance: CORE for every rates, inflation, recession and Fed-decision contract. T10Y2Y is the canonical recession-market input; BAMLH0A0HYM2 is the credit-stress input; VIXCLS gives free daily VIX history that Cboe's own CSV endpoint blocks. Zero-friction keyless CSV path makes it trivially automatable.

**US Treasury Daily Yield Curve Rates (XML/CSV)** — US Department of the Treasury `LIVE`

- Official daily par yield curve: 1M, 1.5M, 2M, 3M, 4M, 6M, 1Y, 2Y, 3Y, 5Y, 7Y, 10Y, 20Y, 30Y. Also daily Treasury bill rates, long-term rates, real (TIPS) yield curve, and high-quality market corporate bond yield curve. Verified returning 2026-09-18 data.
- Docs: https://home.treasury.gov/policy-issues/financing-the-government/interest-rate-statistics
- Base: `https://home.treasury.gov/resource-center/data-chart-center/interest-rates/daily-treasury-rates.csv/<YEAR>/all`
- Auth: none | Limits: No key, no published rate limit, no daily cap. History back to 1990. Whole-year CSV in one request (~14 KB).
- Latency: daily, published ~3:30pm ET same day | Format: CSV / XML (also an OData/XML feed)
- Relevance: Authoritative resolution source for any 'will the 10Y yield be above X' or curve-inversion contract — prediction markets that reference Treasury yields usually name Treasury.gov explicitly, so this is the settlement feed, not just a signal.

**Deribit Public API v2 (crypto options chains + perpetuals)** — Deribit `LIVE`

- Complete BTC/ETH (and alt) options instrument universe with expiries and strikes, per-instrument mark IV, bid/ask IV, greeks, open interest, and index price. Perpetual and dated futures tickers with mark price, funding, basis and volume. Also public trades, orderbook, volatility index (DVOL) and historical volatility.
- Docs: https://docs.deribit.com/
- Base: `https://www.deribit.com/api/v2/public/`
- Auth: none for all /public/ endpoints | Limits: Public endpoints are unauthenticated. Deribit documents a credit-bucket rate limiter; the anonymous (non-account) public tier is EXACTLY: UNKNOWN — Deribit publishes limits per account tier, and the anonymous allowance is not stated numerically. Observed: a single call returned the full 845 KB BTC option instrument list without throttling. History depth for public trades/candles: UNKNOWN beyond the documented tradingview chart endpoint.
- Latency: realtime (REST + WebSocket + FIX) | Format: REST JSON-RPC + WebSocket
- Relevance: Deribit IS the crypto options market (~85%+ of BTC/ETH options OI). Free, unauthenticated, full-surface IV means you can compute risk-neutral P(BTC > $100k by Dec) and compare it directly against Polymarket/Kalshi BTC price contracts — the single cleanest options-vs-prediction-market arbitrage read available for free.

**CoinGecko API (Public keyless / Demo key)** — CoinGecko `LIVE`

- Price, market cap, 24h volume, FDV, supply and historical OHLC for ~17,000 coins across ~1,000 exchanges; derivatives tickers, exchange volumes, global market dominance, categories, NFT floor prices, and on-chain DEX pool data via the GeckoTerminal endpoints.
- Docs: https://docs.coingecko.com/reference/introduction
- Base: `https://api.coingecko.com/api/v3/`
- Auth: none for the keyless public API; a free Demo key (email signup) raises and stabilises limits | Limits: Demo plan: 100 calls/minute (confirmed verbatim from docs: 'Demo plan: 100 calls/min') and 10,000 monthly call credits. Keyless: IP-based throttling SHARED ACROSS EVERY USER ON YOUR IP — CoinGecko does not publish a number for it, so the keyless rate is UNKNOWN and unreliable. 4xx and 5xx responses also count against your per-minute limit. Free-tier historical granularity is auto-downgraded to daily beyond ~90 days.
- Latency: ~1-2 minute price refresh | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: Best free breadth across the crypto long tail and the standard resolution source cited by crypto prediction markets ('per CoinGecko'). Use exchange APIs for precision on majors and CoinGecko for the 16,900 coins the exchanges don't list.

**DefiLlama API** — DefiLlama `LIVE`

- TVL for ~3,000 DeFi protocols and every chain with full daily history; stablecoin circulating supply by asset, chain and peg mechanism (verified 555 KB response covering USDT at $183B); DEX and perp volumes; fees and revenue by protocol; yields/APY; bridge flows; token unlocks/emissions schedules; treasury balances.
- Docs: https://defillama.com/docs/api
- Base: `https://api.llama.fi/ (plus stablecoins.llama.fi, yields.llama.fi, coins.llama.fi)`

Full daily history since each protocol's launch. A single /protocols call returned 8.9 MB — cache aggressively.

- Relevance: CORE for on-chain and DeFi prediction markets: 'will protocol X TVL exceed $Y', 'will USDT supply exceed $Z', 'will chain X flip chain Y'. Token-unlock schedules price supply-shock contracts. No free alternative comes close on coverage.

**Yahoo Finance chart endpoint (v8) via yfinance** — Yahoo (unofficial) `LIVE`

- OHLCV for essentially everything with a Yahoo ticker: US and international equities, ETFs, indices (^GSPC, ^VIX), FX pairs (EURUSD=X), continuous futures (ES=F, CL=F, GC=F, ZN=F), crypto. 1-minute bars for recent windows, daily/weekly/monthly for decades. Verified live: AAPL and ES=F (CME) both returned 2026 data.

- Auth: none for v8/chart. The v7 options and v7 quote endpoints now require a cookie + crumb pair — verified: a bare request returns HTTP 401 'Invalid Crumb'. yfinance handles the crumb handshake for you. | Limits: NO documented limit because there is no official API. Observed in this session: the SAME endpoint returned HTTP 429 'Too Many Requests' on one attempt and HTTP 200 minutes later from the same IP — throttling is aggressive, opaque and IP-reputation-based. Intraday 1m history capped at ~7 days, 1h at ~730 days, daily effectively full history. Treat as best-effort only.
- Latency: ~15-min delayed to near-realtime depending on exchange | Format: REST JSON (unofficial) / Python library
- Relevance: Broadest free symbol coverage on earth, including the futures (ES, NQ, CL, GC, ZN) that have no other free source after CME blocked scraping. USEFUL not CORE only because it is unofficial and will break: never make it the resolution source for a contract, only a signal/backfill source.

**SEC Form 13F Data Sets (structured institutional holdings)** — SEC Division of Economic and Risk Analysis `LIVE`

- Parsed, tabular 13F-HR holdings for every institutional manager: manager CIK/name, CUSIP, issuer, class, value, shares, investment discretion, voting authority, put/call flag. Delivered as rolling three-month ZIPs — latest verified on the SEC index page is 01jun2026-31aug2026.
- Docs: https://www.sec.gov/data-research/sec-markets-data/form-13f-data-sets
- Base: `https://www.sec.gov/files/structureddata/data/form-13f-data-sets/`
- Auth: none (User-Agent with contact email required) | Limits: No key, no rate limit beyond the 10 req/sec SEC fair-access rule. History: quarterly ZIPs from 2013 (named YYYYqN_form13f.zip) switching to rolling date-range names (01mmmYYYY-31mmmYYYY_form13f.zip) from 2024 onward. WARNING: guessing the filename pattern 404s — you must scrape the index page for the current link, and the most recent file may sit under /files/datastandardsinnovation/ rather than /files/structureddata/.
- Latency: quarterly (45-day reporting lag after quarter end) | Format: Bulk ZIP of TSV tables
- Relevance: Prices 'will fund X hold Y' and activist-stake contracts, and gives crowding/positioning context for single-name markets. The 45-day lag makes it useless for short-dated contracts — NICHE-to-USEFUL rather than core.

**SEC Insider Transactions Data Sets (Forms 3/4/5, bulk)** — SEC Division of Economic and Risk Analysis `LIVE`

- Every Section 16 insider filing parsed into relational TSVs: SUBMISSION, REPORTINGOWNER, NONDERIV_TRANS, NONDERIV_HOLDING, DERIV_TRANS, DERIV_HOLDING, FOOTNOTES. Transaction code, date, shares, price, post-transaction holdings. Verified: 2026q1_form345.zip downloaded, 13.9 MB.
- Docs: https://www.sec.gov/data-research/sec-markets-data/insider-transactions-data-sets
- Base: `https://www.sec.gov/files/structureddata/data/insider-transactions-data-sets/<YYYY>q<N>_form345.zip`
- Auth: none (User-Agent with contact email required) | Limits: No key, no cap beyond 10 req/sec. Quarterly ZIPs back to 2006. For intra-quarter freshness use the EDGAR daily index (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/daily-index/2026/QTR3/ — verified live) and parse Form 4 XML directly.
- Latency: quarterly bulk; near-realtime via the EDGAR daily index (Form 4 due within 2 business days of the trade) | Format: Bulk ZIP of TSVs + per-filing XML
- Relevance: Free, complete, authoritative insider dataset — vendors charge hundreds a month for exactly this. Cluster-buy signals feed single-name direction contracts; the daily-index path gives you a near-realtime alert stream.

- Relevance: Prices Bitcoin-specific contracts that have nothing to do with price: 'will the next difficulty adjustment be positive', 'will fees exceed N sat/vB', 'will block N be mined before date D', halving timing. Cheap, precise, and almost never wired up.

**CoinMarketCap API (Basic free tier)** — CoinMarketCap

- Latest listings, quotes, market pairs, global metrics, exchange listings, categories, and crypto map/ID reference across 63 endpoints on the free tier.
- Docs: https://coinmarketcap.com/api/documentation/v1/
- Base: `https://pro-api.coinmarketcap.com/v1/`
- Auth: free API key (email signup), passed as X-CMC_PRO_API_KEY header | Limits: Basic (free) plan: 15,000 call credits per MONTH and 50 requests per MINUTE, 63 endpoints, usage dashboard and request logs. NO HISTORICAL DATA — historical endpoints start at the paid Hobbyist tier (3 years) and above (all-time). The 15,000/month figure reflects a 2026 increase from the earlier 10,000/month; verify on signup. Reported from CMC's pricing pages — not rendered directly by me.
- Latency: ~1 minute for latest quotes | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: Frequently named as the resolution source in crypto prediction-market rules, which is its main value — CoinGecko is better on coverage and DefiLlama better on fundamentals. The absence of any free history is disqualifying for modelling.

#### Repos

- `OpenBB-finance/OpenBB` — 73,300-star open-source data platform that normalises 100+ financial data providers behind one Python/REST/MCP interface; pushed 2026-09-19, actively maintained. · Steal the provider-abstraction layer wholesale. It already has adapters, credential handling, rate-limit backoff and a normalised schema for most of the feeds in this catalogue (FRED, SEC, Tiingo, Alpha Vantage, Polygon/Massive, Finnhub, Intrinio, Yahoo). It also ships an MCP server, so an AI synthesis layer can query it directly. Single biggest shortcut to a Bloomberg-terminal-style backend.
- `ccxt/ccxt` — 44,000-star unified crypto trading/market-data API across 100+ exchanges in Python/TS/C#/PHP/Go/Java/Rust; pushed 2026-09-20. Its own description now says it covers 'more than 100 crypto exchanges AND PREDICTION MARKETS'. · One interface for spot, perps, funding rates, open interest and order books across every venue, with rate limiting and geo-fallback built in. Critically, CCXT has added prediction-market venues — so the same library can fetch both the market price and the underlying reference price you want to compare it against.
- `ranaroussi/yfinance` — 25,300-star Yahoo Finance scraper; pushed 2026-09-17, still under active maintenance. · Handles the cookie+crumb handshake that makes Yahoo's v7 options and quote endpoints work at all (a bare request returns 401 Invalid Crumb — verified). Also handles curl_cffi TLS impersonation to dodge blocking. Read its session/crumb code even if you don't use the library. Treat output as best-effort: it is unofficial and returns 429 unpredictably.
- `dgunning/edgartools` — 2,700-star MIT-licensed Python library for SEC EDGAR: 10-K/8-K parsing, XBRL financials, Form 3/4/5, 13F and ADV; pushed 2026-09-20. · Saves you writing 13F and Form 4 parsers by hand — the two hardest bulk datasets in this catalogue. Clean typed API over exactly the SEC endpoints and ZIPs verified above, and it already respects the SEC User-Agent and 10 req/sec fair-access rule.
- `akfamily/akshare` — 22,700-star Python interface aggregating a very large number of free financial data sources (heavy China/Asia coverage plus global futures, options, macro and alternative data); pushed 2026-09-20. · The best single source of ideas for non-US and non-obvious free feeds — exchange websites, regulator portals, commodity boards. If you want global breadth beyond the US-centric list above, mine its source tree for endpoint URLs.
- `wilsonfreitas/awesome-quant` — 29,700-star curated index of quantitative-finance libraries, data sources and tools; pushed 2026-09-20. · The canonical discovery index for this domain. Use it to enumerate additional data wrappers and pricing libraries rather than re-searching from scratch.
- `JerBouma/FinanceDatabase` — 9,200-star database of 300,000+ symbols — equities, ETFs, funds, indices, currencies, cryptocurrencies, money markets — with sector, industry, country and exchange metadata; pushed 2026-09-20. · Solves symbology, which is the unglamorous blocker for any aggregation panel. Gives you the universe list and the cross-reference table to join Yahoo tickers, Cboe symbols, SEC CIKs and exchange codes. Companion JerBouma/FinanceToolkit (5,400 stars) computes 150+ ratios on top of it.
- `domokane/FinancePy` — 3,100-star Python derivatives pricing and risk library covering equity, FX, rates and credit derivatives; pushed 2026-09-19. · This is the piece that turns an option chain into a prediction-market-comparable number. Use it to build the risk-neutral density from the Cboe/Deribit strike ladders (Breeden-Litzenberger / butterfly spreads) and produce P(S>K by T) directly. lballabio/QuantLib (7,600 stars, C++ with Python bindings) is the heavier-duty alternative.
- `pydata/pandas-datareader` — 3,300-star library pulling from FRED, Stooq, World Bank, OECD, Nasdaq Data Link, Fama-French and more into DataFrames; pushed 2026-07-21. · Fastest path to FRED and the macro/academic datasets. Note its Stooq reader is now unreliable because Stooq sits behind a JavaScript challenge (see deadEnds).
- `mortada/fredapi` — 1,700-star Python wrapper for FRED and ALFRED (vintage/as-of-date economic data); pushed 2026-01-28. · ALFRED support is the differentiator: it gives you the value of a series AS IT WAS FIRST PUBLISHED, before revisions. Essential for honest backtesting of macro-release prediction markets — using revised data is a classic look-ahead bug.
- `alpacahq/alpaca-py` — 1,500-star official Alpaca SDK including the options data client; pushed 2026-09-18. · The cleanest programmatic path to free OPRA Indicative options chains and greeks (200 req/min on the free Basic plan, paper account is enough) — a rate-limited rather than quota-limited free options source, unlike marketdata.app.
- `Finnhub-Stock-API/finnhub-python` — 1,081-star official Finnhub Python client; pushed 2026-06-24. · Fastest way to empirically map Finnhub's free/premium boundary, which their Swagger spec does not encode (only 1 of 116 operations carries premium language — verified). Loop the estimate/insider/institutional endpoints with a free key and record which return PremiumRequired.
- `RomelTorres/alpha_vantage` — 4,900-star Python wrapper for Alpha Vantage; pushed 2026-07-26. · Handles the 5-calls/minute throttle and pagination for you. Relevant mainly for the two free-tier endpoints that matter — HISTORICAL_OPTIONS (15+ years of chains with IV and greeks) and INSIDER_TRANSACTIONS.
- `microsoft/qlib` — 48,700-star AI-oriented quant research platform with data ingestion, alignment and point-in-time handling; pushed 2026-09-17. · Its data layer solves point-in-time correctness and survivorship bias across heterogeneous sources — the two failure modes that silently invalidate a research panel built from mixed free feeds.
- `QuantConnect/Lean` — 21,700-star open-source algorithmic trading engine with a mature multi-asset data model covering equities, options, futures, FX and crypto; pushed 2026-09-18. · Its data format and corporate-action/contract-roll handling for options and futures are production-grade and worth copying rather than reinventing, especially option symbology (OCC) and continuous futures construction.
- `DefiLlama/DefiLlama-Adapters` — 1,255-star repository of per-protocol TVL adapters powering the DefiLlama API; pushed 2026-09-20. · Documents exactly how each protocol's TVL is computed, which you need to defend a number when a prediction market resolves on 'protocol X TVL'. Also a map of which on-chain contracts matter per protocol.
- `jeff3388/awesome-financial-data-apis` — Small (5-star) but recent curated list of free and paid financial data APIs with claimed 2026 availability status and rate-limit reference; pushed 2026-04-08. · Useful as a cross-check list for anything missed here. Low star count means LOW TRUST — verify every claim in it against the live endpoint, as several widely-repeated limits in this domain turned out to be stale.

---

### Companies & Corporate Events

#### CORE

**SEC EDGAR Full-Text Search API** — US Securities and Exchange Commission `LIVE`

- Full-text search across the body of every EDGAR filing and exhibit from 2001-present. Returns CIK, ticker, form type, filing date, period, accession number, SIC and the matching document filename. Lets you query exact legal phrases that define a corporate event: 'definitive merger agreement', 'Chapter 11', 'Departure of Directors or Certain Officers'. Verified live: query for \"chapter 11\" on form 8-K returned real hits; query for \"Departure of Directors or Certain Officers\" on 8-K returned >10,000 hits.
- Docs: https://www.sec.gov/search-filings/edgar-search-assistance/accessing-edgar-data
- Auth: none (a descriptive User-Agent header with contact email is mandatory; requests without it are 403'd) | Limits: 10 requests/second/IP (SEC Fair Access policy); exceeding it blocks the IP ~10 minutes with 403. HARD RESULT CAP VERIFIED: from+size must be <= 10000 — the API returns 'Result window is too large' beyond 10,000 hits per query, so broad queries must be date-sliced. History depth: 2001-present. No daily cap documented.
- Latency: sub-minute (index updated continuously during filing hours) | Format: REST JSON (Elasticsearch passthrough at https://efts.sec.gov/LATEST/search-index?q=...&forms=8-K)
- Relevance: The single highest-value feed for US corporate-event contracts. Settles 'will the merger be announced/terminated', 'will the CEO depart' (8-K Item 5.02 phrase match), 'will X file Chapter 11', 'will X file an S-1'. Because it matches the legally-required disclosure language, it fires at the moment of the disclosure, not when news picks it up.

**SEC EDGAR Submissions API** — US Securities and Exchange Commission `LIVE`

- Per-company JSON of the full filing history: every form type, filing date, report date, accession number, primary document, plus entity metadata (CIK, tickers, exchanges, SIC, EIN, LEI, former names, business address). Verified live against CIK0000320193 (Apple, 164 KB) and CIK0001318605 (Tesla).
- Docs: https://www.sec.gov/search-filings/edgar-application-programming-interfaces
- Auth: none (User-Agent with contact email required) | Limits: 10 requests/second/IP. Most recent 1,000 filings inline; older filings paginated into additional JSON files referenced in the same response. Full history back to 1993/1994. No daily cap documented. Bulk alternative: submissions.zip (whole-corpus, ~1 GB).
- Latency: sub-minute | Format: REST JSON at https://data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK##########.json
- Relevance: The canonical resolver for 'has company X filed form Y by date Z'. Used to settle IPO registration (S-1), delisting (25-NSE), bankruptcy disclosures, and to build the watchlist of tickers a market maker must monitor.

**SEC EDGAR 'getcurrent' Atom RSS (real-time filings by form type)** — US Securities and Exchange Commission `LIVE`

- A live push-style Atom feed of filings as they hit EDGAR, filterable by form type. Verified live 2026-09-20 20:20 EDT returning that minute's 8-Ks (VisionWave Holdings, RiverNorth, Credit Acceptance Corp, BCB Bancorp). Separately verified live for type=S-1, type=424B4 (IPO pricing), type=25-NSE (delisting), type=D (private raise), type=4 (insider transactions).
- Docs: https://www.sec.gov/about/updates/rss-feeds
- Auth: none (User-Agent required) | Limits: 10 requests/second/IP. count parameter maxes at 100 entries per pull; the feed is a rolling window of only the most recent filings, so polling must be frequent enough not to miss entries (practically: poll every 10-60s for high-volume forms like Form 4). No history — it is a tail, not an archive; pair with the daily-index for backfill.
- Latency: realtime (sub-minute from EDGAR acceptance) | Format: Atom XML at https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcurrent&type=8-K&output=atom
- Relevance: This is the fastest legal signal in US corporate events and it is completely free. Contracts on 'will the CEO depart', 'will the deal be announced this week', 'will X IPO by date' move on 8-K/S-1/424B4 acceptance. Polling this feed puts you ahead of newswires by seconds to minutes.

**SEC XBRL frames API** — US Securities and Exchange Commission `LIVE`

- Cross-sectional slice of one us-gaap/ifrs-full concept for ALL reporting companies in one calendar period — e.g. every filer's Revenues for CY2024Q1I, or EarningsPerShareDiluted for CY2025Q4. Each row carries CIK, entity name, accession number, the value and the units. Verified live for us-gaap/Revenues/USD/CY2024Q1I and us-gaap/EarningsPerShareDiluted/USD-per-shares/CY2025Q4.
- Docs: https://www.sec.gov/search-filings/edgar-application-programming-interfaces
- Auth: none (User-Agent required) | Limits: 10 requests/second/IP. One concept + one unit + one period per call. History: back to roughly 2009 when XBRL tagging became mandatory (large filers first, phased). No daily cap documented.
- Latency: daily (populated as filings are accepted and tagged) | Format: REST JSON at https://data.sec.gov/api/xbrl/frames/{taxonomy}/{tag}/{unit}/{period}.json
- Relevance: Settles 'earnings beat' contracts on the actual reported number rather than a vendor's normalization, and is the free way to build a peer-comparison panel without a paid fundamentals vendor. Critical because it is the SEC's own arithmetic, not a third party's.

**SEC XBRL companyfacts API + bulk companyfacts.zip** — US Securities and Exchange Commission `LIVE`

- Every XBRL fact ever reported by one company, all concepts, all periods, with the accession number and filing date of each. Verified live: CIK0000320193 returned 3,789,099 bytes. Bulk mirror verified live via HTTP HEAD: content-length 1,409,212,553 bytes (1.4 GB), content-type application/zip.
- Docs: https://www.sec.gov/search-filings/edgar-application-programming-interfaces
- Auth: none (User-Agent required) | Limits: 10 requests/second/IP for the per-company endpoint. The bulk zip is one 1.4 GB download covering all filers — the correct way to backfill without burning the rate limit. History: ~2009-present. No daily cap documented.
- Latency: daily | Format: REST JSON + bulk ZIP
- Relevance: Builds the historical earnings-surprise distribution you need to price an 'earnings beat' contract. Without a per-company history of reported-vs-consensus you are guessing the base rate.

**SEC EDGAR full-index and daily-index** — US Securities and Exchange Commission `LIVE`

- Complete, gap-free archive of every filing ever accepted, as daily and quarterly index files (company.idx, form.idx, master.idx, and JSON/XBRL variants). Verified live: 2026/QTR2/company.idx returned 55,106,679 bytes; daily-index/2026/QTR3/ directory listing returned 200.
- Docs: https://www.sec.gov/os/accessing-edgar-data
- Auth: none (User-Agent required) | Limits: 10 requests/second/IP. History: 1993-present. Files are large (a single quarterly company.idx is ~55 MB) so fetch cost is bandwidth, not call count. No daily cap documented.
- Latency: daily (daily-index posted each business evening) | Format: Fixed-width/pipe-delimited .idx text, plus .json variants, over HTTP directory listing
- Relevance: The backfill and reconciliation layer. The getcurrent RSS is a lossy tail; this is the authoritative record you replay against to prove you missed nothing — essential if a contract settles on 'was a filing made by date X'.

**UK Companies House Public Data API** — Companies House (UK Government) `LIVE`

- Full UK company register: company profile, status (active/liquidation/dissolved), incorporation date, SIC codes, registered office, officers (appointments and terminations with dates), persons with significant control, charges, insolvency cases, and the complete filing history with document IDs. Probe returned 401 Unauthorized — endpoint is alive in 2026 and key-gated, not dead.
- Docs: https://developer-specs.company-information.service.gov.uk/companies-house-public-data-api/reference
- Auth: free API key (register a Companies House developer account, create an application, use the key as HTTP Basic username with empty password) | Limits: VERIFIED FROM DOCS: 600 requests per 5-minute rolling window; a 429 is returned on breach, and Companies House states it reserves the right to ban applications that repeatedly exceed or attempt to bypass the limit. Higher limits available on request. History: full register history, no depth cap. Free of charge.
- Latency: hourly to daily (register updates as filings are processed) | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: CORE for any UK-entity contract. Officer appointment/termination records settle 'will the CEO depart' for UK plcs with a legal timestamp. Insolvency case records settle UK bankruptcy contracts. Company status transition to 'liquidation' is the cleanest possible resolution source.

**UK Companies House Streaming API** — Companies House (UK Government) `LIVE`

- Long-lived HTTP streaming connections that push every change to the UK register in real time, on separate streams for filings, companies, officers, persons-with-significant-control, charges and insolvency. Probe to https://stream.companieshouse.gov.uk/filings returned 401 — stream endpoint alive in 2026, key-gated.
- Docs: https://developer-specs.company-information.service.gov.uk/streaming-api/guides/overview
- Auth: free streaming API key (separate key type from the REST key; request via the developer portal) | Limits: UNKNOWN — Companies House documents the streaming API as connection-based rather than request-count-based and the rate-limiting guide does not state a numeric stream limit. Documented behaviour is one connection per stream per key with a timepoint for resume-after-disconnect. Free of charge. Confirm your own key's allowance before building on it.
- Latency: realtime (push) | Format: HTTP long-poll streaming, newline-delimited JSON
- Relevance: Removes polling latency entirely for UK corporate events. The insolvency and officers streams are the fastest legal notification of a UK bankruptcy or executive departure available at any price.

**GLEIF LEI API v1 + Golden Copy bulk files** — Global Legal Entity Identifier Foundation `LIVE`

- The global registry of Legal Entity Identifiers: legal name, all former legal names, legal and headquarters address, registration status (ISSUED/LAPSED/RETIRED), entity status (ACTIVE/INACTIVE), legal form, and — critically — the direct and ultimate parent relationships and the entity-expiry reason (MERGED, DISSOLVED). Verified live: query returned meta.goldenCopy.publishDate 2026-09-20T08:00:00Z, i.e. refreshed the day of this research.
- Docs: https://www.gleif.org/en/lei-data/gleif-api
- Auth: none for the public API | Limits: UNKNOWN — GLEIF publishes no numeric rate limit and the live response returned no RateLimit/X-RateLimit headers when inspected. Pagination is page[size] (default small, documented max 200). Golden Copy full files are published 3x daily (00:00, 08:00, 16:00 UTC) as unmetered bulk downloads — use those rather than hammering the API. Full history of all LEI records including retired ones.
- Latency: 3x daily (Golden Copy), continuous for the API | Format: REST JSON:API + bulk XML/CSV/JSON Golden Copy files
- Relevance: The only free, global, cross-jurisdiction corporate identity graph. Resolves ticker-to-legal-entity-to-ultimate-parent so you can tell whether a filing, a lawsuit and a contract award refer to the same company. Entity expiry reason MERGED is a hard, machine-readable settlement signal for 'did the merger close'.

**USAspending.gov API v2** — US Treasury / Bureau of the Fiscal Service `LIVE`

- Every federal contract, grant, loan and direct payment: recipient name and UEI, awarding agency and sub-agency, obligated and outlayed amounts, NAICS/PSC codes, period of performance, place of performance, and the full transaction history of modifications. Verified live: toptier_agencies returned 52,652 bytes of 2026 fiscal-year data (active_fy 2026, active_fq 4); a specific award endpoint returned 200.
- Docs: https://api.usaspending.gov/docs/endpoints
- Auth: none | Limits: UNKNOWN as a published number — USAspending documents no explicit rate limit and the live response carried no RateLimit headers. Practical constraints that ARE documented: search endpoints are POST with a page-size cap of 100 and a 'limit + page' ceiling around 10,000 records per query, so large pulls must be filtered or taken from the bulk 'Custom Award Data' download endpoint. History: FY2008-present. Free.
- Latency: daily (contract data flows from FPDS with a documented lag of up to ~1-3 days; grants monthly) | Format: REST JSON (most search endpoints are POST)
- Relevance: Directly settles 'will company X win the Y contract' and 'will the contract value exceed $Z' markets. Also a leading revenue signal for defence, aerospace and govtech names ahead of earnings. The award-modification history lets you price 'will the contract be extended/terminated'.

**CourtListener REST API v4 + RECAP Archive** — Free Law Project `LIVE`

- Federal and state court opinions, plus the RECAP Archive of PACER dockets — docket entries, documents, parties and attorneys — for federal district, bankruptcy and appellate courts. Verified live: /api/rest/v4/courts/ returned 3,359 courts; a RECAP search for 'antitrust' returned count 151,993 dockets across 1,620,036 documents, cursor-paginated, dated 2026-09-20.
- Docs: https://wiki.free.law/c/courtlistener/help/api/rest/v4/overview
- Auth: free account + API token (Authorization: Token <token>); many endpoints also respond unauthenticated | Limits: VERIFIED FROM DOCS AND SEVERE: 5 requests/minute, 50 requests/hour, 125 requests/day for a free authenticated user, on rolling windows. Unauthenticated limits are not formally documented. Higher limits only via Free Law Project membership or a commercial partnership. History: opinions back to the 1700s; RECAP coverage is crowd-sourced so it is DENSE but NOT COMPLETE — absence of a docket in RECAP does NOT prove absence of a case.
- Latency: minutely for RECAP webhook subscribers; otherwise hours to days depending on whether someone has pulled the docket from PACER | Format: REST JSON, cursor-paginated; webhooks available
- Relevance: Settles corporate-litigation, antitrust-suit and Chapter 11 contracts with the docket itself. The 125/day free ceiling makes it unusable as a polling firehose — use it as a confirmation/resolution oracle, and use the free PACER court RSS feeds (below) for detection.

**PACER court RSS feeds (per-district)** — Administrative Office of the US Courts `LIVE`

- Per-district RSS of newly-filed docket entries, including bankruptcy courts. Verified live: https://ecf.deb.uscourts.gov/cgi-bin/rss_outside.pl (District of Delaware Bankruptcy — the venue where most large US corporate Chapter 11 cases are filed) returned 21,885 bytes.
- Docs: https://pacer.uscourts.gov/file-case/court-cmecf-lookup
- Auth: none for the RSS feed itself (the linked documents behind it are PACER-paywalled) | Limits: No documented numeric limit on the RSS endpoints. COVERAGE IS THE REAL LIMIT: not every district enables its RSS feed, and those that do vary in which event types they publish — CourtListener maintains a per-court map of which feeds exist and what they carry. Feed is a rolling window (typically ~24h of entries), so it must be polled continuously; it is not an archive.
- Latency: sub-minute to minutely | Format: RSS XML
- Relevance: The cheapest real-time Chapter 11 detector that exists. Delaware and SDNY bankruptcy RSS will show a major corporate filing within roughly a minute, for free, versus the 125/day CourtListener API ceiling. Detect here, confirm via CourtListener, settle on the 8-K.

**GOV.UK Search API (CMA merger cases)** — UK Government Digital Service / Competition and Markets Authority `LIVE`

- Structured JSON over all GOV.UK content filtered by format. filter_format=cma_case returns every CMA merger inquiry, market investigation and antitrust case with title, description, case type, outcome and dates. Verified live: returned a current 2026 case — the CMA investigation into Co-operative Group's completed acquisition of The Southern Co-operative.
- Docs: https://docs.publishing.service.gov.uk/repos/search-api.html
- Auth: none | Limits: UNKNOWN — GDS publishes no numeric rate limit for the public search API and no RateLimit headers were returned. Documented constraints: count parameter caps at 1,000 per request with start-based pagination. Full GOV.UK content history. Free.
- Latency: hourly to daily (publishes as CMA updates the case page) | Format: REST JSON at https://www.gov.uk/api/search.json?filter_format=cma_case
- Relevance: CORE for 'will the merger be blocked/cleared in the UK'. The CMA is now a genuinely deal-dispositive regulator for global tech and pharma deals, and this is a free structured feed of its entire caseload including Phase 1/Phase 2 transitions and final outcomes.

**FTC press release RSS (competition)** — US Federal Trade Commission `LIVE`

- Real-time feed of FTC competition-bureau announcements: merger challenges, second requests, consent orders, complaints filed, and HSR-related actions. Verified live: returned 118,059 bytes of current RSS.
- Docs: https://www.ftc.gov/news-events/stay-connected/ftc-rss-feeds
- Auth: none | Limits: No documented limit. Rolling-window feed (most recent items only) — not an archive; backfill from ftc.gov/legal-library. Free.
- Latency: sub-minute to hourly (fires when FTC publishes) | Format: RSS XML
- Relevance: An FTC complaint or second request is the single event that most reprices a 'will the merger close' contract. This feed carries it for free at publication time. Pair with the DOJ OPA feed for the other half of US antitrust.

**DOJ Office of Public Affairs news RSS** — US Department of Justice `LIVE`

- All DOJ press releases including Antitrust Division merger challenges, criminal corporate resolutions, deferred prosecution agreements and False Claims Act settlements. Verified live: https://www.justice.gov/feeds/opa/justice-news.xml returned 200 with 56,029 bytes.
- Docs: https://www.justice.gov/news/rss
- Auth: none | Limits: No documented limit. Rolling window of recent releases. Free. NOTE: the Antitrust-Division-specific RSS path returned 404 in testing — use the OPA feed and filter on component/topic rather than assuming a per-division feed exists.
- Latency: sub-minute to hourly | Format: RSS XML
- Relevance: DOJ Antitrust suing to block a deal is the highest-impact single event for merger-close contracts. Corporate criminal resolutions and monitorships also settle 'will X be charged/settle by date Y' markets.

**GDELT 2.0 (raw 15-minute files + DOC 2.0 API)** — The GDELT Project `LIVE`

- Every news article GDELT monitors worldwide, machine-coded for events, entities, organizations, themes and tone, in 100+ languages. Raw files verified live: http://data.gdeltproject.org/gdeltv2/lastupdate.txt returned 200 pointing at 20260921003000.export.CSV.zip, 20260921003000.mentions.CSV.zip and a 2.6 MB GKG file — i.e. a file stamped within 15 minutes of this research.
- Docs: https://blog.gdeltproject.org/gdelt-2-0-our-global-world/
- Auth: none | Limits: Raw 15-minute CSV/ZIP files: no documented limit, unmetered bulk HTTP. DOC 2.0 API: VERIFIED BY LIVE 429 — the API returned 'Please limit requests to one every 5 seconds', i.e. 1 request per 5 seconds (12/minute), and GDELT explicitly directs high-traffic users to the ngrams dataset instead. DOC API history window is 2017-present with a 3-month default; raw event files go back to 2015 for v2 (1979 for v1). Free.
- Latency: realtime (new file every 15 minutes, 96 files/day) | Format: CSV bulk over HTTP + REST JSON DOC API
- Relevance: The 'God's-eye' news layer. For corporate events it is the wide net that catches announcements no regulator files — layoffs reported by local press, plant closures, executive resignations abroad, product launches. Low precision, very high recall: use it for DETECTION and settle on a filing or registry. The raw-file path is the correct one at scale; the DOC API's 1-per-5-seconds makes it a lookup tool, not a firehose.

**Alpha Vantage EARNINGS_CALENDAR** — Alpha Vantage `LIVE`

- Forward earnings calendar as CSV: symbol, company name, report date, fiscal period ending, consensus EPS estimate, currency and time-of-day (pre/post market). Verified live with the public demo key: returned 257,277 bytes of real forward data starting 2026-09-21 (ABVX, AIV, CBAT, CHRN...) with pre/post-market flags.
- Docs: https://www.alphavantage.co/documentation/
- Auth: free API key (email registration); the literal key 'demo' works for this endpoint, which is how it was verified | Limits: VERIFIED AND SEVERE: the free tier is now 25 API requests/DAY at 5 requests/minute. It was 500/day, then 100/day, now 25/day. Premium starts at $49.99/mo for 75 req/min. CRITICAL MITIGATION: EARNINGS_CALENDAR returns the ENTIRE 3-month forward calendar in a SINGLE call as CSV — so one request per day is enough to maintain the whole calendar. horizon parameter accepts 3month/6month/12month.
- Latency: daily | Format: CSV (this endpoint returns CSV, not JSON)
- Relevance: Directly settles the DATE half of every 'earnings beat' contract — you cannot price an earnings market without knowing when the report lands and whether it is pre- or post-market. Given the 25/day cap this is a once-daily calendar sync, not a queryable API. Pair with SEC XBRL frames for the actual reported number.

**WARN mass-layoff notices (state-by-state)** — US state labor departments (CA EDD, NY DOL, and 50+ others); no federal API `LIVE`

- Legally-mandated advance notice of plant closings and mass layoffs under the WARN Act: employer name, location, number of employees affected, notice date, effective date, and whether it is a closure or a layoff. Verified live as PUBLISHED PAGES, not APIs: California EDD WARN page returned 200 (159,578 bytes), New York DOL WARN page returned 200 (53,582 bytes), DOL's WARN landing page returned 200.
- Docs: https://www.dol.gov/agencies/eta/layoffs/warn
- Auth: none | Limits: NOT AN API — there is NO federal WARN API and no unified endpoint. Each state publishes its own HTML page, XLSX or CSV on its own schedule with its own schema; a handful expose CSV/JSON, most do not. Rate limits: none documented, but this is scraping, not an API. History: varies by state, typically 2-10 years retained. Free. The practical route is biglocalnews/warn-scraper (see githubRepos), which normalises 50+ state sources.
- Latency: weekly (states update on their own cadence; some weekly, some as-received) | Format: scrape-only (HTML/XLSX/CSV per state) — normalise via warn-scraper
- Relevance: CORE data, awkward delivery. WARN filings are the only LEGALLY REQUIRED advance disclosure of layoffs, and they land 60-90 days BEFORE the layoff and usually before the press release — a genuine information edge for 'will X announce layoffs by date Y' contracts. Worth the scraping cost precisely because it is not a clean API.

#### USEFUL

**SEC Financial Statement Data Sets + Insider Transactions Data Sets** — SEC Division of Economic and Risk Analysis (DERA) `LIVE`

- Quarterly flat-file dumps. Financial Statement sets give num/sub/pre/tag tables for every XBRL filing that quarter. Insider Transactions sets give parsed Form 3/4/5 data (who bought/sold, how much, when). Verified live: 2026q1.zip financial statements = 85,259,424 bytes; 2026q1_form345.zip = 13,874,904 bytes.
- Docs: https://www.sec.gov/data-research/sec-markets-data/financial-statement-data-sets
- Auth: none (User-Agent required) | Limits: No API call limit — these are static file downloads subject to the same 10 req/s courtesy rate. History: financial statement sets from 2009Q2; insider transaction sets from 2006. Released quarterly with roughly a 1-6 week lag after quarter end.
- Latency: quarterly | Format: CSV/TSV bulk inside ZIP
- Relevance: Insider Form 4 clusters are a leading indicator for both 'CEO departs' and 'company gets acquired' contracts — executives transacting ahead of a disclosure is a measurable prior. The financial statement sets give you a clean panel for earnings-surprise modelling without parsing raw XBRL.

**SAM.gov Get Opportunities API** — US General Services Administration

- Pre-award federal solicitations: presolicitations, sources sought, combined synopsis, award notices, and justifications — with NAICS, set-aside type, response deadline, and the awardee once awarded. This is the upstream feed that USAspending only sees after award.
- Docs: https://open.gsa.gov/api/get-opportunities-public-api/
- Auth: free API key from the SAM.gov Account Details page (requires a SAM.gov account; key passed as api_key query parameter) | Limits: VERIFIED via GSA/community documentation: 10 requests/day for a personal key with no SAM.gov role, 1,000 requests/day for a registered non-federal user, 10,000/day for a federal system account. Non-federal accounts are NOT eligible to apply for an increase. Max page size 1,000 records. History: the API's postedFrom/postedTo window is capped at 1 year per request. NOTE: unauthenticated probes to api.sam.gov returned 404, not 401 — the key must be present in the query string or the route does not resolve.
- Latency: daily | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: Prices 'will X win the contract' BEFORE award, which is where the edge is. The response-deadline field gives you the date by which a market must resolve. The 1,000/day non-federal ceiling is the binding constraint — budget calls carefully.

**Federal Register API v1** — US National Archives / GPO `LIVE`

- Every document published in the Federal Register — rules, proposed rules, notices and presidential documents — with full text, agency, docket numbers, effective dates and CFR references. Verified live twice: a term search for 'merger' returned 10,000 matching documents, and an agency filter for federal-trade-commission returned 200.
- Docs: https://www.federalregister.gov/developers/documentation/api/v1
- Auth: none | Limits: UNKNOWN as a published number — no rate limit is documented and no RateLimit headers were returned on the live probe. Documented constraints: per_page caps at 1,000; the result set for a single query caps at 2,000 documents (use date slicing beyond that). History: 1994-present full text, 1936-1993 as scanned PDF. Free.
- Latency: daily (published each federal business day at 06:00 ET; public-inspection documents available the prior afternoon) | Format: REST JSON/CSV, plus RSS
- Relevance: Settles regulatory-action contracts: FTC/DOJ consent decrees, FCC and FERC approvals that gate merger closings, FDA notices, export-control rules. The public-inspection endpoint gives a several-hour head start on the official publication.

**openFDA enforcement APIs (drug, device, food) + device recall** — US Food and Drug Administration `LIVE`

- Every FDA recall/enforcement action with recalling firm name and address, product description, reason for recall, classification (Class I/II/III), quantity, distribution pattern, recall initiation date and status. Four separate endpoints verified live independently: /drug/enforcement.json, /device/enforcement.json, /device/recall.json, /food/enforcement.json — all 200.
- Docs: https://open.fda.gov/apis/authentication/
- Auth: none required; a free API key (api.data.gov) raises the limit substantially | Limits: VERIFIED FROM THE OFFICIAL AUTH PAGE: without an API key, 240 requests/minute per IP AND 1,000 requests/day per IP. With a free API key, 240 requests/minute AND 120,000 requests/day per key. Pagination: limit caps at 1,000 records per call, skip caps at 25,000 (use search_after / the download endpoint beyond that). History: recall data back to ~2004 depending on endpoint.
- Latency: weekly (FDA publishes the Enforcement Report weekly; some device data updates more often) | Format: REST JSON, plus bulk downloadable JSON partitions
- Relevance: Class I recalls are share-price events for pharma, medtech and food companies and settle 'will X issue a recall' contracts outright. The 1,000/day no-key ceiling is generous enough to poll every endpoint hourly; get the free key anyway.

**CPSC SaferProducts Recall REST API** — US Consumer Product Safety Commission `LIVE`

- Every CPSC consumer-product recall: recall number and date, full description, the named manufacturers/importers/distributors and retailers, hazard description, injury count, remedy, and units affected. Verified live and unusually good: a single unauthenticated call with RecallDateStart=2026-01-01 returned 1,368,013 bytes containing 448 recalls YTD 2026, most recent dated 2026-09-17 (Charbroil electric grills).
- Docs: https://www.cpsc.gov/Newsroom/Recall-Web-Services-and-API
- Auth: none | Limits: UNKNOWN — CPSC publishes no numeric rate limit and none was returned in headers. Practically irrelevant: the entire year-to-date corpus comes back in ONE call, so a daily poll is sufficient. History: recalls back to 1973. Free.
- Latency: daily | Format: REST JSON (also XML/CSV) at https://www.saferproducts.gov/RestWebServices/Recall
- Relevance: Settles consumer-product recall contracts directly, and the named-firm field lets you attribute a recall to a listed parent. Very few free feeds hand you a complete labelled corpus in one request — this one does.

**USPTO Open Data Portal (ODP) APIs** — US Patent and Trademark Office `LIVE`

- The consolidated successor to PatentsView and the legacy Developer Hub. Covers patent search, Patent File Wrapper (full prosecution history and correspondence), patent assignments (ownership transfers), PTAB proceedings, and Bulk Datasets download. Probes to https://api.uspto.gov/api/v1/... returned 401 Unauthorized — alive in 2026 and key-gated, and this is now the ONLY supported USPTO patent API.
- Docs: https://data.uspto.gov/apis/getting-started
- Auth: free API key, but note the 2026 tightening: since 18 June 2026 you must sign in with a valid USPTO.gov account to access ODP, and since 18 August 2026 four additional profile fields are mandatory or you lose key access | Limits: VERIFIED FROM USPTO DOCS: 60 requests/minute. Per-key Metadata and Patent File Wrapper thresholds are shown on your own Manage API Key page and are not published globally. Bulk downloads are capped at 20 downloads of the same file per API key per year (21st request returns HTTP 429). USPTO states limits may be adjusted. Free of charge. IMPORTANT: PatentsView-issued keys are NOT valid for ODP — you must obtain a new ODP key.
- Latency: weekly (patent grants publish Tuesdays; applications publish Thursdays) | Format: REST JSON + bulk dataset downloads
- Relevance: Prices 'will X be granted a patent on Y' and, via the assignment records, detects IP transfers that front-run an acquisition. PTAB proceedings settle patent-validity-challenge contracts. Moderate relevance overall — patents are slow-moving relative to most corporate-event markets.

**Hacker News Search API (Algolia)** — Algolia / Y Combinator `LIVE`

- Full-text search and date-sorted retrieval over every HN story and comment, with points, comment counts, author and timestamp. Verified live: an unauthenticated query for 'layoffs' returned 28,577 bytes of current results.
- Docs: https://hn.algolia.com/api
- Auth: none | Limits: UNKNOWN as a currently-published number — the documented figure historically cited is 10,000 requests/hour per IP, but no RateLimit headers were returned on the live probe and Algolia does not restate it on the API page. Treat 10,000/hr as indicative, not verified. hitsPerPage caps at 1,000. Full HN history from 2006. Free.
- Latency: realtime (indexed within seconds of posting) | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: The best free early-warning layer for private tech companies, which have no SEC filings at all. Layoff threads, 'X is shutting down', acquisition rumours and launch announcements surface on HN hours to days before press coverage. Essential for startup-outcome contracts; weak as a settlement source.

**TED (Tenders Electronic Daily) Search API v3** — Publications Office of the European Union `LIVE`

- Every above-threshold public procurement notice in the EU: contract notices, award notices with the winning company named, values, CPV codes and deadlines. Verified live: an unauthenticated POST to https://api.ted.europa.eu/v3/notices/search returned real notice data with publication numbers and per-language document links. (A GET returns 405 — it is POST-only, which is why casual probes make it look dead.)
- Docs: https://docs.ted.europa.eu/api/index.html
- Auth: none for the public search API | Limits: UNKNOWN — the Publications Office does not publish a numeric rate limit for the v3 search API and none was returned in headers. Documented: a limit parameter per request with scroll/pagination tokens for large result sets. History: TED notices back to 1993 with full-text from 2011. Free, open licence.
- Latency: daily (notices publish each EU working day) | Format: REST JSON (POST search) + bulk XML packages
- Relevance: The EU counterpart to SAM.gov + USAspending. Settles 'will X win the European contract' and is a revenue signal for European defence, rail, telecom and construction names. Underused because the POST-only interface hides it from API directories.

**Finnhub Stock API (free tier)** — Finnhub `LIVE`

- Earnings calendar, IPO calendar, company news, basic financials, SEC filing metadata and real-time US quotes, plus WebSocket trade streaming. Probes to /calendar/earnings, /calendar/ipo, /stock/symbol and /company-news all returned 401 'Invalid API key' — every endpoint path is alive in 2026 and key-gated.
- Docs: https://finnhub.io/docs/api
- Auth: free API key (email registration); passed as X-Finnhub-Token header or token query parameter | Limits: 60 API calls/minute on the free tier per Finnhub's published pricing, with WebSocket streaming limited to 50 symbols. PER-ENDPOINT free availability is UNKNOWN AND MUST BE VERIFIED WITH YOUR OWN KEY — Finnhub's pricing page is client-side rendered and could not be read programmatically, and Finnhub has historically moved individual endpoints (including calendar endpoints) behind paid tiers without changing the free-tier call count. History depth on free tier: UNKNOWN. Do not build on the IPO calendar until you have confirmed it against your key.
- Latency: realtime for quotes; daily for calendars | Format: REST JSON + WebSocket
- Relevance: If the IPO calendar is free on your key it is a CORE feed for 'will X IPO by date Y' — that is the single hardest corporate-event field to source free. Ranked USEFUL rather than CORE precisely because the free-tier endpoint list could not be verified.

**Financial Modeling Prep (free tier)** — Financial Modeling Prep `LIVE`

- Earnings calendar with estimates and actuals, IPO calendar, M&A RSS, delisted-companies list, executive-compensation and key-executives endpoints, and SEC-filings-derived fundamentals. Probes to both the legacy /api/v3/earning_calendar and the current /stable/earnings-calendar returned 401 — both paths alive in 2026, key-gated.
- Docs: https://site.financialmodelingprep.com/developer/docs
- Auth: free API key (email registration, no credit card); passed as apikey query parameter | Limits: VERIFIED: 250 API requests/DAY on the free Basic plan, resetting on a 24-hour cycle, returning 429 on breach with no overage charge. Access to 150+ endpoints. HISTORY DEPTH IS THE REAL LIMIT: 5 years of stock data and only 5 QUARTERS of financial statement data on free — insufficient to build an earnings-surprise base rate. FMP has also been migrating v3 endpoints to /stable; assume v3 paths are deprecated.
- Latency: daily | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: Its M&A RSS and delisted-companies endpoints cover event types that are genuinely hard to get free. But 250 calls/day and 5 quarters of history make it a supplement, not a backbone. Verify each endpoint you need is on the free plan before depending on it.

**FDIC BankFind Suite API** — US Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation `LIVE`

- Every FDIC-insured institution with charter class, active/inactive status, assets, deposits, branch counts, and — critically — the failures and acquisitions endpoints recording bank failures and who assumed the deposits. Verified live unauthenticated: an ACTIVE:1 filter returned 4,232 active institutions from index institutions_20260918090006, i.e. an index rebuilt 2026-09-18.
- Docs: https://banks.data.fdic.gov/docs/
- Auth: none | Limits: UNKNOWN — no numeric rate limit published and none in headers. Documented: limit parameter with offset paging (limit caps at 10,000 per request). History: institutions back to 1934, failures back to 1934. Free, public domain.
- Latency: daily for institution data; failures posted as they occur (Friday evenings by convention) | Format: REST JSON/CSV
- Relevance: The authoritative settlement source for 'will bank X fail by date Y' — a live contract category since 2023. The acquisitions endpoint also settles bank-M&A contracts. The active-institution count is itself a consolidation metric.

#### NICHE

**NHTSA Recalls API** — US National Highway Traffic Safety Administration `LIVE`

- Vehicle safety recalls by make/model/year or by VIN: NHTSA campaign number, manufacturer, component, summary, consequence, remedy, report received date, and park-it/park-outside severity flags. Verified live: a query for Ford F-150 model year 2024 returned Count 11 with campaign 24V329000.
- Docs: https://www.nhtsa.gov/nhtsa-datasets-and-apis
- Auth: none | Limits: UNKNOWN — no published numeric limit and no RateLimit headers observed. Complementary bulk flat files are published on the NHTSA datasets page. History: recall campaigns back to 1966. Free.
- Latency: daily | Format: REST JSON at https://api.nhtsa.gov/recalls/recallsByVehicle
- Relevance: Auto and EV recall contracts, and a direct cost/liability input for automaker earnings. The park-it flag distinguishes a severe recall from a routine one, which is exactly the distinction a well-written contract turns on.

**EPO Open Patent Services (OPS) v3.2** — European Patent Office `LIVE`

- European and worldwide patent bibliographic data, full-text, legal status (INPADOC), family data, and the European Patent Register including opposition proceedings and ownership changes. Probe to https://ops.epo.org/3.2/rest-services/... returned a structured 403 'This request has been rejected due to the violation of Fair Use policy' — the service is demonstrably alive in 2026 and enforcing its documented fair-use tiers against unauthenticated callers.
- Docs: https://www.epo.org/en/searching-for-patents/data/web-services/ops
- Auth: free developer registration at the EPO Developer Portal; OAuth2 Consumer Key + Consumer Secret; select the 'Non-paying' access method | Limits: Free 'Non-paying' tier is metered by DATA VOLUME, not call count. Published figures are inconsistent across EPO materials: the EPO fair-use charter has been cited at both 4 GB/week and 3.5 GB/week for a free registered account — treat the exact figure as UNKNOWN and verify on your own portal dashboard. Additional documented throttling by request type (retrieval vs search) applies, and breaching fair use returns the 403 observed here. History: worldwide collection, 100M+ documents.
- Latency: weekly | Format: REST XML/JSON over OAuth2
- Relevance: The non-US half of patent coverage, and the European Patent Register's opposition and transfer-of-rights records are a real signal for pharma patent-cliff and biotech-acquisition contracts. NICHE for general corporate-event pricing.

**GitHub REST API + GH Archive** — GitHub / Ilya Grigorik (GH Archive) `LIVE`

- GitHub REST API gives repos, releases, org membership and the public events stream. GH Archive gives the complete public event firehose as hourly JSON files. Both verified live: api.github.com/rate_limit returned the live quota object, /events returned 19,935 bytes, and https://data.gharchive.org/2026-09-01-0.json.gz returned 6,905,011 bytes.
- Docs: https://docs.github.com/en/rest/rate-limit
- Auth: none for basic use; free personal access token raises limits substantially | Limits: VERIFIED FROM THE LIVE /rate_limit RESPONSE: unauthenticated core = 60 requests/hour, and unauthenticated code_search = 60/hour. Search API is separately throttled and returned 'API rate limit exceeded' after ~10 search calls in a minute during this research — unauthenticated search is 10 requests/minute. With a free token: 5,000 requests/hour core, 30 requests/minute search. GH Archive hourly files are unmetered static downloads with history from 2011. Free.
- Latency: realtime for the events API; hourly for GH Archive files | Format: REST JSON + GraphQL; GH Archive is gzipped newline-delimited JSON
- Relevance: Proxy signal only, but a real one: release cadence and contributor-count collapse in an org's repos is a measurable leading indicator of a product being abandoned or a team being cut. Useful for dev-tool and infrastructure-company contracts where no filing exists.

**Brønnøysund Register Centre API (Norway)** — Brønnøysundregistrene (Norwegian Government) `LIVE`

- The full Norwegian company register: organisation number, name, legal form, registration and deletion dates, industry codes, addresses, and status flags. Verified live twice, both unauthenticated: a name query returned EQUINOR ASA (org 923609016), and — notably — a query with konkurs=true returned 200, i.e. the register exposes a direct BANKRUPTCY FILTER as a first-class query parameter.
- Docs: https://data.brreg.no/enhetsregisteret/api/dokumentasjon
- Auth: none | Limits: UNKNOWN — Brønnøysund publishes no numeric rate limit and none appeared in headers. Documented: size parameter with paged results; full-register bulk download available as an alternative to paging. Full register history including deleted entities. Free and genuinely open, no registration.
- Latency: daily | Format: REST JSON (HAL) + bulk download
- Relevance: NICHE by geography but the cleanest bankruptcy signal of any registry tested — konkurs=true is a machine-readable insolvency flag with no auth at all. The model for what a good registry feed looks like; useful for Nordic-entity contracts and for Equinor/Norwegian energy names.

**Recherche d'entreprises API (France)** — DINUM / data.gouv.fr (French Government) `LIVE`

- Open, key-free search over the French SIRENE register: SIREN/SIRET, legal name, trade name, NAF/APE activity code, headquarters address, establishment counts (total and currently open), administrative status, and dirigeants (company officers). Verified live unauthenticated: a query for 'airbus' returned 90,058 bytes including AIRBUS SIREN 383474814 with 11 establishments, 6 open.
- Docs: https://recherche-entreprises.api.gouv.fr/docs/
- Auth: none | Limits: Documented as 7 requests/second per IP for the public search endpoint. Page size capped at 25 per page. Covers the full French register. Free, no registration. (The older api.insee.fr Sirene endpoint returned 401 in testing — see deadEnds.)
- Latency: daily | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: NICHE by geography. Matters because establishment-count changes and the cessation/radiation status are a free, structured signal for French corporate closures and restructurings — relevant to LVMH, Airbus, TotalEnergies and French industrial contracts.

**CFPB Consumer Complaint Database API** — US Consumer Financial Protection Bureau `LIVE`

- Every consumer complaint submitted to the CFPB, named to the company complained about: product and sub-product, issue, complaint narrative, state, submission date, company response and whether it was disputed. Verified live unauthenticated: returned 400,348 bytes with a total of 17,886,553 complaints indexed.
- Docs: https://cfpb.github.io/api/ccdb/
- Auth: none | Limits: UNKNOWN — no numeric rate limit published and none in headers. Documented: size parameter with search_after-style deep pagination; the full dataset is also available as a bulk CSV download. History: complaints from 2011-present. Free, public domain.
- Latency: daily | Format: REST JSON (Elasticsearch passthrough) + bulk CSV
- Relevance: NICHE but genuinely predictive for banks, fintechs, BNPL and credit bureaus: a spike in complaints against one institution has historically preceded CFPB enforcement actions and reputational events. Settles 'will the CFPB act against X' as a leading indicator, not as a resolution source.

**Regulations.gov API v4** — US General Services Administration / eRulemaking Program `LIVE`

- Federal dockets, proposed rules and every public comment submitted, including corporate comment letters that reveal which companies are lobbying against a rule. Probe returned a clean 403 with body {'error':{'code':'API_KEY_MISSING','message':'No api_key was supplied. Get one at https://api.regulations.gov'}} — live in 2026 and key-gated, with the API self-documenting where to get the key.
- Docs: https://open.gsa.gov/api/regulationsgov/
- Auth: free api.data.gov API key (instant email signup), passed as X-Api-Key header or api_key parameter | Limits: 1,000 requests/hour per api.data.gov key is the standard api.data.gov default and is what Regulations.gov documents; higher limits available on request. Page size caps at 250 with a 20-page (5,000-record) ceiling per query, so large pulls need date/docket slicing. History: dockets back to 2003. Free.
- Latency: daily | Format: REST JSON:API
- Relevance: NICHE for direct settlement, but the comment corpus is a real edge on rulemaking contracts: counting which firms filed opposing comments on a proposed rule is a measurable predictor of whether the rule survives or is litigated.

**Wikidata entity data + Wikipedia Pageviews API** — Wikimedia Foundation `LIVE`

- Wikidata gives structured company facts with references: CEO (P169) with start/end dates, parent organisation, subsidiaries, stock exchange listings, ticker symbols, LEI, dissolution date and successor entity. Pageviews gives per-article daily traffic. Wikidata Special:EntityData verified live (720,662 bytes for Q312/Apple). Pageviews returned 429 from this shared IP and the SPARQL endpoint returned 502/400 during testing — both are known to be intermittent under load rather than retired.
- Docs: https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Wikidata:Data_access
- Auth: none (a descriptive User-Agent with contact info is required by Wikimedia policy and enforced) | Limits: Wikimedia REST/Action APIs: documented at 200 requests/second for anonymous clients across Wikimedia infrastructure, but per-endpoint throttling is applied aggressively to shared/datacenter IPs — this research was 429'd on pageviews from a cloud IP. WDQS SPARQL: 60 seconds query timeout, 5 concurrent queries per IP, and returns 502 under load (observed here). Full history. Free.
- Latency: minutely for Wikidata edits; daily for pageviews | Format: REST JSON + SPARQL + bulk dumps
- Relevance: Wikidata's CEO property with start/end dates is a free structured executive-change record covering non-US companies that file nothing with the SEC. It is crowd-edited so it LAGS and must never be a settlement source — but as a global roster of who currently runs what, nothing free matches it. Use the bulk dumps, not the live endpoints.

**Australian Business Register ABN Lookup** — Australian Business Register / ATO `LIVE`

- ABN and ACN lookup: entity legal name, all trading/business names, entity type, ABN status with effective-from date, GST registration status, and state/postcode. Verified live: a JSON callback response returned unauthenticated for ABN 51824753556 (the endpoint responded with a well-formed callback object; a valid free GUID is required for populated data).
- Docs: https://abr.business.gov.au/Documentation/Default
- Auth: free registration for a GUID (authentication token) passed as a query parameter | Limits: UNKNOWN as a numeric figure — the ABR does not publish a per-GUID request limit, though it reserves the right to suspend GUIDs for excessive use. Bulk extract of the full register is separately available as a free download. Full register history. Free.
- Latency: daily | Format: REST JSON/XML (JSONP-style callback) + bulk extract
- Relevance: NICHE by geography. The ABN status field with its effective-from date is a clean deregistration/insolvency signal for Australian entities — relevant to BHP, Rio Tinto, Macquarie and ASX-listed contracts.

#### Repos

- `dgunning/edgartools` — Python library for reading and analysing SEC EDGAR filings — 10-K, 8-K, XBRL financials, Form 3/4/5, 13F, ADV. 2,732 stars, actively maintained. · The single best starting point in this domain. It already implements SEC-compliant User-Agent handling, the 10 req/s throttle, XBRL fact extraction and Form 4 insider parsing. Building an EDGAR client from scratch is wasted work — fork this and add your event extractors on top.
- `jadchaar/sec-edgar-downloader` — Bulk downloader for EDGAR filings by ticker/CIK and form type. 716 stars. · Handles the archive/backfill half that the getcurrent RSS cannot: pulling every historical 8-K for a company so you can compute base rates for 'how often does this company do X'.
- `edgarminers/python-edgar` — Downloads and parses the SEC full-index files (the quarterly master/company/form indexes) back to 1993. 355 stars. · Directly implements the full-index feed listed above. This is the reconciliation layer that proves your real-time RSS ingestion missed no filings — the exact guarantee a settlement oracle needs.
- `toddwschneider/sec-13f-filings` — Parser and analysis pipeline for SEC 13F institutional holdings filings, with a Postgres schema. 440 stars. · 13F position changes are a leading signal for both takeover targets and distressed names. The repo ships the schema and loader, which is most of the work.
- `freelawproject/courtlistener` — The full CourtListener platform — the source of the REST v4 API and RECAP archive listed above. 1,029 stars. · The free API is capped at 125 requests/day, which is unusable as a firehose. The source shows exactly how the RECAP ingest and the per-court PACER RSS subscriptions work, so you can run the same pattern against the free court RSS feeds yourself.
- `freelawproject/juriscraper` — Production scraper library covering American court websites, including the per-district PACER RSS feeds and their per-court quirks. 640 stars. · Solves the hardest part of the PACER RSS feed: knowing which of the ~200 federal courts actually publish RSS, what event types each one includes, and how each formats its entries. That map is the value.
- `freelawproject/eyecite` — Extracts and normalises legal citations from arbitrary text. 283 stars. · Links an 8-K's litigation disclosure to the actual docket in RECAP. Without citation normalisation you cannot join the SEC-filing view of a lawsuit to the court view of the same lawsuit.
- `biglocalnews/warn-scraper` — CLI that downloads and normalises WARN Act mass-layoff notices across 50+ US state labor department sites into a consistent schema. 44 stars, maintained by Big Local News (Stanford). · This is THE answer to the WARN problem. There is no federal WARN API; every state publishes differently. This repo has already done the per-state parsing and is the only maintained option. Pair with chriszs/warn-scraper-bot, which runs it on a schedule and commits the diffs — giving you a free change-detection feed.
- `fedspendingtransparency/usaspending-api` — The official Treasury source for the USAspending.gov API listed above. 467 stars. · Authoritative reference for the undocumented pagination ceilings and the POST search request shapes, which the public docs under-specify. Reading the serializers saves a day of trial and error against the 10,000-record cap.
- `lukerosiak/pysec` — Parses XBRL filings from SEC EDGAR into normalised financial statements. 346 stars. · Useful reference for XBRL tag normalisation across filers — companies use different us-gaap tags for the same concept, which is the main reason naive earnings comparisons break.
- `tooksoi/ScraXBRL` — SEC EDGAR scraper plus XBRL parser and renderer. 306 stars. · Complementary XBRL approach with rendering of the filer's own presentation linkbase — helps when you need the number as the company presented it, not as you re-derived it.
- `stefanoamorelli/sec-edgar-toolkit` — Open-source toolkit for SEC EDGAR financial data with both Python and TypeScript/JavaScript clients. 38 stars. · The only maintained option here with a first-class TypeScript client — relevant if the research panel's ingestion layer is Node rather than Python.
