Useful for 'will state X enact law Y this session' and for session-adjournment deadline contracts, where the sine die date is a hard forcing function.

**House Clerk Electronic Voting System XML + Senate roll-call vote XML** — US House Clerk / US Senate (official primary sources) `LIVE`

- The authoritative, fastest official record of individual roll-call votes, published by each chamber itself. Verified live: https://clerk.house.gov/evs/2026/index.asp returned HTTP 200, and https://www.senate.gov/legislative/LIS/roll_call_votes/vote1192/vote_119_2_00001.xml returned HTTP 200 with 28,742 bytes of XML. Each file gives vote number, question, bill, date/time, result, and every member's Yea/Nay/Present/Not Voting with party and state.
- Docs: https://clerk.house.gov/Votes and https://www.senate.gov/legislative/votes_new.htm
- Base: `https://clerk.house.gov/evs/{year}/ and https://www.senate.gov/legislative/LIS/roll_call_votes/vote{congress}{session}/`
- Auth: none | Limits: No key, no registration, no published rate limit — UNKNOWN exact cap; these are static XML/HTML files, so practical limits are courtesy-bound (throttle yourself). History depth: House EVS from 1990; Senate roll calls from 1989 in this XML form, earlier via other archives. URL pattern is predictable and enumerable, e.g. vote_119_2_00001.xml through the session's final vote.
- Latency: MINUTES after the vote closes — faster than Congress.gov, Voteview or any aggregator | Format: XML / HTML (scrape-adjacent but stable, documented URL patterns)
- Relevance: This is the LATENCY play for legislative contracts. Aggregators lag the chambers by hours to days; the Clerk and Senate XML post within minutes of the gavel. For any 'will the bill pass today' or 'will cloture be invoked' contract, polling these two URL patterns is the difference between trading the news and reading it. Use Voteview and Congress.gov for history, use these for the live event.

**OpenElections — precinct and county-level US election results** — OpenElections (volunteer open-data project, Knight-funded origins) `LIVE`

- Certified election results standardized to a common CSV schema, down to PRECINCT level where states publish it, for federal, state and many local races. Organized as one GitHub repo per state (openelections-data-{st}) plus openelections-core for the acquisition/transform pipeline. Verified live and actively maintained: openelections-data-pa pushed 2026-09-19, -ga 2026-08-31, -or 2026-08-30, -tx 2026-08-22, -ny 2026-08-17; openelections-core pushed 2026-05-20 with 193 stars.
- Docs: http://docs.openelections.net/ and https://github.com/openelections/docs
- Base: `https://github.com/openelections (per-state repos; raw CSVs via raw.githubusercontent.com)`
- Auth: none | Limits: No key. Constrained only by GitHub limits: 60 API requests/hour unauthenticated, 5,000/hour authenticated (I hit the unauthenticated search throttle live, so it is enforced); raw file fetch cap UNKNOWN. Clone the repos rather than fetching file-by-file. History depth and COMPLETENESS VARY SHARPLY BY STATE — some states are near-complete back to 2000, others are sparse. Check per-state coverage before relying on it; treat a missing state as unmeasured, not as zero.
- Latency: weeks-to-months after certification (volunteer transcription) | Format: CSV bulk via Git
- Relevance: Precinct-level history is what lets you do serious election-night modelling: when 30% of a county reports, you need to know WHICH precincts those are and how they voted last time to project the remainder. That is the core of any live 'who wins' contract price between poll close and the call. MEDSL gives you county/state; OpenElections is the only free source that goes below it.

**US Census Bureau APIs (decennial, ACS, CPS Voting and Registration Supplement)** — US Census Bureau `LIVE`

- Demographics by geography down to block group, the PL 94-171 redistricting file (the legal basis for every district map), American Community Survey estimates, and the CPS Voting and Registration Supplement — the official biennial measurement of turnout and registration by race, age, education and state. TIGER/Line shapefiles supply congressional, state-legislative and precinct-adjacent geographies.
- Docs: https://www.census.gov/data/developers/data-sets.html
- Base: `https://api.census.gov/data/`
- Auth: free API key recommended; small volumes permitted without one | Limits: PARTIALLY VERIFIED, reporting honestly: https://api.census.gov/data.json (the dataset catalog) returned HTTP 200 with 5,224,311 bytes, so the service is live. But my actual data queries (2020/dec/pl and 2023/acs/acs1) returned HTTP 200 with an EMPTY body and content-type text/html — most likely key-gating or a malformed variable list on my part, but I did not resolve it, so treat data-query behaviour as unconfirmed. Census documents ~500 queries per day per IP without a key, unlimited with a free key — that figure is from Census documentation, NOT something I measured. History depth: decennial 1790-2020 (varies by product), ACS 2005-present, CPS voting supplement biennial since 1964.
- Latency: annual (ACS), decennial, biennial (CPS voting supplement) | Format: REST JSON + shapefile/TIGER bulk
- Relevance: The denominator for turnout models and the input to every redistricting contract — PL 94-171 population counts are literally what determines whether a map is legal. Demographic composition by district is how you translate a national swing into a district-specific one. NICHE-to-USEFUL for direct pricing, structurally important for anything district-level.

**Wikimedia REST API + Wikidata Query Service** — Wikimedia Foundation `LIVE`

- The broadest free coverage of WORLD elections, officeholders, cabinets and political parties. Wikidata holds structured records for heads of state and government, election events with dates, parties, seat counts and officeholder term start/end — queryable in SPARQL. English Wikipedia's election articles are the de facto real-time aggregator for countries with no machine-readable election commission. Verified live: https://api.wikimedia.org/core/v1/wikipedia/en/page/2026_United_States_elections/bare returned HTTP 200. My WDQS test returned HTTP 400 because my SPARQL was malformed, not because the service is down — so treat WDQS specifically as UNVERIFIED in this session.
- Docs: https://api.wikimedia.org/wiki/Main_page and https://query.wikidata.org/
- Base: `https://api.wikimedia.org/core/v1/ and https://query.wikidata.org/sparql`
- Auth: none for anonymous use; free Wikimedia account token raises limits | Limits: Wikimedia REST API: 500 requests/hour anonymous, 5,000/hour with a free account token — documented by Wikimedia, not measured by me. WDQS: no key, but a 60-second per-query timeout and concurrency throttling apply; exact concurrent-query cap UNKNOWN. History depth: effectively unlimited, and revision history gives you a timestamped audit trail of when a result was first reported.
- Latency: minutes (crowd-edited) for major events; often the FIRST machine-readable source for a foreign election result | Format: REST JSON + SPARQL + full database dumps
- Relevance: For international political contracts this is frequently the only viable free feed, and the page-revision timestamp is itself a signal — an edit to a 'List of current heads of government' page is often the earliest structured indication of a resignation or coup. Treat as untrusted, adversarially-editable input: never let it be authoritative for settlement, use it to trigger verification against an official source.

**Manifold Markets API** — Manifold `LIVE`

- Full read access to a large play-money prediction market with heavy political coverage: markets, probabilities, price history, bets, comments, users and groups. Verified live: https://api.manifold.markets/v0/markets?limit=1 returned HTTP 200 JSON. Unusually open — full bet-level history is downloadable, which is rare among prediction markets.
- Docs: https://docs.manifold.markets/api
- Base: `https://api.manifold.markets/v0/`
- Auth: none for reads; free API key for writes/betting | Limits: Reads are open with no key. History depth: platform launched 2021, complete bet history retained.
- Latency: realtime | Format: REST JSON (+ bulk dumps)
- Relevance: Play-money, so prices are noisier and less sharp than Kalshi or Polymarket — but Manifold covers a far wider tail of political questions, including many that no real-money venue lists, and the complete bet-level history makes it the best free dataset for STUDYING prediction-market calibration and price dynamics. Use it to backtest your edge-detection methodology before risking capital on the real venues.

**Metaculus API** — Metaculus `LIVE`

- Forecast questions with aggregated community predictions, the Metaculus Prediction, individual forecast time series, resolution criteria and resolution outcomes — with a strong geopolitics, elections and governance category and an explicit public track record of calibration.
- Docs: https://www.metaculus.com/api/
- Base: `https://www.metaculus.com/api/`
- Auth: CHANGED — now requires a free account and API token | Limits: IMPORTANT CHANGE I VERIFIED THIS SESSION: anonymous access is gone. Both /api2/questions/ and /api/posts/ returned HTTP 403 with the body 'Permission Error: The API is only available to authenticated users. Please create an account and use your API token to access the API.' Account and token are free. Exact post-authentication rate limit: UNKNOWN — not stated. History depth: platform from 2015, full forecast time series per question. Any older integration or tutorial assuming open anonymous access is now broken.
- Latency: near-realtime (forecast-update driven) | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: Metaculus is a forecast aggregator rather than a market, so it has no liquidity constraint and no favourite-longshot bias — which makes it an excellent independent cross-check on market-implied probabilities. Where Metaculus and Kalshi diverge materially on the same political question, one of them is mispriced, and Metaculus's published calibration record tells you how much weight it has earned. Strong on geopolitical and 'will war/treaty/leadership-change happen' questions that markets list thinly.

**PredictIt API (market data)** — PredictIt (Victoria University of Wellington, CFTC no-action history) `LIVE`

- All open markets with per-contract last trade price, best buy/sell, and daily open/high/low/close — heavily weighted toward US political contracts (presidential, congressional control, primaries, cabinet departures, approval thresholds). Verified live: https://www.predictit.org/api/marketdata/all/ returned HTTP 200 with 418,724 bytes of market data.
- Docs: https://www.predictit.org/api/marketdata/all/ (undocumented public JSON endpoint; no formal developer docs page)
- Base: `https://www.predictit.org/api/marketdata/`
- Auth: none | Limits: No key. No published rate limit — UNKNOWN exact cap; the community convention is one call per minute or slower since the payload is the entire market universe in a single response. NOTE the host asymmetry I measured: api.predictit.org failed to connect while www.predictit.org/api/... succeeded — use the www host. History depth: the endpoint returns current state plus daily OHLC only; there is NO deep historical archive via this API, so you must snapshot it yourself to build history. PredictIt has faced repeated CFTC regulatory uncertainty since 2022 — the feed is live today but its long-term existence is a real risk, not a certainty.
- Latency: realtime-ish (single snapshot of all markets) | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: The longest-running US political prediction market, with contracts that often differ in construction from Kalshi's — the position limits and fee structure create persistent, measurable pricing distortions versus the newer venues. Valuable as a third cross-venue reference and for its long historical presence in academic forecasting literature.

- Members of the Commons and Lords with party, constituency, term history, contact details and portrait; plus sibling APIs for Bills, Divisions (roll-call votes), Committees, Written Questions, Early Day Motions and Hansard. - Latency: daily; divisions posted within hours of the vote | Format: REST JSON (OpenAPI described)
- Relevance: The UK is the second-most-traded political jurisdiction on prediction markets after the US, and this is a genuinely first-class free official API — better documented and less restricted than most US equivalents. **Redistricting Data Hub** — Redistricting Data Hub (nonprofit) `LIVE`

- Cleaned, standardized redistricting inputs for all 50 states: enacted congressional and state-legislative district shapefiles, precinct boundaries with election results joined, PL 94-171 census blocks, block-to-precinct assignment files and voter-file-derived aggregates. Verified live: the download-data page returned HTTP 200 with 109,546 bytes.
- Docs: https://redistrictingdatahub.org/data/download-data/
- Base: `https://redistrictingdatahub.org/`
- Auth: free registration required (account, then download); use is restricted to non-commercial/public-interest purposes under their terms | Limits: Free but gated behind an account and a terms-of-use agreement. Exact download quota: UNKNOWN — none published; it is a file-download portal, not a metered API, and there is no public REST API. COMMERCIAL USE RESTRICTION: read their terms before building a paid product on it — this is the kind of licence that quietly disqualifies a commercial panel. History depth: 2010 and 2020 cycles, with post-2020 enacted and litigated maps tracked as they change.
- Latency: event-driven — updated when maps are enacted or struck down | Format: Shapefile / CSV bulk download (registration-gated)
- Relevance: Directly prices redistricting contracts ('will state X have a new map before the 2026 midterms', 'how many seats does the new map favour'). Precincts-with-results joined to new district boundaries is exactly how you compute a new district's partisan lean — the input to every House-seat forecast after a map changes mid-decade. Doing this join yourself from raw sources is weeks of work.

**Clarity Elections live results platform (results.enr.clarityelections.com)** — Scytl/Clarity (private vendor used by many US states and counties) `LIVE`

- Election-night live results feeds for a large share of US counties and several statewide offices, served as structured JSON/XML/ZIP detail files (detail.xml, detail.zip, summary.json) under a predictable per-jurisdiction path with a version key. Verified live: the root https://results.enr.clarityelections.com/ returned HTTP 200 (a 368-byte landing/redirect shell — jurisdiction-specific paths carry the actual data).
- Docs: No official public developer documentation exists — endpoint structure is community-reverse-engineered; see OpenElections and Elex-adjacent tooling for path patterns
- Base: `https://results.enr.clarityelections.com/{STATE}/{jurisdiction}/{electionid}/{versionid}/`
- Auth: none | Limits: No key, no registration. No published rate limit — UNKNOWN; this is an undocumented vendor endpoint, so self-throttle hard and expect the structure to change without notice between elections. History depth: current and recent past elections per jurisdiction only; old election IDs are eventually retired. Treat as SEMI-SCRAPE: stable in practice, contractually unsupported, and it will break on you at the worst possible moment (election night) if you have no fallback.
- Latency: realtime on election night — refreshes every few minutes as precincts report | Format: JSON/XML/ZIP over HTTP (undocumented)
- Relevance: On election night this is the fastest FREE path to precinct-and-county-level reporting in the many jurisdictions that use Clarity — the AP and Decision Desk equivalents cost real money. Combined with OpenElections precinct history for the same geography, it is what lets you project a final margin from partial returns and price a live winner contract ahead of the official call. Highest-latency-value feed in this domain for exactly a few hours every cycle.

#### NICHE

**GovTrack legacy API (v2)** — GovTrack.us (Civic Impulse LLC) `LIVE`

- Members and their roles across all Congresses, bills, votes and vote positions, committees. Verified live and genuinely returning data despite its deprecation: https://www.govtrack.us/api/v2/role?limit=1 returned HTTP 200 with meta.total_count = 45,666 role records going back to the 99th Congress and earlier.
- Docs: https://www.govtrack.us/api/v2/ (browsable); the deprecation notice is at https://www.govtrack.us/posts/124/2016-12-10_ending-govtracks-bulk-data-and-api
- Auth: none | Limits: No key. No rate limit published — UNKNOWN. THE CATCH: GovTrack formally ANNOUNCED THE END of its bulk data and API in December 2016, with shutdown targeted for summer 2017, directing users to ProPublica (now itself dead) and the unitedstates/congress scrapers. Nearly a decade later the v2 endpoints still serve real data, but they are unsupported, undocumented-going-forward and could vanish without notice. Do not build a dependency on this; use it as a convenience layer or a cross-check only. History depth: 1789-present for roles.
- Latency: UNKNOWN — freshness of the still-running instance is unverified; assume it lags official sources | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: Convenient shape for member-history and vote-position queries, and useful as an independent cross-check against Voteview and congress-legislators when those two disagree. But it is a zombie service: NICHE only, and never as a sole source for anything that settles money.

**Google Civic Information API — Elections and Divisions endpoints (Representatives is DEAD)** — Google `LIVE`

- What SURVIVES: the Elections API (upcoming election metadata, voterInfoQuery for polling places, early vote sites, drop boxes, contests and ballot content by address where a data partner supplies it) and the Divisions API (Open Civic Data IDs, including the address-to-OCD-ID lookup method added September 2024). Verified live: the API responded to my unkeyed request with a well-formed HTTP 400 'API key not valid' — the service is up and key-gated.
- Docs: https://developers.google.com/civic-information/docs/v2/
- Base: `https://www.googleapis.com/civicinfo/v2/`
- Auth: free Google Cloud API key | Limits: Free with a Google Cloud API key. Exact quota: UNKNOWN — Google's published civic-info quota is not clearly stated in the current docs and the Cloud console default governs it; historically 25,000 queries/day, but I could not confirm that for 2026 so I will not assert it. CRITICAL SCOPE WARNING, verified: representativeInfoByAddress and representativeInfoByDivision WERE TURNED DOWN ON 30 APRIL 2025. Any integration or tutorial that returns 'your elected officials for an address' is dead. Use unitedstates/congress-legislators plus Open States /people.geo for that capability instead. Ballot/election coverage is also partner-dependent and has thinned considerably.
- Latency: event-driven around election dates | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: NICHE now that Representatives is gone. OCD-IDs remain genuinely useful as a canonical geographic identifier for joining election data across sources — that crosswalk role is the main reason to keep it. Election-date metadata is a weak, partner-dependent secondary source for election-calendar contracts; prefer official state sources.

**ParlGov — Parliaments and Governments database** — University of Bremen (Döring & Manow) `LIVE`

- The academic reference for comparative party politics: elections, parties, cabinets and cabinet composition for ~37 democracies (EU, OECD) since roughly 1945, with vote shares, seat counts, cabinet formation and termination dates, and party ideology placements (left-right, EU-anti/pro) linked across sources. Verified live: https://www.parlgov.org/data/parlgov-development_csv-utf-8/view_election.csv returned HTTP 200 with 1,142,264 bytes of CSV.
- Docs: https://www.parlgov.org/data/
- Base: `https://www.parlgov.org/data/`
- Auth: none | Limits: No key, no registration — direct CSV/SQLite download. No rate limit published — UNKNOWN; static files. History depth: approximately 1945 to present, released in periodic stable versions plus a rolling development version. No API and no realtime component.
- Latency: periodic academic releases — months | Format: CSV / SQLite bulk
- Relevance: The historical base-rate engine for European political contracts. It answers 'how long does a coalition of this composition typically last' and 'how often does the largest party fail to form a government' — empirical priors for cabinet-collapse, snap-election and coalition-formation contracts that are otherwise priced on vibes. Not realtime; pair with IPU Parline and national sources for current state.

**V-Dem (Varieties of Democracy) dataset** — V-Dem Institute, University of Gothenburg `LIVE`

- ~500 indicators of democracy and governance for 202 polities from 1789 to the present, including electoral integrity, freedom of expression, judicial constraints on the executive, clean-elections index, and the headline Liberal/Electoral Democracy indices — plus expert-coded uncertainty intervals. Verified live: the dataset page returned HTTP 200 with 42,405 bytes.
- Docs: https://v-dem.net/data/the-v-dem-dataset/
- Base: `https://v-dem.net/data/`
- Auth: none for the public dataset download (an R package, vdemdata, is also published) | Limits: Free bulk download, no key. No API and therefore no rate limit — UNKNOWN/not applicable. History depth: 1789-2025+ with annual releases (typically each March). Because it is expert-coded and released annually, there is NO within-year signal — it is a slow-moving structural covariate, never a live feed.
- Latency: annual | Format: CSV / Stata / R package bulk
- Relevance: NICHE and strictly as a prior, not a signal. Useful for pricing contracts about democratic backsliding, coup risk, election-integrity disputes and 'will the incumbent accept the result' in countries with thin data. The judicial-constraints and clean-elections indicators help you set a base rate for whether a nominally scheduled election will actually occur and be honoured — a risk most models set to zero by default.

**Oyez API** — Oyez / Cornell LII / Justia / Chicago-Kent `LIVE`

- US Supreme Court cases with docket numbers, question presented, term, argument and decision dates, per-justice votes and opinion authorship, plus synchronized oral-argument audio and transcripts. Verified live: https://api.oyez.org/cases?per_page=1 returned HTTP 200 JSON.
- Docs: No official developer documentation — the API is public but undocumented; community write-ups describe /cases, /cases/{term}/{docket}, /case_media endpoints
- Base: `https://api.oyez.org/`
- Auth: none | Limits: No key, no registration. No published rate limit — UNKNOWN. Undocumented and unsupported, so the schema may change without notice. History depth: SCOTUS cases from 1789 with audio from 1955 onward. For anything that settles money, use CourtListener as the authoritative source and Oyez as enrichment.
- Latency: days-to-weeks after argument or decision | Format: REST JSON (undocumented)
- Relevance: NICHE but well-shaped for SCOTUS contracts: per-justice vote records let you build justice-level voting priors, and argument-date metadata gives you the calendar of forced decision windows (a case argued in December is overwhelmingly likely to be decided before the end of June term). Oral-argument transcripts are a genuine leading indicator — question counts and direction by justice have measurable predictive power on outcomes.

**USAspending API** — US Department of the Treasury / Bureau of the Fiscal Service `LIVE`

- All federal spending: awards, contracts, grants, loans, recipients, agency budget authority, obligations and outlays by account and program, plus DEFC codes for supplemental appropriations. Verified live: https://api.usaspending.gov/api/v2/references/agency/456/ returned HTTP 200 JSON.
- Docs: https://api.usaspending.gov/
- Base: `https://api.usaspending.gov/api/v2/`
- Auth: none | Limits: No API key and no registration required. Exact rate limit: UNKNOWN — none published; fair-use expected, and some POST search endpoints are heavy so self-throttle. Bulk downloads available via the /bulk_download endpoints and the site's Custom Award Data download. History depth: FY2001 onward for awards, with better completeness from FY2008.
- Latency: daily-to-monthly depending on the account and reporting deadline | Format: REST JSON + bulk CSV/ZIP
- Relevance: NICHE for direct contract pricing but strong for shutdown and appropriations markets: obligation and outlay rates against enacted budget authority show you how much runway an agency actually has, which is the real mechanism behind 'will the shutdown extend past date D'. Also supports 'will program X be funded' contracts and detects policy implementation that has not yet been announced.

**ALARM Project — 50-State Redistricting Simulations** — ALARM Project, Harvard (Imai lab) — alarm-redist `LIVE`

- Large ensembles of computationally simulated redistricting plans for all 50 states, generated with the redist sequential-Monte-Carlo algorithm, with per-plan partisan and compactness summary statistics. This is the standard evidence base for gerrymandering claims in litigation. Verified live: https://alarm-redist.org/fifty-states/ returned HTTP 200 with 175,882 bytes. The redist R package repo was pushed 2026-08-04 (74 stars), so the toolchain is actively maintained.
- Docs: https://alarm-redist.org/fifty-states/
- Base: `https://alarm-redist.org/fifty-states/ (per-state plan ensembles; also distributed via Harvard Dataverse)`
- Auth: none | Limits: Free, open, no key, no registration. No rate limit — UNKNOWN/not applicable, these are static downloads. History depth: 2020-cycle congressional and state-legislative plans, with coverage added state-by-state. Academic release cadence, not a live feed.
- Latency: periodic — updated as new maps are enacted and new simulations are run | Format: CSV / RDS bulk + R package (redist)
- Relevance: NICHE but decisive for redistricting litigation contracts. When a map is challenged, the plaintiff's case is usually built on exactly this kind of ensemble showing the enacted plan is an extreme outlier. Having the ensemble yourself lets you assess how strong the legal claim actually is — and therefore price 'will the court strike down the map' on evidence rather than on headlines.

**Vote Smart API** — Vote Smart (formerly Project Vote Smart) `LIVE`

- Candidate and officeholder biographical data, voting records, public statements, interest-group ratings and NPAT issue positions across federal and state offices. Verified that the SERVICE IS ALIVE in 2026: https://api.votesmart.org/Officials.getByOfficeState with a dummy key returned HTTP 200 with a well-formed XML body '<error><errorMessage>Authorization failed</errorMessage></error>' — the server is responding, not dead.
- Docs: https://votesmart.org/share/api
- Base: `https://api.votesmart.org/`
- Auth: API key by request/registration — issuance status in 2026 UNVERIFIED | Limits: EXACT limits: UNKNOWN — no published calls/day or calls/minute figure that I could confirm. More importantly, whether new free keys are still being issued is UNVERIFIED: the organization has contracted substantially over the past decade and the developer program appears dormant, though the API host itself is clearly still running. Do not plan around this until you have actually obtained a working key. History depth: UNKNOWN for 2026; historically deep coverage of interest-group ratings back to the 1990s.
- Latency: UNKNOWN — freshness of the current dataset is unverified | Format: REST XML/JSON
- Relevance: NICHE. Interest-group ratings are a useful alternative ideology measure to DW-NOMINATE, particularly for state legislators and challengers who have no congressional voting record and therefore no NOMINATE score — relevant for primary-outcome contracts. But given the unverified key issuance and unknown freshness, treat it as a bonus source, never a dependency.

#### Repos

- `fivethirtyeight/data` — The full FiveThirtyEight data archive — 17,453 stars, last push 2025-02-25, NOT archived but permanently frozen. Contains pollster-ratings/raw_polls.csv (4.96 MB), pollster-ratings-combined.csv, polls/pres_pollaverages_1968-2016.csv (50.4 MB), pres_primary_avgs_1980-2016.csv (30.1 MB), partisan-lean, forecast-review, election-deniers, state-of-the-polls-2024, redistricting-atlas-data. · The open-CSV source of HISTORICAL POLLING ERROR — the variance term that converts a poll into a probability. ABC has already deleted the 538 website archives and the standalone pollster-ratings repo; this one survives but is not guaranteed to. CLONE IT TO COLD STORAGE TODAY, before you write a line of code against it.
- `Turn-Left-Now/FiveThirtyEight-Archive` — A community preservation mirror of FiveThirtyEight's GitHub repositories, created in March 2025 specifically in case ABC deleted the originals. Last push 2025-03-12. · Insurance. Given that ABC killed the article archives in May 2026 and the standalone pollster-ratings repo now 404s, an independent mirror of the 538 data is worth more than its zero-star count suggests. Verify its contents against the live fivethirtyeight/data repo while both still exist.
- `unitedstates/congress` — Public-domain scrapers for the work of Congress — bills, amendments, votes, nominations — the community-maintained successor to GovTrack's bulk data, producing the same JSON shape. · Builds a complete local legislative database without touching any metered API. This is the recommended path when Congress.gov's 5,000/hour and GovInfo's 1,000/hour quotas are too tight for a full historical backfill.
- `unitedstates/congress-legislators` — Every member of Congress 1789-present in YAML/JSON/CSV with bioguide, ICPSR, THOMAS, GovTrack, CRP/OpenSecrets, VoteSmart, FEC and Wikidata IDs, plus full term and committee history. 2,440 stars, pushed 2026-09-03. · THE identity crosswalk. It is the join key that connects FEC money, Voteview votes, Congress.gov bills and polling to the same human being. Without it every political feed is an unjoinable island. Highest structural value per byte in this entire list.
- `LibraryOfCongress/api.congress.gov` — Official Congress.gov API repo — 994 stars, pushed 2026-08-31. Holds the OpenAPI documentation, a detailed ChangeLog, and the issue tracker where rate-limit-increase requests are filed publicly. · Authoritative source for endpoint behaviour and for tracking breaking changes. The ChangeLog is where the 1,000→5,000 requests/hour increase is recorded, and open issues reveal known data gaps before they corrupt your backfill.
- `openelections/openelections-core` — The acquisition/transform/output pipeline behind OpenElections (193 stars, pushed 2026-05-20), alongside ~50 openelections-data-{state} repos of standardized certified results — several pushed within the last month (PA 2026-09-19, GA 2026-08-31, OR 2026-08-30). · The only free source of PRECINCT-level US election results at national scope. Precinct history is what makes election-night projection from partial returns possible — the core of pricing a live winner contract before the call. Check per-state completeness first; coverage is genuinely uneven.
- `openstates/openstates-scrapers` — Source for the Open States 50-state legislative scrapers — 915 stars, pushed 2026-09-18, very actively maintained. · Lets you run the state-legislature pipeline yourself and sidestep the Open States API's ~500/day free quota entirely. Also documents, per state, exactly which fields are reliably available — invaluable for knowing what is genuinely missing versus merely unscraped.
- `qualiaenjoyer/polymarket-apis` — Unified Python client for all Polymarket v2 APIs — Clob, Gamma, Data, Web3 and WebSocket — with Pydantic data validation. 193 stars, pushed 2026-09-13, the most-starred and most current Polymarket wrapper. · Polymarket's endpoints are split across several hosts with inconsistent schemas (I hit exactly this: gamma.polymarket.com fails, gamma-api.polymarket.com works). This wraps all of them behind validated models, which is precisely the boilerplate you do not want to rewrite for a live trading panel.
- `ammario/kalshi-docs` — LLM-friendly, auto-updating markdown mirror of the complete Kalshi API documentation. Pushed 2026-09-19 — updated within days of this research. · Kalshi's official docs are a JS-heavy readme.io site that is awkward to fetch and diff programmatically. This repo gives you the same content as plain markdown that an AI synthesis layer can ingest directly, and its commit history is a free changelog of Kalshi API changes.
- `arvchahal/kalshi-rs` — Full-coverage Kalshi SDK spanning 50+ endpoints with WebSocket support, in Rust. 36 stars, pushed 2026-09-02. (ammario/kalshi is the Go equivalent; hurley451/KalshiSharp for C#.) · The most complete endpoint coverage of any open Kalshi client, which makes it the best reference for what the API actually exposes — including endpoints the official docs describe poorly. Useful even if you build in Python.
- `ian-nason/fec-database` — A clean, queryable DuckDB database of FEC campaign finance data covering 2004-2026. Pushed 2026-09-16. · Skips the entire FEC bulk-download-and-normalize problem. FEC raw files are fixed-width, schema-drifting and painful; a prebuilt DuckDB covering 22 years of cycles is a very large head start, and DuckDB queries locally at speeds no API quota could ever match.
- `simonw/fec-to-sqlite` — Loads FEC campaign finance data into SQLite, from Simon Willison (author of Datasette). 12 stars, last push 2023-08-10. · Older but well-built and pairs directly with Datasette for instant exploratory querying and a JSON API over the result. Good for standing up an internal FEC research surface fast, even if you rebuild the loader for current cycles.
- `cgorski/hardmoney` — A single Rust crate covering FEC campaign-finance end to end: a .fec filing-format parser plus Postgres bulk ETL. Pushed 2026-09-17. · The .fec electronic filing format parser is the hard part and the reason most projects only ever use the API. Parsing raw filings yourself means you see a filing the moment it hits the FEC's electronic system — hours ahead of the API — which is real latency edge on quarterly-filing-deadline contracts.
- `hodgesmr/agent-fecfile` — A Claude Code plugin, Agent Skill and MCP server for analyzing FEC filings. 41 stars, pushed 2026-06-12. (See also cyanheads/openfec-mcp-server pushed 2026-09-19 and sh-patterson/fec-mcp-server pushed 2026-08-24.) · Directly relevant to the AI-synthesis half of the research panel: a ready-made MCP surface over campaign finance means your model can query FEC data as a tool rather than you pre-flattening it. The three competing MCP servers are worth diffing for endpoint coverage.
- `alarm-redist/redist` — The R package implementing sequential-Monte-Carlo redistricting simulation — the algorithm behind the ALARM Project's 50-state plan ensembles. 74 stars, pushed 2026-08-04. · Lets you generate your own plan ensembles for a newly enacted or proposed map rather than waiting for an academic release. That is how you independently assess whether a challenged map is a statistical outlier, and therefore how you price redistricting-litigation contracts on evidence.
- `mggg/maup` — The geospatial toolkit for redistricting data from the MGGG Redistricting Lab — handles the messy business of aggregating and disaggregating data between mismatched geographies (blocks, precincts, districts). 74 stars, pushed 2025-08-20. · Solves the specific, brutal problem of joining old precinct-level election results onto new district boundaries when the boundaries do not nest. That join is the only way to compute a new district's partisan lean, and doing it wrong silently corrupts every downstream seat forecast.
- `nvkelso/election-geodata` — Precinct shapes with vote results for US elections, past and present. 327 stars — the most-starred precinct geodata collection — though last pushed 2019-02-17. · Stale for recent cycles, but still the widest free collection of historical precinct geometry, which is exactly what you need for pre-2020 backtests. Pair with Redistricting Data Hub for current-cycle boundaries.
- `christopherkenny/congress` — R client for the Congress.gov API. 21 stars, pushed 2026-06-26. (Python equivalents: harryziyuhe/CongressLib; MCP servers: amurshak/congressMCP pushed 2026-08-27, nawagner/congress-mcp.) · Actively maintained thin wrapper that handles pagination and the 250-item page cap correctly — the two things every hand-rolled Congress.gov client gets wrong on the first attempt. The MCP variants matter if the panel's AI layer should query Congress directly as a tool.
- `districtr/districtr` — Free, open-source web app for drawing districting plans, from the MGGG lab. 78 stars, pushed 2026-08-04. (See also PublicMapping/districtbuilder and PrincetonUniversity/gerrymandertests for gerrymandering metrics.) · Its underlying data layer — precinct geometries joined to election results for every state — is directly reusable, and gerrymandertests implements the standard quantitative measures (efficiency gap, mean-median, partisan bias) you would otherwise have to derive from papers.
- `TheEconomist/us-potus-model` — The Economist's open-sourced US presidential election forecasting model (Stan/R), originally built with G. Elliott Morris. Verified to still exist via the GitHub API. (See also TheEconomist/2021-germany-election-model-PUBLIC.) · A complete, published, peer-reviewed-in-public Bayesian forecasting model that consumes exactly the inputs this domain provides — polls, pollster house effects, economic fundamentals, state correlation structure. It is the single best free worked example of how to turn poll-plus-error data into a calibrated probability, which is the whole job of the research panel.

### Geopolitics, War and Conflict

#### CORE

**GDELT 2.0 Raw Files (Events, Mentions, GKG)** — GDELT Project / Google Jigsaw `LIVE`

- Every 15 minutes, a zipped CSV of globally-coded news events using CAMEO event codes (incl. codes 18-20: assault, fight, unconventional mass violence), with actor1/actor2, geolocation to city level, Goldstein conflict-cooperation score, average tone, and source URL. The Mentions table gives every re-mention of an event over time (escalation signal). GKG gives themes, persons, orgs, locations and emotional dimensions per article. Coverage from Feb 2015 to now; GDELT 1.0 back to 1979.
- Docs: http://data.gdeltproject.org/gdeltv2/lastupdate.txt
- Auth: none | Limits: No API key, no documented per-caller quota. New file set every 15 min (~96 event files/day). File sizes typically 50KB-3MB zipped per 15-min slice; masterfilelist.txt enumerates the entire archive. GDELT asks for polite use; no published hard cap. UNKNOWN whether an undocumented IP throttle exists.
- Latency: sub-minute | Format: CSV bulk
- Relevance: The single highest-value conflict feed for market pricing. Drives contracts on 'will there be an attack on X by date Y', escalation/de-escalation between named dyads, coup chatter, protest onset, and ceasefire collapse. Mentions-table volume spikes are a leading indicator that resolves faster than any curated dataset. Also the only free feed with enough history to backtest a conflict-event model.

**GDELT DOC 2.0 API** — GDELT Project `LIVE`

- Query-able full-text index over global news in 65 languages. Modes: ArtList (article list), TimelineVol / TimelineVolRaw (normalized coverage volume over time), TimelineTone, TimelineLang, TimelineSourceCountry, ToneChart, WordCloud. Returns JSON/CSV/RSS. Supports boolean queries, domain filters, country filters, theme filters, 15-minute resolution.
- Docs: https://blog.gdeltproject.org/gdelt-doc-2-0-api-debuts/
- Auth: none | Limits: No API key. Rolling 3-month window only (content back to 2017-01-01 is indexed but the API window is the trailing ~3 months). maxrecords cap is 250 per ArtList call. No published calls/day or calls/min limit — UNKNOWN; GDELT has historically throttled abusive IPs without documenting the threshold.
- Latency: sub-minute | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: Cheapest way to build a real-time 'narrative intensity' feature for any named conflict, leader, or sanction. TimelineVol on a market's own keywords is directly usable as a prior for binary event contracts; divergence between coverage volume and market price is a tradable edge. Good for fast resolution of 'was X reported by date Y' markets.

**OCHA HAPI — Humanitarian API v2 (conflict-events endpoint)** — UN OCHA / Centre for Humanitarian Data (HDX) `LIVE`

- ACLED-derived conflict event counts and fatalities aggregated to admin1/admin2 level, monthly, by event_type (political_violence, civilian_targeting, demonstration). Plus sibling endpoints: idps, refugees-persons-of-concern, returnees, humanitarian-needs, funding, operational-presence, national-risk (INFORM), food-security, baseline-population, rainfall. This is the free back door to ACLED-family numbers without an institutional ACLED account.
- Docs: https://hapi.humdata.org/docs
- Auth: free API key | Limits: app_identifier is a self-service base64 of 'appname:email' — no registration, no approval, no email confirmation. Verified working with a self-generated identifier. Max limit=10000 rows per call (limit=10001 returns HTTP 422). No rate-limit headers returned and no documented calls/day — UNKNOWN. History: verified data back to 2017-01 for AFG and 2018-01 for UKR.
- Latency: monthly | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: The only free, structured, admin2-resolution fatality series. Use it as the resolution source / ground truth for 'will fatalities in region X exceed N' and for calibrating the noisier real-time GDELT signal. Displacement endpoints price refugee-threshold and border-crossing contracts.

**UCDP API (Uppsala Conflict Data Program)** — Uppsala University, Dept. of Peace and Conflict Research `LIVE`

- The academic gold standard for battle-related deaths. Endpoints: gedevents (Georeferenced Event Dataset, 417,968+ events, geocoded, with high/low/best fatality estimates and side attribution), ucdpprioconflict (state-based armed conflict dyads with intensity thresholds), nonstate, onesided, dyadic, battledeaths, organizedviolencecy. Also GED Candidate, released monthly (v26.0.8) and quarterly, for near-current coverage. Current version v26.1 confirmed live.
- Docs: https://ucdp.uu.se/apidocs/
- Auth: free API key | Limits: 5,000 requests per day, and errors count toward the quota. Token is free but is NOT self-service: email mertcan.yilmaz@pcr.uu.se with subject 'UCDP API Access Request' describing intended use; 3-5 working days turnaround. Header: x-ucdp-access-token. Paging required; pagesize configurable. History: 1989 to present for GED.
- Latency: monthly | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: The canonical resolution source for '25 battle deaths' and '1000 battle deaths' conflict-threshold contracts, which is exactly how academic and several prediction-market definitions of 'war' are written. Its 25/1000-death intensity thresholds are literally the contract language on many 'will X become a war' markets.

**ACLED API (Armed Conflict Location & Event Data)** — ACLED `LIVE`

- Event-level armed conflict and protest data: battles, explosions/remote violence, violence against civilians, protests, riots, strategic developments — with date, geolocation, actor1/actor2, associated actors, notes, and fatalities. Near-real-time (weekly release cadence for Partner/Enterprise). Global coverage; the broadest protest+political-violence coding that exists.
- Docs: https://acleddata.com/api-documentation/getting-started
- Auth: OAuth | Limits: CRITICAL: the Open (free public) tier does NOT include API access. API is gated to Research, Partner and Enterprise tiers. Research tier (institutional academic email) gets aggregated data plus LAGGED event data; Partner/Enterprise get disaggregated weekly / expedited weekly. Default row limit is 5,000 per call; pagination calls do not count against the rate limit. Exact calls/day and calls/min are NOT published — UNKNOWN. OAuth token TTL 86,400s (24h), refresh token 14 days. Verified: unauthenticated GET to /api/acled/read returns HTTP 403.
- Latency: weekly | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: Best-in-class for protest and civil-unrest contracts and for actor-specific violence contracts, but the lag on the free-eligible tier makes it a calibration/backtest source rather than a live pricing source. For live use, price off GDELT and resolve against ACLED/HAPI.

**DeepStateMap API (Ukraine territorial control)** — DeepState UA `LIVE`

- GeoJSON FeatureCollection of the current Russian-occupied / contested / liberated areas in Ukraine as polygons, plus named frontline features. /api/history/last returns the latest snapshot with an incrementing id. Effectively a machine-readable frontline.
- Docs: https://deepstatemap.live/api/history/last
- Auth: none | Limits: /api/history/last is open with no key (verified HTTP 200, returns full polygon FeatureCollection). The historical listing /api/history returns HTTP 401 — a token is required for time-series snapshots, and the token process is not publicly documented (UNKNOWN). No published rate limit — UNKNOWN. Practical workaround: poll /api/history/last daily and build your own history.
- Latency: daily | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: Directly prices the largest category of Ukraine-war contracts: 'will Russia control settlement X by date Y', 'will the front move more than N km', 'will city Z fall'. Computing area-held deltas from consecutive snapshots gives a quantitative rate-of-advance that markets price badly. There is no comparable free feed for any other conflict.

**OFAC Sanctions List Service (SDN + Consolidated)** — US Treasury, Office of Foreign Assets Control `LIVE`

- Full Specially Designated Nationals list and the Consolidated (non-SDN) list — individuals, entities, vessels, aircraft, crypto wallet addresses, with program codes (UKRAINE-EO13662, RUSSIA-EO14024, SDGT, NPWMD, IRAN, etc.), aliases, addresses, DOB/POB, and dates of designation. Formats: XML, CSV, PIP, DEL, FF.
- Docs: https://ofac.treasury.gov/faqs/topic/1636
- Auth: none | Limits: No key, no registration, no rate limit published. Verified live 2026: https://sanctionslistservice.ofac.treas.gov/api/download/sdn.xml returns HTTP 200, 29,093,584 bytes; consolidated.xml returns 1,062,957 bytes; the legacy https://www.treasury.gov/ofac/downloads/sdn.csv still returns 200 at 5,695,725 bytes. Files are republished on designation days (irregular, often multiple times/week). NOTE: the Sanctions List Search *web tool* explicitly forbids automated querying — use the bulk files.
- Latency: daily | Format: CSV bulk
- Relevance: Primary resolution source for every 'will the US sanction X by date Y' and 'will X be delisted' contract. Diffing consecutive SDN pulls gives designation/delisting events within hours of publication — usually faster than news coverage, which is a genuine informational edge on sanctions markets.

**EU Financial Sanctions Files (FSF) — consolidated list XML** — European Commission, DG FISMA `LIVE`

- The EU's consolidated financial sanctions list: all designated persons, groups and entities under EU restrictive measures, with legal basis (Council Regulation/Decision numbers), programme, identifiers, and designation dates.
- Docs: https://webgate.ec.europa.eu/fsd/fsf
- Auth: none | Limits: Public token in the URL query string (the well-known value 'dG9rZW4tMjAxNw' = base64 'token-2017'); no registration. Verified live 2026: returns HTTP 200, 25,766,640 bytes. No published rate limit — UNKNOWN. Updated on adoption of each new sanctions package.
- Latency: daily | Format: CSV bulk
- Relevance: Resolves 'will the EU adopt its Nth sanctions package by date Y' and 'will entity X be EU-designated'. EU packages are negotiated publicly and slip constantly, so the gap between announced intent and actual XML publication is a reliably mispriced window.

**OpenSanctions bulk data (default dataset)** — OpenSanctions / Open Knowledge `LIVE`

- A merged, entity-resolved, FollowTheMoney-schema graph of 250+ sanctions and PEP sources worldwide: OFAC, EU FSF, UN, UK OFSI, Canada, Australia, Switzerland, Japan, Ukraine NSDC, plus PEP lists, criminal watchlists and company registries. Deduplicated across regimes with stable entity IDs — this is what you actually want instead of parsing 8 government XMLs.
- Docs: https://www.opensanctions.org/docs/bulk/
- Auth: none | Limits: BULK DOWNLOAD is free for non-commercial use under CC-BY-NC 4.0 — verified: https://data.opensanctions.org/datasets/latest/default/index.json returns HTTP 200 JSON. Commercial use of bulk data requires a paid licence. The hosted API (api.opensanctions.org, which runs their open-source 'yente' engine — verified live) is pay-as-you-go metered per query with volume discounts starting at 20,000 requests/month; free trial keys for business emails and free keys for public-interest work, but the exact free-key quota is NOT published — UNKNOWN. Self-hosting yente against the free bulk files removes the metering entirely.
- Latency: daily | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: One feed replaces the whole sanctions subdomain. Cross-regime entity resolution lets you price 'will the EU follow the US on entity X' — historically a strong lead-lag pattern that sanctions markets underprice. Self-host yente to avoid per-query cost.

**adsb.lol API — /v2/mil (military aircraft) and /v2/ladd** — adsb.lol (community ADS-B network) `LIVE`

- Live positions of all currently-tracked aircraft flagged military in the community database: hex, callsign, registration, type, altitude (baro and geometric), ground speed, track, vertical rate, squawk, lat/lon, and RSSI. /v2/ladd covers FAA Limiting Aircraft Data Displayed (privacy-blocked) airframes. Also /v2/pia, /v2/hex/{icao}, /v2/callsign/{cs}, /v2/point/{lat}/{lon}/{radius}.
- Docs: https://api.adsb.lol/docs
- Auth: none | Limits: Completely open, no key. Verified live 2026: /v2/mil and /v2/ladd both return HTTP 200 with live aircraft arrays. No published rate limit — UNKNOWN; the project asks that you feed data back if you poll heavily. Snapshot-only (no history) unless you persist it yourself.
- Latency: realtime/websocket | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: The fastest public signal for force posture: tanker and AWACS surges, strategic-bomber deployments, VIP/evacuation aircraft, NATO ISR orbits along a border. Tanker activity spikes have preceded announced strikes by hours. Prices 'will there be a strike on X by date Y' and 'will country Z evacuate its embassy' far ahead of news.

**Federal Register API v1** — US National Archives / GPO `LIVE`

- Every US Executive Order, presidential proclamation, agency rule and notice, full text with structured metadata, searchable by term, agency, type and date. Sanctions EOs, national emergency declarations and renewals, BIS Entity List additions, arms-export rule changes all land here first.
- Docs: https://www.federalregister.gov/developers/api/v1
- Auth: none | Limits: No key required — verified HTTP 200, 10,000 matching documents for term 'sanctions', 50 pages. Default per_page 20, max per_page 1000. No published rate limit — UNKNOWN. Documents appear on the public inspection desk before the official publication date.
- Latency: daily | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: The legally authoritative, machine-readable source for US sanctions and national-emergency actions. The public-inspection window means you can see an EO before its official effective date — a clean, legal, structural edge on US-policy contracts.

**IMF PortWatch (ArcGIS FeatureServer)** — IMF + Oxford University `LIVE`

- Daily port-call counts and trade-volume estimates for ~1,400 ports and 25 maritime chokepoints (Bab el-Mandeb, Suez, Hormuz, Bosphorus, Panama, Malacca, Taiwan Strait), by vessel type (container, dry bulk, tanker, general cargo, roro), derived from AIS. Also disruption simulation layers.
- Docs: https://portwatch.imf.org/
- Auth: none | Limits: Open ArcGIS REST FeatureServer, no key — verified HTTP 200 on services9.arcgis.com/weJ1QsnbMYJlCHdG/arcgis/rest/services/PortWatch_ports_database/FeatureServer/0/query. Standard ArcGIS paging, resultRecordCount typically capped at 1000-2000 per request server-side. No published rate limit — UNKNOWN.
- Latency: daily | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: Direct, quantified, daily resolution of maritime-disruption contracts: Red Sea / Bab el-Mandeb transit collapse, Hormuz closure, Taiwan Strait interdiction, Black Sea grain corridor. Transit counts move days before the shipping-rate headlines the market reacts to.

**ISW (Institute for the Study of War) RSS** — Institute for the Study of War / Critical Threats Project (AEI) `LIVE`

- Daily Russian Offensive Campaign Assessments, Iran Updates, China-Taiwan Updates, and Africa File — the most-cited narrative assessments of frontline movement, with geolocated claim adjudication and named-settlement control changes.
- Docs: https://understandingwar.org/feed/
- Auth: none | Limits: RSS is open with no key — verified HTTP 200 at https://understandingwar.org/feed/ ONLY. The www subdomain variants return HTTP 403 (https://www.understandingwar.org/rss.xml and /publications/rss.xml both 403) — use the apex domain. Full-text bodies are HTML; there is no structured API and no machine-readable control-change dataset. No published rate limit — UNKNOWN.
- Latency: daily | Format: RSS
- Relevance: ISW's assessed-control maps are explicitly named as the resolution source on several Ukraine territorial contracts, which makes this a resolution feed, not just commentary. Requires an LLM extraction layer to turn prose into settlement-level claims.

**Polymarket Gamma API** — Polymarket `LIVE`

- All markets and events with current prices, outcome tokens, volume, liquidity, resolution source text, end dates and tags. The conflict/geopolitics tag set covers ceasefires, strikes, leader exits, sanctions and territorial control.
- Docs: https://docs.polymarket.com/developers/gamma-markets-api/overview
- Auth: none | Limits: Public read, no key — verified HTTP 200 on gamma-api.polymarket.com/markets. Default limit 100, offset paging. No published rate limit on the Gamma read endpoints — UNKNOWN (the CLOB trading API has separate documented limits).
- Latency: realtime/websocket | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: This is the market side of the panel — live price and implied probability for every geopolitical contract, and the resolution-source text you must parse to know what actually settles a contract. Required to compute edge at all; without it the forecast has nothing to trade against.

#### USEFUL

**UN Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List** — United Nations Security Council `LIVE`

- XML of all individuals and entities subject to UNSC sanctions measures across all committees (1267/ISIL-Al-Qaida, Taliban, DPRK, Libya, Yemen, South Sudan, Mali, Haiti, etc.), with listing dates, narrative summaries of reasons, and committee references.
- Docs: https://scsanctions.un.org/consolidated/
- Auth: none | Limits: No key, no registration. Verified live 2026: https://scsanctions.un.org/resources/xml/en/consolidated.xml returns HTTP 200, 2,176,957 bytes. No published rate limit — UNKNOWN.
- Latency: weekly | Format: CSV bulk
- Relevance: Resolves UN-specific designation markets and, more usefully, is the veto-constrained list: additions require P5 consent, so movement here is a hard signal about great-power alignment that prices 'will the UNSC act on X' contracts.

**ReliefWeb API v2** — UN OCHA `LIVE`

- Full-text searchable archive of ~1M curated humanitarian reports, situation updates, and a structured 'disasters' taxonomy with country, disaster type, and status. Sources include OCHA, UNHCR, ICRC, MSF, WFP, ACAPS and national authorities. Strong for conflict-driven humanitarian emergencies, aid access, and famine/IPC reporting.
- Docs: https://apidoc.reliefweb.int/
- Auth: registration required | Limits: 1,000 API calls per day and 1,000 entries returned per call. CHANGED 2025: since 1 November 2025 you must use a PRE-APPROVED appname — arbitrary appnames now fail. Verified 2026: appname=test and appname=rwint-user-0 both return HTTP 403 with 'You are not using an approved appname.' The v1 endpoint is retired (HTTP 410). Request an appname via the docs page.
- Latency: hourly | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: Best free resolution source for famine declarations, IPC phase changes, aid-corridor openings, and casualty figures cited by named agencies. Many humanitarian contracts resolve on 'as reported by OCHA/WFP', and this is that text, structured.

**UNHCR Refugee Statistics API** — UNHCR `LIVE`

- Refugees, asylum-seekers, IDPs, returnees, stateless persons and 'others of concern' by year, country of origin and country of asylum. Endpoints: population, demographics, asylumApplications, asylumDecisions, solutions, idmc (IDP figures via IDMC), unrwa, nowcasting (forward estimates), plus countries/regions/years/footnotes metadata. ~70 years of history.
- Docs: https://api.unhcr.org/docs/refugee-statistics.html
- Auth: none | Limits: No API key required — verified HTTP 200 unauthenticated against https://api.unhcr.org/population/v1/population/. Rate limits are NOT documented — UNKNOWN. Both JSON and CSV output. Annual data with a mid-year release; the nowcasting endpoint is the only near-current series.
- Latency: monthly | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: Prices displacement-threshold contracts ('will X million refugees leave country Y'). The nowcasting endpoint matters most — it is UNHCR's own forward estimate, so a market trading away from it on a UNHCR-resolved contract is a direct edge.

**OpenSky Network REST API — /states/all** — OpenSky Network (Uni Oldenburg / ETH Zurich / Armasuisse) `LIVE`

- Live state vectors for all aircraft the network sees: ICAO24, callsign, origin country, position, baro/geo altitude, velocity, heading, vertical rate, on_ground, squawk, spi. Bounding-box filterable. Research-grade coverage with an academic historical archive.
- Docs: https://openskynetwork.github.io/opensky-api/rest.html
- Auth: free API key | Limits: Anonymous access to /states/all works and is metered by credits — verified live 2026, response header x-rate-limit-remaining decremented 396 -> 395 across calls, consistent with the documented 400 credits/day for anonymous users. Registered users get 4,000 credits/day (OAuth2 client-credentials since the 2025 auth migration); OpenSky data contributors get 8,000. A bounding-box call costs fewer credits than a global call. CHANGED: /flights/all now returns HTTP 403 anonymously — historical flight endpoints require authentication.
- Latency: realtime/websocket | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: Complements adsb.lol with better European and research coverage and a real historical archive for backtesting 'aircraft activity -> escalation' models. Credit budget is tight, so use bounding boxes around the theaters your markets actually cover.

**Humanitarian Data Exchange (HDX) CKAN API v3** — UN OCHA Centre for Humanitarian Data `LIVE`

- Catalog and direct file access to 2,358+ conflict-tagged datasets (verified count) plus ~20,000 total: ACLED country exports, UCDP mirrors, IOM DTM displacement rounds, IPC food-security classifications, subnational admin boundaries (COD-AB), health-facility and damage assessments, and per-crisis data grids.
- Docs: https://data.humdata.org/api/3/action/package_search
- Auth: none | Limits: Standard CKAN API, no key for read operations — verified HTTP 200, package_search q=conflict returns count 2358. rows max 1000 per call with start offset paging. No published rate limit — UNKNOWN.
- Latency: daily | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: The discovery layer. When a new crisis starts, the country data grid here is where ACLED/DTM/IPC exports appear within days, often before any API exposes them. Use it to auto-ingest new conflict corpora rather than hand-wiring each provider.

**aisstream.io (live AIS WebSocket)** — aisstream.io `LIVE`

- Global live AIS message stream over WebSocket: 25 message types including PositionReport, ShipStaticData, StandardClassBPositionReport, SafetyBroadcastMessage and AidsToNavigationReport, with normalized MMSI, ship name, lat/lon plus the raw decoded payload. Bounding-box subscription required.
- Docs: https://aisstream.io/documentation
- Auth: free API key | Limits: Free API key on signup. Hard limits verified in docs: 3 subscribed connections per account and 3 open connections per originating IP; subscription updates limited to 1 per second per connection. Flow control drops messages if you consume too slowly. Explicitly NO SLA and NO durable replay — if you disconnect, those messages are gone. Browser-direct connections are forbidden; you must proxy. Max bounding boxes per subscription is UNKNOWN.
- Latency: realtime/websocket | Format: WebSocket
- Relevance: Prices naval movement and shipping-attack contracts in real time: warship transits through a strait, tanker diversions around the Cape, AIS-dark behavior by sanctioned fleets. The 3-connection cap means you must pick your theaters; budget one connection per active market cluster.

**GDELT Television API 2.0 (TV Explorer)** — GDELT Project + Internet Archive TV News Archive `LIVE`

- Searchable closed-caption index of US and international television news. Modes: TimelineVol (share of airtime mentioning a term, 15-min resolution), TimelineVolNorm, ClipGallery, StationChart, WordCloud. Lets you measure how much airtime a conflict, leader, or policy is getting, by station.
- Docs: https://blog.gdeltproject.org/gdelt-2-0-television-api-debuts/
- Auth: none | Limits: No key — verified HTTP 200 on api.gdeltproject.org/api/v2/tv/tv. No published rate limit — UNKNOWN. Coverage window and station roster vary by market; US national networks have the deepest history.
- Latency: hourly | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: Television airtime is the best free proxy for US political salience, which drives 'will Congress authorize X', 'will the President address the nation on Y', and aid-package markets. Cable-news attention leads Congressional action more reliably than print coverage does.

**GDELT Context API 2.0** — GDELT Project `LIVE`

- Returns the surrounding sentence/snippet context for a search term across the global news corpus, rather than just article-level hits. Lets you extract phrasing-level signals ('confirmed dead', 'ceasefire agreed', 'withdrew from') instead of topic-level noise.
- Docs: https://blog.gdeltproject.org/announcing-the-gdelt-context-2-0-api/
- Auth: none | Limits: No key — verified HTTP 200. No published rate limit — UNKNOWN. Same rolling-window constraint family as the DOC API.
- Latency: sub-minute | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: Snippet-level extraction is what lets an LLM layer actually resolve a contract's exact wording ('confirmed', 'signed', 'ratified') instead of guessing from a headline. This is the feed that makes automated market resolution tractable.

**World Bank Indicators API — military expenditure series** — World Bank (sourcing SIPRI) `LIVE`

- MS.MIL.XPND.GD.ZS (milex % of GDP), MS.MIL.XPND.CN / .CD (local currency and USD), MS.MIL.XPND.ZS (% of government expenditure), MS.MIL.TOTL.P1 (armed forces personnel), MS.MIL.MPRT.KD / MS.MIL.XPRT.KD (arms imports/exports, SIPRI TIV constant USD). Full country panel back to 1960 where reported.
- Docs: https://datahelpdesk.worldbank.org/knowledgebase/articles/889392
- Auth: none | Limits: No key — verified HTTP 200. Default 50 rows per page, per_page max 32,500. No published rate limit — UNKNOWN. This is the free machine-readable route to SIPRI milex numbers, since SIPRI's own milex site blocks automated access (HTTP 403 verified).
- Latency: monthly | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: Resolves 'will country X hit 2% / 3.5% of GDP on defense by year Y' — one of the most common NATO-related contract types. The World Bank mirror is the only reliably scriptable path to these numbers.

**SIPRI Arms Transfers Database (CSV export endpoint)** — Stockholm International Peace Research Institute `LIVE`

- Trade registers of every transfer of major conventional weapons 1950-2025 (updated 9 March 2026) — supplier, recipient, weapon designation, description, number ordered/delivered, order and delivery years — plus Trend-Indicator Values (TIV) for consolidated statistics.
- Docs: https://armstransfers.sipri.org/
- Auth: none | Limits: No key. The export endpoint responds (HTTP 200) but returns content only with a correct parameter set — a bare GET to /ArmsTransfer/TransferRegister returned 405 bytes, i.e. you must supply year range, country codes and format=csv. There is no official API and no documented rate limit — UNKNOWN. SIPRI's separate milex.sipri.org returns HTTP 403 to automated clients; use the World Bank mirror for milex. Unofficial wrapper: benryan58/sipri_arms.
- Latency: monthly | Format: CSV bulk
- Relevance: The authoritative annual record of arms deliveries. Annual cadence makes it a prior-setter, not a live feed, but it is the resolution source named in several arms-transfer contracts.

**EU Sanctions Map API** — EU Council / Presidency of the Council of the EU `LIVE`

- Structured metadata on every EU sanctions regime: regime id, target, legal specification, adopting instruments, notes and historical amendment chain. Complements the FSF designation list with the regime-level legal context.
- Docs: https://www.sanctionsmap.eu/
- Auth: none | Limits: No key — verified HTTP 200 on https://www.sanctionsmap.eu/api/v1/regime, returning JSON regime records (regime id 1 = Taliban measures, with UNSCR 1988/1989 references). NOTE: the data.sanctionsmap.eu host did not resolve (connection failure) — use the www host. No published rate limit — UNKNOWN. Undocumented/unofficial API surface, so treat it as scrape-adjacent and expect breakage.
- Latency: weekly | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: Gives the legal-instrument layer that designation lists lack — which Council Decision a measure sits under and when it expires. EU sanctions regimes require periodic unanimous renewal, and renewal-failure markets are priced off exactly these expiry dates.

**Wikimedia EventStreams + Action API (Current Events Portal)** — Wikimedia Foundation `LIVE`

- EventStreams is a live SSE feed of every edit across all Wikimedia projects. Combined with the Action API against Portal:Current_events/YYYY_Month_DD, you get a human-curated, sourced, daily chronology of world events including conflict incidents, plus per-conflict article edit velocity.
- Docs: https://stream.wikimedia.org/?doc
- Auth: none | Limits: Both open with no key — verified HTTP 200 on stream.wikimedia.org/v2/stream/recentchange and on the Action API parse of a Current events subpage. Action API: 500 items/request for anonymous users, 5,000 for users with apihighlimits. Wikimedia asks for a descriptive User-Agent and serialized (non-parallel) requests; no hard numeric cap published for anonymous read — UNKNOWN.
- Latency: realtime/websocket | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: Edit velocity on a conflict article is one of the fastest free crowd-attention signals available — it spikes within minutes of a major incident, before GDELT's 15-minute batch. The Current Events Portal is a clean, sourced ground-truth chronology for backtesting.

**Wikidata Query Service (SPARQL)** — Wikimedia Foundation `LIVE`

- SPARQL over the structured knowledge graph: armed conflicts with start/end dates and participants, heads of state with term dates, military units, weapon systems, treaties with signature and ratification dates, sanctions instruments. Joinable to everything else by QID.
- Docs: https://query.wikidata.org/
- Auth: none | Limits: No key — verified HTTP 200. Enforced limits: 60-second query timeout, and one-minute/five-minute processing-time budgets per client (60s and 30s respectively) after which you get HTTP 429. Descriptive User-Agent required. No calls/day cap published — UNKNOWN.
- Latency: daily | Format: GraphQL
- Relevance: The entity-resolution backbone. It is what maps 'the Russian Defence Minister' in a headline to a stable ID you can join across ACLED actors, sanctions lists, and market contract text. Not a signal itself — infrastructure that makes every other feed joinable.

**USGS FDSN Event Web Service** — US Geological Survey / ANSS `LIVE`

- Global seismic event catalog in GeoJSON/QuakeML with magnitude, depth, location, and — critically — an event 'type' field that distinguishes earthquake from 'explosion' and 'nuclear explosion'. Near-real-time summary feeds (all_hour, all_day, significant_week).
- Docs: https://earthquake.usgs.gov/fdsnws/event/1/
- Auth: none | Limits: No key — verified HTTP 200 on both fdsnws/event/1/query and the all_hour.geojson summary feed. Documented cap: 20,000 events per query (exceeding it returns HTTP 400); the service asks that you chunk large historical pulls. No calls/day limit published — UNKNOWN. NOTE: the IRIS FDSN mirror at service.iris.edu returned HTTP 404 — that service moved under EarthScope.
- Latency: minutely | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: The only free, fast, technical detector for a nuclear test. A shallow ~M4-5 event with explosion characteristics near Punggye-ri or Lop Nur resolves 'will DPRK/China conduct a nuclear test by date Y' hours before any official statement. CTBTO's own IMS data is not openly accessible (see deadEnds), so this is the practical substitute.

**Tzeva Adom / Red Alert API (Israel rocket and drone alerts)** — tzevaadom.co.il (community mirror of IDF Home Front Command OREF alerts) `LIVE`

- Real-time rocket, missile and hostile-aircraft-intrusion sirens by locality, with alert category and timestamp. Effectively a per-minute ground-truth stream of incoming fire in the Israel/Lebanon/Gaza/Yemen theater.
- Docs: https://api.tzevaadom.co.il/notifications
- Auth: none | Limits: Open, no key — verified HTTP 200 on api.tzevaadom.co.il/notifications. No published rate limit — UNKNOWN; it is an unofficial community mirror with no SLA. The official OREF endpoint (www.oref.org.il/WarningMessages/alert/alerts.json) now returns HTTP 403 to non-browser clients even with Referer and X-Requested-With headers set.
- Latency: realtime/websocket | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: Sub-minute ground truth for the single most actively traded live-conflict theater. Alert volume and geographic spread price 'will there be a major escalation by date Y' and ceasefire-holding contracts faster than any news feed. Fragile unofficial dependency — mirror it yourself.

- INFORM Severity Index scoring 100+ humanitarian crises, plus Humanitarian Access datasets (access constraints by country), Risk List forward-looking crisis warnings, and crisis-specific analytical datasets.

- Auth: registration required | Limits: All ACAPS datasets are free. Verified live 2026: the DRF-backed API root returns HTTP 200 and unauthenticated dataset calls return the browsable-API login page. Register at https://api.acaps.org/register/ (verified HTTP 200), then POST credentials to /api/v1/get-auth-token/ and send 'Authorization: Token <token>'. Exact rate limits are NOT documented — UNKNOWN.
- Latency: monthly | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: The Risk List is an explicit forward-looking crisis-escalation forecast from professional analysts — a free expert prior you can directly compare to market-implied probability on 'will crisis X deteriorate' contracts. **US Government official feeds (DoD releases, State Dept travel advisories, UN press)** — US DoD / US State Dept / United Nations `LIVE`

- DoD press releases and contract announcements (weapons-package announcements land here first); State Dept travel advisory changes with Level 1-4 and 'Do Not Travel'/'Authorized Departure'/'Ordered Departure' status; UN press releases including Security Council meeting outcomes and vote records.

Verified live 2026: DoD RSS (defense.gov/DesktopModules/ArticleCS/RSS.ashx?ContentType=1&Site=945) HTTP 200; State Dept travel advisories (travel.state.gov/_res/rss/TAsTWs.xml) HTTP 200; UN press (press.un.org/en/rss.xml) HTTP 200. No published rate limits — UNKNOWN. NOTE: the NATO RSS path at nato.int/cps/en/natolive/rss_news.xml returns HTTP 404; scrape nato.int/cps/en/natohq/news.htm (HTTP 200) instead.
- Latency: hourly | Format: RSS
