- Relevance: The only free-ish source for dark-fleet and AIS-spoofing detection — central to Russian/Iranian/Venezuelan oil-sanctions-evasion contracts and shadow-fleet interdiction markets. Check the non-commercial clause before building a paid product on it.

**GDELT Global Entity Graph (GEG) 3.0** — GDELT Project (using Google Cloud Natural Language API) `LIVE`

- Per-article named-entity extraction with entity types, salience scores and sentiment, published as daily JSON-newline files. Turns raw news into a people/orgs/places graph — who is being talked about, how centrally, and with what sentiment.
- Docs: http://data.gdeltproject.org/gdeltv3/geg_gcnlapi/MASTERFILELIST.TXT
- Auth: none | Limits: No key, plain HTTP file fetch — verified HTTP 200 on the master file list. No rate limit published — UNKNOWN.
- Latency: daily | Format: CSV bulk
- Relevance: Builds the actor graph behind conflict markets: which commanders, ministers, or armed groups are rising in salience. Sharp salience jumps for a defense minister or a rebel leader often precede coup, purge, or assassination markets moving.

**UN Comtrade Public Preview API (HS Chapter 93 — arms and ammunition)** — UN Statistics Division `LIVE`

- Reported bilateral trade flows by HS commodity code. HS 93 is arms and ammunition; HS 8710 armoured fighting vehicles; HS 8802/8806 aircraft and drones. Gives reporter, partner, flow (import/export), period, trade value and quantity.
- Docs: https://comtradedeveloper.un.org/
- Auth: none | Limits: The /public/v1/preview/ path works with no key — verified HTTP 200, returned 160 rows for reporterCode=842 (USA), period=2023, cmdCode=93, flowCode=X. The preview path is capped at 500 records per call. Authenticated free-tier keys (self-service registration) raise this to 100,000 records. Requests/hour on the preview path are NOT documented — UNKNOWN. Annual data lags 1-2 years; monthly available for some reporters.
- Latency: monthly | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: Official declared arms-trade flows. Lags badly, so it is a backtest and baseline source, not a live signal — but it is the only free structured record of who legally ships weapons to whom, which anchors priors on 'will country X supply weapon Y to Z'.

**Harvard Dataverse Search API (ICEWS, Mass Mobilization, Correlates of War)** — Harvard IQSS Dataverse `LIVE`

- Programmatic search and file download for the major academic conflict corpora hosted there: ICEWS coded event data (Lockheed/DARPA political event stream), the Mass Mobilization Protest dataset, Correlates of War Militarized Interstate Disputes, and assorted replication datasets for conflict-forecasting papers.
- Docs: https://guides.dataverse.org/en/latest/api/search.html
- Auth: none | Limits: Search API is open with no key — verified HTTP 200 on dataverse.harvard.edu/api/search?q=ICEWS&type=dataset. per_page max 1000. Restricted files require an API token; most conflict datasets here are public. No published rate limit — UNKNOWN. These are static archival datasets — ICEWS public releases stopped updating years ago, so treat as historical only.
- Latency: monthly | Format: CSV bulk
- Relevance: Backtesting corpus, not a live feed. ICEWS and COW-MID give decades of labeled interstate-dispute outcomes to fit and validate a conflict-escalation model before you point it at GDELT in real time.

#### Repos

- `alex9smith/gdelt-doc-api` — Python client for the GDELT 2.0 DOC API — wraps ArtList and all Timeline modes, returns pandas DataFrames. 231 stars, last pushed 2025-04-22. · Saves a day of parameter-fiddling against GDELT's undocumented query grammar. The Timeline wrappers give you a coverage-volume series per market keyword in about five lines, which is the fastest path to a working narrative-intensity feature.
- `RBozydar/py-gdelt` — Comprehensive Python client covering GDELT DOC, GEO, TV and the raw v2 file feeds. Last pushed 2026-09-19 — the most actively maintained GDELT wrapper found. · The only GDELT library still being updated in 2026. Covers the raw 15-minute file ingest as well as the APIs, so one dependency handles both the streaming and the query paths.
- `linwoodc3/gdeltPyR` — The long-standing Python library for pulling and parsing GDELT 1.0/2.0 raw event and GKG files into DataFrames, with correct column schemas for both versions. · Hand-parsing the 61-column GDELT event schema and the GKG v2.1 format is error-prone; this has the schemas already correct. Use it for the historical backfill even though it is less actively maintained than py-gdelt.
- `koala73/worldmonitor` — A production geopolitical-intelligence dashboard aggregating ACLED, UCDP, GDELT, IMF PortWatch, adsb.lol, OREF, UN OCHA HAPI, CelesTrak, gpsjam, World Bank MS.MIL.*, Taiwan MND, Japan Joint Staff, Polymarket and a large tiered RSS network. 87.1k stars, 7,627 commits. · This is the closest existing thing to the Bloomberg-terminal-for-conflict being described. Its docs/data-sources page catalogs every feed with provider, feed-tier, license posture and collection method — the single best starting map for this domain. Read its source rather than rediscovering the same feeds.
- `chris-dworschak/ucdp.api` — R package (also on CRAN) that wraps the UCDP API — handles paging, version selection across gedevents/ucdpprioconflict/nonstate/onesided, and the new token header. · Encodes the UCDP paging and version-pinning logic correctly, which matters because the API requires paging and versions bump (currently v26.1) in ways that silently break naive clients. Port the version-handling even if you work in Python.
- `chris-dworschak/acled.api` — R package on CRAN for the ACLED API, with the OAuth flow and the 5,000-row default-limit pagination handled. 10 stars, pushed 2024-10-02. · Reference implementation of ACLED's OAuth token/refresh dance (24h token, 14d refresh) and its pagination semantics — notably that pagination calls do not count against the rate limit, which changes how you should batch pulls.
- `scarnecchia/oryx_data` — Daily CSV scrape of Oryx's visually-confirmed Russia/Ukraine equipment-loss lists: totals_by_system.csv, totals_by_type.csv, daily_count.csv, and per-status event files (destroyed, damaged, abandoned, captured). 37 stars. · The only machine-readable Oryx mirror with a real schema — Oryx itself publishes only HTML. STALE WARNING: last pushed 2025-08-21 despite claiming daily updates, so treat the CSVs as a frozen historical corpus and fork the scrape_oryx.R scraper if you need current data.
- `openskynetwork/opensky-api` — Official OpenSky Network client libraries (Python and Java) for the REST and historical-flights APIs. · Handles the 2025 OAuth2 client-credentials migration that broke every older OpenSky client. Since /flights/all now returns 403 anonymously, you need this auth flow to reach any historical aircraft data.
- `aisstream/aisstream` — Official aisstream.io client examples and message-type definitions across languages for the AIS WebSocket. · Decoding the 25 AIS message types and implementing the required flow-control/reconnect behavior is the whole job; the examples give you correct bounding-box subscription and reconnect handling, which matters because the service explicitly does not replay dropped messages.
- `pipeworx-io/mcp-ucdp` — MCP server exposing UCDP armed-conflict deaths, active wars and violence events per country since 1989 as tool calls. · Directly relevant if the research panel's AI synthesis layer is MCP-based — it turns UCDP into a tool an LLM can query during analysis instead of a batch ingest you have to pre-join.
- `l0v3m0n3y/deepstatemap` — Small web API wrapper around deepstatemap.live's endpoints for Ukraine occupied-territory polygons. Pushed 2026-08-25. · Documents the undocumented DeepStateMap endpoint surface, including which paths need auth (/api/history returns 401 while /api/history/last is open). Saves you reverse-engineering the frontline feed.
- `dmitriwamback/ukraine-war-map` — Uses the DeepStateMap API with folium to render and track occupied territory over time. · Shows the polygon-to-area-delta computation — turning consecutive GeoJSON snapshots into a quantitative km²-per-week rate of advance, which is the actual feature you need to price territorial-control contracts.
- `opensanctions/yente` — The open-source entity-matching and sanctions-screening API engine that powers api.opensanctions.org (confirmed — the public API root serves yente's own ReDoc page). · Self-host yente against the free CC-BY-NC bulk data files and you get the full OpenSanctions matching API with no per-query metering. This is the single biggest cost avoidance available in the sanctions subdomain.
- `omnitraceapp/ofac-sdn-parser` — Fetches and parses the OFAC SDN list, with specific handling for crypto wallet addresses embedded in SDN entries. Pushed 2026-09-06. · Actively maintained against the current sanctionslistservice.ofac.treas.gov endpoints (the ones verified live here, not the deprecated treasury.gov paths). The diffing logic is what turns a 29MB static file into a designation-event stream.
- `benryan58/sipri_arms` — Unofficial pseudo-API wrapper for the SIPRI Arms Transfers Database, hitting both the Trade Register and TIV export endpoints, plus manipulation and visualization helpers. · SIPRI publishes no API and the bare export endpoint returns almost nothing without a correct parameter set. This repo has the working parameter combinations for year ranges, country codes and CSV format.
- `bad-antics/n01d-overwatch` — Real-time Middle East and global conflict intelligence dashboard combining OSINT aggregation, flight tracking and warzone monitoring. 10 stars, actively forked (Lapk0m fork pushed 2026-09-20). · A current, working reference architecture for exactly this panel at smaller scale — useful for seeing which feeds survive contact with production and how they handle the unofficial ones (OREF, Telegram) that break often.
- `swilliams9772/gdelt-toolkit` — GDELT 2.0 toolkit bundling a Python API client, a 41-tool MCP server, a Streamlit dashboard, and live-validated DOC API coverage. Pushed 2026-05-30. · The MCP server is the piece worth taking — it exposes GDELT as 41 discrete tools an LLM synthesis layer can call, which is the pattern needed for the AI layer of the research panel.

### Sports (all major leagues) — free data feeds for prediction-market pricing, verified September 2026

#### CORE

**MLB Stats API (statsapi.mlb.com)** — MLB Advanced Media `LIVE`

- The single most complete free feed in sports. /api/v1/schedule (fixtures), /api/v1.1/game/{pk}/feed/live (full pitch-by-pitch play-by-play, 68+ plays in the game I fetched), boxscore, linescore, rosters, probable pitchers, transactions, and an /injuries feed. VERIFIED PAYLOAD: gameData.weather returns {condition:'Partly Cloudy', temp:'83', wind:'4 mph, In From LF'} and liveData.boxscore.officials returns the full umpire crew by position (Dan Bellino/Home Plate, Tony Randazzo/First Base, Phil Cuzzi/Second Base, Alex Tosi/Third Base). Venue weather + umpire assignment + PBP in one unauthenticated call. Statcast-adjacent fields present. History back to 1901 for schedules.
- Docs: https://statsapi.mlb.com/docs/ (also the community reference at https://github.com/toddrob99/MLB-StatsAPI/wiki)
- Auth: none | Limits: No API key, no published quota. MLB's terms ask for non-commercial use and reasonable request rates; there is no documented calls/day or calls/min number — UNKNOWN. History depth: schedules back to 1901, full PBP reliably 2008+.
- Latency: realtime (live feed updates during play, roughly every 5-15s) | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: CORE for every MLB contract. Umpire crew drives strike-zone/total markets; wind direction at venue is the single biggest free edge on MLB run totals. Probable pitchers + late scratches settle 'will X start' markets.

**ESPN Core API (sports.core.api.espn.com) — including free sportsbook odds** — ESPN / Disney (undocumented but public) `LIVE`

- Sport-agnostic entity API: /v2/sports/{sport}/leagues/{league}/events, /athletes, /teams, /seasons, /competitions/{id}/odds, /competitions/{id}/probabilities, /competitions/{id}/predictor. VERIFIED: NFL, MMA/UFC, ATP tennis, PGA golf all return 200 with no auth. The odds endpoint is the headline find — for NFL event 401872945 it returned provider DraftKings (id 100) with details 'KC -6' and overUnder 46.5, plus per-provider moneyline/spread/total objects and openingOdds/closingOdds sub-resources. Covers NFL, NBA, WNBA, NCAAF, NCAAB, MLB, NHL, soccer (dozens of leagues), tennis, golf, MMA, F1, NASCAR.
- Docs: No official docs. Best community references: https://github.com/pseudo-r/Public-NHL-API and the widely mirrored ESPN endpoint gist at https://gist.github.com/akeaswaran/b48b02f1c94f873c6655e7129910fc3b
- Auth: none | Limits: No key and no published quota — UNKNOWN. Undocumented and unsupported; ESPN can revoke at will. Practical observed behaviour: sustained polling above roughly 1-2 req/s invites throttling. History depth varies by sport; NFL events go back to 2002.
- Latency: sub-minute for scores; odds refresh roughly every 1-5 min | Format: REST JSON (heavily $ref-linked — expect 2-4 hops per entity)
- Relevance: CORE. This is free closing-line data, which the task correctly identifies as the thing that actually moves sports prediction markets. openingOdds vs closingOdds on the same event object gives you line movement without paying an odds vendor. Also the only free cross-sport spine covering tennis, golf and MMA together.

**Sleeper API — NFL player status and injury designations** — Sleeper (fantasy platform) `LIVE`

- GET /v1/players/nfl returns the complete NFL player universe. VERIFIED PAYLOAD: 12,228 players, of which 870 carried a non-null injury_status, with fields injury_status ('Out', 'Questionable', 'Doubtful', 'IR'), injury_body_part ('Groin'), injury_notes, injury_start_date, plus team, depth_chart_order, depth_chart_position, practice_participation, and cross-IDs to espn_id, gsis_id, yahoo_id, rotowire_id, sportradar_id. Also /v1/state/nfl for current week/season phase, and league/roster/transaction endpoints.
- Docs: https://docs.sleeper.com/
- Auth: none | Limits: No API key. Sleeper's docs state a limit of 1000 calls per minute per IP and explicitly ask that you NOT call /v1/players/nfl more than once per day (it is a ~5MB dump meant to be cached).
- Latency: minutely for status changes; the players dump is refreshed daily | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: CORE for NFL injury markets and any NFL player-prop contract. This is the best free, no-auth, no-scrape injury designation feed in existence for the NFL — the cross-ID map alone (espn_id + gsis_id + sportradar_id on one record) solves entity resolution against every other feed here.

**nflverse-data (GitHub Releases bulk datasets)** — nflverse open-source collective `LIVE`

- VERIFIED release tags on the live repo: pbp, injuries, officials, depth_charts, nextgen_stats, snap_counts, rosters, weekly_rosters, schedules, players, player_stats, stats_player, stats_team, pfr_advstats, ftn_charting, draft_picks, combine, contracts, trades, espn_data, pbp_participation, misc. Verified asset URLs: .../download/injuries/injuries_2009.csv (per-season, 2009+), .../download/officials/officials.csv (referee crew assignments per game), .../download/pbp/play_by_play_1999.csv.gz (PBP with EPA/WPA/CPOE back to 1999). Each tag ships csv, csv.gz, parquet, rds and qs.
- Docs: https://github.com/nflverse/nflverse-data and https://nflreadr.nflverse.com/
- Auth: none (GitHub Releases; anonymous GitHub API is 60 req/hr, but raw asset downloads are unmetered) | Limits: No quota on release asset downloads. Anonymous api.github.com metadata calls are limited to 60/hr (I hit this during verification — use a token for 5,000/hr). History depth: PBP 1999+, injuries 2009+, snap counts 2012+, Next Gen Stats 2016+, depth charts 2001+.
- Latency: daily during season (repo pushed 2026-09-16 at time of check); PBP typically updated within hours of game end | Format: CSV / CSV.gz / Parquet bulk
- Relevance: CORE for NFL. The injuries dataset gives you the official Wed/Thu/Fri practice-report progression, not just the final designation — that progression is the leading indicator that prices 'will he play' markets before the Friday report. officials.csv lets you build referee-crew priors for penalty and total markets. Contractually the most stable NFL source here because it is a git repo, not an endpoint someone can revoke.

**NHL Web API (api-web.nhle.com)** — National Hockey League (undocumented but public) `LIVE`

- VERIFIED: /v1/schedule/{date} 200; /v1/gamecenter/{gameId}/play-by-play returned 323 plays for game 2024020500 with eventId, periodDescriptor, timeInPeriod, timeRemaining, situationCode (on-ice strength), homeTeamDefendingSide, typeCode/typeDescKey, plus venue, venueLocation, startTimeUTC, tvBroadcasts and gameState at the root. Also /v1/standings/now (307-redirects to a dated path — follow redirects), /v1/club-schedule-season/{team}/{season}, /v1/player/{id}/landing, /v1/gamecenter/{id}/boxscore, /v1/gamecenter/{id}/right-rail, and roster endpoints.
- Docs: https://github.com/Zmalski/NHL-API-Reference (601 stars, the de-facto reference)
- Auth: none | Limits: No key, no published quota — UNKNOWN. Undocumented; the NHL replaced the old statsapi.web.nhl.com host in 2023 without notice, so treat the contract as unstable.
- Latency: realtime during games (shift-level updates) | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: CORE for all NHL contracts. situationCode gives power-play state for in-play totals. The right-rail endpoint carries scratches and goalie confirmations, which is the NHL equivalent of an injury report and moves puck-line markets at warmup.

**The Odds API** — The Odds API (theoddsapi.com) `LIVE`

- Normalized odds from 70+ bookmakers (DraftKings, FanDuel, BetMGM, Pinnacle, William Hill, Ladbrokes, 1xBet, Sportsbet, TAB) across NFL, NCAAF, CFL, AFL, NBA, WNBA, NCAAB, MLB, KBO, NPB, NHL, SHL, EPL, UCL, La Liga, Serie A, cricket, rugby, golf, tennis and politics. Markets: h2h, spreads, totals, outrights, and player props on higher tiers. Separate Historical Odds API with snapshots back to 2020.
- Docs: https://the-odds-api.com/liveapi/guides/v4/
- Auth: free API key (email registration) | Limits: VERIFIED on the pricing page: Starter plan is free with 500 credits per month. Credits are consumed per region x market combination, not per HTTP call — one request covering 3 regions and 2 markets costs 6 credits, so 500 credits is far less than 500 useful requests. No documented per-minute cap. Paid: 20K/$30, 100K/$59, 5M/$119, 15M/$249 per month. Historical odds listed as included on the free tier; depth back to 2020.
- Latency: sub-minute (roughly 1-5 min refresh depending on sport) | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: CORE, with a hard caveat. This is the cleanest normalized closing-line source, and closing line value is the benchmark every sports prediction market is implicitly quoted against. But 500 credits/month is roughly 16/day — enough to snapshot one league's closing line once a day, not to monitor line movement. Use it as the calibration reference and use ESPN core odds for volume.

**Jolpica F1 (Ergast successor)** — Jolpica open-source project `LIVE`

- VERIFIED: https://api.jolpi.ca/ergast/f1/2025/last/results.json returned 200. Drop-in Ergast-compatible replacement — race schedules, results, qualifying, sprint results, driver and constructor standings, lap times, pit stops, circuits, and full historical archive from 1950 to present.
- Docs: https://github.com/jolpica/jolpica-f1 and https://api.jolpi.ca/ergast/
- Auth: none currently | Limits: VERIFIED from the project's rate-limit docs: unauthenticated burst limit 4 requests/second, sustained 500 requests/hour. Token-based access is in development and the docs explicitly warn these limits WILL DECREASE as token access rolls out. History depth: 1950 to present, complete.
- Latency: hourly to daily post-session | Format: REST JSON (Ergast-compatible schema)
- Relevance: CORE for F1 contracts and the only free source with a complete 75-year archive for building driver/constructor priors. The Ergast-compatible schema means every F1 model written in the last decade works against it unchanged.

**CollegeFootballData (CFBD)** — CollegeFootballData.com `LIVE`

- NCAA football: games, drives, play-by-play, box scores, team and player season/advanced stats, SP+/Elo/FPI ratings, recruiting rankings, transfer portal, coaching records, venues, and — critically — betting lines with consensus and per-book spreads and totals. GraphQL available on Tier 3+.
- Docs: https://api.collegefootballdata.com/api/docs/ and https://collegefootballdata.com/
- Auth: free API key required (request at https://collegefootballdata.com/key) — I confirmed an unauthenticated call to /games returns HTTP 401, so the old keyless access is gone | Limits: VERIFIED from the api-tiers page: free tier is 1,000 API calls per month. Paid Patreon tiers: Academic 3,000, Tier 1 5,000, Tier 2 30,000, Tier 3 75,000, Tier 4 125,000, Tier 5 200,000, Tier 6 500,000 calls/month. No per-minute limit published — UNKNOWN. Exceeding the monthly cap temporarily disables the key until the next month. History depth: 2001+ for most endpoints, betting lines roughly 2013+.
- Latency: daily; lines update through the week | Format: REST JSON (+ GraphQL on Tier 3+)
- Relevance: CORE for NCAAF contracts and the only free source that bundles advanced team ratings WITH historical betting lines — that pairing is what lets you backtest a model against closing lines without buying odds history. 1,000 calls/month is tight; cache aggressively.

**API-Sports / API-Football** — API-Sports (api-sports.io) `LIVE`

- Multi-sport suite with separate endpoints per sport: football/soccer (1,100+ leagues), NBA, NFL/NCAA, MLB, NHL, rugby, handball, volleyball, baseball, basketball, formula-1. Football tier includes fixtures with events, lineups (confirmed XI), player and team statistics, standings, top scorers, transfers, INJURIES, predictions, and pre-match plus live ODDS.
- Docs: https://www.api-football.com/documentation-v3 (api-sports.io returned HTTP 403 to my datacenter IP — docs are browser-reachable, the API host itself is not IP-blocked in the same way)
- Auth: free API key (registration on api-sports.io dashboard, or via RapidAPI) | Limits: 100 requests per day on the free plan, resetting at 00:00 UTC with unused calls lost. Free plan includes all endpoint types (no feature paywall) including odds, injuries and lineups — the limit is volume only. Paid: Pro $19/mo for 7,500/day, Mega $39/mo for 150,000/day. Per-minute limit UNKNOWN. History depth on free plan is restricted (paid plans advertise 2010+); exact free depth UNKNOWN.
- Latency: realtime for live scores and odds (15s refresh on paid) | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: CORE by coverage, crippled by quota. It is the only free feed that carries injuries + confirmed lineups + odds together across 1,100 football leagues. But 100 calls/day prices out anything but a single league. Use it for confirmed-lineup snapshots ~1hr before kickoff, which is the highest-information moment in football markets.

**Open-Meteo** — Open-Meteo (open-source, ECMWF/GFS/ICON/HRRR blend) `LIVE`

- VERIFIED: forecast call for Kansas City coordinates returned 200. Hourly and 15-minutely forecasts for temperature, wind speed and direction, gusts, precipitation, snowfall, humidity, pressure and cloud cover at arbitrary lat/lon, plus a historical archive API back to 1940 (ERA5) for backtesting.
- Docs: https://open-meteo.com/en/docs
- Auth: none for non-commercial | Limits: Free tier is capped at 10,000 API calls per day, 5,000 per hour and 600 per minute, for non-commercial use, with no API key. Commercial use requires a paid plan. History depth: 1940+ via the archive API.
- Latency: hourly model updates; HRRR sub-hourly for US | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: CORE for weather-dependent contracts. Wind and precipitation at an outdoor NFL stadium or MLB park is a direct input to totals; pair the venue lat/lon from MLB StatsAPI or ESPN with this feed. The 1940+ archive lets you backtest weather effects on totals, which almost nobody does.

**CricketData.org (formerly CricAPI)** — CricketData.org `LIVE`

- VERIFIED: https://api.cricapi.com/v1/currentMatches returned 200. Live scores, ball-by-ball commentary, scorecards, series and match schedules, squads, player profiles and stats, and fantasy-points endpoints. Covers internationals (Test/ODI/T20I), IPL, BBL, PSL, The Hundred, county cricket and World Cups.
- Docs: https://cricketdata.org/ and https://cricapi.com/
- Auth: free API key (registration at https://cricketdata.org/signup.aspx) | Limits: 100 API hits per day on the lifetime-free tier, no expiry. Paid: $5.99/mo for 2,000/day, $12.99/mo for 10,000/day, $29.99/mo for 100,000/day, $64.99/mo unlimited. One source quoted 500/day — treat 100/day as the conservative figure until confirmed with your own key. History depth UNKNOWN.
- Latency: realtime (ball-by-ball on live matches) | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: CORE for cricket contracts — cricket is one of the largest global prediction-market categories and this is the best free feed. 100 hits/day means you can follow roughly one live match; cache the schedule endpoints and spend your quota on in-play.

- bootstrap-static returns every EPL player with position, team, price, form, points, plus chance_of_playing_this_round and chance_of_playing_next_round (0/25/50/75/100) and a news field carrying the injury description. - Auth: none for public endpoints | Limits: No key, no published quota — UNKNOWN. Undocumented and unsupported; the League has changed the schema between seasons without notice.

- Relevance: CORE for EPL availability markets. chance_of_playing_next_round is a NUMERIC availability probability published by the league itself — that is a directly usable prior for 'will player X start' contracts, and it is free. The closest free analogue to a bookmaker's own injury model for football.

**stats.nba.com (official NBA stats endpoints)** — NBA (undocumented) `LIVE`

- The full nba.com/stats backend — boxscoreadvancedv3, playbyplayv3, shotchartdetail, leaguedashplayerstats, hustle stats, tracking stats, lineups, and synergy play types. Richest basketball dataset that exists outside a paid contract.
- Docs: No official docs. The reference implementation is https://github.com/swar/nba_api (3,778 stars, pushed 2026-08-16) which documents every endpoint and parameter.

In practice aggressive IP-based throttling: the community consensus is roughly 1 request per 0.6-1.0 seconds from a residential IP, and DATACENTER IPs ARE BLOCKED OUTRIGHT. My probe from a server timed out with no response at all (curl exit code 000), and cdn.nba.com returned HTTP 403. History depth: 1996-97 onward for most endpoints, tracking data 2013-14+.
- Latency: sub-minute during games | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: CORE by data quality, but operationally hostile. If you can route through a residential proxy it is the best NBA source by a wide margin. From cloud infrastructure it does not work at all — plan for balldontlie or ESPN core as the fallback and treat this as a proxy-dependent enrichment path.

Complements api-web (which is game-centric) with league-wide leaderboards.
- Docs: https://github.com/Zmalski/NHL-API-Reference#stats-api
- Auth: none | Limits: No key, no published quota — UNKNOWN.
- Latency: daily (post-game aggregation) | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: USEFUL. Season-long aggregates for award markets (Hart, Vezina, Rocket Richard) and team-total futures. Not needed for single-game pricing where api-web is richer.

**balldontlie** — balldontlie.io `LIVE`

- NBA, NFL, MLB, NHL, EPL, WNBA, NCAAF, NCAAB. Teams, players, games, season averages, and on paid tiers live box scores, advanced stats, odds, player props and injuries. Separate sub-APIs at epl.balldontlie.io and fifa.balldontlie.io (World Cup).
- Docs: https://docs.balldontlie.io/
- Auth: free API key (registration) — it returned HTTP 401 without a key when I probed /v1/teams, confirming the key requirement changed from the old keyless era | Limits: CONFLICTING SOURCES — I could not fetch the authenticated docs page to resolve it. Published figures range from 5 requests/minute (free tier, NBA core endpoints only: teams, players, games) to 60 requests/minute. Treat the free limit as 5 req/min until you confirm against your own key. Injuries, odds, live box scores and advanced stats are explicitly paid-tier. History depth UNKNOWN.
- Latency: daily on free tier; live box scores are paid | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: USEFUL, downgraded from what its reputation suggests. It used to be the default free NBA API; in 2026 the free tier is basic NBA only, and everything a prediction market actually needs (injuries, odds, live) sits behind payment.

**football-data.org** — football-data.org (Daniel Freitag) `LIVE`

- European and international football: fixtures, results, league tables, squads, scorers, head-to-head. Free tier covers 12 competitions — Premier League, Championship, Bundesliga, Serie A, La Liga, Ligue 1, Eredivisie, Primeira Liga, Brazilian Série A, Champions League, European Championship and World Cup.
- Docs: https://www.football-data.org/documentation/quickstart
- Auth: free API key (email registration), sent as X-Auth-Token header | Limits: VERIFIED from the pricing page: 10 calls per minute on the free tier, 12 competitions. Free tier EXCLUDES live scores, lineups, substitutions, goal scorers, bookings/cards, squads, odds and advanced statistics — scores and schedules are delayed. History depth on free tier is not published (UNKNOWN); paid tiers advertise deeper archives.
- Latency: delayed (explicitly not live on free tier) — effectively hourly | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: USEFUL but weaker than its reputation. No lineups and no live data on the free tier removes exactly the two things that price football match markets. Good for settling completed results and for league-table/relegation futures.

**OpenLigaDB** — heise / community (Germany) `LIVE`

- VERIFIED: /getmatchdata/bl1/2025 returned 200. Bundesliga 1 and 2, DFB-Pokal, and a community-extended set including Champions League, Premier League and others. Match data, goals with scorer and minute, league tables, matchday schedules, team metadata. Fully crowd-maintained and open.
- Docs: https://api.openligadb.de/index.html (Swagger UI) — project page https://www.openligadb.de/
- Auth: none | Limits: No API key, no published rate limit — UNKNOWN. Community-funded and explicitly free for any use including commercial. History depth: Bundesliga back to 2002.
- Latency: minutely during matches (crowd-updated, so occasional lag) | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: USEFUL for German football contracts specifically. Genuinely unlimited and unauthenticated, which makes it the best free football source for high-frequency polling — but coverage outside the German pyramid is thin and crowd-quality.

**OpenF1** — OpenF1 open-source project `LIVE`

- VERIFIED: /v1/sessions?year=2025 and /v1/car_data?session_key=latest&driver_number=1 both returned 200. Real-time and historical F1 telemetry — car_data (speed, throttle, brake, DRS, gear, RPM at ~3.7Hz), location (x/y/z on track), intervals, laps, pit, position, stints, weather (air/track temp, humidity, rainfall, wind), team_radio, and race_control messages (flags, safety cars, penalties).
- Docs: https://openf1.org/
- Auth: none for historical; real-time streaming requires a paid account | Limits: Historical data is free with no key and no documented quota — UNKNOWN. Real-time/live access moved behind a paid tier. History depth: 2023 season onward.
- Latency: realtime (paid) / post-session for free historical | Format: REST JSON + MQTT streaming on paid
- Relevance: USEFUL. race_control messages (safety car, red flag, penalty) are what actually resolve in-race F1 markets, and weather-at-circuit prices wet-race contracts. Free tier being historical-only limits live pricing use.

**openfootball/football.json** — openfootball (public domain project) `LIVE`

- VERIFIED: raw 2024-25/en.1.json returned 200, repo pushed 2026-09-19 (actively maintained). Plain JSON fixtures, results and scores for Premier League, Bundesliga, La Liga, Serie A, Ligue 1, MLS, World Cup and more. Companion repo openfootball/worldcup (703 stars) has complete World Cup history.
- Docs: https://github.com/openfootball/football.json
- Auth: none | Limits: No limits — static files served from GitHub raw / jsDelivr. Public domain licence, commercial use permitted. History depth varies by league, typically 2010-11 season onward.
- Latency: daily to weekly (community-committed) | Format: JSON bulk (git repo)
- Relevance: USEFUL. Public domain licence is the differentiator — no attribution or non-commercial restriction, unlike StatsBomb. Good for backfilling results and settling historical football contracts without licence risk.

**henrygd/ncaa-api** — Open-source (henrygd), self-hostable `LIVE`

- VERIFIED: https://ncaa-api.henrygd.me/scoreboard/football/fbs/2025/03/all-conf returned 200. Wraps NCAA.com's own data into a clean REST API across ALL NCAA sports and all three divisions — scoreboards, game details, box scores, play-by-play, rankings, standings and statistics for football, basketball (M/W), baseball, softball, hockey, lacrosse, soccer, volleyball and more.
- Docs: https://github.com/henrygd/ncaa-api (265 stars, pushed 2026-09-17)
- Auth: none on the public instance; self-hosted instances can set a header key | Limits: Public instance is rate-limited to 5 requests per minute per IP (the README directs heavy users to self-host via the published Docker image, which removes the limit). History depth depends on NCAA.com's own archive, generally recent seasons only.
- Latency: sub-minute during games | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: USEFUL, and the only realistic free path to NCAA sports beyond football and basketball. Self-hosting the Docker image converts it from a 5 req/min toy into an unmetered feed, which is the single highest-leverage move in this list for college markets.

**Understat** — Understat (scrape-only) `LIVE`

- VERIFIED: https://understat.com/league/EPL returned 200 and the page embeds its data as JSON.parse() blobs in inline script tags. Shot-level xG data with per-shot coordinates, xA, xGChain and xGBuildup for EPL, La Liga, Bundesliga, Serie A, Ligue 1 and RFPL, from the 2014-15 season.
- Docs: No API and no docs. Community wrappers: https://github.com/amosbastian/understat (Python, async)
- Auth: none | Limits: No API, therefore no documented limit — UNKNOWN. Scraping etiquette applies; the data is embedded in HTML so every request is a full page load. History depth: 2014-15 onward for six leagues.
- Latency: daily (updated post-matchday) | Format: scrape-only (JSON embedded in HTML script tags)
- Relevance: USEFUL for football model inputs. xG is the standard predictor for football match markets and this is the only free source of shot-level xG with this league breadth. SCRAPE-FRAGILE: one template change breaks your parser, and there is no contract or status page.

**NASCAR public cacher feeds (cf.nascar.com)** — NASCAR (undocumented CDN) `LIVE`

- VERIFIED: https://cf.nascar.com/cacher/2025/1/schedule-feed.json returned 200 with real data — start_time, end_time, event_name ('Practice'), race_id 5585, track_id 84, track_name 'Phoenix Raceway', race_name 'NASCAR Cup Series Championship', series_id 1, run_type. Sibling feeds cover live timing/scoring, lap-by-lap results, driver points, and race results across Cup (series_id 1), Xfinity (2) and Truck (3).
- Docs: No official docs. Note that www.nascar.com/cacher/... returns HTTP 403 from a server while cf.nascar.com/cacher/... returns 200 — use the cf host.
- Auth: none | Limits: No key, no published quota — UNKNOWN. Entirely undocumented and unsupported.
- Latency: realtime during races (live timing/scoring feed updates per lap) | Format: REST JSON (static CDN objects)
- Relevance: USEFUL and effectively the only free NASCAR source. Live lap-by-lap timing is what prices in-race NASCAR markets; nothing else free offers it.

**NWS / weather.gov API** — US National Weather Service (NOAA) `LIVE`

- VERIFIED: /points/39.0997,-94.5786 returned 200. Official US forecasts, hourly gridpoint data, active alerts and warnings, and station observations. Gives authoritative US government forecasts for any US venue.
- Docs: https://www.weather.gov/documentation/services-web-api
- Auth: none (a descriptive User-Agent header is requested) | Limits: No API key. NWS does not publish a hard numeric limit; the documented guidance is a generous but unspecified rate with 429 responses on abuse — exact number UNKNOWN. US coverage only. Forecast horizon 7 days.
- Latency: hourly | Format: REST JSON (GeoJSON)
- Relevance: USEFUL. Redundancy for Open-Meteo on US venues and the authoritative source if a contract's resolution criteria reference official NWS readings — which weather-linked contracts often do.

**Wikipedia / Wikimedia REST API** — Wikimedia Foundation `LIVE`

- VERIFIED: both /api/rest_v1/page/summary/2026_FIFA_World_Cup and the action API for 2026 Winter Olympics returned 200. Structured and semi-structured data on tournaments, medal tables, championship results, rosters, records and honours across every sport, with full revision history and a recent-changes stream.
- Docs: https://www.mediawiki.org/wiki/API:REST_API and https://api.wikimedia.org/wiki/Main_Page
- Auth: none (optional free account raises limits) | Limits: Anonymous access to api.wikimedia.org is 500 requests per hour; authenticated with a free account it is 5,000 requests per hour. The older en.wikipedia.org/w/api.php has no hard published cap but requests a descriptive User-Agent and serial requests. History: complete revision history.
- Latency: minutely (recent-changes stream is near-realtime) | Format: REST JSON + EventStreams SSE
- Relevance: USEFUL and systematically underrated. For Olympics medal-count contracts, award winners, and 'first team to win X' style markets, Wikipedia is often the DE FACTO RESOLUTION SOURCE — many prediction-market contracts name it in their resolution criteria. The EventStreams feed lets you detect the edit that settles a contract within seconds.

**PandaScore (esports)** — PandaScore `LIVE`

- Esports across CS2, League of Legends, Dota 2, Valorant, Overwatch, Rocket League, CoD and more — tournaments, matches, live match state, team and player stats, and betting odds.
- Docs: https://developers.pandascore.co/docs
- Auth: API token required — I confirmed /tournaments returns HTTP 401 without one | Limits: A free developer tier exists with historical/reference data access; live match data and odds are paid. Exact free call limits are not published on the public docs — UNKNOWN. History depth UNKNOWN.
- Latency: realtime on paid tiers | Format: REST JSON + webhooks
- Relevance: USEFUL for esports contracts, which are a growing prediction-market category with poor free coverage. The free tier's reference-only nature limits it to entity mapping and historical backtesting.

#### NICHE

**TheSportsDB** — TheSportsDB (community/Patreon funded) `LIVE`

- Broadest league coverage of any free API — hundreds of leagues across football, basketball, baseball, hockey, soccer, rugby, cricket, motorsport, MMA, esports and more. Events, schedules, results, teams, players, venues, league tables, plus a large media/artwork library.
- Docs: https://www.thesportsdb.com/documentation
- Auth: free test key '3' or '123' embedded in the v1 URL path; premium requires a Patreon key | Limits: VERIFIED from the docs page: free tier is 30 requests per minute (429 on exceed, one minute cooldown). Free results are severely truncated — searches capped at 1 result, list endpoints capped at 2-50 items depending on call. V1 is the free version; V2 is premium-only and I confirmed https://www.thesportsdb.com/api/v2/json/all/leagues returns HTTP 400 without a premium key. Premium is $9/month for 100 req/min plus livescores. History depth varies by league, generally 2010+.
- Latency: hourly to daily on free; livescores are premium-only | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: NICHE for pricing, CORE for coverage discovery. The 1-result search cap makes it useless as a pricing feed, but it is the best free way to enumerate which leagues, teams and venues exist so you can build your entity map. Use it to bootstrap identifiers, not to price contracts.

**StatsBomb Open Data (now hudl/open-data)** — Hudl / StatsBomb `LIVE`

- VERIFIED: the repo redirects from statsbomb/open-data to hudl/open-data (3,633 stars, pushed 2026-09-07) and raw competitions.json returns 200. Free event-level football data with StatsBomb's full 360 spec where available — every pass, shot, carry, pressure with x/y coordinates, xG, shot freeze-frames, and player positions. Covers multiple World Cups, Women's World Cups, FA WSL, La Liga (full Messi career at Barcelona), Champions League finals, Euro 2020/2024, and NWSL.
- Docs: https://github.com/hudl/open-data (spec in /doc)
- Auth: none | Limits: Unlimited bulk download from GitHub. Licence is non-commercial and requires attribution — a real constraint if your prediction-market product is commercial. History depth: selected competitions only, not continuous league coverage.
- Latency: static / occasional releases (not a live feed) | Format: JSON bulk (git repo)
- Relevance: NICHE for live pricing, CORE for model training. You cannot price tomorrow's match with it, but it is the only free source of true event-level football data to fit an xG or possession-value model that you then apply to live feeds.

**Retrosheet (chadwickbureau mirror)** — Retrosheet / Chadwick Bureau `LIVE`

- VERIFIED: repo chadwickbureau/retrosheet live, 143 stars, pushed 2026-08-13. Complete play-by-play for essentially every MLB game since 1914, game logs back to 1871, plus rosters, schedules, ejections, park factors, and umpire assignments. The Chadwick mirror ships it as clean CSV rather than the original fixed-width event files.
- Docs: https://www.retrosheet.org/ and https://github.com/chadwickbureau/retrosheet
- Auth: none | Limits: Unlimited bulk download. Licence requires the standard Retrosheet attribution notice. History depth: game logs 1871+, full play-by-play 1914+ (near-complete 1950+).
- Latency: annual (season files released after each season ends) | Format: CSV bulk (git repo)
- Relevance: NICHE for live pricing, CORE for priors. A century of umpire assignments and park-level outcomes is the reference dataset for MLB base rates. Nothing else free goes back this far.

**Squiggle API (AFL)** — Squiggle (Max Barry) `LIVE`

- VERIFIED: https://api.squiggle.com.au/?q=games;year=2025 returned 200. Australian Football League fixtures, results, ladder, and — unusually — the published tips and win probabilities from every public AFL prediction model, plus each model's historical accuracy and margin error. Effectively a free model-ensemble feed.
- Docs: https://api.squiggle.com.au/ (docs at the root URL)
- Auth: none (a User-Agent identifying your app and contact is required by the terms) | Limits: No key. The terms request you cache results and avoid hammering; no numeric limit published — UNKNOWN. History depth: 1897+ for results, model tips from 2017.
- Latency: daily; tips published before each round | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: NICHE by sport, but structurally interesting: it is the only free feed that ships a MODEL ENSEMBLE with tracked historical error per model. That is exactly the 'ensemble forecast, model spread, historical error' shape a research panel wants — worth studying as a template even outside AFL.

**Scorebat Video API** — Scorebat `LIVE`

- VERIFIED: https://www.scorebat.com/video-api/v3/ returned 200. Football match highlights and goal videos with match metadata, competition, teams and dates across major European leagues.
- Docs: https://www.scorebat.com/video-api/
- Auth: none for the free v3 feed; a token unlocks the full feed | Limits: Free feed is limited to a subset of matches and competitions; no numeric call limit published — UNKNOWN. Free tier is non-commercial with an attribution/embed requirement.
- Latency: minutely after goals | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: NICHE. Video metadata does not price contracts, but goal timestamps arrive fast and can serve as a low-latency corroboration signal that a goal occurred before slower score feeds update.

**Sportmonks** — Sportmonks (Netherlands) `LIVE`

- Football, cricket, Formula 1. Football coverage includes fixtures, livescores, lineups, events, statistics, standings, topscorers, predictions and odds from 100+ bookmakers.

- Auth: free API token required — I confirmed an unauthenticated call to /v3/football/leagues returns HTTP 401 | Limits: The free plan covers only the Danish Superliga and Scottish Premiership, at 3,000 API calls per day with a 180 calls/hour entity limit. Odds, predictions and most advanced features are NOT in the free plan. History depth on free plan UNKNOWN.
- Latency: realtime on paid; free plan livescores limited | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: NICHE. The two-league free restriction makes it useless for prediction-market breadth. Listed so you do not spend a day integrating it expecting Premier League coverage.

#### Repos

- `swar/nba_api` — Python client documenting and wrapping every stats.nba.com endpoint. 3,778 stars, pushed 2026-08-16. · The only complete documentation of the NBA's undocumented API — endpoint list, every parameter, and the exact header set required to avoid a block. Even if you write your own client, this repo is the spec.
- `nflverse/nflverse-data` — Automated NFL data repository publishing 25 dataset families as GitHub Release assets. 398 stars, pushed 2026-09-16. · Verified release tags include injuries, officials, depth_charts, pbp, nextgen_stats and snap_counts — the injury and referee data that prices NFL markets, as stable bulk files rather than a revocable endpoint.
- `nflverse/nflfastR` — R package computing EPA, WPA, CPOE and win probability from NFL play-by-play. 545 stars, pushed 2026-09-19. · The reference implementation of NFL win-probability models. Its WP model is a free, well-validated baseline to price in-game NFL contracts against.
- `nflverse/nfl_data_py` — Python port of nflreadr for pulling nflverse datasets. 439 stars. · Python path into all nflverse bulk data without writing your own GitHub Release asset resolver.
- `Zmalski/NHL-API-Reference` — Unofficial but comprehensive documentation of both api-web.nhle.com and api.nhle.com/stats/rest. 601 stars. · The NHL publishes no documentation at all. This is the de-facto spec for both hosts and the reason NHL integration is tractable.
- `dfleis/nhl-api-docs` — Automated parsing and documentation of 500+ NHL API endpoints. 10 stars. · Machine-generated and auto-refreshed, so it catches endpoint changes that the hand-written reference misses.
- `hudl/open-data` — StatsBomb's free event-level football data, now under the Hudl org. 3,633 stars, pushed 2026-09-07. · IMPORTANT: the repo moved from statsbomb/open-data to hudl/open-data. Every tutorial and hardcoded URL still points at the old path. Event-level data with shot freeze-frames for training xG and possession-value models.
- `theOehrly/Fast-F1` — Python package for F1 timing, telemetry and session data with local caching. 5,382 stars, pushed 2026-08-28. · Highest-starred repo in this whole domain. Handles F1's live timing protocol and telemetry alignment, which is genuinely hard to implement from scratch.
- `jolpica/jolpica-f1` — The open-source Ergast successor, both the hosted API and its backend. 910 stars, pushed 2026-09-14. · Ergast is dead. This is the migration target, and the repo documents the rate limits (4 req/s burst, 500 req/hr sustained) that the API itself does not advertise.
- `chadwickbureau/retrosheet` — Retrosheet's century of MLB play-by-play republished as clean CSV. 143 stars, pushed 2026-08-13. · Saves you from parsing Retrosheet's original fixed-width event-file format, which is a multi-day job. Includes umpire assignments back decades.
- `sportsdataverse/sportsdataverse-py` — Unified Python access to NFL, NBA, NHL, MLB, NCAA football and NCAA basketball data. 118 stars, pushed 2026-09-19. · One import surface across six leagues. The fastest way to prototype a multi-sport panel before committing to per-league integrations.
- `sportsdataverse/hoopR` — R package for NBA and men's college basketball play-by-play and box scores. 145 stars. · Mirrors nflfastR's approach for basketball, including bulk PBP releases that sidestep the stats.nba.com datacenter block entirely.
- `sportsdataverse/cfbfastR` — R package for college football PBP with EPA/WPA. 111 stars, pushed 2026-09-19. · Pairs with CFBD's 1,000-call/month limit — pull bulk PBP from here and spend your scarce CFBD calls on betting lines.
- `henrygd/ncaa-api` — Self-hostable REST wrapper over NCAA.com covering all NCAA sports and divisions. 265 stars, pushed 2026-09-17. · Self-hosting the published Docker image removes the 5 req/min public-instance limit. Highest-leverage single move for college-sports coverage.
- `openfootball/football.json` — Public domain football fixtures and results in plain JSON. 1,023 stars, pushed 2026-09-19. · Public domain licence, no attribution or non-commercial clause — unlike StatsBomb and Understat. The only football dataset here with zero licence risk for a commercial product.
- `openfootball/worldcup` — Complete World Cup history in JSON, including 2026. 703 stars, pushed 2026-08-22. · World Cup 2026 is the largest prediction-market football event in the cycle; this is free, public domain structured data for it.
- `vaastav/Fantasy-Premier-League` — Historical FPL data scraped season by season, plus documentation of the undocumented FPL API. 1,806 stars, pushed 2026-08-28. · Documents the chance_of_playing_next_round field — a league-published numeric availability probability. Also ships the historical archive so you can backtest how well that field predicts actual starts.
- `jaebradley/basketball_reference_web_scraper` — Python scraper for Basketball Reference. 556 stars, pushed 2026-09-20. · Actively maintained fallback for NBA historical data when stats.nba.com blocks your IP. Note Sports Reference sites are increasingly Cloudflare-protected — treat as scrape-fragile.
- `Aneeshers/tennis-sackmann-archive` — Archival mirror of Jeff Sackmann's ATP, WTA and Grand Slam point-by-point datasets, snapshotted June 2026. 11 stars. · CRITICAL: the original JeffSackmann/tennis_atp and tennis_wta repos now return 404. This mirror (and its Hugging Face copy) is how you still get the canonical tennis match archive. CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, so non-commercial only.
- `JeffSackmann/tennis_MatchChartingProject` — Crowd-sourced point-by-point charting for pro tennis matches. 431 stars, pushed 2026-09-18 — still live. · The one Sackmann tennis repo that survived. Point-level data for serve/return modelling, which is the basis of almost every tennis match-winner model.
- `Tennismylife/TML-Database` — Live-updated ATP tournament and match database. 83 stars, pushed 2026-01-27. · Independent tennis archive, useful as a second source now that the main Sackmann repos are gone.
- `amosbastian/understat` — Async Python wrapper that parses Understat's embedded JSON blobs. · Understat has no API — the data is inside JSON.parse() calls in the HTML. This handles the extraction so you do not maintain a regex parser.
- `dcaribou/transfermarkt-datasets` — Extracted, cleaned and published Transfermarkt data — players, clubs, valuations, appearances, transfers. 507 stars, pushed 2026-09-05. · Player market valuations and transfer history, which price transfer and manager-move contracts. Transfermarkt itself is hostile to scraping; this is the maintained extraction.
- `cwendt94/espn-api` — Python client for ESPN fantasy football and basketball APIs. 974 stars, pushed 2026-09-18. · Documents ESPN's auth flow and endpoint structure, which transfers to the public ESPN core API endpoints.
- `droher/boxball` — Retrosheet, Lahman, Chadwick and Baseball Databank packaged into ready-to-query Postgres, Parquet, CSV and Docker images. 132 stars, pushed 2026-05-20. · IMPORTANT: chadwickbureau/baseballdatabank now returns 404. Boxball is the maintained path to the Lahman/Databank tables, and it ships them pre-joined with Retrosheet so you skip the ETL entirely.
- `roclark/sportsipy` — Free Python sports API across NFL, NBA, MLB, NHL, NCAAF and NCAAB. 571 stars, last pushed 2025-01-31. · Broad multi-sport surface, but note the repo has not been touched in ~20 months and it scrapes Sports Reference, which has added bot protection. Use with low expectations — listed for completeness.
- `pseudo-r/Public-NHL-API` — Documentation of undocumented NHL and ESPN endpoints with live curl examples. · One of the few places that documents the ESPN hidden endpoints alongside working curl invocations, including which hosts respond from a server.

### Health, Disease & Medicine (surveillance, regulatory, clinical trials, pharma supply)

#### CORE

**openFDA — Drugs@FDA (drug/drugsfda)** — US Food and Drug Administration `LIVE`

- Every FDA-approved drug application since 1939: application number (NDA/BLA/ANDA), sponsor, submission type (ORIG-1, SUPPL-n), submission_status (AP/TA), submission_status_date, review priority (PRIORITY/STANDARD), chemical type, products, dosage forms, marketing status. Confirmed 29,335 application records live.
- Docs: https://open.fda.gov/apis/drug/drugsfda/
- Auth: none (optional free API key raises quota) | Limits: Without key: 240 requests/minute per IP AND 1,000 requests/day per IP. With free key: 240 requests/minute per key AND 120,000 requests/day per key. Max limit=1000 records per call; skip capped at 25,000 (use _sort+search paging or bulk download beyond that). History: approvals back to 1939.
- Latency: daily (verified meta.last_updated = 2026-09-16) | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: THE settlement source for 'Will FDA approve drug X by date Y?' contracts. submission_status flipping to 'AP' with a submission_status_date is the machine-readable approval event. Priority-review flag lets you shorten the expected review clock (6mo vs 10mo). Supplements (SUPPL) settle label-expansion contracts.

**openFDA — Drug Shortages (drug/shortages)** — US Food and Drug Administration `LIVE`

- FDA Drug Shortage Database as JSON: generic name, company, dosage form, presentation, shortage status (Current/Resolved), initial posting date, change date, reason for shortage, estimated recovery, therapeutic category, related_info. 1,603 total records; 1,153 currently in 'Current' status at time of check.
- Docs: https://open.fda.gov/apis/drug/drugshortages/
- Auth: none (optional free API key) | Limits: Same as all openFDA: 240/min + 1,000/day per IP unkeyed; 240/min + 120,000/day per free key. History: 2012 onwards. Max limit=100 per call on this endpoint (lower than other openFDA endpoints).
- Latency: daily (verified meta.last_updated = 2026-09-18) | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: Prices 'Will drug X be in shortage on date Y?' and IV-fluid / GLP-1 / ADHD-stimulant supply contracts. The status transition Current->Resolved with a dated change is a clean binary settlement. Also a leading indicator for hospital-capacity and manufacturer-guidance markets.

**openFDA — Drug Recall Enforcement (drug/enforcement)** — US Food and Drug Administration `LIVE`

- Drug recall enforcement reports: recall_number, classification (Class I/II/III), status (Ongoing/Completed/Terminated), reason_for_recall, product_description, recalling_firm, recall_initiation_date, report_date, distribution_pattern, quantity, voluntary_mandated. 17,965 records.
- Docs: https://open.fda.gov/apis/drug/enforcement/
- Auth: none (optional free API key) | Limits: 240/min + 1,000/day per IP unkeyed; 240/min + 120,000/day per free key. History: 2004 onwards.
- Latency: weekly-to-daily (verified meta.last_updated = 2026-09-09) | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: Settles 'Will product X be recalled?' and Class-I-recall contracts. Recall classification is a hard regulatory label, not a judgement call, so it settles unambiguously. Paired with device/enforcement it covers most pharma safety-event markets.

**openFDA — Device 510(k) Clearances and PMA Approvals** — US Food and Drug Administration `LIVE`

- device/510k: premarket notification clearances with k_number, applicant, decision_date, decision_code (SESE=substantially equivalent), product_code, advisory_committee, clearance_type. device/pma: Class III premarket approvals with pma_number, supplement_number, decision_date, decision_code, advisory_committee, expedited_review_flag. device/classification gives 7,093 product-code-to-class mappings.
- Docs: https://open.fda.gov/apis/device/510k/
- Auth: none (optional free API key) | Limits: 240/min + 1,000/day per IP unkeyed; 240/min + 120,000/day per free key. History: 510(k) back to 1976; PMA back to 1976.
- Latency: weekly (verified 510k meta.last_updated = 2026-09-07) | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: Settles medical-device approval contracts (CGM systems, AI diagnostics, neuromodulation, surgical robots). decision_date + decision_code is the settlement pair. expedited_review_flag on PMA is a timing signal. Device markets are thinner than drug markets, so a live feed is more of an edge here.

**ClinicalTrials.gov API v2** — US National Library of Medicine / NIH `LIVE`

- 603,494 registered studies. Full protocol + results modules: NCT ID, phase, status (Recruiting/Active/Completed/Terminated/Suspended), sponsor, enrollment (actual vs estimated), primary completion date (actual vs anticipated), study start, primary/secondary outcome measures, results posting, adverse event tables, locations. Also /studies/{nctId}, /stats, /studies/metadata field enumerations.
- Docs: https://clinicaltrials.gov/data-api/api
- Auth: none | Limits: UNKNOWN — no numeric rate limit is published in the official API docs. Community implementations converge on ~50 requests/minute per IP and recommend 150ms–1.5s spacing, but this is observed behaviour, not a documented quota. Paging: pageSize max 1000, cursor-based via nextPageToken. History: registrations from 1999 onward, full version history per study.
- Latency: daily (verified apiVersion 2.0.5, dataTimestamp = 2026-09-18T09:00:04) | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: CORE for trial-readout contracts. Primary completion date (anticipated -> actual) is the single best predictor of a topline-data announcement. Status flipping to Terminated/Suspended settles trial-failure markets. Slippage of anticipated PCD is a quantifiable, tradeable signal — pdufa.bio actually surfaces exactly this as an nct_id.slip field.

**pdufa.bio Catalyst API (PDUFA dates, AdComms, readouts)** — pdufa.bio (independent) `LIVE`

- Structured FDA catalyst calendar. Endpoints verified live: /api/v1/pdufa, /api/v1/events, /api/v1/adcomm, /api/v1/readouts, /api/v1/conferences, /api/v1/health, /api/v1/usage, /api/v1/export, /api/v1/calendar.ics, /api/v1/runup. Fields: id, ticker, company, date, date_precision, name, type, therapeutic_area, market_cap_tier, status (Pending/Decided), indication, url, updated_at, and a joined nct_id object {nct, status, ongoing, pcd, pcd_type, slip}. 86 PDUFA rows at time of check.
- Docs: https://www.pdufa.bio/developers
- Auth: none for anonymous tier; optional free API key via x-api-key header for the higher free tier | Limits: Anonymous: 1,000 requests/day with 10/min burst — CONFIRMED from live response header x-ratelimit-limit: 1000. Free keyed tier: 10,000 requests/month, 30/min burst. Paid: Pro $10/mo (100,000/mo, 120/min) adds run-up price series, bulk export, .ics calendar and webhooks; Quant $149/mo (2,000,000/mo). License requires attribution + link-back.
- Latency: daily (meta.as_of = 2026-09-20, same day as check) | Format: REST JSON (+ CSV via format=csv, iCal via calendar.ics on paid)
- Relevance: This is the specific thing the task asked for and the hardest to get free: a machine-readable PDUFA target-action-date calendar. FDA does not publish one. Everything else (MarketBeat, BiopharmCatalyst, RTTNews, BPIQ) is HTML-only or paywalled. The adcomm endpoint prices advisory-committee-vote contracts, which often trade separately from the approval itself. Caveat: independent aggregator, not an authoritative source — settle on openFDA drugsfda, use this for the forward calendar.

**WHO Disease Outbreak News (DON) API** — World Health Organization `LIVE`

- OData feed of every WHO Disease Outbreak News item. 3,196 items confirmed, latest 2026-09-10 ('Ebola disease caused by Bundibugyo virus – Democratic Republic of the Congo'). Fields include Id, Title, UrlName, PublicationDate, PublicationDateAndTime, LastModified, DateCreated, plus the full DON body. Supports $orderby, $top, $skip, $count, $filter.
- Docs: https://www.who.int/emergencies/disease-outbreak-news
- Auth: none | Limits: UNKNOWN — no published quota, no rate-limit headers returned. Full archive is reachable via $skip paging.
- Latency: per-event, typically within days of WHO verification (event-driven, not scheduled) | Format: REST JSON (OData v4)
- Relevance: CORE for 'Will WHO declare X?' and outbreak-existence contracts. A DON publication is the canonical, citable, timestamped WHO acknowledgement of an outbreak — exactly what a contract can settle on. Pair with the WHO news RSS (verified live) to catch PHEIC/IHR Emergency Committee declarations, which DON alone does not always carry.

**CDC Open Data (data.cdc.gov Socrata SODA v2/v3)** — US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention `LIVE`

- ~10,000 datasets, each a queryable SoQL endpoint at /resource/{id}.json. The market-relevant ones verified live: x9gk-5huc (NNDSS weekly notifiable disease tables, confirmed at 2026 week 36), ua7e-t2fy + rhwp-grxi + vdzy-6i9v (NHSN weekly hospital respiratory data, confirmed week ending 2026-09-12), j9g8-acpt / ymmh-divb / akvg-8vrb / 2ew6-ywp6 (wastewater: SARS-CoV-2, influenza A, measles, NWSS metrics — all updated 2026-09-18), f3zz-zga5 (ARI activity level by state), 7ce8-bpr6 (respiratory illness ED/inpatient/outpatient visits), 29hc-w46k (RSV-NET), ijqb-a7ye (kindergarten vaccination coverage + exemptions), vh55-3he6 / aetd-68ew / h7pm-wmjc (flu, adult, pregnancy vaccination coverage), hc4f-j6nb / ynw2-4viq (provisional COVID/flu/pneumonia death counts), xkb8-kh2a / 8hzs-zshh (provisional drug overdose deaths), jbhn-e8xn (BEAM enteric pathogen/AMR dashboard). Full SoQL: $where, $group, $order, $select, $limit, $offset.
- Docs: https://dev.socrata.com/consumers/getting-started.html
- Auth: none required; free app token (X-App-Token header) recommended | Limits: UNKNOWN — Socrata explicitly declines to publish numbers. Documented behaviour only: without an app token you draw from a shared per-IP pool with a 'much lower throttling limit'; with a free app token 'we do not throttle API requests that are using an application token, unless those requests are determined to be abusive or malicious.' Default $limit is 1000, max 50,000 per call via $limit with $offset paging. History depth varies per dataset (NNDSS back to 2014+, wastewater from 2020).
- Latency: daily to weekly depending on dataset (wastewater and ARI refreshed 2026-09-18; NHSN weekly) | Format: REST JSON / CSV / GeoJSON (SODA)
- Relevance: The single widest CORE surface for US health contracts. Prices measles/pertussis/dengue case-count markets (NNDSS), hospital-strain markets (NHSN), 'will wastewater exceed X' markets, vaccination-rate and exemption-rate markets, and provisional mortality markets. Always get an app token — the unkeyed pool throttles hard under any real polling load.

**CDC NWSS Wastewater Surveillance** — CDC National Wastewater Surveillance System (via data.cdc.gov) `LIVE`

- Site-level and jurisdiction-level wastewater viral concentrations. Verified live datasets: 2ew6-ywp6 (NWSS public SARS-CoV-2 metrics — wwtp_id, jurisdiction, sample location, percentile, ptc_15d, detect_prop_15d), j9g8-acpt (SARS-CoV-2 activity level), ymmh-divb (influenza A), akvg-8vrb (measles). All four returned 2026 data.
- Docs: https://www.cdc.gov/nwss/rv/COVID19-nationaltrend.html
- Auth: none (free Socrata app token recommended) | Limits: Same as data.cdc.gov Socrata — exact numbers UNKNOWN; unkeyed shared-IP throttle, effectively unthrottled with a free app token. History: SARS-CoV-2 from 2020; influenza A and measles panels added later (shorter history).
- Latency: weekly, published ~2 days after sample week (verified updatedAt 2026-09-18) | Format: REST JSON / CSV (Socrata)
- Relevance: Wastewater is the earliest quantitative leading indicator of a respiratory or measles wave — typically 1–2 weeks ahead of reported cases and 2–3 weeks ahead of hospitalizations. For case-count and hospitalization-threshold contracts this is where the edge actually lives, because the market usually anchors on the lagging clinical numbers.

**Delphi Epidata API (FluView, COVIDcast, and ~20 signal sources)** — Carnegie Mellon University Delphi Group `LIVE`

- Unified epidemiological API. /fluview returns ILINet with num_ili, num_patients, num_providers, wili, ili, by region and epiweek, WITH issue/lag fields so you can reconstruct exactly what was known on any past date. /covidcast exposes ~20 signal sources (Change Healthcare claims, Quidel test positivity, Google symptom search, HHS hospitalization, NCHS mortality, Doctor visits) at state and county level. Also /flusurv, /gft, /nowcast, /delphi. Verified: fluview epiweek 202540 returned with release_date 2026-09-18.
- Docs: https://cmu-delphi.github.io/delphi-epidata/
- Auth: none for anonymous; free API key via registration form for unlimited | Limits: Anonymous: 60 requests/hour, public datasets only, max two parameters with multiple selections. Registered free key: documented as 'no rate limit' and 'no limit on multiple selections' — exact ceiling not stated. Registration needs only an email. History: ILINet back to 1997; COVIDcast signals from 2020.
- Latency: weekly for ILINet (Friday release); daily for several COVIDcast signals | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: The ONLY free source that gives you vintaged/as-of-date epidemiological data (the issue+lag fields). That is decisive for prediction markets: CDC revises ILINet retroactively, so backtesting a flu-season model against final data overstates your skill badly. Delphi lets you replay what was actually knowable. Also the cleanest programmatic path to FluView ILINet, which CDC's own site serves only as a download widget.

**ECDC ERVISS — European Respiratory Virus Surveillance Summary** — European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control + WHO/Europe (GitHub-distributed) `LIVE`

- Weekly EU/EEA respiratory virus data as flat CSVs, updated in the repo. Verified live files: data/nonSentinelTestsDetections.csv (7.9MB), data/sentinelTestsDetectionsPositivity.csv (4.1MB), data/ILIARIRates.csv (2.5MB), data/nonSentinelSeverity.csv (4.4MB). Columns: surveytype, countryname, yearweek, pathogen, pathogentype, pathogensubtype, indicator, age, value. Confirmed current through 2026-W37; repo last commit 2026-09-18T13:41:23Z.
- Docs: https://github.com/EU-ECDC/Respiratory_viruses_weekly_data
- Auth: none | Limits: None beyond GitHub raw-content fair use (raw.githubusercontent.com is unauthenticated and effectively unlimited for this volume; the GitHub REST API itself is 60 req/hr unauthenticated, 5,000/hr with a free token — use raw, not the API). History: 2014-W40 onward for most series.
- Latency: weekly (published Fridays) | Format: CSV bulk over HTTPS (GitHub raw)
- Relevance: CORE for any European flu/RSV/COVID contract. ECDC's own Surveillance Atlas is an ASP.NET interactive with no API — this repo is the machine-readable escape hatch and it is officially maintained by ECDC. Country-level positivity and ILI/ARI rates settle European wave-timing and peak-week markets.

**WHO xMart Public OData — FluMart/FluNet, MPX, WIISE immunization** — World Health Organization `LIVE`

- Several public data marts at xmart-api-public.who.int, each an OData endpoint. FLUMART: 22 entity sets including VIW_FNT (FluNet virological surveillance — WHOREGION, COUNTRY_CODE, ISO_WEEKSTARTDATE, SPEC_PROCESSED_NB, AH1N12009, AH3, AH5, AH7N9, INF_A, INF_B breakdowns), VIW_FID_EPI (FluID epidemiological), plus reference tables. MPX: V_MPX_VALIDATED_DAILY (COUNTRY, DATE, ISO3, WHO_REGION, TOTAL_CONF_CASES, NEW_CONF_CASES, TOTAL_CONF_DEATHS) — confirmed current to 2026-08-19. WIISE: 163 tables covering immunization coverage (AD_COVERAGES, WUENIC), AEFI, vaccine introductions, SIA campaigns, outbreaks, measles/rubella susceptibility. Marts GHO, DEX_CMS, POLIO, NCD, EMERGENCY also respond 200 (POLIO and EMERGENCY returned empty entity-set lists).
- Docs: https://www.who.int/tools/flunet
- Auth: none | Limits: UNKNOWN — no published quota, no rate-limit headers. Full OData paging via $top/$skip. History: FluNet from 1995ish (sample row returned 2017); MPX from 2022-05; WIISE immunization from 1980.
- Latency: weekly for FluNet; weekly-to-monthly for MPX; annual for WUENIC coverage | Format: REST JSON / CSV (OData v4, $format=csv supported)
- Relevance: FluNet is the global settlement source for influenza subtype-dominance contracts ('will H3N2 be the dominant subtype this season?') and for H5N1/H7N9 human-case-count markets — those subtype columns are exactly the fields. MPX prices mpox outbreak markets. WIISE prices national vaccination-coverage contracts. This whole surface is almost undocumented publicly, which is precisely why it is an edge.

**CDC FluSight and COVID-19 Forecast Hubs (hubverse)** — CDC Center for Forecasting and Outbreak Analytics + Reich Lab / hubverse `LIVE`

- Every submitted model forecast, weekly, in a standardized quantile format (reference_date, target, horizon, location, output_type, output_type_id, value) plus the official ensemble and the realized target data. cdcepi/FluSight-forecast-hub verified live for the 2026-2027 season, last commit 2026-09-15. CDCgov/covid19-forecast-hub last commit 2026-09-18. reichlab/variant-nowcast-hub (SARS-CoV-2 clade nowcasts) last commit 2026-09-18. hubverse-org/hubData and hubUtils give R/Python readers.
- Docs: https://github.com/cdcepi/FluSight-forecast-hub
- Auth: none | Limits: None beyond GitHub fair use. Use raw.githubusercontent.com or the S3 mirrors rather than the GitHub REST API (which is 60 req/hr unauthenticated). Full forecast archive retained per season.
- Latency: weekly (Wednesday submission deadline, ensemble published Thursday/Friday) | Format: CSV / parquet bulk over GitHub + S3
- Relevance: This is the model-spread and ensemble-forecast layer the research panel needs. You get ~30 independent models' full predictive quantiles for flu hospitalizations by state, plus the official ensemble, plus historical forecast-vs-outcome so you can score each model's calibration. That is directly the 'ensemble forecast, model spread, historical error' triad — and it lets you compute whether the market's implied probability sits inside or outside the ensemble's interval.

#### USEFUL

**openFDA — Device Recalls, Enforcement, Adverse Events (MAUDE), UDI** — US Food and Drug Administration `LIVE`

- device/recall (59,222 records, incl. root cause + Class), device/enforcement (39,949), device/event = MAUDE adverse event reports (26,136,889 records: deaths, serious injuries, malfunctions by brand/manufacturer), device/udi = GUDID device identifiers (5,182,695 records).
- Docs: https://open.fda.gov/apis/device/
- Auth: none (optional free API key) | Limits: 240/min + 1,000/day per IP unkeyed; 240/min + 120,000/day per free key. MAUDE history from 1991.
- Latency: daily-to-weekly (verified: device/recall 2026-09-17, device/event 2026-09-08, device/udi 2026-09-02) | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: Device safety-event and Class-I-device-recall contracts. MAUDE death/injury counts by manufacturer are the leading indicator that precedes a recall — genuine edge for anyone pricing 'will device X be recalled by date Y'.

**openFDA — FAERS Adverse Events (drug/event) + quarterly bulk files** — US Food and Drug Administration `LIVE`

- 20,692,690 individual case safety reports: patient demographics, drugs (with characterization primary/secondary/concomitant), MedDRA reactions, seriousness flags (death, hospitalization, disability, life-threatening), outcome, report source, receipt dates. Quarterly ASCII/XML bulk ZIPs also available from fis.fda.gov (faers_ascii_2026q1.zip verified live, 35MB).
- Docs: https://open.fda.gov/apis/drug/event/
- Auth: none (optional free API key) | Limits: 240/min + 1,000/day per IP unkeyed; 240/min + 120,000/day per free key. History: 2004 onwards. Bulk quarterly files unmetered.
- Latency: quarterly-ish for the API index (verified meta.last_updated = 2026-07-30 — noticeably staler than other openFDA endpoints) | Format: REST JSON + ZIP bulk
- Relevance: Prices safety-signal, black-box-warning and market-withdrawal contracts. Note the ~7-week index lag: do NOT use this for fast-moving safety markets without cross-checking MedWatch RSS.

**openFDA — Drug Labels (SPL) and NDC Directory** — US Food and Drug Administration `LIVE`

- drug/label: 262,883 structured product labels — indications, dosage, warnings, boxed warnings, contraindications, adverse reactions, effective_time, full text. drug/ndc: 138,046 NDC directory entries with marketing category, start/end marketing dates, DEA schedule, pharm_class.
- Docs: https://open.fda.gov/apis/drug/label/
- Auth: none (optional free API key) | Limits: 240/min + 1,000/day per IP unkeyed; 240/min + 120,000/day per free key.
- Latency: daily (verified both = 2026-09-18) | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: Boxed-warning additions and label-expansion contracts settle on label text changes; the effective_time field timestamps them. NDC marketing_end_date is how you detect a quiet product discontinuation before it hits the shortage list.

**WHO Global Health Observatory (GHO) OData API** — World Health Organization `LIVE`

- 3,099 indicators (confirmed count) across mortality, life expectancy, disease burden, immunization coverage, health systems, risk factors, NCDs, AMR enrolment. /api/Indicator lists them; /api/{IndicatorCode} returns the value series with SpatialDim (country ISO3), TimeDim, Dim1 (sex/age), NumericValue, Low, High, Date. Full OData: $filter, $select, $top, $skip, $count.
- Docs: https://www.who.int/data/gho/info/gho-odata-api
- Auth: none | Limits: UNKNOWN — no documented quota and no rate-limit headers returned. Responses are Azure-CDN cached (cache-control: public, max-age=3600), so polling more than hourly gains nothing. History: varies by indicator, many series back to 1990 or 2000.
- Latency: annual-to-irregular (most indicators update yearly) | Format: REST JSON (OData v4)
- Relevance: Backdrop rather than settlement data — the denominators and base rates you need to price outbreak severity, vaccination-target and global-health-goal contracts. Useful for 'will country X reach Y% coverage by Z' markets. Too slow for anything with a sub-annual resolution.

**WHO COVID-19 Global Daily Data (bulk CSV)** — World Health Organization `LIVE`

- Single CSV, 26.5MB: Date_reported, Country_code, Country, WHO_region, New_cases, Cumulative_cases, New_deaths, Cumulative_deaths for every country. Confirmed live and still updating — last row 2026-08-30. There are companion files for vaccination and hospitalization on the same blob container.
- Docs: https://data.who.int/dashboards/covid19/data
- Auth: none | Limits: None documented. Single static blob on Azure — pull once per update cycle, do not poll. History: 2020-01-04 to present.
- Latency: weekly-to-monthly (reporting cadence collapsed post-emergency; verified through 2026-08-30) | Format: CSV bulk
- Relevance: The last surviving authoritative global COVID case/death series — note this is important because BOTH of the sources people reach for first (JHU CSSE and the OWID GitHub repo) are dead. Settles remaining country-level COVID contracts. Reporting is now sparse and lagged, so treat low counts as 'not reported' rather than 'zero' when pricing.

**UKHSA Data Dashboard API** — UK Health Security Agency `LIVE`

- Hierarchical REST API: /themes -> sub_themes -> topics -> geography_types -> geographies -> metrics. Covers infectious_disease (COVID-19, influenza, RSV, measles), immunisation, climate_and_environment. Verified live: COVID-19_cases_casesByDay for England returned 2,422 daily records. Metrics include cases, deaths, healthcare admissions, testing, vaccination uptake at Nation/Region/UTLA/LTLA geographies.
- Docs: https://ukhsa-dashboard.data.gov.uk/access-our-data
- Auth: none | Limits: UNKNOWN — no numeric rate limit published on the access-our-data pages or the Swagger endpoint. Paging via page_size/page. History: COVID-19 daily series back to 2020 (2,422 points confirmed).
- Latency: daily to weekly by metric | Format: REST JSON (+ CSV)
- Relevance: The cleanest national-level API in Europe for UK-specific health contracts. Genuinely well-structured compared to most ministry feeds — the geography hierarchy lets you settle sub-national contracts without scraping.

**Our World in Data — ETL Catalog and Grapher CSV API** — Our World in Data (Global Change Data Lab) `LIVE`

- Two live paths. (1) Catalog: catalog.ourworldindata.org/garden/covid/latest/compact/compact.csv — 182MB, verified current to 2026-08-30 with cases, deaths, hospitalizations, ICU, testing, vaccinations, excess mortality per country-day. Also garden/who/latest/monkeypox/monkeypox.csv. (2) Grapher CSV: ourworldindata.org/grapher/{slug}.csv?csvType=filtered — verified on life-expectancy and on the GLASS AMR enrolment chart. (3) api.ourworldindata.org/v1/indicators/{id}.metadata.json and .data.json for individual indicator series.
- Docs: https://docs.owid.io/projects/etl/api/
- Auth: none | Limits: UNKNOWN — no published quota. Files are large (182MB for covid compact); cache locally and refresh daily at most. History: full, back to source origin.
- Latency: daily for COVID compact; varies by dataset otherwise | Format: CSV bulk + REST JSON
- Relevance: Best single normalized cross-country panel for health contracts that span borders. Critical operational note: the OWID GitHub repos everyone links to are FROZEN — you must use the catalog paths listed here instead. Excess-mortality and vaccination series are the market-relevant columns.

**EU Clinical Trials Information System (CTIS) Public API** — European Medicines Agency `LIVE`

- Public search over EU clinical trials submitted under Regulation 536/2014: trial ID, sponsor, therapeutic area, member states concerned, decision dates, trial status, medicinal products. Verified: POST https://euclinicaltrials.eu/ctis-public-api/search returns a valid paginated envelope {showWarning, pagination{totalRecords,currentPage,totalPages,nextPage,prevPage}, data[]}. Retrieve endpoint /ctis-public-api/retrieve/{ctNumber} also responds 200.
