- Latency: daily | Format: REST JSON (POST-only search)
- Relevance: European counterpart to ClinicalTrials.gov for EU-authorisation and EU-trial contracts. Coverage starts 2022, so for anything older you need the legacy EU Clinical Trials Register (clinicaltrialsregister.eu/ctr-search/rest/download/summary — verified live, returns plain-text summaries).

**EMA Medicine Data (bulk spreadsheets)** — European Medicines Agency `LIVE`

- Daily-refreshed XLSX exports of every EMA medicine: EPARs for human medicines (verified live, 622KB XLSX), veterinary medicines, orphan designations, herbal monographs, referrals, shortages, PSUSA. Columns include medicine name, INN, therapeutic area, marketing-authorisation holder, ATC code, authorisation status, decision date, CHMP opinion date, revision number.
- Docs: https://www.ema.europa.eu/en/medicines/download-medicine-data
- Auth: none | Limits: None documented. Static files, refreshed daily. History: all currently and previously authorised EU medicines.
- Latency: daily | Format: XLSX bulk (no REST API exists)
- Relevance: Settles EU drug-approval contracts. Hard caveat: EMA has NO REST API and NO working RSS (ema.europa.eu/en/rss.xml returns 404 — I checked). CHMP monthly opinion outcomes are published as web highlights, not as structured data, so the monthly CHMP-meeting contracts require either diffing this spreadsheet or scraping. Diffing the XLSX daily is the honest free approach.

**FDA RSS Feeds — Press Releases, Recalls/Safety Alerts, MedWatch** — US Food and Drug Administration `LIVE`

- Three verified-live RSS feeds: /rss-feeds/press-releases/rss.xml (FDA Press Releases), /rss-feeds/recalls/rss.xml (Recalls, Market Withdrawals and Safety Alerts), /rss-feeds/medwatch/rss.xml (MedWatch Safety Alerts). Each carries title, link, pubDate, dc:creator, description.
- Docs: https://www.fda.gov/about-fda/contact-fda/stay-informed/rss-feeds
- Auth: none | Limits: None documented. Standard RSS — poll every few minutes at most. History: feeds carry a rolling window (roughly the most recent 50–100 items), not an archive.
- Latency: sub-minute to minutes after FDA publication — the fastest FDA surface available | Format: RSS
- Relevance: Latency arbitrage. openFDA structured endpoints lag by days (drug/event by ~7 weeks); the press-release RSS carries a novel-drug approval within minutes of announcement. For any contract resolving on an FDA action, this is your fast leg and openFDA drugsfda is your settlement leg. Note there is NO advisory-committee RSS — that feed 404s; use pdufa.bio /adcomm or scrape the calendar page.

**Europe PMC RESTful Web Service** — EMBL-EBI / Europe PMC Consortium `LIVE`

- Search across ~47M abstracts and ~10M full texts including PubMed, PMC, preprints (bioRxiv/medRxiv), patents, clinical guidelines, NHS evidence. Verified live: query 'influenza' returned hitCount 473,443 with cursorMark paging. Endpoints: /search, /{source}/{id}/fullTextXML, /citations, /references, /textMinedTerms, /annotations_api.
- Docs: https://europepmc.org/RestfulWebService
- Auth: none | Limits: UNKNOWN officially — Europe PMC does not publish a numeric quota in its terms. Community and the ropensci/europepmc client converge on ~10 requests/second. pageSize max 1000, deep paging via cursorMark (not offset). History: complete, back to the 1800s for indexed literature. Note the docs page itself sits behind a Cloudflare challenge from datacenter IPs even though the API does not.
- Latency: daily indexing | Format: REST JSON / XML / DC
- Relevance: NICHE-to-USEFUL for markets. Its real value is as the earliest public appearance of trial results — a preprint or conference abstract often predates the company press release. Also the annotations API gives you machine-extracted gene/disease/chemical mentions for building an early-signal detector.

**NCBI E-utilities (PubMed, PMC, Gene, Taxonomy)** — US National Library of Medicine / NCBI `LIVE`

- esearch/efetch/esummary/elink/epost across 38 NCBI databases. Verified live: esearch on PubMed for 'measles' returned count 34,861 with JSON retmode. Gives PMIDs, full MEDLINE records, MeSH terms, publication dates, linked datasets.
- Docs: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK25501/
- Auth: none required; free API key available via NCBI account | Limits: Without API key: 3 requests/second per IP. With free API key: 10 requests/second. Exceeding 10/s returns HTTP 429. Higher limits by written request to info@ncbi.nlm.nih.gov. retmax max 10,000 per esearch; use retstart or the history server (WebEnv/query_key) beyond that. History: complete PubMed back to 1946 (and OLDMEDLINE to 1809).
- Latency: daily indexing | Format: REST JSON / XML
- Relevance: Same role as Europe PMC — literature-signal layer rather than settlement. The clean numeric rate limits make it the better choice for high-volume systematic pulls.

**Nextstrain — Charon API and data.nextstrain.org** — Nextstrain (Fred Hutch / Biozentrum Basel) `LIVE`

- Live phylogenetic builds as JSON. Verified: /charon/getAvailable?prefix=/ enumerates all public datasets (includes avian-flu/h5n1-cattle-outbreak with genome + per-segment builds); /charon/getDataset?prefix=/seasonal-flu/h3n2/ha/2y returned a 6.6MB v2 dataset dated 2026-09-17 with full tree, clade assignments and metadata. data.nextstrain.org serves bulk TSV/gz including forecasts-ncov clade frequency and growth-advantage estimates (verified 1.5MB gz download).
- Docs: https://docs.nextstrain.org/en/latest/
- Auth: none | Limits: None documented. Datasets are multi-MB JSON — cache aggressively, refresh daily at most. History: builds are rolling windows (2y, 6m, 12y variants per pathogen).
- Latency: daily-to-weekly rebuilds (h3n2 build stamped 2026-09-17) | Format: REST JSON + TSV/gz bulk
- Relevance: Prices variant-dominance contracts ('will clade X exceed Y% of sequences by date Z'). The forecasts-ncov files carry explicit clade growth-advantage and frequency projections — that is a ready-made model output to compare against market-implied variant probabilities. Also the settlement source for H5N1 genotype/reassortment questions.

**Global.health outbreak-data (GitHub)** — Global.health consortium `LIVE`

- Curated outbreak line-lists and aggregate counts per outbreak, distributed through a GitHub repo and its wiki. Repo last commit verified 2026-09-18T18:10:48Z — actively maintained. Historically covers mpox, Marburg, Ebola, COVID-19 with per-case fields (location, dates, demographics, travel history, outcome).
- Docs: https://github.com/globaldothealth/outbreak-data
- Auth: none | Limits: None beyond GitHub raw fair use. History: per outbreak, from that outbreak's start. IMPORTANT: data.global.health/api/* paths return the SPA HTML shell, not JSON — there is no public REST API despite the URL shape. GitHub is the real access path.
- Latency: daily-to-weekly during an active outbreak | Format: CSV bulk over GitHub
- Relevance: The only free case-level (not just aggregate) outbreak data for emerging pathogens. Line-list granularity lets you estimate CFR, serial interval and Rt directly rather than trusting a published number — real edge on outbreak-severity contracts where the market prices off headline counts.

#### NICHE

**Health Canada Drug Product Database API** — Health Canada `LIVE`

- Every drug authorised in Canada: DIN, brand name, company, active ingredients, ai_group_no, class (Human/Vet), schedule, dosage form, route, status, marketing dates. Verified live with DIN 00326925 returning a full record. Sub-resources: /drugproduct, /activeingredient, /company, /status, /form, /route, /schedule, /therapeuticclass, /packaging, /pharmaceuticalstd.
- Docs: https://health-products.canada.ca/api/documentation/dpd-documentation-en.html
- Auth: none | Limits: UNKNOWN — no published quota. Query by din, id, lang, status, brandname, active_ingredient_name. History: currently and historically marketed products.
- Latency: daily | Format: REST JSON / XML
- Relevance: NICHE for most markets but the cleanest non-US regulatory API that exists, and the settlement source for Canadian approval contracts. Also useful as a cross-check when a drug is approved in one jurisdiction before another.

**DailyMed SPL API** — US National Library of Medicine `LIVE`

- Structured Product Labels for every marketed US drug: setid, title, spl_version, published_date, labeler, NDC codes, and the full label XML. Verified live returning labels published 2026-09-18. Endpoints: /spls.json, /spls/{setid}.json, /drugnames.json, /ndcs.json, /rxcuis.json, /drugclasses.json.
- Docs: https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/app-support-mapi.cfm
- Auth: none | Limits: UNKNOWN — no published quota. Paging via page/pagesize (default 100). History: current labels plus version history per setid.
- Latency: daily (verified published_date 2026-09-18, same-week) | Format: REST JSON / XML
- Relevance: Faster and more granular than openFDA drug/label for detecting the exact moment a label changes — spl_version increments are the event. Prices boxed-warning-addition and indication-expansion contracts. The version history is what lets you prove when a change happened.

**RxNav / RxNorm / RxClass APIs** — US National Library of Medicine `LIVE`

- Drug terminology normalisation: RxCUI lookup by name, NDC<->RxCUI mapping, ingredient/brand/dose-form relationships, ATC classification (verified: rxclass/allClasses returned the full ATC1-4 tree), drug interactions, historical NDC status. Verified: rxcui.json?name=prednisone -> 8640.
- Docs: https://lhncbc.nlm.nih.gov/RxNav/APIs/
- Auth: none | Limits: 20 requests/second per IP (explicitly documented). No API key. NLM recommends caching results 12–24 hours; for higher volume they offer RxNav-in-a-Box (local Docker). History: RxNorm monthly releases with full history.
- Latency: monthly releases (weekly for some sub-sets) | Format: REST JSON / XML
- Relevance: Plumbing, not signal. But essential plumbing: FDA shortage records, openFDA labels, clinical trials and payer data all name drugs differently, and RxNorm is what joins them. Without it your shortage feed and your approval feed will silently fail to match on the same molecule.

**AccessGUDID API** — US National Library of Medicine / FDA `LIVE`

- Global Unique Device Identification Database: device identifier (DI) lookup returning brand name, company, version/model, GMDN terms, FDA product codes, sterility, MRI safety, sizes, device record status and version history. Verified live on DI 00844588018923.
- Docs: https://accessgudid.nlm.nih.gov/resources/home
- Auth: none | Limits: UNKNOWN — no published quota. Endpoints: /api/v3/devices/lookup.json, /api/v3/devices/search.json, plus full weekly bulk delimited-file downloads. History: devices from 2014 (UDI rule phase-in).
- Latency: daily record updates; weekly full bulk files | Format: REST JSON / XML + delimited bulk
- Relevance: NICHE. Joins openFDA device recall and MAUDE records to actual marketed products, which openFDA alone does not do cleanly. Only matters if you trade device markets seriously.

**healthdata.gov (HHS Socrata)** — US Department of Health and Human Services `LIVE`

- 10,000 datasets (confirmed catalog size) spanning HHS agencies: hospital utilisation, HRSA workforce, CMS, SAMHSA behavioural health, community health centres. Same SoQL interface as data.cdc.gov at /resource/{id}.json. Includes the archived COVID-19 hospital capacity series (g62h-syeh) — verified queryable but frozen.
- Docs: https://healthdata.gov/
- Auth: none; free Socrata app token recommended | Limits: UNKNOWN exact numbers — same undocumented Socrata policy as data.cdc.gov: shared-IP throttle without a token, effectively unthrottled with a free app token. $limit default 1000, max 50,000.
- Latency: varies by dataset, many are archival | Format: REST JSON / CSV (SODA)
- Relevance: Secondary to data.cdc.gov. Its hospital-capacity holdings are largely historical now — live hospital data moved to CDC NHSN (ua7e-t2fy). Worth crawling the catalog once for anything CDC does not carry, but do not build a live pipeline on it without checking each dataset's update date.

**ECDC Open Data downloads** — European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control `LIVE`

- Bulk JSON/CSV/XML at opendata.ecdc.europa.eu. Verified live: /covid19/nationalcasedeath/json/ (3.7MB, country-week cases and deaths) and /covid19/vaccine_tracker/json/ (93MB — doses by week, brand, target group, ISO country). Additional topic files for other pathogens.
- Docs: https://www.ecdc.europa.eu/en/publications-data
- Auth: none | Limits: None documented. Files are large (the vaccine tracker is 93MB); pull on a schedule, never poll. History: 2020-W01 onward for COVID series. WARNING: opendata.ecdc.europa.eu carries a banner noting some COVID files stopped daily updates on 14 December — check each file's max date before relying on it.
- Latency: weekly for the maintained files; several COVID files are frozen | Format: JSON / CSV bulk
- Relevance: Secondary to ERVISS for live European work. Its live value is the vaccination-dose series (vaccination-rate contracts). Verify freshness per file — this endpoint mixes maintained and abandoned datasets under one roof, which is exactly the trap the task warned about.

**medRxiv / bioRxiv API** — Cold Spring Harbor Laboratory `LIVE`

- /details/{server}/{start}/{end} returns preprints posted in a date window with title, authors, DOI, category, abstract, version, date. /pubs/{server}/{range} returns preprint-to-journal publication links. Verified: medRxiv 2026-09-01 to 2026-09-02 returned 30 records (120 total, 96 new).
- Docs: https://api.biorxiv.org/
- Auth: none | Limits: UNKNOWN — no published quota. Cursor paging in 100-record blocks. History: medRxiv from 2019, bioRxiv from 2013.
- Latency: daily | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: NICHE but genuinely early. Outbreak characterisation papers, vaccine-effectiveness estimates and variant-severity analyses appear here weeks before peer review and often before the agency statement that a contract settles on. Category filtering on 'epidemiology' and 'infectious diseases' gives a tractable daily stream.

**CMS Provider Data Catalog API** — Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services `LIVE`

- DCAT-formatted metastore over hospital, nursing-home, hospice, dialysis and physician quality datasets — Hospital Compare star ratings, HAI/infection measures, readmission and mortality measures, staffing. Verified live: /provider-data/api/1/metastore/schemas/dataset/items returned a 552KB catalog with records modified 2026-06-16.
- Docs: https://data.cms.gov/provider-data/docs
- Auth: none | Limits: UNKNOWN — no published quota. Datastore query endpoint supports SQL-like filtering with paging. History: quarterly refresh cycles, multi-year.
- Latency: quarterly | Format: REST JSON (DKAN/DCAT)
- Relevance: NICHE. Quarterly cadence makes it useless for fast markets. Its use is structural: hospital-level infection rates and staffing are the base rates behind hospital-strain and healthcare-associated-infection contracts.

**World Bank Health Indicators API + Eurostat Health Statistics API** — World Bank / Eurostat `LIVE`

- World Bank v2 API: ~1,500 health indicators by country-year (SH.DYN.MORT under-5 mortality verified live, 17,490 observations, lastupdated 2026-07-13), health expenditure, immunisation, hospital beds, physicians per capita. Eurostat dissemination API: JSON-stat 2.0 for EU health statistics — verified live on hlth_cd_asdr2 (standardised death rate by cause and NUTS-2 region), updated 2026-06-08.
- Docs: https://datahelpdesk.worldbank.org/knowledgebase/articles/889392
- Auth: none for either | Limits: UNKNOWN for both — neither publishes a numeric quota. World Bank: per_page max 32,767, page-based. Eurostat: response capped around 1,000,000 cells per query, filter with dimension params. History: World Bank mostly 1960 onward; Eurostat varies by table.
- Latency: annual (World Bank), annual-to-quarterly (Eurostat) | Format: REST JSON / JSON-stat 2.0
- Relevance: Base rates only. Useful for long-horizon global-health-goal contracts and for normalising outbreak counts by population and health-system capacity. Annual cadence rules them out for anything resolving inside a year.

**NIH RePORTER API v2** — US National Institutes of Health `LIVE`

- Every NIH-funded project: project number, title, abstract, PI, organisation, fiscal year, award amount, study section, terms, linked publications and patents. Verified live: POST /v2/projects/search with fiscal_years 2025 returned total 76,352.
- Docs: https://api.reporter.nih.gov/
- Auth: none | Limits: UNKNOWN — no published quota. POST-based search with limit max 500 and offset capped at 14,999 per query (partition by fiscal year or institute to exceed). History: FY1985 onward.
- Latency: weekly | Format: REST JSON (POST)
- Relevance: NICHE. Prices NIH-funding-level and research-priority contracts, and gives early warning of which pathogens and platforms are getting money — a slow leading indicator for which trials will exist in two years. Not a settlement source for anything fast.

**CDC Content Syndication API** — US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention `LIVE`

- 6,756 syndicated CDC media items (confirmed pagination total): health topic pages, MMWR content, guidance documents, with datepublished, title, description, sourceUrl, and full HTML. Sortable by -datepublished for a reverse-chronological CDC publication stream.
- Docs: https://tools.cdc.gov/medialibrary/index.aspx
- Auth: none | Limits: UNKNOWN — no published quota. Paging via max/offset/pagenum. History: rolling CDC content library.
- Latency: daily | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: NICHE. The value is latency on CDC guidance changes — ACIP recommendation updates, travel notices and MMWR early releases show up here as structured records with timestamps, which is better than diffing cdc.gov HTML. MMWR early releases in particular often carry the first official case counts for an emerging outbreak.

**CDC WONDER API** — US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention

- XML-over-HTTP query interface to WONDER databases: D76/D77 (Multiple Cause of Death, detailed mortality by ICD-10, age, race, state, county), D66 (natality), VAERS, cancer statistics, TB, STD. Returns cross-tabulated counts, rates and population denominators.
- Docs: https://wonder.cdc.gov/wonder/help/WONDER-API.html
- Auth: none | Limits: UNKNOWN — and I could not verify, see below. Documented structural limits: the API refuses sub-national (county/state-level) queries for several mortality databases even though the web UI permits them, and it enforces suppression of counts under 10.
- Latency: monthly for provisional mortality; annual for final | Format: XML over HTTP POST
- Relevance: USEFUL in principle for mortality-threshold and cause-of-death contracts — WONDER is the authoritative US mortality source. NOT VERIFIED LIVE: every wonder.cdc.gov request from this environment returned HTTP 403 Access Denied from Akamai, including the documentation page itself, with both a generic and a full browser User-Agent. This reads as a datacenter-IP block rather than a dead service. Assume you will need residential/allow-listed egress, and prefer data.cdc.gov's VSRR provisional mortality datasets (verified live) for anything time-sensitive.

**ISRCTN Registry API + EU Clinical Trials Register (legacy)** — BMC/Springer Nature (ISRCTN) / European Medicines Agency (EU CTR) `LIVE`

- ISRCTN: XML query API over ~25,000 registered trials — verified live, query 'influenza' returned totalCount 233 with full trial records (lastUpdated, version, sponsor, condition, intervention, recruitment dates). EU CTR legacy: /ctr-search/rest/download/summary?query=X returns plain-text EudraCT trial summaries — verified live (39KB returned).
- Docs: https://www.isrctn.com/page/api
- Auth: none for either | Limits: UNKNOWN for both. ISRCTN: limit/offset paging, XML only. EU CTR: mode=current_page vs all-pages download. History: ISRCTN from 2000; EU CTR covers pre-2022 EudraCT trials (post-2022 trials are in CTIS instead).
- Latency: daily | Format: XML (ISRCTN) / plain text (EU CTR)
- Relevance: NICHE completeness layer. A non-trivial number of European and UK trials register here and NOT on ClinicalTrials.gov, so if you are pricing a readout for a European sponsor and find nothing on CT.gov, check these before concluding the trial does not exist.

**NLM Clinical Tables + MedlinePlus Connect** — US National Library of Medicine `LIVE`

- Clinical Tables: autocomplete/lookup APIs over ICD-10-CM, ICD-9, SNOMED conditions, RxTerms, LOINC, NPI, HCPCS, UCUM. Verified: icd10cm/v3/search?terms=influenza returned J11.81 with its full descriptor. MedlinePlus Connect: maps an ICD-10 or RxCUI code to consumer health information — verified live returning a JSON feed for J10.
- Docs: https://clinicaltables.nlm.nih.gov/
- Auth: none for either | Limits: UNKNOWN — no published quota on either. Clinical Tables maxList default 7, configurable. History: current code releases.
- Latency: annual code releases | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: Plumbing. ICD-10 code resolution is what lets you join WONDER mortality, NNDSS case definitions, hospital discharge data and Eurostat cause-of-death tables to the same disease concept. Contracts written in plain language ('deaths from influenza') need a defensible code list, and this is where it comes from.

**disease.sh — COVID / Influenza aggregator** — disease.sh (community, open source) `LIVE`

- Normalised JSON aggregation over JHU, WorldoMeters, CDC and NYT COVID data plus influenza endpoints. Verified live: /v3/covid-19/all returned a full global object (704.75M cases, 7.01M deaths) with an 'updated' epoch timestamp.
- Docs: https://disease.sh/docs/
- Auth: none | Limits: UNKNOWN — no published numeric quota; the project historically asked for reasonable use and cached responses. History: rolling.
- Latency: the endpoint reports frequent updates, but the underlying upstreams are largely frozen | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: NICHE and use with real caution. It is convenient and it responds, but its principal upstream (JHU CSSE) stopped collecting on 2023-03-10, so 'live' here means 'the API is up', not 'the numbers are current' — note todayCases: 0 and todayDeaths: 0 in the verified response. Good for historical convenience, unsafe as a settlement source. Exactly the kind of feed that looks alive and is not.

#### Repos

- `FDA/openfda` — The FDA's own source code for openFDA — Luigi/Python pipelines that convert raw FDA datasets (FAERS, SPL, NDC, device clearance, device PMA, device event, NSDE, substance data) into the JSON that api.fda.gov serves, loaded into Elasticsearch. 710 stars. · If you ever need to exceed openFDA's 120,000/day ceiling or want the raw pre-annotation records, this shows you exactly which source files FDA ingests and how they normalise them. It also documents field semantics far better than the public API docs, which matters when you are settling a contract on a specific field value.
- `cmu-delphi/delphi-epidata` — Server and client source for the Delphi Epidata API, plus documentation for every signal source. 105 stars. Companion clients: cmu-delphi/epidatpy (Python) and cmu-delphi/epidatr (R). · The documentation in this repo is the only clear explanation of the issue/lag vintaging model, which is the whole reason Delphi matters for backtesting. Also lists exactly which COVIDcast signals are still maintained versus retired — important because several were discontinued.
- `EU-ECDC/Respiratory_viruses_weekly_data` — ECDC's official GitHub distribution of ERVISS — weekly EU/EEA influenza, RSV and SARS-CoV-2 surveillance as flat CSVs. 24 stars, last commit 2026-09-18, data current to 2026-W37. · This is not a third-party scrape; it is ECDC's own machine-readable channel, and it is the only practical way to get European respiratory surveillance programmatically since the ECDC Surveillance Atlas is an ASP.NET app with no API. Four CSVs cover sentinel, non-sentinel, severity and ILI/ARI rates.
- `cdcepi/FluSight-forecast-hub` — CDC's collaborative influenza forecasting hub for the 2026-2027 season. 66 stars, last commit 2026-09-15. Collects weekly quantile forecasts of new hospital admissions by state from ~30 modelling teams, plus the official ensemble and the realized target data. · Gives you model spread and an ensemble forecast for free, plus the full historical forecast archive so you can score each team's calibration and compute that team's own historical error. That is directly the ensemble/spread/historical-error triad a research panel needs, and it lets you check a market's implied probability against a proper predictive distribution rather than a point estimate.
- `CDCgov/covid19-forecast-hub` — CDC's COVID-19 forecast hub, last commit 2026-09-18. Same hubverse format as FluSight. Note this SUPERSEDED reichlab/covid19-forecast-hub, which has been stale since 2024-11-21. · Active COVID hospitalization forecasts in a standard format. The reichlab repo is the one most search results and tutorials still point at, and it is dead — this is the live one.
- `reichlab/variant-nowcast-hub` — Collaborative nowcasting hub for SARS-CoV-2 clade frequencies in the US. Last commit 2026-09-18. · Directly prices variant-dominance contracts. Multiple independent teams' nowcasts of clade proportion give you a spread around the point estimate that a single dashboard will not.
- `hubverse-org/hubData` — R tooling for reading hubverse-format forecast hubs from local or S3 storage; hubverse-org/hub-data is the Python equivalent; hubEnsembles builds ensembles; hubEvals scores them. Last commit 2026-08-31. · Saves you writing the parquet/CSV partition reader for every hub. hubEvals in particular implements WIS and pinball loss correctly, which is what you want for converting forecast distributions into calibrated probabilities to compare against market prices.
- `globaldothealth/outbreak-data` — Global.health's curated outbreak datasets, distributed via the repo and its wiki. Last commit 2026-09-18. · Case-level line-lists for emerging outbreaks (mpox, Marburg, Ebola) rather than aggregate counts. Critically, this is the ACTUAL access path — data.global.health's /api/* URLs return the SPA HTML shell, not JSON, so anyone who assumes a REST API exists there will get HTML and not notice.
- `nextstrain/ncov` — The SARS-CoV-2 Nextstrain build (1,363 stars). Siblings: nextstrain/seasonal-flu (64), nextstrain/avian-flu, nextstrain/augur (279, the pipeline toolkit), nextstrain/nextclade (262, clade assignment). · Reproduces the clade-frequency and growth-advantage estimates that price variant contracts, and nextclade can assign clades to your own sequences offline. The avian-flu builds are the settlement reference for H5N1 genotype questions.
- `ASHP-Software/drugShortagesDoc` — Official API documentation for the ASHP (American Society of Health-System Pharmacists) Drug Shortages database — the pharmacist-maintained shortage list that often diverges from FDA's. · Read it to understand the schema and the divergence, but note the access terms: the docs state 'To request an API key and licensing information, contact softwaresupport@ashp.org', and the route format is /drugShortages/{id}/latest.json?auth={apiKey}. This is a licensed commercial API, not a free one — see deadEnds.
- `jvfe/pytrials` — Python wrapper for the ClinicalTrials.gov API (61 stars). Alternatives: mcnamamj/ctg-python-client and jrenewhite/clinical-trials-api-wrapper, both written against API v2. · Handles the v2 cursor paging (nextPageToken) and field-selection syntax, which are the two things people get wrong first. pytrials is the most-used, but check it targets v2 rather than the retired classic API.
- `cyanheads/clinicaltrialsgov-mcp-server` — MCP server exposing ClinicalTrials.gov search, study detail retrieval and eligibility matching as tools (94 stars). · If the research panel's synthesis layer is an LLM, this is a ready-made tool surface for trial queries rather than a hand-rolled wrapper. Pairs with Augmented-Nature/OpenFDA-MCP-Server (24 stars) and SuyashEkhande/OpenFDA-Semantic-MCP (14) for the FDA side.
- `rOpenHealth/openfda` — R client for the openFDA API (65 stars). ropensci/europepmc is the equivalent for Europe PMC. · The ropensci europepmc client is where the ~10 requests/second Europe PMC figure is actually encoded and battle-tested, since Europe PMC does not document a limit. Worth reading its throttling code before you build your own.
- `PHES-ODM/PHES-ODM` — Public Health Environmental Surveillance Open Data Model (58 stars) — a standard schema for wastewater surveillance data. Delatolla-lab/PHESD (17 stars) is a Canadian dataset using it. · CDC NWSS, WastewaterSCAN and each national programme all use different units, normalisation targets (PMMoV vs flow) and site identifiers. This is the community schema for reconciling them, which you need before comparing a US wastewater threshold contract to a European one.
- `owid/covid-19-data` — Our World in Data's COVID-19 repository (archived for updates). Last data row 2024-08-04; the README carries an explicit red 'Data has been moved' warning and points to catalog.ourworldindata.org. · Still the best-documented historical COVID panel and useful for backtesting. Listed here mainly as a warning: it is the single most-linked COVID dataset on the internet and it has been frozen since 2024-08-19.
- `cdcepi/zika` — CDC's public Zika data repository (165 stars) — the archetype for how CDC publishes an outbreak dataset on GitHub. · Historical Zika counts for backtesting arbovirus outbreak models, and a template for what to expect if CDC opens a repo for the next emerging pathogen.

### Science, Space, Technology and Discovery

#### CORE

**Launch Library 2 (The Space Devs)** — The Space Devs `LIVE`

- The single best launch-settlement feed. Every orbital and suborbital launch worldwide: provider, rocket, pad, mission, payload, T-0 window (net, window_start, window_end), plus a status enum (Go / TBD / TBC / Success / Failure / Hold) and slip history. Also upcoming space events (dockings, EVAs, landings), astronaut rosters, space stations, expeditions and agency records. Covers full history back to 1957 and ~370 upcoming launches at the time of check.
- Docs: https://thespacedevs.com/llapi
- Auth: none for the free 'lldev' tier and the main ll.thespacedevs.com host; free registration raises limits | Limits: 15 requests per hour, no API key (stated on thespacedevs.com/llapi). No documented daily cap. History depth: complete launch database from 1957 to present. Pagination via limit/offset. The ll.thespacedevs.com/lldev/ mirror is uncapped but returns cached data.
- Latency: minutely — launch status flips (Go/Hold/Success) propagate within minutes of the event | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: THE core feed for 'will SpaceX/Rocket Lab/ULA launch X by date' contracts. The status enum plus net timestamp is literally the settlement source. Also settles 'how many orbital launches in 2026', 'will Starship fly again before D', 'will Artemis slip past D'. The slip history lets you build an empirical slip-distribution model per provider, which is what actually prices a date contract.

**NASA Open APIs (APOD, Asteroids NeoWs, DONKI, EONET, EPIC, Techport, TechTransfer, Exoplanet, SSC, TLE)** — NASA / api.data.gov `LIVE`

- One key unlocks ~16 APIs. Highest-value for markets: NeoWs (near-earth asteroid close approaches with miss distance, diameter estimate, hazard flag), DONKI (solar flares with class/peak time, CMEs with speed, geomagnetic storms with Kp, SEP events, radiation belt enhancements), EONET (open natural-event tracker: wildfires, storms, volcanoes with geometry and dates), Techport (NASA technology project records with funding and TRL), EPIC (full-disk Earth imagery). Verified 2026-09 data in APOD, NeoWs, DONKI, EPIC, EONET and Techport.
- Docs: https://api.nasa.gov/
- Auth: free API key (instant, email only); DEMO_KEY works for testing | Limits: DEMO_KEY: 30 requests per IP per hour AND 50 per IP per day. Registered free key: 1,000 requests per hour, no documented daily cap. Live X-RateLimit-Limit header on DEMO_KEY read 10 from our IP (shared pool depletion), so treat 30/hr as a ceiling not a guarantee. History: DONKI from 2010, NeoWs full catalog, APOD from 1995-06-16.
- Latency: DONKI/NeoWs hourly to daily; EONET daily; APOD daily | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: DONKI settles 'will an X-class flare occur by D' and 'will a G4+ geomagnetic storm hit by D'. NeoWs settles asteroid close-approach and 'potentially hazardous object' contracts. Techport gives forward signal on NASA program funding for 'will NASA cancel/fund X' markets.

**CelesTrak GP / SATCAT** — CelesTrak (Dr T.S. Kelso) `LIVE`

- Authoritative public orbital element sets. GP (general perturbations) data in TLE, 3LE, JSON, CSV, XML and KVN for every unclassified tracked object, queryable by NORAD ID, international designator, name or group (stations, starlink, active, geo, weather, gnss, last-30-days, analyst objects). Plus SATCAT: the full satellite catalog CSV with launch date, decay date, orbital status, owner and object type. Verified live: ISS TLE at epoch 26263 (2026 day 263) and Starlink JSON at epoch 2026-09-20.
- Docs: https://celestrak.org/NORAD/documentation/gp-data-formats.php
- Auth: none | Limits: No API key and NO published numeric rate limit — UNKNOWN. CelesTrak's stated policy is to query no more often than the data updates (GP sets refresh a few times per day) and it actively blocks clients that poll abusively. History depth: SATCAT covers every catalogued object since 1957; GP endpoint serves current elements only (use Space-Track for historical element sets).
- Latency: hourly to several-times-daily refresh | Format: REST (TLE / JSON / CSV / XML)
- Relevance: Settles 'will satellite X deorbit/reenter by D' (decay date in SATCAT), 'how many Starlink satellites in orbit on D' (group count), 'will constellation Y exceed N satellites'. Propagating the TLE with SGP4 gives you reentry timing days ahead of the news, which is real edge on decay markets.

**NOAA SWPC Services** — NOAA Space Weather Prediction Center `LIVE`

- The operational US space-weather feed, entirely open. Verified live 2026-09-20/21: planetary_k_index_1m.json (1-minute Kp), products/alerts.json (official watch/warning/alert messages with product codes like WARK04), json/goes/primary/xray-flares-latest.json (current GOES X-ray class, e.g. B3.6), text/3-day-forecast.txt (official NOAA geomagnetic/radio/radiation 3-day forecast), json/solar-cycle/observed-solar-cycle-indices.json (monthly SSN and F10.7 back to 1749). Also solar wind plasma/mag from DSCOVR and ACE, aurora ovation probability grids, and proton flux.
- Docs: https://www.swpc.noaa.gov/products-and-data
- Auth: none | Limits: No key and NO published rate limit — UNKNOWN. US federal open data, generally tolerant of 1-minute polling matching the data cadence. History depth: solar-cycle indices from 1749-01; most JSON products serve rolling 1-day / 3-day / 7-day windows; deeper archives via ftp.swpc.noaa.gov.
- Latency: realtime — 1-minute cadence on Kp, solar wind and X-ray flux | Format: REST JSON + plain text
- Relevance: Settles every aurora and geomagnetic-storm contract ('will Kp reach 7 by D', 'will a G5 storm occur in 2026'), and the official NOAA scale in alerts.json is usually the named settlement source. The 3-day forecast is a free published prior you can arbitrage against a market that has not priced it in yet.

**JPL SSD/CNEOS APIs (CAD, Fireball, SBDB, Sentry, Horizons)** — NASA JPL Solar System Dynamics `LIVE`

- cad.api: asteroid/comet close-approach data with exact JD/calendar date, nominal and min/max miss distance, relative velocity and uncertainty (48 approaches inside 0.05 AU on the day checked). fireball.api: detected atmospheric impact events with date, radiated energy, impact energy, lat/lon and altitude. sbdb.api and sbdb_query.api: full small-body physical and orbital parameters. sentry.api: impact-risk table with Torino/Palermo scale. horizons.api: precision ephemerides for any solar-system body. All verified live.
- Docs: https://ssd-api.jpl.nasa.gov/doc/
- Auth: none | Limits: No API key and NO published numeric rate limit — UNKNOWN. JPL asks for reasonable use and reserves the right to throttle. History: CAD covers 1900-2200 computed approaches; fireball data from 1988 to present; Horizons spans -9999 to +9999 for major bodies.
- Latency: daily (orbit solutions update as new observations arrive); Sentry recomputed on new astrometry | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: Settles 'will asteroid X pass within N km on D', 'will a new PHA be discovered', 'will an impact event of >N kT energy be recorded'. Sentry's Palermo scale is the settlement authority for impact-probability markets. Because these are deterministic orbit solutions, you can price the contract to near-certainty before the market does.

**Minor Planet Center NEOCP and MPEC feeds** — IAU Minor Planet Center (Harvard/CfA) `LIVE`

- Extended_Files/neocp.json is the live NEO Confirmation Page as machine-readable JSON: every unconfirmed object awaiting designation, with temporary designation, digest2 score, discovery date (verified 2026-09-20), RA/Dec, magnitude, and observation count. Plus RecentMPECs.html for newly issued Minor Planet Electronic Circulars (the official instrument by which a discovery becomes real), and bulk MPCORB.DAT / mpn_*.txt orbit files.
- Docs: https://www.minorplanetcenter.net/data
- Auth: none | Limits: No key, NO published rate limit — UNKNOWN. MPC requests clients not hammer the site and offers bulk files for volume use. History: MPCORB contains every numbered and multi-opposition object; NEOCP is a live queue showing only currently-unconfirmed objects (hours to days of depth).
- Latency: sub-minute to hourly on NEOCP; MPECs issued continuously | Format: REST JSON + HTML (MPEC listing is scrape-only)
- Relevance: Settles 'will a new near-earth asteroid be discovered by D' and 'will object X be confirmed'. The digest2 score on NEOCP is a calibrated NEO-likelihood number — you can price confirmation probability directly from it before any MPEC is issued, which is a genuine informational edge.

**arXiv API + OAI-PMH + RSS** — Cornell University / arXiv `LIVE`

- Full-text-searchable metadata for every preprint: title, abstract, authors, categories, DOI, submission and revision dates, version history. Three access paths all verified live: the Atom query API (export.arxiv.org/api/query — note HTTP is 301, must use HTTPS), per-category RSS (rss.arxiv.org/rss/cs.AI) for new-submission push, and OAI-PMH (oaipmh.arxiv.org/oai) for complete bulk harvest with datestamp ranges.
- Docs: https://info.arxiv.org/help/api/user-manual.html
- Auth: none | Limits: Terms of use (verified on the ToU page): no more than ONE request every THREE seconds, and a single connection at a time, aggregated across all machines you control. Per-call max_results cap: UNKNOWN (not stated on the ToU page). History depth: complete, 1991 to present, ~2.5M papers. Full bulk PDFs/source available via requester-pays S3.
- Latency: daily — new submissions announced once per weekday at 20:00 ET | Format: REST Atom XML + RSS + OAI-PMH
- Relevance: Settles 'will a paper on X appear by D' and gives leading indicators for AI-capability markets: a lab's arXiv posting pattern often precedes a model release by weeks. Category submission volume is a clean proxy for field momentum in 'will field X produce a breakthrough' contracts.

**Hugging Face Hub API** — Hugging Face `LIVE`

- The de-facto registry of AI model releases. /api/models returns every public model with id, author, createdAt, downloads, likes, trendingScore, tags, pipeline tag and library; sorted by trending it surfaces new frontier releases within hours. /api/datasets and /api/spaces likewise. Model cards, config.json (parameter counts, architecture) and file trees are all reachable. Leaderboard results live as datasets (e.g. open-llm-leaderboard/contents, hf-audio/open-asr-leaderboard) queryable through the same API. Verified live with 2026-09 models.
- Docs: https://huggingface.co/docs/hub/api
- Auth: none for public reads; free token raises limits and is required for gated repos | Limits: Anonymous reads work but HF publishes no hard numeric anonymous rate limit — UNKNOWN. A free account token materially raises throughput (HF documents limits per-account rather than as a fixed public number). History depth: full since 2020; createdAt on every repo. Dataset rows are served via the free datasets-server with a documented 100-row-per-request page size.
- Latency: sub-minute — a model appears on the Hub the moment it is published | Format: REST JSON (+ Parquet for dataset rows)
- Relevance: Directly settles 'will lab X release an open-weight model by D' and 'will a model exceed N downloads'. This is the fastest public confirmation that a release happened — usually ahead of press coverage. Combined with leaderboard datasets it also feeds 'will a model score above X on benchmark Y'.

**Epoch AI data downloads (Notable AI Models, Benchmarking Hub)** — Epoch AI `LIVE`

- The best-curated quantitative AI dataset in existence and it is free CSV. notable_ai_models.csv (verified live, columns include Model, Organization, Publication date, Domain, Task, Parameters, Training compute FLOP, Training dataset size, Compute notes) covering 3,600+ models. Sibling datasets for Frontier AI Models, Large-scale AI Models, All AI Models, plus the Benchmarking Hub with model-by-model eval results (GPQA Diamond, FrontierMath, SWE-Bench Verified, etc.) and an AI data-centers directory. A pip-installable `epochai` client wraps the underlying Airtable.
- Docs: https://epoch.ai/data/ai-models-documentation/downloads
- Auth: none | Limits: Plain CSV over HTTPS, no key, no rate limit — effectively unlimited. Licensed CC-BY. History depth: models back to the 1950s for compute-trend series; benchmark results from 2023 to present, updated as of September 2026. Note: /data/benchmark_results.csv is NOT a valid path (404) — use the per-benchmark download links on the Benchmarking Hub.
- Latency: weekly to monthly (curated, not automated) | Format: CSV bulk + Python client
- Relevance: The reference denominator for compute-milestone markets: 'will a model be trained with >10^27 FLOP by D', 'will parameter count exceed N'. The Benchmarking Hub is a defensible settlement source for 'will any model score above X on FrontierMath/GPQA by D' — its numbers are independently run rather than self-reported by labs, which is exactly the distinction that decides those contracts.

**OpenAlex** — OurResearch `LIVE`

- Open bibliographic graph of ~327 million works (verified live count), plus authors, institutions, sources, publishers, funders, topics and concepts, with citation counts, open-access status, and full filter/group-by/aggregate query language. Successor to Microsoft Academic Graph.
- Docs: https://help.openalex.org/
- Auth: free API key strongly recommended as of Feb 2026; anonymous still works at a much smaller budget | Limits: CHANGED IN FEB 2026 — the old '100,000 calls/day, polite pool' model is GONE, replaced by a USD credit budget, and the polite pool was abolished. Measured live on an anonymous request: X-RateLimit-Limit 1000 credits, X-RateLimit-Limit-USD 0.1 per day. Documented per-call costs: singleton ID/DOI lookup $0, list request $0.0001, search $0.001, content/semantic/text endpoints $0.01. Official docs state a free API key raises the daily budget 10x (one third-party source reports $1.00/day with a key vs $0.01/day without, which CONFLICTS with the $0.1 we measured anonymously — treat the exact key-tier figure as UNKNOWN and read the live X-RateLimit-Limit-USD header). Full monthly snapshot is free on S3 with no limit. History: complete, back to earliest indexed literature.
- Latency: daily | Format: REST JSON + S3 bulk snapshot
- Relevance: Prices 'will paper/author X be highly cited by D' and Nobel-prediction models — Nobel laureates are reliably in the top citation percentile of their field for years beforehand, and OpenAlex lets you compute that percentile for free. Also settles institutional-output and open-access-share contracts.

**NOAA/NASA GCN — General Coordinates Network** — NASA GSFC `LIVE`

- The alert backbone of transient astronomy. Real-time notices and human-written Circulars for gamma-ray bursts (Swift, Fermi, SVOM, Einstein Probe), gravitational-wave candidates (LIGO/Virgo/KAGRA), high-energy neutrinos (IceCube), fast radio bursts and optical transients. Kafka streaming with per-topic subscription, plus a browsable and searchable Circulars archive.
- Docs: https://gcn.nasa.gov/docs/client
- Auth: free client credentials (OAuth-style client id/secret) generated self-service on gcn.nasa.gov for Kafka; the Circulars web archive is open | Limits: No published numeric rate limit on the Kafka stream — UNKNOWN; it is a push subscription rather than a polled quota. History: Circulars archive complete from 1997 to present. Note the docs and archive pages return 200 but there is NO working public REST JSON endpoint — /api/circulars returned HTTP 400 and /circulars.json returned 404. Use the Kafka client or scrape the archive.
- Latency: realtime/websocket — notices arrive seconds to minutes after detection | Format: Kafka streaming (+ HTML archive)
- Relevance: Settles 'will a gravitational-wave event be detected by D', 'will a neutrino alert coincide with a GRB', 'will a naked-eye transient occur'. Sub-minute alert latency versus a market that reprices on news coverage is one of the largest structural speed edges available in this whole domain.

**Nobel Prize API v2.1** — Nobel Prize Outreach AB `LIVE`

- The official structured record. /nobelPrizes gives every prize 1901 to present with award year, category, motivation, prize amount and share; /laureates gives every laureate with full name, birth/death dates and places, affiliations at time of award, gender, and prize links. Verified live on both endpoints. Multilingual (en/no/se).
- Docs: https://api.nobelprize.org/2.1/
- Auth: none | Limits: No key, no published rate limit — UNKNOWN. History depth: complete, 1901 to present, ~1,000 laureates. Announcements are added within hours of the October ceremony announcements.
- Latency: annual (October announcements); API updated within hours | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: The settlement source for every 'will X win the Nobel in Y' contract. More importantly, the historical table is the training set: affiliation, career stage, prior-prize history and co-laureate patterns in this data are what make a Nobel model beat the crowd. Pair with OpenAlex/Semantic Scholar citation percentiles and Clarivate Citation Laureate lists.

**Space-Track.org** — US Space Force / 18th Space Defense Squadron `LIVE`

- The authoritative source CelesTrak itself derives from: full SATCAT, historical element sets (every TLE ever published for every object, not just current), TIP messages (Tracking and Impact Prediction — the official reentry forecast), conjunction data messages, decay messages, launch site and boxscore data. Historical element sets are the key differentiator over CelesTrak.
- Docs: https://www.space-track.org/documentation
- Auth: free account registration required (name, email, stated purpose, manual approval); session cookie auth | Limits: Fewer than 30 requests per minute AND fewer than 300 requests per hour (documented, enforced). History depth: complete element-set history for every catalogued object since 1957 — tens of millions of TLEs. Bulk queries strongly preferred over per-object polling.
- Latency: hourly to daily | Format: REST JSON/CSV/XML/TLE
- Relevance: CORE for reentry and decay markets — the TIP message IS the official reentry prediction and is usually the named settlement source. Historical TLEs let you backtest a decay model rather than guess. Registration friction keeps most retail participants out, which is precisely why the edge persists.

**Wikidata SPARQL + Wikimedia REST API** — Wikimedia Foundation `LIVE`

- The connective tissue for this whole panel. Wikidata SPARQL (verified live) answers arbitrary structured questions — every Nobel laureate with field, nationality and affiliation; every spacecraft with launch date and operator; every chemical element with discovery year. Wikimedia REST (verified live) gives page revision timestamps, which is a surprisingly good real-time 'has this been announced yet' detector.
- Docs: https://query.wikidata.org/ and https://api.wikimedia.org/wiki/Main_Page
- Auth: none; free Wikimedia account token raises REST API limits | Limits: SPARQL: no key; 60-second query timeout, approximately 5 concurrent queries per IP, and a descriptive User-Agent is REQUIRED or you get blocked. Wikimedia REST: anonymous 500 requests/hour, authenticated 5,000 requests/hour (documented per-app limits). History: complete edit history since 2001; Wikidata since 2012.
- Latency: sub-minute on page revisions; SPARQL endpoint lags Wikidata edits by minutes | Format: SPARQL + REST JSON
- Relevance: The join key across every other feed in this panel — Wikidata QIDs reconcile a NASA mission, an arXiv author, an ORCID and a Nobel laureate into one entity. Also a genuine leading indicator: Wikipedia page edits on a laureate or a launch spike within minutes of an announcement, often before the official API updates.

#### USEFUL

**USPTO Open Data Portal (ODP) APIs** — US Patent and Trademark Office `LIVE`

- The replacement for the retired PatentsView and legacy Developer Hub APIs. Patent File Wrapper search, patent and application full-text search, assignment data, PTAB proceedings, and Bulk Datasets API (which now also serves the PatentsView-derived disambiguated inventor/assignee tables). Grant and application records with filing date, grant date, CPC classification, assignee, inventor and claims.
- Docs: https://data.uspto.gov/apis/getting-started
- Auth: free API key required, obtained through a USPTO.gov account (sign-in has been mandatory since 18 June 2026); endpoints return 401 Unauthorized without it, which we confirmed live | Limits: 60 requests per API key per minute for standard API calls; 4 requests per API key per minute for PDF and ZIP downloads. No documented daily cap. History depth: full-text US patents from 1976, bibliographic back to 1790, pre-grant publications from 2001. Note: previously-issued PatentsView PatentSearch keys are NOT valid here — you must obtain a new ODP key.
- Latency: weekly (grants issue every Tuesday); bulk files weekly | Format: REST JSON + bulk ZIP
- Relevance: Settles 'will company X be granted a patent on Y by D' and patent-count contracts. Grant-date predictability (Tuesday issuance, published issue-notification lead time) makes these markets tractable if you have the feed and your counterparty does not.

**GraceDB — Gravitational-Wave Candidate Event Database** — LIGO / Virgo / KAGRA Collaboration `LIVE`

- Public superevent records with superevent_id, GW designation, creation timestamp, category (production vs MDC test), far (false-alarm rate), classification probabilities (BBH/BNS/NSBH/terrestrial), sky localization and EM follow-up status. Verified live: 6,299 superevents, most recent created 2026-09-21.
- Docs: https://gracedb.ligo.org/documentation/
- Auth: none for public superevents; LVK membership for internal alerts | Limits: No key and no published rate limit for public reads — UNKNOWN. History: all public alerts since O1 (2015), including full O4 and current run. Note the feed mixes MDC (mock data challenge) entries with production events — filter on category or you will settle a market on a simulation.
- Latency: sub-minute for public alerts | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: The authoritative settlement source for 'will N gravitational-wave detections occur in observing run X', 'will a BNS merger be detected by D', 'will a GW event have an EM counterpart'. The FAR field lets you price 'will this candidate be confirmed' before the collaboration publishes.

**NASA Exoplanet Archive TAP service** — NASA / IPAC Caltech `LIVE`

- Full ADQL/SQL over the confirmed-planet table (ps), planetary systems composite table (pscomppars), TESS Objects of Interest, Kepler/K2 candidates, transit ephemerides, and microlensing events. Verified live: 40,155 rows in the ps table. Every column — discovery method, discovery year, discovery facility, orbital period, radius, mass, equilibrium temperature — is queryable and filterable.
- Docs: https://exoplanetarchive.ipac.caltech.edu/docs/TAP/usingTAP.html
- Auth: none | Limits: No key; sync queries subject to a server-side timeout (async available for large jobs); no published request-per-minute cap — UNKNOWN. History: complete confirmed-exoplanet record from 1992 to present, updated weekly.
- Latency: weekly | Format: REST TAP/ADQL (JSON, CSV, VOTable)
- Relevance: Settles 'will the confirmed exoplanet count exceed N by D' and 'will an earth-analogue be confirmed by D' — the count is a single COUNT(*) query. Because confirmation lags detection by months and the TOI table is public, you can forecast the count curve with real accuracy.

**Crossref REST API** — Crossref `LIVE`

- Metadata for 186,763,093 registered DOIs (verified live count): journal articles, preprints, books, datasets, with title, authors with ORCID, publication and online dates, funder registry data, license, reference lists and citation counts. Funder-based querying makes grant-to-output tracing possible.
- Docs: https://api.crossref.org/swagger-ui/index.html
- Auth: none; a mailto in the User-Agent or query puts you in the higher-throughput polite pool; paid Plus tier for guaranteed rates | Limits: MEASURED LIVE from response headers on an anonymous request: X-Rate-Limit-Limit 1, X-Rate-Limit-Interval 1s — i.e. 1 request per second on the public pool. The polite pool (identify yourself with mailto) is documented as higher but Crossref does not publish a fixed number — UNKNOWN. Always read the live headers. History: complete DOI registry, 1900s to present. Full metadata torrent/snapshot available free.
- Latency: daily (registration is near-realtime; indexing lags hours) | Format: REST JSON + bulk snapshot
- Relevance: Settles publication-existence and retraction contracts, and supplies the denominators for research-output markets. Funder linkage settles 'will grant X produce a publication by D'.

**Semantic Scholar Academic Graph API** — Allen Institute for AI (AI2) `LIVE`

- 200M+ papers with the best-in-class citation graph, plus influentialCitationCount, tldr auto-summaries, SPECTER embeddings, author disambiguation, venue normalization, open-access PDF links, and a paper-recommendations endpoint. Both /paper/search and the cursor-paginated /paper/search/bulk verified live (383,055 hits on a transformer query). Full bulk datasets released periodically.
- Docs: https://api.semanticscholar.org/api-docs/
- Auth: none for the shared pool; free API key on request (form, human review, usually days) | Limits: CONFLICTING PUBLISHED FIGURES — report both. Current official overview (Aug 2026) states unauthenticated calls share a 1,000 requests-per-second POOL across all anonymous users and may be throttled at any time. Earlier release notes stated 5,000 requests per 5 minutes as the shared anonymous pool. An individual free API key gives a dedicated 1 request per second across all endpoints (occasionally raised on review). Treat the anonymous figure as UNKNOWN in practice — it is a shared pool, not a personal quota. History: complete, and full-corpus bulk snapshots are free with a key.
- Latency: daily to weekly | Format: REST JSON + bulk datasets
- Relevance: The influentialCitationCount and citation-velocity fields are the strongest free quantitative input to Nobel and prize-prediction models. Also prices 'will paper X exceed N citations by D' and identifies breakout AI papers before they trend.

**NIH RePORTER API v2** — US National Institutes of Health `LIVE`

- Every NIH-funded project: award amount, fiscal year, PI names with profile ids, organization, activity code, study section, abstract, public-health relevance statement, project start/end dates, and linked publications and patents. Verified live: 67,675 FY2026 projects. POST-only JSON criteria search with rich filters (agency, IC, fiscal year, org state, award type, text search across abstracts).
- Docs: https://api.reporter.nih.gov/
- Auth: none | Limits: No API key. Documented guidance: post no more than 1 URL request per second or NIH may block your IP. Maximum 500 records per call (limit param); offset caps at 9,999, so any single query can surface at most 10,000 records — partition by fiscal year or IC to get past it. Large jobs requested to run weekends or 21:00–05:00 EST. History: projects from FY1985 to present. Note: GET returns 405, you must POST.
- Latency: weekly to monthly | Format: REST JSON (POST)
- Relevance: Settles 'will NIH funding for X exceed $N in FY26', 'will program Y be funded/cut'. Award obligation dates are a leading indicator for US biomedical policy markets, and the linked-publication field ties funding to output for downstream research-productivity contracts.

- All NSF awards with award id, title, full abstract text, PI and co-PIs, awardee institution and state, program element and reference codes, obligated amount, start and expiration dates, and directorate. - Docs: https://resources.research.gov/common/webapi/awardapisearch-v1.htm
- Auth: none | Limits: No API key. Maximum 25 records per page (rpp param), paginated via offset. No published requests-per-minute limit — UNKNOWN. History: awards from 1959 to present.

- Relevance: Settles US federal science-funding contracts and 'will NSF fund a program in area X by D'. - Auth: none | Limits: No key. No published hard request cap — UNKNOWN; EBI asks for considerate use. Max 1,000 results per page, deep paging via nextCursorMark with no total depth limit. - USGS FDSN event service (verified live): every seismic event globally with magnitude, depth, location, origin time, felt reports, alert level (PAGER) and tsunami flag, in GeoJSON, queryable by magnitude/time/region, plus a 1-minute real-time GeoJSON summary feed. - Relevance: Settles 'will an M7+ earthquake occur by D' and volcanic/natural-disaster contracts directly, with the USGS magnitude as the named settlement value.
