History: complete, every list since June 1993. XML/Excel downloads have historically been offered per list but require checking each list page.
- Latency: twice yearly | Format: scrape-only
- Relevance: Settles 'will a system exceed N exaflops by D', 'will China/US hold the #1 spot in the November list', 'will an AI-specific system enter the top 10'. The twice-yearly cadence makes these clean date-bounded contracts, and the lack of an API means most participants are working from news summaries rather than the table.

**RocketLaunch.Live** — RocketLaunch.Live `LIVE`

- Independent second source on launch schedules — provider, vehicle, mission, pad, window, sort_date and quick-look status. Valuable specifically as a cross-check against Launch Library 2, since the two disagree on slip timing often enough to matter.
- Docs: https://www.rocketlaunch.live/api
- Auth: none for the free tier; paid key unlocks full result sets | Limits: Free anonymous tier returns exactly 5 launches per call (verified live: valid_auth false, count 5, limit 5). That is the hard cap without a key — no pagination past it. Paid tiers lift it. History depth on the free tier: next 5 launches only.
- Latency: minutely | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: USEFUL as a disagreement detector, not a primary. When LL2 and RocketLaunch.Live disagree on a T-0, that divergence is itself the signal that the date is unstable — which is exactly what a launch-by-date contract is pricing.

**Our World in Data (grapher CSV + indicators API)** — Our World in Data / Global Change Data Lab `LIVE`

- Thousands of harmonized long-run technology and science indicator series with country-year granularity: internet adoption, electricity access, R&D spending as share of GDP, researchers per million, patent applications, solar/battery cost curves, semiconductor trends. Verified live on both the /grapher/{slug}.csv download path and the api.ourworldindata.org/v1/indicators/{id}.data.json path.
- Docs: https://docs.owid.io/projects/etl/api/
- Auth: none | Limits: No key, no published rate limit — UNKNOWN. CSV downloads are unmetered. History: series run as far back as the underlying source allows, often to the 1800s. Note: catalog.ourworldindata.org root returns 404 and metadata paths only resolve for real indicator ids — you must look the id up first.
- Latency: monthly to annual (source-dependent) | Format: CSV bulk + REST JSON
- Relevance: Settles technology-adoption contracts ('will internet penetration in X exceed N% by D', 'will solar cost fall below $Y/W'). The long-run series are the right base rate for any diffusion-curve market — OWID is doing the harmonization work that would otherwise cost you weeks.

**GitHub REST API (releases, repos, activity)** — GitHub / Microsoft `LIVE`

- Release events, tags, commit activity and star velocity for every public repository — verified live against huggingface/transformers releases. For this domain it is the fastest confirmation that a model, framework version, or research codebase actually shipped, often hours before any announcement.
- Docs: https://docs.github.com/en/rest
- Auth: none for public reads; free personal access token raises limits enormously | Limits: Unauthenticated: 60 requests per hour per IP for the core REST API and 10 per minute for search — we hit exactly this ceiling during research, confirming it is enforced hard. Authenticated with a free PAT: 5,000 requests per hour core, 30 per minute search. GitHub Apps on a free org: 15,000/hour. History: complete repository history. Use a token; the anonymous tier is unusable for anything real.
- Latency: sub-minute — release webhooks and the events API are effectively realtime | Format: REST JSON + GraphQL + webhooks
- Relevance: Settles 'will project X ship version N by D' and open-source milestone contracts. More broadly it is the release-detection layer for AI markets: a tagged release plus a Hugging Face upload is the two-source confirmation that a model launched.

#### NICHE

**CERN Open Data Portal API** — CERN `LIVE`

- 82,385 records (verified live) of particle-physics datasets, software, documentation and educational resources from ATLAS, CMS, LHCb, ALICE, OPERA and PHENIX. Searchable by experiment, collision energy, year, data type and availability (51,957 online, 20,144 partial). Includes the actual collision datasets plus the analysis code to reproduce published results.
- Docs: https://opendata.cern.ch/docs/about-api
- Auth: none | Limits: No key, no published rate limit — UNKNOWN. History: LHC Run 1 and Run 2 data releases from 2013 onward, with a multi-year embargo before release. Faceted aggregations returned inline.
- Latency: monthly to annual (release-driven, not streaming) | Format: REST JSON (Invenio)
- Relevance: Thin for date-settled markets — CERN data releases lag discoveries by years. NICHE for 'will CERN publish data on X' and for grounding particle-physics discovery contracts. It does NOT carry live LHC status or luminosity, which is what a collider-milestone market would actually need.

**IETF Datatracker API** — Internet Engineering Task Force `LIVE`

- Every RFC and Internet-Draft with document state, working group, authors, revision history, ballot positions, IESG state changes and publication dates. The full standards-track pipeline is machine-readable: you can see a draft move from WG adoption to Last Call to RFC.
- Docs: https://datatracker.ietf.org/api/
- Auth: none | Limits: No key, no published rate limit — UNKNOWN. Tastypie-style REST with limit/offset. History: complete, RFC 1 (1969) to present.
- Latency: daily | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: Settles 'will RFC for protocol X be published by D' and internet-standards contracts. The IESG state field is a strong forward indicator — a document in 'Approved-announcement to be sent' will almost certainly publish within weeks, which prices the date contract for you.

**W3C API** — World Wide Web Consortium `LIVE`

- 1,713 specifications (verified live count) with their version history, maturity level (Working Draft / Candidate Recommendation / Proposed Recommendation / Recommendation), working groups, editors, and transition dates. Also groups, participants and translations.
- Docs: https://w3c.github.io/w3c-api/
- Auth: none observed on the specifications endpoint (historically an API key was required; our anonymous request returned HTTP 200) | Limits: No rate limit published — UNKNOWN. Paginated via items/page. History: complete W3C specification record.
- Latency: weekly to monthly | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: NICHE. Settles 'will spec X reach Recommendation by D'. Web-standards markets are rare but when they exist the maturity-level field is the exact settlement criterion.

**NASA Techport** — NASA `LIVE`

- Every NASA technology development project with project id, title, description, technology readiness level (start and current TRL), responsible center, program and directorate, funding, start/end dates, work locations, co-funding partners and library of deliverables. Verified live with projects updated 2026-09-18. updatedSince parameter gives a clean change feed.
- Docs: https://techport.nasa.gov/help/articles/api
- Auth: none for the public projects endpoint; api.nasa.gov key for the mirrored route | Limits: No key on techport.nasa.gov directly; through api.nasa.gov it inherits the 1,000/hr registered-key limit. No independent rate limit published — UNKNOWN. History: projects from 2010 to present.
- Latency: weekly to monthly | Format: REST JSON/XML
- Relevance: NICHE but genuinely predictive: the TRL field tells you how mature a NASA technology actually is, which prices 'will NASA demonstrate X by D' far better than press releases. Program cancellations show up here as end-date changes before they are announced.

**SIMBAD / VizieR / ESA Gaia TAP services** — CDS Strasbourg / ESA `LIVE`

- Three ADQL-queryable astronomical databases, all verified live. SIMBAD: identifiers, coordinates, object types, radial velocities and the full bibliography for ~13M objects beyond the solar system. VizieR: 20,000+ published astronomical catalogues as queryable tables. ESA Gaia Archive: DR3/DR4 astrometry, photometry and radial velocities for ~1.8 billion sources.
- Docs: https://simbad.cds.unistra.fr/simbad/sim-tap and https://gea.esac.esa.int/archive/
- Auth: none for anonymous sync/async queries; free ESA account raises Gaia async job quotas | Limits: No key. Sync queries capped by server-side timeout and row limits (use TOP N); async jobs for large extractions. No published requests-per-minute figure — UNKNOWN. Gaia anonymous async jobs have a smaller row/storage quota than registered users (exact figure UNKNOWN). History: SIMBAD bibliography from 1850; Gaia DR3 epoch 2016.0.
- Latency: weekly to per-data-release (Gaia DRs are years apart) | Format: REST TAP/ADQL (JSON, CSV, VOTable)
- Relevance: NICHE for date-settled markets, but these are the ground truth for 'is object X actually a new discovery' disputes and for settling stellar-parameter and astrometric contracts. SIMBAD's bibliography count is a usable novelty test.

**Nobel-adjacent scholarly infrastructure: ORCID, ROR, DOAJ, OpenAIRE, CORE, Figshare** — ORCID Inc / ROR / DOAJ / OpenAIRE / Jisc / Digital Science `LIVE`

- Six free services, all verified live in one pass, that together let you resolve and enrich any researcher or institution. ORCID public API: researcher records with works, employments, educations and funding. ROR: 134,298 research organizations with canonical ids, aliases and relationships. DOAJ: 94,098+ open-access articles searchable. OpenAIRE: EU-funded research outputs with project linkage (covers ERC and Horizon, which NIH/NSF feeds miss). CORE v3: 6.5M+ aggregated open-access full texts. Figshare: datasets, figures and supplementary materials with DOIs.
- Docs: https://info.orcid.org/documentation/api-tutorials/, https://ror.readme.io/, https://doaj.org/api/docs, https://graph.openaire.eu/develop/, https://api.core.ac.uk/docs/v3, https://docs.figshare.com/
- Auth: ORCID public API: none for public records. ROR: none. DOAJ: none for search. OpenAIRE: none for basic search. CORE: free API key documented (our anonymous call returned results anyway — treat anonymous access as unreliable). Figshare: none for public reads. | Limits: ORCID public: 24 requests/second burst, 40 requests/second sustained (documented). ROR: no published limit — UNKNOWN; 10,000 requests/day is the commonly cited soft cap. DOAJ: 2 requests/second (documented soft limit). OpenAIRE: 7,200 requests/hour anonymous, higher with a free token. CORE: free tier documented at 10,000 tokens/day and 10 requests/minute with a registered key. Figshare: no published limit — UNKNOWN. History: all complete from each service's inception.
- Latency: daily | Format: REST JSON/XML
- Relevance: Supporting infrastructure rather than direct settlement. ROR and ORCID are how you deduplicate 'the same researcher' across arXiv, OpenAlex, NIH and Nobel data — without that join your prize-prediction model is counting the same person three times. OpenAIRE is the only free EU research-funding feed here.

#### Repos

- `r-spacex/SpaceX-API` — The 10,913-star community SpaceX REST API. ARCHIVED by its owner on 2026-06-06; api.spacexdata.com now fails with a TLS 525 error. · Do NOT build on the live endpoint — it is dead. The repo still has value as a self-hostable historical SpaceX dataset (launches, cores, capsules, Starlink, landpads) up to its maintenance freeze, and the schema is worth copying if you model launch data yourself.
- `TheSpaceDevs/Tutorials` — Official tutorials and FAQ for the Launch Library 2 API from the maintainers. · Documents the filtering, pagination and 'mode=detailed/normal/list' response modes that are not obvious from the endpoint alone — critical for staying inside the 15-requests-per-hour free cap.
- `skyfielders/python-skyfield` — 1,769-star precision astronomy library for Python — positions of planets, satellites and stars from JPL ephemerides and TLEs. · Turns a CelesTrak TLE into an actual predicted position or reentry estimate. This is how you price a decay or visibility market yourself instead of waiting for someone to publish the answer.
- `brandon-rhodes/python-sgp4` — 470-star reference implementation of the SGP4/SDP4 orbital propagator, the same algorithm the TLE format is designed for. · The propagation core underneath Skyfield. Use it directly for high-volume batch propagation of the full CelesTrak catalog when you need constellation-wide counts rather than single-object precision.
- `thkruz/ootk-core` — Modern typed TypeScript orbital-object toolkit — SGP4 propagation and TLE parsing, a maintained replacement for satellite.js. · The right choice if the research panel does orbital math in the browser rather than server-side. Typed, so the TLE field semantics are enforced at compile time.
- `astropy/astroquery` — 792-star Astropy-affiliated package with unified clients for 50+ astronomical archives — SIMBAD, VizieR, Gaia, MPC, JPL Horizons, NASA ADS, IRSA, ESO and more. · One dependency replaces a dozen hand-rolled clients for the astronomy feeds in this catalog. It already handles each archive's pagination, timeouts and result-format quirks, which is most of the work.
- `lukasschwab/arxiv.py` — 1,545-star Python wrapper for the arXiv API with a Client class that enforces the request delay. · It implements arXiv's mandatory 3-second-per-request rate limit and single-connection rule for you. Rolling your own is the fastest way to get IP-blocked from arXiv.
- `J535D165/pyalex` — 413-star Python client for OpenAlex covering works, authors, sources, institutions, concepts and funders with cursor pagination. · Handles the cursor paging and polite-pool conventions. Verify it has been updated for the February 2026 credit-budget change — the old polite-pool logic is now obsolete and the library may still assume the retired 100k/day model.
- `ourresearch/openalex-api-tutorials` — 148-star collection of Jupyter notebooks from the OpenAlex team walking through real bibliometric analyses. · Contains the actual query patterns for citation-percentile and institutional-ranking computations — which is exactly the analysis a Nobel-prediction model needs, already written.
- `paperswithcode/paperswithcode-data` — 941-star full data export behind the now-dead paperswithcode.com — papers, methods, datasets and evaluation/leaderboard tables as JSON. · The only surviving structured archive of PWC's task-by-task SOTA leaderboards, which the Hugging Face successor did not replicate. Essential as the historical baseline for 'has benchmark X been beaten' markets — the live site sunset in July 2025 and now redirects to huggingface.co/papers/trending.
- `nasa-gcn/gcn-kafka-python` — Official NASA Python client for the General Coordinates Network Kafka streams. · GCN has no usable public REST endpoint (we confirmed /api/circulars returns 400 and circulars.json returns 404), so this client is effectively the only supported programmatic path to real-time GRB, gravitational-wave and neutrino alerts.
- `nasa/api-docs` — 554-star source for api.nasa.gov, including assets/json/apis.json — the machine-readable catalog of all 16 NASA APIs. · Fetch apis.json directly (raw.githubusercontent.com/nasa/api-docs/gh-pages/assets/json/apis.json, verified live) to enumerate every NASA endpoint programmatically rather than scraping the portal page.
- `nasa/apod-api` — 1,085-star reference implementation of the Astronomy Picture of the Day service. · Shows how NASA's api.data.gov passthrough layer actually works, which explains the rate-limit header behavior you will hit across all NASA endpoints.
- `earthaccess-dev/earthaccess` — 643-star Python library for NASA Earthdata — wraps CMR search plus authenticated data access and cloud-direct S3 reads. · Removes the Earthdata Login OAuth dance and handles CMR's 2,000-result page cap and search-after paging. The only practical way to pull NASA Earth-observation granules at volume.
- `nasa/Common-Metadata-Repository` — 397-star source of the CMR itself. · The authoritative reference for CMR's query parameters and UMM schema when the public docs are ambiguous about a field's semantics.
- `ropensci/patentsview` — 39-star rOpenSci R client for PatentsView, which shipped a breaking release in March 2026. · Read its api-changes vignette and that breaking-release note — it is the clearest public account of the PatentsView-to-USPTO-ODP migration, including that old PatentSearch API keys do not work against ODP.
- `huggingface/huggingface_hub` — 3,916-star official Python client and CLI for the Hugging Face Hub. · HfApi.list_models with sort='createdAt' or 'trendingScore' is the cleanest model-release detector available, and the client handles the Hub's pagination and token auth.
- `juliensimon/space-datasets` — 200+ auto-updated space, astronomy and physics datasets published on Hugging Face, aggregated from NASA, NOAA, ESA, JPL, SpaceX and Wikidata. · Someone has already built the ingestion for a large slice of this catalog and refreshes it automatically. Worth reading the collection pipeline before writing your own — and worth using directly for backfill.
- `tcarwash/swpclib` — Small Python wrapper for the NOAA SWPC product endpoints. · SWPC's JSON paths are undocumented and unstable — several well-known paths returned 404 during our checks (solar-wind/mag-1-day.json, goes/primary/xrays-1-day.json). This library encodes the paths that currently work, saving a lot of trial and error.
- `corincerami/mars-photo-api` — 399-star Rails API serving NASA Mars rover photo data (the service behind the Mars Rover Photos API). · Self-hostable if you need rover imagery without consuming your api.nasa.gov hourly quota; also a clean example of wrapping a NASA data source as a stable API.
- `ourresearch/openalex-guts` — 157-star internals of OpenAlex — the code that computes the graph. · Definitive answer to how OpenAlex derives citation counts, author disambiguation and topic assignment. If you are building a prize-prediction model on their numbers, you need to know how they were made.

---

### Transport, Logistics & Supply Chain

#### CORE

**IMF PortWatch — Chokepoint Transit Calls & Trade Volume** — International Monetary Fund / UN Global Platform / Oxford `LIVE`

- Daily transit call counts and estimated transit trade volume (cargo, tanker, container, dry bulk, general cargo) for 28 global maritime chokepoints including Suez, Panama, Bab el-Mandeb, Hormuz, Malacca, Gibraltar, Bosphorus, Cape of Good Hope. Derived from satellite AIS on ~90k ships. Daily granularity, history back to 1 Jan 2019.
- Docs: https://portwatch.imf.org/pages/data-and-methodology
- Auth: none | Limits: No API key, no registration, no published call quota. ArcGIS FeatureServer default paging caps a single query at 1,000-2,000 records; use resultOffset to page. Data refresh: weekly, Tuesdays 09:00 ET (daily observations delivered in a weekly batch, so there is a lag of up to 7 days on the most recent day). History depth: 2019-01-01 to present. Per-call quota: UNKNOWN (none published).
- Latency: daily (observations) delivered weekly | Format: REST JSON (ArcGIS FeatureServer query), plus CSV/GeoJSON/KML bulk download
- Relevance: The single best free instrument for 'will Suez/Panama/Hormuz transits exceed N', 'will Red Sea diversions continue', 'will Cape of Good Hope routings stay elevated' contracts. Directly resolves chokepoint-volume markets and is a leading indicator for container-rate and port-congestion contracts.

**IMF PortWatch — Daily Port Activity (2,065 ports)** — International Monetary Fund / UN Global Platform `LIVE`

- Daily port call counts and estimated import/export trade volumes by cargo type for 2,065 ports worldwide, with port metadata (name, country, lat/lon, industry share). Same satellite-AIS backbone as the chokepoint dataset.
- Docs: https://portwatch.imf.org/pages/port-monitor
- Auth: none | Limits: No API key. ArcGIS FeatureServer paging limit 1,000-2,000 records per query. Refresh weekly Tuesdays 09:00 ET. History 2019-01-01 to present. No published rate limit — UNKNOWN.
- Latency: daily (observations) delivered weekly | Format: REST JSON (ArcGIS FeatureServer), CSV/GeoJSON bulk
- Relevance: Prices port-throughput and congestion contracts (LA/Long Beach, Rotterdam, Shanghai, Singapore), and 'will country X exports exceed Y' when official customs data lags 6-8 weeks. Free daily port-call proxy for trade that otherwise costs six figures.

**OpenSky Network REST API** — OpenSky Network (ETH Zurich / community ADS-B) `LIVE`

- Live aircraft state vectors globally (ICAO24, callsign, lat/lon, baro+geo altitude, velocity, heading, vertical rate, squawk, on-ground flag), plus flights by airport (arrivals/departures), flights by aircraft, and full trajectory tracks.
- Docs: https://openskynetwork.github.io/opensky-api/rest.html
- Auth: none for anonymous (reduced quota); free OAuth2 client-credentials for registered users | Limits: Anonymous: 400 credits/day, most-recent state vectors only (time parameter ignored), 10-second resolution. Registered (free account + API client): 4,000 credits/day, state vectors up to 1 hour in the past, 5-second resolution. Active ADS-B feeders: 8,000 credits/day. /states/all costs 1-4 credits depending on bounding-box area (>400 sq deg = 4 credits). /flights/* and /tracks/* cost 4x-960x depending on day partitions queried. Tracks limited to 30 days in the past. Flights data is batch-updated nightly (previous day or earlier). Access tokens expire after 30 minutes. BREAKING CHANGE: HTTP basic auth was retired 18 March 2026 — OAuth2 client credentials only.
- Latency: realtime (5-10s resolution) | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: Prices 'will flight X operate', aircraft-movement, sanctions-evasion-flight, VIP/government aircraft, and military-airlift-surge contracts. Airport arrival/departure counts give a free independent check on airline capacity and disruption markets. Also the cheapest live read on airspace closures.

**adsb.fi Open Data API** — adsb.fi (volunteer ADS-B feeder network) `LIVE`

- Unauthenticated live ADS-B aircraft data, ADSBexchange-v2-compatible schema: query by hex, ICAO, callsign, registration, squawk, military-only filter, or geographic radius up to 250 NM. Rich fields (alt_baro, alt_geom, gs, ias, tas, mach, track, baro_rate, squawk, wind, OAT).
- Docs: https://github.com/adsbfi/opendata
- Auth: none | Limits: Public endpoints: 1 request per second, no API key, no registration. Feeder-only /v2/snapshot endpoint (all aircraft, twice per minute): 1 request per 30 seconds, granted automatically by receiver IP. Personal / NON-COMMERCIAL use only, attribution with link required. Invalid requests (400/401/403/404/429) can trigger temporary IP bans. No history — live snapshot only.
- Latency: realtime | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: The best surviving free drop-in replacement for the old ADS-B Exchange API, including the military-aircraft filter that prices geopolitical/airlift markets. 1 req/s is enough to poll a dozen airports or conflict zones continuously. Commercial-use restriction is the binding constraint for a paid terminal.

**adsb.lol API** — adsb.lol (open-source volunteer ADS-B network) `LIVE`

- Unauthenticated live ADS-B aircraft data on an ADSBexchange-v2-compatible schema (/v2/lat/{lat}/lon/{lon}/dist/{nm}, plus hex/callsign/registration/squawk/mil endpoints). Open-source, ODbL-licensed feeder network.
- Docs: https://api.adsb.lol/docs
- Auth: none | Limits: No API key, no registration. Exact published rate limit: UNKNOWN (OpenAPI docs at /docs respond but do not state a hard numeric quota; community convention is ~1 req/s). No historical depth via this API — live snapshot only; separate daily bulk ADS-B archives are published on GitHub/HuggingFace.
- Latency: realtime | Format: REST JSON (OpenAPI/Swagger documented)
- Relevance: Redundancy partner to adsb.fi — running both removes single-point-of-failure risk on live aviation contracts. More permissive licensing (ODbL) than adsb.fi, which matters for a commercial terminal.

**FAA National Airspace System Status (NASSTATUS)** — US Federal Aviation Administration `LIVE`

- Live US airport delay state: Ground Stop Programs (airport, reason, end time), Ground Delay Programs, Arrival/Departure delays with average delay minutes and trend, airport closures, and airport-specific weather. Reason codes include WEATHER, STAFFING, VOLUME, EQUIPMENT, RUNWAY.
- Docs: https://nasstatus.faa.gov/
- Auth: none | Limits: No API key, no registration. No published rate limit — UNKNOWN. This endpoint is UNDOCUMENTED/UNOFFICIAL: the FAA does not publish it as a supported public API, so it can change or disappear without notice. No history — current snapshot only (poll and store your own history). Verified 2026-09-21: HTTP 200, application/xml, 3.6KB, live Update_Time and an active TEB ground stop for STAFFING.
- Latency: sub-minute to minutely | Format: REST XML (https://nasstatus.faa.gov/api/airport-status-information)
- Relevance: Directly resolves 'will there be a ground stop at EWR/LGA/JFK today', 'will ATC staffing cause delays during the shutdown', and airline-cancellation contracts. The STAFFING reason code in particular is the live tape for government-shutdown and controller-staffing markets. Highest signal-per-byte free feed in US aviation.

**UN Comtrade API** — United Nations Statistics Division `LIVE`

- Bilateral merchandise trade by reporter, partner, HS commodity code, flow (import/export/re-export), annual and monthly, in USD value, net weight and supplementary quantity. Covers ~200 reporters back to 1962.
- Docs: https://comtradedeveloper.un.org/
- Auth: none for the public preview endpoint; free API key (registration) for the full endpoint | Limits: Public preview endpoint (comtradeapi.un.org/public/v1/preview/...) works with NO key and is capped at 500 records per call. Free registered key tier is documented at 500 calls/day with 100,000 records per call — that figure comes from UN Comtrade documentation and was NOT independently verified in this session. History: 1962-present annual, monthly where reported. Reporting lag: 2-12 months depending on country. Verified 2026-09-21: preview endpoint returned HTTP 200, 223 rows, 200KB JSON with no key.
- Latency: monthly (with multi-month reporting lag) | Format: REST JSON, bulk file download
- Relevance: Ground truth for tariff-impact, export-control, and bilateral-trade contracts ('will China-US goods trade fall below $X', 'will Taiwan semiconductor exports exceed Y'). The lag makes it a resolution source rather than a live pricing source — pair with PortWatch for the nowcast.

**US Census International Trade API (incl. port-level)** — US Census Bureau Foreign Trade Division `LIVE`

- US monthly imports and exports by HS/NAICS commodity, country, district and PORT of entry (porths/portnaics endpoints), with value, quantity, shipping weight, vessel/air/containerized breakouts. Port-level detail is the key differentiator over Comtrade.
- Docs: https://www.census.gov/data/developers/data-sets/international-trade.html
- Auth: free API key (email registration) | Limits: Up to 500 queries per IP address per day WITHOUT a key; with a free key the documented cap is effectively unlimited for normal use (no published hard number — UNKNOWN). History: monthly from 2013 for the timeseries endpoints, earlier via bulk. Release lag ~5 weeks after month end. Verified 2026-09-21: api.census.gov responded HTTP 200 and served the official 'Missing Key' page, confirming the service is live and key-gated.
- Latency: monthly (≈5-week lag) | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: Port-of-entry granularity lets you price 'will LA/Long Beach import value exceed $X' and tariff front-running contracts that no other free source resolves. Also the official resolution source for US trade-deficit markets.

**FRED API (Federal Reserve Economic Data)** — Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis `LIVE`

- Hundreds of thousands of series including truck tonnage index (TRUCKD11), rail freight carloads (RAILFRTCARLOADSD11), intermodal traffic, air revenue passenger miles, inventories-to-sales ratios, manufacturing and trade inventories, port throughput series, jet fuel and diesel prices, and mirrors of the NY Fed GSCPI. Full revision history via ALFRED.
- Docs: https://fred.stlouisfed.org/docs/api/fred/
- Auth: free API key (registration) | Limits: Free key. Documented rate limit 120 requests per minute per key. No daily cap published. History: full series history, typically decades; vintage/as-of-date queries available via ALFRED. Verified 2026-09-21: api.stlouisfed.org returned HTTP 400 with 'Variable api_key is not set' — service live, key-gated.
- Latency: monthly / weekly depending on series | Format: REST JSON/XML
- Relevance: The cheapest universal resolution layer for macro-logistics contracts: truck tonnage, rail carloads, inventory/sales ratios. Because FRED carries the official published series, it is usually the literal resolution source named in contract rules.

**NY Fed Global Supply Chain Pressure Index (GSCPI)** — Federal Reserve Bank of New York `LIVE`

- Monthly composite index of global supply-chain pressure built from cross-border transportation costs (Baltic Dry, Harpex, BLS air freight) and PMI supply-chain subcomponents for seven economies, normalized to standard deviations from average. Full monthly history from 1997.
- Docs: https://www.newyorkfed.org/research/policy/gscpi
- Auth: none | Limits: No key, no registration, direct file download. No rate limit published — UNKNOWN (it is a static XLSX, poll monthly). History: 1997-09 to present, monthly, revised each release. Verified 2026-09-21: gscpi_data.xlsx returned HTTP 200, 106KB, application/vnd.ms-excel.
- Latency: monthly | Format: XLSX bulk download (also mirrored as FRED series)
- Relevance: The named resolution source for 'will supply chain pressure exceed N standard deviations' contracts, and the standard normalizer for any composite disruption score you build. Being a Fed publication, it is contract-grade.

**AIS Stream (aisstream.io)** — AISStream `LIVE`

- Real-time global AIS vessel messages over WebSocket — position reports, static and voyage data (destination, ETA, draught), ship type, navigation status — filterable by bounding box and MMSI.
- Docs: https://aisstream.io/documentation
- Auth: free API key (registration) | Limits: Free API key. Concurrency limits: 3 subscribed connections per account, 3 open connections per IP, subscription message must arrive within 3 seconds of connect, 1 subscription update per second per connection. No message-volume cap published — UNKNOWN. NO historical replay: events are not durably replayed and there is NO SLA or uptime guarantee. Direct browser connections prohibited — must proxy through your own server. Verified 2026-09-21: documentation live, © 2026.
- Latency: realtime/websocket | Format: WebSocket JSON
- Relevance: The only genuinely free realtime global AIS stream with no hardware requirement. Feeds live chokepoint counting, port-queue building, and Red Sea / sanctioned-tanker tracking before PortWatch's weekly batch catches up. The no-SLA caveat means you must pair it with a second source for contract-grade claims.

**STB Rail Service Data (Surface Transportation Board)** — US Surface Transportation Board `LIVE`

- Mandatory weekly filings from Class I railroads: average train speed by train type, terminal dwell by terminal, cars on line, loaded and empty car counts, trains holding for crew/power/other, grain car order fulfillment, and Chicago gateway interchange performance. Also service recovery plans during disruptions.
- Docs: https://www.stb.gov/reports-data/rail-service-data/
- Auth: none | Limits: No key, no registration — direct file downloads (XLSX/CSV) from the STB site. No rate limit published — UNKNOWN (static files, poll weekly). History: weekly filings archived back to 2014 (EP 724 reporting). Release: weekly, typically Wednesday. Verified 2026-09-21: page returned HTTP 200, 1.8MB.
- Latency: weekly | Format: XLSX/CSV bulk download (no JSON API — scrape the file links)
- Relevance: Prices US rail-strike, rail-service-crisis and grain-shipping contracts with regulator-filed numbers rather than press releases. Train speed and terminal dwell are the standard 'is the network melting down' metrics that rail-disruption contracts are written on.

**BTS data.bts.gov (Socrata) + TranStats bulk** — US Bureau of Transportation Statistics `LIVE`

- Airline On-Time Performance (every scheduled domestic flight: scheduled vs actual departure/arrival, delay minutes by cause — carrier, weather, NAS, security, late aircraft — cancellations and diversions), Amtrak on-time performance, freight transportation services index, border crossing/entry counts, port cargo tonnage, and North American transborder freight by mode.
- Docs: https://data.bts.gov/ and https://www.transtats.bts.gov/
- Auth: none for Socrata reads; free Socrata app token recommended | Limits: Socrata (data.bts.gov): anonymous reads work but are throttled on a shared pool; a free app token raises you to a per-token pool. Socrata's standard documented limit is 1,000 requests per rolling hour per app token — NOT independently verified for this host in this session. Default page size 1,000 rows, $limit max 50,000 per request with $offset paging. History: monthly on-time performance back to 1987 via TranStats bulk ZIP/CSV. Release lag ~2 months. Verified 2026-09-21: data.bts.gov catalog API returned HTTP 200, 32KB, and surfaced the Amtrak On-Time Performance dataset (id 98fi-ujit).
- Latency: monthly (≈2-month lag); TranStats bulk monthly | Format: REST JSON (Socrata SoQL), CSV/ZIP bulk
- Relevance: The official resolution source for 'will airline X's on-time rate exceed Y', 'will cancellations exceed N%', and delay-cause attribution contracts. The 2-month lag means it resolves markets rather than prices them — use FAA NASSTATUS for the live leg.

**Panama Canal Authority (ACP) transit and restriction notices** — Autoridad del Canal de Panamá

- Daily booked and unbooked transit slot counts, maximum authorized draft (TFW) and its changes, Gatun Lake water level, vessel waiting times northbound/southbound, transit auction results and slot prices, and Advisories to Shipping announcing restriction changes.
- Docs: https://pancanal.com/en/maritime-services/vessel-eta-and-transit-booking/ and https://pancanal.com/en/advisories/
- Auth: none | Limits: No API exists. Data is published as HTML pages, PDF Advisories to Shipping, and the Canal Operations Summary — all free and unauthenticated, but you must scrape or parse PDFs. No rate limit published — UNKNOWN. Update cadence: advisories as issued, waiting times daily. Historical archive of advisories available on site. NOT VERIFIED LIVE in this session — only secondary reporting on 2026 transit caps (34/day from 4 Sep, 32/day from 15 Sep 2026) was confirmed.
- Latency: daily | Format: scrape-only (HTML + PDF advisories)
- Relevance: CORE by importance despite being scrape-only: Panama draft restrictions and daily slot counts are the literal resolution criteria for canal-capacity and slot-auction-price contracts, and drive Asia-US East Coast container rate markets. Cross-check with IMF PortWatch chokepoint transits, which IS an API.

#### USEFUL

**Amtrak live train tracking (Amtraker v3)** — Amtraker (community reverse-engineered Amtrak track-a-train API) `LIVE`

- Live positions of every active Amtrak train: lat/lon, train number, route name, heading, speed, plus full station list per train with scheduled vs estimated arrival/departure, delay status and service disruption flags.
- Docs: https://api-v3.amtraker.com/v3/docs
- Auth: none | Limits: No API key, no registration. No published rate limit — UNKNOWN. Community-run and UNOFFICIAL — Amtrak does not sanction it and it can break when Amtrak changes its internal API. No historical archive — live snapshot only. Verified 2026-09-21: /v3/trains returned HTTP 200 with 1.19MB of live train JSON.
- Latency: realtime (roughly minutely refresh) | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: Live leg for US passenger-rail disruption contracts and Northeast Corridor service markets, where BTS on-time data arrives two months late. Also a usable proxy for regional weather/infrastructure disruption.

**Eurostat dissemination API** — European Commission / Eurostat `LIVE`

- EU harmonized transport and trade statistics: road freight transport (tonnes, tonne-km, vehicle-km), rail freight and passenger volumes, maritime port cargo and passenger throughput by port, air transport of passengers and freight by airport, inland waterway freight, and Comext bilateral trade by HS code.
- Docs: https://wikis.ec.europa.eu/display/EUROSTATHELP/API+-+Getting+started+with+statistics+API
- Auth: none | Limits: No API key, no registration. No published hard rate limit — UNKNOWN (Eurostat asks for reasonable use; very large extracts should use bulk download). Response size cap: a single query is limited to roughly 1,000,000 cells. History: varies by dataset, typically 2000-present annual/quarterly, some monthly. Verified 2026-09-21: road_go_ta_tott returned HTTP 200, 37KB JSON-stat, 'updated':'2026-07-30'.
- Latency: monthly to annual depending on dataset | Format: REST JSON-stat 2.0, SDMX, TSV bulk
- Relevance: Resolution source for European freight-volume, port-throughput and air-cargo contracts. The only free harmonized cross-EU dataset — national statistics offices are not comparable to each other without it.

**NOAA Marine Cadastre — bulk historical AIS** — NOAA Office for Coastal Management / BOEM / US Coast Guard `LIVE`

- Complete terrestrial AIS message archive for US waters and EEZ — every vessel position, MMSI, vessel type, length, draft, cargo code, status — as daily CSV files. This is the raw material for building your own historical port-queue, anchorage-dwell and transit-count series.
- Docs: https://hub.marinecadastre.gov/pages/vesseltraffic
- Auth: none | Limits: No key, no registration — open HTTP directory of daily CSV/ZIP files. No rate limit published — UNKNOWN. History: 2009 to roughly present (typically a 6-18 month lag on the newest year). Volume is large — each day is hundreds of MB; a full year is multi-TB uncompressed. US waters ONLY (terrestrial receivers, no satellite AIS, so open-ocean coverage is absent). Verified 2026-09-21: coast.noaa.gov 2023 index returned HTTP 200 with the CSV file listing.
- Latency: daily files, published with a 6-18 month lag | Format: CSV bulk download (also GeoPackage/raster derivatives)
- Relevance: Not a live feed — it is the free backtest corpus. You cannot calibrate a port-congestion or chokepoint model against live AIS alone; this is how you compute historical base rates and station-level error that a research panel needs to show alongside a forecast.

**Global Fishing Watch API v3** — Global Fishing Watch (Oceana / SkyTruth / Google) `LIVE`

- Vessel identity search across AIS self-reported data plus public regional and national registries; AIS-based apparent fishing effort and vessel presence rasters; vessel encounters, loitering events, port visits, and AIS gap (dark vessel) events; marine protected area boundaries.
- Docs: https://globalfishingwatch.org/our-apis/documentation/docs/license-rate-limits
- Auth: free API token (registration); non-commercial license | Limits: 50,000 requests per day and 1,500,000 requests per month, enforced at USER level across all tokens (max 5 tokens per user). Exceeding returns HTTP 429 and blocks for 24 hours (daily cap) or 30 days (monthly cap). Per-minute limit: UNKNOWN (not published). Rate-limit headers returned on every response. History: AIS-derived events from 2012 to present. LICENSE CONSTRAINT: free for non-commercial use only — academic research, NGOs, public good. Commercial use requires separate agreement.
- Latency: daily (events typically 1-3 day lag) | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: The best free source for sanctioned-vessel and dark-fleet contracts: AIS gap events and loitering/encounter detections are exactly what 'will shadow-fleet tanker activity increase' markets are written on. Port-visit events are a free cross-check on PortWatch. The non-commercial license is a hard blocker for a paid terminal.

**FAA NOTAM API** — US Federal Aviation Administration `LIVE`

- Notices to Air Missions in ICAO and AIXM format: runway and taxiway closures, navaid outages, airspace restrictions (TFRs), obstacle notices, GPS interference and jamming notices, and airport service changes, queryable by ICAO location, coordinates, effective date range or NOTAM type.
- Docs: https://api.faa.gov/s/
- Auth: free API key (registration via FAA developer portal; client_id + client_secret headers) | Limits: Free registration. Exact published quota: UNKNOWN — the FAA developer portal does not publish a numeric calls/day or calls/minute limit for the NOTAM API. Default page size 50 records, max 1,000 per request with pagination. History: active and recently expired NOTAMs; long-term archive not provided. Verified 2026-09-21: external-api.faa.gov/notamapi/v1/notams returned HTTP 401 {'message':'Unauthorized'} — service live and key-gated.
- Latency: sub-minute (NOTAMs publish continuously) | Format: REST JSON (AIXM/ICAO NOTAM schema)
- Relevance: Prices airport-closure, runway-outage, GPS-jamming and temporary-flight-restriction contracts, and gives early warning on airspace closures during conflicts before news reports them. GPS interference NOTAMs are a distinctive geopolitical signal.

**FAA SWIM Cloud Distribution Service (SCDS)** — US Federal Aviation Administration

- Near-realtime streaming FAA operational data over Solace JMS/AMQP: SFDPS (flight data — flight plans, departures, arrivals, cancellations), TFMS/TFMData (traffic flow management — ground stops, ground delay programs, airspace flow programs, reroutes), TBFM (time-based flow management), ITWS and STDDS (surface/terminal weather and surveillance), and AIM (aeronautical information).
- Docs: https://www.faa.gov/air_traffic/technology/swim/products/get_connected
- Auth: free registration + signed Service Access Agreement (SWIFT Portal account); no payment | Limits: Free of charge but NOT instant — you must register on the SWIFT Portal and execute a Service Access Agreement, and each data product subscription is individually approved. Onboarding typically takes days to weeks. All SCDS products are pre-approved by the NAS Data Release Board for public, NON-OPERATIONAL use. Message-volume limits: UNKNOWN (not published; SFDPS is high-volume — expect millions of messages per day). History: streaming only, no replay — you must persist it yourself.
- Latency: realtime (streaming JMS) | Format: Solace JMS / AMQP message stream (FIXM/AIXM/WXXM XML payloads)
- Relevance: The authoritative upstream of everything NASSTATUS shows, with far more detail: you see ground delay programs being issued with their exact parameters rather than a summary page. For serious US aviation-delay market making this is the real feed; NASSTATUS is the consolation prize. The access-agreement friction and non-operational-use clause are the catches.

**TomTom Traffic APIs (Flow + Incidents)** — TomTom `LIVE`

- Real-time traffic flow segment data (current speed, free-flow speed, current travel time, confidence) and traffic incidents (accidents, closures, jams, roadworks) with geometry, delay magnitude and category, plus Traffic Stats for historical analysis.
- Docs: https://developer.tomtom.com/traffic-api/documentation/product-information/introduction
- Auth: free API key (registration) | Limits: Free tier: 2,500 non-tile requests per day and 50,000 tile requests per day, shared across ALL TomTom APIs on the key. Overages are BLOCKED, not billed, unless you add prepaid credit. Pricing was revised effective July 2026 — confirm current terms on the portal. History: live flow/incidents only on the free tier; Traffic Stats (historical) is a separate paid product. Verified 2026-09-21: api.tomtom.com returned HTTP 401 'You are missing valid authentication credentials' — service live and key-gated.
- Latency: sub-minute | Format: REST JSON/XML, vector/raster tiles
- Relevance: Prices road-congestion, border-crossing-wait and 'will highway X reopen' contracts, and gives a live read on evacuation and protest-blockade traffic. 2,500 calls/day is tight — enough for a fixed watchlist of corridors, not for broad sweeps.

NOT VERIFIED LIVE in this session — 2026 figures (9,602 vessels in Jan-Aug 2026, +17.3% y/y; 1,358 vessels and $567.1M in Aug 2026) were confirmed only through secondary reporting.

- Weekly composite spot freight rate in USD per 40ft container across eight major East-West trade routes, published every Thursday, with per-route detail (Shanghai-Rotterdam, Shanghai-LA, etc.). Plus the Cancelled Sailings Tracker (blank sailings by trade lane) and Port Throughput Indices.

There is NO official public API and no documented free programmatic access — retrieval is scraping the weekly page. No rate limit published — UNKNOWN. History on the free viewer: typically rolling ~1-5 years on the chart; full history is a paid subscription. NOT VERIFIED LIVE in this session.
- Latency: weekly (Thursdays) | Format: scrape-only (web viewer; CSV export is paid)
- Relevance: WCI is one of the two most-cited container rate benchmarks and is frequently named in contract resolution language for freight-rate markets. Blank-sailings counts are the best free leading indicator of a rate spike. Scrape-only status is the friction.

Free access is limited to viewing the index on the public web page. No numeric free quota exists — N/A. - Relevance: FBX is the other major container-rate benchmark alongside Drewry WCI and is daily rather than weekly, making it the better pricing feed — if you can get it. Free access is scrape-only, which is fragile for a production terminal. Budget for the enterprise feed if container-rate markets matter.

- Relevance: Gives you the dependency graph — which country and which firm controls each chokepoint input (EUV, photoresist, neon, HBM, advanced packaging). EXCLUDED on free: historical flight data, airline routes, autocomplete, flight schedules, future flights. No support. NON-COMMERCIAL use only. Verified 2026-09-21 on the product page.
- Latency: minutely (varies by route) | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: Effectively useless at 100 calls/month — that is three calls a day. Listed only so it is not mistaken for a viable free flight feed. Use OpenSky + adsb.fi + BTS instead; they give more data for free with far higher quotas.

**AISHub** — AISHub (cooperative AIS data-sharing network) `LIVE`

- Aggregated real-time AIS feed from 1,500+ volunteer receiver stations across 80+ countries — vessel positions, MMSI, IMO, callsign, ship type, navigational status, destination, ETA, draught — plus station metadata.
- Docs: https://www.aishub.net/api
- Auth: free username, but ONLY granted to members who operate and stream from a physical AIS receiver | Limits: Polling limit: no more often than once per minute — the web service returns nothing if called more frequently. No monetary cost and no pay-for-access tier at any price. HARD BARRIER: you must operate an AIS receiver and stream a raw NMEA feed to AISHub over UDP; credentials are granted only once your feed demonstrates coverage of at least ~10 vessels and ~90% uptime over a rolling 7 days with message delay under 10 seconds. Applications without an operational station are not approved. Coverage is terrestrial only (no satellite AIS). Verified 2026-09-21: /api docs page live.
- Latency: minutely (1 req/min ceiling) | Format: REST XML / JSON / CSV, optional ZIP/GZIP/BZIP2 compression
- Relevance: Good coverage and genuinely free, but the receiver requirement means it costs hardware and a hosting location, not money. Worth doing if you want AIS redundancy that does not depend on a single no-SLA vendor — otherwise treat AISStream as the primary and this as a hardware project.

**USACE Lock Performance Monitoring System (LPMS) / Corps Locks** — US Army Corps of Engineers

- Inland waterway lock operations: vessel and barge transit counts by lock, lockage times, delay and queue times, tonnage by commodity through each lock, and lock outages/closures on the Mississippi, Ohio, Illinois and Gulf Intracoastal systems. Plus Waterborne Commerce Statistics.
- Docs: https://corpslocks.usace.army.mil/
- Auth: none | Limits: Free, no key, no registration. Oracle APEX web application with report exports — no documented REST API. No rate limit — UNKNOWN. History: lock transit and delay data back to the 1990s; Waterborne Commerce published annually with a ~1-2 year lag. NOT VERIFIED LIVE in this session — my probe returned HTTP 000 (connection failed/timed out), which may be transient, a TLS/user-agent issue, or a real outage. Re-check before depending on it.
- Latency: daily (lock status) / monthly-annual (commerce statistics) | Format: scrape-only (APEX web app with export), annual bulk statistics
- Relevance: Prices US grain-export and Mississippi-barge contracts, which spike during low-water events and lock failures. When drought closes the lower Mississippi, this is where the delay numbers come from before they reach the news. Narrow but high-conviction for agricultural logistics markets.

**FlightAware AeroAPI** — FlightAware (Collins Aerospace)

- Flight status and tracking, scheduled and actual times, airport arrival/departure boards, flight search, position tracks, and historical flight records — substantially cleaner and better-deduplicated than raw ADS-B.
- Docs: https://www.flightaware.com/commercial/aeroapi/
- Auth: account + API key; metered billing with a free allowance | Limits: Personal tier: NO monthly minimum fee, with up to $5 of free usage per month ($10/month for ADS-B feeders). Rate ceiling 10 result sets per minute. Billing is per result set, not per call, so the effective free request count depends on which endpoints you hit — exact free call count: UNKNOWN by design. Endpoint families are gated by tier, so some historical and alerting endpoints are not available on Personal. Historical depth on paid tiers extends years back. NOT VERIFIED LIVE in this session.
- Latency: realtime to minutely | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: The metered free allowance is too small for broad coverage but is well suited to resolving specific named-flight contracts where you need an authoritative, cleaned answer rather than raw ADS-B. Treat it as a tiebreaker feed, not a firehose.

#### Repos

- `openskynetwork/opensky-api` — Official OpenSky Network API clients (Python and Java) plus the reStructuredText source of the REST and Trino documentation. · Verified live (repo page HTTP 200). The docs/ directory is the authoritative record of the credit costs and the March 2026 basic-auth retirement — read the .rst source rather than trusting cached third-party write-ups. The Python client handles the OAuth2 token refresh for you.
- `open-aviation/pyopensky` — Python interface to the OpenSky Trino historical database and REST API, with typed dataframe outputs. · Verified live (HTTP 200). This is the supported path into the Trino archive — writing raw Trino SQL against the MinIO partitions by hand is painful and easy to get wrong on partition pruning, which is where the query cost lives.
- `xoolive/traffic` — Mature Python library for air traffic data: trajectory processing, flight segmentation, airspace/airport joins, and unified access to OpenSky (REST and Trino), Eurocontrol DDR, and ADS-B files. · Verified live (HTTP 200). Solves the hard part of aviation data — turning raw state vectors into discrete flights with phases. If you want 'did flight X actually operate and was it late', this does the inference layer you would otherwise build badly.
- `M0r13n/pyais` — Pure-Python AIS message encoder/decoder (AIVDM/AIVDO) with multi-part message reassembly and per-vessel state tracking over time. · Verified live (HTTP 200). Required if you ingest raw NMEA from AISHub or your own receiver rather than pre-decoded JSON. The vessel-state-over-time feature matters because AIS splits static data (destination, draught) and position into different message types that must be joined per MMSI.
- `aisstream/aisstream` — Official AISStream client examples and message schema definitions across several languages. · Verified live (HTTP 200). The schema definitions are the practical documentation for the WebSocket payloads, and the examples encode the connection etiquette the docs require (subscribe within 3 seconds, one subscription update per second) that will otherwise get you disconnected.
- `adsbfi/opendata` — Documentation repo for the adsb.fi free open ADS-B API — endpoint list, rate limits and usage policy. · Verified live (HTTP 200, content fetched). The canonical statement of the 1 req/s public limit, the 250 NM radius cap, the feeder-only /v2/snapshot endpoint, and the non-commercial restriction. Also confirms the schema is ADSBexchange-v2-compatible, so old ADSBx client code ports over with only a base-URL change.
- `georgetown-cset/eto-chip-explorer` — CSV data and application code behind the ETO Chip Explorer semiconductor supply chain dataset. · Verified live (GitHub API HTTP 200, repo id 486710167). The CSVs in this repo are the actual dataset — you do not need to use the web app. Gives you the stage/tool/material/country/firm dependency graph as joinable tables for wiring export-control news to affected downstream markets.
- `davidmegginson/ourairports-data` — Daily-regenerated public-domain CSV dumps of the OurAirports database: airports, runways, navaids, frequencies, countries, regions. · Verified live (airports.csv fetched, HTTP 200, 12.7MB). Public domain, so no attribution or licensing friction in a commercial product. This is the crosswalk table between ICAO, IATA and FAA local identifiers that OpenSky, adsb.fi, FAA NOTAM and BTS each use differently.
- `api-evangelist/aishub` — Independent third-party profile of the AISHub API surface — schemas, endpoint documentation and an account of the reciprocal access model. · NOT independently verified in this session (surfaced via search). Useful mainly because it documents the receiver-contribution requirement and the coverage/uptime thresholds plainly, which AISHub's own site states less directly. Read it before investing in AIS receiver hardware.
- `openwatersio/aiscast` — Open Waters AIS network — aisstream.io-compatible AIS streams assembled from open feeds and volunteer receivers. · NOT independently verified in this session (surfaced via search). Directly addresses the single-point-of-failure problem with aisstream.io: because it is wire-compatible, it can be a drop-in failover with no client changes. Verify its coverage and liveness before relying on it.
- `rbuilder80-sudo/carrgo-uk-port-congestion-data` — Open CC BY 4.0 dataset of congestion at 17 UK and Ireland ports — health scores, vessel queues, berth utilisation, week-over-week movement — with pandas loading examples. · NOT independently verified in this session (surfaced via search). Notable because permissively licensed port-congestion data is rare — most of it is behind Kpler/Sea-Intelligence paywalls. Narrow geography, but a usable template for the schema a congestion panel needs.
- `alex9smith/gdelt-doc-api` — Python client for the GDELT 2.0 Document API — global news article search and timeline volume by theme, country and tone. · NOT independently verified in this session (named in the task's catalog list). The relevant angle for this domain is that GDELT themes cover port strikes, rail strikes, canal closures, customs actions and factory shutdowns — it is the free event-detection layer that tells you WHY a transport metric moved, which is what a research panel has to display alongside the number.
