### Agriculture, Food and Land

#### CORE

**USDA NASS Quick Stats API** — USDA National Agricultural Statistics Service `LIVE`

- The authoritative US agricultural statistics database: county/state/national crop acreage, yield, production, price received, stocks, livestock inventories, AND the weekly Crop Progress and crop condition (%% planted, %% harvested, %% good/excellent) series. Millions of rows, 1866-present for some series. This is the single most contract-relevant US ag feed.
- Docs: https://quickstats.nass.usda.gov/api
- Auth: free API key (email registration, instant) | Limits: Documented hard cap: 50,000 data records per request ('exceeds limit = 50000' error above that). Calls per day and calls per minute: UNKNOWN — NASS publishes no documented request-rate limit. History depth: varies by series, back to 1866 for some crop series.
- Latency: weekly for Crop Progress (Mondays 4pm ET during season); monthly/quarterly/annual for surveys | Format: REST JSON / XML / CSV
- Relevance: Directly settles or resolves contracts on US corn/soy/wheat yield and production, harvested acreage, planting pace, condition ratings, and quarterly grain stocks. Most US ag prediction-market contracts cite a NASS number as the resolution source.

**USDA FAS PSD Online bulk CSV downloads** — USDA Foreign Agricultural Service `LIVE`

- World Production, Supply and Distribution balance sheets for every major commodity and country: area harvested, yield, production, imports, exports, domestic consumption, ending stocks. Grains/pulses, oilseeds, livestock, cotton, sugar, coffee, dairy. Historical back to 1960 for many series.
- Docs: https://apps.fas.usda.gov/psdonline/app/index.html#/app/downloads
- Auth: none for the bulk ZIP files | Limits: No key, no documented request limit for the static ZIPs. Files are ~2.9 MB (grains/pulses). History depth: 1960-present for major commodities. Refreshed on the WASDE cycle.
- Latency: monthly (WASDE release cycle, ~12th of month 12:00 ET) | Format: CSV bulk (ZIP)
- Relevance: The denominator for every global stocks-to-use, ending-stocks and world-production contract. Brazil/Argentina soybean production, Black Sea wheat exports, China corn imports — all priced off PSD.

**USDA FAS Open Data API (PSD / ESR / GATS)** — USDA Foreign Agricultural Service `LIVE`

- Programmatic access to PSD balance sheets, the WEEKLY Export Sales Report (ESR — net sales and accumulated exports by commodity and destination), and GATS trade data (US Census + UN Comtrade).
- Docs: https://apps.fas.usda.gov/opendata/swagger/ui/index
- Auth: free API key from the FAS Open Data portal (register, then generate under 'API Keys'); sent as an API_KEY header | Limits: UNKNOWN — FAS publishes no documented calls/day or calls/minute limit. History depth: ESR marketing-year weekly data back to 1999; PSD back to 1960.
- Latency: weekly for ESR (Thursday 8:30am ET); monthly for PSD | Format: REST JSON/XML
- Relevance: ESR weekly export sales is one of the highest-frequency USDA prints that moves grain futures — directly tradeable against 'will weekly corn export sales exceed X' style contracts. GATS prices trade-flow and export-ban contracts.

**WASDE + USDA ESMIS report archive** — USDA Office of the Chief Economist / National Agricultural Library (ESMIS) `LIVE`

- The World Agricultural Supply and Demand Estimates itself, plus the full ESMIS archive of NASS/ERS/AMS reports: Crop Production, Crop Progress, Grain Stocks, Prospective Plantings, Acreage, Cattle on Feed, Hogs and Pigs, Cold Storage. PDF, TXT and XLS per release, with release calendars.
- Docs: https://esmis.nal.usda.gov/
- Auth: none for browsing and file download | Limits: No key. No documented rate limit. NOTE: the old Cornell 'usda.library.cornell.edu/api/v1/release' JSON API now returns HTTP 405/404 — the programmatic release endpoint is no longer working as documented; treat as scrape/bulk-download only. History depth: WASDE back to 1973.
- Latency: monthly (WASDE, 12th of month 12:00 ET); other reports on published calendar | Format: PDF / TXT / XLS bulk, scrape-only for structured extraction
- Relevance: WASDE is THE scheduled event that reprices grain markets. Prediction markets write contracts directly on WASDE ending-stocks and yield numbers. Knowing the release calendar to the minute is itself alpha.

**FAOSTAT bulk download service** — UN FAO `LIVE`

- 69 datasets: crop and livestock production (QCL), food balance sheets, producer prices, consumer food price indices, trade matrices, land use, fertilizer use by nutrient, pesticides, emissions, employment in agriculture. 245 countries, 1961-present.
- Docs: https://bulks-faostat.fao.org/production/datasets_E.json
- Auth: none | Limits: No key, no documented rate limit on the bulk host. 69 dataset codes enumerated in datasets_E.json. History depth: 1961-present for most domains; annual frequency.
- Latency: annual to monthly depending on domain (producer prices and CPI monthly; production annual) | Format: CSV bulk (ZIP), JSON dataset manifest
- Relevance: The global denominator for country-level production, food-balance and fertilizer-use contracts. Too slow for in-season pricing but essential for base rates and for normalizing any 'record harvest' style contract.

**FAO Food Price Index (FFPI)** — UN FAO `LIVE`

- The headline monthly global food price index (2014-2016=100) plus sub-indices for Meat, Dairy, Cereals, Vegetable Oils and Sugar. Nominal and real. Full monthly series from 1990-01.
- Docs: https://www.fao.org/worldfoodsituation/foodpricesindex/en/
- Auth: none | Limits: No key, no rate limit. Static CSV/XLSX file. History depth: 1990-01 to current month. Verified current file is the 2026-09 release (ffpi-data-2026-09.xlsx).
- Latency: monthly — released the first Friday of each month | Format: CSV / XLSX direct download (food_price_indices_data.csv)
- Relevance: Directly resolvable: 'Will the FAO Food Price Index exceed X in month M' is a standard contract shape. The sub-indices give you five separately tradeable series. Scheduled, unambiguous, single-number resolution.

**FEWS NET Data Warehouse (FDW) REST API** — USAID Famine Early Warning Systems Network `LIVE`

- IPC-compatible acute food insecurity phase classifications by subnational admin unit (/ipcphase/), food-insecure population estimates (/ipcpopulationsize/), market price facts (/marketpricefacts/), cross-border trade flows (/tradeflowquantityvalue/), commodity balance sheets, and the geographic unit hierarchy (tabular + GeoJSON/KML).
- Docs: https://help.fews.net/fdw/fews-net-api
- Auth: none for public data (anonymous requests succeed and return public data); token/session auth only unlocks restricted datasets | Limits: No documented calls/day or calls/minute limit. VERIFIED: an anonymous GET of /api/ipcphase/?format=json&country_code=SO returned HTTP 200 with a 56.2 MB payload — no pagination cap enforced, so the practical limit is your own bandwidth. History depth: projections back to at least 2009 (verified rows from 2023 in the Somalia pull).
- Latency: monthly to quarterly (FEWS NET reporting cycle); market prices monthly | Format: REST JSON / CSV / XML / GeoJSON / KML
- Relevance: CORE for famine-declaration and food-crisis contracts. 'Will country X be classified IPC Phase 4/5 by date D' resolves straight off /ipcphase/. The market price endpoint prices local staple-price contracts in fragile states.

**IPC / Cadre Harmonisé Public API** — IPC Global Partnership (hosted by FAO) `LIVE`

- The official Integrated Food Security Phase Classification data: country-level, area-level and population-level acute food insecurity and acute malnutrition classifications for 45+ countries, including current, projection and second-projection periods.
- Docs: https://docs.api.ipcinfo.org/
- Auth: API key REQUIRED and NOT self-serve — you submit a request and IPC validates it internally before issuing a key | Limits: UNKNOWN — no published calls/day or calls/minute. Verified gating: https://api.ipcinfo.org/population?key=<invalid> returns HTTP 401. History depth: UNKNOWN without a key; the public analysis platform shows analyses back to 2017.
- Latency: per-analysis, typically quarterly to biannual per country | Format: REST JSON/CSV
- Relevance: The formal authority for famine declarations. IPC Phase 5 classification is what most 'will famine be declared in X' contracts resolve on — FEWS NET is the fast proxy, IPC is the settlement source. Worth the key-request friction.

**World Bank Real Time Food Prices (RTFP) / Monthly Food Price Inflation** — World Bank DECDG `LIVE`

- Weekly-updated ML-imputed food prices for 37 countries across 3,128 markets, plus monthly food price inflation estimates by country. Sub-series: RTFP (food), RTEP (energy/fuel), RTFX (exchange rates).
- Docs: https://datacatalog.worldbank.org/search/dataset/0060165/monthly-food-price-inflation-estimates-by-country
- Auth: none for the data catalog download | Limits: No key. Rate limit UNKNOWN — the DDH download endpoint returned HTTP 429 on probe, so there IS throttling but the threshold is undocumented. Coverage verified in catalog metadata: 37 countries, 3,128 markets, 2007-01-01 to 2026-08-01, version 2026/08/24. History depth: 2007-present.
- Latency: weekly updates, monthly published series | Format: CSV bulk via Data Catalog / Microdata Library
- Relevance: CORE for fragile-state food price contracts. The weekly refresh is unusually fast for a World Bank product and the ML imputation fills gaps where WFP market surveys are missing — which is exactly where the markets are mispriced.

**World Bank Commodity Markets 'Pink Sheet'** — World Bank `LIVE`

- Monthly nominal prices for ~70 commodities including wheat (US HRW, US SRW), maize, rice (Thai 5%), soybeans, soybean oil, palm oil, sugar, coffee, cocoa, beef, chicken — AND the fertilizer block: urea, DAP, TSP, potassium chloride, phosphate rock. Plus annual and quarterly aggregates and price indices.
- Docs: https://www.worldbank.org/en/research/commodity-markets
- Auth: none | Limits: No key, no documented rate limit. Static XLSX. History depth: monthly series from 1960 (CMO-Historical-Data-Monthly.xlsx verified HTTP 200).
- Latency: monthly (released first week of month) | Format: XLSX bulk
- Relevance: The single best free source for FERTILIZER prices — urea, DAP and potash are otherwise paywalled (Argus/CRU/Profercy). Fertilizer price contracts, and fertilizer-driven planted-acreage contracts, price off this.

**USDA AMS MARS / MyMarketNews API** — USDA Agricultural Marketing Service `LIVE`

- Daily US cash market news: grain bids and basis by elevator, livestock auction prices, boxed beef cutout, pork cutout, dairy, fruit and vegetable terminal prices, organic prices. Thousands of report slugs.
- Docs: https://mymarketnews.ams.usda.gov/mymarketnews-api
- Auth: free API key by registration (email confirmation within a few hours); a sample key exists but AMS states it will be removed | Limits: EXACT documented limits: unregistered users are capped at 5,000 rows per request; registered users at 100,000 rows per request. Calls per day / per minute: UNKNOWN (not published). History depth: varies by report, many back to the 1990s.
- Latency: daily, some reports intraday | Format: REST JSON (Basic auth with key as username)
- Relevance: Daily cash/basis data is the highest-frequency free USDA price feed. Basis levels lead futures on delivery-driven contracts, and boxed beef / pork cutout are directly tradeable series.

**CFTC Commitments of Traders (Socrata Open Data)** — US Commodity Futures Trading Commission `LIVE`

- Weekly positioning by trader category (commercial, non-commercial/managed money, swap dealers, non-reportable) and open interest for every CBOT/CME agricultural contract: WHEAT-SRW, WHEAT-HRW, CORN, SOYBEANS, SOYBEAN OIL, SOYBEAN MEAL, LIVE CATTLE, LEAN HOGS, SUGAR, COFFEE, COCOA, COTTON.
- Docs: https://publicreporting.cftc.gov/
- Auth: none (optional free Socrata app token raises limits) | Limits: Socrata: unauthenticated requests are throttled by a shared per-IP pool (exact threshold UNKNOWN/undisclosed); with a free app token you get a documented higher per-application limit — CFTC does not publish the number. Default $limit is 1,000 rows, max $limit 50,000 per request. History depth: verified rows back to 2022 in the legacy dataset; full COT history to 1986 across dataset variants.
- Latency: weekly (Friday 3:30pm ET, as of Tuesday close) | Format: REST JSON / CSV (Socrata SoQL)
- Relevance: CORE for any contract on grain price direction. Managed-money net length in corn/wheat/soy is the standard positioning signal, and extreme readings are themselves contract subjects.

**US Drought Monitor (USDM) data services API** — National Drought Mitigation Center, UNL / USDA / NOAA `LIVE`

- Weekly percent-area of the US (national, state, county, HUC, congressional district, and USDA crop-specific masks) in each drought category None/D0/D1/D2/D3/D4, plus DSCI. Also GIS shapefiles.
- Docs: https://droughtmonitor.unl.edu/DmData/GISData.aspx
- Auth: none | Limits: No key, no documented rate limit. VERIFIED LIVE 2026: a CONUS query returned HTTP 200 with rows through MapDate 20260127 (ValidStart 2026-01-27). History depth: weekly back to 2000-01-04.
- Latency: weekly (Thursday 8:30am ET) | Format: REST, returns CSV or JSON
- Relevance: CORE and directly resolvable. 'Will more than X%% of the US winter wheat area be in D2+ drought on date D' is a clean USDM-resolved contract, and USDM area percentages are a leading indicator for NASS condition ratings and yield.

**NOAA CPC / PSL soil moisture and climate division data** — NOAA Climate Prediction Center / Physical Sciences Laboratory `LIVE`

- CPC global monthly soil moisture (0.5 degree, water-balance model), US monthly soil moisture, and the nClimDiv climate division dataset (precipitation, temperature, PDSI, Palmer Z-index, SPI by US climate division).
- Docs: https://psl.noaa.gov/data/gridded/data.cpcsoil.html
- Auth: none | Limits: No key, no documented rate limit on the PSL download host or the NCEI climdiv FTP. History depth: CPC soil moisture 1948-present monthly; nClimDiv 1895-present monthly.
- Latency: monthly (CPC soil moisture); monthly (climdiv, ~5th of month) | Format: NetCDF bulk (PSL), fixed-width text bulk (NCEI climdiv)
- Relevance: Soil moisture is the physical driver behind yield contracts. Climate-division PDSI is the standard input for statistical yield models. Links directly to the weather domain — same NOAA infrastructure.

**NASA POWER agroclimatology API** — NASA Langley Research Center `LIVE`

- Point and regional daily/hourly/monthly agroclimatology: temperature, precipitation, solar radiation, relative humidity, wind, evapotranspiration, growing degree days. The AG community preset is purpose-built for crop modeling.
- Docs: https://power.larc.nasa.gov/docs/services/api/temporal/daily/
- Auth: none | Limits: No key. DOCUMENTED: maximum 20 parameters per single-point request; regional requests limited to 1 parameter. Requests per minute/hour: UNKNOWN — NASA publishes no numeric rate limit but warns that repeatedly requesting the same location 'will potentially be blocked', and the API returns HTTP 429 when throttled. History depth: 1981-01-01 to near-real-time.
- Latency: daily, near-real-time (a few days lag) | Format: REST JSON / CSV / ASCII / NetCDF
- Relevance: Free global gridded weather at field scale with no key. Feeds GDD accumulation and water-stress models that drive yield forecasts in regions with no ground network (Black Sea, Sahel, Argentina interior).

**CHIRPS rainfall (UCSB Climate Hazards Center)** — UC Santa Barbara CHC / USGS EROS `LIVE`

- Quasi-global (50S-50N) 0.05 degree gridded precipitation blending satellite and station data — daily, pentad, dekadal, monthly — plus anomaly and SPI products. The standard rainfall input for African and South Asian crop monitoring.
- Docs: https://chc.ucsb.edu/data/chirps
- Auth: none | Limits: No key, no documented rate limit on data.chc.ucsb.edu or the USGS EROS mirror. History depth: 1981-present. Both the UCSB host and the USGS FEWS mirror returned HTTP 200.
- Latency: pentad/dekadal near-real-time (CHIRPS-prelim ~2 day lag); final monthly ~3 week lag | Format: GeoTIFF / NetCDF / BIL bulk over HTTP
- Relevance: CORE for Sahel, Horn of Africa and South Asia food-security and rainfall-failure contracts, where no station network exists. FEWS NET's own famine models run on CHIRPS, so using it aligns you with the resolution source.

**Global Forest Watch Data API** — World Resources Institute / Vizzuality `LIVE`

- Deforestation and land-cover datasets with SQL query and on-the-fly zonal statistics: integrated deforestation alerts (GLAD-L, GLAD-S2, RADD), annual tree cover loss (Hansen/UMD), tree cover gain, primary forest loss, fire alerts (VIIRS), plus Aqueduct crop water-risk layers.
- Docs: https://data-api.globalforestwatch.org/
- Auth: free API key — create an account, get an access token, POST to /auth/apikey with alias/email/organization/domains | Limits: UNKNOWN — GFW documents rate-limit TIERS but publishes no numbers. Documented qualitative rule: 'If you don't specify any domains, your API key will default to the lowest rate limit tier.' API keys EXPIRE AFTER ONE YEAR. The unauthenticated /datasets listing works (HTTP 200 verified) but /query requires a key. History depth: tree cover loss 2001-present annual; GLAD alerts 2015-present near-real-time.
- Latency: weekly for integrated deforestation alerts; near-real-time for VIIRS fire; annual for tree cover loss | Format: REST JSON, SQL-over-HTTP, GeoJSON
- Relevance: CORE for Amazon/Congo/Indonesia deforestation contracts, EUDR-compliance contracts, and palm oil / soy / cattle supply-chain contracts. Weekly alerts are fast enough to price a quarter.

**INPE TerraBrasilis (PRODES / DETER)** — Instituto Nacional de Pesquisas Espaciais, Brazil `LIVE`

- The official Brazilian government deforestation numbers: PRODES annual clear-cut deforestation rate for the Legal Amazon and Cerrado, and DETER near-real-time monthly deforestation and degradation alerts with polygons.
- Docs: https://terrabrasilis.dpi.inpe.br/
- Auth: none | Limits: No key, no documented rate limit. Shapefile and GeoServer WFS/WMS download endpoints verified HTTP 200/302. History depth: PRODES annual from 1988; DETER monthly from 2015.
- Latency: monthly (DETER alerts); annual (PRODES, November consolidated estimate) | Format: Shapefile / GeoJSON bulk, GeoServer WFS/WMS
- Relevance: PRODES is the number Brazilian deforestation contracts actually resolve on — GFW/Hansen is a useful proxy but INPE is the settlement authority. DETER monthly gives you the in-year trajectory.

**Copernicus Data Space Ecosystem (NDVI 300m v3, Sentinel-2)** — ESA / European Commission `LIVE`

- Copernicus Global Land NDVI 300m v3 (10-daily, global), plus FAPAR, LAI, FCOVER, Dry Matter Productivity, Soil Water Index, and full Sentinel-1/2/3 archives for crop mapping. NOTE the 2026 change: CLMS Global datasets have fully migrated from land.copernicus.eu to CDSE; PROBA-V NDVI v1.0 and Sentinel-3 NDVI v2.0 production was DISCONTINUED on 2025-12-31 — v3.0 replaced both.
- Docs: https://dataspace.copernicus.eu/
- Auth: free account registration; OData/STAC browse is open, S3 download needs credentials | Limits: UNKNOWN exact numbers — CDSE applies per-user quotas on concurrent requests and download volume but the published figures vary by service. OData catalogue query verified HTTP 200 unauthenticated. History depth: NDVI v3.0 January 2014-present; Sentinel-2 2015-present.
- Latency: 10-daily (dekadal) for NDVI; 5-day revisit for Sentinel-2 | Format: NetCDF / GeoTIFF over S3, OData and STAC REST catalogue
- Relevance: NDVI anomaly vs the 10-year mean is the single best free in-season crop-condition proxy outside the US. Prices yield contracts in Ukraine, Russia, India, Argentina and Brazil 6-10 weeks before any official statistic is published.

**Copernicus Climate Data Store (CDS) — agro-indicators and ERA5** — ECMWF / Copernicus Climate Change Service `LIVE`

- ERA5 and ERA5-Land reanalysis (1940-present), 'Agroclimatic indicators from 1951 to 2099', crop productivity and evapotranspiration indicators, seasonal forecasts, and soil moisture from the Climate Change Initiative.
- Docs: https://cds.climate.copernicus.eu/
- Auth: free account + personal API token (cdsapi client) | Limits: UNKNOWN exact numbers — CDS enforces per-user queue limits on concurrent and queued requests rather than a published calls/day figure. The catalogue endpoint verified HTTP 200 unauthenticated (ERA5 single-levels collection returned). History depth: ERA5 1940-present; agroclimatic indicators 1951-2099.
- Latency: ERA5 ~5 day lag; ERA5T ~5 day preliminary; seasonal forecasts monthly | Format: REST API (cdsapi), GRIB / NetCDF
- Relevance: The reanalysis backbone for any weather-to-yield model, and the seasonal forecast feed for pre-season planting and production contracts. Directly bridges the agriculture and weather domains.

**HDX (Humanitarian Data Exchange) CKAN API** — UN OCHA `LIVE`

- The aggregation layer: WFP global food prices by market and commodity (monthly, ~90 countries), FEWS NET IPC layers, FAO crop data, IPC population figures, conflict-displacement data — all as versioned CSV resources with a searchable CKAN API.
- Docs: https://data.humdata.org/
- Auth: none for the CKAN package_search/package_show API | Limits: No key for CKAN. No documented calls/day or calls/minute. Verified HTTP 200 on package_search. NOTE: the newer HDX HAPI (hdx-hapi.humdata.org) is a DIFFERENT service and REQUIRES an approved app_identifier — it returned 403/no-response without one. History depth: WFP food prices back to 1992 for some markets.
- Latency: monthly for WFP food prices (stated as 'every month, may occur more or less frequently') | Format: REST JSON (CKAN) + CSV bulk resources
- Relevance: The fastest free route to WFP market-level staple prices in 90+ countries — the underlying data for most food-crisis contracts. One API instead of scraping 90 national portals.

**USGS NWIS water services** — US Geological Survey `LIVE`

- Real-time and daily-value streamflow, gage height, reservoir storage, groundwater levels and water quality for ~1.9 million US sites. Instantaneous values at 15-minute resolution.
- Docs: https://waterservices.usgs.gov/
- Auth: none | Limits: No key. No documented calls/day limit; USGS asks that large historical pulls use the bulk services rather than the real-time endpoint. Verified HTTP 200 on the daily-values endpoint. History depth: daily values back to the 1890s at long-record gages; instantaneous values ~2007-present.
- Latency: 15-minute realtime for instantaneous values; daily for DV | Format: REST JSON (WaterML) / RDB / CSV
- Relevance: CORE for irrigation-water and Western-US water-allocation contracts (Colorado River, Central Valley), Mississippi barge-draft/grain-logistics contracts, and reservoir-level contracts. Bridges directly to the weather domain.

**CONAB (Brazilian crop survey)** — Companhia Nacional de Abastecimento, Brazil `LIVE`

- Brazil's official monthly grain survey: soybean, corn (first and second safrinha crop), rice, cotton, wheat — area, yield and production by state, plus historical series and stocks.
- Docs: https://portaldeinformacoes.conab.gov.br/safra-serie-historica-graos.html
- Auth: none | Limits: No key. No documented rate limit. No documented REST API — data is XLSX/CSV download from the Portal de Informações Agropecuárias plus monthly PDF bulletins. Verified HTTP 200 on both the safras page and the historical series portal. History depth: grain series from 1976/77.
- Latency: monthly (typically the second week, during the Brazilian crop year) | Format: XLSX / CSV bulk download, PDF bulletin, scrape-only for structured extraction
- Relevance: CORE for South American production contracts. CONAB is the resolution authority for Brazilian soybean and corn production, and the CONAB-vs-USDA gap is one of the most reliably mispriced spreads in agricultural prediction markets.

#### USEFUL

**FAOSTAT REST API (fenixservices / faostatservices)** — UN FAO `LIVE`

- Query-level REST access to every FAOSTAT domain without downloading bulk files. This is the base URL almost every Python/R FAOSTAT wrapper points at.
- Docs: https://www.fao.org/faostat/en/#developer-portal/sign-in
- Auth: CHANGED IN 2026 — now requires registration via the FAOSTAT API developer portal | Limits: BROKEN/GATED as of 2026-09-20: https://fenixservices.fao.org/faostat/api/v1/en/* returns HTTP 521 (origin down) on every endpoint tested; https://faostatservices.fao.org/api/v1/en/* returns HTTP 401 (auth required). Exact post-registration rate limits: UNKNOWN — FAO states only that 'rate limiting may apply'. Use the bulk host instead.
- Latency: annual to monthly | Format: REST JSON/CSV
- Relevance: Would be CORE if it worked anonymously. Right now it is a liability — any wrapper you pull off GitHub will silently fail against fenixservices.

**World Bank Indicators API v2** — World Bank `LIVE`

- ~1,500 development indicators including cereal yield (AG.YLD.CREL.KG), crop production index (AG.PRD.CROP.XD), food production index (AG.PRD.FOOD.XD), arable land, agricultural land %, fertilizer consumption, agriculture value added, food CPI. All countries, 1960-present.
- Docs: https://datahelpdesk.worldbank.org/knowledgebase/topics/125589-developer-information
- Auth: none | Limits: No key, no documented calls/day limit. Verified per_page=20000 returns HTTP 200 in a single request. History depth: 1960-present. Note: these are ANNUAL series with a 1-2 year publication lag.
- Latency: annual (lagged) | Format: REST JSON / XML
- Relevance: USEFUL not CORE — the lag kills in-season pricing. Use it for base rates, long-horizon contracts and cross-country normalization.

**World Bank Data360 API** — World Bank `LIVE`

- Unified API over World Bank + partner databases including FAO Consumer Price Indices (FAO_CP), FAOSTAT-derived series, and food-inflation datasets. Verified: FAO_CP alone returns 189,036 observations.
- Docs: https://data360.worldbank.org/
- Auth: none | Limits: No key. No documented calls/day or calls/minute limit. Verified HTTP 200 with a 189,036-row count for DATABASE_ID=FAO_CP. Pagination via skip/limit. History depth: varies by database.
- Latency: monthly for CPI-food series; annual for most others | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: Best single access point for cross-country food CPI without scraping national statistics offices. Prices 'food inflation above X%% in country Y' contracts.

**USDA CropScape / Cropland Data Layer (CDLService)** — USDA NASS + George Mason University CSISS `LIVE`

- 30m annual crop-type classification for the entire US — which pixel grew corn vs soybeans vs wheat vs cotton. Web service returns per-county GeoTIFFs, per-point crop values, and area statistics by crop and geography.
- Docs: https://nassgeodata.gmu.edu/CropScape/
- Auth: none | Limits: No key, no documented rate limit. Verified: GetCDLFile?year=2024&fips=19015 returned HTTP 200. Note GetCDLValue with an out-of-domain projected coordinate returns a SOAP fault, so coordinates must be in the CDL Albers projection. History depth: national CDL 2008-present; some states from 1997.
- Latency: annual (released late January/February for the prior crop year) | Format: SOAP/REST web service returning GeoTIFF and XML
- Relevance: USEFUL — the ground truth for planted-area contracts and the mask you need to compute crop-specific NDVI or drought exposure rather than whole-state averages. Too slow to price in-season on its own.

**UN Comtrade public preview API** — United Nations Statistics Division `LIVE`

- Bilateral merchandise trade flows by HS code — wheat (1001), maize (1005), soybeans (1201), rice (1006), fertilizers (31xx) — reporter, partner, flow, quantity and value.
- Docs: https://comtradeplus.un.org/
- Auth: none for the /public/v1/preview endpoint; a free subscription key raises limits on the full endpoint | Limits: Preview endpoint verified HTTP 200 with no key. DOCUMENTED free-tier behaviour: the preview endpoint caps the response at a small number of records per call (UN documents 500 for preview); the registered free tier is documented at 500 calls per day with a 100,000-record per-call cap — CONFIRM against your own key before relying on it, UN has changed these numbers repeatedly. History depth: annual from 1962, monthly from 2010 for most reporters.
- Latency: monthly, with a 1-3 month reporting lag | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: Prices export-ban, tariff and trade-flow contracts: 'will India export more than X tonnes of rice', 'will China import more than Y tonnes of US soybeans'. The lag makes it confirmatory rather than predictive.

**FAO GIEWS — Country Briefs, FPMA and ASIS** — UN FAO Global Information and Early Warning System `LIVE`

- Country Briefs (cereal production, import requirements, food security narrative per country), the Food Price Monitoring and Analysis tool (domestic staple prices and price warnings), and the Agricultural Stress Index System (satellite-derived crop-stress % of cropland per country/province).
- Docs: https://www.fao.org/giews/countrybrief/index.jsp
- Auth: none | Limits: No key. No documented rate limit. HONEST CAVEAT: there is no stable documented public API — https://fpma.fao.org/giews/v4/price_module/api/ endpoints return HTTP 307 redirects rather than JSON, so treat FPMA and Country Briefs as SCRAPE-ONLY. The ASIS viewer (index_1.jsp) returned HTTP 200. History depth: ASIS dekadal from 1984; Country Briefs from 2010.
- Latency: dekadal (ASIS); monthly-to-quarterly (Country Briefs, FPMA price warnings) | Format: scrape-only (HTML/JSP), some CSV export from the FPMA tool UI
- Relevance: ASIS is a direct crop-stress percentage per country — a clean numeric input for yield-shortfall contracts. FAO's own price-warning flags often precede formal IPC deterioration.

**Global Fishing Watch API v3** — Global Fishing Watch (Oceana / SkyTruth / Google) `LIVE`

- AIS-derived apparent fishing effort by gear type, vessel identity and registry, encounters at sea, loitering, port visits, and 4wings gridded activity rasters. Near-real-time vessel behaviour.
- Docs: https://globalfishingwatch.org/our-apis/documentation/docs/license-rate-limits
- Auth: free access token — register and create a token (verified: unauthenticated /v3/datasets returns HTTP 401) | Limits: EXACT DOCUMENTED LIMITS: 50,000 requests per day and 1,500,000 requests per month, enforced at the USER level across all tokens; each user may create a maximum of 5 tokens. Rate-limit metadata is returned in HTTP response headers. LICENSE CONSTRAINT: CC BY-NC 4.0 — NONCOMMERCIAL USE ONLY. History depth: 2012-present.
- Latency: near-real-time (AIS), daily aggregates | Format: REST JSON + gridded raster (4wings) tiles
- Relevance: USEFUL for IUU-fishing, marine-protected-area and fishing-fleet-activity contracts. CRITICAL: the noncommercial license makes this unusable for a commercial prediction-market product — read the license before you build on it.

**NASA Harvest Portal (CKAN) + GLAM** — NASA Harvest Consortium / University of Maryland `LIVE`

- Agricultural geospatial data repository: crop type maps, in-season crop masks, labeled field boundary datasets, yield benchmarks. GLAM (glam.nasaharvest.org and glam1.gsfc.nasa.gov) provides MODIS/VIIRS NDVI time series over crop masks by admin region.
- Docs: https://data.harvestportal.org/
- Auth: none for CKAN read; GLAM has a browse UI | Limits: No key on the CKAN API. No documented calls/day or calls/minute. Verified HTTP 200 on package_search and on both GLAM hosts. History depth: MODIS NDVI 2000-present in GLAM.
- Latency: 8-day / 16-day composites for NDVI; dataset-dependent for the repository | Format: REST JSON (CKAN), GeoTIFF/NetCDF bulk, GLAM web charts
- Relevance: USEFUL. GLAM's crop-masked NDVI by admin unit is exactly the aggregation you want for yield contracts, and it is already computed for you — saves building the CDL-mask pipeline yourself.

**GEOGLAM Crop Monitor** — GEOGLAM / G20 (hosted by University of Maryland) `LIVE`

- Monthly consensus crop-condition assessments covering 97%+ of global production of wheat, maize, rice and soybeans — exceptional/favourable/watch/poor/failure per country and crop, with the drivers (drought, flood, heat) named. Crop Monitor for AMIS and Crop Monitor for Early Warning.
- Docs: https://www.cropmonitor.org/
- Auth: none | Limits: No key. NO PUBLIC API FOUND — api.cropmonitor.org does not resolve. Data is published as monthly PDF bulletins plus GeoTIFF/shapefile condition layers and the CMET web tool. Treat as scrape/bulk-download. History depth: monthly from 2013.
- Latency: monthly (released with the AMIS Market Monitor, first week of month) | Format: PDF bulletin + GeoTIFF/shapefile bulk, scrape-only for the tabular assessments
- Relevance: CORE signal value, USEFUL access. This is the closest thing to a global 'crop condition rating' and it is a consensus of USDA, FAO, EC-JRC, CONAB and national agencies — i.e. it aggregates the very agencies whose later prints resolve the contracts.

**AMIS Market Monitor + IGC Grain Market Report** — G20 Agricultural Market Information System (FAO) / International Grains Council `LIVE`

- Monthly global supply-demand balances and price commentary for wheat, maize, rice and soybeans, with the AMIS Market Database of country-level production/stocks/trade; IGC publishes the Grains and Oilseeds Index (GOI) and its own world S&D forecasts.
- Docs: https://www.amis-outlook.org/amis-monitoring/en/
- Auth: none | Limits: No key. NO PUBLIC REST API — api.igc.int does not resolve. AMIS data is CSV/XLSX export from the web tool; IGC publishes a free monthly GMR summary PDF (gmrsumme.pdf verified HTTP 200) with the full report paywalled. History depth: AMIS from 2000; IGC GOI from 2011.
- Latency: monthly (AMIS first week; IGC GMR mid-month) | Format: CSV/XLSX export + PDF, scrape-only
- Relevance: USEFUL. IGC's world wheat and maize S&D is the main independent cross-check on USDA PSD — divergence between IGC and USDA forecasts is itself a tradeable signal on WASDE revision direction.

**USDA ERS data APIs (ARMS, Fertilizer Use and Price, Food Price Outlook)** — USDA Economic Research Service `LIVE`

- ARMS farm financial and production-practice survey via API; Fertilizer Use and Price (US farm-gate prices for nitrogen, phosphate, potash, 1960-present); Food Price Outlook (CPI-food forecasts by category); Food Expenditure Series; International Food Security Assessment.
- Docs: https://www.ers.usda.gov/developer/data-apis
- Auth: free API key by registration (verified: api.ers.usda.gov returns HTTP 403 without a key) | Limits: UNKNOWN — ERS publishes no calls/day or calls/minute figure. Only the ARMS dataset is exposed as a true REST API; Fertilizer Use and Price, Food Price Outlook and the Food Expenditure Series are XLSX bulk downloads only. History depth: fertilizer prices 1960-present annual; ARMS 1996-present.
- Latency: annual (ARMS, fertilizer); monthly (Food Price Outlook forecast updates) | Format: REST JSON (ARMS only) + XLSX bulk for the rest
- Relevance: USEFUL. ERS Food Price Outlook publishes an official forecast range for US food CPI — contracts on US food inflation can be priced against, or written on, that forecast. Fertilizer Use and Price is the US farm-gate complement to the World Bank Pink Sheet.

**ClimateSERV (SERVIR / NASA / USAID)** — NASA SERVIR + USAID `LIVE`

- Zonal-statistic API over CHIRPS rainfall, NDVI (eMODIS/MODIS), evapotranspiration, and seasonal forecasts — you POST a polygon and get a time series back, no raster handling required. Built specifically for food-security analysts.
- Docs: https://climateserv.servirglobal.net/
- Auth: none | Limits: No key. No documented calls/day or calls/minute limit. Verified HTTP 200 on getParameterTypes and getDataFromRequest. History depth: CHIRPS 1981-present; eMODIS NDVI 2001-present.
- Latency: dekadal / near-real-time depending on the underlying product | Format: REST JSON (async job submit + poll)
- Relevance: USEFUL and underrated. It turns 'compute NDVI anomaly over Ukraine oblast X' from a multi-hour raster pipeline into one HTTP call — which matters a lot when you are pricing dozens of regions per day.

**EU Agri-food Data Portal API** — European Commission DG AGRI `LIVE`

- Weekly EU member-state prices for cereals, beef, pigmeat, dairy, oilseeds, sugar, poultry, eggs, fruit and vegetables, plus production, trade and CAP indicator dashboards.
- Docs: https://agridata.ec.europa.eu/extensions/DataPortal/home.html
- Auth: none | Limits: No key. No documented rate limit. RELIABILITY WARNING: the API base moved to https://api.tech.ec.europa.eu/agrifood/api/ and is INTERMITTENTLY SUSPENDED — repeated probes returned {'code':'303001','message':'Runtime Error','description':'Address endpoint ... [State : SUSPENDED]'} for most /prices endpoints, while /cereal/products returned HTTP 200 with real product codes (BLTPAN, DUR, ORGFOUR). Retry logic is mandatory. History depth: weekly price series from ~2006.
- Latency: weekly | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: USEFUL for EU wheat/barley/rapeseed and EU dairy price contracts. MATIF milling wheat is the European benchmark and EU physical prices anchor it — but the instability makes this a feed you must monitor, not trust.

#### NICHE

**SoilGrids REST API** — ISRIC World Soil Information `LIVE`

- Global 250m predictions of soil properties at six depth intervals: clay, sand, silt, organic carbon, bulk density, CEC, pH, nitrogen, plus soil classification (WRB). Point query and coverage service.
- Docs: https://rest.isric.org/soilgrids/v2.0/docs
- Auth: none | Limits: UNKNOWN exact numbers — ISRIC applies fair-use throttling but publishes no calls/minute figure in the OpenAPI spec, and no RateLimit headers were returned on probe. Verified: a point query at lon=5, lat=52 returned HTTP 200 with real clay values in g/kg. History depth: N/A (static prediction, v2.0).
- Latency: static (versioned releases) | Format: REST JSON, WCS/WMS coverage
- Relevance: NICHE for pricing directly, but the correct static covariate for any yield model that needs water-holding capacity. Explains why the same rainfall anomaly produces different yield outcomes in different districts.

**FAO FishStat / Global Production bulk datasets** — UN FAO Fisheries and Aquaculture Division `LIVE`

- Global capture fisheries and aquaculture production by species, country, FAO major fishing area and year; plus commodities trade, fleet and employment datasets.
- Docs: https://www.fao.org/fishery/en/collection/capture
- Auth: none | Limits: No key, no documented rate limit. Verified: GlobalProduction_2025.1.0.zip returned HTTP 200. History depth: 1950-present, annual.
- Latency: annual (with ~18 month lag) | Format: CSV bulk (ZIP), FishStatJ desktop tool
- Relevance: NICHE-to-USEFUL. Resolves long-horizon fisheries-collapse and aquaculture-production contracts. The lag rules it out for in-season pricing.

**NOAA Fisheries FOSS landings API** — NOAA National Marine Fisheries Service `LIVE`

- US commercial and recreational fisheries landings by species, state, region and year — pounds, dollars and counts. ORDS REST API with self-describing HATEOAS links.
- Docs: https://www.fisheries.noaa.gov/foss/
- Auth: none | Limits: No key. No documented calls/day or calls/minute. Verified HTTP 200 with real rows (Hawaii recreational landings, 2011-2012) via offset/limit pagination. History depth: commercial landings from 1950.
- Latency: annual, with a partial-year lag | Format: REST JSON (Oracle ORDS)
- Relevance: NICHE. Prices US fishery quota and stock-status contracts. Annual cadence limits it to slow-horizon markets.

**GDELT 2.0 DOC API** — The GDELT Project `LIVE`

- Full-text-indexed global news monitoring updated every 15 minutes, queryable by theme — including agricultural themes (CROP_FAILURE, FOOD_SECURITY, DROUGHT, EXPORT_BAN, FERTILIZER) — with tone, volume timelines and article lists in 100+ languages.
- Docs: https://blog.gdeltproject.org/gdelt-doc-2-0-api-debuts/
- Auth: none | Limits: UNKNOWN exact numbers — GDELT publishes no formal rate limit but throttles aggressively per IP. HONEST RESULT: my probes returned HTTP 429 (Too Many Requests) from a shared IP on both attempts, so I confirmed the endpoint is LIVE and responding in 2026 but did NOT retrieve a data payload. History depth: DOC API rolling 3-month window; the BigQuery/raw files go back to 1979.
- Latency: 15-minute updates | Format: REST JSON/CSV, plus raw 15-minute file dumps and a public BigQuery dataset
- Relevance: NICHE for agriculture specifically, but it is the fastest free detector of export bans, harvest-failure reports and food-riot events — often hours to days ahead of any official statistical release.

#### Repos

- `brycejohnston/awesome-agriculture` — The canonical curated list of open-source agriculture technology, data sources and APIs. 1,882 stars, last updated 2026-09-20. · Actively maintained as of today — this is the index to raid for anything this catalog missed. Has dedicated sections for datasets, APIs, remote sensing and farm management.
- `ropensci/rnassqs` — rOpenSci-reviewed R client for the USDA NASS Quick Stats API. 47 stars, updated 2025-09-22. · The only Quick Stats wrapper that correctly handles the 50,000-record cap, parameter enumeration and the awkward WHAT/WHERE/WHEN query grammar. Steal the query-splitting logic even if you write Python.
- `jackheinemann/nasspython` — Python wrapper for the NASS Quick Stats API. · Minimal, readable Python port of the Quick Stats interface — quicker to read than the official docs for figuring out parameter names.
- `berba-q/faostat-mcp` — MCP server exposing the full FAOSTAT API as tools. 17 stars, updated 2026-09-15. Implements 2 req/s client-side rate limiting. · Recent enough to reflect the 2026 FAOSTAT access changes. Directly droppable into an AI-synthesis research panel as an MCP tool.
- `cyanheads/faostat-mcp-server` — Serves FAOSTAT statistics from a LOCAL SQLITE MIRROR of the bulk-download corpus. Updated 2026-09-19. · This is the correct architecture given that fenixservices.fao.org is returning HTTP 521 — mirror the bulk files locally and query SQLite instead of depending on a flaky FAO origin.
- `FAOSTAT/faostat-api` — FAO's own public API source code. 11 stars. · Read the source to learn the real domain codes, element codes and item codes — the public docs never enumerate them completely.
- `mkao006/FAOSTATpackage` — The full FAOSTAT R package including build tooling. 27 stars, updated 2026-03-24. · Contains the most complete mapping of FAOSTAT area/item/element code tables anywhere outside FAO.
- `JGCRI/gcamfaostat` — R package from PNNL/JGCRI to prepare, process and synthesize FAOSTAT data for global agroeconomic modeling. 17 stars, updated 2026-09-03. · Solves the hard part: reconciling FAOSTAT's inconsistent commodity balances into a coherent supply-utilization account. Production-grade cleaning code.
- `OCHA-DAP/hdx-scraper-wfp-foodprices` — OCHA's own production scraper that builds the WFP global food prices datasets on HDX. Updated 2026-07-27. · This is the upstream code that produces the WFP price CSVs everyone uses. Reading it tells you exactly how markets, commodities and currencies are normalized — and where the joins break.
- `OCHA-DAP/hdx-python-api` — Official Python client for the HDX CKAN data portal. 95 stars, updated 2026-09-16. · Handles HDX resource versioning, dataset date ranges and download caching. The right way to keep a local mirror of WFP prices, IPC layers and FEWS NET resources in sync.
- `OliverSherouse/wbdata` — Mature Python library for the World Bank Indicators API. 212 stars, updated 2026-08-16. · Pandas-native, handles the World Bank's pagination and its irritating two-element JSON envelope. Fastest path to agricultural indicators and food CPI.
- `cbw1243/CropScapeR` — R package for the USDA CropScape / Cropland Data Layer web service. 7 stars. · Documents the CDL Albers projection requirement that makes raw GetCDLValue calls fail with a SOAP fault, and wraps the county-level GeoTIFF retrieval.
- `stactools-packages/usda-cdl` — STAC packaging of the USDA Cropland Data Layer. · Turns CDL into cloud-native COGs with a STAC catalog — far better than pulling full-state GeoTIFFs if you only need county-level crop masks.
- `chhayly/usda-fas-sdk` — Python SDK for the USDA FAS Open Data API (PSD, ESR, GATS). Updated 2026-05-10, also on PyPI as usda-fas-sdk. · The only maintained wrapper for the FAS API-key auth flow and the weekly Export Sales Report endpoints. Low stars but current.
- `R0bD/fewsnet-mcp` — MCP server for FEWS NET data. Updated 2026-05-12. · Early but current — shows the FDW endpoint patterns and query parameters that the FEWS NET help center documents only partially.
- `TRN-HAC/WASDE-parser` — Parser for USDA WASDE reports. Updated 2025-09-25. · WASDE is published as fixed-width text and PDF with no API. Any WASDE-resolved contract needs a parser; this is a starting point rather than a finished one.
- `Open-ET/openet-ssebop` — The SSEBop evapotranspiration model implemented in Google Earth Engine. 55 stars, updated 2026-09-08. · Lets you compute field-scale ET yourself in Earth Engine instead of fighting OpenET's undocumented free-tier quota. Irrigation-demand and crop-water-stress signals without the API dependency.
- `JiaxuanYou/crop_yield_prediction` — The original Deep Gaussian Process crop yield prediction from remote sensing (AAAI'17). 421 stars, still updated 2026-08-28. · The reference architecture for county-level yield forecasting from MODIS histograms. If you are pricing US yield contracts, this is the baseline your model must beat.
- `gabrieltseng/pycrop-yield-prediction` — Clean PyTorch reimplementation of the Deep Gaussian Process yield model. 199 stars, updated 2026-08-24. · Far more readable than the original, with a working NASS + MODIS data pipeline you can lift wholesale.
- `saeedkhaki92/CNN-RNN-Yield-Prediction` — CNN-RNN framework for crop yield prediction. 163 stars, updated 2026-09-08. · Handles the weather-sequence + soil-covariate fusion that the DGP model ignores. Good template for combining NASA POWER dailies with SoilGrids statics.
- `fineprint-global/fabio` — Food and Agriculture Biomass Input-Output tables. 39 stars, updated 2026-09-07. · Physical supply-chain linkages between crops, feed, livestock and trade. The right structure for reasoning about second-order contracts (drought in Brazil -> soymeal -> EU pork prices).
- `WorldCereal/worldcereal-cop4geoglam` — ESA WorldCereal crop classification extended for Copernicus4GEOGLAM. Updated 2026-01-19. · Global 10m crop-type and irrigation maps via openEO — the non-US equivalent of CDL, which is otherwise the biggest gap in global crop-area data.
- `alex9smith/gdelt-doc-api` — Python client for the GDELT 2.0 DOC API. 231 stars, updated 2026-09-19. · Handles GDELT's aggressive per-IP throttling with backoff — important given that raw probes return HTTP 429. Use it for export-ban and food-riot event detection.
- `linwoodc3/gdeltPyR` — Python framework for GDELT 1.0 and 2.0 event and mention data. 257 stars, updated 2026-08-21. · Pulls the raw 15-minute event files rather than the throttled DOC API — the only practical way to do high-volume GDELT ingestion for free.
- `MelvinJoshuvaSeelanM/agmarknet-scraper` — Python scraper for India's Agmarknet mandi price portal, exports CSV. Updated 2025-11-29. · Agmarknet and api.data.gov.in return HTTP 403 to non-Indian IPs. Indian staple prices (onion, wheat, rice, pulses) drive real food-inflation and export-ban contracts, and scraping is the only route.
- `OCHA-DAP/hdx-scraper-faostat` — OCHA's FAOSTAT collector for HDX. · A working reference for pulling FAOSTAT country-by-country without hitting the now-401 REST API — it goes through the bulk corpus.

### News, Media, Social & Attention — the firehose layer

#### CORE

**GDELT 2.0 DOC API (Document Search)** — The GDELT Project (Kalev Leetaru / Google Jigsaw) `LIVE`

- Query-time search over GDELT's index of worldwide online news in 65+ languages. Modes: artlist (article metadata), timelinevol / timelinevolraw / timelinetone / timelinelang / timelinesourcecountry (volume & tone time series), tonechart, wordcloud, imagecollage. HEADLINES/METADATA ONLY — confirmed live response fields are url, url_mobile, title, seendate, socialimage, domain, language, sourcecountry. NO article body. Full text must be fetched separately (trafilatura/news-please) or pulled from Common Crawl CC-NEWS.
- Docs: https://blog.gdeltproject.org/gdelt-doc-2-0-api-debuts/
- Base: `https://api.gdeltproject.org/api/v2/doc/doc`
- Auth: none | Limits: EXACT, quoted from the server's own HTTP 429 body: 'Please limit requests to one every 5 seconds' = 12 req/min, ~17,280 req/day. maxrecords caps at 250 per call. Rolling window is the last 3 months only via timespan/startdatetime; deeper history requires the bulk GKG files. I hit 429 repeatedly during testing — the limit is enforced hard, not advisory.
- Latency: sub-minute to 15-minute (GDELT ingests on a 15-min cycle; seendate on returned articles was 20260920T151500Z) | Format: REST JSON / JSONP / CSV / RSS / HTML
- Relevance: The single best free instrument for 'will X be in the news / how much' contracts: media-volume and media-tone time series price attention-driven markets (resignations, scandals, indictments, ceasefires, product launches). timelinetone is a directional signal for sentiment-conditioned contracts. sourcecountry/language splits let you detect a story breaking in one country before it crosses over.

**GDELT 2.0 Bulk Files — Events, Mentions, GKG (Global Knowledge Graph)** — The GDELT Project `LIVE`

- The raw 15-minute firehose. Three CSV.zip files every 15 minutes: .export.CSV (CAMEO-coded events with actors, event codes, Goldstein scale, geocoding), .mentions.CSV (every re-mention of an event with confidence and tone), .gkg.csv (Global Knowledge Graph: themes, persons, organizations, locations, 2,300+ emotional/thematic dimensions, quotations, image tags, per-article tone). GKG is where entity extraction lives. Metadata + extracted entities, NOT full article body.
- Docs: https://www.gdeltproject.org/data.html#rawdatafiles
- Base: `http://data.gdeltproject.org/gdeltv2/lastupdate.txt`
- Auth: none | Limits: No API key, no published rate limit on the file server. Backfill depth VERIFIED: masterfilelist.txt contains 1,197,033 file entries (I counted it), covering Feb 2015 → present at 15-min granularity. GDELT 1.0 daily files extend back to 1979. Latest file at test time: 20260921004500.gkg.csv.zip (2.37 MB). Practical constraint is your own bandwidth: ~230 MB/day of GKG alone.
- Latency: 15-minute batch (fixed cadence, files land on :00/:15/:30/:45) | Format: CSV bulk (zipped), also mirrored in Google BigQuery
- Relevance: CORE backbone. Mentions + Events give you an event-count series per CAMEO code per country — directly prices conflict-escalation, protest, sanction, and coup contracts. GKG themes/persons/orgs give a named-entity mention counter you can key any 'will person X be mentioned alongside Y' market on. Goldstein scale is a ready-made escalation index.

**GDELT Translingual (machine-translated non-English firehose)** — The GDELT Project `LIVE`

- Parallel 15-minute bulk stream of the same Events/Mentions/GKG schema, but built from live machine translation of 65 non-English languages. Separate file series: .translation.export.CSV.zip, .translation.mentions.CSV.zip, .translation.gkg.csv.zip.
- Docs: https://blog.gdeltproject.org/gdelt-translingual-translating-the-planet/
- Base: `http://data.gdeltproject.org/gdeltv2/lastupdate-translation.txt`
- Auth: none | Limits: No key, no published rate limit. Confirmed live: 20260921003000.translation.gkg.csv.zip (3.9 MB) — note the translingual series ran 15 min behind the English series at test time. Backfill to 2015.
- Latency: 15-minute batch (observed ~15 min behind the English series) | Format: CSV bulk (zipped)
- Relevance: This is the edge nobody uses. Non-English media breaks regional stories (Russian, Farsi, Mandarin, Turkish, Hindi outlets) hours before English wires. For geopolitical contracts — border incidents, leadership changes, currency interventions — the translingual GKG is a genuine latency advantage over English-only news APIs.

**GDELT 2.0 Television API (TV Explorer)** — The GDELT Project + Internet Archive TV News Archive `LIVE`

- Full-text search over closed-caption transcripts of US and international television news. Modes: TimelineVol, TimelineVolNorm, TimelineVolHeatmap, TimelineVolStream, StationChart, ShowChart, StationDetails, ClipGallery, WordCloud, TrendingTopics. Operators include station: / Network: / market:"National". Returns airtime-share time series and 30-60s clip links with caption text — FULL CAPTION TEXT for clips, aggregate percentages for timelines.
- Docs: https://blog.gdeltproject.org/gdelt-2-0-television-api-debuts/
- Base: `https://api.gdeltproject.org/api/v2/tv/tv`
- Auth: none | Limits: No key. Rate limit not separately documented; the shared api.gdeltproject.org 1-request-per-5-seconds guidance applies. Backfill depth VERIFIED BY LIVE QUERY: a station:CNN query returned a monthly series spanning '06/05/2009 - 09/19/2026' — i.e. 17+ years, 163 stations, 2M+ hours. ClipGallery is capped at the most recent results per query.
- Latency: roughly 24-72 hours behind broadcast (Internet Archive caption ingest lag); timeline aggregates are daily/monthly | Format: REST JSON / JSONP / CSV / RSS / HTML
- Relevance: Share-of-voice on cable news is a leading indicator for US political contracts — primary viability, cabinet departures, impeachment odds, Fed-speak intensity. 'Percentage of CNN/Fox/MSNBC airtime mentioning X' is a cleaner, less gameable attention metric than social media because the denominator (total airtime) is fixed. Nobody in retail prediction markets is pricing off this.

**Common Crawl CC-NEWS** — Common Crawl Foundation `LIVE`

- Raw WARC archives of news articles crawled continuously from RSS feeds and news sitemaps worldwide. This is the FULL TEXT layer — complete raw HTTP responses including full article HTML, headers and crawl timestamps. The counterpart to GDELT's metadata.
- Docs: https://commoncrawl.org/blog/news-dataset-available
- Base: `https://data.commoncrawl.org/crawl-data/CC-NEWS/{YYYY}/{MM}/warc.paths.gz`
- Auth: none | Limits: Completely free, no key, no documented rate limit on data.commoncrawl.org (S3 also available; the s3:// path is requester-pays, the https:// path is not). VERIFIED LIVE: CC-NEWS/2026/09/warc.paths.gz returns 200 with 251 WARC files, latest CC-NEWS-20260920202638-00137.warc.gz — i.e. current to within hours of my test. Backfill depth: continuous monthly since August 2016. Each WARC ~1 GB.
- Latency: hourly-to-daily (new WARC roughly every 2-4 hours based on observed filename timestamps) | Format: WARC bulk (gzipped)
- Relevance: FULL TEXT is what lets an LLM actually resolve a contract rather than guess from a headline. For any market whose resolution hinges on exact wording — 'does the statement contain the word recession', 'was the figure revised', 'did the company confirm' — you need the body, and this is the only free source of news bodies at global scale with a 10-year backfill. Pair with GDELT for discovery, CC-NEWS for evidence.

**Wikimedia EventStreams (recentchange)** — Wikimedia Foundation `LIVE`

- Server-Sent-Events stream of EVERY edit across all Wikimedia projects in real time. Confirmed live payload fields: page title, title_url, user, bot flag, edit comment, namespace, timestamp, notify_url (the diff link), domain, and Kafka topic/partition/offset for resumable consumption.
- Docs: https://wikitech.wikimedia.org/wiki/Event_Platform/EventStreams
- Base: `https://stream.wikimedia.org/v2/stream/recentchange`
- Auth: none | Limits: Free, no key. No hard connection limit published, but WMF asks for a meaningful User-Agent with contact info and reserves the right to block. Stream is replayable from an offset for approximately the LAST 7 DAYS only (Kafka retention) — deeper history requires the Pageviews API or dumps. VERIFIED LIVE: I consumed the stream and captured a real edit to en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WCMU-TV at 2026-09-21T00:39:39.557Z.
- Latency: realtime (server-sent events, sub-second) | Format: SSE (Server-Sent Events) JSON
- Relevance: Wikipedia edit velocity is a genuinely fast breaking-news detector — a spike of edits to a politician's page, especially to the infobox 'term ended' field, frequently precedes wire confirmation of a resignation or death. For 'will X leave office / will X be appointed' contracts this is a sub-minute alarm. Filter on bot:false and on specific page-watchlists per active market.

**Wikimedia Pageviews / Analytics REST API** — Wikimedia Foundation `LIVE`

- Per-article pageview counts at hourly, daily and monthly granularity, sliceable by access method (desktop/mobile-web/mobile-app) and agent (user/spider/automated). Also top-N most-viewed per day, per-project aggregates, unique devices, and editor/edit counts.
- Docs: https://doc.wikimedia.org/generated-data-platform/aqs/analytics-api/
- Base: `https://wikimedia.org/api/rest_v1/metrics/pageviews/per-article/{project}/{access}/{agent}/{article}/{granularity}/{start}/{end}`
- Auth: none | Limits: Free, no key. Meaningful User-Agent with contact info REQUIRED (requests without one are throttled or blocked). Per mediawiki.org/wiki/Wikimedia_APIs/Rate_limits: unidentified clients 10 req/min, unauthenticated browser-like 200 req/min, authenticated established accounts 2,000 req/min, bot-flagged exempt. Backfill: daily pageviews from 2015-07-01; legacy pagecounts back to 2007. VERIFIED LIVE: returned real daily counts for 'Ukraine' (8,039 views on 2026-09-01, 7,770 on 09-02, 7,815 on 09-03, 7,150 on 09-04).
- Latency: hourly granularity, published with roughly 24-48h lag for the daily endpoint | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: The cleanest free public-attention index that exists. Unlike social metrics it is not bot-inflatable at scale (spider traffic is separated out), has a decade of history for base rates, and covers every named entity on earth. For 'will X become famous / will this story break out' and for normalizing a media-volume spike against genuine public interest, this is the denominator.

**Bluesky Jetstream** — Bluesky Social PBC `LIVE`

- Lightweight JSON WebSocket firehose of the entire AT Protocol network — every public post, like, repost, follow and profile change, filterable server-side by collection (e.g. wantedCollections=app.bsky.feed.post) and by DID. Confirmed live frame contains did, time_us, kind, commit.operation, commit.collection, and the FULL post record including text, langs, createdAt and CID.
- Docs: https://github.com/bluesky-social/jetstream
- Base: `wss://jetstream2.us-east.bsky.network/subscribe?wantedCollections=app.bsky.feed.post`
- Auth: none | Limits: Free, no key, no documented rate limit. Four public instances all confirmed responding: jetstream1/2.us-east and jetstream1/2.us-west .bsky.network. Server-side filtering keeps bandwidth manageable. Replay: supports a cursor parameter for backfill, retention window UNKNOWN. VERIFIED LIVE AND HARDEST-CONFIRMED OF ALL FEEDS HERE: I completed the WebSocket handshake (HTTP/1.1 101 Switching Protocols) and read a real post frame with createdAt 2026-09-21T00:39:55.076118+00:00.
- Latency: realtime/websocket (sub-second) | Format: WebSocket JSON
- Relevance: With X/Twitter's free tier gone (see deadEnds), this is now THE free real-time social firehose. Full post text at zero cost means you can run live sentiment, breakout-term detection and source-account monitoring on the entire network. Journalists, politicians and finance accounts have migrated here in volume. For 'first report' timing on breaking events this competes with wire services.

**Google News RSS** — Google `LIVE`

- Unofficial but long-stable RSS endpoints for Google News search results, topics, and geo editions. Returns headline, publisher name, publication timestamp and a redirect link. HEADLINES ONLY — no body, and links are Google redirect URLs that must be resolved.
- Docs: https://support.google.com/news/publisher-center/answer/9606710
- Base: `https://news.google.com/rss/search?q={query}&hl=en-US&gl=US&ceid=US:en`
- Auth: none | Limits: No key and no published rate limit — it is an undocumented endpoint, so any limit is UNKNOWN and Google may throttle or remove it without notice. Result set is capped at roughly 100 items per feed. History depth: the 'when:' operator supports roughly the last year, but the feed itself returns only recent items. VERIFIED LIVE: a 'federal reserve' query returned current 2026 headlines from Fox News and NPR.
- Latency: minutely (Google's own indexing cadence) | Format: RSS/XML
- Relevance: The cheapest possible 'is this in the news yet' boolean, available per-query with zero setup, and it covers publishers GDELT's crawl list may miss. Good as a redundancy check against GDELT rather than a primary. Treat as fragile infrastructure: it is undocumented and has no SLA.

**RSS/Atom aggregation at scale (self-hosted)** — Self-hosted — feedparser, FreshRSS, RSS-Bridge, openrss.org `LIVE`

- Direct polling of publisher-operated RSS/Atom feeds. Most major outlets, every government press office, central banks, regulators, courts, sports leagues and company IR pages still publish RSS. Content varies by publisher: many emit full-text feeds, others headline+summary. RSS-Bridge synthesizes feeds for sites that removed theirs; openrss.org does the same as a hosted service.
- Docs: https://github.com/RSS-Bridge/rss-bridge
- Base: `per-publisher; RSS-Bridge at https://rss-bridge.org/bridge01/`
- Auth: none | Limits: No key and no aggregate limit — you are bound only by each publisher's own politeness expectations (honor ETag / If-Modified-Since and robots.txt). History depth is typically 10-100 items per feed with NO backfill, so you must capture continuously and store it yourself. VERIFIED LIVE: rss-bridge.org, openrss.org, FreshRSS repo and Google News RSS all responded in 2026.
- Latency: minutely (your polling interval is the only constraint) | Format: RSS/Atom XML
- Relevance: CORE and consistently underrated. The authoritative resolution source for most contracts is a PRIMARY feed, not a news aggregator: the central bank's own release feed, the court's docket feed, the regulator's announcement feed, the league's results feed. These are first-party, fast, free, unlimited and legally unambiguous. Build a curated registry of a few hundred primary-source feeds per market domain — that registry is a real moat, and it is the piece no vendor API sells you.

#### USEFUL

**GDELT Web News NGrams 3.0** — The GDELT Project `LIVE`

- Per-minute quadgram index of global online news. Two files per timestamp: .ngrams.txt.gz (tab-delimited DOCID / QUADGRAM / COUNT) and .toc.json.gz (table of contents: id, date, image URL, language, title, article URL). GDELT's own 429 message explicitly redirects high-traffic users here instead of the DOC API.
- Docs: https://blog.gdeltproject.org/using-the-new-web-ngrams-dataset-to-find-relevant-coverage/
- Base: `https://data.gdeltproject.org/gdeltv5/weblegacy/ngrams/`
- Auth: none | Limits: No key, no rate limit. VERIFIED: https://data.gdeltproject.org/gdeltv5/weblegacy/ngrams/20260920201600.toc.json.gz returns HTTP 200. IMPORTANT CAVEAT — I could NOT find a working lastupdate.txt or MASTERFILELIST at this path (all returned 404), and several nearby timestamps (20260921000000, 20260920235800, 20260920230000) also 404'd. The file-discovery mechanism is UNKNOWN; you must derive timestamps or find the index. Backfill depth UNKNOWN.
- Latency: per-minute (docs state 'every minute the file for two minutes ago is produced') | Format: Bulk gzipped TSV + JSON
- Relevance: The intended high-volume substitute for the rate-limited DOC API. Quadgram counts let you build your own phrase-frequency alerting ('rate cut', 'state of emergency', 'ceasefire agreed') at minute resolution across all of global news, without hitting any API limit. This is the scaling path if the terminal needs continuous monitoring rather than polled queries.

**Common Crawl Main Corpus + CDX/Columnar Index** — Common Crawl Foundation `LIVE`

- Petabyte-scale general web crawl (~2.5-3B pages per monthly crawl) with a queryable CDX index for URL lookup and a columnar (Parquet) index for SQL-style filtering. Full raw HTML.
- Docs: https://commoncrawl.org/get-started
- Base: `https://index.commoncrawl.org/collinfo.json`
- Auth: none | Limits: Free, no key. VERIFIED: collinfo.json returns 200 and lists CC-MAIN-2026-39 ('September 2026 Index', from 2026-09-04T13:16:03 to 2026-09-17T05:59:21) as current. Backfill: monthly crawls since 2008. HONEST CAVEAT — the CDX query server was FLAKY during testing: CC-MAIN-2026-39-index returned 404 (index likely not yet built for the newest crawl) and CC-MAIN-2026-30-index returned 502. Do not build a hot path on the CDX server; use the columnar index on S3 instead.
- Latency: monthly | Format: WARC/WAT/WET bulk + CDX JSON API + Parquet columnar index
- Relevance: Backfill and deep-history layer. Useful for constructing historical base rates (how often has this phrasing appeared before an event), for scraping niche sources no news API indexes, and for building the station/source reliability priors the task asks for. Not a real-time signal.

- Clean machine-readable article content — FULL ARTICLE BODY AS HTML — plus Structured Contents endpoints (infoboxes, sections, references parsed into JSON) across all Wikimedia projects including Wikidata, through a single token. Snapshot (bulk dump) and On-demand (per-article) APIs.

I did not exercise it with a token, so the 50,000 figure is vendor-reported, not measured by me.

- Relevance: Structured Contents is the underrated piece: it hands you infobox fields as typed JSON. 'Who currently holds office X', 'what is company Y's CEO', 'what date did Z occur' become a parsed field lookup instead of an LLM extraction. That is exactly the resolution-source problem for political and corporate contracts.

VERIFIED LIVE: returns HTTP 200 in 2026.

- Relevance: This is the market-universe generator, not a price signal. Enumerate every scheduled election, every office holder, every listed company officer, every sports fixture — and get the authoritative ID to key every other feed on. Treat the stream itself as IMPLEMENTED / NOT LIVE-VALIDATED by me.
- Latency: realtime/websocket | Format: WebSocket (CBOR / CAR blocks)
- Relevance: Use only if you need cryptographic provenance — e.g. proving a post existed at a timestamp for contract resolution, or detecting deletions/edits that Jetstream's simplified view may drop. For ordinary sentiment and volume work, Jetstream is strictly easier and carries the same content.

- Relevance: Broadcast is still where US political opinion is formed, and caption text is a verbatim, timestamped record of what a named person actually said on air.
