- Base: `https://factchecktools.googleapis.com/v1alpha1/claims:search`
- Auth: free API key (Google Cloud project) | Limits: Free — no per-call charge for either searching fact checks or registering ClaimReview pages. Rate limit: standard Google per-project quota, typically defaulting to 600 read requests per minute. DAILY LIMIT: UNKNOWN — I could not find a published per-day figure and will not invent one. Backfill: the full ClaimReview corpus, which in practice reaches back to roughly 2016 when the schema was adopted. VERIFIED LIVE: the endpoint returned a well-formed 403 PERMISSION_DENIED ('Method doesn't allow unregistered callers') in 2026, confirming the service is up and key-gated.
- Latency: daily-to-weekly (fact-checks are published with inherent lag) | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: Two real uses. First, a claim being fact-checked is itself a signal that a contested narrative has reached critical mass — a leading indicator for rumor-driven markets. Second, and more important, it is a truth-filter on your own ingest: before an LLM synthesizes a position from news, check whether the underlying claim has already been rated false. That prevents the terminal from pricing off debunked material.

**Media Cloud Online News Archive + Search API** — Media Cloud (UMass Amherst / Northeastern, non-profit) `LIVE`

- Open news archive of 200M+ stories across curated source collections by country and media type, with a search API that also queries the Wayback Machine news archive. Curated collections are the differentiator — hand-maintained lists of national and local outlets per country.
- Docs: https://www.mediacloud.org/documentation/search-api-guide
- Base: `https://search.mediacloud.org/api/`
- Auth: free API key (request an account) | Limits: UNKNOWN — I fetched the Search API guide page (HTTP 200 in 2026) and it does NOT publish rate limits, quotas or searchable date ranges; it redirects readers to the Python package and support@mediacloud.org. The docs do state the archive holds '200 million+ stories and growing every day', and note that the Wayback Machine news search is matched against TITLE TEXT only, not full body. I did not obtain a key, so no limit is measured. Do not assume it is unlimited.
- Latency: daily batch | Format: REST JSON + Python client
- Relevance: Best free source of CURATED source lists — 'all national dailies in Brazil', 'US local TV news sites'. That matters because GDELT's crawl is broad but unweighted, so you cannot tell mainstream coverage from content-farm echo. Media Cloud's collections give you the weighting, which is what turns raw article counts into a credible media-salience index.

**NewsData.io** — NewsData.io (Algodom Media LLP) `LIVE`

- Latest news, archive, crypto and sources endpoints across 150+ countries with sentiment, category and entity enrichment on higher tiers.
- Docs: https://newsdata.io/documentation
- Base: `https://newsdata.io/api/1/latest`
- Auth: free API key | Limits: Free plan: 200 API credits/day, rate-limited to 30 credits per 15 minutes, 10 articles per credit. Archive search and advanced filters burn 2+ credits per call, so 200/day is realistically 60-80 useful requests. Archive reaches back 2 years in their database, with ~6 months self-serve from the dashboard and older data by request. Full article content is a PAID field on this provider. FIGURES ARE VENDOR/SECONDARY-SOURCED: newsdata.io/pricing and /documentation are JavaScript-rendered and returned only a title to my fetcher, so I confirmed the pages respond (HTTP 200 in 2026) but could NOT read the limits off the page myself.
- Latency: minutely-to-hourly | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: A reasonable redundancy tier behind GDELT — broader publisher coverage in some emerging markets and built-in categorization. At 200 credits/day it cannot carry continuous monitoring; use it for targeted lookups on active contracts only.

**Guardian Open Platform** — Guardian News & Media `LIVE`

- The Guardian's complete content API — and crucially it returns FULL ARTICLE BODY TEXT, plus tags, sections, contributor data and structured fields. One of very few outlets giving away its own full text.
- Docs: https://open-platform.theguardian.com/documentation/
- Base: `https://content.guardianapis.com/search`
- Auth: free API key (developer tier, self-service registration) | Limits: Developer tier documented at 12 calls/second and 5,000 calls/day, non-commercial use, with full text access. Backfill: the complete Guardian archive from 1999. CONFIRMED 2026 CHANGE: the legacy api-key=test value NO LONGER WORKS — content.guardianapis.com returned HTTP 401 {"message":"Unauthorized"} to it during my test. You must register. NOTE the non-commercial restriction: a commercial terminal needs their Commercial tier.
- Latency: realtime (published articles available within minutes) | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: High-quality full text with a 27-year backfill from a single reputable outlet, free. Excellent for building and backtesting text-based resolution logic where you need real article bodies and GDELT only gives you URLs. The non-commercial clause is the constraint to resolve before production.

**New York Times Developer APIs** — The New York Times `LIVE`

- Article Search (1851-present), Top Stories, Most Popular, Books, Movie Reviews, and the Archive API which returns every article's metadata for a given month. Metadata, abstracts and lead paragraphs — NOT full body text.
- Docs: https://developer.nytimes.com/apis
- Base: `https://api.nytimes.com/svc/`
- Auth: free API key (self-service registration) | Limits: Documented free limits: 500 requests/day and 5 requests/minute per API, non-commercial use. Article Search backfill reaches 1851. Full body text is NOT provided — abstract, snippet and lead_paragraph only. VERIFIED LIVE: api.nytimes.com returned HTTP 401 without a key in 2026, confirming the service is up and key-gated.
- Latency: realtime for Top Stories; Archive API is monthly batch | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: The 1851 Archive API is the standout: a 175-year, month-by-month metadata series for constructing long-run base rates on how often a topic, country or person has been front-page news. That is the historical prior layer that GDELT (2015+) and Common Crawl (2016+) cannot give you. 500/day is fine for backfill, useless for monitoring.

#### NICHE

**GDELT Context API + Summary API** — The GDELT Project `LIVE`

- Context API returns snippet-level contextual matches around a search phrase across GDELT's article index (keyword-in-context rather than whole-article). Summary API drives the GDELT Summary/Trends explorer surface.
- Docs: https://blog.gdeltproject.org/announcing-the-gdelt-context-2-0-api/
- Base: `https://api.gdeltproject.org/api/v2/context/context and https://api.gdeltproject.org/api/v2/summary/summary`
- Auth: none | Limits: No key; same 1-request-per-5-seconds shared guidance. HONEST RESULT: both endpoints returned HTTP 200 in 2026, but my Context API query (query=inflation&mode=artlist&timespan=1d&format=json) returned an EMPTY result set: {"articles": [ ]}. The endpoint is alive; whether it still has a populated index, and its exact query syntax and history depth, are UNKNOWN — I did not get a non-empty response.
- Latency: UNKNOWN (no populated response obtained) | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: Would be valuable for extracting the sentence around a claim rather than just the headline — useful for resolving 'did official X actually say Y' contracts. Downgraded to NICHE because I could not demonstrate it returns data.

**Mastodon public timelines, trends and streaming** — Mastodon gGmbH + independent instance operators `LIVE`

- Per-instance public timeline (local and federated), trending links / tags / statuses, and a WebSocket/SSE streaming API. Full post text.
- Docs: https://docs.joinmastodon.org/methods/streaming/
- Base: `https://{instance}/api/v1/timelines/public and https://{instance}/api/v1/streaming`
- Auth: varies BY INSTANCE — this is the key 2026 finding | Limits: Default Mastodon rate limit is 300 requests per 5 minutes per account (and 300 per 5 min per IP for unauthenticated), but EVERY INSTANCE CAN OVERRIDE THIS. CRITICAL 2026 CHANGE I VERIFIED DIRECTLY: mastodon.social/api/v1/timelines/public now returns HTTP 422 {"error":"This method requires an authenticated user"} — the flagship instance has CLOSED anonymous public-timeline reads. Meanwhile fosstodon.org and mstdn.social both still return HTTP 200 unauthenticated, and mastodon.social/api/v1/trends/links still returns 200 without auth, as does the streaming health endpoint. There is no single network-wide firehose; you must federate across instances yourself. History depth: instance-dependent, typically shallow.
- Latency: realtime (WebSocket/SSE) where permitted | Format: REST JSON + WebSocket/SSE
- Relevance: Thin and fragmenting. Volume is far below Bluesky and the per-instance auth divergence makes reliable coverage expensive to maintain. Worth wiring only for the trends/links endpoint as a cheap cross-check on what the fediverse is amplifying. Do not build a primary sentiment signal on it.

**Stack Exchange API v2.3** — Stack Exchange / Stack Overflow `LIVE`

- Questions, answers, comments, tags, users and activity across all 170+ Stack Exchange sites, with full body text, vote counts, view counts and timestamps.
- Docs: https://api.stackexchange.com/docs
- Base: `https://api.stackexchange.com/2.3/`
- Auth: none for 300/day; free registered app key for 10,000/day | Limits: EXACT AND MEASURED BY ME: I called /2.3/info?site=stackoverflow live and the response body returned quota_max: 300, quota_remaining: 298 — confirming 300 requests/day without a key. With a free registered app key the documented quota is 10,000 requests/day per IP. A dynamic backoff field in the response forces a pause when triggered. Responses must be gzip-decoded (the API always compresses). Backfill: full site history since 2008; bulk Stack Exchange Data Dumps also exist.
- Latency: near-realtime (query-time) | Format: REST JSON (always gzipped)
- Relevance: Genuinely marginal for prediction markets. Tag-velocity is a slow technology-adoption indicator (useful for 'will framework X overtake Y' style long-horizon contracts) and nothing else. Include for completeness of the attention layer, not for pricing.

**Lemmy API v3** — Lemmy (federated, per-instance) `LIVE`

- Post listings, comments, communities and search across federated Lemmy instances, with full post and comment body text and vote scores.
- Docs: https://join-lemmy.org/api/
- Base: `https://lemmy.world/api/v3/`
- Auth: none for public reads | Limits: No key required for public reads. Rate limits are per-instance and configurable by the operator; exact numbers UNKNOWN. History depth: instance-dependent. VERIFIED LIVE: lemmy.world/api/v3/post/list?limit=1 returned a real post (id 52149640) in 2026.
- Latency: realtime (query-time) | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: Very low volume relative to Reddit. Its only real advantage is being completely free and unrestricted for commercial use, unlike Reddit. Use as a legally-unencumbered proxy for Reddit-style community sentiment when the Reddit licensing cost is not justified.

**4chan Read-Only JSON API** — 4chan `LIVE`

- Board catalogs, thread listings and full post text across all boards, updated continuously. Includes /pol/ and /biz/, which are meaningful early-signal venues for political and crypto rumor.
- Docs: https://github.com/4chan/4chan-API
- Base: `https://a.4cdn.org/{board}/catalog.json`
- Auth: none | Limits: No key. Published policy: do NOT make more than one request per second, and you must respect If-Modified-Since / Last-Modified headers. History: threads are ephemeral and prune within hours to days — there is essentially NO backfill from the API itself. VERIFIED LIVE: a.4cdn.org/pol/catalog.json returned a real catalog in 2026.
- Latency: realtime (poll at 1 req/sec) | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: High noise, occasionally very early. Rumors about leaks, resignations and crypto events sometimes appear here first. Because threads vanish, you must capture continuously or lose the data permanently. Useful strictly as an unverified early-warning tripwire that triggers verification against real sources — never as a resolution source, and be aware the content is adversarial and injection-prone.

**GH Archive** — GH Archive (Ilya Grigorik, community-maintained) `LIVE`

- Hourly gzipped JSON archive of every public GitHub event — pushes, PRs, issues, stars, forks, releases — since 2011. Also mirrored as a public BigQuery dataset.
- Docs: https://www.gharchive.org/
- Base: `https://data.gharchive.org/{YYYY-MM-DD}-{H}.json.gz`
- Auth: none | Limits: Free, no key, no documented rate limit on the file server. Backfill: hourly files continuously since 2011-02-12. BigQuery mirror is subject to Google's own free-tier query allowance (1 TB/month). VERIFIED LIVE: https://data.gharchive.org/2026-09-19-0.json.gz returns HTTP 200.
- Latency: hourly batch | Format: Bulk gzipped JSON (one file per hour) + BigQuery
- Relevance: Narrow. Prices 'will project X hit N stars', 'will release vN ship by date D', and AI/OSS adoption contracts. Release events are a hard, timestamped, auditable resolution source for software-shipping markets — that auditability is its real value, more than the attention signal.

**APITube News API** — APITube.io `LIVE`

- Real-time and historical news with pre-computed entities, sentiment, categories and SOURCE BIAS RATINGS attached to every response.
- Docs: https://docs.apitube.io/platform/news-api/quick-start
- Base: `https://api.apitube.io/v1/news/everything`
- Auth: free API key (no credit card) | Limits: Free tier reported as 1,000 requests/day with a 30-requests-per-30-minute window (some sources say 10/min), 10 results per request, first 5 pages of any result set, commercial use allowed, any-origin CORS. TWO IMPORTANT FREE-TIER CATCHES: articles arrive with a 12-HOUR DELAY, and the body is a 200-CHARACTER PREVIEW only — no full content. VENDOR-SOURCED FIGURES: I confirmed apitube.io responds (HTTP 200 in 2026) but the limits come from the vendor's own blog posts, not from a measured API response.
- Latency: 12-hour delayed on the free tier (realtime only on paid) | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: The 12-hour delay disqualifies the free tier for pricing anything time-sensitive — which is most of a prediction market. Its one genuine draw is the built-in source-bias rating, useful for weighting coverage. Treat as a research/backfill convenience, not a live feed.

**GNews API** — GNews.io `LIVE`

- Search and top-headlines endpoints across a Google-News-like index, returning title, description, url, image, publishedAt, source and a content field.
- Docs: https://gnews.io/docs/v4
- Base: `https://gnews.io/api/v4/search`
- Auth: free API key | Limits: EXACT, read off the vendor pricing page (fetched live, HTTP 200 in 2026): 100 requests/day, up to 10 articles per request, 30 days historical data, CORS enabled for localhost only. Two disqualifying free-tier restrictions stated on the page: a 12-HOUR DELAY on article availability, and the content field is TRUNCATED TO A SHORT EXCERPT — full text is paid only.
- Latency: 12-hour delayed on free tier | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: 100 requests/day with a 12-hour delay and localhost-only CORS makes this a prototyping toy. It cannot price anything. Listed so you do not waste a day discovering that yourself.

**Podcast Index API** — Podcast Index LLC (open, community-funded) `LIVE`

- Open index of 4M+ podcasts and their episodes — search by term, by feed, by person; episode metadata, enclosure URLs, transcripts where publishers supply them, and recent-episode feeds. An open alternative to Apple/Spotify's closed catalogs.
- Docs: https://podcastindex-org.github.io/docs-api/
- Base: `https://api.podcastindex.org/api/1.0/`
- Auth: free API key + secret (free self-service, SHA-1 signed requests) | Limits: Free for developers; exact request-per-day limits UNKNOWN and not published. VERIFIED LIVE with a real constraint discovered: the API rejected my request with 'You must set a proper User-Agent string that identifies your application. Sample code UA strings, default http library UA strings and generic or vague UA strings are not allowed.' — a genuine, enforced requirement you must handle. Backfill depth UNKNOWN.
- Latency: near-realtime for new episodes | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: An underexploited channel. Political and financial commentary increasingly breaks on podcasts before print, and episode titles/descriptions are timestamped and searchable. Where transcripts exist it becomes a quotable resolution source. Low effort to wire, genuinely differentiated coverage.

**YouTube Data API v3** — Google `LIVE`

- Video, channel, playlist and comment-thread metadata; search; view/like/comment counts. No transcripts via the official API (captions.download requires channel ownership).
- Docs: https://developers.google.com/youtube/v3/determine_quota_cost
- Base: `https://www.googleapis.com/youtube/v3/`
- Auth: free API key (Google Cloud project); OAuth for user data | Limits: MATERIAL 2026 CHANGE, verified against Google's own quota page: the model changed in June 2026. Projects now get 100 search.list calls/day and 100 videos.insert calls/day as SEPARATE buckets, plus 10,000 units/day combined for all other endpoints. search.list no longer draws from the 10,000 pool — it is hard-capped at 100 calls/day. videos.list, channels.list and commentThreads.list remain 1 unit each. Quota increases require an audited application.
- Latency: near-realtime (statistics update with lag) | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: Badly crippled for discovery by the 100-search/day cap — you cannot sweep YouTube for emerging topics. Still workable for MONITORING a known fixed set of channels (official government, central bank and company channels) via videos.list and commentThreads.list at 1 unit each. Design around ID lookups, never around search.

**Currents API** — Currents API `LIVE`

- Latest-news and search endpoints across multiple languages and regions with category tagging.
- Docs: https://currentsapi.services/en/docs/
- Base: `https://api.currentsapi.services/v1/latest-news`
- Auth: free API key | Limits: UNKNOWN — I confirmed the API is alive (HTTP 401 {"status":"401","msg":"Invalid token"} in 2026) but I could not obtain published free-tier request-per-day, rate-limit or history-depth figures from a source I fetched. Commonly cited as 600 requests/day, but I did not verify that and will not assert it.
- Latency: UNKNOWN | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: Low priority. Coverage overlaps what GDELT already gives you for free at far higher volume. Register only if you specifically need its category taxonomy. Verify its actual limits before depending on it.

**Wikipedia Clickstream dumps** — Wikimedia Foundation `LIVE`

- Monthly aggregated referer→article click pairs with counts — how readers actually navigate between articles, and what external sources (Google, social, other Wikipedia pages) send them there.
- Docs: https://meta.wikimedia.org/wiki/Research:Wikipedia_clickstream
- Base: `https://dumps.wikimedia.org/other/clickstream/`
- Auth: none | Limits: Free, no key, no rate limit. Monthly TSV dumps, counts below 10 are suppressed for privacy. Backfill: monthly files from 2015 to present. VERIFIED LIVE: the dumps directory returns HTTP 200 in 2026.
- Latency: monthly batch | Format: Bulk TSV (gzipped)
- Relevance: Monthly latency rules it out for pricing. Its value is structural: it reveals which entities people associate with each other, which is how you build the related-entity graph for a market ('who reads about candidate A also reads about scandal B'). Use it to construct the research panel's contextual links, not its prices.

**Fact-check publisher RSS feeds (Snopes, Full Fact, EUvsDisinfo)** — Snopes Media Group; Full Fact (UK); EU East StratCom Task Force `LIVE`

- Direct feeds of individual fact-check verdicts with claim text, rating and full reasoning. EUvsDisinfo specifically catalogs pro-Kremlin disinformation cases with the originating outlet, date, country and the debunk — a structured disinformation database rather than a general fact-checker.
- Docs: https://euvsdisinfo.eu/disinformation-cases/
- Base: `https://www.snopes.com/feed/ ; https://fullfact.org/ ; https://euvsdisinfo.eu/disinformation-cases/`
- Auth: none | Limits: No key. No published rate limits (UNKNOWN) — poll politely with conditional requests. RSS gives only recent items; EUvsDisinfo's searchable case database carries the deeper archive (2015-present). VERIFIED LIVE: all three returned HTTP 200 in 2026.
- Latency: daily-to-weekly | Format: RSS + HTML (scrape-or-parameterized-search for the EUvsDisinfo archive)
- Relevance: Complements the Google ClaimReview API with direct, unaggregated access and richer reasoning text. EUvsDisinfo is the specialist tool for geopolitical contracts: knowing that a claim about troop movements originated in a catalogued disinformation channel is directly price-relevant, and no general news API surfaces that.

#### Repos

- `alex9smith/gdelt-doc-api` — Python client for the GDELT 2.0 DOC API returning pandas DataFrames for article lists and all timeline modes. · Fastest path to a working GDELT integration. Wraps the awkward query-operator syntax and the timeline JSON shapes. Read its rate-limit handling before you write your own — the live API enforces 1 request per 5 seconds hard, and I hit 429 repeatedly without backoff.
- `linwoodc3/gdeltPyR` — Python library for pulling and parsing the GDELT 1.0/2.0 BULK CSV files (Events, Mentions, GKG) into DataFrames. · The bulk-file counterpart to the API client, and the more important one for a terminal. Handles the undocumented column schemas of the 15-minute GKG/Events/Mentions files, which are the real firehose (verified current: 20260921004500).
- `gdelt/gdelt.github.io` — Open interface and documentation hub for the GDELT APIs. · Reference for query operators and modes across DOC/TV/Context/Summary. Useful precisely because GDELT's own blog posts are scattered and some describe endpoints that no longer exist — the GEO 2.0 API being the example I confirmed dead.
- `bluesky-social/jetstream` — The official Jetstream server implementation — the lightweight JSON WebSocket firehose for AT Protocol. · Source of truth for the wantedCollections/wantedDids filter syntax and the cursor/replay semantics. Since this is now the best free real-time social firehose (I verified a live 2026-09-21 post frame), you can also self-host it against a relay to remove your dependency on the public instances.
- `bluesky-social/atproto` — The AT Protocol monorepo — lexicons, TypeScript SDK, and the canonical XRPC schemas. · Needed for the authenticated endpoints. I confirmed app.bsky.feed.searchPosts now returns 403 unauthenticated, so you will need session handling from this SDK (or the Python atproto port) for any keyword search.
- `commoncrawl/news-crawl` — The actual StormCrawler-based crawler that produces the CC-NEWS dataset, plus its seed and sitemap logic. · Shows exactly which publishers are in CC-NEWS and how they are discovered, so you know the coverage boundary of your full-text layer. Also a ready-made blueprint if you decide to run your own continuous news crawl for sources CC-NEWS misses.
- `fhamborg/news-please` — Integrated news crawler and extractor that can consume CC-NEWS WARC files directly and also crawl live sites, outputting normalized articles with title, body, authors and publish date. · The single best bridge between GDELT (URLs only) and full text. Point it at GDELT article URLs or at CC-NEWS WARCs and get structured full-text articles out, without writing your own extraction.
- `adbar/trafilatura` — High-accuracy main-content and metadata extractor for web pages, with strong benchmark results against alternatives. · This is the component that turns a GDELT URL into usable article text. Its extraction quality is measurably better than newspaper3k on modern JS-heavy news sites. Also handles feed discovery and sitemap crawling, so it doubles as your RSS registry builder.
- `codelucas/newspaper` — The long-standing newspaper3k article extraction and NLP library. · Widely used and easy, but verify maintenance status before committing — trafilatura generally outperforms it now. Worth knowing because most GDELT tutorials you will find online assume it.
- `kurtmckee/feedparser` — The universal RSS/Atom parser for Python, tolerant of the malformed feeds that dominate the real world. · Foundation of the primary-source RSS registry, which I rank CORE. Handles ETag/Last-Modified conditional fetching natively, which is what keeps you welcome when polling a few hundred publisher feeds every minute.
- `RSS-Bridge/rss-bridge` — Generates RSS/Atom feeds for sites that removed or never had them, via hundreds of site-specific bridges. · Recovers feed access to sources that killed their RSS. Self-host it (the public instance responded 200 but is shared and rate-limited) and you extend your primary-source registry to sites that otherwise require scraping.
- `FreshRSS/FreshRSS` — Self-hosted feed aggregator with a REST API, WebSub/PubSubHubbub push support, and multi-user handling. · Turns 'poll a few hundred feeds' into managed infrastructure with dedup, retention and an API your terminal can query. WebSub support means push rather than poll for publishers that support it — meaningfully lower latency on breaking releases.
- `mediacloud/wayback-news-client` — Python client for searching the Wayback Machine news archive that backs Media Cloud. · Access to a large historical news index without a Media Cloud key. Note the documented limitation: that search matches TITLE TEXT only, not article bodies — do not mistake it for a full-text archive.
- `mediacloud/api-client` — Official Python client for the Media Cloud Search API and source/collection directory. · The way to pull Media Cloud's curated per-country source collections. Those collections are what let you weight media salience by outlet importance instead of treating a content farm and a national daily as equal — the weakness of raw GDELT counts.
- `ArthurHeitmann/arctic_shift` — Actively maintained Reddit archive project providing bulk monthly dumps and a search API, built as the successor to Pushshift for the general public. · Essential, because Pushshift is gone for non-moderators — I confirmed api.pushshift.io now returns 403 'Not authenticated'. This is the only realistic route to historical Reddit data for backtesting, and it sidesteps the Reddit commercial-licensing problem for research use.
- `pushshift/api` — The historical Pushshift API repo and issue tracker. · Reference and cautionary tale only. Keep it on the list so nobody on the team rediscovers Pushshift in a tutorial and wastes time — I verified it returns 403 to unauthenticated callers and is now restricted to Reddit moderators.
- `yiromo/pytrends-modern` — Actively maintained Google Trends client combining features from pytrends and trendspyg, with familiar pytrends-style methods. · The practical replacement for pytrends, which was archived 17 April 2025 and now 429s immediately. Use this (or the trending RSS endpoint I verified live) rather than the dead original.
- `GeneralMills/pytrends` — The original, now-ARCHIVED pseudo-API for Google Trends. · Listed as a dead end marker. Archived April 2025, unmaintained, returns 429 on first call. Still the top search result for 'Google Trends API Python', so flag it explicitly for the team.
- `halcy/Mastodon.py` — Comprehensive Python client for the Mastodon API including the streaming endpoints. · Handles the per-instance auth divergence you will hit — I confirmed mastodon.social now requires authentication for its public timeline (HTTP 422) while fosstodon.org and mstdn.social do not. This library abstracts that and manages app registration per instance.
- `praw-dev/praw` — The Python Reddit API Wrapper — the standard OAuth client for the Reddit Data API. · Implements the OAuth flow and the 100 QPM rolling-window rate limiting correctly. Necessary if you pursue Reddit access, but pair it with a licensing decision first: free tier is non-commercial only.
- `mattpodolak/pmaw` — Multithreaded Pushshift API wrapper for bulk historical Reddit pulls. · Its concurrency and pagination patterns are worth reading and porting to arctic_shift, even though its Pushshift backend is now dead. Good reference for bulk social backfill architecture.
- `LonamiWebs/Telethon` — Full Python implementation of Telegram's MTProto client API. · Telegram public channels are a major, entirely free breaking-news and conflict-reporting venue that none of the news APIs here index — and Telegram's API has no per-call pricing. For geopolitical and crypto contracts this fills a real coverage gap left by X's paywall.
- `JustAnotherArchivist/snscrape` — Scraper for social networking services including Twitter/X, Facebook, Instagram, Telegram and Reddit, requiring no API keys. · Historically the standard free X workaround. Verify current functionality before relying on it — X has repeatedly broken these scrapers, and scraping likely violates X's terms, so treat it as research tooling with legal review, not production infrastructure.
- `vladkens/twscrape` — X/Twitter scraper using authenticated account pools to access the GraphQL API. · The most current free-X approach circulating, relevant because X removed its free tier entirely in February 2026. Same caveat applies in stronger form: account-pool scraping is against X's terms and carries real ban and legal risk. Listed for completeness, not recommended.
- `bytewax/awesome-public-real-time-datasets` — Curated list of publicly available real-time data streams, including GDELT 2.0, Wikimedia EventStreams and news APIs. · The best single index for finding streaming (not batch) sources across every domain the terminal needs. Filtered specifically for real-time, which is what separates a pricing feed from a research dataset.
- `Cyclododecene/newsfeed` — CLI tool built on GDELT that queries the GDELT databases and downloads full-text articles from the command line. · A compact working example of the exact GDELT-discovery-plus-fetch-full-text pattern this domain requires. Good starting reference for the pipeline shape before you build your own.

### Entertainment, Culture & Consumer

#### CORE

**TMDB API (v3)** — The Movie Database `LIVE`

- ~1M+ movies and TV series: titles, release dates per country/type (theatrical, digital, physical), runtime, cast/crew, person 'popularity' score, trending/day and trending/week lists, now_playing, upcoming, discover with date filters, TV season/episode air dates, and watch/providers (JustWatch-licensed streaming availability per country). Also a /changes endpoint that lists every entity changed in the last 24h — this is the key feed for change-detection rather than polling.
- Docs: https://developer.themoviedb.org/docs/getting-started
- Auth: free API key (v3 key or v4 read access token) — register a TMDB account, agree to terms | Limits: No published per-day quota. TMDB removed the old 40-req/10s limit in Dec 2019; current documented guidance is an anti-bulk-scrape ceiling 'in the 40 requests per second range', subject to change, and clients must honour HTTP 429. History depth: full catalogue back to earliest cinema. Non-commercial use free; COMMERCIAL use requires a separate written agreement with TMDB — this matters for a paid terminal.
- Latency: daily (changes endpoint is 24h-windowed; trending recomputed daily/weekly) | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: Anchor entity/ID layer for every film-and-TV contract. Directly prices: 'will film X release on date Y', 'will X premiere on streaming before date Y', streaming-availability contracts, and via person.popularity gives a crude celebrity-attention series. Does NOT give box office dollars.

**Netflix Tudum Top 10 bulk TSV** — Netflix `LIVE`

- Official weekly Top 10 with hours viewed, views, runtime, weeks-in-top-10, per title. Three files: all-weeks-global.tsv (~893 KB, global films+TV, English and non-English lists, weekly back to 28 Jun 2021), all-weeks-countries.tsv (~32 MB, 90+ countries, weekly rank per country), most-popular.tsv (all-time 91-day view leaderboards). Netflix also publishes a half-yearly 'What We Watched' engagement report covering essentially all titles.
- Docs: https://www.netflix.com/tudum/top10
- Auth: none | Limits: No key, no documented rate limit — these are three static files behind a CDN. Full history from 2021-06-28 to present. Updated weekly, normally Tuesday (data week ends Sunday). Pull once a week; do not hammer.
- Latency: weekly | Format: CSV bulk (tab-separated .tsv over HTTPS)
- Relevance: CORE for 'will title X be #1 on Netflix in week Y', 'will X stay in the Top 10 for N weeks', 'hours viewed above/below threshold'. This is the single best free streaming-viewership ground truth in existence — everything else is a panel estimate. Verified live: all-weeks-global.tsv returned HTTP 200 / 893,380 bytes; all-weeks-countries.tsv 200 / 32,208,603 bytes.

**Steam Web API — ISteamChartsService (GetMostPlayedGames, GetGamesByConcurrentPlayers)** — Valve `LIVE`

- Official Steam charts as JSON with NO API key. GetGamesByConcurrentPlayers returns live rank, appid, concurrent_in_game and 24h peak_in_game for the top ~100 games plus a last_update unix timestamp. GetMostPlayedGames returns weekly rollup rank, appid, last_week_rank and peak_in_game with a rollup_date. Verified live payload sample: appid 730 concurrent_in_game 526,952 / peak 1,364,115.
- Docs: https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/webapi/ISteamChartsService
- Auth: none (no key required for these two methods) | Limits: No key, no documented rate limit for these endpoints. Valve's general Web API terms cap keyed access at 100,000 calls/day; these unkeyed chart methods have no published number — UNKNOWN. History depth: snapshot only (current + last week's rank), so you must store your own time series.
- Latency: sub-minute to minutely for concurrent players (last_update advances continuously); weekly for the most-played rollup | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: CORE for every 'peak concurrent players of game X above N on date Y' contract, 'will game X enter the Steam top 10', and launch-day CCU markets. This is Valve's own number — the same number Steam Charts sites derive from — so it is the settlement source, not a proxy.

**Steam per-app endpoints — ISteamUserStats/GetNumberOfCurrentPlayers + store appdetails** — Valve `LIVE`

- GetNumberOfCurrentPlayers/v1/?appid=N returns the instantaneous concurrent player count for ANY appid, not just top-100 (no key needed). store.steampowered.com/api/appdetails?appids=N returns release date, price, publisher, genres, metacritic score, platform support and DLC list for any app.
- Docs: https://steamcommunity.com/dev
- Auth: none for these two; a free Steam Web API key is needed for most other ISteam* interfaces | Limits: GetNumberOfCurrentPlayers: no published limit — UNKNOWN; verified 200. store appdetails is an undocumented storefront endpoint, community-observed at roughly 200 requests per 5 minutes per IP before 429, and it is NOT covered by the Steam Web API terms — treat as best-effort. History depth: none, snapshot only.
- Latency: sub-minute (polled on demand) | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: CORE. Lets you track CCU for a specific game that is not in the top 100 — essential for markets on mid-tier or newly launched titles, and for pre-launch release-date verification via appdetails.

**Apple Marketing Tools RSS Feed Generator** — Apple `LIVE`

- Country-scoped chart JSON for Apple Music (most-played songs, most-played albums, top songs, top albums, new releases, music videos), Apple Books (top free, top paid), Podcasts (top shows, top episodes) and App Store (top free/paid apps). Configurable list length (10/25/50/100) and 175 storefronts.
- Docs: https://rss.marketingtools.apple.com/
- Auth: none | Limits: No key, no published rate limit — UNKNOWN; treat as a CDN JSON file and poll hourly at most. History depth: current chart only, no archive — you must snapshot. NOTE: the older rss.applemarketingtools.com host now 301-redirects to rss.marketingtools.apple.com, and the MOVIES feeds (movies/top-movies) return 404 — Apple retired the iTunes movie charts.
- Latency: daily | Format: REST JSON (chart feed)
- Relevance: CORE for music-chart contracts where Billboard has no free API. 'Will song X be #1 on Apple Music US on date Y' is directly settleable here. Also the only free, no-auth podcast and book chart.

**TVmaze API** — TVmaze `LIVE`

- Full TV schedule: /schedule?country=US&date=YYYY-MM-DD (today's episodes), /schedule/full (every future episode known, one large file), /schedule/web for streaming-only releases, show lookup with premiered/ended/status/network/webChannel, episode lists with airdate and airstamp, cast, and an /updates/shows endpoint returning every show id with its last-update timestamp for incremental sync.
- Docs: https://www.tvmaze.com/api
- Auth: none for the public API; premium key only for user-specific and some extended endpoints | Limits: Documented: approximately 20 calls every 10 seconds per IP on the free public API (429 on exceed). No daily cap published — UNKNOWN. History depth: full historical episode airdates plus the complete forward schedule. Free API is CC BY-SA licensed; commercial use is permitted with attribution.
- Latency: daily | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: CORE for TV-release and premiere-date contracts. /schedule/full plus /updates/shows gives you a complete, incrementally syncable forward TV calendar for free — nothing else free matches this for television.

**New York Times Developer APIs (Books, Movie Reviews, Top Stories, Archive)** — The New York Times `LIVE`

- Books API: the full NYT Bestseller lists (hardcover fiction/nonfiction, combined print & e-book, etc.) for the current week or ANY historical week back to 2008, with rank, rank_last_week, weeks_on_list, ISBNs. Movie Reviews API: NYT critic reviews searchable by opening date and Critics' Pick flag. Archive API: every NYT article back to 1851 by month.
- Docs: https://developer.nytimes.com/apis
- Auth: free API key — NYT developer account, register an app per API | Limits: CONFLICTING SOURCES — treat as UNKNOWN pending your own 429 test. NYT's general documented figure is 500 requests per DAY and 5 requests per MINUTE per API; the Archive API is documented separately at 2,000/day; several third-party write-ups cite 4,000/day and 10/min for the Books API specifically. Do not build assuming more than 500/day. History depth: Bestseller lists from 2008-06-01; Archive from 1851. 401 confirmed live without a key.
- Latency: weekly (bestseller lists publish weekly); daily for reviews | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: CORE for books — 'will book X debut at #1 on the NYT hardcover fiction list' is settleable directly, with full historical lists for base rates. The Movie Reviews API with Critics' Pick is a weak but free awards-season signal.

**Wikimedia Pageviews API** — Wikimedia Foundation `LIVE`

- Daily and hourly pageview counts for ANY Wikipedia article on any language edition, split by access method (desktop/mobile-web/mobile-app) and agent (user/spider/automated), from 2015-07-01 to yesterday. Also top-1000-most-viewed per day per project, per-country aggregates, and unique-devices.
- Docs: https://doc.wikimedia.org/generated-data-platform/aqs/analytics-api/
- Auth: none (descriptive User-Agent required by policy) | Limits: Documented: 100 requests per SECOND per IP for the unauthenticated tier (Wikimedia asks you to stay well under and to set a real User-Agent). History depth: 2015-07-01 to present, daily and hourly granularity. Confirmed live: daily pageviews for a 2021 film returned 200.
- Latency: hourly (hourly endpoint lags ~1-2h; daily settles next day) | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: CORE as a universal attention proxy. Pageview spikes on a film, a nominee, a celebrity or a game are the fastest free leading indicator that exists for award-win markets, celebrity-event markets and opening-weekend markets. Eleven years of daily history means you can actually fit and backtest the attention→outcome mapping instead of guessing.

**Wikidata Query Service (SPARQL)** — Wikimedia Foundation `LIVE`

- Structured, queryable award graph: P166 (award received), P1411 (nominated for), P2453 (nominee), P805, with qualifiers for year, category, and 'for work'. You can enumerate every Oscar/Grammy/Emmy/Golden Globe/BAFTA nomination and win ever recorded, joined to IMDb IDs (P345), TMDB IDs (P4947), MusicBrainz IDs (P434) and Spotify IDs (P1902). Also box-office (P2142), budget (P2130), publication date (P577).
- Docs: https://query.wikidata.org/
- Auth: none (User-Agent required) | Limits: Documented: 60-second query timeout; concurrency capped at 5 parallel queries per IP and 30 queries per MINUTE per IP on the public endpoint; exceeding gets you a 429 then a temporary ban. Bulk work should use the dumps or the new Wikidata Query Service Graph Split endpoints instead. History depth: complete award history back to 1927 for the Oscars.
- Latency: daily (edits propagate to WDQS with lag, typically minutes to hours) | Format: GraphQL-adjacent (SPARQL over HTTP, JSON results)
- Relevance: CORE for awards contracts. This is the only free, structured, cross-award, machine-queryable nomination-and-win database with stable identifiers joining to film/music feeds. It gives you the historical base rates ('how often does the SAG winner take Best Actor') that a market maker actually needs. Weakness: current-year nominations appear only after volunteers enter them — latency on fresh announcements is hours to days, so pair it with a scrape.

**FRED API** — Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis `LIVE`

- 800,000+ economic time series with full revision history. Relevant series: UMCSENT (University of Michigan Consumer Sentiment — the free route to a paywalled survey), CSUSHPINSA (Case-Shiller national home price), MSPUS (median sales price), MORTGAGE30US, RRSFS / RSXFS (retail sales), CPIAUCSL and every CPI component, CUSR0000SEFV (food away from home), HOUST (housing starts), and tourism/lodging series.
- Docs: https://fred.stlouisfed.org/docs/api/fred/
- Auth: free API key — 32-character alphanumeric, self-service registration, no approval step | Limits: Documented: 120 requests per MINUTE per API key (unauthenticated/degraded access is 30/min). 429 on exceed. No daily cap. Single free tier — no paid plans. History depth: varies by series, many back to 1947 or earlier; ALFRED vintages give point-in-time values as originally published, which is what you need to avoid look-ahead bias in backtests. Confirmed live: returned HTTP 400 'Bad Request. The value for variable api_key is not registered' for a fake key.
- Latency: monthly (most consumer series); some weekly (MORTGAGE30US) | Format: REST JSON/XML
- Relevance: CORE for consumer, housing and retail contracts. UMCSENT via FRED is the only free path to Michigan consumer sentiment. The ALFRED vintage feature is the difference between an honest backtest and a fictional one.

**BLS Public Data API v2** — U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics `LIVE`

- CPI (all items and every component down to 'Admission to movies, theaters, and concerts' CUUR0000SERF02 and 'Food away from home'), PPI, average price data for specific goods, employment by industry including leisure and hospitality, and the CPI release calendar.
- Docs: https://www.bls.gov/developers/api_signature_v2.htm
- Auth: free registration key for v2; v1 works with no key at a much lower cap | Limits: Documented exactly. v2 (registered): 500 queries per DAY, 50 series per query, 20 years per query, 50 requests per 10 seconds. v1 (unregistered): 25 queries per DAY, 25 series per query, 10 years per query, 25 requests per 10 seconds. Confirmed live: v2 series endpoint returned 200 unauthenticated.
- Latency: monthly | Format: REST JSON (POST for multi-series)
- Relevance: CORE for 'will CPI print above X' and consumer-price contracts, and it is the settlement source for those. The entertainment-specific CPI components (movie/concert admissions, cable/streaming services) are a genuinely differentiated culture-economics signal almost nobody uses.

**U.S. Census Bureau APIs (MARTS retail, New Residential Construction, ACS)** — U.S. Census Bureau `LIVE`

- Advance Monthly Retail Trade Survey (MARTS) timeseries — retail and food-services sales by NAICS category including 'Food services and drinking places' and 'Electronic shopping'; New Residential Construction (starts, permits, completions); New Home Sales; plus ACS demographics for market-sizing.
- Docs: https://www.census.gov/data/developers/data-sets.html
- Auth: none for light use; free API key recommended and required above the threshold | Limits: Documented: 500 queries per DAY per IP without a key; with a free key the daily cap is lifted (Census does not publish a keyed numeric cap — UNKNOWN). History depth: MARTS monthly back to 1992; NRC back to 1959. Confirmed live: timeseries/eits/marts returned 200 unauthenticated.
- Latency: monthly | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: CORE for retail-sales and housing-starts contracts — this is the primary release, not a derivative. Restaurant-sector contracts settle off the MARTS 722 food-services line.

**Zillow Research public CSVs** — Zillow `LIVE`

- Bulk CSVs of ZHVI (home value index) and ZORI (observed rent index) at national, metro, county, city, ZIP and neighbourhood granularity; plus for-sale inventory, new listings, days-to-pending, median sale-to-list ratio, share of listings with a price cut, and market heat index. Monthly and in some series weekly.
- Docs: https://www.zillow.com/research/data/
- Auth: none | Limits: No key, no rate limit — static CSVs on files.zillowstatic.com. History depth: ZHVI back to 2000, ZORI back to 2015. Licensed for use with attribution to Zillow; Zillow's own API (Bridge Interactive) is partner-restricted and is NOT the free path. Confirmed live: metro ZHVI CSV returned 200 / 4,477,489 bytes.
- Latency: monthly (some weekly series) | Format: CSV bulk
- Relevance: CORE for housing-market contracts at metro granularity — 'will median home value in metro X exceed Y', 'will price cuts exceed N% of listings'. Zillow is what most housing prediction markets actually reference.

**Redfin Data Center bulk TSV** — Redfin `LIVE`

- Weekly and monthly housing market tracker at national, state, metro, county, city, ZIP and neighbourhood level: median sale price, homes sold, new listings, inventory, months of supply, median days on market, share sold above list, price drops, off-market-in-two-weeks. Weekly file gives near-real-time housing.
- Docs: https://www.redfin.com/news/data-center/
- Auth: none | Limits: No key, no rate limit — gzipped TSVs on a public S3 bucket (redfin-public-data.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com). History depth: monthly back to 2012, weekly back to 2015. Free to use with attribution per Redfin's stated terms. Confirmed live: us_national_market_tracker.tsv000.gz returned 200 / 486,979 bytes.
- Latency: weekly | Format: CSV bulk (gzipped TSV on S3)
- Relevance: CORE, and the WEEKLY cadence makes it strictly better than Zillow for short-dated housing contracts. Redfin publishes weekly while Zillow's headline series are monthly — that gap is the edge.

**Awards organisation sites (Emmys.com, Oscars.org, Grammy.com, GoldenGlobes.com)** — ATAS / AMPAS / Recording Academy / Golden Globe Foundation `LIVE`

- Authoritative nominations and winners lists, and — critically — the OFFICIAL CALENDARS: submission deadlines, eligibility windows, nominations-voting open/close dates, nominations announcement date, final-voting window, and ceremony date. These calendar dates are what most award contracts key off.
- Docs: https://www.emmys.com/awards/nominees-winners
- Auth: none | Limits: NO API EXISTS for any of the four. Scrape-only HTML. No published rate limit — scrape politely, once or twice daily, and expect the page structure to change every award cycle. History depth: Emmys back to 1949, Oscars back to 1927 via the AMPAS database. Confirmed live: emmys.com/awards/nominees-winners returned 200 / 703,598 bytes.
- Latency: daily during award season; otherwise static between announcements | Format: scrape-only
- Relevance: CORE for awards contracts despite being scrape-only, because it is the settlement source. Wikidata gives you the clean historical graph; these sites give you the fresh announcement hours-to-days earlier and give you the voting calendar that Wikidata does not model. Build the scraper, accept the maintenance cost, and cross-check against Wikidata.

#### USEFUL

**SteamSpy API** — Sergey Galyonkin (independent) `LIVE`

- Estimated owner counts (bucketed ranges), average and median playtime, concurrent-user estimates, price, developer/publisher, tags and score rank for Steam titles. Endpoints: appdetails, top100in2weeks, top100forever, top100owned, genre, tag, and all (paged, ~1000 apps/page).
- Docs: https://steamspy.com/api.php
- Auth: none | Limits: Documented: 1 request per second for most requests; the 'all' request is limited to 1 request per MINUTE per page. History depth: current snapshot plus 2-week rolling window. Owner numbers are ESTIMATES derived from a shrinking public-profile sample since Valve made profiles private in 2018 — accuracy is degraded and unmeasured.
- Latency: daily | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: USEFUL, not settlement-grade. Good for 'will game X sell above N copies' priors and for ranking which appids deserve a CCU poll. Never settle a contract on a SteamSpy estimate.

**Deezer Public API** — Deezer `LIVE`

- /chart returns top tracks, albums, artists, playlists and podcasts per country with rank; /chart/{genre_id}/tracks for genre charts; full catalogue search, album/track/artist metadata, release dates, ISRC and UPC codes. No auth needed for public (non-user) data.
- Docs: https://developers.deezer.com/api
- Auth: none for public endpoints; OAuth only for user-scoped data | Limits: Documented: 50 requests per 5 seconds per IP; quota headers returned. History depth: current chart only, no archive. Commercial use of Deezer data requires their API terms agreement.
- Latency: daily | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: USEFUL — a second, independent music-chart source to cross-check Apple. ISRC/UPC codes make it the cheapest free way to join a track across Spotify/Apple/MusicBrainz/Billboard scrapes.

**Last.fm API** — Last.fm / CBS Interactive `LIVE`

- chart.getTopArtists, chart.getTopTracks, chart.getTopTags (global scrobble-weighted charts), geo.getTopArtists/Tracks per country, artist.getInfo with global listener and playcount totals, track.getInfo playcounts, tag.getTopArtists, and user-level history. Scrobble counts are a real global listening-volume proxy going back to 2002.
- Docs: https://www.last.fm/api
- Auth: free API key (registration required); API secret + session for write/scrobble | Limits: NOT published in the docs or ToS. The ToS says Last.fm 'sets and enforces limits ... in our sole discretion' and gives no number — EXACT LIMIT UNKNOWN. Widely observed ceiling is ~5 requests/second per originating IP, but that is community folklore, not documentation. History depth: charts back to 2002 via weekly chart list endpoints. IMPORTANT: free use is NON-COMMERCIAL ONLY; commercial or research use requires a separate agreement via partners@last.fm.
- Latency: daily (charts); weekly chart archive endpoints | Format: REST JSON/XML
- Relevance: USEFUL. Global listener and playcount deltas are a leading indicator for chart-position contracts, and the weekly chart archive is one of the few free long-history music-popularity time series. Licensing blocks commercial settlement use.

**Spotify Web API (metadata subset only)** — Spotify `LIVE`

- STILL WORKING for new apps: search, albums (incl. new-releases), tracks, artists (incl. top-tracks), track/album popularity score 0-100, markets, ISRC/UPC in external_ids, and user-owned playlist read/write. NOT working for apps created after 27 Nov 2024: /v1/recommendations, /v1/artists/{id}/related-artists, /v1/audio-features, /v1/audio-analysis, algorithmic and Spotify-owned editorial playlists, 30-second preview URLs in multi-get responses — these return 403.
- Docs: https://developer.spotify.com/documentation/web-api
- Auth: OAuth 2.0 — client credentials for catalogue data; a Spotify PREMIUM account is now required to create an app and use the Web API | Limits: Rate limit is a rolling 30-second window whose size Spotify does not publish — EXACT LIMIT UNKNOWN; apps start in 'development mode' capped at 25 users, and quota-extension requests are reviewed manually and routinely refused. History depth: none (no historical chart or play-count endpoints; spotifycharts.com is gone and charts.spotify.com is login-walled).
- Latency: daily | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: USEFUL for identity (ISRC join keys) and for release-date contracts via new-releases. The popularity field is the only free Spotify-side popularity signal left. Do NOT design a music-market pricer around Spotify — the useful half of the API was removed in Nov 2024 and there is still no replacement in 2026.

**IGDB API v4** — Twitch / Amazon `LIVE`

- ~300k games with first_release_date, per-platform release_dates, status (early access, alpha, cancelled), hypes (pre-release anticipation counter), aggregated critic rating and rating_count, franchises, involved_companies, game_modes, websites, and a /release_dates endpoint you can filter by date range. Apicalypse query language allows server-side filtering and sorting.
- Docs: https://api-docs.igdb.com/
- Auth: free — Twitch developer app, OAuth client-credentials token (Client-ID + Bearer) | Limits: Documented exactly: 4 requests per second, and a maximum of 8 concurrently open requests. 429 on exceed. Max 500 rows per query. Free for commercial and non-commercial use under Twitch developer terms. History depth: full catalogue including historical releases.
- Latency: daily | Format: REST JSON (Apicalypse POST body)
- Relevance: CORE-adjacent for 'will game X ship by date Y' and for delay/slip markets — the release_dates and status fields are the cleanest free structured game-release calendar. The 'hypes' counter is a genuine pre-launch demand proxy.

**RAWG Video Games Database API** — RAWG `LIVE`

- 500,000+ games across 50 platforms: release dates, Metacritic score, ESRB, genres, tags, developers/publishers, 'added' counts (how many RAWG users own/track it), ratings distribution, screenshots, stores and where-to-buy links (paid tier only).
- Docs: https://rawg.io/apidocs
- Auth: free API key on registration | Limits: Documented exactly: 20,000 requests per MONTH on the free plan, NON-COMMERCIAL USE ONLY, attribution + backlink to RAWG required, redistribution of the data prohibited. Business tier $149/month for 50,000 req/month with commercial rights; Enterprise up to 1,000,000/month. History depth: full catalogue.
- Latency: daily | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: USEFUL for game metadata breadth and the crowd 'added' counts as a popularity proxy. The non-commercial clause and the no-redistribution clause make it unusable as a settlement feed for a paid terminal — budget the $149/mo or use IGDB instead.

**OMDb API** — Brian Fritz (independent, IMDb-derived) `LIVE`

- Per-title lookup by IMDb ID or title: IMDb rating and vote count, Rotten Tomatoes and Metacritic scores (Ratings array), BoxOffice field (domestic gross, US titles, sparse), Released/DVD dates, Runtime, Rated, Awards free-text string ('Won 7 Oscars. 178 wins & 267 nominations'), Director/Writer/Actors, and season/episode lookup.
- Docs: https://www.omdbapi.com/
- Auth: free API key emailed on request (email address required) | Limits: Documented exactly: 1,000 requests per DAY on the free key. Patreon tiers raise it (100,000/day at $1/mo tier). No per-minute limit published — UNKNOWN. History depth: full IMDb-derived catalogue. Poster images require the separate poster API key.
- Latency: daily | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: USEFUL — the BoxOffice field is the only free per-title domestic gross available via API at all, though it is incomplete and lags. The Awards string is machine-parseable for award-count contracts. 1,000/day is too small to be a primary feed; use it as an enrichment lookup on the handful of titles that have live markets.

**IMDb Non-Commercial Datasets** — IMDb `LIVE`

- Seven gzipped TSVs refreshed daily: title.basics (every title, type, start/end year, runtime, genres), title.ratings (averageRating + numVotes for every rated title), title.akas, title.crew, title.principals, title.episode, name.basics. title.ratings alone is ~8.6 MB gzipped and is the definitive free vote-count time series if you snapshot it daily.
- Docs: https://developer.imdb.com/non-commercial-datasets/
- Auth: none | Limits: No key, no rate limit — static files at datasets.imdbws.com refreshed daily. History depth: current snapshot only (IMDb does not publish an archive; you must snapshot daily to build history). LICENCE: personal and NON-COMMERCIAL use only. Commercial use requires IMDb's paid API via AWS Data Exchange.
- Latency: daily | Format: CSV bulk (gzipped TSV)
- Relevance: USEFUL for the full title universe and for rating/vote-velocity signals around a release (vote count ramp in the first 72h correlates with opening-weekend interest). The non-commercial licence is a hard blocker for a commercial terminal — verify before building on it.

**Trakt API** — Trakt `LIVE`

- /movies/trending and /shows/trending (ranked by how many Trakt users are watching RIGHT NOW), /movies/played, /watched, /collected, /anticipated (pre-release list counts), /boxoffice (weekend domestic top 10, sourced from a licensed provider), plus calendars: /calendars/all/movies/{date}/{days} and .../shows for release schedules.
- Docs: https://trakt.docs.apiary.io/
- Auth: free API key (client_id) for public endpoints; OAuth for user data | Limits: Documented: 1,000 GET requests every 5 MINUTES per client_id (POST/PUT/DELETE: 1 per second). History depth: trending is a rolling snapshot; played/watched/collected have all-time / yearly / monthly / weekly / daily windows. 403 returned without a client_id (confirmed live).
- Latency: minutely for trending; weekly for boxoffice | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: USEFUL, and the /boxoffice endpoint is notable — it is the only free API surface returning weekend domestic box-office top 10, which is exactly the settlement data for opening-weekend contracts. Verify the number against a second source before settling. /anticipated is a decent pre-release demand proxy.

**Watchmode API** — Watchmode `LIVE`

- Streaming availability across 200+ services in 50+ countries: /title/{id}/sources with deeplinks and price for rent/buy/subscription, /releases (titles newly added to streaming services on a given date), /list-titles with filters, /networks, and mappings between Watchmode IDs and TMDB/IMDb IDs.
- Docs: https://api.watchmode.com/docs
- Auth: free API key on request (email, no credit card) | Limits: Documented: 2,500 API credits per MONTH on the free Developer plan, non-commercial, limited to 3 countries. Different endpoints cost different credit amounts. Paid plans from ~$20/mo. History depth: current availability plus the /releases date feed. 401 confirmed live without a key.
- Latency: daily | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: USEFUL for 'will title X appear on service Y by date Z' windowing contracts. 2,500 credits/month is tight — use it for targeted checks on titles that have live markets, not for corpus-wide sweeps.

**Open Library API + monthly bulk dumps** — Internet Archive `LIVE`

- search.json (full-text-ish catalogue search with first_publish_year, edition counts, ratings, reading-log counts), /works and /books by OLID/ISBN/LCCN, /search/inside full-text search, subject and author endpoints, plus monthly complete bulk dumps of editions, works, authors and ratings.
- Docs: https://openlibrary.org/developers/api
- Auth: none (User-Agent with app name + contact strongly encouraged) | Limits: Documented exactly: 1 request per SECOND for anonymous clients; 3 requests per SECOND if you send a descriptive User-Agent with contact info. Bulk download via the API is explicitly PROHIBITED — use the monthly dumps at openlibrary.org/developers/dumps instead. History depth: full catalogue; dumps monthly.
- Latency: daily (API); monthly (dumps) | Format: REST JSON + CSV bulk (gzipped TSV dumps)
- Relevance: USEFUL. ISBN/OLID resolution layer for book markets, and the reading-log / want-to-read counts are a free demand proxy that partially replaces the dead Goodreads API.

**Google Books API** — Google `LIVE`

- Volume search by title/author/ISBN/publisher with publishedDate, pageCount, categories, averageRating and ratingsCount, industryIdentifiers (ISBN-10/13), and saleInfo with list price and retail price by country.
- Docs: https://developers.google.com/books/docs/v1/using
- Auth: none for public search (heavily throttled); free Google Cloud API key raises the quota; OAuth for user bookshelves | Limits: Documented: 1,000 requests per DAY per project by default (raisable by request in the Cloud Console). Unkeyed requests are throttled far harder — my unauthenticated probe returned HTTP 429 immediately, confirming the endpoint is live but aggressively per-IP limited. History depth: full catalogue.
- Latency: daily | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: USEFUL for publication-date verification and price data on book contracts. Secondary to Open Library because of the 1,000/day cap.

**Wikimedia EventStreams (recentchange)** — Wikimedia Foundation `LIVE`

- Server-sent-event firehose of every edit across all Wikimedia projects in real time: page title, namespace, user, comment, timestamp, byte delta. Filterable client-side by title or wiki.
- Docs: https://wikitech.wikimedia.org/wiki/Event_Platform/EventStreams
- Auth: none | Limits: No key; Wikimedia asks for a descriptive User-Agent and a reasonable number of concurrent connections (no published numeric cap — UNKNOWN). History depth: the stream supports resuming from a `since` offset up to roughly 7 days back. Confirmed live: 200 with a continuous SSE payload.
- Latency: realtime/websocket (server-sent events, sub-second) | Format: WebSocket (SSE)
- Relevance: USEFUL and underrated. An edit burst on 'Academy Award for Best Picture' or a celebrity's page is often the FIRST public machine-readable trace that something happened — faster than the pageview API (hourly lag) and faster than most news wires. Good for celebrity-event and award-announcement contracts.

**Realtor.com Residential Listings economic data (econdata S3)** — Realtor.com / Move Inc. `LIVE`

- Monthly and weekly inventory core metrics at national, state, metro, county and ZIP level: active listing count, median listing price, median days on market, new listings, price-reduced count, pending listings, and year-over-year deltas. Also a historical median-listing-price series.
- Docs: https://www.realtor.com/research/data/
- Auth: none | Limits: No key, no rate limit — static CSVs on econdata.s3-us-west-2.amazonaws.com. History depth: monthly back to July 2016; weekly series available. Free for non-commercial and press use with attribution; commercial redistribution terms are ambiguous — check before shipping. Confirmed live: RDC_Inventory_Core_Metrics_Metro.csv returned 200 / 297,583 bytes.
- Latency: weekly | Format: CSV bulk
- Relevance: USEFUL as the third independent housing source. Zillow, Redfin and Realtor.com disagree on the same metro by meaningful margins; a market maker wants all three and should know which one the contract names as settlement.

**Eurostat REST API** — European Commission `LIVE`

- Tourism statistics (tour_occ_nim monthly nights spent at tourist accommodation by country and NUTS region, arrivals, occupancy rates), HICP consumer prices, retail trade volume, house price index (prc_hpi_q), and consumer confidence indicators — all for 27 EU states plus EFTA.
- Docs: https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/web/main/data/web-services
- Auth: none | Limits: No key. Documented soft limits: 50 requests per user per 10 seconds; a single response is capped at 1,000,000 cells and 50 categories per dimension. History depth: tourism monthly back to 1990 for many countries; HICP back to 1996. Confirmed live: tour_occ_nim returned 200.
- Latency: monthly | Format: REST JSON (JSON-stat / SDMX)
- Relevance: USEFUL — the best free structured tourism feed anywhere, since UNWTO is paywalled. Prices European travel, hotel-occupancy and consumer-price contracts. US-only terminals can skip it.

**TSA Passenger Throughput** — U.S. Transportation Security Administration `LIVE`

- Daily count of travellers screened at all TSA checkpoints nationwide, with the same-weekday prior-year comparison. The canonical high-frequency US domestic travel-demand indicator.
- Docs: https://www.tsa.gov/travel/passenger-volumes
- Auth: none | Limits: NO API — this is an HTML table on a government page; scrape-only. No rate limit published; scrape once daily. History depth: 2019 to present on the live page, with prior years in archived tables. Confirmed live: page returned 200 / 186,441 bytes.
- Latency: daily (posted next morning for the prior day) | Format: scrape-only (HTML table)
- Relevance: USEFUL for travel-and-tourism contracts and as a broad consumer-discretionary-spending nowcast. Daily cadence with a government source makes it unusually clean for a scraped feed. Several GitHub repos already publish it as CSV — reuse one rather than writing your own parser.

**iTunes Search API** — Apple `LIVE`

- Search across Apple's catalogue of music, movies, TV, books, podcasts and apps: trackName, collectionName, artistName, releaseDate, trackPrice, collectionPrice, primaryGenreName, contentAdvisoryRating, plus the lookup endpoint by id/upc/isbn/amgArtistId.
- Docs: https://performance-partners.apple.com/search-api
- Auth: none | Limits: Documented: approximately 20 calls per MINUTE per IP (Apple states the limit is not guaranteed and may vary; 403 on exceed). History depth: full catalogue with release dates. Confirmed live: returned 200.
- Latency: daily | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: USEFUL as a free, no-auth cross-media release-date and price lookup — one endpoint covers film, TV, music, books and podcasts, which is rare. Good fallback when TMDB or the music feeds disagree on a release date.

**MusicBrainz API + bulk dumps** — MetaBrainz Foundation `LIVE`

- Open music encyclopedia: artists, release groups, releases with exact release dates per country, recordings with ISRC, labels, works, and stable MBIDs. Plus complete twice-weekly database dumps (Postgres-loadable) and the ListenBrainz companion service for open listen counts.
- Docs: https://musicbrainz.org/doc/MusicBrainz_API
- Auth: none (a meaningful User-Agent with app name, version and contact URL/email is MANDATORY) | Limits: Documented exactly: approximately 1 request per SECOND per IP sustained (bursts tolerated, then HTTP 503); the whole service averages 300 req/s globally; anonymous or generic User-Agents (blank, 'Java', 'Python-urllib') are throttled to a stricter 50 req/s shared bucket and risk being blocked. Bulk download via the API is prohibited — use the twice-weekly dumps. History depth: full recorded-music history. Data is CC0/CC-BY-NC depending on table. Confirmed live: ws/2 artist search returned 200.
- Latency: daily (live DB); twice-weekly (dumps) | Format: REST JSON/XML + CSV bulk (Postgres dumps)
- Relevance: USEFUL as the identity backbone for music markets — MBID + ISRC is how you join a Billboard scrape to an Apple chart to a Spotify record without fuzzy string matching. Not a popularity feed itself.

#### NICHE

**Simkl API** — Simkl `LIVE`

- /movies/trending, /tv/trending, /anime/trending with configurable time windows, plus calendar/release endpoints, user watchlists, and ID mappings across TMDB/IMDb/TVDB/MAL/AniDB. Streaming links are JustWatch-powered.
- Docs: https://simkl.docs.apiary.io/
- Auth: free client_id (app registration); OAuth only for user data | Limits: No published numeric rate limit — UNKNOWN. Trending endpoints returned 200 with ~37 KB payload with no key at all (confirmed live). History depth: rolling trending windows only.
- Latency: daily | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: NICHE. Its real value is the cross-service ID mapping table (TMDB↔IMDb↔TVDB↔MAL), which saves you building your own entity resolution across film/TV/anime feeds.

**Jikan API (unofficial MyAnimeList)** — Jikan community project `LIVE`

- MyAnimeList data without MAL auth: /top/anime and /top/manga rankings, /seasons/{year}/{season} seasonal charts, /anime with score, scored_by (vote count), members, favorites, rank, popularity, airing status and broadcast day, plus /schedules for the weekly airing calendar.
- Docs: https://docs.api.jikan.moe/
- Auth: none | Limits: Documented exactly: 3 requests per SECOND and 60 requests per MINUTE per IP; daily limit is unlimited. Responses cached ~24h. History depth: full MAL catalogue with seasonal archives back to 1917.
- Latency: daily | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: NICHE but the best free anime feed. Members/scored_by deltas price 'will anime X be the top-rated of the season' and seasonal-premiere contracts. Prediction markets on anime are thin but exist.

**AniList GraphQL API** — AniList `LIVE`

- Anime/manga with averageScore, popularity, trending score, rankings, airingSchedule (exact next-episode timestamps), status, startDate/endDate, and staff/studio links. GraphQL lets you fetch exactly the fields you need in one call.
- Docs: https://docs.anilist.co/
- Auth: none for public queries; OAuth for user data | Limits: Documented: 90 requests per MINUTE per IP (reduced from 90 to a lower degraded rate during incidents; check X-RateLimit-Remaining header). History depth: full catalogue with airing schedules. GET returns 404 — the endpoint is POST-only (confirmed live: POST returned 200).
- Latency: realtime/websocket-adjacent (airingSchedule gives exact future episode timestamps); daily for trending | Format: GraphQL
- Relevance: NICHE. Best free source of exact future episode air timestamps for any medium — useful as a scheduling primitive well beyond anime.

**Discogs API** — Discogs `LIVE`

- Release and master metadata with exact release dates, formats, labels, catalogue numbers, and — distinctively — the Discogs MARKETPLACE: num_for_sale, lowest_price, and community have/want counts per release. A real secondary-market price signal for physical music.
- Docs: https://www.discogs.com/developers
- Auth: none for basic public queries; free personal access token or OAuth for higher limits and marketplace data | Limits: Documented exactly: 60 requests per MINUTE for authenticated requests, 25 requests per MINUTE for unauthenticated, per source IP, measured over a rolling 60-second window; X-Discogs-Ratelimit headers returned. Custom User-Agent mandatory. History depth: full catalogue. Confirmed live: api.discogs.com returned 200.
- Latency: daily | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: NICHE for prediction markets, but the have/want ratio and lowest_price are a genuine collectibles-and-vinyl demand signal — relevant if anyone writes contracts on reissue value or physical sales.

**TheAudioDB API** — TheAudioDB (community) `LIVE`

- Artist and album metadata, discographies, music videos, genre and mood tags, artist biographies in multiple languages, and album review scores. Test key '2' is open for development.
- Docs: https://www.theaudiodb.com/api_guide.php
- Auth: test key '2' works with no registration; a Patreon supporter key ($;low monthly) unlocks the full endpoint set | Limits: NOT published — UNKNOWN. The free test key is explicitly development-only and returns a reduced endpoint set; production use requires the Patreon key. Confirmed live: search.php with key 2 returned 200 / 30,098 bytes.
- Latency: daily | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: NICHE. Enrichment only — biographies and artwork. Nothing here settles a contract. Include for completeness, do not build on it.

**Gutendex (Project Gutenberg API)** — Gutendex / Project Gutenberg `LIVE`

- Full Project Gutenberg catalogue of ~75,000 public-domain books with per-book DOWNLOAD COUNTS, authors with birth/death years, subjects, bookshelves, languages and format links.
- Docs: https://gutendex.com/
- Auth: none | Limits: No key, no published rate limit — UNKNOWN. Self-hostable (open source) if you need volume. History depth: full catalogue; download counts are a rolling 30-day figure. Confirmed live: returned 200 / 23,830 bytes.
- Latency: daily | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: NICHE. The download-count field is a free public-domain reading-demand signal — spikes when a classic gets a film adaptation, which is a small but real cross-domain leading indicator for adaptation-related markets.

**World Bank Indicators API** — World Bank `LIVE`

- Country-year indicators including ST.INT.ARVL (international tourism arrivals), ST.INT.RCPT.CD (tourism receipts), NE.CON.PRVT.KD.ZG (household consumption growth), FP.CPI.TOTL (CPI), and several hundred consumer and services indicators for ~215 economies.
- Docs: https://datahelpdesk.worldbank.org/knowledgebase/topics/125589
- Auth: none | Limits: No key, no published rate limit — UNKNOWN (the service is tolerant; page size max 32,500 per request). History depth: most series 1960 to present, ANNUAL only. Confirmed live: US tourism arrivals returned 200 / 11,335 bytes.
- Latency: monthly at best — in practice ANNUAL with a 12-24 month publication lag | Format: REST JSON/XML
- Relevance: NICHE. The annual cadence and long lag make it near-useless for short-dated contracts. Value is structural: base rates and country-level priors for tourism markets. Do not treat it as a live feed.

#### Repos

- `DLu/oscar_data` — Curated Academy Award nominations dataset, every ceremony 1927 to present, with IMDb tconst/nconst identifiers already joined. 31 stars, last pushed 2026-04-22 — actively maintained through the 2026 ceremony. · Saves you the entire Oscars entity-resolution problem. The IMDb-ID join is the hard part and it is already done; you can go straight from a nomination row to a TMDB/OMDb lookup. Use it as the historical base-rate table and scrape Oscars.org only for the current cycle.
- `SteamTracking/SteamTracking` — Automated, continuously-updated tracking of every Steam client, storefront and Web API change. Includes API/IStoreService.json and the full machine-readable inventory of Steam Web API interfaces and methods. 1,101 stars, last pushed 2026-09-19. · The authoritative answer to 'which Steam endpoints actually exist right now'. This is how you find out that ISteamApps/GetAppList died and ISteamChartsService appeared, without guessing. Poll it to detect Steam API breakage before your feed silently goes stale.
- `guoguo12/billboard-charts` — The de-facto Python client for Billboard chart data, scraping billboard.com. Supports Hot 100, Billboard 200, Global 200 and ~hundreds of other charts, with historical date lookup and rank/peak/weeks-on-chart fields. 433 stars, last pushed 2024-08-13. · Billboard has no API and Luminate data is expensive, so this is the only practical free route to chart-position contracts. CAVEAT: last push was 2024 — Billboard changes its page markup regularly, so verify it still parses before depending on it, and be aware scraping billboard.com is against their ToS.
- `tjwaterman99/boxofficemojo-scraper` — GitHub Actions-based scraper that publishes a nightly CSV of domestic box office statistics to the repo's Releases tab. 19 stars, last pushed 2025-01-07. · A working pattern for free box-office data: someone else runs the scraper on Actions and you just download the release asset. Even if this specific repo goes stale, the architecture (Actions cron → scrape → publish CSV as a release) is the right way to build your own box-office feed without hosting infrastructure.
- `jacobkap/boxoffice` — R scraper covering BOTH boxofficemojo.com and the-numbers.com, with weekend and daily gross extraction. 10 stars, last pushed 2020-07-21. · Stale, but it documents the the-numbers.com page structure and URL patterns, which is worth more than the code — the-numbers.com now returns HTTP 403 to plain clients behind Cloudflare, so you need the URL map plus a browser-grade fetcher.
- `dawoudt/JustWatchAPI` — Python 3 client for JustWatch's undocumented internal API — streaming availability, offers, prices and popularity per country. 345 stars, last pushed 2024-05-21. · The only free route to JustWatch's raw availability and popularity data. CAVEAT: this is an unofficial reverse-engineered client against an undocumented endpoint, JustWatch's terms forbid commercial use, and the repo has not been touched since 2024. For anything commercial, use TMDB's licensed /watch/providers instead — TMDB pays JustWatch for exactly this.
- `twitchtv/igdb-api-node` — Official Twitch-maintained Node.js client for IGDB API v4, wrapping the Apicalypse query language. 136 stars, last pushed 2025-02-18. · Official and current. Apicalypse's query syntax is unusual enough that hand-rolling it wastes a day; this handles auth token refresh against Twitch OAuth too. Sister repos exist for Python, PHP and Ruby under the same org.
- `internetarchive/openlibrary` — The full Open Library application source plus documentation for the bulk dumps, the search schema and the ratings/reading-log data model. 6,692 stars, last pushed 2026-09-21 — very actively maintained. · Authoritative reference for the dump file formats and field semantics, which are not fully documented on the public API page. If you plan to ingest the monthly editions/works/ratings dumps rather than hit the 1 req/s API, you need this repo to parse them correctly.
- `metabrainz/listenbrainz-server` — Open-source, CC0-licensed listening-history service and the source of the ListenBrainz API and its full public data dumps. 1,014 stars, last pushed 2026-09-18. · The open replacement for Last.fm's commercially-restricted scrobble data. ListenBrainz publishes complete listen dumps under CC0, so unlike Last.fm you can legally use the aggregate listening counts in a commercial product. Smaller panel than Last.fm, but unencumbered.
- `woctezuma/steam-store-snapshots` — Periodic snapshots of the complete Steam app list, preserved as dated files. 7 stars, last pushed 2025-11-25. · Directly solves the ISteamApps/GetAppList removal: it gives you a historical and current Steam appid universe without needing an API key or hitting IStoreService. Also useful for detecting delistings — an appid present in an old snapshot and absent from the current store is a removal event.
