### GAPS AND MISSING COVERAGE

#### CORE

**World Bank Indicators API v2** — World Bank

- ~16,000 indicators for 200+ economies: GDP, population, poverty, education, health, energy, governance. Annual, some quarterly. Also Global Economic Prospects forecasts.
- Docs: https://datahelpdesk.worldbank.org/knowledgebase/articles/889392
- Auth: none | Limits: No published hard limit; no key. Pagination default 50/page, per_page up to 32500. UNKNOWN throttle.
- Latency: daily-to-annual depending on series | Format: REST JSON/XML
- Relevance: Baseline denominators for nearly every non-US macro contract; country-level GDP/population/inflation thresholds; the standard cross-country join spine.

**IMF DataMapper API v2** — International Monetary Fund `LIVE`

- WEO projections and historical series by country/indicator/group — GDP growth, inflation, fiscal balance, debt, current account. Includes IMF's own forecast, which is itself a market-relevant prior.
- Docs: https://www.imf.org/external/datamapper/api/help
- Auth: none | Limits: No key, no documented limit. UNKNOWN throttle.
- Latency: WEO twice yearly (April/October); some series quarterly | Format: REST JSON (base https://www.imf.org/external/datamapper/api/v2/)
- Relevance: 'Will country X's IMF-projected growth exceed N', IMF program approvals, debt-distress and default markets. The April/October WEO release dates are themselves scheduled contract events.

**OECD SDMX REST API** — OECD

- OECD Data Explorer full catalog over SDMX 2.1/3.0 — CPI, unemployment, PISA, DAC aid flows, taxation, productivity, composite leading indicators for 38 members plus partners.
- Docs: https://gitlab.com/sis-cc/dotstatsuite-documentation/-/wikis/Using-Application-Programming-Interfaces-(APIs)
- Auth: none | Limits: No key. SDMX queries throttled by response size; bulk pulls should use dataflow-scoped queries. UNKNOWN exact limit.
- Latency: monthly to annual | Format: SDMX-ML / SDMX-JSON REST (base https://sdmx.oecd.org/public/rest/)
- Relevance: Non-US inflation and unemployment contracts, PISA score markets, OECD aid and tax-policy milestones.

**BIS Statistics API v2** — Bank for International Settlements

- Cross-border banking claims, credit-to-GDP gaps, residential property prices, effective exchange rates, FX/OTC derivatives turnover (Triennial Survey), central bank policy rates for ~40 jurisdictions.
- Docs: https://stats.bis.org/api-doc/v2/
- Auth: none | Limits: No key. UNKNOWN throttle.
- Latency: monthly/quarterly; Triennial Survey every 3 years | Format: SDMX REST (JSON/CSV)
- Relevance: The single cleanest free source for non-US policy rates — essential for 'will the BoJ/RBA/Banxico hike by date X' contracts that FRED covers poorly.

**ALFRED — ArchivaL Federal Reserve Economic Data** — Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis

- VINTAGE data: what every FRED series said on every past date. Retrieves the ORIGINAL first print of CPI, payrolls, GDP before revision, plus the full revision history.
- Docs: https://fred.stlouisfed.org/docs/api/fred/series_observations.html
- Auth: free API key (same key as FRED) | Limits: Shares the FRED key; FRED documents 120 requests/minute.
- Latency: same as FRED, with vintage dimension | Format: REST JSON/XML (realtime_start / realtime_end / vintage_dates params)
- Relevance: CRITICAL AND ENTIRELY ABSENT FROM THE INVENTORY. Economic contracts settle on the FIRST PRINT, not the revised value. Backtesting a CPI or payrolls model against current-vintage FRED data is a silent, severe look-ahead bias. Also required to settle disputes about what a number 'was'.

**Philadelphia Fed Survey of Professional Forecasters** — Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia

- Quarterly consensus and full individual-forecaster distributions for GDP, CPI, unemployment, recession probability (the Anxious Index), plus historical forecast-error records per forecaster.
- Docs: https://www.philadelphiafed.org/surveys-and-data/real-time-data-research/survey-of-professional-forecasters
- Auth: none | Limits: Bulk XLSX/CSV download, unmetered.
- Latency: quarterly | Format: XLSX / CSV bulk
- Relevance: The free consensus prior. Also the Real-Time Data Research Center publishes real-time vintage macro datasets — the academic complement to ALFRED. Anxious Index directly prices recession contracts.

**Metaculus API** — Metaculus

- Question metadata, resolution criteria text, community prediction time series, Metaculus Prediction, resolution status and historical Brier/log scores per question.
- Docs: https://www.metaculus.com/api/
- Auth: none for public reads; token for writes | Limits: UNKNOWN — fetch of the docs page returned empty in this session. Community wrappers suggest unauthenticated reads are permitted with modest throttling.
- Latency: near-realtime as forecasts update | Format: REST JSON (/api2/questions/ legacy, /api/ current)
- Relevance: A calibrated, scored non-market prior on exactly the geopolitical and science questions where Polymarket/Kalshi are thin. Its resolution-criteria text is a free corpus of well-written settlement definitions.

**Manifold Markets API v0** — Manifold

- All markets, full bet history, comments, user positions, liquidity. Play-money but very broad question coverage and fully open.
- Docs: https://docs.manifold.markets/api
- Auth: none for reads; key for trading | Limits: Documented as ~500 reads/min per IP; bulk dumps published separately. UNKNOWN current figure.
- Latency: realtime | Format: REST JSON + full bulk data dumps
- Relevance: The broadest free cross-section of forecastable questions anywhere, including long-tail questions no real-money venue lists. Bet-level history makes it the only free dataset for studying probability dynamics end-to-end.

**Adjacent News API** — Adjacent (adj.news)

- Normalized cross-venue prediction-market data — Polymarket, Kalshi, Manifold, Metaculus and others mapped to common question entities, with news linkage.
- Docs: https://docs.adj.news/
- Auth: free API key (registration) | Limits: UNKNOWN — free developer tier advertised, exact quota not confirmed.
- Latency: near-realtime | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: Solves the cross-venue entity-resolution problem the inventory never mentions: the same real-world question priced on three venues under three different titles. This IS the arbitrage/edge layer of the terminal.

**UMA Optimistic Oracle — subgraph and API** — UMA Protocol

- Every Polymarket resolution proposal, the proposed outcome, the bond, disputes raised, and final DVM vote. On-chain and queryable.
- Docs: https://docs.uma.xyz/developers/optimistic-oracle-v3
- Auth: none (public subgraph / RPC) | Limits: Public subgraph via The Graph free tier; rate limits per gateway key. UNKNOWN exact.
- Latency: realtime (block-time) | Format: GraphQL subgraph + EVM RPC
- Relevance: Polymarket contracts do not settle on reality, they settle on what UMA proposers assert and nobody successfully disputes. Disputed-resolution risk is a first-class, tradeable, entirely unmodeled factor. The inventory lists Gamma/CLOB for prices but nothing for HOW markets actually resolve.

**OpenFIGI API v3** — Bloomberg (open, free)

- Maps ISIN, SEDOL, CUSIP, ticker, exchange code, composite and share-class identifiers to FIGI and to each other. Free bulk mapping and search.
- Docs: https://www.openfigi.com/api
- Auth: free API key (registration; works keyless at lower limits) | Limits: Documented as ~25 requests/min keyless and 25 jobs per request; ~250 requests/min with a free key, 100 jobs per request. UNKNOWN whether 2026 figures still match. Fetch returned 503 in this session.
- Latency: daily reference | Format: REST JSON (POST /v3/mapping, /v3/search)
- Relevance: The only free path from an ISIN or CUSIP to a tradeable ticker. Without it, equity, ETF and corporate-event feeds cannot be joined to each other or to SEC filings. Absent from the inventory entirely.

**SEC company_tickers.json + CIK lookup** — US SEC

- Authoritative ticker↔CIK↔company-name mapping, plus ticker-to-exchange file. The join key for every EDGAR-derived feed.
- Docs: https://www.sec.gov/file/company-tickersjson
- Auth: none (User-Agent header required) | Limits: SEC fair-access: 10 requests/second across all sec.gov endpoints.
- Latency: daily | Format: static JSON
- Relevance: Trivial but load-bearing. The inventory lists five EDGAR endpoints and no way to get from a ticker on Kalshi to a CIK.

**OurAirports + OpenFlights reference data** — OurAirports (public domain) / OpenFlights

- Every airport worldwide with IATA, ICAO, local code, lat/lon, elevation, runways, frequencies; airline IATA/ICAO codes and route data.
- Docs: https://ourairports.com/data/
- Auth: none | Limits: Public-domain CSV bulk, unmetered.
- Latency: continuous community updates; daily CSV rebuild | Format: CSV bulk
- Relevance: Required to resolve ADS-B hex codes, NOTAMs, FAA ground stops and BTS on-time statistics to a single airport entity. The inventory has four aviation feeds and no airport registry.

**US Census Geocoder + TIGERweb + GEOID/FIPS** — US Census Bureau

- Free batch and single-address geocoding to block-group, plus every FIPS state/county/tract/place code and TIGER boundary geometry.
- Docs: https://geocoding.geo.census.gov/geocoder/
- Auth: none | Limits: Batch geocoder accepts 10,000 addresses per file upload; no key. UNKNOWN per-IP throttle.
- Latency: annual vintage updates | Format: REST JSON + batch CSV upload + TIGER shapefiles
- Relevance: FIPS is the join key between election results, BLS/BEA regional data, FEMA declarations, drought monitor polygons and NWS zones. Named in the task as missing and genuinely absent.

**Nominatim / Overpass / Overture Maps** — OpenStreetMap Foundation / Overture Maps Foundation

- Global forward and reverse geocoding, arbitrary OSM feature queries, and Overture's cloud-native GeoParquet places/buildings/transportation/divisions layers on AWS and Azure.
- Docs: https://nominatim.org/release-docs/latest/api/Overview/
- Auth: none (public Nominatim: strict 1 req/sec + User-Agent); Overture: none | Limits: Public Nominatim: 1 request/second absolute maximum, no bulk — self-host for real volume. Overture: unmetered S3/Azure parquet.
- Latency: OSM minutely diffs; Overture monthly releases | Format: REST JSON (Nominatim), Overpass QL, GeoParquet (Overture)
- Relevance: Turning ACLED/GDELT/news place names into coordinates and coordinates into admin units. Overture's divisions layer is the best free global admin-boundary hierarchy for resolving 'which oblast/province' questions.

**GeoNames API + bulk dump** — GeoNames

- 11M+ placenames with alternate names in all languages, admin hierarchy, population, timezone; country-info, timezone and hierarchy web services.
- Docs: https://www.geonames.org/export/web-services.html
- Auth: free username registration | Limits: Free account: 20,000 credits/day and 1,000/hour (credits, not calls — some endpoints cost more). Bulk dumps unmetered.
- Latency: daily dump rebuild | Format: REST JSON/XML + tab-delimited bulk
- Relevance: Alternate-name resolution is what lets you match 'Bakhmut'/'Artemivsk'/'Бахмут' across ACLED, GDELT, DeepStateMap and Telegram sources — the hardest unaddressed problem in the whole inventory.

**Wikidata Query Service (SPARQL) as universal join + future-event calendar** — Wikimedia Foundation

- Cross-identifier mapping (LEI↔ticker↔CIK↔ISIN↔VIAF↔IMDb↔FIPS↔ICAO), plus queryable scheduled future events: elections, launches, tournaments, film releases, treaty deadlines, terms of office with end dates.
- Docs: https://query.wikidata.org/
- Auth: none (User-Agent required) | Limits: 60-second query timeout; ~5 concurrent queries per IP; heavy use should mirror the dumps or use the split Scholarly/Main graphs.
- Latency: near-realtime edits, minutes to index | Format: SPARQL endpoint + weekly RDF dumps
- Relevance: The inventory lists Wikidata twice as an attention proxy and never as what it actually is: the only free, queryable registry of KNOWN FUTURE EVENTS and the universal identifier crosswalk. 'List every national election scheduled in the next 18 months' is one SPARQL query.

**RIPEstat Data API + RIPE Atlas** — RIPE NCC

- RIPEstat: BGP routing state, announced prefixes, AS neighbours, routing history, country routing stats, abuse contacts, RPKI validity. RIPE Atlas: 10,000+ hardware probes running on-demand ping/traceroute/DNS measurements worldwide.
- Docs: https://stat.ripe.net/docs/02.data-api/
- Auth: none for RIPEstat; free account + credits for Atlas measurements | Limits: RIPEstat: no key, soft-limited, UNKNOWN exact. Atlas: hosting a probe earns credits; results of all public measurements are free to read.
- Latency: BGP near-realtime (8-minute RIS updates); Atlas measurements on demand | Format: REST JSON; Atlas streaming API
- Relevance: Country-level internet shutdown contracts, submarine-cable-cut detection, sanctions-driven routing withdrawal, and verifying censorship claims that GDELT only reports secondhand.

**Cloudflare Radar API** — Cloudflare `LIVE`

- Country and ASN traffic levels, detected internet outages with cause annotations, BGP hijack/leak events, DDoS attack trends, DNS query composition, protocol and browser adoption, top domains.
- Docs: https://developers.cloudflare.com/radar/
- Auth: free Cloudflare API token | Limits: Free. LICENSE TRAP: data is CC BY-NC 4.0 — NON-COMMERCIAL ONLY. A revenue-generating terminal cannot redistribute it without a separate agreement.
- Latency: sub-hourly; outage annotations near-realtime | Format: REST JSON
- Relevance: The fastest free confirmation that a country went dark — election-related shutdowns, coup-adjacent blackouts, cable cuts. Note the non-commercial restriction before building on it.

**NVD CVE API 2.0** — NIST National Vulnerability Database

- Every CVE with CVSS v2/v3.1/v4 scores, CPE applicability, CWE, references, and change history. Plus CPE dictionary and CVE Change History APIs.
- Docs: https://nvd.nist.gov/developers/vulnerabilities
- Auth: free API key (strongly recommended) | Limits: Without key: 5 requests per 30-second rolling window. With free key: 50 requests per 30 seconds. Full JSON feeds also available for bulk.
- Latency: hours to days after CVE publication (NVD enrichment backlog is a known 2024-2026 problem) | Format: REST JSON + bulk JSON feeds
- Relevance: Base layer for any cyber contract. NOTE the enrichment backlog: NVD is slower than the CVE Program itself, so pair with cveawg.mitre.org for speed and NVD for scores.

**CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog** — CISA `LIVE`

- Authoritative US-government list of CVEs confirmed exploited in the wild, with date added, required remediation date, ransomware-use flag and vendor/product.
- Docs: https://www.cisa.gov/known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog
- Auth: none | Limits: Static JSON and CSV at /sites/default/files/feeds/known_exploited_vulnerabilities.json and /sites/default/files/csv/known_exploited_vulnerabilities.csv. Unmetered.
- Latency: updated on CISA determination, typically same-day for major events | Format: static JSON / CSV
- Relevance: 'Will CVE-X be added to KEV by date Y' is a directly settleable contract, and KEV addition is the standard trigger for enterprise emergency patching — a tradeable event for security vendors.

**NOAA NCEI Billion-Dollar Weather and Climate Disasters** — NOAA NCEI

- Every US weather/climate disaster exceeding $1B (CPI-adjusted) since 1980: event type, dates, deaths, and CPI-adjusted cost with 90% confidence intervals.
- Docs: https://www.ncei.noaa.gov/access/billions/
- Auth: none | Limits: CSV/JSON download and a documented API endpoint. Unmetered. NOTE: this product's future funding has been politically contested — verify it is still being updated in 2026.
- Latency: quarterly updates; event costs finalized months later | Format: CSV / JSON API
- Relevance: 'Will 2026 see N+ billion-dollar disasters' and total-annual-cost contracts. The canonical US settlement source for disaster cost. Entirely absent from the Natural Disasters domain despite being the most-cited number in it.

**OpenFEMA API** — FEMA

- Disaster declarations summaries, Individual Assistance and Public Assistance obligations, NFIP claims (2.6M+ records) and policies, Hazard Mitigation grants, IPAWS alerts archive.
- Docs: https://www.fema.gov/about/reports-and-data/openfema/api
- Auth: none | Limits: 1,000 records per page default, 10,000 max per call; full CSV/JSON bulk files. No key. UNKNOWN throttle.
- Latency: daily; declarations posted within days of signing | Format: REST JSON/CSV (OData-style $filter/$select) + bulk
- Relevance: 'Will a federal disaster be declared for county X' is directly settleable. NFIP claims give real insured-loss magnitude for flood events — the only free granular US catastrophe-loss data.

**FDIC BankFind Suite API** — US FDIC `LIVE`

- All insured institutions, branch locations, quarterly financials (call-report derived), structure-change history, Summary of Deposits, and the failed-institution list.
- Docs: https://api.fdic.gov/banks/docs
- Auth: none required (optional free key for monitoring) | Limits: No key required as of this check. UNKNOWN throttle.
- Latency: financials quarterly; failures posted on the Friday they occur | Format: REST JSON (OpenAPI/swagger published)
- Relevance: 'Will a US bank with >$N assets fail before date X' was a top-volume 2023 contract class and has no feed in the inventory despite 'bank failures' appearing as a listed subdomain. The failures endpoint settles it directly.

**NGA Maritime Safety Information — ASAM and NAVAREA warnings** — US National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency

- Anti-Shipping Activity Messages (piracy, hijacking, attacks on vessels with lat/lon and narrative), Broadcast Warnings, NAVAREA navigational warnings, and the World Port Index.
- Docs: https://msi.nga.mil/api/swagger-ui/index.html
- Auth: none | Limits: Public API, no key. UNKNOWN throttle.
- Latency: warnings posted as issued; ASAM within days | Format: REST JSON/GeoJSON + Swagger
- Relevance: Red Sea / Bab el-Mandeb attack-count contracts, Gulf of Guinea piracy, Strait of Hormuz incidents. The inventory covers AIS positions and chokepoint transit counts but has NO feed for attacks on shipping — the actual tradeable event.

**USBR RISE API + CDEC + NOAA National Water Prediction Service** — US Bureau of Reclamation / California DWR / NOAA

- RISE: Reclamation reservoir storage, elevation, inflow/outflow for Lake Mead, Powell and hundreds more. CDEC: California reservoir, snow sensor and river gauge realtime. NWPS: river forecasts and flood stage at 10,000+ points.
- Docs: https://data.usbr.gov/rise-api
- Auth: none | Limits: All three free without keys. UNKNOWN throttles.
- Latency: hourly to daily | Format: REST JSON (RISE, JSON:API spec); CDEC CSV/JSON; NWPS REST JSON
- Relevance: 'Will Lake Mead fall below elevation 1,050 ft by date X' and Colorado River shortage-tier declarations are real, recurring contracts settled on exactly these gauges. The inventory has USGS NWIS but not the reservoir operators.

**OpenAQ API v3** — OpenAQ

- Aggregated global air quality from government reference monitors and low-cost sensors — PM2.5, PM10, NO2, O3, SO2, CO — by location, parameter and time range.
- Docs: https://docs.openaq.org/
- Auth: free API key (v3 requires registration) | Limits: Documented free tier with per-key rate limiting; exact figures UNKNOWN — the docs landing page did not expose them in this fetch.
- Latency: hourly to sub-hourly depending on source | Format: REST JSON + S3 open bucket (openaq-data-archive)
- Relevance: The only global AQI source. Settles air-quality contracts for Delhi, Beijing, Lahore, Jakarta — cities where no US EPA feed exists. Named as a subdomain in the weather inventory with no supporting feed.

**IAEA PRIS — Power Reactor Information System** — International Atomic Energy Agency

- Every power reactor worldwide: operational status, construction start, grid connection, permanent shutdown, annual and monthly energy availability/load factors, planned and unplanned outages.
- Docs: https://pris.iaea.org/ (redirects to https://pris-stats.iaea.org/)
- Auth: none for the public web database | Limits: No documented public API; data is web-query plus published country/reactor reports. Effectively SCRAPE-ASSISTED. UNKNOWN whether pris-stats.iaea.org exposes a JSON backend.
- Latency: status changes within days; performance statistics annual | Format: HTML / downloadable reports (no confirmed API)
- Relevance: 'Will reactor X connect to the grid by date Y' (Flamanville, Vogtle, Barakah, Akkuyu, Hinkley), national nuclear-capacity milestones, and Zaporizhzhia status. The inventory covers only US NRC — nothing for the other ~400 reactors.

**SIPRI databases — arms transfers, military expenditure, nuclear forces** — Stockholm International Peace Research Institute

- Arms Transfers Database (every major conventional weapons transfer since 1950 with TIV valuation), Military Expenditure Database (170 countries since 1949), arms industry top-100, multilateral peace operations.
- Docs: https://www.sipri.org/databases
- Auth: none | Limits: Free web query and bulk XLSX/CSV export. No API. Attribution required.
- Latency: arms transfers updated annually (March); milex annually (April) | Format: XLSX / CSV bulk, web query
- Relevance: 'Will NATO member X reach 2%/3.5% of GDP on defense', arms-package delivery confirmations, and the standard denominator for defense-spending contracts. The Geopolitics domain lists 'military expenditure' as a subdomain with no feed — SIPRI is the answer.

**FBI Crime Data Explorer API (NIBRS/UCR)** — FBI CJIS

- National, state and agency-level offense, arrest, clearance, hate crime, LEOKA and use-of-force counts from NIBRS/SRS submissions.
- Docs: https://cde.ucr.cjis.gov/LATEST/webapp/#/pages/docApi
- Auth: api.data.gov key (free) | Limits: api.data.gov default 1,000 requests/hour. Note the base path moved (api.usa.gov/crime/fbi/cde); the older api.data.gov/docs/fbi path 404s.
- Latency: quarterly preliminary releases; annual final (Crime in the Nation, ~September) | Format: REST JSON + bulk CSV/ZIP by state/year
- Relevance: 'Will murders in city X decline in 2026', national violent-crime-rate direction — recurring contracts. The annual release date is itself a scheduled event. Crime was completely absent from the inventory.

**IOM Displacement Tracking Matrix API + Missing Migrants Project** — International Organization for Migration

- DTM: IDP and mobility figures by country, admin level and round — the operational ground truth for displacement. Missing Migrants: deaths and disappearances on migration routes with location and cause.
- Docs: https://dtm.iom.int/data-and-analysis/dtm-api
- Auth: none for the public API | Limits: Free public API; UNKNOWN throttle. Also mirrored on HDX.
- Latency: per assessment round, weeks to months; emergency rounds faster | Format: REST JSON + HDX CKAN mirror
- Relevance: Displacement-threshold contracts for Sudan, Gaza, Ukraine, Myanmar, Haiti. The inventory lists 'refugee and displacement flows' as a subdomain twice with no feed. UNHCR gives the annual official stock; DTM gives the fast-moving operational count.

**UNHCR Refugee Statistics API** — UNHCR `LIVE`

- Refugees, asylum-seekers, IDPs, stateless persons and returnees by origin and asylum country, ~70 years of history; plus asylum applications and decisions.
- Docs: https://api.unhcr.org/docs/refugee-statistics.html
- Auth: none | Limits: No documented authentication or rate limit.
- Latency: mid-year and annual official statistics; some monthly emergency portals | Format: REST JSON (https://api.unhcr.org/population/v1/)
- Relevance: The official settlement source for refugee-population contracts. Pair with IOM DTM for speed.

**Open States API v3 + Legistar Web API + LocalView** — Plural (Open States) / Granicus Legistar / academic `LIVE`

- Open States: bills, votes, legislators, committees and events across all 50 state legislatures, DC and PR. Legistar: agendas, minutes, votes and matters for hundreds of US city councils and counties. LocalView: transcripts of 150,000+ local government meetings.
- Docs: https://docs.openstates.org/api-v3/
- Auth: Open States: free API key via X-API-KEY header or ?apikey. Legistar: none for most tenants. | Limits: Open States: free key required; published tier is modest (historically ~250 requests/day, higher on request) — UNKNOWN current figure. Bulk CSV/JSON downloads are unmetered and are the right path for volume. Legistar: per-tenant, UNKNOWN.
- Latency: Open States scrapes daily; Legistar realtime per tenant | Format: GraphQL + REST JSON + bulk CSV; Legistar REST JSON (webapi.legistar.com/v1/{client})
- Relevance: State-level abortion, cannabis, crypto, AI and election-law legislation contracts — a large and growing category with zero coverage in the inventory beyond the word 'subdomain'. Municipal: stadium deals, zoning, local ballot measures.

**International IDEA Voter Turnout Database + CLEA + NELDA + V-Dem** — International IDEA / Univ. of Michigan / Yale / V-Dem Institute

- IDEA: turnout, compulsory voting and electoral system for every national election worldwide since 1945. CLEA: constituency-level results for 1,900+ elections in 170 countries. NELDA: pre/post-election event coding (was it competitive, was there violence, was the opposition barred). V-Dem: 500+ democracy indicators for 202 countries, 1789-present.
- Docs: https://www.idea.int/data-tools/data/voter-turnout-database
- Auth: none (V-Dem and CLEA require free registration for some files) | Limits: All bulk download; no APIs. V-Dem also ships as an R package (vdemdata).
- Latency: IDEA within weeks of an election; V-Dem annual (March); CLEA periodic | Format: CSV / XLSX / Stata bulk; R package
- Relevance: The Politics domain covered US elections thoroughly and non-Western elections with one feed (IPU Parline). These supply the base rates: incumbent-survival rates, turnout distributions, and coded histories of whether elections in a given regime type are actually competitive — the prior for every 'will the opposition win' contract in Africa, Asia and MENA.

**UN World Population Prospects + Census IDB + Our World in Data catalog** — UN DESA Population Division / US Census Bureau / Our World in Data

- WPP: population, fertility, mortality, migration estimates and projections to 2100 for every country, with variants. Census IDB: independent US-government projections. OWID: ~5,000 harmonized long-run series with a documented ETL catalog and per-chart CSV endpoints.
- Docs: https://population.un.org/wpp/downloads
- Auth: none | Limits: WPP: bulk CSV/XLSX, unmetered (an API exists at population.un.org/dataportalapi with free registration). OWID: every grapher chart exposes .csv/.metadata.json; catalog on S3; unmetered but be polite.
- Latency: WPP revised every 2 years; OWID continuous | Format: CSV/XLSX bulk + REST JSON (UN Data Portal) + OWID grapher CSV endpoints
- Relevance: Population-milestone contracts ('when does India/world reach N billion', 'will China's population fall by X'). OWID is separately the single best free harmonization layer across health, energy, food and conflict — it has already solved the country-code and unit-reconciliation problem that this terminal will otherwise solve badly 40 times.

**National statistics offices outside US/EU — Japan e-Stat, India, Brazil IBGE, Canada, Australia, Korea, Indonesia, Mexico, Singapore** — Various national statistical agencies

- e-Stat (Japan): all official Japanese statistics via REST API. data.gov.in + MoSPI (India): CPI, IIP, GDP. IBGE SIDRA/servicodados (Brazil): IPCA inflation, PNAD employment, agricultural surveys. StatCan WDS (Canada): 15 API methods over all CANSIM/table data. ABS Data API (Australia): SDMX. KOSIS (Korea), BPS (Indonesia), INEGI (Mexico), data.gov.sg (Singapore).
- Docs: https://www.e-stat.go.jp/api/ ; https://servicodados.ibge.gov.br/api/docs ; https://www.statcan.gc.ca/en/developers/wds ; https://dataapi.abs.gov.au/
- Auth: e-Stat: free appId registration. IBGE: none. StatCan: none. ABS: none. data.gov.in: free key. INEGI: free token. | Limits: e-Stat: free with registered appId, UNKNOWN quota. IBGE/StatCan/ABS: no key, UNKNOWN throttle. Verified only that StatCan WDS exists with 15 documented methods.
- Latency: monthly to annual per series | Format: REST JSON (e-Stat, IBGE, StatCan, INEGI); SDMX (ABS, StatCan)
- Relevance: Japan CPI and BoJ policy, India CPI and RBI, Brazil IPCA and Selic, Banxico, RBA — all heavily traded and all invisible to FRED/Eurostat. CHINA IS A DEAD END: NBS has no public API and actively restricts bulk access; use CEIC (paid), Wind (paid), or triangulate from customs partner-country mirror statistics.

**BigQuery public datasets** — Google Cloud

- GDELT full archive, GH Archive, Google Patents, Google Trends (the only sanctioned Trends access), Ethereum/Bitcoin/Crypto ledgers, NOAA GSOD and GHCN, US Census, FDA, Stack Overflow, Wikipedia pageviews, M-Lab, Chicago/NYC open data.
- Docs: https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/public-data
- Auth: Google Cloud account (free tier, no card for sandbox) | Limits: 1 TB of query processing per month free, 10 GB storage. Storage of the public datasets is paid for by Google — you pay only for bytes scanned. Partition and cluster aggressively.
- Latency: per dataset; GDELT and GH Archive near-realtime | Format: BigQuery SQL + Storage Read API
- Relevance: Google Trends via BigQuery is the ONLY compliant way to get search-attention data — the inventory lists 'search and attention trends' as a subdomain and pytrends-style scraping is both rate-limited and against ToS. An entire delivery mechanism the inventory never names.

**Registry of Open Data on AWS + Azure Open Datasets + NOAA NODD + NASA Earthdata** — AWS / Microsoft / NOAA / NASA `LIVE`

- Hundreds of petabyte-scale datasets in S3/Blob with no egress cost in-region: NOAA models (already partly covered), Sentinel-2 and Landsat, Copernicus DEM, OpenStreetMap planet, Common Crawl, 1000 Genomes, IRS 990, Overture, Amazon Berkeley Objects.
- Docs: https://registry.opendata.aws/
- Auth: none for most buckets (some requester-pays); NASA Earthdata requires free login | Limits: Unmetered reads from within the same AWS region; egress charged if you pull out. The registry itself is a machine-readable YAML index in github.com/awslabs/open-data-registry.
- Latency: per dataset; many are near-realtime mirrors of government feeds | Format: S3/Blob objects (NetCDF, GRIB, COG, Zarr, Parquet) + YAML catalog
- Relevance: The bulk-delivery tier. Pulling GFS via NOMADS one GRIB at a time will not scale; the S3 mirrors will. Also the correct answer to 'government bulk FTP' — most agencies have moved to S3 and the FTP endpoints are being retired.

**CME/ICE/LME settlement price files + CFTC datasets** — CME Group / ICE / LME / CFTC

- CME: daily settlement prices, volume and open interest per contract as free end-of-day files; the settlement price is the contractual number. CFTC: Commitments of Traders (already in inventory), plus swaps data, bank participation and the full public reporting datasets.
- Docs: https://www.cmegroup.com/market-data/settlements.html
- Auth: none for delayed/EOD settlement files; CME DataMine requires account for history | Limits: EOD settlements free; intraday and historical tick data are paid. LME publishes official prices with a delay; full history is licensed.
- Latency: EOD, published after each settlement window | Format: CSV / JSON files
- Relevance: Commodity and rate contracts settle on the EXCHANGE SETTLEMENT PRICE at a specific time, not on a spot quote from an aggregator. The inventory's commodity feeds give physical fundamentals and LBMA fixings but never the futures settlement that actually resolves the contract.

**State Secretary of State election-night result feeds** — 50 US state election authorities (e.g. Florida DOS, Georgia SOS, Texas SOS, Pennsylvania DOS)

- Precinct- and county-level vote counts published directly by the legal certifying authority, usually as JSON/XML/CSV refreshed every few minutes on election night, plus certified canvass files afterward.
- Docs: https://results.elections.myflorida.com/ ; https://results.enr.clarityelections.com/ (Clarity/Scytl powers many states)
- Auth: none | Limits: No keys; formats and stability vary wildly by state. Many use Clarity Elections, which exposes a consistent JSON/ZIP structure across tenants.
- Latency: 1-5 minute refresh on election night | Format: JSON / XML / CSV / Clarity ZIP bundles
- Relevance: Election contracts settle on official certification, not on a network call. AP's Elections API and Decision Desk are PAID; these state feeds are the free, and legally authoritative, primary source. The Politics domain listed 'election results — live/election-night reporting' as a subdomain and supplied no feed for it — the single most glaring settlement gap in the whole inventory.

- Auth: none | Limits: Public API at api.ioda.inetintel.cc.gatech.edu; UNKNOWN throttle. Landing page fetch in this session returned no usable detail — endpoint shape unconfirmed.

- Crowdsourced censorship measurements: which sites/apps are blocked in which country on which network, with raw measurement evidence. Signal, WhatsApp, Telegram, Tor reachability tests.

- Global disaster events since 1900: type, country, deaths, affected, damage estimates in USD, with a documented entry threshold.

- Relevance: The standard denominator for global disaster-count and disaster-mortality contracts outside the US. Check the licence before building a paid product on it.

#### Repos

- `awslabs/open-data-registry` — The machine-readable YAML source of the AWS Registry of Open Data — one file per dataset with S3 paths, license, update cadence and usage examples. · Confirmed live in this session. Parse the YAML directory to auto-generate an ingestion catalog for every petabyte-scale public dataset on S3, instead of hand-listing them.
- `awesome-selfhosted/awesome-selfhosted` — Catalog of self-hostable services including RSS aggregators, monitoring, scrapers and API gateways. · The terminal will need to self-host LibreTranslate, Nominatim, a RSS fetcher and a scheduler — public instances of all four are rate-limited into uselessness at this scale.
- `telegeography/www.submarinecablemap.com` — TeleGeography's submarine cable map published as open GeoJSON/JSON in git. · The free subset of an otherwise expensive database. Git history also gives you cable RFS-date changes over time for free.
- `washingtonpost/data-police-shootings` — Every US fatal police shooting since 2015, maintained as CSV in git, CC-licensed. · Faster and more complete than FBI use-of-force reporting, and openly licensed unlike Gun Violence Archive.
- `vz-risk/VCDB` — VERIS Community Database — thousands of security incidents coded to a common schema (actor, action, asset, attribute). · The only free structured incident taxonomy for cyber. Gives base rates for breach-type contracts rather than just a stream of headlines.
- `mitre-attack/attack-stix-data` — MITRE ATT&CK enterprise/mobile/ICS matrices as versioned STIX 2.1 bundles. · Canonical technique and threat-group identifiers — the entity-resolution layer for attributing a reported attack to a named actor across CISA, abuse.ch and vendor reporting.
- `owid/owid-datasets` — Our World in Data's harmonized dataset repository plus the etl repo that builds it. · Country-code harmonization, unit reconciliation and long-run series stitching already solved and documented. Reuse the mapping tables rather than rebuilding them per-domain.
- `datasets/country-codes` — Frictionless Data's consolidated country-code table: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2/3/numeric, FIPS, ITU, IOC, FIFA, M49, currency, TLD, calling code, capital. · One file that joins nearly every international feed in the inventory. The single highest ratio of usefulness to effort in this entire list.
- `unitedstates/districts` — Congressional and state-legislative district boundaries as GeoJSON, by the same group as congress-legislators (already in inventory). · Joins election results, polling, campaign finance and Census demographics to a common geographic key.
- `public-apis/public-apis` — Already in the inventory, but noted here for a different reason: its category taxonomy is itself a gap-detection tool. · Diffing its category list against the domains covered is a cheap, repeatable completeness audit — it surfaced several of the gaps above.
- `pandas-dev/pandas-market-calendars` — Trading calendars, holidays, early closes and settlement schedules for ~50 global exchanges. · Answers 'does the settling print land before expiry'. Nothing in the inventory can compute that.
- `man-group/ArcticDB` — Production-grade DataFrame time-series store on S3, built for versioned, bitemporal financial data. · The inventory has no storage layer. Bitemporality matters specifically: you must be able to reproduce what a feed said at the moment a market traded, not just what it says now. Same reason ALFRED matters.
- `awesome-mlss/awesome-time-series` — Catalog of time-series databases, forecasting libraries and benchmark datasets. · Survey of the storage/forecast tooling choices (TimescaleDB, QuestDB, ClickHouse, DuckDB) before committing to one.
- `nvdlib/nvdlib` — Python wrapper for the NVD CVE and CPE APIs with automatic rate-limit handling. · NVD's 5-per-30-seconds keyless limit is punishing; the wrapper handles backoff and key rotation correctly.
- `OpenSanctions/opensanctions` — The full ETL pipeline behind OpenSanctions, built on the FollowTheMoney entity schema. · FtM is a working, battle-tested entity-resolution schema for people, companies, vessels and assets across jurisdictions. OCCRP Aleph uses it too. Adopt it rather than inventing an entity model.
- `dathere/qsv` — Very fast CSV toolkit for indexing, joining, validating and geocoding large delimited files. · Enormous fractions of the feeds above ship as bulk CSV, not JSON. This is the pragmatic ingest tool for them.
- `pytorch/fairseq (NLLB-200 weights via HuggingFace facebook/nllb-200-distilled-600M)` — 200-language translation model, distilled variants runnable on a single GPU. · Covers the low-resource languages where conflict, election and disaster signal originates and where no free commercial API exists.
- `ropensci/vdemdata` — V-Dem's 500+ democracy indicators packaged for direct programmatic load. · Base rates for regime-change, coup and election-competitiveness contracts. Saves parsing a 3 GB Stata file.
- `palewire/news-homepages` — Automated hourly archive of hundreds of news homepages as screenshots, HTML and extracted links. · Point-in-time evidence of what was being reported when — the archival retrieval capability the News domain lists as a subdomain with no implementation.
- `public-transport/transitous or mobilitydata/mobility-database-catalogs` — Catalog of ~2,000 GTFS and GTFS-Realtime transit feeds worldwide. · Public transit is entirely absent from the Transport domain. GTFS-RT is also a useful ground-truth signal for strikes, city shutdowns and disaster disruption.

---

## 3. Dead ends — do not build on these

### API catalogs and open-data indexes

- api.publicapis.org — DEAD. Verified 2026-09-20: HTTP 000 (connection failure, not even a DNS/TLS error page). This was THE canonical JSON endpoint for the public-apis list and is still referenced in thousands of blog posts and tutorials. Use https://public-api-lists.github.io/public-api-lists/api/all.json instead, or parse public-apis' README.md yourself.
- catalog.data.gov CKAN Action API — DEAD. Verified 2026-09-20: every /api/3/action/* call returns HTTP 404 with body {"detail":{},"message":"Not Found"}. data.gov replaced CKAN with a custom Flask/OpenSearch application in 2025 (announced 2026-04-15). Use https://api.gsa.gov/technology/datagov/v4/search?q=...&api_key=DEMO_KEY, which returns DCAT-wrapped results with CURSOR pagination (an opaque `after` token) — offset-based paging code will not port. Generic CKAN client libraries (including CKAN MCP servers) still ship data.gov as a CKAN portal and fail confusingly.
- catalog-old.data.gov — RETIRED. Verified 2026-09-20: returns HTTP 301. The legacy CKAN instance was documented as remaining available through fall 2026; that window has closed. Do not plan a migration path through it.
- jdorfman/awesome-json-datasets — ARCHIVED 2026-03-01, read-only, 3,616 stars. Historically the go-to list of no-auth JSON endpoints. Its links are now unmaintained and decaying; treat every entry as needing a live health check.
- jimaek/Awesome-JSON-Datasets — NOT a successor despite appearing in search results as the fork of the archived list. Verified: 5 stars, fork=true, last pushed 2015-09-01. It is eleven years stale. There is no maintained successor to awesome-json-datasets; the closest functional replacement is public-api-lists' auth==='No' subset (397 entries).
- toddmotto/public-apis — SUPERSEDED. 2,743 stars but last pushed 2024-06-23. Its homepage points at public-apis.org. This is the historical origin of the list; the live lineage is public-apis/public-apis. Do not integrate.
- TonnyL/Awesome_APIs — ARCHIVED, last pushed 2020-02-29 despite 13,126 stars. High star count on a six-year-dead repo is exactly the trap that makes star-sorted GitHub search misleading here.
- datahub.io CKAN API — DEAD. Verified 2026-09-20: /api/3/action/package_search returns HTTP 404 rendered as a Next.js error page; /api/search also 404. The site is now DataHub Cloud, a commercial PortalJS product. old.datahub.io (the documented read-only legacy mirror) returned HTTP 000 — connection failure. The Open Knowledge Labs DataHub as a queryable open-data catalog is effectively gone.
- data.world — REGISTRATION-WALLED with no anonymous discovery. Verified 2026-09-20: both https://api.data.world/v0/ and /v0/search/datasets?query=test return HTTP 404 with a JSON error body when unauthenticated. The company has pivoted to enterprise data cataloging and no longer publishes free-tier quotas. Poor cost-to-value versus Kaggle/HuggingFace/Socrata.
- Google Dataset Search — NO API, and there never has been one. Verified 2026-09-20: datasetsearch.research.google.com returns 524,254 bytes of HTML only. It is a web UI over schema.org/Dataset markup. If you want that coverage, crawl schema.org Dataset JSON-LD yourself; do not plan around a Google endpoint.
- RapidAPI Hub — NO free bulk catalog API. It hosts 40,000+ APIs but provides no programmatic way to enumerate them; third parties resort to paid scrapers (e.g. the Apify RapidAPI Hub Scraper) to get the list. Free per-API plans are documented at 1,000 req/hour and 500K/month but each provider overrides this, and 100-500 calls/MONTH is common. Unified auth does not mean unified limits.
- APILayer — free tiers are prototype-only, not production. Verified example: Currencylayer's free plan is 100 calls/MONTH and hard-locks the base currency to USD. Most APILayer products sit in the 100-1,000 calls/month band. Note also that APILayer sponsors public-apis/public-apis and is that repo's homepage link — the most-starred 'free API' list is commercially affiliated with a paid marketplace. Worth knowing when weighing its curation.
- open.canada.ca CKAN — BLOCKED BY WAF. Verified 2026-09-20: returns an HTML 'Request Rejected' page with a support ID rather than JSON, on a standard browser User-Agent. The CKAN API may exist behind it but is not reachable by naive clients; budget for WAF negotiation or skip.
- data.gov.au Magda API — /api/v0/search/datasets returns HTTP 404 (verified 2026-09-20, 17,904 bytes of HTML). The Magda contract for data.gov.au concluded in June 2025. Magda remains a viable open-source federation platform, but the Australian national deployment's v0 API path is not a working endpoint.
- Zenodo WAF User-Agent trap — NOT a dead end but a silent failure mode. Verified 2026-09-20 with paired requests: https://zenodo.org/api/records?size=1 returns HTTP 200 with a default curl User-Agent and HTTP 403 with 'Mozilla/5.0'. Spoofing a browser UA — standard defensive practice elsewhere — is what breaks it. Send your own honest UA.
- DataCite bracket-parameter trap — page[size] and page[number] are JSON:API bracket params that curl and several HTTP clients glob or mangle. Must be percent-encoded as page%5Bsize%5D. An unencoded request silently returns the wrong thing rather than erroring.
- awesome-public-datasets README.md — returns HTTP 404. The list is README.rst (reStructuredText). Scrapers assuming the near-universal README.md convention get nothing and, if they do not check status codes, record an empty catalog as a successful zero.
- chrieke/awesome-satellite-imagery-datasets — ARCHIVED, last pushed 2022-07-14 (3,916 stars). Still surfaces high in geospatial dataset searches. Four years stale for a field that moved fast.
- arainho/awesome-api-security — ARCHIVED (3,862 stars, last push 2026-05-01). Archived-but-recent is easy to miss; check the archived flag, not just pushed_at.
- freepublicapis.com pagination — the /api/apis endpoint returns exactly 100 entries and ignores a naive ?limit= parameter (verified: identical 100-item response with and without it). It appears to serve a trending slice, not the full catalog, and documents no way to page to completion. Its per-API health/latency/reliability scores are genuinely unique and worth having — just do not mistake the 100 you get for everything it knows.
- publicapis.io / publicapi.dev / apilist.fun — all respond 200 but none publishes a documented JSON API. They are Next.js or static sites whose internal /_next/data routes are implementation details that change without notice. Content overlaps almost entirely with public-apis and public-api-lists, both better sourced. Low value for a programmatic pipeline.
- Star count is an actively misleading maintenance signal in this domain. TonnyL/Awesome_APIs has 13,126 stars and died in 2020; api-evangelist/specifications has 1 star and was pushed the day of verification. Always check pushed_at AND the archived boolean via the GitHub API (https://api.github.com/repos/{owner}/{name}) before trusting any list — search-result ranking will not tell you.
- GDELT rate limiting — not a catalog, but a trap you will hit while crawling one: api.gdeltproject.org returns HTTP 429 with a plaintext body reading 'Please limit requests to one every 5 seconds', not a JSON error. One request per five seconds is the hard ceiling; GDELT directs high-volume users to its web n-grams bulk dataset instead.
- Socrata deep pagination — the Discovery API reports resultSetSize capped at 10,000 for broad queries. Paginating past that silently truncates rather than erroring. Partition by domain or facet instead of walking a global offset.
- Anonymous rate limits are mostly UNDOCUMENTED across this domain. data.europa.eu, Figshare, HuggingFace anonymous, OpenDataSoft per-tenant and apis.io all publish no anonymous quota. Do not infer 'unlimited' from 'unpublished' — that is an unmeasured case, not a measured absence of limits. Build backoff before you build breadth.

### OSINT and real-time world monitoring

- GDELT GEO 2.0 API IS DEAD. Verified exhaustively on 2026-09-20: https://api.gdeltproject.org/api/v2/geo/geo returns HTTP 404 for EVERY variant tested, including the exact example URL from GDELT's own announcement blog post (?query=trump&mode=country), plus mode=PointData, format=GeoJSON, format=geojson, uppercase params, and format=imagehtml. The documentation is still live and still advertises it. Do not plan a geospatial news-mapping layer on this endpoint. Get lat/lon from the raw GKG files or the BigQuery gkg table instead — both are confirmed working.
- GDELT Global Entity Graph (GEG) HAS STOPPED UPDATING. Its MASTERFILELIST.TXT is live and huge (95MB, 1,137,658 lines), which makes it look perfectly healthy — but the final entry is 20260618223100, meaning it has produced nothing for three months as of 2026-09-20. This is the exact failure mode where 'the endpoint responds' is mistaken for 'the data is current'. Check the tail of the masterfile, not the HTTP status. Related: the gdeltv3 paths for webngrams and iatv/ngrams that appear in older blog posts return 404 — only gdeltv3/gfg/alpha/ was confirmed current (20260920230000).
- GDELT DOC API WILL RATE-LIMIT YOU HARDER THAN DOCUMENTED. Verified: the documented limit is 1 request per 5 seconds, but after two rapid calls the endpoint returned HTTP 429 and stayed 429 for over 60 seconds despite a 20-second wait. Worse, the 429 body is PLAIN TEXT, not JSON — a naive json.loads() will raise on it and may be caught as a generic network error, silently turning a rate-limit into 'no articles found'. That is an absence-vs-zero bug waiting to happen. Never build a polling panel on the DOC API; use the raw 15-minute files or BigQuery.
- ReliefWeb API v1 IS DECOMMISSIONED. Verified: returns HTTP 410 with "The API version 'v1' has been decommissioned. Please use version 'v2' instead." And v2 will NOT accept an arbitrary appname — passing an unregistered one returns HTTP 403 'You are not using an approved appname.' You must request an approved appname from ReliefWeb before a single call works. Every code sample, blog post and library written before this change is broken.
- ACLED's LEGACY API IS GONE. api.acleddata.com/acled/read with the old email+key scheme now fails (verified: connection failure / HTTP 403). Authentication moved to OAuth2 at https://acleddata.com/oauth/token with 24-hour access tokens and 14-day refresh tokens against the new base https://acleddata.com/api/acled/read. Separately and more importantly: ACLED is free for academic, non-profit and personal research ONLY. A prediction-market product is commercial use and needs a paid license. Read the terms before you architect around it.
- UCDP's API IS NO LONGER OPEN. Verified: an unauthenticated request to ucdpapi.pcr.uu.se returns HTTP 401 with the plain-text body 'API token required. Add header: x-ucdp-access-token: <your-token>'. Tokens are free but you must request one. Also note the dataset version is embedded in the URL path (e.g. /gedevents/25.1) and changes annually — hardcoding it guarantees a silent break at the next release.
- abuse.ch APIs NOW REQUIRE AN AUTH-KEY. Verified: urlhaus-api.abuse.ch and threatfox-api.abuse.ch both return HTTP 401 unauthenticated, a change from their historically open access. The bulk CSV downloads (urlhaus.abuse.ch/downloads/csv_recent/) are still open and returned 2.4MB with no auth — use those if you want to avoid the account.
- ADS-B EXCHANGE IS NO LONGER FREE. It was acquired by Jetnet in 2024 and now requires a paid RapidAPI subscription. The genuinely free, unauthenticated replacements are api.adsb.lol/v2/mil and opendata.adsb.fi/api/v2/mil, both verified working on 2026-09-20 with no key at all. Note that airplanes.live returned HTTP 403 to a plain curl (User-Agent blocking), so it needs a browser-like UA if you use it.
- api.worldmonitor.app IS NOT A FREE FEED. Every one of the 231 endpoints tested returned HTTP 403 {"error":"Forbidden","code":"agent_request_blocked"} — they block agent user-agents AND require an X-WorldMonitor-Key header, with the MCP server returning a JSON-RPC -32001 auth error pointing at a Pro upgrade funnel. What IS free and extremely valuable: the OpenAPI 3.1.0 spec at api.worldmonitor.app/openapi.json (948KB, HTTP 200, no auth) and the MCP tools/list response. Read the spec as a blueprint, then self-host the AGPL repo.
- AGPL-3.0 IS A REAL CONSTRAINT, NOT A FORMALITY. koala73/worldmonitor is AGPL-3.0-only. The AGPL's network clause means that if you run a modified version as a network service, you must offer your complete corresponding source to users of that service. For a commercial prediction-market terminal this is a significant decision, not a footnote. ilhamhakm/Spectre (MIT) and lockfale/OSINT-Framework (MIT) do not carry this obligation.
- NewsAPI.org's FREE TIER IS DEVELOPMENT-ONLY. Verified HTTP 401 without a key; with a free key it is restricted to localhost, non-production use, 100 requests/day and a 24-hour article delay. It is unusable for a live panel. GDELT's raw files cover the same ground with no key and no delay.
- METACULUS's API IS CLOSED TO ANONYMOUS ACCESS. Verified: www.metaculus.com/api2/questions/ returns HTTP 403. Its community forecasts would be an excellent ensemble input, but you need an authenticated account and should check their terms for programmatic access.
- KEY-REQUIRED, NOT FREE-ON-DEMAND (each verified rejecting anonymous calls on 2026-09-20): Cloudflare Radar (HTTP 400, error 9106 missing auth headers), OpenAQ v3 (401), ENTSO-E Transparency (401), Global Fishing Watch v3 (401), UN OCHA HAPI (403), PDC DisasterAWARE (403), Shodan, GreyNoise. All are obtainable but none is a drop-in anonymous fetch — budget signup time for each.
- BROKEN OR MOVED ENDPOINTS FOUND WHILE PROBING: IODA's v2 API at api.ioda.inetintel.cc.gatech.edu returned 400/404 on the paths in its published docs; GreyNoise's v3 community endpoint returned 404; Our World in Data's /v1/indicators path returned 404; OpenMHz returned 403. Re-derive these from their current docs rather than trusting any cached example URL.
- SCRAPE-ONLY, NO API: Liveuamap (HTTP 403 to curl, no public API — /api returns a 66-byte stub; worldmonitor and Spectre both resort to scraping it), start.me OSINT collections (403), HealthMap (no documented open API in 2026), Taiwan MND and Japan Joint Staff daily activity reports (worldmonitor web-scrapes both), China NBS/SAFE/PBoC (scraped). Treat all of these as fragile and legally grey; do not put one on a critical path. The bright exception is DeepStateMap, whose undocumented /api/history/last endpoint returned 627KB of real front-line GeoJSON with no auth.
- PLANET HAS NO GENERAL FREE TIER. Access to PlanetScope/RapidEye is via the Education & Research program, which requires verified university affiliation, is non-commercial only, and expires after one year pending re-confirmation. For a commercial product, plan on Copernicus Sentinel (free, 10m optical + SAR) and accept the coarser resolution. Also do not confuse the commercial sentinel-hub.com 30-day trial with the Copernicus Data Space Sentinel Hub free tier — they are different offerings with very different quotas.
- TWO SOURCES THAT LOOK FREE BUT AREN'T, FOR REASONS OF RECIPROCITY OR LICENSE: AISHub is free only if you contribute your own AIS receiver hardware feed — there is no non-contributor tier. SIPRI arms-transfer data is fair-use non-commercial only and worldmonitor deliberately ingests aggregates rather than raw records because of it.
- REDDIT'S JSON ENDPOINTS ARE EFFECTIVELY CLOSED. Verified: reddit.com/r/worldnews/new.json returned HTTP 403 to a plain client. Reddit now requires OAuth and enforces aggressive user-agent and rate policies, with commercial use requiring a paid agreement. Bluesky Jetstream is the only remaining large, free, unauthenticated social firehose — build social-velocity signals on that instead.
- A GENERAL WARNING THAT COST ME THE MOST TIME HERE: for this class of source, HTTP 200 does not mean the data is current, and a live documentation page does not mean the endpoint exists. GDELT GEO has perfect docs and a 404 endpoint. GDELT GEG has a healthy 95MB index and three-month-old data. Before depending on any feed in this report, assert on the timestamp of the newest record, not on the status code — and treat 'the check could not be performed' as distinct from 'the check found nothing'.

### Weather, Climate and Atmosphere

- Dark Sky / forecast.io API — DEAD. Shut down 31 March 2023 after Apple's acquisition. VERIFIED: curl to https://api.darksky.net/forecast/... returns connection code 000 (host does not resolve/refuses). Yet ZeevG/python-forecast.io (423 stars) and lukaskubis/darkskylib (114 stars) are still the top GitHub hits for 'weather api wrapper python' — do not follow them. Apple WeatherKit is the successor and is NOT free (see below).
- Apple WeatherKit — NOT FREE. The '500,000 calls/month included' requires a paid Apple Developer Program membership (USD 99/year). There is no membership-free tier. Frequently listed as free in API roundups; it is not.
- Windy Point Forecast API free tier — TRAP. The free tier does give 500 requests/day, but the pricing page states in a footnote that free-tier responses are 'randomly shuffled and slightly modified data'. VERIFIED by reading https://api.windy.com/point-forecast/pricing. It is a functional sandbox, not usable data. Any model comparison built on it is silently garbage.
- NOAA NEXRAD Level II on AWS (s3://noaa-nexrad-level2) — anonymous bucket LISTING is blocked. VERIFIED: ListObjectsV2 returns <Code>AccessDenied</Code> both on the global and the us-east-1 endpoint, with and without a prefix. Object GETs work if you already know the key, but you cannot discover keys from the bucket. Get the key index from Iowa Environmental Mesonet or use ARM-DOE/pyart's helpers instead of writing a lister.
- ERA5 on AWS (s3://era5-pds) — anonymous listing also returns 403 AccessDenied (VERIFIED, both global and regional endpoints). This bucket is widely cited as the easy free ERA5 route; it is not currently browsable. Use Copernicus CDS, google-research/arco-era5 Zarr on GCS, or Open-Meteo's archive API instead.
- NSIDC Sea Ice Index v3.0 file paths — RETIRED, now 404. VERIFIED: .../G02135/north/daily/data/N_seaice_extent_daily_v3.0.csv returns 404, and masie_web.apps.nsidc.org does not resolve at all (code 000). Almost every tutorial and cached code sample still uses these. The live path is v4.0: https://noaadata.apps.nsidc.org/NOAA/G02135/north/daily/data/N_seaice_extent_daily_v4.0.csv (VERIFIED 200, current through 2026-09-19).
- Blitzortung API — DEAD. VERIFIED: api.blitzortung.org does not resolve (code 000). The lightning data still exists but only via an unofficial, undocumented WebSocket whose terms prohibit commercial redistribution. For free realtime lightning use GOES GLM on AWS instead (s3://noaa-goes19, VERIFIED live).
- Meteostat JSON API free tier — effectively unusable. 500 calls PER MONTH on RapidAPI (~16/day). VERIFIED that the endpoint returns 401 without a RapidAPI key. The project is alive and good; just use the keyless bulk endpoints (bulk.meteostat.net, VERIFIED 200) and ignore the REST API entirely.
- WeatherAPI.com free tier — history is 'Past 1 days' ONLY. VERIFIED on their pricing page. The 100,000 calls/month headline number makes it look like the most generous free tier in the category; it cannot backtest anything, and the forecast horizon is 3 days. Marine, pollen and AQ history are all paid.
- Weatherbit free tier — 50 calls per day, 7-day forecast, NO historical data at all, non-commercial only. VERIFIED on their pricing page. Listed as a Dark Sky replacement in many roundups; the quota makes it a toy.
- OpenWeatherMap One Call API 3.0 — 'free' with a mandatory payment card on file. The 1,000 calls/day allowance is real but overage bills automatically unless you manually set a cap in your account. The genuinely card-free product set is the older Free Access APIs (current weather, 3-hour forecast, air pollution, geocoding) at 60 calls/min and 1,000,000/month — a different, weaker set of endpoints with no minutely precipitation and no historical time machine.
- Met Office DataHub free plan — 55 calls per day for site-specific forecasts. VERIFIED verbatim on https://datahub.metoffice.gov.uk/pricing/site-specific ('Up to 55 calls per day'). That is under three calls per hour. Get UKMO model data from Open-Meteo's /v1/ukmo endpoint at 10,000 calls/day instead.
- Weather Underground PWS API — not open. A free key exists but ONLY for people who own a registered personal weather station actively uploading data to WU. The general free API was killed by IBM in 2018/2019. VERIFIED: api.weather.com PWS endpoint returns 401 without a key. Its 250,000-station network is genuinely attractive and genuinely gated.
- Tomorrow.io official free rate limits — UNVERIFIABLE. The support article at support.tomorrow.io/hc/en-us/articles/20273728362644 is behind a Cloudflare JavaScript challenge (403/'Enable JavaScript and cookies to continue' on direct fetch), and docs.tomorrow.io/reference/rate-limiting gives no numbers. Secondary sources consistently say 500/day, 25/hour, 3/second. Do not treat those figures as confirmed.
- Bureau of Meteorology Australia (api.weather.bom.gov.au) — no usable public API. VERIFIED: connection returns code 000 from our probe. The endpoint that circulates on GitHub is an undocumented internal API for BoM's own app, with no published terms, no versioning guarantee and geo/agent filtering. Use Open-Meteo's /v1/bom endpoint for ACCESS-G model data instead.
- Météo-France public API — registration wall with unknown free limits. VERIFIED: portail-api.meteofrance.fr returns 200 but https://public-api.meteofrance.fr/public/DPObs/v1/stations returns 404 without an OAuth token. Requires an application registration and OAuth2 client-credentials flow; free-tier call limits are UNKNOWN and not published. Open-Meteo's /v1/meteofrance endpoint gives you AROME and ARPEGE with no registration.
- EPA Envirofacts base path https://api.epa.gov/enviro/efservice/ — 404. The working host is enviro.epa.gov/enviro/efservice/ (VERIFIED 200 for getEnvirofactsUVDAILY). The hourly UV table redirects 301 — follow redirects or the call silently returns HTML instead of JSON.
- NOAA CDO API v2 for bulk work — live but wrong tool. 5 req/sec and 10,000 req/day sounds fine until you hit the 1,000-record pagination ceiling and the frequent gateway timeouts on multi-year GHCND pulls. Use RCC-ACIS, the NCEI Access Data Service, or s3://noaa-ghcn-pds for anything larger than a lookup.
- NOAA NOMADS for production polling — you will be IP-blocked. NOMADS enforces an undocumented abuse throttle (commonly reported around 120 hits/minute, official number UNKNOWN) and retains only ~7-10 days. It is for interactive subsetting, not for a terminal's ingest loop. Use the AWS NODD buckets, which have no call limit.
- RainViewer free public API — licence, not rate, is the blocker. The terms restrict free use to 'personal and educational' purposes and explicitly disclaim data availability. A commercial Bloomberg-style terminal is neither. Verify licensing before shipping; MRMS on AWS is unrestricted for US coverage.
- Google WeatherNext / Earth Engine — free only for non-commercial. Earth Engine is free for research, education and nonprofit use; commercial use requires a paid plan. BigQuery gives 1 TiB of query processing free per month, then bills. The datasets are public; the compute is not.
- Copernicus CDS and ADS — free but latency-hostile. There is no published rate limit because there is no rate limit in the usual sense: requests enter a cost-weighted queue and a large ERA5 pull can take hours. Never put a CDS call on a user-facing code path. Pre-stage everything, or use arco-era5 / Open-Meteo archive for interactive work.
- A general warning on the catalog repos named in the task: public-apis/public-apis and its forks carry roughly eight weather entries, several of which are Dark Sky-era corpses. This domain's live inventory is not in the general API lists — it is in awslabs/open-data-registry (structured, current) and pangeo-data/awesome-open-climate-science (domain-curated). Searching the general lists for weather is close to a waste of time.
- The settlement-vs-forecast mismatch — the most expensive trap in this domain, and it is not an API failure. Daily city temperature contracts settle on the NWS CLI daily climate report for one designated station (NYC = Central Park, USW00094728), not on a gridded model value, not on an airport METAR, and not on any commercial API's 'current temperature'. ERA5 grid cells, Open-Meteo point interpolations and OpenWeatherMap readings will all differ from the CLI value by amounts that routinely exceed a contract's strike spacing. Price with models; settle with NWS CLI (api.weather.gov/products/types/CLI) or RCC-ACIS. Both are VERIFIED live and both are free.

### Natural Disasters & Geophysical Hazards

- ReliefWeb API v1 — HARD DEAD. Returns HTTP 410 with body: 'The API version v1 has been decommissioned. Please use version v2 instead.' Every tutorial, every awesome-list entry, and most GitHub clients still point at v1. Verified 2026-09-20.
- ReliefWeb API v2 without a pre-approved appname — returns HTTP 403 AccessDeniedHttpException. Since 1 November 2025 an arbitrary appname string no longer works; you must request approval. Verified with appname=echo-research. This breaks the long-standing 'just put any string in appname' pattern that nearly every code sample uses.
- usgs/libcomcat — ARCHIVED on GitHub, last pushed 2023-03-02 (verified via GitHub API, archived:true). It is still the top Google result for programmatic ComCat access. Do not build on it; query the FDSN event service directly, which is stable and documented.
- IRIS FDSN event service (service.iris.edu/fdsnws/event/1/query) — HTTP 404. IRIS merged into EarthScope, and I also tried service.earthscope.org/fdsnws/event/1/query which likewise returned 404. IRIS/EarthScope still serve station and waveform data, but for the EVENT catalog use USGS or EMSC. Many awesome-lists still cite the IRIS event endpoint.
- EMSC legacy RSS (emsc-csem.org/service/rss/rss.php?typ=emsc) — HTTP 404. Superseded by the seismicportal.eu FDSN service and WebSocket. Widely cited in older OSINT lists.
- MeteoAlarm legacy RSS (feeds.meteoalarm.org/feeds/meteoalarm-legacy-rss-europe) — returns HTTP 200 but the body is only a deprecation notice pointing at meteoalarm-legacy-atom-europe, and THAT Atom URL returned HTTP 404 in my test. Both legacy paths are effectively dead; use the /api/v1/warnings/feeds-{country} endpoints. This is a 200-that-is-really-a-404, so a naive health check will not catch it.
- NOAA NCEI Billion-Dollar Weather and Climate Disasters — RETIRED. NOAA announced 8 May 2025 that NCEI will no longer update the product; data is frozen at calendar year 2024 and the /access/monitoring/dyk/billions URL returns HTTP 404. The 1980–2024 archive remains available, but there will be no 2025+ figures. Any contract or model that assumed a live US disaster-cost series needs a different source (Gallagher Re / Aon / Munich Re, all paid).
- Smithsonian volcano.si.edu/api — HTTP 403 to any non-browser client (returns a 5.5 KB block page). The API appears to exist but is bot-blocked. Use the GeoServer WFS at webservices.volcano.si.edu/geoserver/GVP-VOTW/wfs instead, which returned HTTP 200 for both GetCapabilities and GetFeature.
- EM-DAT (emdat.be) — site is live but this is NOT a free API. Access is by registered account, is restricted to non-commercial academic/humanitarian use, and is delivered as manual Excel/CSV downloads rather than a queryable endpoint. A commercial prediction-market product does not qualify under the free licence. Frequently miscategorized as free in awesome-lists.
- Pacific Disaster Center (pdc.org) — HTTP 403 to non-browser clients. The underlying DisasterAWARE API is partner-gated (government/NGO agreements), not publicly self-service. Listed as 'free' in several OSINT lists; it is not.
- api.gdacs.org — HTTP 404. The correct host is www.gdacs.org with the /gdacsapi/api/... path prefix. A plausible-looking hostname that does not exist.
- Copernicus CDS legacy API (cds.climate.copernicus.eu/api/v2) — HTTP 404. The legacy CDS API was retired in the 2024–2025 Data Stores migration. GloFAS and other early-warning datasets moved to the Early Warning Data Store (ewds.climate.copernicus.eu), which requires a new account and a new API token. Every pre-2025 cdsapi code sample is broken.
- api2.effis.emergency.copernicus.eu — HTTP 404 for the statistics paths I tried. The working EFFIS endpoints are still on effis.jrc.ec.europa.eu/apps/... The new-looking hostname resolves but does not serve the documented paths.
- Copernicus EMS Rapid Mapping (EMSR activations) — emergency.copernicus.eu/mapping/list-of-components/EMSR returned HTTP 404, and more fundamentally this is not a live feed: Rapid Mapping products are generated only on authorized activation, delivered as PDF maps and vector packages days after an event. Not pollable, not a settlement source. Use GDACS and GloFAS for the live Copernicus signal instead.
- Xweather / Aeris Weather (data.api.xweather.com) — HTTP 401. Fully commercial, paid. Its old 'free developer tier' branding still circulates in API lists.
- Synoptic Data / MesoWest (api.mesowest.net/v2) — HTTP 401 without a token. There is a free tier but it requires registration and is capped; the open-access era ended. Commonly listed as free.
- JMA bosai JSON endpoints (www.jma.go.jp/bosai/volcano/data/list.json, /bosai/quake/data/quake.json, /bosai/volcano/data/forecast/volcano_list.json) — all HTTP 404. These paths circulate widely in blog posts. Only /bosai/quake/data/list.json still worked in my test (279 KB). The stable, intended machine interface is the developer XML feed at www.data.jma.go.jp/developer/xml/feed/eqvol.xml.
- Environment Canada dd.weather.gc.ca/alerts/cap/ — HTTP 404. The datamart was reorganized into date-partitioned trees; CAP alerts now live at dd.weather.gc.ca/YYYYMMDD/WXO-DD/alerts/cap/ (verified 200). Also tried dd.meteo.gc.ca/alerts/cap/ and dd.alpha.meteo.gc.ca/alerts/cap/ — both 404. Every older Canadian-alerts integration is pointing at a dead path.
- NASA disaster mapping ArcGIS roots (maps.disasters.nasa.gov/arcgis/rest/services returned 404; maps.nccs.nasa.gov/arcgis/rest/services did not connect at all). NASA's disaster GIS delivery has moved; verify current hosting before depending on it.
- GDELT DOC 2.0 API — live but returned HTTP 429 Too Many Requests on the very first request from a cold IP. It is technically free and technically alive, but the shared rate pool is so contended that it is unusable as a reliable production feed. Architect against the free raw 15-minute CSV files or the free GDELT BigQuery dataset instead of the live API.
- SPC today.csv (spc.noaa.gov/climo/reports/today.csv) — returns HTTP 200 with ZERO bytes early in the UTC day before any storm reports exist. An empty 200, not an error. A pipeline that trusts the status code will silently ingest nothing; use the date-keyed YYMMDD_rpts.csv and check content length.
- NOAA NWPS gauge search (api.water.noaa.gov/nwps/v1/gauges?srch=...) — did not respond (connection failure), while the direct /nwps/v1/gauges/{id} path returned 200 with 44 KB. Resolve gauge IDs from USGS NWIS or the NWPS station list, then fetch by explicit ID.
- tsunami.gov /events/xml/ directory listing — HTTP 403. You cannot enumerate available feeds; you must know the four-letter product codes (PAAQ = National Tsunami Warning Center, PHEB = Pacific Tsunami Warning Center Caribbean, etc.) out of band.
- NASA FIRMS without a MAP_KEY — HTTP 401 (verified with a placeholder key). The key is free and instant, but every request needs it embedded in the URL path, which means the key leaks into logs and referrers. Plan key rotation accordingly.
- Open-Meteo free tier for a commercial product — a LICENSING dead end rather than a technical one. All endpoints (forecast, ensemble, archive, flood) return HTTP 200 with no key, so nothing stops you technically. But the free tier is explicitly non-commercial; a prediction-market terminal is commercial use. Budget for the subscription or migrate to ECMWF Open Data + NOMADS, which are commercially licence-clean.
- NOAA api.weather.gov 'limit' parameter — returns HTTP 400 'Query parameter limit is not recognized'. A very common wrong assumption carried over from other REST APIs; use pagination cursors instead.
- NOAA api.weather.gov rate limit — NOT a dead end but an unquantifiable one: NOAA explicitly states the limit 'is not public information'. You cannot capacity-plan against it. Implement adaptive backoff on 429 rather than a fixed budget, and note NOAA says User-Agent auth will be replaced by API keys at some future date, which will be a breaking change.

### Economics & Macro Statistics

- Trading Economics free/guest tier — DEAD, CONFIRMED. The long-standing c=guest:guest credential now returns HTTP 410 Gone with the literal body 'We are sorry, but the guest account has been discontinued. Please subscribe to a plan.' This is the single most commonly cited 'free economic API' in tutorials, blog posts and awesome-lists, and every one of those references is now stale. Both /calendar and /country endpoints confirmed 410. There is no free tier at all — paid only.
- ONS (UK) legacy timeseries API — DEAD, CONFIRMED. https://api.ons.gov.uk/timeseries/{id}/dataset/{ds}/data returns a plain-text decommission notice: 'This API has been decommissioned... It was fully retired on 25/11/2024.' Note it returns HTTP 404 with that text, so a naive client that only checks for a 200 will silently ingest the notice string. Use https://api.beta.ons.gov.uk/v1/ instead.
- IMF legacy SDMX 2.0 service (dataservices.imf.org/REST/SDMX_JSON.svc/) — DEAD, CONFIRMED. Connection failed entirely (HTTP 000, not even a 404). The IMF migrated to SDMX 3.0 on data.imf.org and broke every downstream client without a deprecation window — the imfp and imfr packages stopped working overnight. I also could not confirm the new base path: https://api.imf.org/external/sdmx/3.0/dataflow returned 404. Until you verify the correct endpoint against the live portal, route IMF data through DBnomics.
- CME FedWatch API — NOT FREE. The web tool is free to look at; programmatic access starts around $25/month for end-of-day snapshots, more for intraday and the 60-second probability stream. Historical settlement archives sit behind CME DataMine, also paid. The public quotes page is bot-protected and scrape-only. Use the Atlanta Fed Market Probability Tracker instead — it is free, official, and methodologically better (full option-implied distribution rather than a futures-implied point estimate); its only cost is a one-session lag.
- Nasdaq Data Link (formerly Quandl) — EFFECTIVELY DEAD for free programmatic use. Both https://data.nasdaq.com/api/v3/datasets/FRED/GDP.json and the metadata endpoint returned HTTP 403 behind an Incapsula bot wall. The free-table catalogue has been progressively gutted since the Nasdaq acquisition (WIKI equity prices already discontinued for new users). Whatever free economic tables remain are FRED mirrors you can get uncapped and unblocked from FRED directly. Do not build on this.
- ISM Manufacturing and Services PMI — LEGALLY RESTRICTED, not technically blocked. ISM grants only a 'limited, revocable, nonsublicensable license... solely for personal, non-commercial use' and explicitly forbids creating, recreating, distributing or incorporating the index into other work without prior written authorization. Third-party mirrors (DBnomics ISM/pmi, various CSV sites) are technically reachable but redistributing ISM values in a commercial product is a licensing problem, not a data problem. Get written authorization before shipping ISM numbers in a paid panel. Same caution applies to S&P Global PMI and Conference Board Consumer Confidence — both are commercial licensed products with no free API.
- EconDB — NO LONGER FREE for series data. The API root (https://www.econdb.com/api/) still enumerates endpoints publicly, but https://www.econdb.com/api/series/{code}/ now returns HTTP 401 {'detail':'Authentication credentials were not provided.'}. Many 2023-2025 listings still describe it as 'no API key needed for public access' — that is out of date. A free registered tier may exist but its limits are undocumented and unverified.
- Finnhub and Financial Modeling Prep economic calendars — PAID. Both returned HTTP 401 on demo/no-key probes. FMP's economic calendar and Finnhub's /calendar/economic are premium-tier endpoints; their free tiers cover equities, not macro releases. Use the ForexFactory JSON endpoint for a free calendar with consensus.
- www.bls.gov HTML pages (schedule, news releases) — BOT-BLOCKED. https://www.bls.gov/schedule/2026/home.htm and the .ics calendar export both return HTTP 403 'Access Denied' to non-browser user agents. This traps anyone trying to scrape the BLS release schedule. The API host api.bls.gov is completely unaffected and works without a key on v1 — and the FRED releases/dates endpoint carries the BLS schedule in structured form. Never scrape bls.gov; use the APIs.
- Atlanta Fed guessed file paths — a practical trap worth naming. The Atlanta Fed serves 404 pages with HTTP 200 status, so a status-code check will happily accept an HTML error page as your data file. The real paths are under /-/media/Project/Atlanta/FRBA/Documents/... (not the shorter /-/media/documents/... that older links and blog posts use). Always validate content-type and magic bytes, not just the status code — this is exactly the 'a missing measurement is not a measured zero' failure mode, where a broken fetch silently looks like an empty dataset.
- OECD SDMX structure queries with format=jsondata — WRONG PARAMETER, returns HTTP 406. Structure endpoints accept only structure, xml-structure-3.0.0, sdmx-3.0 or json-structure-2.0.0; jsondata is valid for DATA queries only. Helpfully the 406 body enumerates the legal values, but this will look like an outage if you only log status codes.
- Apify-hosted 'free economic calendar APIs' — these dominate search results for economic calendar APIs and are all commercial scraper-rental actors with per-run compute billing, not free feeds. They are reselling ForexFactory, Nasdaq and BLS data you can get directly for free. Skip them.
- ForexFactory JSON endpoint — USE IT, BUT KNOW THE RISK. nfs.faireconomy.media is undocumented, has no published terms, and carries only a three-week window (last/this/next). There is no archive, so history exists only if you snapshot it daily starting now. Undocumented endpoints disappear without notice. It is the best free consensus-forecast source available, but architect it as a fragile dependency with a cached fallback, not as a load-bearing primary.
- Free consensus/forecast data generally — the structural gap in this entire domain. Official statistical agencies publish the ACTUAL number; almost none publish the market CONSENSUS. Since a contract's price is driven by the surprise (actual minus expected), the consensus is half the signal and is overwhelmingly a paid product (Bloomberg, Refinitiv, Econoday, Action Economics). The only free structured exceptions found: ForexFactory's forecast field (undocumented, fragile), Brazil's BCB Focus survey (excellent, full distribution, but Brazil only), the ECB Survey of Professional Forecasters, the Fed's own SEP dot plot (quarterly, US only), and model-based nowcasts (Cleveland Fed, Atlanta Fed GDPNow) which substitute a model forecast for a survey consensus. Plan around this gap explicitly rather than assuming a free consensus feed exists.

### Financial Markets (equities, options/IV, rates, credit, FX, futures, crypto, volatility, breadth, positioning, filings)

- IEX Cloud — FULLY DEAD. IEX Group announced retirement on 2024-05-31 and shut down all API products on 2024-08-31; every endpoint is off and accounts are inactive. Customers were referred to Intrinio (paid). Any tutorial, library or catalogue still listing IEX Cloud is stale. Do not build against it.
- Stooq CSV bulk download — EFFECTIVELY DEAD for automation.
