Both https://stooq.com/q/d/l/?s=spy.us&i=d and the .pl mirror now return a 796-byte JavaScript browser-verification challenge ('This site requires JavaScript to verify your browser') instead of CSV, with HTTP 200 so naive code thinks it succeeded. Verified 2026-09-20. pandas-datareader's Stooq reader is broken by this. Requires a headless browser to work at all.
- Binance.com global API — GEO-BLOCKED from US IPs with HTTP 451 on both api.binance.com (spot) and fapi.binance.com (USD-M futures). Verified 2026-09-20. This kills the most commonly cited free source of perpetual FUNDING RATES and futures open interest. Workarounds: api.binance.us (spot only — NO perps, NO funding) or OKX v5 public (has funding, verified working).
- Bybit API — GEO-BLOCKED. api.bybit.com returns HTTP 403 'The Amazon CloudFront distribution is configured to block access from your country'. Verified 2026-09-20. Another commonly-listed free funding-rate source that does not work from a US host.
- CME Group web services — BLOCKED AND HOSTILE. https://www.cmegroup.com/services/... returns HTTP 403 with 'This IP address is blocked due to suspected web scraping activity'; the CmeWS settlement endpoint (/CmeWS/mvc/Settlements/Futures/...) drops the HTTP/2 stream. Verified 2026-09-20. There is NO free programmatic CME settlement or futures feed. For futures prices use Yahoo continuous contracts (ES=F, CL=F, GC=F, ZN=F — verified working) and accept that they are not official settlements.
- Dune Analytics free tier — FUNCTIONALLY DEAD FOR API USE as of 2026. Dune's own docs state 'free executions are not supported via the API' — free credits cannot be spent through the API at all. Worse, from 2026-09-10 accounts created before 2026-07-21 were converted to VIEW-ONLY and can no longer run queries without a paid plan (paid tiers start around $399/mo). The 2,500 monthly credits are a web-UI allowance, not an API allowance. Do not plan on Dune as a free on-chain query layer.
- Yahoo Finance v7 options endpoint — requires an authenticated cookie + crumb pair. A bare GET to query2.finance.yahoo.com/v7/finance/options/SPY returns HTTP 401 {'code':'Unauthorized','description':'Invalid Crumb'}. Verified 2026-09-20. Only reachable via yfinance's session handshake, and subject to the same unpredictable blocking.
- Yahoo Finance v8 chart endpoint — WORKS but is unreliable in a way that will bite you. The identical URL returned HTTP 429 'Too Many Requests' on one call and HTTP 200 minutes later from the same IP, with no documented limit, no Retry-After and no key to raise it. Verified both outcomes 2026-09-20. Never use it as a settlement/resolution source; only as a signal with a fallback.
- Nasdaq Data Link /api/v3/datasets/ path — Akamai bot-blocked, returns HTTP 403 with a NOINDEX interstitial regardless of User-Agent or api_key, including for classic free datasets like LBMA/GOLD and FRED/GDP. The /api/v3/datatables/ path still works (verified with api_key=demo). Separately, the free dataset catalogue has shrunk enormously since the Quandl era — most of what made Quandl worth using is now paid.
- Cboe historical CSV paths — 403 AccessDenied, despite the delayed-quote CDN being wide open. Both https://cdn.cboe.com/api/global/us_indices/daily_prices/_VIX_History.csv and https://cdn.cboe.com/data/us/options/market_statistics/daily/... are blocked. Only /api/global/delayed_quotes/, /api/global/us_indices/definitions/ and /resources/options/volume_and_call_put_ratios/ are public. Use FRED (VIXCLS) for VIX history instead.
- Alpha Vantage REALTIME_OPTIONS — PREMIUM ONLY. Free and low-tier keys receive placeholder/demo data rather than real market data, which is the dangerous failure mode: you get a 200 and a well-formed payload that is not real. Only HISTORICAL_OPTIONS works on the free tier. Also note the free daily quota has been cut repeatedly (500/day → 100/day → 25/day) — any tutorial quoting 500/day is stale.
- Massive / Polygon.io free tier — NO OPTIONS DATA. Options access begins on a paid plan (~$79/mo). Combined with 5 calls/minute, the free tier cannot support live pricing of anything. Also note the rebrand: Polygon.io became Massive.com on 2025-10-30 and the primary host is now api.massive.com (api.polygon.io still resolves but is legacy).
- Twelve Data free Basic plan — NO OPTIONS and NO FUNDAMENTALS. Those start at the paid Grow tier. Global symbols are trial-only on free; you get US equities, forex and crypto.
- marketdata.app free tier for full chains — a TRAP. The plan advertises 100 requests/day, but an options chain bills ONE CREDIT PER CONTRACT RETURNED. A single SPX chain (20,000+ contracts) exhausts the entire daily allowance in one call. Free data is also delayed by at least 24 hours. Fine for single-strike lookups, useless for surfaces.
- Finnhub free/premium boundary — NOT DETERMINABLE FROM DOCS. Both finnhub.io/pricing and finnhub.io/docs/api are JavaScript-rendered and return no substantive text to a fetcher. The official Swagger spec (588 KB, fetched successfully) flags only 1 of 116 operations as premium, so it cannot be used to tell which of /stock/insider-transactions, /institutional/ownership, /stock/eps-estimate and /stock/recommendation are actually free. /stock/option-chain is reported as premium. You must probe with a live free key before depending on any of these. The widely-repeated '60 calls/min' free limit is from secondary sources, not a primary page render.
- SEC EDGAR with a generic browser User-Agent — HTTP 403. https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar returned 403 with a Chrome UA and 200 with 'ECHO Research research@example.com'. SEC requires a descriptive User-Agent containing a real contact email on EVERY request. This silently breaks any library that sets a browser UA.
- SEC Form 13F dataset filenames — do NOT guess them. The old YYYYqN_form13f.zip pattern stopped after 2023q4; files are now rolling three-month ranges (01jun2026-31aug2026_form13f.zip) and the most recent one is served from /files/datastandardsinnovation/ rather than /files/structureddata/. Guessed URLs like 2026q2_form13f.zip return 404. Scrape the index page for the current link. Note the insider-transactions datasets still DO use the YYYYqN pattern (2026q1_form345.zip verified working) — the two datasets diverge.
- CoinGecko keyless public API — the rate limit is IP-based and SHARED ACROSS EVERY USER ON THAT IP, with no published number. On shared infrastructure (cloud NAT, CI runners, Google Sheets) you will get 429s that have nothing to do with your own usage. 4xx and 5xx responses ALSO count against the limit. Register a free Demo key (100 calls/min, 10,000 credits/month) rather than relying on keyless.
- CoinMarketCap free Basic tier — NO HISTORICAL DATA AT ALL. Historical endpoints start at the paid Hobbyist tier. The free tier is latest-snapshot only, which makes it unusable for any modelling or backtest.
- Etherscan free tier chain coverage — REDUCED. A policy change announced 2025-11-22 cut free-tier chain coverage to roughly 90% of supported chain IDs; about 10% of chains now require the paid Lite plan. The 5 calls/sec limit is also shared across ALL chains on one key, not per chain.
- Tradier sandbox — not anonymously accessible. https://sandbox.tradier.com/v1/markets/options/chains returns 'Invalid access token'. It is free with signup but requires an account and token, so it is not a drop-in keyless options source.
- GDELT DOC API — aggressive undocumented throttle. Returned HTTP 429 'Please limit requests to one every 5 seconds' on a single first request. Usable, but only at 0.2 req/sec; GDELT directs high-traffic users to its bulk ngrams datasets instead.
- General warning on secondary sources in this domain: many 2026 blog posts, comparison sites and 'awesome' lists still quote Alpha Vantage at 500 calls/day, list IEX Cloud as live, cite Polygon.io rather than Massive, and present Binance global as freely reachable. Every one of those is wrong as of 2026-09-20. Verify against the live endpoint before committing to any limit.

### Companies & Corporate Events

- PatentsView Search API (search.patentsview.org) — CONFIRMED DEAD. The hostname does not resolve at all: DNS lookup failed from two independent network paths (curl returned code 000, WebFetch returned ENOTFOUND). PatentsView ended legacy-API support 1 May 2025, migrated to the USPTO Open Data Portal on 20 March 2026, and the legacy Developer Hub was decommissioned 5 June 2026. Critically, PatentsView-issued API keys are NOT compatible with ODP — you must obtain a new key. Every GitHub wrapper targeting PatentsView is now broken. Use data.uspto.gov / api.uspto.gov instead.
- developer.uspto.gov legacy API catalog (PTAB API, IBD publications API, etc.) — DEAD. Both endpoints tested returned 301 redirects with no working target. The legacy USPTO Developer Hub was decommissioned 5 June 2026. Its functionality moved to ODP.
- USPTO Patent Assignment API (assignment-api.uspto.gov) — connection failed entirely (curl code 000, no DNS resolution). Assignment data is now served through the ODP APIs instead.
- OpenCorporates — LOOKS free, is not. API returned 401 'Invalid Api Token'. Free API accounts exist ONLY if you publish results under an open licence with share-alike attribution, and are rate-limited to roughly 50 requests/day and 200/month. Commercial use requires a paid plan starting around £2,250/year for 500 calls/month. Despite its reputation as the open company database, it is not a usable free feed for a commercial prediction-market panel. Use GLEIF plus national registries (Companies House, Brønnøysund, recherche-entreprises) instead.
- EU Business Registers / BRIS via the European e-Justice Portal — NO MACHINE API. Both e-justice.europa.eu URLs tested returned 403. BRIS is a human-facing search portal that federates national registers; there is no public REST endpoint. Go to each national register individually.
- Netherlands KvK API (api.kvk.nl) — returned 401 with a zero-byte body. Requires a paid subscription; there is no free tier for commercial use.
- Germany OffeneRegister (db.offeneregister.de) — returned 502 Bad Gateway. The community mirror of the German Handelsregister appears to be down. The official Handelsregister has no free API. Germany is a genuine coverage gap.
- Denmark cvrapi.dk — returned {'error':'QUOTA_EXCEEDED'} on the very first unauthenticated request from this IP. The free tier is shared-IP quota-limited to effectively nothing. Use the official Virk/CVR service with registration instead.
- France INSEE Sirene API (api.insee.fr/api-sirene) — returned 401. INSEE moved to a portal-based key system. The genuinely free, key-free alternative is recherche-entreprises.api.gouv.fr, which is listed in feeds and was verified working.
- Canada federated corporate registry search (searchapi.mrasservice.ca) — connection failed entirely (curl code 000). No working public endpoint found.
- Singapore data.gov.sg API — returned 403 to unauthenticated requests. ACRA company data requires registration/payment.
- India MCA (mca.gov.in) — returned 403. No public API; the MCA21 portal is captcha-gated and pay-per-document.
- Crunchbase API — returned 401. The free/basic API tier for general developers has been discontinued; free access is now limited to academic and journalist programs by application. Do NOT plan around a Crunchbase free tier for private-company funding or M&A data.
- Nasdaq Data Link (Quandl) — returned 403. The free WIKI equities dataset has been discontinued for years and the platform is now paid/enterprise.
- api.nasdaq.com (unofficial earnings and IPO calendar endpoints) — connection failed entirely (code 000) for both the earnings and IPO calendar paths. Nasdaq blocks datacenter and cloud IP ranges. These are unofficial, undocumented endpoints with no terms permitting use; do not build on them.
- IEX Cloud — connection failed (code 000). IEX Cloud shut down in August 2024. Any repo or directory still listing it is stale.
- Yahoo Finance unofficial APIs (query1/query2.finance.yahoo.com) — returned 405. There is no official free Yahoo Finance API; the unofficial endpoints now require crumb/cookie handshakes, break without notice, and are outside Yahoo's terms. Not a foundation to build on.
- Tiingo (403), EODHD (403 'Forbidden. Please contact support'), Polygon.io (401), Marketstack (401) — all alive but key-gated with restrictive free tiers. None returned usable data without registration. Listed here so they are not mistaken for open feeds; each may be worth a free key but none is an open endpoint.
- layoffs.fyi — NO API. The site returned 200 but the underlying Airtable embed returned 404, and no documented public API exists. The dataset is human-curated and presented through a UI. Scrape-only, and the terms do not clearly permit it. Use WARN notices (legally mandated, earlier, structured) as the primary layoff feed instead.
- warntracker.com — NO PUBLIC API. The site loads (200) but /api/notices returned 404. It is a Next.js front end over its own scrape. Use biglocalnews/warn-scraper directly rather than depending on a third party's undocumented internals.
- USDA FSIS recall API (fsis.usda.gov/fsis/api/recall/v/1) — returned 403 Access Denied with an explicit block page. Meat and poultry recalls are therefore not available via this path; openFDA /food/enforcement covers FDA-regulated food only, so USDA-regulated products are a gap.
- SEC litigation releases RSS (sec.gov/rss/litigation/litreleases.xml) — returned 404. This widely-cited feed is dead. The administrative proceedings feed (sec.gov/rss/litigation/admin.xml) DOES still work and returned 200 — use that one.
- DOJ Antitrust Division-specific RSS — returned 404. Only the general Office of Public Affairs feed (justice.gov/feeds/opa/justice-news.xml) works; filter it by component rather than assuming a per-division feed.
- EU Commission press corner API (ec.europa.eu/commission/presscorner/api/documents) — returned 400. No working documented public API found for EU merger-decision press releases. The competition-cases.ec.europa.eu site returned 200 but serves a JavaScript single-page app with no JSON API behind the tested path — treat EU merger decisions as scrape-only, or proxy them via GDELT and the Federal Register equivalents.
- ProductHunt API — returned 404 on the GraphQL endpoint without OAuth. Requires an OAuth application; there is no key-free path. Product-launch signal is better taken from Hacker News (free, no auth) and GitHub releases.
- Lens.org API — returned 401. Free access is restricted to non-commercial academic use by application; commercial use is paid.
- OpenSanctions API — returned 401 'No API key provided'. The hosted API is free only for non-commercial use with a key; commercial use requires a licence. The bulk data files are separately available under their own licence terms — check those before assuming sanctions data is free for a commercial panel.
- Google Patents — has no official public API. The xhr/query endpoint returned 200 but is undocumented, unofficial and outside Google's terms. The legitimate free path is Google Patents Public Data on BigQuery, which is free to query only within BigQuery's own free tier (1 TB/month) and is not a REST feed.
- Wikidata Query Service SPARQL endpoint — returned 502 Bad Gateway and 400 during this research. WDQS is chronically overloaded, enforces a 60-second query timeout and 5 concurrent queries per IP, and returns 502 under load. Do NOT put it on a critical settlement path; use the Wikidata bulk dumps or Special:EntityData (which did return 200) instead.
- Wikipedia Pageviews API — returned 429 from this datacenter IP on the first request. Wikimedia throttles cloud/shared IPs aggressively regardless of the documented 200 req/s anonymous figure. Budget for rejection and use the bulk pageview dumps for any systematic collection.
- GDELT DOC 2.0 API — NOT dead but severely throttled: returned 429 with the explicit message 'Please limit requests to one every 5 seconds', and GDELT directs high-traffic users to its ngrams dataset. It is a lookup tool, not a firehose. The raw 15-minute CSV files at data.gdeltproject.org DID return 200 and are the correct path at scale.
- SAM.gov api.sam.gov endpoints without a key — returned 404, NOT 401. The route does not resolve unless the api_key query parameter is present, which makes the API look dead to casual probing. It is alive; you simply cannot verify it without a key. Also note the hard ceiling: 1,000 requests/day for non-federal accounts with NO application process to raise it.
- GitHub Search API unauthenticated — hit 'API rate limit exceeded' after roughly 10 search calls in one minute during this research. Unauthenticated core is 60 requests/hour and search is 10 requests/minute (both confirmed live). Always use a free personal access token: 5,000/hour core and 30/minute search.

### Energy, Commodities, Mining & Minerals

- Nasdaq Data Link / Quandl (data.nasdaq.com) — returns 403. The free community datasets that this domain historically depended on (LBMA/GOLD, LBMA/SILVER, ODA commodity series, CHRIS continuous futures) have been retired or moved behind Nasdaq's commercial licensing. Every tutorial and GitHub repo still importing quandl for commodity data is stale. Use LBMA's own JSON and World Bank Pink Sheet instead — both are free and both are the actual primary sources Quandl was republishing.
- Trading Economics guest API (api.tradingeconomics.com with c=guest:guest) — returns HTTP 410 Gone. The guest credential that half the internet's commodity tutorials use is permanently retired. Trading Economics is now fully paid. The web pages also refuse programmatic fetches.
- CME Group settlement endpoints (cmegroup.com/CmeWS/mvc/Settlements/...) — HTTP 403 from Akamai bot protection. Official crude, gas, gold and copper futures settlements are not freely accessible programmatically despite the settlement pages rendering in a browser. Any repo claiming a free CME settlements feed is either scraping through a proxy or reselling. Treat exchange-official futures settlement as a paid dependency.
- LME (lme.com) historical data — HTTP 403, and the underlying data is licensed and paid regardless. LME official copper/aluminium/nickel prices and warehouse stocks are NOT free in any form. This is the single biggest genuine gap in free base-metals coverage — there is no free equivalent of LBMA for base metals. Budget for it or accept a proxy.
- IEA (iea.org) data and statistics, including the Critical Minerals Policy Tracker — HTTP 403 to programmatic fetch, and the substantive datasets (World Energy Outlook, Oil Market Report, monthly oil statistics) are paid subscription. Only a thin free browsing layer exists. The user's brief named 'IEA free data' — the honest answer is that there is very little of it, and JODI (which the IEA co-sponsors) is the free substitute.
- OPEC (opec.org, momr.opec.org, asb.opec.org) — HTTP 403 across all paths, and there is no api.opec.org (does not resolve). The Monthly Oil Market Report is a PDF with no machine-readable feed and no API, ever. OPEC production and quota decisions must be sourced from JODI (self-reported member data), from secondary-source estimates inside the MOMR PDF, or from news via GDELT. There is no clean structured OPEC feed at any price tier that is free.
- Kpler and Vortexa — no free tier for cargo tracking. Both are enterprise-priced. The brief asked to check 'Kpler/Vortexa free tiers'; there are none. MarineTraffic (Kpler-owned) has a freemium web product but returns 403 to automated fetches and its API is paid. Free AIS alternatives worth trying instead: aisstream.io (free WebSocket with registration — I could not verify the handshake, its HTTP root does not respond, which is expected for a WebSocket service) and the Norwegian Coastal Administration's open AIS feed.
- CEIC — fully commercial, no free tier, no public API. Named in the brief; it does not belong in a free-sources build.
- Stooq CSV download (stooq.com/q/d/l/) — now serves a JavaScript proof-of-work browser challenge instead of CSV. The long-standing free path to continuous futures history for CL.F, NG.F, GC.F is effectively closed to plain HTTP clients. Many GitHub commodity backtesting repos still depend on it and are silently broken.
- api.nationalgrideso.com — DEAD, does not resolve at all. National Grid ESO became NESO and the data portal moved to api.neso.energy. Multiple GitHub wrappers, Home Assistant integrations and tutorials still point at the old host.
- Panama Canal transit statistics (pcweb.pancanal.com) — connection failed, no response. Canal transit and draft restriction data, which was a genuinely high-signal feed during the 2023-24 drought, has no reliable free programmatic endpoint. Suez Canal Authority's statistics page does respond but is HTML tables only, no API.
- Investing.com commodities — HTTP 403 to automated fetches; scraping violates their terms. Not a viable source despite appearing in many 'free commodity API' listicles.
- EPA CAMPD API (api.epa.gov/easey/...) — HTTP 403 without an API key, and the beta/dev bulk-file paths in older documentation now 404. A free key is obtainable but the endpoint paths in most existing tutorials are stale. The web portal at epa.gov/power-sector/cam-api-portal is live; go through it rather than guessing endpoints.
- The commercial metals API cluster (Metals-API, MetalpriceAPI, Commodities-API, metals.dev, GoldAPI.io, OilPriceAPI) — these respond and do have free tiers, but they are aggregators reselling data you can get from primary sources, their free quotas are small (GoldAPI cited at 1,000 calls/month; others UNKNOWN and undisclosed on their public pages), they apply delays on free tiers, and none of them are a valid contract resolution source. Specifically: do not use any of them for precious metals when LBMA publishes the actual benchmark fixings free with 58 years of history and no key.
- Apify 'scrapers' for USGS MCS, USGS MRDS and Ember data — these appear in search results as if they were APIs. They are paid per-result wrappers ($2.00/1,000 results for the commodity monitor) around data that is free and directly downloadable from USGS ScienceBase and api.ember-energy.org. Pure middleman cost.
- USGS MRDS caveat (not dead, but misleading) — MRDS responds and the CSV dump downloads, but it is a legacy static database that is no longer maintained as a live register of operating mines. Records describe historical occurrences and past producers. Treating an MRDS 'producer' flag as current operating status will be wrong for a large fraction of rows. Use Global Energy Monitor's trackers for current asset status.
- Open Power System Data caveat (not dead, but frozen) — the portal and downloads work, but the project has concluded. Time series stop at their last versioned release. Excellent historical corpus, useless as a live feed, and it is presented in enough places as a current EU data source to mislead.

### Politics, Elections and Government (US + international) — free data feeds, verified September 2026

- ProPublica Congress API — DEAD, confirmed two ways. The propublica/congress-api-docs repo was ARCHIVED by the owner on 4 February 2025 with a notice that the docs are historical reference only, and I got HTTP 401 from https://api.propublica.org/congress/v1/113/senate/members.json. No replacement was offered. This is the single most common stale recommendation in this domain — nearly every tutorial, awesome-list and LLM answer still names it first. Replacements: Congress.gov API v3 (bills/members/nominations), Voteview (roll calls), unitedstates/congress-legislators (member crosswalk). Note eyeseast/propublica-congress on GitHub is also archived.
- OpenSecrets API — DEAD as of 15 APRIL 2025, stated on their own page: 'As of April 15, 2025, our API offerings have been discontinued', after 17 years. No free replacement. They now direct users to commercial@opensecrets.org for paid 'custom data solutions', or OS Pro at $15/month / $120/year for a search UI (not an API). Use the FEC's openFEC API and FEC bulk files instead — you lose OpenSecrets' industry/sector classification and lobbying coverage, which has no free equivalent.
- projects.fivethirtyeight.com CSV endpoints — A SOFT-404 TRAP, THE NASTIEST FINDING HERE. https://projects.fivethirtyeight.com/polls/data/president_polls.csv, .../polls-page/data/generic_ballot_polls.csv and .../pollster-ratings/pollster-ratings.csv ALL RETURN HTTP 200. They are not 404s. But the body is 305,461 bytes of ABC News HTML with content-type text/html — a site shell, not data. Any pipeline that checks only the status code will silently ingest an HTML page as a CSV and produce garbage, or worse, produce an empty dataframe that a downstream model treats as 'no polls' rather than 'fetch failed'. A missing measurement is not a measured zero. ALWAYS validate content-type and parse the first row. Use the fivethirtyeight/data GitHub repo instead.
- fivethirtyeight/pollster-ratings (the standalone repo) — GONE. Returns HTTP 404, and it does not appear in the GitHub API listing of the fivethirtyeight org's repos (I enumerated all 30). The data survives ONLY inside fivethirtyeight/data under pollster-ratings/raw_polls.csv. Many citations and papers still point at the dead standalone repo.
- FiveThirtyEight as a live source generally — the site was shut down by ABC in March 2025 and on 15 May 2026 ABC redirected thousands of archived 538 articles to its generic politics section, destroying the article archive. Nothing at fivethirtyeight.com should be treated as a live feed. The GitHub data repo is frozen at its final 2025-02-25 push and will never contain a 2025 or 2026 poll. Mirror it now.
- Google Civic Information API — Representatives endpoints TURNED DOWN 30 APRIL 2025. representativeInfoByAddress and representativeInfoByDivision are gone. The Elections API and Divisions API (including the newer address-to-OCD-ID lookup) survive. If your requirement is 'given an address, list the elected officials', that free capability no longer exists from Google — rebuild it from unitedstates/congress-legislators plus Open States /people.geo.
- Ballotpedia API — NOT FREE, and expensive. Access is subscription-based and reported to cost thousands of dollars per month with specific data requests required; the cheapest entry point is a one-time bulk CSV dump of a single requested report at around $600. There is a developer portal at developer.ballotpedia.org which makes it look open — it is not. Its down-ballot and ballot-measure coverage genuinely has no free equivalent, so budget for it or do without.
- CourtListener's rate limit is a trap even though the API is free and live. The documented default for AUTHENTICATED users is 5 requests per minute, 50 per hour and 125 PER DAY — I read this verbatim from the v4 overview wiki. All three throttles apply concurrently on a rolling window. Any design that polls dockets or paginates a large result set will die almost immediately. This is drastically tighter than the multi-thousand-per-day figures that older documentation and blog posts cite. Use the free BULK DATA dumps plus webhooks; treat the REST API as a delta-fetch mechanism only.
- GovTrack's official bulk data and API — formally ENDED (announced December 2016, shutdown targeted summer 2017), with users directed to ProPublica, which has since also died. The v2 endpoints paradoxically still serve real data today (I got 45,666 role records at HTTP 200), but they are unsupported, undocumented-going-forward, of unverified freshness, and can vanish without notice. A zombie service — cross-check only, never a dependency.
- RealClearPolitics / RealClearPolling — NO PUBLIC API AND ACTIVELY BLOCKED. Both https://www.realclearpolling.com/api/polls and their approval-rating pages returned HTTP 403 to my requests (WAF/bot protection). Their polling averages are proprietary and their terms restrict redistribution. Scrape-only in practice, legally uncomfortable, and technically hostile. Use Silver Bulletin and the 538 archive for averages and ratings instead.
- Roper Center iPoll — NOT FREE. The premier academic archive of historical US survey data (back to 1935) is behind institutional subscription; the iPoll page loads but the data requires membership. No API. If you are not at a subscribing university this is closed to you. It is the best source for deep historical approval and issue polling and there is no free substitute — a genuine gap.
- Metaculus anonymous API access — REMOVED. Requests to /api2/questions/ and /api/posts/ now return HTTP 403 with 'Permission Error: The API is only available to authenticated users. Please create an account and use your API token.' The account and token are free, so this is a friction change rather than a death — but every older integration, tutorial and code sample that hits Metaculus without a token is now broken. Not a dead end if you register; a silent breakage if you do not.
- AP Elections API, Decision Desk HQ, Edison Research exit polls, and Cook Political Report — ALL PAID, all commonly assumed free because their numbers appear everywhere in the press. AP's race calls are the settlement source for many election contracts, which makes the API genuinely valuable and genuinely expensive. Free substitutes for live results: the Clarity Elections vendor endpoints plus individual state Secretary of State feeds. There is no free substitute for an AP race call.
- data.ipu.org (the WEBSITE) returns HTTP 403 to non-browser clients — but api.data.ipu.org serves cleanly with no auth. If you test the wrong host you will wrongly conclude IPU Parline is closed. Same class of error: gamma.polymarket.com fails to connect while gamma-api.polymarket.com works, and api.predictit.org fails while www.predictit.org/api/... works. In this domain, host-level asymmetry is common — always test the exact documented host before declaring a source dead.
- Constituency-Level Elections Archive (CLEA) at electiondataarchive.org — returned HTTP 403 to my request (likely bot protection rather than shutdown). Its constituency-level results for ~170 countries would be genuinely valuable for international contracts, but I could NOT verify access, so treat it as UNVERIFIED rather than confirmed-live. Likely requires a browser session or registration.
- International IDEA Voter Turnout Database — the specific path I tried (idea.int/data-tools/vt-advanced-search) returned HTTP 404; the main data-tools page loads. The database exists and is free, but there is NO API — it is a web UI with manual export. Do not plan on programmatic access.
- ACE Electoral Knowledge Network (aceproject.org) — site is live (HTTP 200) but it is a qualitative ENCYCLOPEDIA of electoral administration practice, not a data feed. No API, no structured datasets, no machine-readable election results. Valuable as background reading for how a country's electoral system works; useless as a pipeline input. It appears on many 'election data sources' lists under a misleading implication that it serves data.
- Vote Smart API — ambiguous, flagged as a risk rather than confirmed dead. The host IS alive (returns a clean XML 'Authorization failed' error to a dummy key), but whether new free API keys are still being issued in 2026 is UNVERIFIED, the developer program appears dormant, and data freshness is unknown. Do not design around it until you hold a working key and have spot-checked recency.
- Census API data queries — partial non-result I am reporting rather than papering over. The catalog endpoint https://api.census.gov/data.json returned HTTP 200 with 5.2 MB, so the service is live, but my actual data queries (2020/dec/pl and 2023/acs/acs1) returned HTTP 200 with an EMPTY body and content-type text/html. Cause unresolved — most likely key-gating or a malformed variable list on my part, not a dead service. Another instance of the 200-with-no-data pattern: validate payloads, never status codes alone.
- Adjacent News API (adj.news) — UNVERIFIED. The main site adj.news responds (HTTP 200) but api.adj.news, data.adj.news and docs.adj.news all failed to connect from this environment across repeated attempts. It aggregates prediction markets across venues, which would be genuinely useful for cross-market comparison, but I could not confirm any working endpoint or any rate limit. Do not count on it without independent verification.
- Strength In Numbers / G. Elliott Morris — no data API and no confirmed bulk data. www.gelliottmorris.com loads (HTTP 200), but strengthinnumbers.wtf and strengthinnumbers.news failed to resolve, and I found no downloadable polling-error dataset comparable to Silver Bulletin's. Morris ran 538's model post-Silver and publishes analysis, but as a Substack newsletter, not a feed. Read it; do not pipeline it.
- A general warning for this domain: it has decayed faster than almost any other between 2023 and 2026. In a roughly 14-month window the field lost ProPublica's Congress API (Feb 2025), FiveThirtyEight entirely (Mar 2025), Google Civic's Representatives endpoints (Apr 2025) and the OpenSecrets API (Apr 2025), then the 538 article archive (May 2026). Assume every source named in any pre-2025 tutorial, awesome-list or model answer is dead until you have fetched it yourself. Mirror every bulk dataset you depend on — especially the polling-error files — because the organizations that fund political data are not the ones that profit from it.

### Geopolitics, War and Conflict

- GDELT GEO 2.0 API — DEAD. The documentation blog post is still live (HTTP 200) and contains example URLs, but every call to https://api.gdeltproject.org/api/v2/geo/geo returns HTTP 404, including the exact example URLs from the docs and every documented mode (PointData, ImageHtml, ImageInfo, country) and format (GeoJSON, html). The sibling DOC, TV and Context APIs on the same host all return 200, so this is endpoint-specific removal, not a host outage. Do not build a conflict map on it — use the raw GDELT event files, which carry the same geocoding.
- ACLED Open (free public) tier — NO API ACCESS AT ALL. The single most common mistake in this domain. ACLED's public tier gives you Explorer, the Conflict Index and dashboards, but API access begins at the Research tier, which requires an institutional academic email. Generic/personal email addresses are assigned Open by default. Even Research tier receives LAGGED event data, not current. Verified: unauthenticated GET to https://acleddata.com/api/acled/read returns HTTP 403. If you need free ACLED-derived numbers, go through OCHA HAPI's conflict-events endpoint instead — same underlying data, self-service access.
- Global Terrorism Database (GTD) — EFFECTIVELY DEAD. Frozen at 2020 data, behind a registration/EULA wall requiring personal information, distributed as a ~105MB Excel file with no API and no bulk endpoint. Five-plus years stale as of 2026. Anything needing current terrorism incidents must come from ACLED's explosions/remote-violence and violence-against-civilians categories, or from GDELT CAMEO codes 18xx-20xx.
- Liveuamap — SCRAPE-ONLY and actively blocking. Returns HTTP 403 to automated clients. No public API exists, no documented feed, and the terms of service prohibit scraping. Third-party scraper repos exist (MxpleSticks/liveuamap-scraper-api, Yohannes003/liveuamap-scraper) but they are unmaintained hobby projects sitting on a hostile origin. Named as a source by several dashboards, which creates a false impression of availability.
- ReliefWeb API without a pre-approved appname — BROKEN SINCE 1 NOVEMBER 2025. The historical pattern of passing any arbitrary appname string no longer works. Verified: appname=test and appname=rwint-user-0 both return HTTP 403 with 'You are not using an approved appname.' The v1 endpoint returns HTTP 410 Gone. Every tutorial and wrapper written before late 2025 is wrong. You must request an appname through apidoc.reliefweb.int/parameters#appname.
- UCDP API without a token — CLOSED. The UCDP API was historically fully open; it is not anymore. Verified: https://ucdpapi.pcr.uu.se/api/gedevents/24.1 returns HTTP 401 with 'API token required. Add header: x-ucdp-access-token'. The token is free but is human-gated: email the maintainer describing your project, 3-5 working days. Budget for that lead time; do not assume you can start pulling UCDP the day you start building.
- CTBTO International Monitoring System data — NOT PUBLIC. ctbto.org returns HTTP 403 to automated clients and the vDEC (virtual Data Exploitation Centre) research portal also returns 403; access requires a formal research application and an agreement with the Provisional Technical Secretariat. There is no open nuclear-test detection feed. Substitute the USGS FDSN event service, filtering on event type 'explosion' / 'nuclear explosion' near known test sites.
- IAEA nuclear monitoring — NO OPEN API. iaea.org/newscenter RSS returns HTTP 403. PRIS (Power Reactor Information System) serves HTML only with no API. Safeguards findings, enrichment-level reports and Board of Governors resolutions are published as PDFs with no machine-readable feed. Iran and DPRK nuclear contracts have no structured resolution source — you need PDF ingestion plus an LLM extraction layer.
- SIPRI Military Expenditure Database (milex.sipri.org) — BLOCKS AUTOMATION. Returns HTTP 403 to non-browser clients. Use the World Bank Indicators API MS.MIL.* series instead, which mirrors SIPRI's numbers under an open API. The SIPRI Arms Transfers site (armstransfers.sipri.org) is a separate host and does respond, but its export endpoint returns almost nothing (405 bytes) without a correct parameter set and there is no official API.
- Crisis Group CrisisWatch — HTTP 403 to automated clients. Monthly conflict-trend assessments with escalation/de-escalation arrows, which would be genuinely useful for market pricing, but there is no API, no feed, and the site blocks scrapers. Manual-only.
- EMM NewsBrief (European Commission Joint Research Centre) — HTTP 403 on the RSS endpoints, including with a browser User-Agent. Widely listed in OSINT resource lists as a free conflict news feed; it does not respond to automated clients in 2026.
- OpenSky Network historical flight endpoints — /flights/all now returns HTTP 403 anonymously. Only /states/all (live snapshot) works without auth, metered at 400 credits/day. Historical aircraft-track backtesting requires OAuth2 client credentials after the 2025 auth migration, which broke every pre-2025 client library.
- FAA NOTAM API — requires a developer key. https://external-api.faa.gov/notamapi/v1/notams returns HTTP 401. The legacy DINS public interfaces (notams.faa.gov/dinsQueryWeb/, notamRetrieval.html) failed to connect entirely (curl exit 0 responses / connection failures). There is no free open global NOTAM feed. Airspace-closure contracts — a real category for conflict zones — have no clean free resolution source; nearest free proxies are adsb.lol traffic-absence in a polygon and State Dept advisories.
- scarnecchia/oryx_data — STALE. The README claims 'Updated daily at 22:30 EDT/EST' but the repo's last push was 2025-08-21, over a year before this check. Anyone taking the README at face value will silently ingest year-old equipment-loss totals. Oryx itself publishes only HTML with no API. Fork and rerun the scraper, or treat the CSVs as a frozen corpus.
- gpsjam.org daily data JSON — the site loads (HTTP 200) but the expected data path pattern (/data/YYYY-MM-DD-h3_4.json) returned HTTP 404 and no data URLs were discoverable in the page source. GPS-interference grids are cited by aggregator dashboards as a free feed; the underlying file endpoint could not be confirmed. Treat as UNKNOWN/unavailable rather than working.
- Israel Home Front Command official OREF endpoint (www.oref.org.il/WarningMessages/alert/alerts.json) — HTTP 403 even with Referer and X-Requested-With headers set. The official alert feed is browser-gated. Use the community mirror api.tzevaadom.co.il/notifications (verified 200), accepting that it is unofficial with no SLA.
- UN Digital Library API (digitallibrary.un.org/api/v1/search) — HTTP 403. The MARC-XML search path returns HTTP 202 (queued, not data). There is no reliable machine-readable feed of Security Council resolutions and vote records. UN press RSS (press.un.org/en/rss.xml, HTTP 200) is the practical substitute but is unstructured prose.
- UN Peacekeeping data portal (peacekeeping.un.org/en/data) — HTTP 403. Troop-contribution and mandate data is HTML/PDF only, no API.
- Airwars API and Bellingcat Ukraine TimeMap API — both return HTTP 404 on their expected endpoints (airwars.org/wp-json/wp/v2/posts and ukraine.bellingcat.com/api/v1/incidents). The sites themselves load (HTTP 200) but expose no working public API. Both are frequently cited as civilian-harm data sources; neither is machine-readable without scraping.
- Cline Center (University of Illinois) datasets — databank.illinois.edu returns HTTP 403 to automated clients for both the Coup d'État Project and POLECAT/Phoenix event data. The Coup d'État Project is the canonical coup dataset and would directly price coup contracts; it is not scriptable. Manual download only.
- Metaculus API (www.metaculus.com/api2/questions/) — HTTP 403 to automated clients. Forecast-aggregation data that would be an excellent expert prior against market prices is not freely scriptable in 2026.
- UK Sanctions List CSV — the commonly-cited assets.publishing.service.gov.uk path returns HTTP 404 (and a 5,201-byte error page that a naive fetcher would happily parse as data). GOV.UK rotates the media path on every publication. Get UK designations through OpenSanctions bulk data instead, which tracks the moving target.
- IRIS FDSN event service (service.iris.edu/fdsnws/event/1/query) — HTTP 404. IRIS merged into EarthScope and the endpoint moved. Use USGS earthquake.usgs.gov/fdsnws/event/1/ (verified 200) for seismic event queries.
- NATO RSS (nato.int/cps/en/natolive/rss_news.xml) — HTTP 404. The natolive RSS path is retired. The news page at nato.int/cps/en/natohq/news.htm returns 200 but must be scraped; there is no working NATO RSS feed.
- MarineTraffic, VesselFinder, Spire, Janes, IHS Markit / S&P Global defense data, Dataminr, Recorded Future — all commercial, all expensive, none have a usable free tier. They appear constantly in OSINT resource lists in a way that implies availability. For AIS, aisstream.io (free key, 3-connection cap) and IMF PortWatch (fully open) cover most of what a prediction-market panel needs at zero cost.
- NewsAPI.org, Currents API and similar 'free' news aggregators — currentsapi.services returns HTTP 401 without a key, and the free tiers of this whole category are development-only: delayed results, no commercial use, and typically 100 requests/day. GDELT gives strictly more coverage with no key and no commercial restriction. Do not build the news layer on these.
- A general warning on aggregator dashboards: koala73/worldmonitor (87.1k stars) lists ACLED as a source, but its own issue tracker contains 'ACLED rejects API Key' (issue #290) — a working dashboard listing a feed is not evidence that the feed is accessible to you at your access tier. Verify every feed against your own credentials before depending on it.

### Sports (all major leagues) — free data feeds for prediction-market pricing, verified September 2026

- Ergast F1 API (ergast.com/api/f1) — CONFIRMED DEAD. https://ergast.com/api/f1/2024/last/results.json returned HTTP 404 in my probe. It was deprecated at the end of 2024 and the database is no longer served. Every F1 tutorial written before 2025 points here. Migrate to https://api.jolpi.ca/ergast/ which is schema-compatible.
- site.api.espn.com — HTTP 403 'Access Denied' from datacenter IPs via Akamai. This is THE most commonly cited free sports endpoint on the internet and it does not work from a server. I got an Akamai edgesuite error page for both /football/nfl/scoreboard and /basketball/nba/scoreboard even with full browser headers and a Referer. WORKAROUNDS THAT DO WORK: sports.core.api.espn.com (200) and cdn.espn.com/core/{sport}/...?xhr=1 (200). Do not build on site.api from cloud infrastructure.
- stats.nba.com — blocked outright from datacenter IPs. My request did not even get a response (curl exit 000, connection hung) with the full required header set including x-nba-stats-origin and x-nba-stats-token. cdn.nba.com/static/json/liveData/... returned HTTP 403. Requires a residential proxy. Every 'free NBA API' tutorial omits this.
- FBref / Sports Reference (fbref.com) — HTTP 403 to datacenter IPs. Named in the task brief as a source to check; it is bot-protected and will not serve a server. Also note FBref's StatsBomb-powered advanced stats have had licensing changes. Scrape-fragile and IP-gated.
- Sofascore (api.sofascore.com) — HTTP 403. Popular in scraping circles for lineups and live data; actively blocks datacenter traffic and has no free API tier.
- JeffSackmann/tennis_atp, tennis_wta and tennis_slam_pointbypoint — ALL return HTTP 404 on the GitHub API as of September 2026. The canonical free tennis datasets, cited in hundreds of papers, are gone from their original location. The JeffSackmann account now shows only 1 public repo (tennis_MatchChartingProject, still live). Use Aneeshers/tennis-sackmann-archive (June 2026 snapshot, CC BY-NC-SA, non-commercial only).
- chadwickbureau/baseballdatabank — HTTP 404. The Lahman/Baseball Databank mirror most baseball tooling depends on is gone from that path. Use droher/boxball, which packages the same tables, or cdalzell/Lahman for the R distribution.
- TheSportsDB V2 API — https://www.thesportsdb.com/api/v2/json/all/leagues returned HTTP 400 without a premium key. V2 is Patreon-only ($9/mo) and the docs state V2 'will be the only version developed going forward'. The free V1 still works with key 123 but caps searches at 1 result, which is not a usable pricing feed. Free V1 is a slow deprecation, not a stable free tier.
- PGA Tour statdata (statdata.pgatour.com) — connection failed entirely (curl exit 000). The old free PGA leaderboard JSON feeds are gone; PGA moved to a paid GraphQL API. There is no free official golf feed. Closest free option is ESPN core /sports/golf/leagues/pga/events, which returned 200.
- DataGolf (feeds.datagolf.com) — HTTP 403. Widely recommended for golf predictive models; the API is subscription-only, roughly $30/mo. Not free despite frequent listing as such.
- Sportradar trial API (api.sportradar.com) — HTTP 403 without a key. The trial is time-limited (typically 30 days, 1 QPS) and explicitly prohibits production and commercial use. It is a sales funnel, not a free tier. Same pattern for SportsDataIO.
- Sportmonks free plan — returns HTTP 401 without a token, and the free plan covers ONLY the Danish Superliga and Scottish Premiership at 3,000 calls/day. Named in the task brief; it is effectively a dead end for prediction markets because no major league is included.
- OddsJam — named in the brief. No free tier of any kind; enterprise pricing only, typically four figures per month. Do not plan around it.
- www.nascar.com/cacher/... — HTTP 403, while cf.nascar.com/cacher/... returns 200. Same data, different host. An easy trap since most references cite the www host.
- lolesports API (esports-api.lolesports.com) — HTTP 403. The Riot esports endpoint previously worked with a well-known public API key; it now blocks unauthenticated and datacenter traffic. Riot's official developer API does not cover esports match data.
- ESPN injuries via the core API — sports.core.api.espn.com/v2/sports/{sport}/leagues/{league}/injuries returns HTTP 404 for both NFL and NBA; the path does not exist on that host. The cdn.espn.com injuries page returns a 302 redirect rather than JSON. ESPN injury data is NOT cleanly available from a server. Use Sleeper (NFL) and nflverse injuries instead — this matters because the task correctly flags injuries as market-moving.
- Anonymous GitHub API (api.github.com) — 60 requests/hour unauthenticated. I hit this mid-verification and got HTTP 403 on repos that plainly exist. If you enumerate bulk datasets programmatically, authenticate for 5,000/hr. The raw.githubusercontent.com and release-asset paths are not subject to this limit.
- api-sports.io website — HTTP 403 to datacenter IPs (both the docs pages and v3.football.api-sports.io/status). The API itself works with a valid key; the marketing and docs site blocks servers. Do not conclude the service is dead from a failed docs fetch.
- Big Balls Sports Data — appeared prominently in search results advertising a free injuries API at 1,000-2,000 requests/day. I did NOT verify this endpoint live and cannot confirm the limits or that the service is real and stable. Treat as UNVERIFIED, not as a recommendation.
- General warning on 'free' odds: almost every odds provider that advertises a free tier means a trial or a credits system that runs out in days. The only genuinely free, unauthenticated, unmetered odds I could verify is the ESPN core API odds endpoint (DraftKings lines, confirmed returning 'KC -6' / O/U 46.5). It is undocumented and could disappear without notice — mirror it to your own store daily rather than querying it at decision time.

### Health, Disease & Medicine (surveillance, regulatory, clinical trials, pharma supply)

- OWID covid-19-data GitHub repo (raw.githubusercontent.com/owid/covid-19-data/.../owid-covid-data.csv) — LOOKS alive: the 98MB CSV downloads with HTTP 200 today. It is FROZEN. Last data row is 2024-08-04 and the README carries an explicit red warning: 'Our GitHub datasets are no longer updated since 19 August 2024'. Use catalog.ourworldindata.org/garden/covid/latest/compact/compact.csv instead — verified current to 2026-08-30. This is the highest-risk trap in the domain because the dead URL is the one every tutorial and LLM cites.
- OWID monkeypox GitHub repo (owid/monkeypox) — same pattern, HTTP 200, frozen at 2024-12-29. Even the OWID catalog copy (garden/who/latest/monkeypox/monkeypox.csv) stops at 2024-12-29. For live mpox use WHO xMart MPX/V_MPX_VALIDATED_DAILY, verified current to 2026-08-19.
- JHU CSSE COVID-19 (CSSEGISandData/COVID-19) — repo still resolves and the README downloads fine, but it states plainly that on 2023-03-10 the Johns Hopkins Coronavirus Resource Center ceased collecting and reporting. There is no successor repo. Anything downstream of it inherits frozen data.
- disease.sh — responds HTTP 200 with fresh-looking JSON and an 'updated' epoch stamped to the minute, but todayCases and todayDeaths are 0 because its principal upstream is the dead JHU feed. The API is live; the data is not. Safe for historical convenience, unsafe for settlement. Classic looks-free-and-alive-but-isn't.
- ASHP Drug Shortages API — NOT FREE. The official docs (ASHP-Software/drugShortagesDoc) state 'To request an API key and licensing information, contact softwaresupport@ashp.org'. Routes require ?auth={apiKey}. Separately, www.ashp.org returns an HTTP 403 Cloudflare challenge to datacenter IPs, so scraping the public shortage list is also blocked. Use openFDA drug/shortages instead — free, verified live, 1,603 records.
- HealthMap API (healthmap.org/HMapi.php) — endpoint is still up but returns the plain-text string 'Sorry, you are not authorized to use this service.' An auth key is required and I found no open registration path in 2026. Treat as effectively closed. Its outbreak-news niche is partly covered by WHO DON API plus Outbreak News Today RSS (verified live).
- ProMED-mail — no public API. promedmail.org is a Next.js SPA; /promed-posts/ returns a 404 error page to non-browser clients. ISID gates bulk and programmatic access behind subscription. Do not plan on ProMED as a free machine-readable outbreak feed despite how often it is recommended.
- GISAID — free-to-register but NOT an open API and NOT redistributable. Access requires accepting the EpiCoV/EpiFlu Database Access Agreement, which prohibits redistribution of sequence data and requires acknowledgement of originating labs. There is no REST API for bulk pulls. For a data-aggregation panel this is a licensing dead end; use Nextstrain's public builds and data.nextstrain.org (verified live) instead.
- CDC WONDER API (wonder.cdc.gov/controller/datarequest/D76) — every request from this environment returned HTTP 403 Access Denied from Akamai, including the API documentation page itself, under both a generic and a full Chrome User-Agent. This is a datacenter-IP block, not a service outage, so it may work from residential egress. Also note two documented structural limits even when reachable: the API refuses sub-national queries for several mortality databases that the web UI allows, and counts under 10 are suppressed. Prefer data.cdc.gov VSRR provisional mortality datasets (verified live) for anything time-sensitive.
- Global.health REST API (data.global.health/api/cases, /api/v1/cases, /api/geocode, /api/docs) — all return HTTP 200, which is misleading: it is the single-page-app catch-all serving a 486-byte HTML shell, not JSON. There is no public REST API. The real access path is the globaldothealth/outbreak-data GitHub repo (verified live, last commit 2026-09-18).
- reichlab/covid19-forecast-hub — stale since 2024-11-21. Still the top search result for 'covid forecast hub'. The live successor is CDCgov/covid19-forecast-hub (last commit 2026-09-18).
- Biobot Analytics wastewater data (biobotanalytics/covid19-wastewater-data) — repo returns 404. Gone. For US wastewater use CDC NWSS on data.cdc.gov (verified live, four pathogen datasets updated 2026-09-18).
- WastewaterSCAN — dashboard at data.wastewaterscan.org renders (Nuxt SPA) but every API path I probed (/api/data, /tracker/api, /api/v1/data, /download) returns 404. No documented public API found. Scrape-only at best.
- EMA REST API — does not exist. There is no EMA API of any kind. ema.europa.eu/en/rss.xml returns 404, so there is not even a working RSS feed. The only machine-readable channel is the daily XLSX exports at /en/medicines/download-medicine-data (verified live, 622KB). CHMP monthly opinions are published as web-page highlights only — structured CHMP outcome data requires diffing the spreadsheet or scraping. Every 'EMA API' in search results is a third-party Apify scraper, not an official source.
- CTIS public API via GET query string (euclinicaltrials.eu/ctis-public-api/search?paging=...) — returns HTTP 403 {'message':'Missing Authentication Token'}, which reads like an auth wall but is not. The endpoint is open; you must use POST with a JSON body. Verified working as POST. Easy to wrongly classify as paid/closed.
- OpenPrescribing API (openprescribing.net/api/1.0/...) — HTTP 403 Cloudflare 'Just a moment...' challenge from datacenter IPs. The API is genuinely free and open for normal clients; budget for residential egress or a browser-like client if you want UK prescribing volumes.
- Europe PMC documentation page (europepmc.org/RestfulWebService) — HTTP 403 Cloudflare challenge from datacenter IPs, even though the API at ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest works fine unauthenticated. Do not conclude the service is dead from the docs page being blocked.
- ReliefWeb API v1 — decommissioned, returns HTTP 410 with 'The API version v1 has been decommissioned. Please use version v2 instead.' And v2 returns HTTP 403 unless you use an APPROVED appname registered at apidoc.reliefweb.int — an arbitrary appname string is rejected. Free but requires registration; the commonly copied v1 URLs are dead.
- WHO ICD-11 API (id.who.int/icd/...) — returns HTTP 401 'The request must include a valid and non-expired bearer token.' Free, but requires OAuth2 client-credentials registration at icd.who.int. Not a drop-in anonymous endpoint. For plain ICD-10-CM code lookup, NLM Clinical Tables (verified live, no auth) is simpler.
- IHME GBD Results — no documented free REST API. ghdx.healthdata.org/gbd-results-tool is an interactive VizHub app; the results tool requires a session and registration for large extracts. GBD estimates are downloadable but not programmatically queryable for free. Do not plan a pipeline on it.
- WHO GLASS (antimicrobial resistance) — no API. Access is the Shiny dashboard at worldhealthorg.shinyapps.io/glass-dashboard with manual CSV download; I could not find a stable data endpoint behind it. AMR is therefore the weakest-covered subdomain in this catalog: for programmatic AMR you are limited to CDC's BEAM dashboard data (data.cdc.gov jbhn-e8xn, verified live) and ECDC EARS-Net via the Surveillance Atlas, which is itself an ASP.NET app with no API.
- ECDC Surveillance Atlas (atlas.ecdc.europa.eu) — renders as a legacy ASP.NET page; /public/api/Datasets returns 404. No API. Use the ERVISS GitHub repo (verified live) for respiratory viruses and opendata.ecdc.europa.eu bulk files for the rest.
- HHS Protect hospital capacity (healthdata.gov g62h-syeh) — still queryable and returns HTTP 200, but the series is frozen from the mandatory-reporting era (sample record dated 2021-06-12). Superseded by CDC NHSN Weekly Hospital Respiratory Data (data.cdc.gov ua7e-t2fy), verified current to week ending 2026-09-12.
- FDA Advisory Committee RSS — does not exist. /rss-feeds/advisory-committee/rss.xml returns 404. The advisory committee calendar is HTML-only at fda.gov/advisory-committees/advisory-committee-calendar. For structured AdComm dates use pdufa.bio /api/v1/adcomm (verified live) or scrape.
- Socrata rate limits (data.cdc.gov, healthdata.gov) — the exact numbers are genuinely UNKNOWN, not merely unfound. Socrata's own app-tokens documentation deliberately declines to state figures, saying only that unkeyed requests draw from a throttled shared IP pool and that tokened requests are 'not throttled unless abusive'. Anyone quoting a specific requests-per-hour number for Socrata is inventing it. Get a free app token and monitor for 429s.
- ClinicalTrials.gov v2 rate limit — also genuinely UNKNOWN. No numeric limit appears in the official API docs. The widely repeated '50 requests per minute per IP' comes from community client libraries and blog posts, not from NLM. Treat it as a prudent self-imposed ceiling, not a documented quota.
- PDUFA calendars generally — MarketBeat, BiopharmCatalyst, BPIQ, RTTNews, FDATracker, BiopharmaWatch and Assyro all publish PDUFA calendars, and all are HTML-only, paywalled, or both. The FDA itself publishes NO PDUFA calendar in any form — target action dates are disclosed by sponsors, not by FDA. pdufa.bio is the only free machine-readable PDUFA API I could verify (anonymous 1,000/day, confirmed via x-ratelimit-limit header), and it is an independent aggregator with only 86 PDUFA rows, so settle on openFDA drugsfda and use it for the forward calendar only.
- VAERS bulk downloads — vaers.hhs.gov/data/datasets.html renders, but the direct ZIP path I tried (/eSubDownload/index?fn=2026VAERSData.zip) returned a Tomcat 404. The download is gated behind a form/CAPTCHA-style flow rather than a stable URL, and there is no REST API. VAERS via CDC WONDER is also blocked per the WONDER entry above. Plan on manual retrieval for adverse-event-report contracts.
- CIDRAP news RSS (cidrap.umn.edu/news/rss.xml) — 404. The site moved to a Drupal layout without that feed path. Outbreak News Today (outbreaknewstoday.com/feed/) is verified live if you want an outbreak news RSS.
- GPEI polio data (polioeradication.org/polio-today/polio-now/this-week/) — 404. Polio case counts are published as web tables and PDFs with shifting URLs. WHO's xMart POLIO mart responds HTTP 200 but returns an EMPTY entity-set list, so it is provisioned but carries no public tables. Polio is effectively scrape-only.

### Science, Space, Technology and Discovery

- SpaceX API (api.spacexdata.com) — DEAD. The r-spacex/SpaceX-API repo was ARCHIVED by its owner on 2026-06-06 and the origin now returns a TLS handshake error (HTTP 525) on every version path. We retried it twice and both failed. It had already been in maintenance-only mode since 2024 with new launches not being added. Anything that still lists it as a free SpaceX feed — and many catalogs do — is stale. Use Launch Library 2 instead; it covers SpaceX plus every other provider.
- Papers With Code API (paperswithcode.com/api/v1/) — DEAD. Meta sunset the service on 2025-07-24. The endpoint now 302-redirects to huggingface.co/papers/trending, which is a trending-papers feed with NO leaderboard or SOTA-tracking API. The task brief lists this as a source to check; it does not exist any more. The historical leaderboard data survives only as static JSON in the paperswithcode/paperswithcode-data repo.
- PatentsView PatentSearch API (search.patentsview.org/api/v1/) — DEAD. The hostname does not even resolve in DNS (getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND, confirmed from two independent clients). The API was shut down on 2026-03-20 as PatentsView migrated into the USPTO Open Data Portal. Widely-cited figures like '45 calls per minute' refer to a service that no longer exists.
- PatentsView legacy API (api.patentsview.org) — DEAD since 2025-05-01, returns HTTP 410 Gone. The DNS record still resolves, which makes it look alive to a naive health check. It is not.
- USPTO legacy Developer Hub (developer.uspto.gov) — DECOMMISSIONED 2026-06-05. The host still returns HTTP 200 but serves an Angular shell, not API data. Everything moved to data.uspto.gov / api.uspto.gov, and since 2026-06-18 a USPTO.gov account sign-in is required.
- USPTO ODP without a key (api.uspto.gov) — NOT free-without-registration. Returns HTTP 401 Unauthorized on every request. The key itself is free but requires an approved USPTO.gov account, so it cannot be used for anonymous ingestion.
- NASA ADS (api.adsabs.harvard.edu) — requires a bearer token; returns HTTP 401 'Missing Authorization in headers' anonymously. Free to register, but it is not a no-auth feed and rate limits are per-token and modest (historically 5,000 requests/day per endpoint class). Do not plan on anonymous access.
- EPO Open Patent Services (ops.epo.org) — returns HTTP 403 'rejected due to the violation of Fair Use policy' without registration. The free tier exists but is quota-boxed (historically 4GB/month) and OAuth-gated. Not a drop-in free patent feed for Europe.
- Zenodo API (zenodo.org/api/records) — returned HTTP 403 Forbidden on an anonymous request in 2026, despite being widely documented as open. A personal access token now appears to be required for API reads. Treat published 'no auth needed' claims as stale.
- Unpaywall API — returns HTTP 422 for placeholder emails ('Please use your own email address in API calls'). It is free but the email parameter is validated, so you cannot use it anonymously or with a throwaway string.
- GCN REST/JSON endpoints — there is no working public REST JSON API. gcn.nasa.gov/api/circulars returns HTTP 400 and gcn.nasa.gov/circulars.json returns 404. Only the Kafka stream (with free client credentials) and the HTML archive work. Several aggregator lists imply a JSON API exists; it does not.
- LMArena / LMSYS Chatbot Arena — NO public documented API. The leaderboard page loads (HTTP 200) but lmarena.ai/api/leaderboard returns a 301 with no documented successor. The task brief lists LMSYS/LMArena as a source; it is scrape-only or Gradio-state-scraping in practice, both of which are fragile. Use Epoch AI's Benchmarking Hub for programmatic benchmark scores instead.
- TNS (Transient Name Server, wis-tns.org) — the /api/get path returns HTTP 404 anonymously. TNS requires a registered bot account with a User-Agent carrying credentials in a specific JSON header format. It is free but absolutely not anonymous, and the auth scheme is unusual enough to break generic HTTP clients.
- tle.ivanstanojevic.me (commonly listed as 'the TLE API') — returns HTTP 406 Not Acceptable. This third-party mirror appears in many public-API catalogs as a NASA feed; it is neither NASA-operated nor reliably available. Use CelesTrak or Space-Track.
- OpenAlex 'unlimited 100,000 calls/day' — OBSOLETE as of February 2026. OpenAlex replaced rate limits with a USD credit budget and ABOLISHED the polite pool. Anonymous requests now carry a measured daily budget of $0.10 / 1,000 credits, and search costs 10x a list call. Every catalog and wrapper still advertising the old 100k/day polite-pool model is wrong, and code written against it will silently start getting throttled.
- catalog.ourworldindata.org — returns HTTP 404 at the root, and api.ourworldindata.org/v1/indicators/{id}.metadata.json 404s for ids you have not already resolved. OWID data IS free, but only via the /grapher/{slug}.csv path or a known numeric indicator id. There is no browsable catalog root to crawl.
- arXiv over plain HTTP (export.arxiv.org) — returns a 301 that does not carry the query through cleanly in some clients. Always use HTTPS. Also note arxiv.org/help/bulk_data_s3 now 404s; the bulk S3 access docs moved.
- api.biorxiv.org without the trailing /json — the connection fails outright (no HTTP status at all) rather than returning an error. Easy to misdiagnose as the service being down when it is a path-format requirement.
- DataCite API (api.datacite.org) — returned no HTTP status on our check (connection did not complete). INCONCLUSIVE rather than confirmed dead, but do not assume it is available without testing it yourself.
- Anonymous GitHub API for bulk repo research — 60 requests/hour per IP, which we exhausted mid-research. It looks free and unlimited until it abruptly is not. Always use a free personal access token (5,000/hour) for any systematic repo or release monitoring.
- Generic caution: NASA's DEMO_KEY reported X-RateLimit-Limit of 10 from our IP, not the documented 30/hour — because it is a shared per-IP pool that others on your network or cloud provider are also draining. Never build even a prototype on DEMO_KEY; the free registered key takes thirty seconds to get and gives 1,000/hour.

### Transport, Logistics & Supply Chain

- MarineTraffic free/credit API — DEAD. After Kpler's acquisition, MarineTraffic discontinued credit-based self-serve pricing; all commercial API access is now negotiated through enterprise sales with no published rates. The old PS01/VI01/EV01 credit packs no longer exist as a purchasable free or cheap tier. Do not build on it.
- ADS-B Exchange API — EFFECTIVELY DEAD as a free source. Access is via RapidAPI subscription; the 'Basic $0.00/mo' plan that appears on RapidAPI is a trial-shaped entry point, not a usable production quota, and the Community/API-Lite tier is explicitly non-commercial and gated. ADSBx historically flipped from free to paid after its 2023 acquisition. Use adsb.fi or adsb.lol instead — both are wire-compatible with the ADSBx v2 schema.
- airplanes.live API — NOT OPEN. Probed 2026-09-21: returns HTTP 403 with 'Please contact us at contact@airplanes.live. Your email MUST include any links, a description of the project...'. It looks like a free ADS-B aggregator but anonymous programmatic access is blocked pending manual approval.
- AISHub without physical hardware — IMPOSSIBLE AT ANY PRICE. There is no pay-for-access tier. You must operate an AIS receiver streaming raw NMEA over UDP, and credentials are only granted after your feed shows ~10+ vessel coverage and ~90% uptime over a rolling 7 days. 'Applications without an operational AIS station and feed will not be approved.' This is a hardware and hosting project, not an API signup.
- AviationStack free tier — USELESS IN PRACTICE. 100 requests per MONTH (about three per day), non-commercial only, and historical data, schedules, routes, autocomplete and future flights are all excluded. Verified on the product page 2026-09-21. It appears in every 'free flight API' listicle; it cannot support a panel.
- Freightos Baltic Index (FBX) API — NOT FREE. Verified 2026-09-21: both terminal.freightos.com/wp-json/fbx/v1/index and fbx.freightos.com/api/indexes/FBX return marketing HTML, not JSON. Freightos' own support article states API access is enterprise-package only and CSV download requires a paid personal package. Third-party directory listings claiming a 'free tier, no key' FBX API (e.g. apis.io) are marketing copy that does not resolve to a working endpoint.
- Drewry World Container Index API — DOES NOT EXIST. Drewry publishes WCI, the Cancelled Sailings Tracker and the Intra-Asia index free on the web behind email registration, but there is no official API and no free CSV export. Any 'Drewry WCI API' you find is a third-party reseller (e.g. OilPriceAPI) republishing scraped values — treat their numbers as unverified for contract resolution.
- Xeneta XSI public index — NOT ACCESSIBLE. Probed 2026-09-21: xeneta.com/xeneta-shipping-index returned HTTP 404 against a live site. XSI is a subscription product; there is no free API.
- Waze for Cities (formerly Connected Citizens Program) — GOVERNMENT-ONLY. Free, but membership requires being a government agency or a private road operator. A prediction-market company does not qualify. The GeoRSS traffic feed is not obtainable through any commercial signup. Use TomTom's free tier or state 511 APIs instead.
- FAA ASDI / ASPM / OPSNET dashboards — GATED. ASPM and OPSNET require an approved FAA account and are not open APIs; ASDI as a distinct free product has been superseded by SWIM/SCDS. SCDS itself is free but needs a signed Service Access Agreement and per-product approval, which takes days to weeks — it is not a same-day integration.
- FAA NAS Status has no OFFICIAL public API. The nasstatus.faa.gov/api/airport-status-information endpoint works today (verified HTTP 200, XML, 2026-09-21) but is undocumented and unsupported — the FAA does not publish it as a public API. Build a fallback and monitor for schema changes. The third-party 'FAA NAS Status API' offerings on Anakin, Parse.bot and Apify are paid wrappers around this same free endpoint — do not pay for them.
- EUROCONTROL DDR (Demand Data Repository) — GATED. Trajectory-level data requires a registered account and a data agreement, and is restricted to operational stakeholders and researchers. Only the published open datasets on ansperformance.eu and the weekly European Aviation Overview are freely downloadable.
- OpenSky Trino historical database — FREE BUT ELIGIBILITY-RESTRICTED. Access is limited to university-affiliated researchers, governmental organisations and aviation authorities for aviation-related research, and is NOT auto-approved on registration. A commercial prediction-market terminal will likely be refused. Plan to build your own archive by polling adsb.fi/adsb.lol instead.
- OpenSky REST basic authentication — RETIRED 18 March 2026. Username/password auth no longer works; OAuth2 client credentials only, with 30-minute token expiry. Any tutorial, library or cached code sample using basic auth is broken. This is the single most common stale integration in this domain right now.
- Global Fishing Watch API — NON-COMMERCIAL LICENSE. The quotas are generous (50,000/day, 1.5M/month) but the licence covers academic research, NGOs and free public-good use. Commercial use requires a separate agreement. Do not embed it in a paid product without one.
- adsb.fi — NON-COMMERCIAL AND ATTRIBUTION-REQUIRED. Explicitly personal/non-commercial use only, with a mandatory citation and link. Great for prototyping, a licensing problem for a paid terminal. adsb.lol's ODbL licence is the more commercially workable of the two.
- Panama Canal Authority and Suez Canal Authority — NO APIs. Both publish free data but only as HTML pages, PDF advisories and XLS tables. Every 'canal transit API' is either a scraper or IMF PortWatch repackaged. Use PortWatch for programmatic chokepoint transits and scrape the authorities only for draft restrictions, slot auctions and toll changes, which PortWatch does not carry.
- Project44, Resilinc, Everstream, Sea-Intelligence, S&P Global Panjiva, ImportGenius, Kpler — ALL PAID, no free tier worth integrating. The supply-chain-disruption tracker category is almost entirely commercial. The free substitutes are NY Fed GSCPI, RWI/ISL Container Throughput, Kiel Trade Indicator and IMF PortWatch.
- NewsCatcher 'Semiconductor and Component Shortages Monitor', Apify 'Shipping Disruption Tracker', Datarade supply-chain listings — PAID MARKETPLACE PRODUCTS, not free feeds. They surface in searches for 'free supply chain disruption API' but are commercial datasets with sample previews only.
- Census and FRED are key-gated, not open. api.census.gov returns a 'Missing Key' page (verified HTTP 200 with that page, 2026-09-21) and api.stlouisfed.org returns HTTP 400 'Variable api_key is not set'. Both keys are free and instant, but unkeyed scripts will silently receive HTML/error bodies rather than data — validate content type, not just status code. Census allows 500 queries per IP per day without a key.
- AAR weekly rail traffic — LICENSING RISK. Free to view, but AAR routes redistribution questions to publications@aar.org. Republishing the series commercially may require a licence. Pull the equivalent series from FRED (RAILFRTCARLOADSD11), which carries no such restriction.
- DAT, Truckstop.com and FreightWaves SONAR truckload spot rates — ALL PAID. There is no free US truckload spot rate index. The free substitutes are the FRED truck tonnage index (monthly, lagging) and FMCSA carrier authority churn (a capacity proxy, not a price). Accept that trucking rate contracts cannot be priced from free data alone.
- USACE Corps Locks (corpslocks.usace.army.mil) — DID NOT RESPOND. Probed 2026-09-21 and returned HTTP 000 (connection failure/timeout). May be transient, a TLS or user-agent issue, or a real outage. Re-verify before depending on inland-waterway lock data.
- Kiel Trade Indicator and RWI/ISL Container Throughput download paths have MOVED. Both landing-page URLs I probed returned HTTP 404 or the site's HTML shell rather than the data file, against otherwise live sites. The datasets still exist and are still free — the file paths must be re-derived by scraping the current landing pages. Do not hardcode a URL from an older blog post.
- BTS dataset IDs cannot be guessed. Probing data.bts.gov/resource/ar6d-cxq8.json returned HTTP 404 'dataset.missing'. Always resolve IDs through the catalog API (data.bts.gov/api/catalog/v1?q=...) first — verified working 2026-09-21, and it surfaced the Amtrak On-Time Performance dataset as 98fi-ujit.

### Agriculture, Food and Land

- FAOSTAT REST API at https://fenixservices.fao.org/faostat/api/v1/ — BROKEN. Every endpoint tested (groupsanddomains, definitions, data/QCL) returned HTTP 521 (Cloudflare: origin unreachable) on repeated attempts on 2026-09-20. This is the base URL hardcoded into essentially every FAOSTAT wrapper on GitHub and in the R/Python packages. Use https://bulks-faostat.fao.org/production/ instead.
- FAOSTAT REST API at https://faostatservices.fao.org/api/v1/ — now returns HTTP 401. FAO moved to a registration-gated developer portal (fao.org/faostat/en/#developer-portal/sign-in). It is no longer an anonymous public API, contrary to every tutorial written before 2026.
- USDA FAS IPAD / Crop Explorer (ipad.fas.usda.gov) — returns HTTP 503 with Retry-After: 3600 on every request including the root domain, across multiple attempts and user agents. Could NOT VERIFY it is operational in 2026. This is the source for USDA's global NDVI, crop calendars and country crop summaries. Do not assume it works; test before designing around it. Note the PSD Online bulk downloads on apps.fas.usda.gov are a DIFFERENT host and ARE live.
- ReliefWeb API v1 (api.reliefweb.int/v1/) — DECOMMISSIONED. Returns HTTP 410 with the literal message 'The API version v1 has been decommissioned. Please use version v2 instead.' And v2 returns HTTP 403 'You are not using an approved appname' — you must now REQUEST an approved appname from ReliefWeb, it is no longer a free-text parameter. Every pre-2026 ReliefWeb integration is broken.
- HDX HAPI (hdx-hapi.humdata.org) — requires an approved app_identifier; returns 403 or no response without one. This is DIFFERENT from the open HDX CKAN API at data.humdata.org, which works with no key. Do not confuse them.
- Nasdaq Data Link / Quandl CHRIS continuous futures (data.nasdaq.com/api/v3/datasets/CHRIS/CME_C1) — HTTP 403. The free CME continuous-futures tables that every quant tutorial references are gone. There is NO free API for CBOT corn/wheat/soybean settlement prices.
- CME Group settlement pages (cmegroup.com/markets/agriculture/.../settlements.html) — HTTP 403 to any scripted client. CME blocks non-browser access and there is no free settlement API. The task brief asked for 'Chicago Board of Trade public grain settlements': these are PUBLISHED but NOT FREELY MACHINE-READABLE. Closest free substitutes are CFTC COT (positioning, weekly) and USDA AMS MARS (cash/basis, daily) — neither is a futures settlement price. Budget for a paid feed (Barchart, Databento, Polygon) if settlements are load-bearing.
- USDA ERS 'Data APIs' page — only the ARMS survey is actually a REST API. Fertilizer Use and Price, Food Price Outlook, Food Expenditure Series and the International Food Security Assessment are XLSX downloads with no API despite being listed under the developer section. The page title oversells what exists.
- EU Agri-food Data Portal API — the documented host agridata.ec.europa.eu/api/ 404s; the real host is api.tech.ec.europa.eu/agrifood/api/ and most /prices endpoints return {'State':'SUSPENDED'} intermittently. Only /cereal/products returned clean data on probe. Treat as unreliable, not dead.
- FAO GIEWS FPMA API (fpma.fao.org/giews/v4/price_module/api/) — every endpoint tested returns HTTP 307 redirects, never JSON. There is no stable documented public API for FPMA price data. Scrape-only.
- GEOGLAM Crop Monitor — api.cropmonitor.org does not resolve (DNS failure). Despite being a G20-backed program, the monthly crop-condition assessments are published only as PDF bulletins and GIS layers. Scrape-only.
- International Grains Council (api.igc.int) — does not resolve. The IGC Grains and Oilseeds Index and world S&D forecasts are behind a paid subscription; only a summary PDF (igc.int/downloads/gmrsummary/gmrsumme.pdf) is free. Scrape-only, and the summary omits most tables.
- Agmarknet (agmarknet.gov.in) and api.data.gov.in — HTTP 403. India's national mandi price API is geo-restricted and rejects non-Indian IPs even with the published sample key. Indian staple prices require a proxy or a scraper.
- Ag Data Commons CKAN at data.nal.usda.gov/api/3/ — returns HTTP 302 redirecting to nal.usda.gov/services/agdatacommons. The CKAN API has been retired; agdatacommons.nal.usda.gov now runs a Figshare-style v2 API instead. Old CKAN integrations silently follow the redirect and get HTML.
- Cornell/ESMIS release API (usda.library.cornell.edu/api/v1/release and esmis.nal.usda.gov/api/v1/release) — returns HTTP 405/404. The documented JSON endpoint for programmatically discovering USDA report releases (including WASDE) does not work as documented. The reports themselves are downloadable; the release-discovery API is not usable.
- OpenET API (openet-api.org) — the endpoint is live but the FREE-TIER QUOTA IS NOT PUBLISHED ANYWHERE. Their own FAQ says only that exceeding your monthly request quota blocks you until the 1st of the next month, without stating the number. Requires account approval. Do not plan capacity around it without confirming your specific quota.
