- IPC Public API (api.ipcinfo.org) — free but NOT self-serve. IPC validates each key request internally before issuing. Build in lead time; you cannot sign up and start pulling in the same afternoon. Rate limits undisclosed.
- Global Fishing Watch API — free and generous (50,000/day, 1.5M/month) but licensed CC BY-NC 4.0, NONCOMMERCIAL ONLY. A commercial prediction-market product cannot legally build on it. This is a license dead end, not a technical one.
- FAO WaPOR v3 API (io.apps.fao.org/gismgr/api/v2/) — returned HTTP 502. The underlying data is reachable via the public GCS bucket (storage.googleapis.com/fao-gismgr-wapor-3-data/, HTTP 200) so use the bucket, not the gismgr API.
- Commercial 'free agricultural commodity price API' listings (Commoditic, Trading Economics free tier, and similar) — these are trial tiers with severe call caps and no redistribution rights, not free feeds. They look free in awesome-list catalogs and are not.
- Copernicus land.copernicus.eu Global NDVI v1.0 (PROBA-V) and v2.0 (Sentinel-3) — PRODUCTION DISCONTINUED 2025-12-31. Only v3.0 is in NRT operations, and CLMS Global data has migrated off land.copernicus.eu to the Copernicus Data Space Ecosystem. Old WEkEO dataset IDs must be replaced with EO:JRC:DAT:CLMS identifiers plus a datasetIdentifier parameter. Any pre-2026 NDVI pipeline is broken.

### News, Media, Social & Attention — the firehose layer

- GDELT GEO 2.0 API — CONFIRMED DEAD. https://api.gdeltproject.org/api/v2/geo/geo returns HTTP 404 for every parameter combination I tried, including the exact example URLs from GDELT's own documentation blog post (?query=trump and ?query=trump&mode=country), and with format=GeoJSON and mode=PointData. The docs page is still live and still describes the full parameter set, so you will find it and believe it works. It does not. The sibling endpoints on the same host (doc, tv, context, summary) all responded fine, so this is endpoint-specific removal, not an outage. Get geocoded news from the GKG bulk files' location fields instead.
- X / Twitter API — NO FREE TIER EXISTS. As of 6 February 2026 X replaced tiered pricing with pay-per-use as the default; there is no free tier and new customers cannot sign up for Basic or Pro at all. Reads are $0.005 per post, capped at 2M reads/month. Legacy Basic ($200/mo) subscribers were migrated to pay-per-use after 1 June 2026, and legacy Pro ($5,000/mo) was deprecated on 14 August 2026 with all Pro subscribers auto-migrated after 1 September 2026. Only pay-per-use or Enterprise ($42,000+/mo) remain. Budget for it or use Bluesky Jetstream, which is free and which I verified streaming live.
- Bing Search / Bing News Search API — RETIRED 11 August 2025. The entire family (Web, News, Image, Video, Entity, Custom, Spellcheck, Visual) was decommissioned and existing instances were shut off. The endpoint still returns 401 rather than 404, which makes it look merely key-gated — it is not, it is gone. The official replacement, Grounding with Bing Search in Azure AI Agents, costs $35 per 1,000 transactions (a 40-483% increase) and returns LLM-grounded context rather than structured search results, so it is not a drop-in.
- CrowdTangle — SHUT DOWN 14 August 2024. Its replacement, Meta Content Library and Content Library API, is restricted to researchers at qualified academic or non-profit institutions; FOR-PROFIT NEWSROOMS ARE CATEGORICALLY BANNED, data export is disabled, and external analysis tools cannot be used. A commercial prediction-market terminal cannot qualify. There is no free Facebook or Instagram signal available to you.
- Pushshift — CLOSED to the public. https://api.pushshift.io/reddit/search/submission returns HTTP 403 {"detail":"Not authenticated"} and access is now restricted to Reddit moderators. Every Reddit-history tutorial online still points here. Use ArthurHeitmann/arctic_shift instead.
- pytrends — ARCHIVED 17 April 2025, unmaintained, and returns HTTP 429 on the first call. It still installs cleanly from PyPI, which is why people keep adopting it. Google's official Trends API was announced 24 July 2025 but remains an application-gated limited alpha more than a year later. Use the trending RSS endpoint (which I verified live) for breakouts, or yiromo/pytrends-modern for keyword series.
- NewsAPI.org free tier — NOT USABLE IN PRODUCTION. 100 requests/day, one month of history, and the Developer plan is contractually limited to development and testing: their own FAQ states it cannot be used in a staging or production environment. The pricing page also confirms full article content is not provided on ANY plan. It looks like the obvious default choice and it is a trap for a production terminal.
- Mediastack free tier — 100 CALLS PER MONTH (not per day), delayed news data only, no historical access, and NON-COMMERCIAL USE ONLY. Read off their product page directly. Approximately three requests a day; unusable for anything.
- GNews free tier — has a 12-HOUR DELAY on article availability, truncates content to a short excerpt, allows 100 requests/day, and enables CORS for localhost only. A 12-hour delay makes it worthless for pricing any time-sensitive contract, which is nearly all of them.
- APITube free tier — same fatal flaw: 12-HOUR DELAY on articles and a 200-character body preview instead of full content. The 1,000 requests/day headline number is generous and irrelevant given the delay.
- Event Registry / NewsAPI.ai free tier — IT IS A ONE-TIME TRIAL, NOT A RECURRING FREE TIER. You get 2,000 tokens once; when they are gone you must subscribe (5K plan at $90/month). Archive searches cost roughly 5 tokens per searched year, so a few deep queries exhaust it. The product itself is strong (full article text, 150,000+ sources, archive to 2014) but do not architect against a free tier that does not renew.
- NewsCatcher — NO FREE TIER AT ALL. Requires purchasing credits at $0.01 each before any request, with each article costing 10 credits ($0.10). The 'free trial' is 10,000 trial requests against a paid plan, not an ongoing allowance.
- Reddit Data API for commercial use — the 100 QPM free tier is NON-COMMERCIAL ONLY. A prediction-market product is commercial, requiring explicit written approval plus a paid agreement at $0.24 per 1,000 calls, reported at roughly $12,000/month minimum. Since the Responsible Builder Policy of 5 June 2026 self-service registration is closed and new OAuth tokens need manual approval on a reported 2-4 week timeline. This is a licensing blocker, not a technical one — decide before you build.
- Guardian api-key=test — NO LONGER WORKS. content.guardianapis.com returned HTTP 401 {"message":"Unauthorized"} to the legacy test key that countless tutorials still use. Register for a real developer key, and note the developer tier is non-commercial.
- mastodon.social anonymous public timeline — NOW REQUIRES AUTH. /api/v1/timelines/public returns HTTP 422 {"error":"This method requires an authenticated user"} on the flagship instance, though fosstodon.org and mstdn.social still allow it and mastodon.social's /api/v1/trends/links remains open. There is no network-wide Mastodon firehose; you must federate across instances yourself, and each may close access independently.
- Bluesky app.bsky.feed.searchPosts unauthenticated — returns HTTP 403 on public.api.bsky.app. Profile reads and feed-generator reads (getProfile, getFeed) still work without auth, but KEYWORD SEARCH now needs a session. Do not plan a search-based Bluesky pipeline without app-password auth. Also note: no ratelimit-* headers are returned, so the actual ceiling is UNKNOWN.
- GDELT Web NGrams 3.0 file discovery — the data files exist (I confirmed 20260920201600.toc.json.gz returns 200) but I found NO working lastupdate.txt or MASTERFILELIST at https://data.gdeltproject.org/gdeltv5/weblegacy/ngrams/, and several nearby minute timestamps 404'd. GDELT's own 429 message pushes high-volume users to this dataset, but the enumeration mechanism is undocumented. Budget time to reverse-engineer it, or ask GDELT directly.
- Common Crawl CDX index server — FLAKY, do not put it on a hot path. CC-MAIN-2026-39-index returned 404 (index not yet built for the newest crawl, even though collinfo.json lists it as current) and CC-MAIN-2026-30-index returned 502 during the same test window. Use the columnar Parquet index on S3 for reliable lookups.
- YouTube Data API search.list — effectively removed as a discovery tool. The June 2026 quota change put search.list in its own bucket of 100 CALLS PER DAY, separate from the 10,000-unit pool. You cannot sweep YouTube for emerging topics. Architect around videos.list and commentThreads.list (1 unit each) against known channel IDs only.
- GDELT Context API — responds HTTP 200 but returned an EMPTY result set ({"articles": [ ]}) for my test query. I could not demonstrate it returns data in 2026. Do not assume it works until you get a populated response; its query syntax and index status are UNKNOWN.
- GDELT DOC API at scale — the 1-request-per-5-second limit is REAL AND HARD, not advisory. I received HTTP 429 with an explicit throttle message repeatedly during testing, and one HTTP 503 as well. Anyone planning continuous polling across hundreds of markets will be blocked. The bulk 15-minute GKG/Events files are the correct scaling path, not more API calls.
- Any expectation that news APIs give you FULL ARTICLE TEXT for free — with narrow exceptions they do not. GDELT DOC API returns URL/title/domain/language/country and no body (I verified the exact response fields). NewsAPI.org states no plan includes full content. GNews and APITube truncate on free. NYT gives abstract and lead paragraph only. The free full-text routes are: Common Crawl CC-NEWS (bulk WARC), the Guardian Open Platform (non-commercial), Wikimedia Enterprise for encyclopedia content, or fetching and extracting the URLs yourself with trafilatura. Plan for that extraction step — it is not optional.

### Entertainment, Culture & Consumer

- Goodreads API — DEAD. Stopped issuing new developer keys on 8 Dec 2020 and has been fully retired since; there is no replacement and no restoration planned as of 2026. Every 'Goodreads API' tutorial you will find is stale. Use Open Library reading-log counts, the NYT Books API, or Hardcover for book demand signals instead.
- Spotify /v1/recommendations, /v1/artists/{id}/related-artists, /v1/audio-features, /v1/audio-analysis, algorithmic + Spotify-owned editorial playlists, and 30-second preview URLs — DEAD for any app created after 27 Nov 2024; they return 403. Only apps that already held (or had pending) a quota extension before that date still work. There is still no official replacement in 2026. Additionally, you now need a Spotify PREMIUM account merely to create an app. Spotify metadata endpoints (search, albums, tracks, artists, new-releases) DO still work — do not write off the whole API, just do not plan around the removed half.
- Steam Web API ISteamApps/GetAppList (v1 and v2) — DEAD as of 2026. Returns HTTP 404 with the body 'Method GetAppList not found in interface ISteamApps'. Verified against http and https, with and without trailing slash, with and without format=json. Replacement is IStoreService/GetAppList/v1/ which REQUIRES an API key and returns games only by default (use include_dlc / include_software / include_videos / include_hardware flags for parity). Most tutorials and half the GitHub wrappers still call the dead endpoint.
- Apple Marketing Tools RSS movies feeds — DEAD. rss.marketingtools.apple.com/api/v2/us/movies/top-movies/10/movies.json returns 404; Apple retired the iTunes movie charts. The music, books, podcasts and apps feeds all still work. Also note the old rss.applemarketingtools.com host now 301-redirects to rss.marketingtools.apple.com — update hardcoded hosts.
- Yelp Fusion API — NOT FREE since 2024. There is no free tier; only a 30-day trial. Paid plans run roughly $7.99 / $9.99 / $14.99 per 1,000 API calls (Starter / Plus / Enterprise), with 30,000 calls/month and a 5,000/day cap on the default paid plan. Every 'free restaurant API' listicle that names Yelp is out of date.
- Google Places API — NOT MEANINGFULLY FREE. Google replaced the flat $200/month credit with per-SKU free thresholds on 1 March 2025. Typical place-search now bills through Text Search Pro at ~$32 per 1,000 calls after a 5,000 calls/month free allowance. A Bloomberg-terminal-scale restaurant panel would run into four or five figures a month. Autocomplete sessions linked to Place Details remain free — that is the only genuinely free slice.
- OpenTable — NO PUBLIC API. There is no developer programme, no free tier, and no documented endpoint. Restaurant reservation-availability data is only obtainable via scraping (against their ToS) or via paid resellers. The task brief lists OpenTable; it does not exist as a feed.
- Box Office Mojo / IMDb official API — PAID AND EXPENSIVE. Distributed through AWS Data Exchange / AWS Marketplace as a GraphQL API; entry pricing is reported around $150,000 per year. The boxofficemojo.com website itself returns HTTP 200 and is scrapeable, but scraping it is against IMDb's ToS and the lifetime-gross data is the licensed product. Treat 'free box office API' as false.
- The Numbers (the-numbers.com) — BLOCKED. Returns HTTP 403 to non-browser clients (Cloudflare). Their OpusData product is a paid commercial licence for REST API access. Scraping requires a browser-grade fetcher and is against their terms. Given that box-office opening-weekend is one of the highest-value contract types, the honest finding is that there is NO clean free box-office feed — Trakt's /boxoffice endpoint and OMDb's sparse BoxOffice field are the only free approximations, and neither is settlement-grade.
- Billboard — NO OFFICIAL API, and no free licensed chart data. Billboard charts are compiled from Luminate (formerly Nielsen SoundScan) data, which is a paid commercial product. Every free Billboard feed on GitHub is a scraper of billboard.com, is against Billboard's ToS, and breaks whenever they change their markup. Apple Marketing Tools RSS and Deezer /chart are the legitimate free chart alternatives.
- SteamDB (steamdb.info) — NO API, and scraping is explicitly forbidden and Cloudflare-enforced. SteamDB's own FAQ says to use the Steam Web API instead. The good news: Valve's ISteamChartsService endpoints give you the same concurrent-player numbers SteamDB displays, with no key, so SteamDB is not needed.
- Foursquare Places API — NOT FREE at useful volume. Returns HTTP 401 without a key; the free developer tier is capped and the Places product moved to a paid, credit-based model. Listed in many 'free API' catalogues under outdated terms.
- OpenCritic API — NOT OPENLY AVAILABLE. api.opencritic.com returns HTTP 400 to direct public calls; the documented access path is through RapidAPI with a paid plan above a small free quota. There is no free, unauthenticated game-review-aggregate feed. Metacritic likewise has no API at all.
- Genius API — LIVE but returns 401 without OAuth, and it carries NO chart or popularity data — lyrics and annotations only. It is not a music-markets feed despite appearing in every 'music API' list.
- AcousticBrainz — DEAD. Shut down and stopped accepting submissions in 2022. The data dumps are archived but frozen; do not build on it.
- Songkick API — CLOSED to new applicants; existing keys only, with no public signup path. Use Ticketmaster Discovery or Bandsintown for live-event calendars instead.
- Letterboxd API — CLOSED BETA / invite-only since launch and still not generally available in 2026. Frequently listed as a film data source; it is not obtainable.
- Numbeo API — NOT FREE. The docs page (numbeo.com/api/doc.jsp) is public and lists a rich cost-of-living, restaurant-price and property-price endpoint set, but the pricing page and free-tier terms are not documented publicly and access is sold per-contract via api@numbeo.com. Treat as a paid vendor, not a free feed.
- University of Michigan Consumer Sentiment (direct from sso.umich.edu / Surveys of Consumers) — PAYWALLED for the detailed tables and the full micro data. The HEADLINE index is free via FRED series UMCSENT. Use FRED; do not pay Michigan.
- Conference Board Consumer Confidence Index — PAID. No free API, no free historical file. Unlike UMich there is no free FRED route to the current series. If a contract settles on Conference Board CCI, you cannot get the data for free — price that constraint in.
- UNWTO / UN Tourism statistics — PAID. The International Tourism Statistics database is a subscription product. Eurostat (EU only), World Bank annual indicators, and national tourism boards are the free substitutes; there is no free global monthly tourism feed.
- Nielsen, Comscore, Luminate, STR (hotel occupancy), Circana/NPD (game and toy sales), NAR (existing home sales) — ALL PAID, no free tier, no free historical archive. These are the actual settlement sources for a large share of entertainment and consumer contracts. Any claim that a free stack fully covers this domain is false; be explicit about which contracts you cannot price.
- Google Trends — NO OFFICIAL API. The pytrends library is unofficial, is aggressively rate-limited, returns normalised 0-100 index values rather than absolute volumes, and breaks whenever Google changes the internal endpoint. Wikipedia pageviews is the honest free substitute for a search-interest proxy — it gives absolute counts with eleven years of stable history and a documented API.
- ISBNdb — NOT FREE. Book metadata via the web interface is limited; API access requires a paid subscription. Open Library and Google Books cover the same ground for free.
- RAWG free tier, TMDB free tier, IMDb non-commercial datasets, Last.fm free tier, and Watchmode free tier are all LICENSING dead ends for a COMMERCIAL terminal even though they are technically free: RAWG free is non-commercial with no redistribution; TMDB requires a separate written commercial agreement; IMDb datasets are personal/non-commercial only; Last.fm free use is non-commercial and commercial use needs a partners@last.fm agreement; Watchmode's free plan is non-commercial. These are the feeds most likely to look free in a prototype and become a legal problem in production — resolve licensing before, not after, you build on them.
- Fashion as a domain — LARGELY NO FREE FEED. There is no free API for fashion week calendars, runway coverage, luxury resale pricing, or brand-level sentiment. Vogue Runway, Launchmetrics, Lyst and The RealReal all either have no API or sell data. The only free proxies are Wikipedia pageviews on brands and designers, and apparel CPI components from BLS. If contracts are written on fashion, accept INCONCLUSIVE coverage rather than pretending a proxy settles it.

### GAPS AND MISSING COVERAGE

- CUSIP — licensed by CUSIP Global Services (FactSet/ABA). There is no free tier and no free bulk mapping, ever. Redistribution is aggressively enforced. Use FIGI (OpenFIGI, free) as your internal canonical security identifier and treat CUSIP as an input you may receive but never republish. The task named CUSIP as a registry to find; the honest answer is that it cannot be had.
- ISIN — no free authoritative source. ANNA/national numbering agencies license it. OpenFIGI will map ISIN→FIGI for free (one direction, and only for instruments it covers), and SEC filings expose some ISINs incidentally, but there is no free ISIN master file.
- AP Elections API and Decision Desk HQ — both paid, both expensive, and both are the sources most people assume are free because the results appear everywhere. Use state Secretary-of-State feeds instead; they are the legal authority anyway.
- TRAC Immigration (Syracuse University) — historically the go-to free immigration-court analysis; moved to a paywall. The underlying EOIR FOIA bulk data is still free but is raw pipe-delimited tables you must assemble yourself.
- Google Trends — there is NO official free API. pytrends and similar scrape an undocumented endpoint, are aggressively rate-limited, return relative-not-absolute values that are re-normalized per query, and violate ToS. The only sanctioned access is the Google Trends dataset in BigQuery. The News/Attention domain lists 'search and attention trends' as a subdomain; be explicit that this is not freely solvable the way people assume.
- Twitter/X API — the free tier is 100 post reads per month. It is not a data source. Bluesky Jetstream (already in the inventory) and Mastodon are the only real-time social firehoses actually available for free.
- Reddit API — free tier is OAuth-gated at roughly 100 queries/minute, explicitly bars commercial use, and bars training. Pushshift is restricted to moderators. Historical Reddit dumps exist on Academic Torrents but are legally ambiguous for commercial use. The inventory lists Reddit as a forum-signal subdomain without noting any of this.
- Have I Been Pwned — the breach API is paid (from ~$4/month). Not free, contrary to widespread belief.
- Shodan and Censys — both paid for anything beyond a token free tier. Not viable as a continuous feed.
- Nielsen, Comscore, Circana/NPD, Billboard chart data, Box Office Mojo — all paid or scrape-only-with-legal-risk. The Entertainment domain's box office and music chart subdomains have no lawful free API; Netflix Tudum TSV and Apple RSS (both correctly listed) are the rare exceptions.
- PERILS, PCS, Swiss Re sigma, Munich Re NatCatSERVICE — all paid. NOAA Billion-Dollar Disasters and FEMA NFIP claims are the only free catastrophe-loss data, and both are US-only.
- Lloyd's List Intelligence, Clarksons, Drewry, Baltic Exchange indices — paid. The inventory lists 'Baltic indices' and container freight rates as subdomains; the actual index values are licensed. Freightos FBX publishes a partial free view; the rest is not free.
- CTBTO International Monitoring System — radionuclide and seismic data restricted to National Data Centres of member states. A frequently assumed-free source that is not. Use USGS/EMSC for seismic and EPA RadNet/Safecast for radiation.
- ITU MARS (MMSI registry) — member-administration access only. Resolve MMSI via Global Fishing Watch's vessel registry or AIS-derived registries instead.
- Equasis and IMO GISIS — free registration but no API, and ToS explicitly bars bulk extraction. Scrape-only with real legal exposure. Paris MoU inspection search has the same shape.
- Ethnologue — paid. Glottolog (CLDF, free) is the usable alternative for language classification. World Religion Database is likewise paid; the ARDA offers free downloads.
- OpenCorporates — the API tightened substantially; bulk and most commercial use now require a paid agreement. UK Companies House (already in inventory) is genuinely free; most other national registries are not.
- PredictIt — wound down. Do not build an adapter for it.
- Ergast F1 API — shut down end of 2024. Jolpica (correctly in the inventory) is the successor.
- LICENSE TRAPS, not dead ends, but they will kill a commercial product: ACLED is free only for academic/non-profit use — the inventory lists it as CORE in two domains and commercial use requires a paid licence. Cloudflare Radar is CC BY-NC. Global Fishing Watch is explicitly non-commercial. EM-DAT is non-commercial. IUCN Red List requires permission for commercial use. Space-Track's ToS restricts redistribution. A 'trillion dollar panel' built on four non-commercial feeds is not a product; audit licences before architecture.
- China's National Bureau of Statistics — no public API, no stable bulk endpoint, and access patterns are actively restricted. There is no free equivalent to e-Stat or IBGE. Practical workarounds: mirror statistics from trading partners' customs data (UN Comtrade, Korea/Taiwan/Japan trade, already partly in inventory), satellite-derived proxies, and the CEIC/Wind paid products. State this plainly rather than pretending a Chinese macro feed exists.
- Google Patents BigQuery is free within the BigQuery tier, but EPO OPS full-text and INPADOC legal status beyond 4 GB/week is paid — patent full-text at scale is not a free resource.
- Gun Violence Archive — free to browse, but exports are capped at 500 rows per query, there is no API, and GVA has explicitly objected to bulk redistribution. Treat as scrape-restricted despite being the definitional settlement source for mass-shooting contracts.
- IAEA PRIS — free to view, but no confirmed public API. Building reactor-status monitoring on it means scraping, with all the fragility that implies. The single most important non-US nuclear data source and it has no clean machine interface.
